outlooksByWeek.2: Nico Collins is in danger of sitting out against the Bengals in Week 2 due to a hamstring injury. He paced Houston's passing attack with a 7-75-1 line on 10 targets in the season opener, so he would work as the team's WR1 again in Week 2 against the Bengals if given the green light to suit up. Cincinnati didn't allow a passing TD to the Buccaneers in Week 1 but had one of the league's worst all-around defenses last season, when the Bengals gave up the second-most yards and third-most points in the NFL. Collins remains a set-and-forget fantasy WR1 as he chases his fourth consecutive 1,000-yard receiving season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Nico Collins (hamstring) didn't suit up for the Texans in Week 2 and may not be ready to return against the Colts in Week 3. If Collins recovers, he'll jump back in as the top option in Houston's passing game and a fantasy WR2 at worst. Should Collins sit again, TE Dalton Schultz could continue to work as the primary pass catcher for C.J. Stroud, while the Texans get by with Kayshon Boutte, Xavier Hutchinson, Jaylin Noel and Jared Wayne at WR.
outlooksByWeek.4: Nico Collins (hamstring) could return from a two-week absence in Week 4 against the Cowboys. Houston's No. 1 WR will immediately jump back into the fantasy WR1 range if he plays against a Dallas defense that's giving up 27.3 points per game. The Cowboys have allowed seven touchdowns through the air, though only three of those went to WRs. Houston hasn't garnered much production out of its wide receiver room in Collins' absence. If Collins remains unavailable, TE Dalton Schultz would likely remain the de facto top target for QB C.J. Stroud.
outlooksByWeek.5: Nico Collins returned from a two-game absence due to a hamstring injury in Week 5 and reclaimed his customary spot as Houston's top receiver and a fantasy WR1. He scored twice against the Cowboys and has compiled 14 catches for 194 yards and three TDs in two appearances this season. Collins can be started with confidence in Week 5 against the Titans, who are allowing 167 receiving yards per game to wideouts. DeVonta Smith and Zay Flowers each compiled at least 117 yards and a TD against Tennessee's secondary.
outlooksByWeek.6: Nico Collins is averaging 83 receiving yards and one touchdown per game as the clear No. 1 option in Houston's passing game. His role isn't expected to change in Week 6 against the Jaguars, even with the Texans having traded for 2024 fourth overall pick Marvin Harrison from the Cardinals. Jacksonville boasts the league's best run defense but has a vulnerable secondary, as the Jaguars are the only team to have allowed over 1,000 yards to wide receivers this season. Collins is a top-five fantasy WR for Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.7: Nico Collins has posted at least 79 scrimmage yards in three of his four appearances this season for the Texans ahead of a Week 7 home game against the Giants. The star wideout can be deployed in his usual spot as a fantasy WR1 for Week 7 while facing a Giants secondary that has done a decent job of suppressing yards from WRs but is tied for the fourth-most TDs allowed to the position with seven. Collins has 24 touchdown receptions in 46 games since the start of the 2023 campaign, including three scores in four games this season as the top target for resurgent QB C.J. Stroud.
outlooksByWeek.9: Nico Collins is coming off a rare dud, as the Giants held Houston's star WR to six yards in Week 7, which is 50 yards fewer than Collins' previous season low. After a Week 8 bye to stew over his down game, Collins should come out motivated to bounce back in a Week 9 road game against the winless Chargers. The Chargers rank in the middle of the pack against WRs, allowing 132.7 yards per game to the position. Collins remains a low-end fantasy WR1 until further notice.
outlooksByWeek.10: Nico Collins has shared the wealth in recent weeks as the locked-in C.J. Stroud spreads the ball around to a deep Texans WR room that also includes Xavier Hutchinson, Tank Dell, Marvin Harrison and Kayshon Boutte. Collins has been targeted five or fewer times in each of the past three games, scoring just once over that span while averaging three catches for 45 yards. He'll need to pick up the pace to reach the 1,000-yard receiving mark for a fourth consecutive season. Collins has dropped from his customary fantasy WR1 standing to the WR2 range for a Week 10 matchup with a Browns secondary that's allowing 144 yards per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Nico Collins has had an inconsistent season but remains a borderline fantasy WR1 for Houston's Week 11 matchup with a Colts defense that's allowing 149 yards per game to WRs and could be without top cornerback Sauce Gardner (calf). Collins drew 16 targets in the Week 10 loss to Cleveland after being targeted 14 times over the previous three games combined. His season average of 68 yards per game is his lowest mark since 2022. He exceeded 1,000 yards in every season from 2023 through 2025 but sits at just 478 yards through Houston's first nine games, two of which he missed due to a hamstring injury. Collins has scored five times in seven appearances and continues to work as the top target for C.J. Stroud.
outlooksByWeek.12: Nico Collins takes a three-game touchdown streak into Houston's Week 12 home game against the Ravens. He's still a weekly must-start option in most formats, but Collins has been more of a fantasy WR2 recently despite the strong play of Texans QB C.J. Stroud. Collins' usage has been inconsistent in Houston's deep WR room, as he has exceeded five targets only once in his last five appearances but was targeted 16 times in the outlier during that stretch. The reeling Ravens have lost six in a row, allowing 29.2 points per game over that span, but they have held WRs to just seven TDs all season. Baltimore is allowing a hefty 162 yards per game to the position, and the Texans' poor run blocking may not allow Houston to ride the ground game as the Ravens' recent opponents have.

player.seasonOutlook: Collins heads into his sixth NFL campaign yet to play a full 17-game season, but having been very productive when on the field. The 2021 third-round pick has cleared 1,000 yards and scored either seven or eight touchdowns each of the past three seasons, finishing in the top 10 in fantasy PPG and top 12 in yards per route run in all three. A force near the goal line, Collins ranked fourth among receivers with 13 end zone targets in 2025. The 27-year-old's target share doesn't stack up with other top receivers (he has never cleared 24.4%), but his high-end efficiency is just enough to keep him in the back-end WR1 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: Garrett Wilson should maintain steady volume for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers. He garnered seven targets in a run-heavy situation to open the year, catching six for 79 yards. Green Bay's secondary is suspect and just allowed Vikings' top receiver Justin Jefferson to score twice, despite Carson Wentz being under center. The Jets will likely need to throw more in Week 2, potentially pushing Wilson into double-digit targets and setting him up for elevated numbers.
outlooksByWeek.3: Garrett Wilson's clear lead role in the Jets' passing game could pay dividends against a porous Lions secondary in Week 3. Wilson has registered seven targets in each of the Jets' first two outings, giving him ample opportunity to exploit a defense that's allowing the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing wideouts through two weeks. The Lions' defense is vulnerable to all positions, but Wilson's spot as the top target is unchallenged.
outlooksByWeek.4: Garrett Wilson likely remains a heavily targeted option for the Jets in Week 4 against the Bears. Wilson is coming off a terrific 10-catch, 107-yard Week 3 where he scored his first touchdown of the season and faces minimal competition for volume in the Jets' passing game. Chicago's secondary has rallied over the last two weeks, not allowing more than 153 yards through the air, but the pieces at corner leave plenty to be desired, setting Wilson up to take advantage of continued high looks in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.5: Garrett Wilson seeks a rebound in Week 5 when the Jets face the Browns. After collecting seven or more targets in each of his first three games, Wilson bottomed out with only four looks in Week 4, finishing with a season-low 27 yards. Cleveland's secondary has allowed at least 291 passing yards in each of the last two weeks, and three opposing wideouts have topped 70 yards. With his usual volume, Wilson appears to be in a favorable Week 5 spot.
outlooksByWeek.6: Garrett Wilson commands a heavy volume of targets in the Jets' passing game heading into a Week 6 matchup with the Patriots. Wilson collected 11 looks in Week 5, topping 100 yards for the second time this season, and has now garnered at least seven targets in four of five outings. New England's secondary is banged up, and the availability of star CB Christian Gonzalez remains uncertain. While the Jets don't want to pass heavily, when they do, targets should be funneled toward Wilson. He has a great chance to exploit a defense that has allowed two 100-yard receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Garrett Wilson plays a steady role in the Jets' middling passing game and enters a Week 7 matchup with the Dolphins. Wilson managed just 44 yards in Week 6, his second-lowest output of the year, but still enters Week 7 with seven or more targets in four of his first six games. Miami has been stingy against wideouts, allowing just two touchdown catches and only two receivers to record more than 55 yards, but Wilson's volume should allow him to flirt with the upper end of that production.
outlooksByWeek.8: Garrett Wilson's high-volume role has faded over the last two weeks as the Jets prepare to host the Raiders in Week 8. After recording 57 or more yards in four of his first five games, Wilson has just 70 total yards over the last two weeks, coinciding with Omar Cooper's emergence. While the Raiders are allowing 8.9 yards per target to opposing wideouts, smaller, shifty receivers have given them fits (DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, Xavier Worthy), suggesting Wilson carries ample volatility into Week 8.
outlooksByWeek.9: Garrett Wilson's usage has been inconsistent ahead of the Jets' difficult Week 9 matchup against the Chiefs. After showing frustration following a three-target Week 7, Wilson was peppered with 12 looks in Week 8-the third time he's amassed double-digit targets. However, he's drawn only 27 total looks in the Jets' other five games. Kansas City has allowed the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing wide receivers but was without corners Mansoor Delane and L'Jarius Sneed in Week 8. Week 9 absences would help Wilson's potential.
outlooksByWeek.10: Garrett Wilson needs to clear the concussion protocol to help the Jets against the Bills in Week 10. Wilson has seen sporadic usage when healthy, amassing double-digit targets three times while averaging 5.8 looks in five additional outings. Assuming he receives a clean bill of health, he'll face a secondary that's allowing the eighth-most fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts. With the Jets likely falling into an early hole, a pass-heavy game flow is probable, with Wilson being an active participant.
outlooksByWeek.11: Garrett Wilson continues to dominate targets in the Jets' passing game ahead of a Week 11 matchup with the Chargers. He garnered a season-high 14 targets in Week 10, his fourth outing with double-digit looks, while topping 100 yards for the third time. Wilson has only three touchdowns on the year and faces a bit of quarterback uncertainty with Geno Smith dealing with an ankle injury, but the Chargers have allowed 11 receivers to score in nine games and have surrendered 340-plus passing yards in consecutive weeks. With steady volume, Wilson profiles as a safe lineup cog in Week 11.
outlooksByWeek.12: Garrett Wilson brings inconsistent volume into the Jets' Week 12 matchup with the Dolphins. Wilson drew only five targets in Week 11, with the Jets attempting only 21 passes, and quarterback Geno Smith has not completed 20 passes for three straight outings. Wilson has four games with double-digit targets and four games with 44 receiving yards or fewer through 10 games. With the Jets likely to remain run-first, Wilson's workload could be limited facing a secondary that's allowing a whopping 9.2 yards per target but the fourth-fewest fantasy points per game to receivers due to limited volume.

player.seasonOutlook: Wilson is eyeing a bounce-back following an injury-shortened 2025 that limited him to seven games. It was the first time Wilson had missed time, having appeared in all 51 games during his first three seasons. The 2022 first-round pick ranked no lower than sixth among receivers in targets in each of those years, but he failed to produce a fantasy campaign better than 20th (PPG) due to New York's quarterback woes. Wilson was off to a hot start last season (four TDs, 14.2 fantasy PPG) thanks to a massive 33% target share (second highest). New York's signal-caller problems still aren't completely solved, but veteran Geno Smith should provide an upgrade over last year's Justin Fields/Tyrod Taylor duo. Wilson, 26, is one of the best raw talents at the position and should be valued as a good WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Colston Loveland will look to get more involved as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Loveland disappointed in Week 1 against the Panthers, failing to bring in either of his two targets, even though it was the highest-scoring Week 1 game in NFL history. The second-year tight end's output was hopefully a fluke, especially as he was still on the field for 86 percent of Chicago's offensive snaps. Loveland will also face a Minnesota defense that allowed five catches for 115 yards to Green Bay's tight ends in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Colston Loveland will look to turn things around as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Loveland disappointed again in Week 2, catching just one of three targets for three yards against the Vikings. The second-year tight end now has just one catch on the year, which is nowhere near the breakout season managers were projecting. He'll likely be thrown to by Tyson Bagent against Philly defense that's allowed the fewest PPR fantasy points per game to tight ends this season (5.1).
outlooksByWeek.4: Colston Loveland will look to improve his role even more as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Loveland finally saw more than a chalked role against the Eagles in Week 3, reeling in all four of his targets for 31 yards. This output is far from what was expected of the second-year tight end heading into the season, but it's still optimistic for the future. He'll face a New York defense that's ceded a top-ten 8.0 fantasy points per game to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Colston Loveland will look to build off a season-best performance as the Bears travel to Green Bay in Week 5. Loveland commanded nine targets in Week 4 against the Jets, which allowed him to finish with six catches for 57 yards. The second-year tight end has now increased his yardage from zero to three to 31 to 57 in the first four games of the year. He'll aim to find the end zone for the first time of the campaign against a Packers defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against TEs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Colston Loveland will look to do more as the Bears play the Falcons in Week 6. Loveland wasn't able to build on a solid six catches for 57 yards in Week 4, reeling in just two of five targets for 19 yards versus the Packers in Week 5. The second-year pass catcher has been thrown to by three quarterbacks of varying skill so far this year, which could add to the struggles of his output. He'll take on an Atalnta defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy TEs this year.
outlooksByWeek.7: Colston Loveland will look to build off a season-best outing as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 6. Loveland caught six of seven targets for 65 yards and a touchdown in Caleb Williams' return to the field. The second-year tight has now caught six passes in two of his last three games, and he sits in a favorable spot after a rough start to the year. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to TEs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.8: Colston Loveland will aim to continue producing as the Bears play the Seahawks in Week 8. Loveland stayed hot in a Week 7 win over New England, finishing with season highs in catches (7), targets (12), yards (69) and tacking on a touchdown. The second-year tight end has had a promising turnaround to the season, with 50 or more yards in three of his last four games and back-to-back outings with a score. He'll face a Seattle defense that's ranked fourth in fantasy points allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Colston Loveland will look to remain a high-volume option as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Loveland was solid again in a Week 8 win over the Bears, bringing in seven of nine targets for 65 yards but losing a fumble. The second-year tight end has now brought in six or more receptions in four of his last five games, and he's found the end zone in two of his last three. He'll take on a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked 22nd in fantasy points allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Colston Loveland will remain a top option in Chicago's passing game against the Saints in Week 11. Loveland has seen success lately after a shaky start to the season, surpassing 50 yards in his last four games and finding the end zone twice in that stretch. The second-year tight end has now posted a 37-363-2 receiving line off 57 targets in the first nine outings of the season. He'll face a New Orleans defense that's ranked 25th in fantasy points allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Colston Loveland will seek to keep it rolling in Week 12 as the Bears play the Lions. Loveland found the end zone again in Week 11 against the Saints, pairing his touchdown with three catches for 29 yards. The second-year tight end has now put together a 27-282-3 receiving line over the last five games after a shaky start to the season. Detroit has allowed the most fantasy points per game to the TE position.

player.seasonOutlook: After averaging 4.1 targets and 8.5 fantasy PPG during his first 14 NFL games, Loveland leaped to 12.0 targets (10-plus in each) and 20.0 fantasy PPG during his final four games of 2025 (including the playoffs). For perspective, there have been only 12 instances of a tight end seeing at least 10 targets in four consecutive regular-season games in NFL history (and only one was a rookie). Loveland's overall efficiency was terrific, as he ranked eighth or better among tight ends in YPR, YPT and YPRR. With DJ Moore gone, the 2025 first-round pick enters his age-22 season all but locked into a massive workload alongside Rome Odunze and Luther Burden III. Loveland's ceiling is lofty, and midrange fantasy TE1 should be his floor.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jeremiyah Love's second NFL game for the Cardinals will be a tough Week 2 matchup against Seattle. Love was largely held in check by the Chargers in Week 1, rushing 11 times for 41 yards and catching two passes for nine yards, but he did get into the end zone on a five-yard run. He logged six fewer carries and 20 fewer rushing yards than Tyler Allgeier, which isn't ideal for fantasy managers who drafted the rookie with the expectation that he'd be the lead back right off the bat. Even if Love gets a larger share of the workload against Seattle, he could struggle against a defense that held Patriots No. 1 RB Rhamondre Stevenson to 2.8 YPC in a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jeremiyah Love is still looking for his first big breakout game heading into Arizona's Week 3 clash in San Francisco. Love has notched 20 rushes for 70 yards and touchdown through two games while adding 25 yards on five catches. Meanwhile, Tyler Allgeier has posted a 22-71-0 line, as both RBs have struggled with efficiency in the early going. Love seems likely to eventually separate as the Cardinals' clear-cut top RB, though the veteran Allgeier could cut into his carries throughout the campaign. The 49ers have been impressive in getting off to a 2-0 start, though they're giving up 4.04 YPC to running backs, just 20th in the league so far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jeremiyah Love appears to have ascended to the clear-cut No. 1 RB in Arizona heading into a Week 4 clash versus the Giants. Love handled a career-high 26 touches (21 carries and five catches) this past Sunday in a loss to San Francisco, compiling 90 yards on the ground and 19 (along with a TD) through the air. Tyler Allgeier was the only other Cardinals RB to log a carry in the contest, and he got just two totes. There could be room for Love to run against the Giants, who are giving up 5.05 yards per carry to running backs, the third-worst mark in the league through three weeks.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jeremiyah Love is dealing with an ankle injury, and his status is uncertain for Arizona's Week 5 matchup against Detroit. The rookie running back logged a full workload Week 4 against the Giants, finishing with 14 carries for 63 yards and one catch for minus-8 yards. Fantasy managers who roster Love will likely keep a close eye on the Cardinals' injury reports throughout the week to get a sense of his odds of playing in Week 5. If he does suit up, Love will face a Lions defense that allowed Carolina RB Chuba Hubbard to rumble for 122 rushing yards and two touchdowns in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jeremiyah Love will look to rebound in Arizona's Week 6 matchup against the Rams. Love managed just 22 yards on 12 carries against Detroit this past Sunday, and he finished without a catch for the first time as a pro. The rookie continues to lead the Cardinals' ground attack but has managed a meager 3.7 yards per carry through five weeks. The Rams rank 12th in the NFL by giving up 15.5 fantasy points per game to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jeremiyah Love enters Week 7 with a questionable tag after missing Arizona's Week 6 game against the Rams with an ankle injury. The rookie has rushed 67 times for 245 yards and a touchdown while adding 11 receptions for 36 yards and another score through five appearances. His 3.7 yards per carry shows room for improvement, though his involvement in the passing game adds fantasy value. Denver has allowed the sixth-most fantasy points per game to opposing RBs in 2026, creating an attractive matchup if Love returns. However, Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight could complicate his workload even if he's cleared to play.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jeremiyah Love has missed Arizona's past two games due to an ankle injury but could return in Week 8 against the Cowboys. Love is slated to practice this week, though that doesn't guarantee that he'll suit up versus Dallas. If the rookie running back misses another game, Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight would likely continue to split the Cardinals' backfield work. Arizona's ground game could be set for a big day against a Dallas defense that is giving up 20.9 fantasy points per game to running backs, seventh-worst in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Love was selected by the Cardinals with the No. 3 overall pick of April's draft. Love has good size and terrific speed (4.36 40-yard dash) to go along with a three-down skill set. He led this year's rookie class in both yards per carry (6.66) and yards after contact (4.16) while ranking second in forced missed tackle rate (3.5) during his collegiate career. He's a capable receiver at all levels, a competent pass blocker and protects the ball well (one fumble on 496 career touches). Love will immediately slot in as Arizona's feature back and, especially considering each of the past nine running backs drafted in the top 12 went on to finish top 12 in fantasy points as a rookie, he should be valued as a midrange RB1 with elite upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tucker Kraft should continue to have a big role in Green Bay's offense as they face the Jets in Week 2. Kraft reeled in three of six targets for 65 yards against the Vikings in Week 1, but he was definitely a huge focus of their defensive scheme. The star tight end will luckily face a New York defense that should be less menacing this Sunday, as they ceded a lower-half 15.4 PPR points per game to tight ends in the 2025 campaign.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tucker Kraft will look to get more involved as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Kraft was held to just two catches for 15 yards in Week 2, but Green Bay's passing attack was lacking for most of the game. The bruising tight end will seek to re-establish himself as a top outlet for quarterback Jordan Love. Luckily, an Atlanta defense that's allowed 20.7 PPR points per game to tight ends so far this season, 29th in the league, could be a great place to start.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tucker Kraft will seek to bounce back as the Packers play the Buccaneers in Week 4. Kraft brought in four of eight targets for 26 yards against the Falcons in Week 3, with some drops that are usually caught. The fourth-year tight end has now posted a 9-106-0 receiving line on 17 targets across the first three games of the season, which is underwhelming considering his start to last year. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's been tough on all but tight ends, allowing a bottom-10 183 receiving yards to the position this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tucker Kraft will seek to build on his best performance of the season as the Packers take on Chicago in Week 5. Kraft recorded a season-high six catches in Week 4 against the Buccaneers, which he converted for 42 yards and a touchdown. The star tight end has started the campaign with a 15-148-1 receiving line, which he could expand on well against Green Bay's biggest rival. Kraft will have a tough task against a Bears defense that's ranked top five against fantasy TEs across four games.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tucker Kraft will look to stay busy as the Packers play the Cowboys in Week 6. Kraft finished with a solid five catches for 64 yards and one rush for two yards against the Bears in Week 5, even with teammates Christian Watson and Matthew Golden combining for 12 receptions for 266 yards and two touchdowns. While the featured tight end has served a different purpose in Green Bay's passing game so far, he still holds a 20-212-1 receiving line on the year. He'll face a Dallas defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy TEs this year.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tucker Kraft will look to do more with his targets as the Packers play the Lions in Week 7. Kraft stayed involved in Week 6 against the Cowboys, catching five of eight targets for 37 yards. The fourth-year tight end has continued to get opportunities with a 25-249-1 receiving line off 37 targets, but he still sits behind the two-man punch of Matthew Golden and Christian Watson at this point in the year. Luckily for Kraft, the Lions have allowed the most fantasy points per game (31.9) to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tucker Kraft will look to build off a solid showing as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Kraft brought in four of six targets for 48 yards and his second touchdown of the season in Green Bay's Week 7 loss to the Lions. The featured tight end has now put up a 29-287-2 receiving line through the first seven games of the season. He'll face a Carolina defense that's ranked 20th in fantasy points allowed to TEs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.9: Tucker Kraft will look to keep it rolling as the Packers play the Patriots in Week 9. Kraft found the end zone once again in Week 8 against the Panthers, finishing the game with six catches for 53 yards and his score. The tight end has now posted a 35-350-3 receiving line on 49 targets this season, and he's found the end zone in back-to-back games. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack in fantasy points allowed to TEs this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Tucker Kraft will aim to get back on track as the Packers play the Vikings in Week 10. Kraft didn't get to join in on any of the fun of Green Bay's offensive explosion in Week 9 over the Patriots, as he brought in just one of his three targets for one yard and rushed the ball twice for eight yards. He's now posted a 36-351-3 receiving line across the first nine games of the campaign. He'll face a Minnesota defense that he logged three catches for 65 yards against in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.12: Tucker Kraft will aim to get back on track as the Packers play the Rams in Week 12. Kraft entered Green Bay's bye with back-to-back one-catch games, which was even more disappointing given he looked to finally be getting on track prior. The fourth-year tight end has now sported a 37-370-3 receiving line over 10 outings this campaign. Los Angeles has also ceded the fewest fantasy points per game to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: Kraft's steady career progression had him on the cusp of a full-on breakout last season, but all was derailed by a torn ACL in Week 9. Prior to the injury, Kraft had seen 10 targets in consecutive games, one of which included a career-high 33.3 fantasy points. Through Week 8, only Jake Ferguson had more fantasy points. Granted, Kraft took advantage of a super easy schedule and was way over his head in the TD department (six TDs with an expected total of 1.8 and only two end zone targets), but his boost in usage and terrific RAC skills (he has led the position in the category each of his three seasons) were enough to get him into the weekly TE1 mix. Kraft's recovery will need to be monitored, but even if he's ready for Week 1, a dip in production is possible in his first year back from the major injury. He's a risky middle-round target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Will Reichard will look to stay perfect as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Reichard converted his lone field-goal attempt and four PATs in a come-from-behind Week 1 win over Green Bay. The third-year kicker was only on the field for extra-point tries after nailing a 38-yard field goal in the first quarter, but the nature of the game made Minnesota more ambitious with their offensive scheme. This could give Reichard more opportunities against a Chicago defense that allowed a middle-of-the-pack seven points to Ryan Fitzgerald this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Will Reichard will look to stay hot as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Reichard converted all three of his field-goal attempts in a bad-weather win over the Bears in Week 2. The third-year kicker has now nailed four field goals and all four of his PATs this year. He'll face a Bucs squad that's tied for the most fantasy points per game allowed to kickers (13.0) so far this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: Will Reichard will look to stay perfect as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. Reichard finished with his best game of the season in Week 3 against the Buccaneers, nailing all three of his field-goal attempts (including two 50-plus-yarders) and knocking in two extra-point tries. The third-year kicker will now focus on a Miami team that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 6.7 fantasy points per game to kickers.
outlooksByWeek.5: Will Reichard should be a high-volume option once again as the Vikings travel to New Orleans in Week 5. Reichard stayed busy in Week 4 against the Dolphins, scoring all 15 of Minnesota's points from field goals. The third-year boot has now made three or more field goals in each of his last three games, and he's yet to miss a kick this year. He'll face a Saints squad that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against kickers this season,
outlooksByWeek.7: Will Reichard remains a high-volume option once again as the Vikings play the Colts in Week 5. Reichard stayed busy in Week 5 before Minnesota's bye, nailing all three of his field-goal attempts and two XPAs. The third-year boot has now made three or more field goals in each of his last four games, and he's yet to miss a kick this year. He'll face a Colts squad that's allowed the most fantasy points per game to kickers (10.3) this year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Will Reichard should remain a high-usage option as the Vikings play the Lions in Week 8. Reichard stayed busy in Week 7 against the Colts, but he did miss his first kick of the season going 3-for-4 on field-goal attempts. Even so, the third-year boot has now gone 18-for-19 on field-goal tries, including six makes from 50-plus yards, and nailed all nine of his XPAs this season. Detroit has ranked a tough third in fantasy points allowed to kickers.
outlooksByWeek.9: Will Reichard will aim to get back on track as the Vikings play the Bills in Week 9. Reichard didn't get much usage in a Week 8 loss to the Lions, missing a field goal attempt from 57 yards and converting his sole extra-point try. Even with a field goal miss in each of the last two weeks, the third-year kicker still sits at 18 of 20 on the year, and he's gone a perfect 10-for-10 on XPAs. Buffalo has ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to kickers.
outlooksByWeek.10: Will Reichard will look to stay involved as the Vikings play the Packers in Week 10. Reichard got back on track in a Week 9 loss to the Bills, making both of his two field-goal attempts. The kicker has now made two or more field goals in all but two of his eight outings this campaign, but the efficiency of the Vikings' offense could improve with Kirk Cousins taking over as the starting QB, turning some of his FG volume into PATs. Green Bay has also ranked a tough first in fantasy points allowed to kickers this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.11: Will Reichard will seek to stay hot as the Vikings play the 49ers in Week 11. Reichard was perfect in a Week 10 win over Green Bay, nailing all six of his kicks with three field-goal makes. The third-year kicker has now converted 23 of 25 field-goal attempts and made all 13 of his XPAs across nine showings. The 49ers have allowed a middle-of-the-pack 8.0 points per game to kickers this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Will Reichard will look to bounce back as the Vikings play the Falcons in Week 12. Reichard went 1-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made one XPA in a Week 11 loss to the 49ers. Fortunately, those misses were just his second and third of the season, so there aren't currently any blaring warning signs of regression. He'll face a Falcons squad that's ranked top 10 versus fantasy kickers this campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: Omar Cooper is uncertain to play for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers due to an ankle sprain. In his NFL debut, he caught his only target for 30 yards. The Jets ran a heavy ground game to open the year, and while they will likely need to throw more in Week 2 to keep up, Cooper's role, even if healthy, is uncertain. The passing game should continue to flow heavily through Garrett Wilson, leaving Cooper's fantasy value volatile.
outlooksByWeek.7: Omar Cooper brings momentum into the Jets' Week 7 matchup with the Dolphins. Returning from a four-week absence due to an ankle issue, Cooper flashed with 103 yards and a touchdown on seven targets. The Jets remain a low-volume passing attack, and Miami has allowed the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing wide receivers, but Cooper provides a big-play option, averaging 19.0 yards per catch in limited action. He could offer a high-upside bye-week fill-in.
outlooksByWeek.8: Omar Cooper's two-week surge is set to extend into Week 8 when the Jets have an inviting matchup with the Raiders. Cooper has topped 100 yards and scored in consecutive outings since returning from an ankle injury, while snagging 11 of his 12 targets. The volume remains modest in a run-first offense, but Las Vegas is allowing 8.9 yards per target to opposing wide receivers with seven similar players registering at least 53 receiving yards.
outlooksByWeek.9: Omar Cooper will look for consistent chances when the Jets face the Chiefs in Week 9. After consecutive 100-yard outings, Cooper failed to collect a target despite a 79% snap share in Week 8, with Adonai Mitchell and Garrett Wilson dominating opportunities. Despite a banged-up secondary in Week 8, Kansas City is allowing the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing wideouts, which includes just two touchdown catches. The Jets' offense could be forced to throw more frequently from behind, but the passing game isn't strong enough to support multiple receivers on a regular basis.
outlooksByWeek.10: Omar Cooper will seek a consistent role when the Jets face the Bills in Week 10. Over the last four games, Cooper topped 100 yards twice, collecting double-digit targets in Week 9 after being shut out in Week 8. The additional looks came with Garrett Wilson (concussion) sidelined, and while Wilson likely returns for Week 10, the Jets also figure to need to pass often to keep up with Buffalo's potent offense. Cooper will come with a high ceiling and ample volatility against a secondary that's allowing the eighth-most fantasy points to wideouts but a mere 7.5 yards per target.
outlooksByWeek.11: Omar Cooper is questionable to suit up for the Jets against the Chargers in Week 11 due to an ankle injury. Cooper managed just one snap in Week 10 as the same ankle that cost him four weeks earlier in the season flared up, resulting in his second game in three weeks without a catch. Pairing that with quarterback uncertainty, with Geno Smith also dealing with an ankle injury, Cooper profiles as a volatile, deep option against a secondary that's allowing the sixth-most fantasy points per game to opposing receivers.
outlooksByWeek.12: Omar Cooper's role in the Jets' offense remains inconsistent ahead of a Week 12 matchup with the Dolphins, and his availability remains in question due to ankle and hip woes. Over his last five healthy games, Cooper has no catches in two of them and a combined 19 in the other three outings. He compiled 115 receiving yards and a touchdown against Miami earlier in the year, and their secondary is allowing 9.2 yards per target to receivers, the fifth-highest mark in the league. Cooper is a high-ceiling speculative play if he suits up.

player.seasonOutlook: Cooper was selected by the Jets in the first round of April's draft. The Indiana product is fresh off a breakout 2025 season in which he posted a 69-937-13 receiving line after totaling 46 catches during his first three seasons with the Hoosiers. Primarily a perimeter target in limited action from 2022 to 2024, Cooper aligned in the slot on 80% of his routes last season. He is a short-area target (9.0 aDOT last season), but still posted strong efficiency numbers, including a 2.61 YPRR. He'll begin his career behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell in New York's Geno Smith-led offense and is unlikely to produce consistent flex value as a rookie.

outlooksByWeek.2: Antonio Williams led the Commanders in receiving in Week 1 despite playing just 26 offensive snaps. Williams ended up with four catches for 64 yards and a touchdown in his NFL premiere. He had as many targets as Terry McLaurin. Williams should see the field with increasing frequency if he continues to perform this well. He has a favorable matchup in Week 2 versus a Dallas defense that was the worst in the NFL last season, and surrendered three passing scores in the season-opening loss to the Giants.
outlooksByWeek.3: Antonio Williams snagged all three of his targets for 24 yards in the 37-20 loss to the Cowboys last game. Williams has seven catches for 98 yards and a touchdown through hsi first two NFL contests. Unfortunately, starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, so veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for Williams and the rest of the Washington offense.
outlooksByWeek.4: Antonio Williams finished third in targets for the Commanders last game. Williams caught just two balls on four looks, though, en route to only 15 yards receiving. Williams caught all of his passes from backup Marcus Mariota, who will likely also line up under center in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been rather poor against the pass in 2026, allowing 276 yards per tilt through the air, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Antonio Williams had eight targets last game for Washington, which was second on the squad behind Stefon Diggs. Unfortunately, Williams could muster just three catches for 21 yards in the lackluster loss to the Colts. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels could return to the fold in Week 5 versus the Giants, which would certainly be a boost for Williams, regardless of whether Terry McLaurin also suits up. McLaurin was sidelined with a hamstring issue. New York has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, though, allowing just 205.3 passing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Antonio Williams managed three catches last game for Washington. Even without the services of fellow wideout Stefon Diggs, Williams accumulated fewer than 35 yards receiving for the third-straight contest. In Week 6, the Commanders face the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 199.6 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.8: Antonio Williams should see an uptick in targets for the remainder of the season, as No. 1 wideout Terry McLaurin will miss the rest of the 2026 campaign for the Commanders due to a knee injury. Williams has double-digit catches in every game thus far during his rookie year, and should slot in just behind Stefon Diggs in terms of opportunities in the passing game moving forward. Following the bye, Washington will face division rival Philadelphia in Week 8. The reeling Eagles have been suspect in defending the pass this season.  Philadelphia is giving up 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Antonio Williams tied for third on the Commanders in targets last game.  Unfortunately, despite seeing six targets, Williams managed only three catches for 25 yards in the 20-13 loss to the Rams. Williams is unlikely to break loose in Week 10 versus the Giants either. New York is allowing just 177.8 passing yards per tilt, which is third in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Antonio Williams found the end zone last game for Washington. The rookie snagged two passes for 42 yards and a touchdown in the 24-21 win over the G-Men. Williams has at least two catches in every game this season, and should continue to see steady work in the absence of Terry McLaurin. However, in Week 11, he will be facing a Bengals defense allowing just 216.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the league. In addition, Cincy has yielded just 11 passing scores, which is tied for fifth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: Antonio Williams had a breakout performance last game for the Commanders. Williams snagged nine passes for 122 yards in the thrilling 22-20 win over the Bengals. This included several big catches down the stretch, including a 42-yarder from quarterback Jayden Daniels to put the Commanders in field goal range for the game-winning kick. Williams received a career-high 11 targets. In Week 12, Williams will face a lackluster Arizona pass defense. The Cardinals are allowing 226.4 passing yards per tilt, which is 20th in the NFL. In addition, the Cardinals have surrendered the most passing touchdowns in the league to date.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams was selected by the Commanders in the third round of April's draft. He is an undersized slot receiver (75% slot in his collegiate career) who soaked up 208 catches (fourth most in this rookie class) during his four seasons (43 games) at Clemson. He was primarily a short-range option (8.0 aDOT), but he caught a healthy 75% of his targets and added value as a rusher (career 25-187-2 rushing), punt returner and even as a passer (143 yards and two TDs on four attempts). Williams is in an all-out battle with the likes of Dyami Brown, Luke McCaffrey, Jaylin Lane and Treylon Burks for the No. 3 WR gig behind Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs. He's worth no more than a late pick in deep leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Germie Bernard and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 2 battle with the Patriots. The rookie should remain on waiver wires after playing just three of Pittsburgh's 67 offensive snaps in their season-opening win. Bernard is below DK Metcalf, Michael Pittman, Jaylen Warren, Rico Dowdle, and Pat Freiermuth on the food chain, and it would take an absence or two from his teammates for him to see an uptick in playing time.
outlooksByWeek.3: Germie Bernard and the Steelers host the Bengals for a Week 3 divisional showdown. With Michael Pittman (foot) on the sidelines last Sunday, the rookie stepped into the No. 3 receiver role behind DK Metcalf and Roman Wilson. Bernard caught four of eight targets for 35 yards in the 20-3 loss, seemingly earning the trust of Aaron Rodgers rather quickly. He led the team in yardage, was second in targets, and tied for second in receptions. Bernard faces Cincinnati's 9th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (25.0) to WRs and should be considered a roster stash until we see this type of performance consistently.
outlooksByWeek.4: Germie Bernard and the Steelers travel to take on the division-rival Browns in Week 4. He caught his only target for 14 yards during Pittsburgh's 30-27 victory in Week 3. One week after leading the team in yardage while finishing second in targets, Bernard fell victim to a Steelers offense that prefers to spread the ball around, as Aaron Rodgers completed passes to nine different receivers in the win. Cleveland's defense is susceptible through the air, as they're tied for 29th in receiving TDs allowed (5) through three games, but Bernard is off the fantasy radar for now.
outlooksByWeek.5: Germie Bernard and the Steelers return home to square off against the Colts in Week 5. The rookie wideout caught both of his targets for 11 yards during Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss in Week 4. Bernard should remain on fantasy benches while playing behind veterans DK Metcalf, Michael Pittman, and Jaylen Warren, along with tight ends Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington. Indianapolis allows 35.0 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks 20th, but his limited involvement on offense doesn't inspire much confidence.
outlooksByWeek.6: Germie Bernard and the Steelers are in Tampa Bay for an interconference clash in Week 6. He hauled in six of nine targets for 80 yards and had one carry for four yards during Pittsburgh's 34-22 Week 5 victory. With Roman Wilson (finger) injured in the win and already ruled out for the meeting with the Buccaneers, Bernard has a real opportunity to fill that void and continue contributing in his debut season. The 2026 second-round pick notched career highs but is still searching for his first career touchdown, something he hopes to change against a Tampa Bay defense that allows 29.5 fantasy points per game (12th) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Germie Bernard and the Steelers are in Paris for an interconference clash against the Saints in Week 7. He caught 11 of 12 targets for 87 yards and the game-winning touchdown in Pittsburgh's 26-19 overtime win in Week 6. The rookie erupted for career highs in every receiving category while notching his first-ever TD. Bernard tied DK Metcalf (11-93-0) for the team lead in receptions while finishing a close second in yardage and targets. He'll aim to stay hot against a New Orleans defense that ranks 18th by allowing 32.3 fantasy points per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Germie Bernard and the Steelers welcome the division-rival Browns to town in Week 8. The rookie caught three of five targets for 27 yards in Pittsburgh's 16-10 victory in Week 7 over the Saints in Paris. Bernard was relatively quiet after posting a 17-167-1 receiving line on 21 targets over his previous two outings. He'll look to bounce back versus a Cleveland defense tied for 19th in fantasy points allowed per game (32.4) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.10: In Week 10, Germie Bernard and the Steelers visit the Bengals in an AFC North showdown. He brought in all five of his targets for 30 yards during Pittsburgh's 27-6 victory in Week 8. The rookie paced the team in receptions, finished second in targets behind DK Metcalf (6), and was third in yardage in a game Aaron Rodgers completed just 13 passes for 172 yards. Bernard will try to get back on track against a Cincinnati defense allowing 31.1 fantasy points per game (15th) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Germie Bernard and the Steelers are in Philadelphia for a Week 11 interconference clash. He failed to bring in any of his three targets during Week 10's loss to Cincinnati but did gain 10 yards on his lone carry. Bernard was held without a catch for the first time since Week 1, when he played only three offensive snaps. Pittsburgh's offense struggled all night, gaining just 247 total yards, but the hope is that Bernard will bounce back versus an Eagles defense allowing 37.9 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Germie Bernard and the Steelers play host to the Broncos in a Week 12 clash on Black Friday. He caught six of 10 targets for 40 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 10 defeat. Bernard led his team in targets, tied for first in receptions, and finished third in yardage after failing to record a catch in his last outing. The talented rookie will look to build upon that performance versus a stout Denver defense that ranks sixth in fantasy points allowed per game (28.1) to opposing WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Bernard was selected by the Steelers in the second round of April's draft. Bernard is a solid, reliable receiver with good size who can align all over the formation (55% slot in 53 collegiate games). Despite playing at three schools in four years, Bernard's production increased each season, including a strong 64-862-7 receiving line (plus 18-101-2 rushing) in 2025. He dropped only four of 240 career targets. Bernard is likely to open his career third or fourth in line at receiver behind Michael Pittman Jr., DK Metcalf and perhaps Roman Wilson. That will create a tough path to consistent rookie-season usage and production, so he's only worth draft consideration in the later rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Malachi Fields tied for third on the Giants in targets in Week 1. Fields caught two passes for 25 yards on four targets in his debut. Only Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely had more targets. The Giants are rather thin at wideout behind the aforementioned Nabers, and Fields is a huge target at 6-4, 225-lbs, so expect him to continue to be a decent contributor to the revamped offense. In Week 2, the G-Men will face a Rams defense that allowed 205 passing yards and three passing scores in a lackluster season-opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Malachi Fields finished third in receptions and second in targets for the Giants last game. Despite seeing increased involvement, Fields caught just two passes for just 30 yards in the dismal loss to the Rams. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, Fields will likely see his stock take a hit. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a lackluster Titans defense allowing 233.5 passing yards per clash, which is 20th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Malachi Fields has two catches in each of his first three NFL games for the Giants.  Unfortunately, he has yet to find the end zone, and has not amassed more than 30 yards in any single contest.  Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which limits the upside for Fields as well. Winston should remain under center in Week 4 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Malachi Fields scored his first NFL touchdown last game for the Giants. The rookie flashed his big-play ability, snagging a 40-yarder from quarterback Jameis Winston along with the 12-yard score. He finished with two catches for a career-best 52 yards and the touchdown. In Week 5, Fields and company will face a Commanders defense that has struggled to defend the pass. Washington has allowed 11 passing scores, which is tied for last in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders are yielding 242.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Malachi Fields saw just two targets last game for the Giants. Meanwhile, star teammate Malik Nabers had a staggering 20 looks in the 27-27 tie with the Commanders. The production for the rookie Fields has been rather consistent through five contests, as he has two catches in every outing. In Week 6, the Giants host the Saints. New Orleans has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, allowing just 212.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the league. However, New Orleans has also given up eight passing scores already, which is tied for 20th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Malachi Fields finished third on the Giants in targets last game. Fields was targeted eight times, though managed two catches for just 18 yards in the 34-27 loss to the Saints. Fields has emerged as the No. 2 wideout behind Malik Nabers, though Isaiah Likely at tight end has also been extremely busy as a pass catcher. Fields has at least two catches in every game he's played, though has just 12 catches on the season. In Week 7, the Giants will face a porous Texans secondary allowing 246 passing yards per contest, which is 27th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: Malachi Fields is coming off a career-best performance for the Giants. Fields snagged four passes for 83 yards in the thrilling 27-21 OT win over the Texans. The rookie has caught at least two passes in every game in 2026. In Week 9, the Giants face divisional rival Philadelphia, which has struggled to defend the pass. Philadelphia's defense is allowing 235.4 passing yards per tilt, which is 24th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Malachi Fields has at least five targets in each of the last three games for the Giants. Unfortunately, he has gained more than 40 yards receiving in just one of those three outings. In Week 10, he will look to take advantage of a porous Washington secondary. The Commanders are allowing 240 passing yards per clash, which is 30th in the league. In addition, Washington has surrendered 16 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.11: Malachi Fields has caught at least two passes in every game during his rookie campaign for the Giants. In fact, he caught three passes for 62 yards last game, and has at least four targets in four-straight tilts. In Week 11, the Giants will face a Jacksonville defense that has been mediocre against the pass in 2026. The Jags are allowing 228.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 19th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: Malachi Fields continued his streak of catching at least two balls in every game this season for the Giants. Fields had two receptions for 25 yards in the 23-18 win over the Jags. Fields received five targets for the game. The rookie is averaging a stout 15.6 yards per catch overall. In Week 12, the Giants will face a Colts defense allowing 220.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 14th in the NFL. However, Indy has also surrendered 20 throwing scores, which is 28th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Fields was selected by the Giants in the third round of April's draft. One of the biggest and strongest receivers in this rookie class, Fields figures to work as a perimeter, vertical target in the pros (career 13.3 aDOT during 49 collegiate games). Fields, who dropped just seven passes in college, handled a target share of, at least, 20% and air yard share of, at least, 30% during each of his final three collegiate seasons (two at Virginia, one at Notre Dame). Fields will battle Darnell Mooney and Darius Slayton for New York's No. 2 receiver gig behind Malik Nabers. The rookie is a fine late-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Matthew Golden should remain a top look in Green Bay's passing offense in Week 2 against the Jets. Golden led the Packers in routes (40) and targets (12) in Week 1 against Minnesota, and he converted six catches for 95 yards. He already looks to have a big enough role for a second-year jump, and the pass-heavy nature of Green Bay's offense helps his case even more. He'll face a Jets secondary that allowed a middle-of-the-pack 26.4 PPR points to wide receivers in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Matthew Golden will remain a top option for Jordan Love as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Golden led Green Bay in receiving yards against the Jets in Week 2, catching four of six targets for 58 yards. The second-year wide receiver is also now set to take on a larger role, at least in the short term, with Jayden Reed looking to miss some time with a neck injury.  Golden will look to expand on his 10-153-0 receiving line against an Atlanta defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 30.3 PPR points per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Matthew Golden will aim to keep it rolling as the Packers play the Buccaneers in Week 4. Golden led Green Bay in receiving yards and targets in Week 3 against the Falcons, catching five of 12 targets for 100 yards and a touchdown. The second-year wide receiver is in the middle of a breakout season, outpacing more than half of his 2025 output in just the first three games of this year. He'll take on a Tampa Bay defense that's allowed a top-ten 25.4 fantasy points per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Matthew Golden will look to do more as the Packers play the Bears in Week 5. Golden finished Week 4 against the Buccaneers with a season-low three catches for 21 yards, but he was able to salvage his performance with a touchdown. The second-year pass catcher remains a top option for quarterback Jordan Love, and he has an 18-274-2 receiving line through four games. Golden will be a major factor in Green Bay's success against their big rival, but he will face a Chicago defense that's ranked top five in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.6: Matthew Golden will aim to stay hot as the Packers play the Cowboys in Week 6. Golden finished Week 5 versus the Bears with the highest yardage total of his career, reeling in six catches for 123 yards. The second-year pass catcher has continued to squash bust projections every week this season, with 24 catches for 297 yards and two touchdowns across five outings. He'll face a Dallas defense that's fared even worse against wide receivers, ranking 21st in fantasy points allowed to the position so far.
outlooksByWeek.7: Matthew Golden will look to build off another statement performance as the Packers play the Lions in Week 7. Golden brought in six of 13 targets for 104 yards and a touchdown in a Week 6 win over the Cowboys, which could have been more if not for a pair of dropped touchdowns. The second-year wideout has now recorded a 30-501-3 receiving line off a team-high 57 targets, and he's already outpaced all of his 2025 output in just six games this season. He'll take on a Detroit defense that's ranked 30th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Matthew Golden will look to bounce back as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Golden wasn't abysmal in a Week 7 loss to the Lions, but he logged a season-low 39 yards on six catches. The second-year pass catcher has still totaled 36 grabs for 540 yards and three touchdowns across the seven games of the season, completely obliterating his 39-361-0 receiving line from the 2025 season across 14 games. He'll face a Carolina defense that's ranked a tough fifth in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.9: Matthew Golden remains a high-volume option ahead of Green Bay's Week 9 matchup at New England. Golden surpassed 10 targets for the fifth time this season in a Week 8 win over Carolina, and he finished the night with seven catches for 79 yards and a touchdown. The second-year pass catcher has now posted a 43-619-4 receiving line on 82 targets this season. He should have plenty of opportunities to stay hot against a Patriots defense that's ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers in the last three weeks.
outlooksByWeek.10: Matthew Golden will look to keep his tear rolling as the Packers play the Vikings in Week 10. Golden logged a career-best 164 yards on 10 catches and found the end zone in a Week 9 win over the Patriots. The second-year breakout receiver also caught every one of his targets in the win, which was a huge improvement from some drop-heavy games this season. He'll face a Minnesota defense that he caught six passes for 95 yards against in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.12: Matthew Golden will look to shine against a tough Rams defense in Green Bay's Week 12 matchup out of the bye. Golden was the Packers' leading pass catcher in a Week 10 loss to Minnesota, hauling in five of nine targets for 70 yards. The second-year pass catcher has now recorded a 58-853-5 receiving line across 10 games, impressing after a subpar rookie season. He'll face a Los Angeles squad that's ranked third in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Golden is eyeing a Year 2 leap following a disappointing rookie season in which he was limited to 39 touches and failed to find the end zone in 14 regular-season games. Golden was limited to 53% of the snaps and never cleared six targets in a single outing. Some optimism was generated from Golden's 4-84-1 receiving line in the playoff loss to Chicago, but even with Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks gone, it's unclear if he will actually see a big boost in usage in Matt LaFleur's offense considering that no Green Bay receiver has cleared a 21% target share since Davante Adams' departure prior to 2022. The speedy Golden, who also contributes as a rusher, is a recent first-round pick entering his second season. He's worth a speculative middle-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Drake Maye will hope to clean up mistakes when the Patriots host the Steelers in Week 2. Maye threw three interceptions in the season opener while under constant pressure, and Pittsburgh's defense, led by T.J. Watt, recorded four sacks last week. While the chemistry was still developing, Maye is now also without No. 1 WR A.J. Brown (ankle) for the immediate future, leading to questionable receiving options. While Maye remains a dangerous runner that will keep his floor reasonable, this likely low-scoring game may not be ideal for a true bounce-back performance.
outlooksByWeek.3: Drake Maye will look to get on track when the Patriots face the Jaguars in Week 3. He is averaging just 183 passing yards through two weeks, with only one touchdown pass and four interceptions. Maye was picked off just eight times all last season. Opponents seem to be pressuring Maye, though Jacksonville is middling at getting after the passer. However, they've allowed only two touchdown passes while limiting quarterbacks to 44 rushing yards. With A.J. Brown still sidelined, Maye will be challenged to exhibit his 2025 form.
outlooksByWeek.4: Drake Maye's confidence appears shaken in the face of pressure ahead of the Patriots' Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Maye has a 1:6 TD:INT ratio through three games, completing just 14 passes in each of his last two games while posting a season-high of 208 yards in Week 2. While he remains dangerous with his legs, he's been held to 18 yards or fewer in Weeks 2 and 3. Buffalo's defense is allowing the seventh-most fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks, giving up seven touchdowns with just one interception. The game could be high-scoring or at least force the Patriots to try and match points, but Maye didn't throw a touchdown pass against this unit a year ago.
outlooksByWeek.5: Drake Maye will look to carry momentum in Week 5 when the Patriots face the Raiders. After a dismal 1:6 TD:INT ratio through three games, Maye provided a season-high 269 yards and three touchdowns while adding 54 yards on eight rushes in Week 4 against Buffalo. Las Vegas is surrendering a 7:4 TD:INT ratio through four games, with six of those touchdowns coming in the last two weeks, suggesting Maye can provide the 2025 version expected by his fantasy managers in Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.6: Drake Maye will look to extend his hot streak to three games in Week 6 when the Patriots face the Jets. After a terrible start to his season (one touchdown, six interceptions), Maye has produced eight touchdowns and one interception over the last two weeks. The Jets are statistically stout against the pass, allowing the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks (195.4 yards per game), but it's come against the likes of Cam Ward, Deshaun Watson, and the Bears' backups. Maye averaged 268.5 yards and threw six touchdown passes in two games against the Jets last season, suggesting his surge can continue in Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.7: Drake Maye hopes to extend his hot streak to four games when the Patriots face the Bears in Week 7. After throwing just one touchdown in his first three games, Maye has burst out with 10 touchdown passes and a scoring rush over his last three games. He now has his full complement of receivers with A.J. Brown returning from an ankle injury. Chicago has allowed two 300-yard passers and multiple touchdown passes three times to date, giving Maye an opportunity to continue his current form Thursday night.
outlooksByWeek.8: Drake Maye's recent surge should continue when the Patriots face the Dolphins in Week 8. In Week 7, he topped 300 passing yards for the second time in three weeks and also added a rushing touchdown for the second time in three games, bringing his total to 14 touchdowns over his last four games. Miami's secondary has been decimated by opposing signal-callers, allowing seven touchdown passes in the last two weeks, multiple touchdown passes in five of six games, and the third-worst yards per attempt at 8.1. This firmly entrenches Maye in Week 8 lineups.
outlooksByWeek.9: Drake Maye will look to continue providing elite production when the Patriots face the Packers in Week 9. While his volume was low, Maye completed a season-high 80% of his passes in Week 8, tossing multiple touchdowns for the fifth straight week while running for a score for the third time in four games. The Packers figure to offer fair resistance, allowing multiple touchdown passes just twice all season, snagging as many interceptions as touchdowns (10) while surrendering just 6.2 yards per attempt, the fifth-lowest mark in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Drake Maye appears poised for a busy outing in Week 10 when the Patriots face the Lions. Maye has tossed multiple touchdown passes in six straight outings (17 total), three times going for 299 yards or more, and could be asked to throw at a high rate with running backs TreVeyon Henderson and Rhamondre Stevenson uncertain to suit up. Pair that with a matchup against a Lions secondary that's allowing the most fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks, and Maye could provide elite numbers in Week 10's Sunday morning affair in Germany.

player.seasonOutlook: Maye is entering his third NFL season and second full season as New England's starter. The 2024 No. 3 draft pick is fresh off a breakout 2025 campaign in which he finished in the top five among quarterbacks in pass completions, yards and TDs, as well as rush attempts and yards. Maye, who led the league in completion percentage (72%) and yards per attempt (8.9), trailed only Josh Allen in fantasy points (351.9), fantasy points per game (20.7) and top-10 fantasy weeks (10). The NFL MVP runner-up will need to overcome a tougher schedule, but he has a better supporting cast (including A.J. Brown) and the 24-year-old's combination of passing talent and rushing ability have him well positioned for another top-five fantasy campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jacory Croskey-Merritt found the end zone in Week 1 for Washington.  Bill served as the primary ballcarrier, toting the pigskin 16 times for 63 yards and the score. Meanwhile, fellow running back Rachaad White had seven carries for only 22 years. In Week 2, Croskey-Merritt will have a favorable matchup versus the Cowboys. Dallas allowed 165 yards rushing and one score on the ground to the Giants in the season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jacory Croskey-Merritt took 12 carries for 43 yards in Washington's loss to Dallas last game. Meanwhile, fellow running back Rachaad White took seven carries for 43 yards, while also catching six passes for 40 yards as a receiver with Washington playing from behind. Croskey-Merritt looks like the preferred back between the tackles, with White acting as the pass-catching or third-down option. The timeshare will likely continue against a devastating Seattle defense in Week 3. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. In addition, Seattle has yet to allow a rushing touchdown to the opposition, and the Commanders will be without their starting quarterback, Jayden Daniels due to injury.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jacory Croskey-Merritt was perhaps predictably stymied by the Seattle Seahawks last game. However, the touches were a silver lining, as Croskey-Merritt garnered 20 opportunities in the 33-31 win over the defending champions. Bill rushed 19 times for 36 yards, while also catching a seven-yard pass out of the backfield. However, fellow running back Rachaad White  averaged more than double Croskey-Meritt's yards per carry, while also finding the end zone through the air. However, there could be plenty of room to roam in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been dreadful against the run in 2026, allowing 141.3 yards per contest on he ground, which is 29th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jacory Croskey-Merritt was stymied last game in a dismal loss for the Commanders. Bill had nine carries for a season-low 15 yards in the 30-13 defeat to the Colts. Even with Rachaad White sidelined due to injury, Croskey-Merritt could find little room to roam. Bill is struggling overall this season, averaging just 2.8 yards per tote. In Week 5, Washington will face a Giants run defense that has vastly improved from a season ago. New York is allowing 109 rushing yards per tilt, which is tied for 15th in the league. In addition, the G-Men have surrendered only two rushing touchdowns through four contests.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed for a season-high 82 yards last game for the Commanders. Bill also found the end zone for the second time this season. Croskey-Merritt has seen double-digit touches in every contest thus far in 2026. In Week 6, Washington will face the San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing 97.6 rushing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL. San Francisco has also given up just three rushing touchdowns through five outings, which is tied for sixth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.12: Jacory Croskey-Merritt found the end zone in his return from injury for the Commanders.  Bill rushed 13 times for 54 yards and the score in the surprising 22-20 win over the Bengals. He nearly doubled up backup Austin Ekeler in terms of carries. Croskey-Merritt also caught two passes for 23 yards out of the backfield. Bill looks to be the featured back heading into a juicy matchup with the Cardinals. Arizona is allowing 128.8 rushing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the league. Likewise, Arizona has yielded 12 rushing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 22nd in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: One of the most hyped-up players entering the 2025 fantasy season, Croskey-Merritt didn't quite live up to lofty expectations, but he was certainly very busy for a seventh-round rookie. "Bill" played 39% of Washington's offensive snaps but, while he finished 23rd among backs in rushing yards, he wasn't much of a factor in the passing game (3% target share). Croskey-Merritt will now compete with newcomer Rachaad White in what appears to be setting up as a committee in Washington. The 25-year-old has shown to be an effective rusher (4.60 yards per carry, 2.19 YAC), but he'll need a big boost in receiving work to find his way into the RB2/flex discussion. He's worth only a late-round flier.

Despite leading the league in turnovers generated (33), the Bears' defense finished a middling 16th in fantasy points last season. The team subsequently replaced Jaquan Brisker, Kevin Byard and Tremaine Edmunds with Devin Bush, Coby Bryant and Dillon Thieneman during the offseason, meaning this will probably again be a matchups-oriented unit. Consider the Bears for favorable early matchups against the Panthers (Week 1) and Jets (4).

outlooksByWeek.2: Brian Thomas tied for second on the Jaguars with 40 receiving yards on three targets in the season opener, as Trevor Lawrence threw just 21 passes in a lopsided win over the Browns. Fellow WRs Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers both got into the end zone, while Thomas failed to score. Thomas also left the game to be evaluated for a shoulder injury, though he managed to return. There are a lot of mouths to feed in Jacksonville's passing game, and the team's entire offensive output could be limited in a Week 2 road matchup against a Denver defense that allowed the third-fewest points in the NFL last season and employs star CB Patrick Surtain. Given that context, Thomas is a boom-or-bust fantasy WR3 for Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brian Thomas has notched exactly three catches for 40 yards in each of his first two games this season, providing a baseline expectation for the 2024 first-round pick's production in Jacksonville's Week 3 home game against the Patriots. Thomas is certainly capable of more, considering he averaged over 75 receiving yards per game as a rookie and scored 10 TDs that year, but has only two TDs in 16 games since then and is unlikely to score against a Patriots defense that has allowed only one touchdown this season. Perhaps breakout teammate Parker Washington will draw attention from top Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez to free up some space for Thomas to operate, but Thomas' lackluster production since the start of last season coupled with the tricky matchup make him a low-end flex play at best for Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brian Thomas has played fewer than 40% of Jacksonville's offensive snaps in two of the team's first three games while totaling just 88 yards. He has been outperformed by Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers in the Jaguars' WR room, which leaves Thomas as a risky fantasy option in Week 4 against the Bengals. Benching the struggling Thomas is a defensible move, though he still maintains starter-worthy upside here considering Thomas flashed elite talent en route to an 87-1,282-10 line as a rookie in 2024, and the Bengals just allowed three different Steelers wideouts to score in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Brian Thomas has just 25 receiving yards over Jacksonville's last two games after kicking off the season with consecutive 40-yard performances. The 2024 first-round pick has played fewer than 50% of snaps on offense while being outperformed by Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers. Thomas is too talented to overlook completely, but he's a risky flex option for Week 5 against the Eagles in London. The matchup would become more favorable if Eagles CB Quinyon Mitchell (knee) sits. Philadelphia is allowing 162 receiving yards per game to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.6: Brian Thomas is coming off a Week 5 goose egg against the Eagles and has just 25 receiving yards over Jacksonville's last three games after kicking off the season with consecutive 40-yard performances. The 2024 first-round pick has a snap share below 50% this season heading into a Week 6 matchup against the Texans in London. Houston has struggled to defend WRs, allowing 193 yards per game to the position, but Thomas isn't a trustworthy fantasy option despite the favorable matchup given his recent struggles. Unless you are desperate for a bye-week plug-in in a deeper format, Thomas should be left on the bench if not dropped outright.
outlooksByWeek.8: Brian Thomas has dropped out of fantasy starting consideration in virtually all formats after finishing without a reception in each of Jacksonville's last two games. He has been outplayed by Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers throughout the season, and even Josh Cameron and Travis Hunter have found more success in recent weeks than Thomas among Jacksonville's wide receivers. Thomas will face a Colts defense in Week 8 that's giving up 142 yards per game to WRs, but don't expect him to be a significant contributor considering he has been limited to a 9-105-1 receiving line on 20 targets through six games.
outlooksByWeek.9: Brian Thomas has caught just one of seven targets over Jacksonville's past three games, but at least that one catch went for a 12-yard touchdown in Week 8 against the Colts. Jacksonville is reportedly open to trading the 2024 first-round pick, so perhaps Thomas will be more involved in the Week 9 game plan against the Ravens to showcase his skills. The Jaguars may be able to pull away from a Ravens team that's starting its third-string QB and feed Thomas targets against a Baltimore defense that's allowing 177.6 yards per game to WRs. Thomas could be worth a speculative add if he was dropped in your league since a change of scenery could boost his value, but the upside of a possible uptick in Week 9 usage is overshadowed by the fact he has just one catch in the last three games, so Thomas is best left on the bench.
outlooksByWeek.10: Brian Thomas has been almost completely phased out of Jacksonville's offense, with just one catch over the past four games. Even a favorable Week 10 matchup against a Titans defense that is allowing the most catches and yards per game to WRs won't be enough to get Thomas back on the fantasy radar.
outlooksByWeek.11: Brian Thomas tied his season high with three catches in Week 10 against the Titans, but he produced just 29 yards and remains an afterthought in Jacksonville's prolific passing game. The 2024 first-round pick has just 13 receptions in nine games during what has been a disappointing third NFL season. With Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers both healthy and clearly ahead of him on the WR depth chart, Thomas has minimal fantasy appeal for a Week 11 matchup against a stingy Giants secondary. Even if one of Washington or Meyers were to get hurt, it's unclear if Thomas would inherit additional opportunities over Josh Cameron or Travis Hunter, so Thomas is safely droppable in all but the deepest formats.
outlooksByWeek.12: Brian Thomas has just 84 receiving yards in his last eight games. He has scored three times over that span, giving Thomas an inkling of deep-league fantasy appeal in Jacksonville's Week 12 home matchup against a Titans defense that has allowed the most production in the league to wide receivers. Thomas tied his season high with three catches in the Jaguars' Week 10 win at Tennessee, though he posted just 29 receiving yards. Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers are far more likely to capitalize on this favorable matchup.

player.seasonOutlook: Thomas is one of the biggest wild cards in fantasy after a roller-coaster start to his career. The 2024 first-round pick was fantasy's No. 4-scoring wide receiver as a rookie, but only played at that WR1 level with Mac Jones under center.
