Thomas averaged 5.8 targets and 14.4 fantasy PPG with Trevor Lawrence under center that season, and was even worse with Lawrence in 2025 (6.2 targets, 9.9 PPG). With Jakobi Meyers, Parker Washington and Travis Hunter in the mix, Thomas was utilized as more of a vertical threat in 2025 (his 14.4 aDOT was fourth highest), which led to a big dip in catch rate and touchdowns, as well as more drops. The Jaguars offense is suddenly very crowded, so Thomas is more likely to be a boom/bust flex than he is the superstar we expected one year ago. The 23-year-old's raw talent makes him worth middle-round consideration.

outlooksByWeek.6: Fernando Mendoza saw his first NFL action late in the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots, completing six of eight passes for 48 yards. His lone drive stalled in the red zone after he came up just short on a fourth-and-4 scramble. Kirk Cousins has led the team to a 3-2 record and remains the starter, but after Las Vegas used the first overall pick in the 2026 draft on Mendoza, it's only a matter of time before he gets a proper look under center. Another loss or two, something that seems very possible given the Raiders' upcoming schedule, could prompt coach Klint Kubiak to make the switch. If Mendoza does see action again in Week 6, he could pop for some intriguing numbers against a Bills defense that ranks 29th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Fernando Mendoza will take over under center in Week 10 with the Raiders dealing Kirk Cousins to the Vikings for a 2027 third-round pick. Mendoza has only appeared once this season, playing during garbage time of a Week 5 loss to the Patriots. The No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft was not impressive during camp but has looked solid in recent practices. His first game as a starter will come against the stout Seahawks defense. It won't get any easier in Week 11 versus the Broncos, so it's best to take the wait-and-see approach before trusting the rookie for fantasy production.
outlooksByWeek.11: Fernando Mendoza did the best he could in his first NFL start against an extremely tough opponent, as the Raiders lost to the Seahawks in Week 10. The rookie quarterback completed under 60% of his passes and didn't throw for a touchdown, but he also avoided committing a turnover and ran in a 10-yard score for Las Vegas' only TD. Mendoza could face another obstacle, as star tight end Brock Bowers suffered an ankle injury that might sideline him for a spell and leave the offense without any game-plan targets. Mendoza will do his best with what he has to work with in Week 11 against a Broncos defense that's tied for 21st in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Fernando Mendoza is beginning to show why he was the first overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. In the Raiders' Week 11 loss to the Broncos, the rookie quarterback threw his first three career touchdown passes, and he did it without Brock Bowers in the lineup. Instead, Jack Bech emerged as his top target, while Mendoza's other two scores went to depth tight end Ian Thomas and running back Ashton Jeanty. Mendoza will look to secure his first win as a starter in Week 12 against a Browns defense that ranks seventh in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Mendoza was selected by the Raiders with the No. 1 overall pick in April's draft. The reigning Heisman Trophy winner and national champion, Mendoza is a big, pocket quarterback with elite accuracy (his career 7.1% off-target rate is easily the best in this rookie class) and a solid arm. Mendoza's 2025 campaign at Indiana included class-best marks in passing TDs (41) and QBR (90.3). He posted a 65-440-7 rushing line in 16 games last season and figures to add some value with his legs in the pros. Mendoza will get some run as a rookie, but his supporting cast isn't overly impressive and he will not start in Week 1 (Kirk Cousins will get the call), so there's not much sense in drafting him in most formats. He'll be worth a speculative add only when he's named Las Vegas' starter.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Rodriguez had just six carries to Bhayshul Tuten's 15 in Jacksonville's season opener. Considering Rodriguez contributes almost nothing as a pass-catcher, with just six receptions in 36 career games, he'll be nothing more than a touchdown-dependent deep-league dart throw for fantasy purposes as long as Tuten is healthy. Rodriguez is unlikely to find the end zone in Week 2 against a Broncos defense that allowed the second-fewest rushing yards and fourth-fewest rushing TDs (eight) to RBs last season, though Denver gave up two total TDs to Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Rodriguez has notched just six rushing attempts in each of his first two games with the Jaguars. He's averaging a paltry 3.0 yards per carry and has yet to earn a target in the passing game, where Rodriguez has been a non-factor his entire NFL career. Bhayshul Tuten has 28 carries this season and is the clear lead back for the Jaguars. Rodriguez isn't an advisable fantasy play in Week 3 against a Patriots defense that's allowing a minuscule 8.0 points per game.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chris Rodriguez has recorded between six and eight carries in each of his first three games with the Jaguars heading into a Week 4 road tilt at Cincinnati. He scored his first TD of the season in the Week 3 rout of the Patriots, but Rodriguez will remain a touchdown-dependent deep-league option as long as Bhayshul Tuten is available. The Bengals have allowed the most receiving yards in the league to RBs, but Rodriguez almost certainly won't capitalize on that weakness, as he has yet to earn a target this year and has just six career catches in 38 games.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chris Rodriguez has a consistent role as the Jaguars' No. 2 RB behind Bhayshul Tuten, but Rodriguez's usage level is too low to warrant lineup consideration in most formats. Rodriguez has recorded between six and eight carries in each of his first four games with the Jaguars. He's riding a two-game TD streak but has been a complete non-factor in the passing game with zero targets while averaging a mediocre 4.2 yards per carry. Jacksonville faces an Eagles defense in Week 5 that ranks among the 10 most generous to RBs on the ground, allowing 106 rushing yards per game to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chris Rodriguez has exceeded six rushing attempts in only one of five games with the Jaguars and has just one catch all season. With starting RB Bhayshul Tuten healthy heading into a Week 6 matchup with the Texans, Rodriguez doesn't look like a usable fantasy option in most formats against a stout Houston front seven that's limiting RBs to 3.5 yards per carry. Rodriguez remains a viable bench stash for managers hedging against a Tuten injury.
outlooksByWeek.8: Chris Rodriguez remains No. 2 on Jacksonville's RB depth chart behind Bhayshul Tuten, limiting Rodriguez's Week 8 fantasy appeal to deeper formats. Rodriguez logged a season-high 11 carries in Jacksonville's Week 6 loss to the Texans prior to a Week 7 bye. He has handled fewer than six carries only once all season, but Rodriguez is a non-factor in the passing game, with just one catch in 2026. Rodriguez will be a touchdown-dependent fantasy play in Week 8 against a Colts defense that has allowed five rushing scores to RBs through seven games.
outlooksByWeek.9: Chris Rodriguez is the clear No. 2 RB for the Jaguars behind Bhayshul Tuten heading into a Week 9 trip to Baltimore. Rodriguez has made the most of his opportunities, setting season highs in scrimmage yards in each of the past two games, with 55 in Week 6 against the Texans and 58 in Week 8 against the Colts. He remains a touchdown-dependent fantasy option for Week 9, as Rodriguez has just two catches this season and is averaging just under seven touches per game overall. The Ravens have allowed seven rushing scores to RBs in eight games, but there's an elevated chance of the Jaguars pulling away and leaning on Rodriguez more to run out the clock since Baltimore could be down to its third-string QB.
outlooksByWeek.10: Chris Rodriguez has scored in four of Jacksonville's last six games, but he hasn't topped 58 scrimmage yards in a game all season and is averaging 33 yards per game as Bhayshul Tuten's backup heading into a Week 10 road game against the Titans. Rodriguez will remain a touchdown-dependent Week 10 flex option against a Tennessee defense that has allowed plenty of yards to RBs but limited the position to six TDs in eight games. Tuten was hampered by ankle and foot injuries in Jacksonville's previous game but has since had 10 days to recover, suggesting that Rodriguez's path to a larger role remains blocked.
outlooksByWeek.11: Chris Rodriguez remains a touchdown dependent deep league flex option for Week 11, though his chances of cashing in aren't great against a Giants defense that has allowed just four rushing TDs to RBs all season. Rodriguez had a season low five yards in Jacksonville's Week 10 win over the Titans. He has scored on the ground in four of Jacksonville's nine games while rushing for at least 55 yards twice, but Rodriguez remains a non-factor as a receiver, with just four catches for 36 yards all season. Bhayshul Tuten remains the clear No. 1 RB for the Jaguars.
outlooksByWeek.12: Chris Rodriguez could make a spot start for the Jaguars in a juicy Week 12 matchup against the 1-9 Titans if Bhayshul Tuten (ankle) sits out, in which case Rodriguez would have fantasy RB2 upside. If Tuten suits up, Rodriguez would remain in the deep-league flex conversation as Jacksonville's change-of-pace RB against a Tennessee defense that has allowed 44.7 points per game in its last three. The Jaguars scored 40 points against the Titans in Week 10, though Rodriguez was limited to a season-low five rushing yards in that game while Tuten racked up 113 scrimmage yards and a TD.

player.seasonOutlook: Rodriguez, a 2023 sixth-round NFL draft pick, spent his first three seasons with Washington and has primarily played a depth role, but he did hit career-high marks in touches (115), yardage (530) and touchdowns (six) in 2025. Rodriguez has handled more than 10 touches in nine career games and averaged 13.1 touches, 65.9 yards and 11.7 fantasy points with a total of seven touchdowns in those outings. Though he's an effective rusher, Rodriguez is not an option in the passing game (seven career targets). The 26-year-old's contract included a healthy $6.2 million in guarantees, so he's likely to have a legitimate offensive role as a counterpart to second-year backs Bhayshul Tuten and LeQuint Allen Jr. Rodriguez might score the occasional touchdown, but his role won't allow consistent fantasy output. He's best stashed on benches.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rome Odunze will seek to do more as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Odunze was unable to capitalize on the highest-scoring Week 1 game ever, as he finished the game with two catches for 52 yards. The third-year receiver still figures to be a top target for Caleb Williams moving forward, especially in closer matchups where a consistent option is needed. Odunze will face a Minnesota defense that ceded the second-most PPR points to WRs (55.2) in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rome Odunze will look to remain a top look in Chicago's passing offense in Week 3 against the Eagles. Odunze caught three of four targets for 43 yards against the Vikings in Week 2, and he now sits at a 5-95-0 receiving line across two games. The third-year pass catcher's unimpressive output could continue, given that Tyson Bagent is slotted to start under center in place of Caleb Williams (hamstring). Odunze will face a Philadelphia defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 29.4 PPR points per game to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rome Odunze will look to improve on modest production as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Odunze reeled in three of six targets for 44 yards against the Eagles in Week 3, adding to his already disappointing start to the season. The third-year wide receiver has been consistent, recording three or fewer catches for 52 or fewer yards in each of Chicago's first three games. Odunze will face a Jets squad that has allowed the fourth-fewest receiving yards (337) to WRs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.5: Rome Odunze will look to build off a big performance as the Bears play the Packers in Week 5. Odunze was on fire in Week 4 against the Jets with Tyson Bagent under center, bringing in six of seven targets for 94 yards. The starting wide receiver has now posted a 14-233-0 receiving line on the year, which leaves plenty of room to grow. He'll face a Green Bay defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 31.8 fantasy points per game to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rome Odunze remains a top option in Chicago's passing game ahead of Week 6 at Atlanta. Odunze brought in just three of his nine targets for 40 yards in a Week 5 blowout loss to the Packers, but he still ranked second in receiving yards. The volatility of the Bears' quarterback position has affected Odunze's production so far this season, so the return of Caleb Williams would likely be favorable. Either way, he'll face a Falcons defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Rome Odunze will look to do more as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Odunze brought in just three of four targets for 39 yards in Week 6, which was a bit of a bummer, with Caleb Williams throwing for 305 yards. The third-year pass catcher has been held in check in more games than not this season, catching 20 of 33 targets for 312 yards with zero touchdowns. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack versus fantasy WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Rome Odunze will look to capitalize on his opportunities as the Bears travel to Seattle in Week 8. Odunze was outperformed by teammate Luther Burden once again in Week 7 against the Patriots, logging four catches for 69 yards to Burden's four catches for 130 yards and a touchdown. Odunze has still been solid throughout this year, with a 24-381-0 receiving line over the first seven games of the season. He'll face a Seahawks defense that's ranked first in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Rome Odunze figures to be a top option in Chicago's passing game again as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Odunze finished Week 8 with his second-highest yardage of the season, bringing in four of six targets for 87 yards. The third-year wide receiver has eight catches for 156 yards in the last two weeks, which is his most productive two-game stretch so far this campaign. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Rome Odunze will aim to build on a season-best showing as the Bears play the Saints in Week 11. Odunze notched his first touchdown of the season and paired it with four catches for 60 yards in a Week 9 win over Tampa Bay before Chicago's bye week. The third-year pass catcher has now logged 32 receptions for 528 yards and a touchdown across nine games this season. He'll take on a New Orleans squad that's ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.12: Rome Odunze will be a solid option in Chicago's passing offense again in Week 12 at Detroit. Odunze caught four targets for 45 yards in a Week 11 win over the Saints, increasing his four-catch streak to four games now. The third-year pass catcher has now pieced together a 36-573-1 receiving line on 55 targets this campaign. He'll now shift focus to a Lions defense that's ranked in the middle against fantasy WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Odunze opened the 2025 season with a bang, scoring five touchdowns in his first four games and producing 15-plus fantasy points in each game. Things fell apart from there, as the 2024 first-round pick went on to deliver one touchdown and two double-digit fantasy outings over his next eight games prior to missing Weeks 14 through 18 due to injury. On the plus side, Odunze remained heavily targeted throughout the season, especially near the goal line, and he is ninth in the NFL with 24 end zone targets since he was drafted. On the other hand, his connection with Caleb Williams needs work, as his 48% catch rate ranked near the basement at the position. Odunze, 24, is still ascending and has a clearer path to targets with DJ Moore out of the mix. He's a candidate for a Year 3 leap and should be valued as a WR3 with upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jameson Williams will seek to convert on more of his looks as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. Williams garnered nine targets against the Saints in Week 1, but he reeled in just four of them for 45 yards. The fifth-year wide receiver will need to keep his catch rate well above 50 percent if he hopes to record a third-straight 1,000-yard campaign, but he'll luckily face a Bills defense that allowed the seventh-most PPR points (40.0) to wide receivers in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jameson Williams will look to do more as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3. Williams' output has been disappointing so far this season, with just six catches for 78 yards across two games. The fifth-year wideout has also reaped no benefits from Detroit's struggling defense, with Amon-Ra St. Brown currently carving out a monopoly in the wide receiver room. Williams will face a New York defense that's allowed 27.2 PPR points per game to its first two opponents, a top-10 mark.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jameson Williams has yet to find the end zone heading into the Lions' Week 4 game at Carolina. Williams totaled a season-high 49 yards against the Jets in Week 3, but he's now recorded four or less catches for 50 or fewer yards in every game this year. The fifth-year wideout will seek to get more out of Detroit's offensive success against a Panthers defense that's allowed a top-five 23.2 fantasy points per game to wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jameson Williams will look to build off a big outing as the Lions travel to Arizona in Week 5. Williams had his best game of the year in Week 4 against the Panthers, bringing in six of eight targets for 102 yards. The speedster has still posted just a 16-229-0 receiving line to start the season, but he has seen eight or more targets in two games, which could bode well for his output. He'll also face a Cardinals defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jameson Williams will seek to stay involved as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. Williams found the end zone twice in a Week 5 win over the Cardinals before Detroit's bye week, which was done with two catches for 47 yards. The fifth-year wideout has now totaled 18 grabs for 276 yards and two scores on the season. He'll face a Green Bay secondary that's ranked in the middle versus fantasy WRs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jameson Williams will aim to keep it rolling as the Lions play the Vikings in Week 8. Williams produced his best fantasy performance of the year in a Week 7 win over Green Bay, hauling in five of nine targets for 91 yards and two touchdowns. The speedy wideout has now produced four touchdowns in his last two games, along with seven catches for 138 yards in that stretch. He'll face a Minnesota defense that's ranked fourth in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jameson Williams will look to keep it rolling as the Lions travel to Miami in Week 9. Williams kept his touchdown streak and recent dominance alive in a Week 8 win over Minnesota, reeling in four of six targets for 70 yards and a touchdown. The speedy wideout has now logged 11 catches for 208 yards and a whopping five touchdowns in his last three outings. He'll face a Dolphins defense that's ranked third in fantasy points allowed to WRs on the year.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jameson Williams will look to get more volume as the Lions play the Patriots in Week 10. Williams struggled to get touches with a stagnant passing game against the Dolphins in Week 9, recording one catch for 31 yards and one rush for nine yards. The speedy wideout has now posted a 28-468-5 receiving line on 44 targets across eight games. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jameson Williams will remain a flashy option in Detroit's offense heading into Week 11 against the Buccaneers. Williams didn't benefit, like some of his teammates, from an offensive explosion in a Week 10 win over New England, but he still hauled in four of seven targets for 50 yards. The speedy wideout has now logged 32 catches for 518 yards and five touchdowns so far this season. He'll take on a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked 11th in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Jameson Williams will seek to keep it rolling as the Lions play the Bears in Week 12. Williams led Detroit in receiving yards against the Buccaneers in Week 11, bringing in all four of his targets for 93 yards and a touchdown. The speedster has now posted a 36-611-6 receiving line across 10 games, and he's logged 50 or more yards in four of his last five outings. He'll face a Chicago defense that's ranked a tough 10th in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.

player.seasonOutlook: The slow start to Williams' career is a thing of the past after the speedster delivered 1,000-plus-yard campaigns each of the past two seasons. After breaking out with a 22nd-place fantasy finish (25th PPG) in 2024, Williams set new career highs in targets, catches, yards and touchdowns en route to a 12th-place finish (19th PPG) last season. A lack of goal-line work (eight career end zone targets) and some drop woes (NFL-high eight in 2025) are drawbacks, but Williams' explosive-play ability has led him to finish sixth or better in yards per reception and yards per target each of the past two seasons. The 25-year-old remains one of Jared Goff's top targets in Detroit's high-scoring offense and is a fine fantasy WR3 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns travel to take on the Buccaneers and their 22nd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (26.8) to RBs in Week 2. The second-year back rushed 12 times for 33 yards and caught both targets for 17 yards during Cleveland's 34-10 Week 1 loss. Running lanes and beneficial game flow are two things to be concerned with for Judkins, as the Browns again appear to be one of the worst offenses in the league. If the QB play improves even slightly, he could see an uptick in opportunities in both the running and passing games, but he should be started with caution until that situation improves.
outlooksByWeek.3: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns welcome the Panthers to town for an interconference showdown in Week 3. He finished Cleveland's 23-19 upset win over the Buccaneers in Week 2 with 12 carries for 21 yards and caught all five targets for 27 yards. No other running back tallied more than two carries, so it's clear Judkins is still the No. 1 option out of the backfield, but that hasn't come with much success through two weeks of action. Next up is a Carolina defense that ranks 31st in fantasy points allowed (36.3) and last in TDs surrendered to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns welcome the Steelers to town for an AFC North clash on Thursday night in Week 4. He rushed 18 times for 70 yards and caught both targets for nine yards during Cleveland's upset win over the Panthers in Week 3. Judkins surpassed 35 yards on the ground for the first time this season, and there's a chance he could build upon that against their division rivals. Pittsburgh's defense ranks 20th in fantasy points allowed (22.1) per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns visit the Jets in Week 5, looking for their fourth consecutive win. He had his best performance of 2026 in Week 4, rushing 17 times for 53 yards and his first TD of the season while catching six of seven targets for 43 yards during Cleveland's 27-24 victory. No other back recorded more than two carries, and Judkins led the team in receptions and tied for third in targets. Up next is a Jets defense that allows 28.3 fantasy points per game to RBs, which ranks 30th.
outlooksByWeek.6: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns welcome the division rival Ravens to town in Week 6. He tallied 14 carries for 44 yards and caught three of four targets for six yards during Cleveland's Week 5 loss. Judkins played just 52.9% of snaps, likely due to a right ankle injury suffered in-game, and he was reportedly spotted wearing a walking boot afterward. Head coach Todd Monken called it a "tweak" on Monday and considers his starting running back day-to-day. Judkins' practice participation this week will be worth monitoring, as he'll be facing a Baltimore defense that allows 18.8 fantasy points per game to RBs, which is tied for ninth.
outlooksByWeek.7: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns visit the Titans for an interconference clash in Week 7. He was inactive for Cleveland's 13-10 victory in Week 6 due to an ankle injury he sustained in Week 5. Jaleel McLaughlin (9), Audric Estime (9), and Michael Burton (1) handled the backfield responsibilities, with Estime notching his first TD as a Brown. Judkins is averaging 3.0 yards per carry on 73 attempts, and if he's active for Week 7, he'll face a Tennessee defense allowing 20.3 fantasy points per game (13th) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns are in Pittsburgh for an AFC North showdown in Week 8. He rushed 17 times for 96 yards and two touchdowns and caught his only target for eight yards during Cleveland's 27-24 victory in Week 7. Judkins returned from a one-game absence due to an ankle injury and posted his best performance of the year, setting season highs in rush yards and yards from scrimmage (104). He'll aim to stay hot against a Steelers defense allowing 20.5 fantasy points per game (T-11th) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns travel to face the Saints in Week 9. He rushed 11 times for 25 yards and caught both of his targets for 24 yards during Cleveland's 27-6 Week 8 loss. Judkins handled 11 of 12 carries out of the backfield but took a backseat to Dylan Sampson in the passing game. Judkins will aim to bounce back against a New Orleans defense that ranks last in fantasy points allowed per game (30.8) to opposing RBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: In Week 10, Quinshon Judkins and the Browns return home for the first time in three weeks to host the Texans. He rushed 15 times for 43 yards and caught his only target for two yards during Cleveland's overtime loss in Week 9. Judkins and the entire Browns offense struggled to make much happen on the ground, registering 95 yards on 34 carries for a meager 2.8 yards per attempt. Judkins has been underwhelming in 2026, racking up 385 yards on 116 carries (3.3 YPC) with three TDs and a 22-136-0 receiving line on 25 targets. He'll try to turn things around versus a Houston defense allowing 22.4 fantasy points per game (20th) to opposing RBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: In Week 12, Quinshon Judkins and the Browns welcome the Raiders to town on Sunday Night Football. He had 10 carries for 38 yards and a touchdown and caught three of five targets for 33 yards during Cleveland's Week 10 win. Judkins has struggled to find running room in 2026, rushing 126 times for 423 yards (3.4 YPC) and four scores, but there's hope that could change in Week 12. Las Vegas allows 26.9 fantasy points per game (28th) to RBs and just gave up 133 yards and three TDs on the ground in their latest outing.

player.seasonOutlook: Judkins is entering his second NFL season after a roller-coaster rookie campaign in which a solid 14-game stretch of action was bookended by missed time early because of an off-field issue and late because of a season-ending leg injury in Week 16. When on the field, Judkins handled a massive 71.4% share of Cleveland's designed rush attempts (16.4 per game). Though he was held to 3.6 yards per carry, he was dealing with a league-high 7.4 box defenders per attempt. He wasn't involved much as a receiver (2.6 targets per game), however, and was limited to 12.1 fantasy points per game (26th among RBs). The Cleveland offense has a new coach (Todd Monken) and quarterback questions remain, so while Judkins has a clear path to a big carry total, the 22-year-old might cap out as a midrange RB2 in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tony Pollard got just eight touches in the season opener as the Titans fell behind against the Jets and abandoned the run. Negative game scripts could be a recurring problem for Pollard, and the Titans will be substantial Week 2 underdogs at home against the Eagles. On the bright side, Pollard recorded at least 1,288 scrimmage yards in each of the previous two seasons, even as the Titans posted a 3-14 record both years. Pollard's status as the team's starting running back keeps him in the Week 2 flex/RB3 conversation.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tony Pollard could be worth plugging into Week 3 fantasy lineups as a high-end RB3/flex option for the Titans' road matchup with a Giants defense that has struggled to contain RBs in the early going. Javonte Williams scored two TDs against the Giants in Week 1, then Kyren Williams and Blake Corum each exceeded 90 scrimmage yards against the Giants in Week 2, with Williams tacking on a TD. Pollard has reprised his role as the 1A option in Tennessee's backfield over Tjyae Spears. The former Cowboys RB has averaged 77 scrimmage yards per game since joining the Titans prior to the 2024 campaign, but Pollard has been limited to 99 yards through two games to begin this season. Negative game scripts are often a problem for the Titans, but Tennessee is likely to stay within striking distance and keep Pollard involved on the ground against a Giants team that's missing starting QB Jaxson Dart (knee).
outlooksByWeek.4: Tony Pollard has increased his yardage total in each of Tennessee's first three games heading into a Week 4 road game against the Ravens, who are allowing 99 scrimmage yards per game to RBs. Pollard had just 34 scrimmage yards on eight touches in a lopsided Week 1 loss to the Jets, but he recorded 65 yards on 15 touches in Week 2 and 96 scrimmage yards on 21 touches in Week 3 as the Titans managed to stay within striking distance before falling to the Eagles and Giants, respectively. With second-year QB Cam Ward struggling to move the ball through the air, the Titans will likely try to continue featuring their Pollard-led ground game, though there is a substantial risk of Lamar Jackson and the Ravens pulling away and forcing Tennessee into a more pass-heavy game plan. Given Pollard's status as the lead back in a low-octane offense, he has a decent floor as a flex play but isn't the most exciting Week 4 RB option.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tony Pollard is averaging 61 scrimmage yards per game and scored his first touchdown of the season in Week 4 against the Ravens, though that wasn't enough to keep the Titans from dropping to 0-4. In Week 5, Tennessee hosts the AFC South rival Texans, who are also 0-4. The Titans should manage to stay within striking distance and give Pollard his full workload on the ground, though Houston has held RBs to just 91 scrimmage yards per game. Pollard is a high-floor, low-ceiling flex play as usual for Week 5 given his role as the lead back in a struggling Titans offense that's averaging the fewest yards and second-fewest points per game.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tony Pollard remains a viable flex option in Week 6 against the Colts thanks to his high touch floor as the starting RB in a putrid Titans offense. Pollard has at least 14 touches and 50 scrimmage yards in all but one game this season but has been limited to one TD on a Titans offense that has found the end zone just six times through five games. Indianapolis is giving up 100 rushing yards per game to RBs as well as a league-high 53 receiving yards per game to the position, so Pollard has a higher ceiling than usual in this Week 6 matchup to go with his steady floor.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tony Pollard has at least 14 touches and 50 scrimmage yards in each of the Titans' last five games. He's locked into a high touch floor in any game the 1-5 Titans can keep within striking distance, and Tennessee is unlikely to fall too far behind in Week 7 at home against the Browns, who are scoring just 17.7 points per game, tied for fourth-fewest in the NFL. Cleveland has started 4-2 thanks to a stout defense that's allowing 20.3 points per game and has allowed just one TD to a running back all season, but Pollard's hefty usage keeps him locked in as a viable flex play for Week 7, even though he looks unlikely to add to his season total of one TD in a Titans offense that's tied for the worst in the league at 14.0 points per game.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tony Pollard is coming off his best game of the season, as he racked up 129 rushing yards and three TDs against the Browns in Tennessee's Week 7 loss. The veteran RB is the most consistent offensive player on the Titans, having racked up at least 14 touches and 50 scrimmage yards in six consecutive games. His solid touch floor makes Pollard a passable fantasy RB2 for Week 8, but don't expect a repeat of his Week 7 outburst against a Bengals defense that has limited RBs to three total TDs in six games.
outlooksByWeek.10: Tony Pollard delivered consecutive elite performances prior to Tennessee's Week 9 bye, racking up 292 scrimmage yards and five TDs across losses to the Browns and Bengals. Prior to that two-game stretch, he had just one TD through seven games and no 100-yard performances. If he isn't traded prior to Tuesday's deadline, Pollard would maintain fantasy RB2 upside for Week 10 despite a difficult matchup against a Jaguars defense that's holding RBs to 68 yards per game. Even before his recent uptick in production, Pollard had a solid floor as the clear lead back for Tennessee.
outlooksByWeek.11: Tony Pollard has racked up 391 scrimmage yards and six touchdowns over Tennessee's last three games, putting him in the fantasy RB1 conversation for a Week 11 trip to Dallas. After a pair of dominant rushing performances, Pollard struggled to find running room against Jacksonville's elite front in Week 10 but racked up 66 receiving yards and a TD on a career-high eight catches. The former Cowboys RB is locked into a workhorse role for the Titans, and Pollard's old team has given up the most fantasy production in the league to RBs, allowing 155 scrimmage yards per game, as well as a league-high 16 total TDs to the position through 10 games.
outlooksByWeek.12: Tony Pollard rushed for 110 yards in the Titans' Week 11 loss to Dallas. His touchdown streak was halted at three games and six TDs, but he's up to 501 scrimmage yards over the past four games. Tennessee's entire offense has picked up the pace over that span, with QB Cam Ward stringing together his best three games of the season. Pollard faces a daunting Week 12 matchup against Jacksonville's elite run defense, but he navigated this matchup effectively in Week 10, setting season highs across the board with eight catches for 66 yards and a TD on nine targets to complement his modest 33 rushing yards on nine carries. You may as well keep rolling with the surging Pollard, though the tough opponent drops him to the low-end fantasy RB2 range for Week 12. With Tyjae Spears (knee) on IR, Pollard faces virtually zero competition for carries.

player.seasonOutlook: Pollard has handled a hefty 67.2% of the Titans' designed rushing attempts since his arrival two seasons ago (15.2 per game) and, even with solid efficiency, he has finished 22nd and 30th in fantasy points per game. The culprits? Tennessee's struggling offense (Pollard has exactly five TDs in both seasons) and a limited receiving role when Tyjae Spears has been healthy (Pollard's targets fell from 3.5 per game in 2024 to 2.5 per game in 2025). Barring a major leap from quarterback Cam Ward, Pollard is unlikely to deliver only the second top-20 fantasy campaign (in points per game) of his career. The 29-year-old, entering his eighth NFL season (third with Tennessee), is a low-ceiling flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Stefon Diggs had more than double the targets of teammate Terry McLaurin in Week 1 for Washington. Diggs was targeted a team-high nine times, though managed only four catches. However, he gained 55 yards and also found the end zone, though had a costly celebration penalty on the score that cost Washington a chance to go for two and tie the game late. Still, it was an extremely promising start for Diggs, who will have a favorable matchup in Week 2 versus Dallas. The Cowboys allowed 229 passing yards and three touchdowns through the air to the Giants in their season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Stefon Diggs has scored three times in two games as a member of the Commanders. Diggs snagged five passes for 47 yards and two touchdowns in Washington's loss to Dallas last week. Unfortunately, starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, so veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for Diggs and the rest of the Washington offense, though the newly acquired wideout does seem to have a knack for finding the end zone thus far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Stefon Diggs finished second in targets for the Commanders last game. Diggs caught four balls on seven looks, though managed just 33 yards in the surprising win over Seattle. Diggs was also held out of the end zone for the first time this season. Diggs caught all of his passes from backup Marcus Mariota, who will likely also line up under center in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been rather poor against the pass in 2026, allowing 276 yards per tilt through the air, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Stefon Diggs led the Commanders in targets and receptions last game. With Terry McLaurin sidelined due to a hamstring issue, Diggs managed five catches on nine targets. However, he could only muster 35 yards in the dismal 30-13 loss to the Colts. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels could return to the fold in Week 5 versus the Giants, which would certainly be a boost for Diggs, regardless of whether McLaurin also suits up. New York has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, though, allowing just 205.3 passing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Stefon Diggs missed Washington's last game due to a hamstring issue. In his absence, Terry McLaurin led the squad in receiving with 62 yards on four catches in the 27-27 tie with the Giants. Treylon Burks and rookie Antonio Williams would likely benefit if Diggs cannot suit up in Week 6 versus the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 199.6 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.8: Stefon Diggs will serve as the No. 1 wideout for the Commanders for the remainder of the season, as Terry McLaurin will miss the rest of the 2026 campaign due to a knee injury. Diggs has scored four times in five games played for Washington, following a return from a hamstring injury of his own. Following the bye, Washington will face division rival Philadelphia in Week 8. The reeling Eagles have been suspect in defending the pass this season.  Philadelphia is giving up 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Stefon Diggs found the end zone again last game for Washington. Diggs snagged three balls for 38 yards and the score in the 27-10 win over the Commanders. Diggs has scored in back-to-back outings, and five times overall in 2026. However, in Week 9, Diggs will face a stellar Rams pass defense. Los Angeles is allowing just 191.9 passing yards per game, which is fourth in the NFL. In addition, the Rams have yielded just 10 passing scores this season, which is tied for eighth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Stefon Diggs had a two-game scoring streak snapped last game for Washington. Diggs caught three passes for 51 yards in the 20-13 loss to the Rams. Diggs will look for a return to the end zone in Week 10 versus the Giants. New York has given up 14 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 20th in the league. However, do not expect much in the way of yardage, as the G-Men are yielding just 177.8 passing yards per tilt, which is third in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Stefon Diggs has scored in three of his last four games played for Washington. Diggs scored the game-winning touchdown last Thursday versus the Giants to bring his season total for receiving touchdowns to six. Diggs also posted a season-high 83 receiving yards for the game. He was targeted 10 times for the game, and should continue to see increased looks in the absence if Terry McLaurin. However, in Week 11, he will be facing a Bengals defense allowing just 216.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the league. In addition, Cincy has yielded just 11 passing scores, which is tied for fifth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: Stefon Diggs finished second on the team in targets last game for Washington. Diggs saw six looks en route to four catches for 45 yards in the thrilling 22-20 win over Cincy. Diggs has at least three catches in every game played this season, though has gone over 50 yards receiving on just three occasions. In Week 12, Diggs will face a lackluster Arizona pass defense. The Cardinals are allowing 226.4 passing yards per tilt, which is 20th in the NFL. In addition, the Cardinals have surrendered the most passing touchdowns in the league to date.

player.seasonOutlook: Diggs signed with the Commanders in August after he was released by the Patriots earlier this offseason. Successful in his return from an ACL tear suffered midway through 2024, the veteran receiver's lone season in New England resulted in 85 catches (ninth among wide receivers) and his seventh career 1,000-yard campaign. Diggs paced the position with an incredible 83% catch rate (second highest all time for a receiver with 100-plus targets) and ranked fourth in yards per route run (2.8). Not used much near the goal line, however, Diggs was limited to four touchdowns and finished 23rd in fantasy PPG. He obviously still has something left in the tank, but is now 32 years old and his usage is trending downward. He has a path to a substantial offense role in Washington and can be viewed as a low-ceiling flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kenneth Gainwell is expected to operate as the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns. Gainwell was thought to be Tampa Bay's top receiving back heading into the season. However, he was overshadowed by Bucky Irving in Week 1, who caught all seven of his targets for 48 yards, while Gainwell was targeted just once. He will likely need more receiving work to be fantasy relevant in a Week 2 matchup against a Browns defense that allowed just two receptions for 22 yards to RBs last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kenneth Gainwell is expected to play as the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Gainwell was thought to be Tampa Bay's top receiving back heading into the season, but he's caught just three of four targets through two games, which is far less than Bucky Irving (11 receptions on 11 targets). Additionally, Gainwell has been relatively inefficient, averaging just 2.9 yards per touch. He's set to face one of the best defenses in the NFL in Minnesota, who have allowed just 3.4 yards per carry this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kenneth Gainwell is likely to remain Tampa Bay's No. 2 running back in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Gainwell has logged just 10 rush attempts for 21 yards through three games this season, confirming he's firmly behind Bucky Irving in the Buccaneers' backfield. The first-year Buccaneer has yet to score a touchdown as well, and he'll likely struggle finding fantasy value without a score. Despite this, Gainwell is in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a Packers defense that's already given up six rushing touchdowns this year.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kenny Gainwell is expected to remain Tampa Bay's No. 2 running back in the Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Gainwell found the end zone for the first time this season during the Week 4 loss to the Packers. However, he remains firmly behind Bucky Irving in the Buccaneers' backfield, as Irving out-touched Gainwell 16 to five. Gainwell will likely struggle maintaining fantasy relevance in Week 5 without scoring another touchdown, though the Cowboys defense has already allowed four rushing TDs this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kenny Gainwell is expected to remain the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. Gainwell has operated as Tampa Bay's top receiving back over the last two weeks, getting more targets (six), receptions (five) and yards (32) than Bucky Irving (two catches on three targets for 10 yards). Despite this, Gainwell will likely struggle finding fantasy relevance without scoring a touchdown. He could thrive against a Pittsburgh defense that's allowed 200 receiving yards to RBs through five contests, tied for the third-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kenny Gainwell is expected to remain the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. Gainwell was given few opportunities in the Week 6 overtime loss to the Steelers, accumulating 24 total yards on just three touches. Additionally, Gainwell was on the field for just 15% of Tampa Bay's offensive plays, his lowest mark of the season. It appears as if Gainwell is trending toward receiving less work as the season progresses, but he's in for a favorable Week 7 matchup against a Panthers defense that's allowed 5.1 yards per carry this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Kenny Gainwell is expected to operate as the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 8 matchup against the Falcons. Gainwell had his most productive outing of the 2026 campaign in the Week 7 win over the Panthers, rushing 14 times for 88 yards. Despite his productive day, Gainwell still tallied 10 fewer carries than Bucky Irving (24 rushes for 106 yards and two touchdowns), suggesting he remains firmly behind Irving in Tampa Bay's backfield. However, Gainwell could remain successful in Week 8 against a Falcons defense that's given up 10 total touchdowns to running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Kenny Gainwell will look to stay hot in the Buccaneers' Week 9 matchup against the Bears. He racked up a career-high 140 rushing yards on 25 carries in the Week 8 win over the Falcons, bringing his season total to 289 yards (5.0 yards per carry). Despite Gainwell's huge performance, he still remains firmly behind Bucky Irving in the Buccaneers' backfield. Gainwell could struggle, especially against a strong Bears defense that has allowed just three rushing touchdowns to RBs all season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Kenny Gainwell is expected to remain Tampa Bay's No. 2 running back in the Week 11 matchup against the Lions. Despite Gainwell playing behind Bucky Irving, he's tallied 304 yards from scrimmage over the Buccaneers' last three games. Additionally, head coach Todd Bowles told reporters Monday that the team will aim to lessen Irving's workload going forward, suggesting Gainwell's role on the offense could expand as the year progresses. However, Gainwell may struggle against the Lions in Week 11, as the Detroit has allowed just 3.7 yards per carry to opposing running backs this year.
outlooksByWeek.12: Kenny Gainwell is expected to operate as Tampa Bay's No. 2 running back during the Week 12 matchup against the Panthers. Despite playing behind Bucky Irving, Gainwell has emerged as one of the top playmakers on this Buccaneers offense. Over the team's last four contests, Gainwell has averaged 90.8 scrimmage yards per game but hasn't found the end zone. He could be a valuable fantasy asset in Week 12, as Tampa Bay is set to face a Carolina defense that's allowed the most fantasy points per game to opposing running backs (28.6) in the NFL this year.

player.seasonOutlook: Gainwell signed with the Buccaneers following a second-half breakout with Pittsburgh last season. After playing sparingly during the first four-and-a-half years of his career, Gainwell averaged 13.3 touches, 85.0 yards and 17.8 fantasy points from Week 8 on last season (eight games). Only five backs scored more points than Gainwell after Week 10. He did most of his damage as a receiver (top six among RBs in targets, catches and receiving yards) and will now look to earn a similar role alongside Bucky Irving in Tampa Bay. Gainwell's strong season suggests he'll have a role, but the 23-year-old Irving is likely to operate as the lead back. Gainwell is best valued as a bench/insurance stash with some flex appeal in deep PPR leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: C.J. Stroud has turned the ball over nine times in Houston's last three games, dating back to the start of last season's playoffs. He'll face a Bengals defense in Week 2 that just forced three turnovers from Buccaneers QB Baker Mayfield. Stroud threw for 274 yards and two TDs in Week 1 against the Bills but fumbled away Houston's chance to win the game in the final minute. The Texans' vaunted defense faces another tough test against Joe Burrow and the Bengals, so Stroud and the offense will be relied upon to keep pace. Stroud is a viable fantasy option in superflex or two-QB formats but ranks outside the starting range in single-QB leagues.
outlooksByWeek.3: C.J. Stroud threw for 353 yards but led the Texans to just six points in the absence of top WR Nico Collins (hamstring) during Week 2's loss to the Bengals. If Houston remains without Collins in Week 3 against the Colts, Stroud will likely lean heavily on TE Dalton Schultz once more against a Colts defense that allowed 41 points to the Ravens and then 33 to the Chiefs. Considering the Colts have surrendered the most points and yards in the NFL, Stroud is worth a look in superflex or multi-QB lineups, but he will likely remain ranked outside the starting range in single-QB formats, at least until Collins returns.
outlooksByWeek.4: C.J. Stroud has missed top WR Nico Collins (hamstring) over Houston's past two games, failing to throw a touchdown pass in Week 2 and producing just 167 passing yards in Week 3. The Texans fell to 0-3 heading into a Week 4 home game against the Cowboys. On the bright side, the Texans rebounded from an 0-3 start last season to finish 12-5, and Collins has a realistic chance to return versus Dallas. If Stroud gets his top target back, the slumping QB would have a nice opportunity to get on track as a strong superflex or second fantasy QB against a weak Cowboys secondary that has allowed a 7:0 TD:INT through three games in 2026 after giving up the most QB production in the league last season. Should Collins sit again, Stroud would be a risky choice in all formats despite the favorable matchup.
outlooksByWeek.5: C.J. Stroud has some streaming appeal in single-QB formats for Week 5, when the Texans travel to Tennessee for a battle between 0-4 AFC South squads. He has thrown for at least 347 yards in two of Houston's four losses and has a 5:0 TD:INT. The Titans have been respectable against the pass, with only four touchdowns allowed through the air this season, but other teams were able to build leads and run effectively on Tennessee. The Texans are unlikely to find as much success on the ground, considering RBs David Montgomery and Woody Marks have combined to average 2.9 yards per carry this season. Stroud has been asked to throw the ball 38 times per game, and he's likely to remain busy in Week 5. The Texans got top WR Nico Collins (hamstring) back from a two-game absence in Week 4, and Collins contributed immediately in his return by catching both of Stroud's touchdown passes in a 34-30 loss to the Cowboys.
outlooksByWeek.6: C.J. Stroud could have a key new target for Houston's pivotal Week 6 clash with the AFC South-leading Jaguars in London. The Texans are just 1-4 and have already fallen three games behind Jacksonville in the standings, but Stroud is quietly averaging a career-high 280 passing yards per game to go with a 6:0 TD:INT. Jacksonville gives up the fewest rushing yards and second-most passing yards per game, so Stroud will likely be asked to carry Houston's offense again in Week 6, making him a viable starting QB in fantasy. The Texans notched their first win of the season in Week 5 over the Titans and promptly traded for disgruntled Cardinals WR Marvin Harrison, who hasn't lived up to the hype as the fourth overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft but excelled at Ohio State while catching passes from Stroud in 2022. Harrison likely won't be fully up to speed, but he could still provide an upgrade over Houston's current wideouts behind Nico Collins.
outlooksByWeek.7: C.J. Stroud is averaging a career-high 286 passing yards per game and has posted a 9:1 TD:INT heading into Houston's Week 7 home game against the Giants. He threw a season-high three touchdown passes in the Week 6 win over Jacksonville while topping 300 yards for the third time in six starts. The Giants have surrendered 12 passing TDs, which is sixth-most in the NFL, and their three rushing scores allowed to QBs are tied for the most in the league, though they have also notched six interceptions. Stroud has consistently been asked to put the Texans' offense on his back due to the team's weak running game, and he has mostly been up to the challenge, so he remains a fringe fantasy starter for Week 7.
outlooksByWeek.9: C.J. Stroud posted an 11:1 TD:INT ratio in seven games prior to Houston's Week 8 bye, but the Texans are just 2-5 heading into a Week 9 road game against the 0-7 Chargers. Pass defense hasn't been the Chargers' problem, as they're allowing the seventh-fewest yards per game through the air and have limited QBs to an 8:6 TD:INT ratio. Stroud has often been asked to carry Houston's offense with the team's two main RBs both averaging no more than 3.5 yards per rushing attempt, but the Texans may rely more on their defense and running game in Week 9 to exploit the Chargers' weaknesses. Stroud is a viable fantasy option in deeper formats, but he has a low Week 9 floor based on the matchup.
outlooksByWeek.10: C.J. Stroud is coming off a 384-yard, five-TD masterpiece in Houston's Week 9 win over the Chargers and has thrown 10 touchdown passes over the past three games. He has showcased an elite ceiling with four games north of 300 passing yards this season, so the surging Stroud is a start-worthy Week 10 option, even in a road game against a Browns defense that ranks among the 10 stingiest units against the pass. The Ohio State product is no stranger to playing in the Buckeye State this time of year, though it's worth noting that the Browns are 3-0 at home while allowing just 17.3 points per game at Huntington Bank Field compared to 24.0 points per game in six games elsewhere.
outlooksByWeek.11: C.J. Stroud tossed three more touchdown passes in Houston's Week 10 loss to the Browns, bringing his TD:INT ratio to 19:3 through nine games, with 13 of those scores coming in his last four outings. The fourth-year QB's brilliance has largely been wasted on the 3-6 Texans, as the defense and running game have both declined from last season. Houston's playoff hopes aren't extinguished yet, but Stroud can't afford a Week 11 letdown in a home rematch against a Colts defense that held him to 167 yards and one TD in Week 3, when the Texans lost 19-17 at Indianapolis. The 3-7 Colts have allowed a 16:2 TD:INT ratio, so Stroud is worth starting in this Week 11 rematch Thursday despite his poor performance in the first meeting between these AFC South rivals.
outlooksByWeek.12: C.J. Stroud has thrown 16 touchdown passes in his last five games as he tries to carry the Texans and keep their playoff hopes alive. The surging QB is a top-10 fantasy option at his position in Week 12 against a reeling Ravens defense that has allowed at least 33 points in four of the past five games. Baltimore is on a six-game losing streak, which makes this game close to a must-win for the 4-6 Texans, who trail the Browns and Steelers by two games apiece and the Patriots by one game in the battle for the last two AFC wild-card spots. Houston has gotten subpar efficiency from its RBs, who are averaging a collective 3.6 yards per carry, so Stroud has routinely been asked to carry the offense. He has mostly been up to the task, ranking sixth in the league with 266 passing yards per game and tied for fourth with 22 touchdown passes.

player.seasonOutlook: Stroud enters his fourth NFL season yet to emerge as a quality fantasy option and having seen his passing production dip during each season of his career. Stroud impressed as a rookie with 24 passing TDs, three rushing TDs and a ninth-place finish in fantasy points per game (18.4). During the past two seasons, he failed to clear 20 passing touchdowns, has a total of one rushing TD and averaged 13.8 points, ranking outside the top 20 both years. Stroud's efficiency has been solid at best and thanks in part to Houston's elite defense, he hasn't needed to throw the ball (or scramble) very often. There's little reason to expect much change in 2026, so even with a good, deep group of pass catchers, the 24-year-old is best viewed as a low-upside, fringe QB2 in 12-team leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jalen Coker (ankle) will look to continue shining in Carolina's Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. Coker has shown out in the Panthers last two games (including their wild-card loss to end last season), having recorded a combined 17 receptions for 272 yards and three touchdowns. He's outproduced 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year Tetairoa McMillan and looks to be a major part of Carolina's offense going forward. However, Coker is dealing with an ankle issue and could struggle against a tough Falcons defense that gave up just 5.0 yards per pass attempt in Week 1, the fourth-best mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jalen Coker is expected to remain one of Bryce Young's favorite targets in Carolina's Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Coker has been incredibly productive, leading the Panthers in receptions (16) and yards (204) while being tied for first in targets (18) through two weeks. Across his last three games (including playoffs), the third-year pro has caught 25 of 30 targets for 338 yards and two touchdowns, emerging as one of the NFL's top young wideouts. He's in for a very favorable matchup in Week 3 as well, as the Browns' defense has surrendered 7.2 yards per pass attempt this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jalen Coker (quadriceps) is expected to operate as one of the Panthers' top targets if active for the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Coker has dealt with three separate injuries through three weeks this season (ankle, hamstring and quadriceps). Despite this, the third-year wideout has amassed 222 receiving yards and two touchdowns on 18 catches, leading the Panthers in yards and touchdowns. If Coker is able to suit up in Week 4, he's in for an incredibly favorable matchup, as Detroit's defense has allowed a whopping 31.7 points and 39.0 PPR fantasy points per game to the WR position this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jalen Coker (quadriceps) is expected to return for the Panthers' Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. Coker was on a tear to start the season, catching 16 of 18 targets for 204 yards and two touchdowns in Carolina's first two games. He's expected to continue benefitting from the new, aggressive Panthers offense, led by Bryce Young, who's averaging 40.5 passing attempts per game this year. Coker will likely find success if active in Week 6 against an Eagles defense that's given up seven touchdowns to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jalen Coker is expected to remain one of Bryce Young's top targets in the Panthers' Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers. In Coker's three full games this season, he's caught 22 of 31 targets for 301 yards and two touchdowns. With Young averaging 40.2 passing attempts per game, it appears as if Coker will continue to produce at a high level going forward. Additionally, he's in for a favorable Week 7 matchup against a Tampa Bay secondary that's allowed five touchdowns to wideouts through six games this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jalen Coker (shoulder) is expected to remain one of Bryce Young's top targets if active for Carolina's Week 8 matchup against the Packers. Coker underwhelmed in the Week 7 loss to the Buccaneers, catching just one of four targets for nine yards, his least productive game since Week 7 of 2025. Coker has been one of the league's best wideouts when healthy this season, averaging 5.8 receptions and 77.5 yards per game in his four full games in 2026. If active for Week 8, he could have plenty of scoring opportunities against a Packers secondary that's allowed 35.4 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jalen Coker is expected to remain one of Carolina's top receivers in the Week 9 matchup against the Broncos. Coker has been relatively quiet since returning from injury in the Week 6 win over the Eagles, catching just nine of 22 targets for 142 yards and a touchdown over his last three contests. Despite this, Coker ranks second on the Panthers in targets (7.3), receptions (4.5) and receiving yards per game (60.7) this season, suggesting more production could be in the near future. Coker could struggle in Week 9, however, as Denver's secondary has allowed just 6.8 yards per target to opposing wideouts this year.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jalen Coker is expected to remain one of the Panthers' top receiving options in the Week 10 matchup against the Saints. Coker has cooled down along with the majority of Carolina's offense over the last three weeks, catching just seven of 14 targets for 74 yards and a touchdown during that span. Despite this, Bryce Young is still tied for the most pass attempts per game in the NFL (38.5), which bodes well for Coker's fantasy outlook going forward. Coker could take advantage of a New Orleans secondary that's given up 11.1 yards per completion this year.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jalen Coker will look to bounce back from a poor performance in the Panthers' Week 11 matchup against the Ravens. After catching 16 of 18 targets for 204 yards and two touchdowns across Carolina's first two games this season, Coker has managed just 15 receptions on 35 targets for 189 yards and one touchdown over his last six contests. He remains second on the team in receptions (31), targets (53) and receiving yards (393) but likely can't be trusted after four consecutive performances of less than 10.0 fantasy points. However, Coker is in for a favorable Week 11 matchup against a Baltimore secondary that's allowed 9.2 yards per target to opposing wideouts through nine contests this year.
outlooksByWeek.12: Jalen Coker (concussion) is expected to remain one of Carolina's top weapons if active for the Week 12 matchup against the Buccaneers. Coker entered concussion protocol following a four-catch, 47 yard performance in a win over the Ravens in Week 11, putting his availability for Monday night's contest in jeopardy. He's been relatively underwhelming over his last five games, catching 11 of 25 targets for 121 yards and one touchdown. If active, Coker will likely struggle against an impressive Tampa Bay secondary that's given up just 7.6 yards per target to opposing wideouts this season.

player.seasonOutlook: After missing nearly the entire first half of 2025, Coker passed Xavier Legette and took on a larger offensive role opposite Tetairoa McMillan. From Week 8 onward (11 games, including the playoffs), Coker played 73% of the snaps and handled a 17.8% target share. The fantasy output was inconsistent (below 11.5 points in seven games), but he peaked down the stretch (more than 14 points in four of his final six, including a 9-134-1 showing against the Rams in the playoffs). Coker's strong finish is encouraging, though his rookie season went similarly (14-plus points three times, but under 11 in the other nine games). A healthy 2026 could get Coker to the next level, but flex production is his likely ceiling as long as McMillan is commanding one-quarter (if not more) of the targets in Carolina's Bryce Young-led offense.

outlooksByWeek.2: Geno Smith may be called upon more often in Week 2 when the Jets face the Packers. He wasn't asked to do much last week as the club played with a rare lead for the majority of the game, relying on the run-something unlikely to repeat in Week 2. Green Bay's secondary is vulnerable, allowing three touchdowns to Carson Wentz to start the year. With more volume, Smith can ascend to the second tier of quarterbacks in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Geno Smith will look to be the next quarterback to take advantage of the Lions' secondary when the Jets head to Detroit in Week 3. Smith hasn't topped 250 yards through two games and has just one touchdown pass, but he is in a very favorable spot in Week 3, with Detroit having allowed three touchdown passes in each outing thus far. Smith threw 41 times in Week 2, and so long as the Lions are scoring, Smith will likely have high volume again, putting him in a position to have his best showing of the year.
outlooksByWeek.4: Geno Smith is facing an uphill battle if he hopes to match his Week 3 success when the Jets face the Bears in Week 4. Smith is coming off a sterling outing where he threw for 321 yards and three touchdowns, completing 84% of his passes against the Lions. While the Bears' secondary is vulnerable in individual matchups, their overall body of work has been stout. Chicago hasn't allowed more than 153 yards over the last two weeks, with no touchdowns and three interceptions. Despite Breece Hall's likely absence, the Bears are more suspect against the run, potentially setting Smith up for a game-management approach.
outlooksByWeek.5: Geno Smith hopes for more opportunities in the Jets' Week 5 game against a vulnerable Browns secondary. After completing 31 passes in Week 3, Smith went just 8-for-15 in Week 4 against the Bears. Despite the lack of volume, he has a 5:0 TD:INT ratio and a 7.7 yards-per-attempt average, his highest mark since playing just two games in 2016. Cleveland has allowed nine touchdown passes in four games and at least 291 yards in each of the last two weeks, putting Smith in a spot to exceed his season norms.
outlooksByWeek.6: Geno Smith faces an uphill battle for fantasy success when the Jets face the Patriots in Week 6. Smith has been held to 182 yards or fewer in consecutive weeks and has multiple touchdown passes just once through five games. While the Patriots' secondary is banged up, they've still allowed just a 6:3 TD:INT ratio through five games while holding three quarterbacks to no more than 187 yards. The Jets hope to remain run-first, limiting Smith's opportunities.
outlooksByWeek.7: Geno Smith will look to buck his seasonal trends in an inviting Week 7 matchup when the Jets face the Dolphins. Smith has opened the year with one or zero touchdown passes in five of his six games, but Miami's defense has allowed 11 touchdown throws in five contests. Smith likely needs those timely scoring plays as Miami is allowing just 226 passing yards per game, with teams preferring to exploit its run defense, setting him up as a risky bye-week replacement option.
outlooksByWeek.8: Geno Smith is poised to build on one of his best outings of the year when the Jets host the Raiders in Week 8. He threw for three touchdowns in Week 7 against Miami, his second game in seven outings at that mark, while the other five have produced just one touchdown or none. Las Vegas has allowed multiple touchdowns in five straight games and 16 scores overall, the second-highest total across the league. Smith needs to find paydirt to be a viable option, as the Raiders have surrendered more than 255 passing yards just once.
outlooksByWeek.9: Geno Smith faces an uphill battle to continue his current form when the Jets face the Chiefs in Week 9. Smith has thrown for multiple touchdowns and at least 287 yards in consecutive weeks after tossing only one or no touchdowns in five of his first six outings. Kansas City has allowed only seven touchdown passes, with only two opposing quarterbacks topping 222 yards against them, suggesting fantasy managers are better off looking for streaming options elsewhere.
outlooksByWeek.10: Geno Smith will look to bounce back in Week 10 when the Jets face the Bills. After averaging 288.5 passing yards over two promising showings, Smith managed just 165 yards in Week 9, failing to throw a touchdown for the second time this season. Buffalo's defense is middling in terms of fantasy points allowed to opposing quarterbacks, but they've given up 15 touchdown passes through eight games, and the game flow will likely force the Jets to throw frequently while trailing. Smith has thrown multiple touchdowns in just three games, but there is some streaming appeal given a favorable Week 10 matchup.
outlooksByWeek.11: Geno Smith will need to overcome an ankle injury if he's to help the Jets take down the Chargers in Week 11. Smith was in and out of the lineup in Week 10, his first time ceding snaps under center all season, resulting in his second straight game without a touchdown pass. Smith now has one or zero scores in seven of his 10 outings. While the Chargers have allowed at least 340 passing yards in consecutive games, they've also surrendered multiple touchdown passes just three times in nine games, not setting Smith up for high-end production in Week 11. Cade Klubnik will start if Smith isn't deemed fit.
outlooksByWeek.12: Geno Smith brings low-volume but surging efficiency into the Jets' Week 12 matchup with the Dolphins. While he hasn't topped 176 passing yards in three straight games and has failed to complete more than 18 attempts, Smith is coming off his third three-touchdown pass outing in Week 11. With the Jets preferring a run-first approach paired with an unhealthy receiving corps, Smith is not a fantasy option against a mid-tier secondary that's allowing 7.7 yards per attempt.

player.seasonOutlook: Smith was traded to the Jets following an unsuccessful one-year stint in Las Vegas. Smith, who began his career as a second-round pick with the Jets in 2013, is in line to start, though he's a long shot for consistent fantasy production. Smith peaked with a ninth-place finish in fantasy points per game with Seattle in 2022, but he has finished no better than 16th over the past three seasons. He paced the NFL in both interceptions and sacks in 2025 after finishing third in both categories in 2024 and is no longer much of a factor with his legs. The 35-year-old might bring some stability to the fantasy outlook of the team's pass catchers, but we shouldn't expect much more than that. Consider Smith only in superflex formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jake Bates will aim to stay perfect as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. Bates nailed his only field-goal attempt and all four extra points against the Saints in Week 1. The third-year player led all NFL kickers in PATs last season in Detroit's high-powered offense, so he'll hopefully stay on the field plenty in the coming weeks. Given that the Bills' defense should provide more problems for the Lions, Bates could also get more field-goal shots in what could be a tough away matchup.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jake Bates will seek to stay perfect as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3. Bates has now drilled both of his two field-goal attempts and all eight of his PATs this season. The third-year kicker hasn't been on the field for many field goals this season, and Detroit playing from behind doesn't help his case. Luckily, the team's current high volume of touchdowns has kept Bates relevant. He'll face a New York squad that's allowed 6.0 points per game to kickers across two games, a top-10 mark.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jake Bates will look to stay perfect as the Lions play the Panthers in Week 4. Bates nailed his sole extra-point attempt and all four of his XPAs in Week 3 against the Jets. The third-year boot has now converted all three of his field-goal kicks and each of his 12 extra-point tries. While the field-goal volume isn't quite there, Detroit's ability to score keeps Bates on the field and scoring. Carolina has allowed a middle-of-the-pack 7.0 points per game to kickers this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jake Bates will aim to stay perfect as the Lions play the Cardinals in Week 5. Bates logged his best game of the season in Week 4 against the Panthers, nailing all four of his field-goal attempts and converting two XPAs. The second-year kicker has now gone a perfect 21-for-21 on boots (seven field goals, 14 extra points) this season. He'll face an Arizona defense that's ranked top 10 against fantasy kickers.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jake Bates will look to stay hot as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. Bates has yet to miss a kick this season, nailing eight field-goal attempts and converting all 20 of his XPAs across five games. While the field-goal usage hasn't quite been there, the touchdown-scoring ability of Detroit's offense has kept Bates on the field. He'll face a Green Bay squad that's allowed the fewest fantasy points per game (4.2) to kickers this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jake Bates will aim to stay perfect as the Lions play the Vikings in Week 8. Bates nailed both of his two extra-point tries and two field-goal attempts including a game winner in Week 7 against the Packers. The third-year kicker has yet to miss a kick this season, making 10 field goals and 22 XPAs. He'll face a Minnesota team that's ranked fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to kickers (5.3).
outlooksByWeek.9: Jake Bates will look to stay solid as the Lions play the Dolphins in Week 9. Bates missed his first kick of the season in a Week 8 win over Minnesota, but he still converted two of three field goals and nailed his sole XPA. The second-year kicker has now gone 12-for-13 on field goal attempts and made all 23 of his extra-point tries across seven outings. The Dolphins have ranked in the middle against fantasy kickers this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jake Bates will look to benefit from high volume again as the Lions play the Patriots in Week 10. Bates was perfect in a Week 9 win over Miami, nailing five total kicks which included four field goals. The third-year boot has now made multiple field goals for the third straight game, with Detroit's offense cooling down slightly after a crazy start to the year. New England has ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy kickers so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jake Bates will look to stay reliable as the Lions play the Buccaneers in Week 11. Bates didn't attempt a field goal in a Week 10 win over the Patriots, but 5 XPAs kept his performance solid. The starting boot has now converted 16 of 17 field-goal attempts and made all 29 of his extra-point tries across nine games this campaign. He'll face a Tampa defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy kickers.
outlooksByWeek.12: Jake Bates will look to tighten up as the Lions play the Bears in Week 12. Bates was mostly solid in a Week 11 win over the Buccaneers, but he did miss a 53-yard field goal in the first quarter. Either way, the third-year boot has now converted 17 of 19 field-goal attempts and nailed all 33 of his XPAs across 10 games this season. He'll face a Chicago defense that's a tough second in fantasy points allowed to kickers this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Hill is currently a free agent after being released by Miami. One of the top fantasy players of the past decade, Hill's best days may be behind him as he enters his age-32 campaign. The former fifth-round pick was fantasy's top-scoring receiver from 2017-23, but struggled to an 18th-place finish in 2024 (31st PPG) and then suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 4 of last season. If he's able to play in 2026, Hill may still be able to hit for the occasional explosive play, but considering his age and the major injury, his ceiling is likely that of a boom/bust flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Deebo Samuel will look to build upon a strong season-opening performance when the 49ers face Miami in Week 2. In Samuel's return to San Francisco following a one-year hiatus, he caught six of seven targets for 48 yards and a touchdown in last Thursday's win over the Rams. Samuel and Mike Evans finished with nearly identical receiving lines, suggesting that both veteran wideouts can thrive with QB Brock Purdy. The Dolphins were beat handily by the Raiders in Week 1 while giving up three TDs through the air (though two were to RB Ashton Jeanty).
outlooksByWeek.3: Deebo Samuel is coming off a quiet game heading into San Francisco's Week 3 matchup against the Cardinals. Samuel caught three passes for 31 yards and rushed once for four yards in Sunday's rout of Miami. However, fellow wideouts Demarcus Robinson (ankle) and Mike Evans (hip) both exited that contest due to injury, and though early reports suggest Evans should be fine for Week 3, Samuel could see more looks come his way given his comparatively good health. Arizona has given up the sixth-most fantasy points per game to wideouts so far this year and was just torched by Seattle's Jaxon Smith-Njigba (9-155-3 receiving line) on Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.4: Deebo Samuel could take on the 49ers' No. 1 WR role in Week 4 against Denver if Mike Evans (ribs/oblique) is unable to play. Though Evans left in the second quarter in this past Sunday's win over Arizona, Samuel ended the contest without seeing a target. However, he still had a good fantasy line thanks to an 80-yard TD on a hook-and-ladder play, and Samuel also gained 14 yards on two carries. Should Evans be unable to suit up against Denver, Samuel could face the daunting task of trying to beat star cornerback Patrick Surtain.
outlooksByWeek.5: Deebo Samuel has been a versatile cog for the 49ers heading into a Week 5 matchup against Seattle. Samuel has scored three receiving TDs though four games, and he's also racked up 185 receiving yards, 74 rushing yads and 231 kick-return yards. The veteran wideout has drawn a modest 17 targets so far, but he's been very efficient in hauling in 14 of them. San Francisco may look to use Samuel creatively against a Seahawks defense that is allowing just 246.8 yards per game this season, fewest in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Deebo Samuel is dealing with a hamstring injury and may not be able to play in San Francisco's Week 6 matchup against Washington. Samuel was hurt in the third quarter of this past Sunday's win over Seattle and was quickly ruled out. The veteran receiver is slated for imaging, which should provide clarity about the extent of the injury and a potential return timeline. If Samuel can't play in Week 6, he'll miss the opportunity to feast on a Commanders defense that has struggled mightily against the pass this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Deebo Samuel and the 49ers travel to face the Falcons in Week 7. The veteran receiver missed San Francisco's 23-17 victory in Week 6 with a hamstring injury he suffered in Week 5.
