Head coach Kyle Shanahan stated they would "hold off" on placing him on injured reserve with the Week 8 bye approaching, so it sounds like Samuel is in jeopardy of missing the road tilt against Atlanta. Expect him to work towards a Week 9 return, as long as he doesn't suffer any sort of setback.
outlooksByWeek.9: Deebo Samuel has a chance to return from a two-game absence for San Francisco's Week 9 tilt against Las Vegas. Samuel hurt his hamstring in Week 5 against Seattle and hasn't played since, but the 49ers' Week 8 bye allowed him time for extra rest. Mike Evans (Achilles) and Demarcus Robinson (ankle) also have a chance to return to San Francisco's wideout corps following absences of their own, so the team's passing game could be getting a big boost. The outlook is positive for all of the 49ers' wide receivers given that the Raiders have allowed 10 receiving touchdowns to the position this year, tied for third-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) will look to return from a four-game absence when San Francisco travels to Dallas in Week 10. Samuel hasn't been placed on IR, and the expectation is that he'll return before the end of the season, but his status for this week is hazy, at best. With No. 1 wideout Mike Evans (Achilles) missing the past two games, the 49ers acquired Keenan Allen at the trade deadline to provide additional depth. If Samuel is able to get back on the field against the Cowboys, he could find success against a defense that has given up 159.3 receiving yards per game to wideouts, ninth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Deebo Samuel will look to build on his best performance of the season when the 49ers  host the Vikings in Week 11. Samuel compiled 109 total yards and two touchdowns this past Sunday in a win over Dallas, with most of that yardage coming on a 70-yard rushing score. It was Samuel's first game if five weeks, as he had been sidelined due to a hamstring injury. His versatility could come in handy against a Vikings defense that is tied for the third-fewest receiving TDs (five) allowed to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Deebo Samuel continues to be a Swiss Army knife for San Francisco heading into a Week 12 tilt against the Seahawks. In this past Sunday's win over the Vikings, Samuel recorded two carries for 27 yards, caught three of four targets for 20 yards and returned two kickoffs for 57 yards. While that might not add up to substantial fantasy production, Samuel's skill set could be invaluable for the 49ers against a tough defense like the Seahawks'. Seattle has given up the fewest yards per target (5.89) to wideouts this season, so San Francisco may look to be creative in order to push the ball downfield.

player.seasonOutlook: Samuel reunited with the 49ers in July after solid yet unspectacular lone season in Washington. The former second-round pick cleared 85 touches and 800 scrimmage yards for the fifth consecutive season and finished 25th among receivers in fantasy points -- his third-career top-30 fantasy campaign. Samuel's role as a short-area target and occasional rusher gets the ball in his hands plenty (he's ranked in the top 15 among WRs in touches and RAC five years in a row), but it doesn't allow him much scoring upside (10 TDs over the last two years, and he's never cleared five end zone targets in one season). Now 30 years old, Samuel figures to resume his role as a short-area playmaker in Kyle Shanahan's highly-efficient offense. He's a fine late-round flier with WR3/flex upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Alvin Kamara (knee) is expected to serve as one of the Saints' top running backs if active for the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Kamara was sidelined for Week 1 but is expected to return for Week 2, likely operating as the Saints' top receiving back. He could take work away from Travis Etienne, who caught seven of eight targets in last week's overtime loss. Tyler Shough attempted 56 passes in Week 1, which bodes well for Kamara's potential upside as a receiver. He's in for a solid Week 2 matchup as well, with the Ravens defense giving up 5.3 yards per touch to RBs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Alvin Kamara is expected to operate as the Saints' top pass-catching back in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. In his return from a sprained MCL in the Week 2 win over the Ravens, Kamara led the Saints' backfield in carries (nine), targets (six) and receptions (five). Despite this, Travis Etienne was more efficient with his opportunities, averaging 3.1 yards per carry compared to Kamara's 1.7. Even so, the Saints' backfield is in for a tough Week 3 matchup against a Las Vegas defense that's allowed just 3.8 yards per carry thus far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Alvin Kamara will likely be in for a larger offensive role with Travis Etienne (hamstring)  sidelined for New Orleans' Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. Kamara has received nine carries in each of the last two weeks after sitting out Week 1, but he's struggled with efficiency, averaging just 2.8 yards per carry. Additionally, he saw just one target in the Week 3 loss to the Raiders, suggesting he may not have the same receiving volume as in past years. Regardless, this receiving volume should increase with Etienne out for Week 4. Kamara could still struggle against a Falcons defense that's given up 13.5 PPR fantasy points per game to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Alvin Kamara is expected to remain the Saints' top running back while Travis Etienne (hamstring) is sidelined during the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. In his first game without Etienne this season, Kamara totaled 58 yards on 12 touches, but his workload was largely impacted by the game script. He led New Orleans' backfield in targets (seven), which is a positive sign for his fantasy outlook going forward. Even so, Kamara is in for a tough Week 5 matchup against a Minnesota defense that's allowed just 14.7 fantasy points per game to running backs this season, the fewest in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Alvin Kamara is expected to remain one of the Saints' top running backs in the Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Despite operating as New Orleans' No. 1 RB over the last two weeks, Kamara logged fewer snaps (12) and carries (three) than Kendre Miller (six carries on 13 snaps) in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings. Additionally, he got fewer targets than Miller (two to three), which is a very negative sign for his outlook going forward. Even so, Kamara could be productive against a Giants defense that's given up just 94 receiving yards but two receiving touchdowns to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Alvin Kamara is expected to remain one of the Saints' top running backs in the Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. Kamara had his best game of the 2026 campaign in a Week 6 win over the Giants, accounting for 69 yards and a touchdown on nine touches. Despite this, he logged just 18 offensive snaps, which is fewer both than Kendre Miller (31) and CJ Donaldson (22). Kamara dealt with an injury in the first half, but with Miller receiving 20 carries, it appears as if Kamara's upside is limited, operating primarily as a receiver out of the backfield. Additionally, he's in for a tough Week 7 matchup against a Steelers defense that's given up just 20.8 fantasy points per game to opposing RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Alvin Kamara is expected to remain the Saints' top pass-catching running back in the Week 9 matchup against the Browns. Kamara has received seven targets in two of New Orleans' last four games, proving his value to the team's passing attack. While not the most effective rusher at this stage in his career, Kamara has averaged 43 total yards on 10.5 touches per game through six contests this season. He could struggle against a tough Browns defense that's allowed just 28 total receptions to running backs through eight games this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Kamara is expected to remain the Saints' top pass-catching running back in the Week 10 matchup against the Panthers. Kamara received fewer than 10 touches for the third time in New Orleans' last four games during the Week 9 win over the Browns, despite backfield mate Kendre Miller being release prior to the contest. Regardless, Kamara ranks first amongst Saints RBs in targets (31), receptions (25), receiving yards (150) and receiving touchdowns (one) in seven appearances this year. He could find success against a Panthers defense that's allowed 230 yards and a touchdown through the air to opposing running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Alvin Kamara will remain one of the Saints' top running backs in the Week 11 matchup against the Bears. Kamara was limited to just five touches while Travis Etienne returned from injury in the Week 10 loss to the Panthers. However, Kamara scored two touchdowns on those touches and appeared to be operating as New Orleans' top red-zone RB. With Kamara, Etienne and Audric Estime all playing roles in the Saints' backfield, it may be hard to trust any of them going forward. Kamara could take advantage of a Chicago defense that's allowed 7.3 yards per target and two receiving touchdowns to opposing RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Alvin Kamara will likely play a minimal offensive role during the Saints' Week 12 matchup against the Bengals. Despite finding the end zone during the Week 11 loss to the Saints, Kamara played just eight offensive snaps while Travis Etienne and CJ Donaldson each played 32. Additionally, Kamara has received just seven touches over the Saints' last two games, suggesting his role in the offense has diminished. Expect Kamara to have minimal value in Week 12 against a Bengals defense that's given up just 294 receiving yards to RBs through nine games this year.

player.seasonOutlook: Kamara is entering his age-31 season set to play a change-of-pace role behind Travis Etienne and is unlikely to be a fantasy option. Over the past seven seasons, only two backs age 31 or older have posted a top-30 fantasy campaign, and both required 16-plus touchdowns. (Kamara hasn't cleared nine TDs since 2020 and scored once in 2025). Injuries limited Kamara to career-low marks across the board last season (including a 10% target share, considerably worse than his previous career low of 18%), and he hasn't played a full season since his rookie year (2017). A longtime fantasy star, Kamara is worth no more than a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals are on the road in Week 2 to take on Houston. The Texans have the 27th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (19.7) to TEs, and they are last in receiving yards allowed to the position after Dalton Kincaid and Dawson Knox combined for 137 yards last week. Gesicki led the Bengals in catches (5), targets (7), and receiving yards (78) in Week 1, to go along with one TD. He could be primed for another big performance in what may very well be another high-scoring affair.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals are in Pittsburgh for an AFC North showdown in Week 3. After leading Cincinnati in receptions, yards, and targets in the season opener, Gesicki failed to record a single target versus the Texans in Week 2. Some of that could be chalked up to game flow with the Bengals ahead for most of the game, but it's nonetheless worrisome. The Steelers rank second in fantasy points allowed per game (5.5) and are first in receptions allowed to TEs through two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals welcome the 2-1 Jaguars to town in Week 4. He caught all three of his targets for 37 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's 30-27 loss in Week 3. Gesicki finished third in receiving yards while catching his second TD of the young season, just one week after failing to earn a target. Jacksonville's defense ranks fifth in fantasy points allowed (7.8) and second in receptions (8) to TEs, so he could be in for another quiet day.
outlooksByWeek.5: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals travel to take on the winless Dolphins in Week 5. He grabbed three of five targets for 40 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's Week 4 loss. Gesicki now has two straight outings with a TD and recorded his third overall, and he could be in line for an uptick in opportunities in a favorable matchup versus a Miami defense that allows 18.6 fantasy points to TEs, which is tied for 28th. Ja'Marr Chase (concussion), Tee Higgins (adductor), and Colbie Young (knee) are all questionable, potentially leaving Gesicki as one of Joe Burrow's primary receivers against a Dolphins unit that just gave up 13 receptions and 119 yards to T.J. Hockenson
outlooksByWeek.7: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals are in Baltimore for an AFC North clash in Week 7. He caught one of two targets for a four-yard touchdown during Cincinnati's 31-24 win in Week 5. Fellow tight end Erick All Jr. notched a 3-25-0 line on three targets, finishing second on the team in yardage. Gesicki is hard to trust with Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) healthy, especially versus a Baltimore defense tied for seventh in fantasy points allowed per game (10.5) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals host the 1-6 Titans in Week 8. He caught his only target for a six-yard touchdown during Cincinnati's 35-13 victory over Baltimore. Gesicki extended his TD streak to four consecutive games, as he's now compiled a 13-165-5 receiving line on 18 targets in 2026. He'll try to make it five in a row versus Tennessee's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per contest (11.1) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals are in Spain for a Week 9 interconference tilt against the Falcons. He caught four of six targets for 76 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's 43-36 overtime win in Week 8. The 76 receiving yards were Gesicki's most in a game since he went for 78 in the season opener, and the 31-year-old was able to extend his streak of outings with a TD catch to five. He now owns a 17-241-6 line on 24 targets through seven contests and will try to make it six straight with a score versus an Atlanta defense allowing 14.4 fantasy points per game (T-20th) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals host the Steelers for an AFC North clash in Week 10. He corralled both of his targets for 11 yards during Cincinnati's 34-17 victory in Week 9. Gesicki's five-game streak with a touchdown came to an end with all three of Joe Burrow's TD passes going to Ja'Marr Chase (one) and Tee Higgins (two). Gesicki's fantasy value has been reliant on TDs in 2026, so he'll try to start another streak of consecutive trips to the endzone versus a Pittsburgh defense his initial scoring stretch started against back in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.11: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals are in Washington for a Week 11 tilt on Monday Night Football. He caught one of two targets for nine yards during Cincinnati's Week 10 victory, unable to capitalize on Joe Burrow throwing for 409 yards and four TDs. Gesicki now sports a 3-20-0 receiving line on four targets over his last two outings after catching a touchdown in each of his five previous games. He does, however, get a favorable matchup versus a Commanders defense allowing 20.2 fantasy points per game (31st) to opposing TEs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals look to extend their three-game win streak at home versus the Saints in Week 12. He caught five of six targets for a team-high 77 yards during Cincinnati's Week 11 loss. Gesicki finished third on the team in targets and matched Ja'Marr Chase and Chase Brown for the team lead in receptions. The outing was impressive considering Joe Burrow attempted 40 passes and threw for 300 yards, with Ja'Marr Chase (5-31-0) and Tee Higgins (2-43-1) combining for only 74 of them. Gesicki will attempt to punish a New Orleans defense allowing the seventh-most fantasy points per game (15.7) to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: There was an era when Gesicki was a viable starting option in fantasy, but that time has come and gone. Since posting back-to-back top-eight fantasy campaigns in 2020 and 2021, Gesicki has finished 23rd, 37th, 13th and 41st the past four seasons. The latter came during a 2025 campaign in which he was limited to 41 targets in 13 games. Gesicki is no more than a situational seam stretcher and not much of an option near the goal line (he has exactly two TDs and five end zone targets each of the past three seasons). The 30-year-old will be a risky streaming option even if Ja'Marr Chase or Tee Higgins misses time.

outlooksByWeek.2: DeVonta Smith was fairly quiet in the season opener for the Eagles. Smith finished with three catches for 53 yards in the 24-22 win over Washington. On the plus side, Smith led the team in targets for the game with six. The absence of A. J. Brown should pay dividends for Smith, perhaps as early as Week 2 versus the Titans. Tennessee allowed 215 passing yards and zero touchdowns through the air in its season opener, though the opposing quarterback was Geno Smith of the New York Jets. Expect Smith to become more involved against a suspect defense.
outlooksByWeek.3: DeVonta Smith broke loose last game for the Eagles, snagging 10 passes for 117 yards and a touchdown in a win over the Titans. Smith saw a team-best 13 targets for the game, a pace which should continue in the absence of A.J. Brown. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL. The Eagles could also rely even more on the passing game if Saquon Barkley is sidelined due to injury.
outlooksByWeek.4: DeVonta Smith unsurprisingly led the Eagles in targets, receptions and receiving yardage last game. Unfortunately, the output was rather pedestrian, as Smith managed six catches and 65 yards on eight targets in the ugly 27-7 loss to the Bears. Smith has been held under 70 yards receiving in two of his three games this season. In Week 4, he will face a rather stingy Rams pass defense allowing just 171.3 yards per game through the air, which is fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: DeVonta Smith missed last game for the Eagles with a hamstring issue, and his status is very much up in the air for Week 5 versus the Jags. Philadelphia's passing offense struggled mightily without Smith and tight end Dallas Goedert, and the early departure of Saquon Barkley due to an injury of his own did not help matters. If Smith misses additional time, Dontayvion Wicks, Darius Cooper and rookie Makai Lemon will have some big shoes to fill. An intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 versus the Jags. Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: DeVonta Smith has missed two-straight games for the Eagles. Smith has been nursing a hamstring ailment, and his status for Week 6 versus the Panthers remains up in the air. The Eagles offense has struggled mightily without Smith and running back Saquon Barkley. If Smith can return to the lineup, he would provide a major boost against a Carolina defense allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the league. If Smith cannot suit up, Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper would see added work.
outlooksByWeek.7: DeVonta Smith returned to the Eagles lineup with a bang. Smith snagged seven passes for 75 yards and a touchdown following a two-game absence from a hamstring issue. Even with backup quarterback Tanner McKee under center, Smith was targeted a staggering 14 times. As a result, even with McKee at quarterback for the foreseeable future, Smith should have more than ample opportunities. In Week 7, the Eagles will face a Dallas defense that has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. The Cowboys are allowing 232.7 passing yards per game, which is 23rd in the NFL. In addition, Dallas has surrendered 11 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 24th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: DeVonta Smith missed Philadelphia's last game after aggravating a hamstring injury. Smith has played in just four games this season due to the nagging issue, which could also leave him sidelined in Week 8 versus the Commanders. If he is able to suit up, Smith could have a tasty matchup, even with backup quarterback Tanner McKee under center. Washington is allowing 254 passing yards per game, which is 28th in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders have surrendered 15 passing scores, which is tied for 28th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: DeVonta Smith missed yet another game for the Eagles due to a balky hamstring. Smith has played in just four contests in 2026 in what has been a lost season overall for 2-6 Philadelphia. If he is somehow able to suit up in Week 9, he would be facing a much-improved Giants pass defense. New York is allowing just 184.9 passing yards per clash, which is third in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: DeVonta Smith could return from a hamstring issue for the Eagles following their bye. Smith has missed five of the last six games for Philadelphia due to the ailment. His return, along with that of Dontayvion Wicks, would bolster an extremely depleted wide receiving corps. If he can suit up, the matchup could also be favorable in Week 11, as the Steelers defense has been surprisingly vulnerable to the pass in 2026. Pittsburgh is allowing 242.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 30th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: DeVonta Smith returned from injury for the Eagles and immediately received a heavy workload. Smith saw a team-high 12 targets in the 19-16 win. However, he managed just five catches for 41 yards for the game. Still, he retained his spot as the top target in the offense, and could find more success in Week 12 versus a porous Dallas Cowboys defense. "America's Team" has given up 21 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 29th in the NFL. Dallas is also allowing 237.9 passing yards per tilt, which is 28th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: It's generally tough for a former Heisman Trophy winner and first-round draft pick to fly under the radar, but that has been the case for Smith in recent years. With all eyes on A.J. Brown, Smith has finished no lower than 30th among receivers in fantasy PPG in each of his five seasons (top 30 in PPG each of the last four). The "slim reaper" saw a big dip in touchdowns last season (four, after at least seven the prior three seasons), but remained very efficient (career 9.1 yards per target and 2.1 yards per route run). Smith has handled roughly one-quarter of the Eagles' targets throughout his career, and that may rise slightly after Brown was traded to New England. Smith, 27, is the Eagles' No. 1 receiver for the first time as a non-rookie and is well positioned for a strong WR2 campaign.

The Giants' linebacker corps is their D/ST strength, and it's possible this could be a sneaky-good source of sacks. Nevertheless, it's almost impossible to make a case to draft them, being that they face the Cowboys and Rams to open 2026. Should the Giants impress in those games, however, they could be a prime pickup for a soft Weeks 3-6 portion of their schedule (TEN, ARI, @WSH, NO).

outlooksByWeek.2: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals take on the Texans, who ranked 26th in fantasy points allowed per game (41.5) to WRs in Week 2. After a two-catch, 12-yard dud in the season opener, he'll be aiming for a big bounce-back performance against a vulnerable secondary. Chase logged just four targets in Week 1 despite 35 pass attempts from Joe Burrow. The QB-WR duo should be primed for a rebound against a Houston defense that gave up 409 total yards at home last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals travel to square off against the Steelers' second-ranked pass defense in Week 3. Pittsburgh is allowing just 15.5 fantasy points per game to WRs and is one of six teams that have yet to give up a receiving TD to the position. Chase will surely put that to the test, as he's coming off a 7-75-2 receiving line on nine targets in Cincinnati's Week 2 win over Houston. Across two outings versus the division-rival Steelers in 2025, Chase registered a 19-191-1 line on 33 targets, so Joe Burrow will continue to feed his star wideout regardless of the matchup.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals host the Jaguars for a battle between 2-1 teams in Week 4. He caught nine of 12 targets for 98 yards and his third receiving touchdown of the season during Cincinnati's Week 3 defeat. Chase led the team in receptions, yardage, and targets, and it's clear that his two-catch, 12-yard outing in the season opener was a fluke. He should continue garnering a massive target share from star QB Joe Burrow against Jacksonville's 17th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (31.5) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals travel to face the winless Dolphins in Week 5. He caught all three of his targets for 27 yards in Week 4 before leaving Cincinnati's 22-17 loss with a concussion in the second quarter. Chase was evaluated for the injury after his facemask was pulled following a catch, and he'll have to clear the NFL's five-step concussion protocol before he can return to practice and play in the upcoming contest versus Miami. If he is indeed active, Chase will be going up against the Dolphins, who rank third in fewest fantasy points allowed (22.2) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals are on the road for an AFC North showdown against the Ravens in Week 7. He corralled six of 10 targets for 77 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's 31-24 win in Week 5. Chase cleared concussion protocol in time to pace his team in all receiving categories, as no other Bengal had more than 25 yards or four targets. He'll once again be the primary offensive threat for Joe Burrow versus the Ravens' 22nd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (34.1) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals are set to host the 1-6 Titans in Week 8. He caught five of seven targets for 62 yards and a touchdown in Cincinnati's 35-13 Week 7 victory. Tee Higgins garnered the same number of looks from Joe Burrow, but Chase turned his into six receptions for 148 yards and a score. The good news is that the concussion appears to be behind Chase, and he'll be ready to exploit a Tennessee defense tied for 24th in fantasy points allowed per game (35.8) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals travel to Spain for a Week 9 overseas tilt against the Falcons. He brought in 11 of 16 targets for 141 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's Week 8 overtime victory. Chase eclipsed 100 receiving yards for the first time all season while pacing the team in receptions and targets, but fellow wideout Tee Higgins (10-155-2) finished slightly ahead in yardage. Chase owns a 43-492-6 line on 61 targets through seven contests and will look to build upon that versus Atlanta's 14th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (30.1) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.10: In Week 10, Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals host the Steelers in an AFC North showdown on Sunday Night Football. He caught 10 of 12 targets for 155 yards and a TD during Cincinnati's 34-17 win in Week 9. Chase led his team in receptions, yardage, and targets by a wide margin, and he has now turned in two consecutive games with 10-plus catches, 140-plus yards, and a score. Chase will aim to keep rolling against a Pittsburgh defense he burned for a 9-98-1 line on 12 targets back in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.11: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals face the Commanders in an interconference clash on Monday Night Football in Week 11. He corralled 11 of 14 targets for a season-high 231 yards during Cincinnati's Week 10 victory. After failing to eclipse the 100-yard mark through his first six outings, Chase has done so in three consecutive contests, gaining more than 140 receiving yards in each. He'll take a 64-878-7 line on 87 targets into a matchup against Washington's 20th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (33.5) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals look to get back in the win column when they host the 3-7 Saints in Week 12. He was shockingly quiet during Cincinnati's Week 11 loss, catching five of nine targets for 31 yards. Chase's streak of consecutive games with either a touchdown or 100+ receiving yards ended at five. The rainy weather didn't stop the Bengals from throwing, as Joe Burrow attempted 40 passes, but the superstar duo was unable to establish much of a connection. Chase will attempt to bounce back versus a New Orleans secondary allowing 28.6 fantasy points per game (8th) to opposing WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Chase is fresh off yet another elite fantasy season and he's now finished four of his five NFL campaigns no lower than fifth in fantasy PPG (the exception was 11th in 2023). Chase actually saw a big dip in yardage (1,740 to 1,426), TDs (17 to 8) and fantasy PPG (23.7 to 19.6) from 2024 to 2025 (which was no surprise with Joe Burrow missing nine games), but still put up big numbers thanks to pacing the league in pass routes and targets for the second season in a row. In fact, Chase's 125 receptions make him the third receiver in NFL history with 125-plus catches in multiple seasons. The 26-year-old remains the top target in a high-scoring Bengals offense, and is one of the top players in all of fantasy.

outlooksByWeek.2: Saquon Barkley averaged 5.5 yards per tote in Week 1 for the Eagles. Barkley rushed 15 times for 83 yards, though was held out of the end zone in the 24-22 win over Washington. Barkley should have even greater success in Week 2 versus a dismal Titans squad. Tennessee allowed 367 yards from scrimmage to the Jets in their season opener. Tennessee was torched on the ground in particular, allowing 152 rushing yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Saquon Barkley missed portions of Philadelphia's last game due to a stinger, leaving his status in question for Week 3 versus the Bears. Barkley is slated to undergo an MRI to determine if he will miss any time. Saquon had five carries for just 20 yards in the 24-20 win over the Titans. Meanwhile, Tank Bigsby had 15 touches and a touchdown, while Will Shipley saw nine touches and managed 29 yards overall. Bigsby and Shipley would likely split touches if Barkley cannot go, with Bigsby getting the slight edge. The Eagles will face a Bears run defense in Week 3 allowing 122 yards per clash on the ground, which is 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Saquon Barkley rushed for 82 yards last game for the Eagles. Philadelphia fell behind in the second half, though, which forced the Eagles to all but abandon the run. Barkley has yet to rush for 100 yards in a game this season. In Week 4, Barkley will face a stout defensive line with Aaron Donald when the Eagles clash with the Rams. Los Angeles is allowing 101.3 rushing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the NFL. In addition, the Rams have yielded just one rushing score through the first three games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Saquon Barkley left Philadelphia's last game due to a hamstring ailment. While the injury is not considered serious, it remains to be seen whether Barkley will be able to suit up in London in Week 5 versus the Jags. If Barkley can play, he will face a stiff test, as Jacksonville is allowing just 74.3 rushing yards per tilt, which is second in the NFL. In addition, the Jags have given up just two rushing touchdowns through the first four games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Saquon Barkley missed Philadelphia's last game due to a hamstring injury. His status for Week 6 versus Carolina remains up in the air. The Eagles could be on their fourth-string running back in the form of Dameon Pierce, as Tank Bigsby is on Injured Reserve and Will Shipley started last game but suffered a foot injury of his own and did not return. Whoever lines up in the backfield could have a tasty matchup versus a suspect Panthers run defense, though. Carolina is allowing 156.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is second-to-last in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Saquon Barkley has missed the last two games for the Eagles due to a hamstring ailment, leaving his status for Week 7 versus the Cowboys in jeopardy. Dameon Pierce rushed for 35 yards and a touchdown in Barkley's place, while also catching four balls out of the backfield. If Barkley can somehow suit up, he will be facing a Dallas defense that has allowed the most rushing yards in the NFL to date. Per game, the Cowboys are allowing a brutal 149.8 yards on the ground.
outlooksByWeek.8: Saquon Barkley returned from injury for the Eagles, only to tweak his hamstring while also suffering a compensatory back injury. Barkley rushed seven times for 62 yards and a touchdown, though played sparingly in the second half of the game, and ultimately could be sidelined again in Week 8 versus the Commanders. If Barkley is able to suit up, he will face a Washington defense that has been fairly stingy against the run in 2026.  The Commanders are allowing 100.5 rushing yards per clash, which is 14th in the league. In addition, Washington has allowed just five rushing touchdowns, which is tied for 11th in the league. If neither Barkley nor backup Dameon Pierce can play, Elijah Mitchell would be the only healthy option at running back.
outlooksByWeek.9: Saquon Barkley did find the end zone last game for the Eagles. Unfortunately, Saquon was otherwise held in check with 54 scrimmage yards in a dismal 27-10 loss to Washington. Philadelphia does not appear likely to trade Barkley to a contender, leaving him primed for a revenge game against his former squad, the New York Giants, in Week 9. New York is allowing 128.1 rushing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Saquon Barkley did find the end zone last game for the Eagles, but was otherwise bottled up. Barkley managed just 22 yards on the ground along with the score in the 19-11 loss to the Giants before the bye. With third-string quarterback Joe Milton under center, Saquon will likely see a stacked box in Week 11 versus the Steelers. Pittsburgh has been stellar in defending the run in 2026 as well, allowing just 83.2 yards per tilt on the ground, which is third in the league. Likewise, Pittsburgh has yielded just five rushing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: Saquon Barkley carried the offensive load for the Eagles last game, though exited the contest due to a left arm issue. Barkley rushed 17 times for 75 yards and a touchdown, though did not log a carry during the final eight minutes of the narrow 19-16 win over the Steelers. Barkley should be healthy enough to suit up on Thanksgiving versus the Cowboys, though. Dallas has been abysmal against the run in 2026, allowing 151.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is the worst mark in the NFL. In addition, the Cowboys have given up 15 rushing scores, which is 29th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Barkley is looking to rebound in his ninth NFL season (third with the Eagles) following a big step back in 2025. After producing 2,283 yards and 15 touchdowns on 378 touches in his first season with Philly, Barkley dipped to 1,413 yards and nine scores on 317 touches in 2025. Barkley fell from first among backs in fantasy points per game (22.5) to 15th (14.5). Now 29 years old, it's possible Barkley's best days are behind him, but he's still positioned as a clear feature back in a good offense that will have a healthier line and a new playcaller in Sean Mannion. Barkley is riskier than ever, but he's still worthy of mid- to back-end RB1 consideration.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kenneth Walker earned his big salary in his Kansas City debut, rumbling for a career-high 173 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries while catching three of six targets for 18 yards and another score in a season-opening win over the Broncos. It was the kind of volume Walker rarely garnered in Seattle, but the fifth-year RB is being counted on to handle bell-cow duties with his new team, as rookie Emmett Johnson figures to be his primary backup for most or all of the season. Walker will aim to keep rolling in Week 2 against a Colts defense that just got steamrolled by Derrick Henry, but which ranked 11th in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kenneth Walker has had a dazzling start to his Kansas City tenure, topping 100 rushing yards in each of his first two games and piling up 369 scrimmage yards in total with two touchdowns, one rushing and one receiving. The former Seahawk is thriving in a bell cow role, and his 6.2 yards per carry would be a career high if he can keep it up. Walker will take aim in Week 3 at a Dolphins defense that's been more vulnerable through the air than on the ground so far in 2026, allowing just 3.5 yards per carry, which ranks sixth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kenneth Walker didn't need a ceiling game in Kansas City's Week 3 win over the Dolphins. While he failed to reach 100 rushing yards for the first time this season, he did score his second rushing and second receiving touchdown of the year. Walker's addition has supercharged the entire offense, and he's thriving in a bell-cow role, amassing 360 rushing yards in three games while averaging 5.5 yards per carry. He's also on pace for a career-best campaign as a pass catcher. Walker could face a test in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that is tied for 10th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs and has given up just one touchdown to the position so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kenneth Walker was dominant for Kansas City in the team's first four games prior to a Week 5 bye, rumbling for 537 rushing yards on 6.2 yards per carry while scoring six times-four on the ground and two through the air. Last season's Super Bowl MVP with the Seahawks is earning every penny of his big free-agent contract, and his presence in the backfield is also opening things up for Patrick Mahomes, putting KC in the top five in the NFL in points per game at 29.5 and second in yards per game at 412.0, behind only the Rams. Walker should be able to continue rolling in Week 6 against a Chargers defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kenneth Walker continues to shine as the new focal point of Kansas City's offense. Through his first five games with the team, Walker has piled up eight total touchdowns-six rushing and two receiving-while topping 100 rushing yards in four of those contests. He leads the NFL with 665 rushing yards, despite already having had his bye and having played one fewer game than Bijan Robinson and James Cook, the only other two backs with more than 600 yards. Walker will try to deliver a revenge game in Week 7 against a Seahawks defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Kenneth Walker was on the receiving end of a revenge game by the Seahawks' defense in Week 7, getting held to a season-low 36 rushing yards and zero TDs. Last season's Super Bowl MVP is still second in the NFL in rushing yards with 701, just three behind Bijan Robinson, and Walker has played one fewer game thanks to Kansas City's early Week 5 bye. Walker will try to stay on course for the 2026 rushing crown in Week 8 against a Broncos defense that ranks 23rd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Kenneth Walker has been held out of the end zone and below 100 scrimmage yards in back-to-back games, both Kansas City losses. The star running back still sits third in the race for the NFL rushing crown with 770 yards, just behind Bijan Robinson's 780 yards and Jahmyr Gibbs' 773 yards, but he might need more help from Patrick Mahomes and the passing game to get defenses to stop loading up against him. Walker will look to bounce back in Week 9 against a Jets defense that ranks 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Kenneth Walker is coming off a massive performance in Kansas City's Week 9 win over the Jets, scoring three touchdowns (one rushing, two receiving) while racking up 143 scrimmage yards. The star running back is second in the NFL in rushing yards with 872, just behind Bijan Robinson's 880. He is fourth in scrimmage yards with 1,044, and tied for first with Jahmyr Gibbs in total TDs from scrimmage with 11. Walker could be leaned on even more heavily in Week 10 if Patrick Mahomes' elbow injury keeps him on the sideline, against a Falcons defense that's tied for 29th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Kenneth Walker didn't suit up for Kansas City's Week 10 win over the Falcons due to a minor groin injury. In his place, rookie Emmett Johnson erupted for 171 scrimmage yards and two receiving touchdowns. Walker is expected back in Week 11 against Arizona, but Johnson's performance could lead to more volume for the team's backup RB as the focus shifts toward making sure Walker still has something left for the playoffs, given KC's 7-2 record. Assuming Walker is cleared to return, he'll be facing a Cardinals defense that's tied for 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Kenneth Walker has missed Kansas City's last two games with a groin injury, and in his absence, rookie Emmett Johnson has dazzled. Walker is in no danger of losing his hold on the No. 1 job in the backfield given his own outstanding start to the season, but Johnson's performance could lead to more of a timeshare as Andy Reid keeps one eye on the health of his roster ahead of the playoffs. If Walker is cleared to return for Week 12's Thursday Night Football clash with the Bills, he'll take on a defense that ranks 21st in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Walker signed with the Chiefs after spending his first four NFL seasons with the Seahawks. The reigning Super Bowl MVP and PFF's highest-graded running back from 2025, Walker is poised for feature-back duties in a good, Andy Reid-led offense. Having worked in a committee most of last season, Walker was limited to only five touchdowns and 11.3 fantasy points per game (both career lows), but he still generated 252 touches and a career-high 1,309 yards. He has yet to finish a season better than 18th in fantasy points (12th on a per-game basis) and has missed at least two games in three of four seasons in the league, but the 25-year-old's ability to contribute at a high level as a rusher and receiver is enough to position him as, at least, a fringe RB1 in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jayden Daniels overcame a slow start to nearly lead the Commanders to a comeback win against the Eagles in Week 1. Daniels finished the contest with 164 yards passing and two touchdowns, along with an additional 31 yards rushing for the game. Daniels will look to build some momentum in Week 2 versus an extremely suspect Dallas Cowboys defense. Dallas allowed the most yards in the NFL last season, and the supposedly revamped defense was trounced by the Giants in their 2026 opener. The Cowboys allowed 394 scrimmage yards and four total touchdowns in an ugly 28-20 loss to Jaxson Dart and company.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jayden Daniels dislocated his elbow against the Cowboys in Week 2, the same elbow he injured last year for the Commanders. While the elbow is not fractured, Daniels is almost certain to miss Week 3 vs. the Seahawks. Veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start versus a devastating Seattle defense that is allowing just 8.5 points and 214 yards per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league in both categories. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jayden Daniels is set to practice with the Commanders as the squad heads to London for Week 4.  Daniels is unlikely to play versus the Colts due to his dislocated elbow, though, and especially since backup Marcus Mariota just led an improbable victory over the defending Super Bowl champions. Mariota tossed three touchdowns in the stunning 33-31 win over the Seahawks. Whoever lines up under center in Week 4 will have a tasty matchup versus a suspect Colts pass defense. Indianapolis is allowing 276 passing yards per tilt, which is 30th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jayden Daniels could return in Week 5 for the Commanders from a dislocated elbow. Backup quarterback Marcus Mariota left Washington's last game with a knee injury, which could hasten the need for Daniels to return versus the Giants. if neither quarterback can suit up, seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis would get the nod. The defense for the Giants looks totally revamped in 2026, allowing 205.3 yards per tilt through the air, which is 10th in the league. The Giants are tied for the league-lead with six interceptions.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jayden Daniels returned from injury and appeared to show no ill effects regarding his previously dislocated elbow. Daniels rushed for over 100 yards and two touchdowns, while also passing for 199 yards against the Giants. Unfortunately, poor game management at the end of overtime cost the Commanders the win, and overshadows what was otherwise a solid return to the lineup for Daniels. Unfortunately, a tall task lurks in Week 6 on the road versus the 49ers. San Francisco is undefeated and allowing just 297.2 scrimmage yards per tilt, which is sixth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jayden Daniels produced one of his best games of the season before the bye for the Commanders, and will look to build off of that performance in Week 8 versus the Eagles.  Daniels completed 72.5-percent of his passes for 300 yards and two touchdowns in a narrow loss to the 49ers. In fact, it was the first time in 2026 that Daniels threw for even 200 yards in a contest. Daniels will face an Eagles defense that has been better against the run than the pass this season.  Philadelphia is allowing 244.5 passing yards per contest, which is 27th in the NFL.  However, Philadelphia is still surrendering 119.3 yards per game on the ground, which is just 21st in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jayden Daniels has thrown for at least 215 yards in each of the last two games for Washington. He also has three touchdown passes over that span. However, in Week 9, Daniels will face a stellar Rams pass defense.  Los Angeles is allowing just 191.9 passing yards per game, which is fourth in the NFL. In addition, the Rams have yielded just 10 passing scores this season, which is tied for eighth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jayden Daniels threw for 274 yards and a touchdown last game for Washington. He has passed for at least one touchdown in three-straight outings, and thrown for at least 270 yards in two of those three contests. In Week 10, he will face a Giants defense that has been better against the pass than the run in 2026. New York is allowing just 177.8 passing yards per clash, which is third in the NFL. However, the Giants are surrendering 123.6 rushing yards per tilt, which is 21st in the league, and Daniels ran for 103 yards and two scores when the two teams met earlier this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jayden Daniels tossed three touchdown passes last game for the Commanders. He also threw his first two interceptions of the season in the thrilling 24-21 win over the Giants. Daniels has thrown for at least 215 yards in four-straight contests. He may be more successful with his legs than with his arm in Week 11 versus the Bengals, though. Cincinnati is allowing just 216.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the NFL. By contrast, Cincy is surrendering 123.9 rushing yards per clash, which is 21st in the league.
outlooksByWeek.12: Jayden Daniels did not record a touchdown last game for the Commanders.  However, he threw for 289 yards and rushed for an additional 55 yards in the surprising 22-20 win over the Bengals. It was the second-highest passing total of the season for Daniels, and his third-highest rushing total of the year. Daniels has a tasty matchup in Week 12 versus a suspect Cardinals defense allowing 355.2 scrimmage yards per game, which is 26th in the NFL. In addition, Arizona is allowing 29.4 points per tilt, which is 31st in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Daniels is looking to bounce back after appearing in only seven games due to injury last season. The 2024 Offensive Rookie of the Year began his career with a bang, tossing 25 touchdowns and adding 891 yards and six scores with his legs in his first season. He wasn't quite as dominant when healthy last season (16.3 points per game, compared to 20.9 in 2024), but he remained a major factor with his legs (58-278-2 in seven games, three of which were partial appearances). Daniels' supporting cast is underwhelming and he'll be working with a new playcaller (David Blough), but the dual-threat ability supplies the 25-year-old with elite upside. He's a strong QB1 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Travis Kelce showed he still has plenty left in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, leading the team with 71 receiving yards while catching three of five targets. The veteran tight end's production tailed off the last couple years, but he still topped 800 receiving yards in 12 straight seasons, and Week 1's performance moved him past Jason Witten into second place on the NFL's all-time list for TEs with 13,073 yards, trailing only Tony Gonzalez's 15,127. Kelce will take on a Colts defense in Week 2 that ranked 31st in receiving yards allowed to tight ends in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Travis Kelce continued a strong start to his 14th NFL season in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, posting a 9-101-1 line on 11 targets. The future Hall of Famer last delivered a 1,000-yard campaign in 2022, but he's jumped out to an early pace in 2026 that would see him top 1,400 receiving yards and set a new career high. With Patrick Mahomes spreading the ball around and the offense prioritizing Kenneth Walker and the run game, Kelce may need to rely on spike games rather than steady production for his fantasy value. He'll take on a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's allowed 10.2 yards per target to tight ends through two weeks, 27th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Travis Kelce notched just two targets in Kansas City's Week 3 win over the Dolphins, but he caught both for 59 yards and a touchdown. The future Hall of Famer seems revitalized in his age-36 season, and he's already hauled in two catches of 40 or more yards, just one short of the career-high three he produced way back in 2016. Patrick Mahomes is spreading the ball around effectively, and Kelce, Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy, and Kenneth Walker all have between 15 and 18 targets through three games. The tight end has turned his volume into a strong 14-231-2 line. Kelce will look to keep rolling in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that ranks 31st in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs and has already coughed up five TDs to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Travis Kelce remains on pace for a bounce-back season coming out of Kansas City's Week 5 bye. Through four games, the veteran tight end is on pace for his first 1,000-yard season since 2022, although it's fair to wonder if he can keep that up given his reduced volume, as he's also on track to fall short of 100 targets for the first time since 2014. With Kenneth Walker having rejuvenated the team's rushing game and Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy both capable of handling underneath and intermediate routes, there isn't a clear niche for Kelce to thrive in. He remains Patrick Mahomes' most trustworthy option, and that should keep his floor relatively high. Kelce will take on a Chargers defense in Week 6 that ranks 12th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Travis Kelce wasn't needed much in Kansas City's Week 6 win over the Chargers, catching four of five targets for 53 yards. The veteran tight end has slowed down after a fast start to the season, and through five games he's produced a 20-299-2 line on 27 targets while the offense has leaned heavily on Kenneth Walker. Kelce remains Patrick Mahomes' most trustworthy option, especially while Rashee Rice is sidelined. Kelce faces a tough matchup in Week 7 against a Seahawks defense that's allowed the fewest receiving yards in the league to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Travis Kelce made history again in Week 7, moving into fifth place on the NFL's all-time reception list with 1,104 as Kansas City fell to the Seahawks. The veteran tight end remains Patrick Mahomes' most reliable pass catcher, and through six games, Kelce's delivered a 24-343-2 line on 35 targets. The 37-year-old is no longer as dangerous with the ball in his hands, but he can still move the chains consistently. Kelce will take on a Broncos defense in Week 8 that ranks 23rd in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Travis Kelce caught five of seven targets for 67 yards in Kansas City's Week 8 loss to the Broncos, his best performance since delivering a 9-101-1 line in Week 2. The veteran tight end remains one of Patrick Mahomes' most trusted options, and Kelce has a shot at his first 1,000-yard effort since 2022 if he can maintain his current pace. He could be poised for solid numbers again in Week 9 against a Jets defense that's tied for 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Travis Kelce produced his highest yardage total since Week 2 in Kansas City's Week 9 win over the Jets, hauling in four of six targets for a team-high 72 yards. He also scored his first rushing touchdown since 2021 on a one-yard plunge. Kelce has delivered a 33-482-2 line on 48 targets through eight games, but his outlook would suffer if Patrick Mahomes ends up missing time due to an elbow injury he picked up against the Jets. Regardless of who's under center, Kelce will face a Falcons defense in Week 10 that ranks 16th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Travis Kelce is coming off his least productive game of the season, catching both his targets for 30 yards in Kansas City's Week 10 win over the Falcons. The veteran tight end hasn't caught a touchdown pass since Week 3, and he hasn't hauled in more than five passes or 72 receiving yards since Week 2, but his role as Patrick Mahomes' most reliable security blanket gives him a fairly secure floor. Kelce will look to make a bigger contribution in Week 11 against a Cardinals defense that's tied for 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Travis Kelce is coming off one of his best games of the season, catching six of seven targets for 74 yards and two touchdowns in Kansas City's Week 11 win over the Cardinals. The future Hall of Famer snapped a six-game TD drought with the performance, and with 586 receiving yards through 10 contests, he's still got a real shot at his first 1,000-yard campaign since 2022. Kelce is Patrick Mahomes' most reliable option, but he has plenty of competition for targets in a passing game that features plenty of depth but no clear No. 1 threat. Kelce will look to keep rolling in Week 12 against a Bills defense that ranks 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: Kelce re-signed with the Chiefs and is returning for what might be his final NFL season. The veteran tight end's days as an elite producer are behind him, and he saw a notable dip in usage last season (19.6% target share was his lowest since 2014). Kelce did hold up for 17 games and still finished in the top 10 at the position in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards and fantasy PPG. Kelce has reeled off 10 consecutive top-five fantasy campaigns despite not offering much in the scoring department (he hasn't cleared five TDs in a season since 2022). The 36-year-old's role could dip even further this season, so he's best valued as a fringe TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Michael Pittman and the Steelers travel for a Week 2 tilt against the Patriots. The former Indianapolis Colt secured all three targets for a team-high 58 yards in his debut for Pittsburgh. Pittman finished sixth in targets but still did plenty of damage with his opportunities, and if the Steelers want to throw the ball 40-plus times a game, he could develop into a reliable fantasy receiver. New England's defense ranks 21st in receiving yards allowed to WRs (161), but they will be playing at home with a rest advantage.
outlooksByWeek.3: Michael Pittman and the Steelers host the Bengals in Week 3. After dealing with a foot injury during training camp and the preseason, he suffered a new foot ailment that forced him to miss Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss in New England. Pittman will have to practice in some capacity in order to return for Sunday's contest, but it sounds like his status for Week 3 is very much in question. Consider him doubtful to suit up until we hear otherwise.
outlooksByWeek.4: Michael Pittman and the Steelers travel to take on the division-rival Browns in Week 4. He returned from a one-game absence and caught two of five targets for 16 yards during Pittsburgh's 30-27 win in Week 3. Pittman tied for second on the team in targets but was unable to make much of an impact, as Aaron Rodgers continued spreading the ball around on offense by hitting nine different receivers. However, he has an opportunity to break out against Cleveland's 26th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (36.7) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Michael Pittman and the Steelers host the receiver's former team when the Colts come to town in Week 5. He hauled in two of four targets for 15 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss, giving him a 7-89-0 receiving line on 12 targets across three contests. It's been a slow start for Pittman in his debut season for the Steelers, but Week 5 offers a shot at some payback against the team that drafted him in 2020. Indianapolis' defense ranks 20th in fantasy points allowed (35.0) to WRs, a matchup that could help Pittman's chemistry with Aaron Rodgers.
outlooksByWeek.12: In Week 12, Michael Pittman and Pittsburgh aim to snap a two-game losing skid when they host the Broncos on Black Friday. He hasn't played since Week 4 after being placed on injured reserve due to a foot injury, but the first-year Steeler is ready to make his return versus a talented Denver secondary, which is allowing 28.1 fantasy points per game to WRs. Pittman hasn't played in nearly two months, so fantasy managers needing help at receiver should look elsewhere until he can prove otherwise.

player.seasonOutlook: Pittman was traded to the Steelers after spending his first six NFL seasons with the Colts. The 2020 second-round pick handled a hefty 23.6% of Indianapolis' targets during his tenure, which helped him to four top-20 fantasy campaigns. Pittman has reached 800 receiving yards in five consecutive seasons while primarily operating as a short-to-intermediate target. The role has limited his scoring (he has 25 TDs in 95 games) and that may not change much with DK Metcalf on the other side in Pittsburgh. Of course, Pittman will be a featured target in an offense led by Aaron Rodgers. That's enough to put the 28-year-old squarely in the weekly WR3 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top receiving options in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Johnson paced New Orleans' tight ends in yards (53) during the Week 1 overtime loss but trailed Noah Fant in receptions (three to four) and targets (seven to eight). Despite this, Johnson was on the field for 72 of the Saints' 90 offensive snaps, where Fant played just 37. Thus, Johnson is expected to remain New Orleans' top TE option against a Ravens defense that allowed just 10.3 PPR fantasy points to the position in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of New Orleans' top receiving options in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Despite a dip in snap rate and route share compared to Week 1, Johnson paced the Saints' tight end corps in receptions, targets and yards in Week 2. He ranks third on the team in targets and yards, which is a positive outlook for his value going forward. However, Johnson is in for an unfavorable matchup, as Las Vegas' defense has allowed just 10.3 PPR fantasy points per game to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top weapons in the Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. Johnson has been New Orleans' second-most productive receiver this season, catching 15 of 19 targets for 173 yards and three touchdowns. With head coach Kellen Moore's offense throwing the ball an average of 44 times per game through three weeks, Johnson is expected to remain one of fantasy's top tight ends going forward. Additionally, he's in for a terrific Week 4 matchup against a Falcons defense that's allowed 17.2 PPR fantasy points per game to the TE position this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top pass catchers in the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Johnson had another productive outing in the Week 4 loss to the Falcons, catching six of eight targets for 59 yards. He's now tallied 232 receiving yards through four contests this season, the fourth-most amongst tight ends. Johnson will likely continue to benefit from head coach Kellen Moore's pass-heavy offense that's averaged 45 pass attempts per game this year. Despite this, Johnson is in for a difficult Week 5 matchup against a Vikings defense that's given up just 7.7 fantasy points per game to opposing TEs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top pass catchers in the Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Johnson tallied just 16 yards on four receptions in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings, struggling alongside the rest of New Orleans' offense. Despite this, he's tied for the second-most receptions (25) on the Saints through five weeks, accumulating 248 yards and three touchdowns. Expect Johnson to bounce back in Week 6 against a Giants defense that's allowed 14.2 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this year.
outlooksByWeek.7: Juwan Johnson will look to bounce back from a lackluster performance in the Saints' Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. Johnson has struggled over the last two weeks, catching just four of seven targets for 16 yards. Despite this, he remains third on the team in targets (35), receptions (25) and yards (248) through six games, suggesting more fantasy production in the near future. Johnson is in for a difficult Week 7 matchup, however, as Pittsburgh's defense has allowed just 11.7 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top receiving options in the Week 9 matchup against the Browns. Johnson has really underperformed in the Saints' last two games, catching just one of five targets for seven yards during that span. Despite this recent lack of production, Johnson ranks third on the team in receiving yards (255), targets (38) and receptions (26) while catching three touchdowns across seven contests. Johnson could bounce back against a Cleveland defense that's given up 15.2 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top pass catchers during the Week 10 matchup against the Panthers. Johnson saw little volume but saved his fantasy day with a score in Week 9, catching two of three targets for 34 yards and a touchdown. He's been relatively underwhelming over the last three contests, catching just three of seven targets for 41 yards and a touchdown. This is especially concerning due to the return of 2026 first-round pick Jordyn Tyson, who will likely take more receiving volume away from Johnson as the season progresses. However, Johnson could thrive against a Panthers defense that's allowed 13.5 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top pass catchers in the Week 11 matchup against the Bears. Johnson has really struggled over New Orleans' last four games, catching just five of 10 targets for 69 yards and a touchdown. With Jordyn Tyson breaking out in the Week 10 loss to the Panthers (11-80-0), Johnson will likely receive even less opportunities going forward. He likely needs to score a touchdown to find fantasy relevance in Week 11 against a Bears defense that's allowed just three touchdowns to tight ends all season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Juwan Johnson (hamstring) is expected to remain the Saints' top tight end if active for the Week 12 matchup against the Bengals. Johnson sustained a hamstring injury during the Week 11 loss to the Bears, and the extent of the issue remains TBD. Johnson struggled to find fantasy value before sustaining this injury, catching just five of 10 targets for 69 yards and one touchdown from Weeks 7 through 10 (three games). If active, Johnson could find fantasy value but is likely still too inconsistent to start, even with a favorable matchup against a Bengals defense that's given up 15.2 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Johnson's impressive progression continued in 2025, as the converted wide receiver posted career-high marks in targets, catches, yardage and fantasy points (all four were eighth or better among tight ends). Johnson produced nine top-12 fantasy weeks, which tied for second at the position. He has finished in the top 12 in aDOT each of the past four seasons but hasn't been much of an option near the goal line (no more than four TDs or end zone targets in each of the past three seasons). The 29-year-old has added target competition, including eighth-overall pick Jordyn Tyson (once healthy), but he very well could settle in as high as third in target priority in the Saints' Tyler Shough-led offense. Johnson is a fine TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rachaad White found himself on the losing end of the timeshare out of the backfield in Week 1 for Washington.  White had seven carries for 22 yards, while fellow rusher Jacory Croskey-Merritt managed 16 carries for 63 yards and a touchdown. White only had one more reception than Croskey-Merritt as well. In Week 2, Washington has a favorable matchup with the Cowboys, as Dallas allowed 165 rushing yards on the ground to the Giants in their season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rachaad White recorded 13 touches for 83 yards out of the backfield last game for the Commanders. White took seven carries for 43 yards, while also catching six passes for 40 yards as a receiver with Washington playing from behind. White remains in a timeshare for touches with Jacory Croskey-Merritt, though, and will face a devastating Seattle defense in Week 3.  The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points and 214 yards per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league in both categories.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rachaad White found the end zone last game for Washington. White caught a six-yard touchdown pass from backup quarterback Marcus Mariota during the stunning 33-31 win over the Seahawks. White also doubled up starting running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt in terms of yards per carry. However, Bill out-touched White by a margin of 20-9 for the game. Nevertheless, both backs should remain involved in Week 4 versus a suspect Colts defense. Indianapolis is allowing the most yards per game in the NFL through three contests.
outlooksByWeek.5: Rachaad White missed Washington's last game due to a shoulder issue, leaving his status in question for Week 5 versus the Giants. An argument can be made that White has been more productive than fellow rusher Jacory Croskey-Merritt in 2026, though that point may be moot as long as White is sidelined. Austin Ekeler will be the backup to Bill if White remains shelved. In Week 5, Washington will face a Giants run defense that has vastly improved from a season ago. New York is allowing 109 rushing yards per tilt, which is tied for 15th in the league. In addition, the G-Men have surrendered only two rushing touchdowns through four contests.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rachaad White returned to the lineup for Washington following a one-game absence due to a shoulder issue. However, White failed to have much of an impact. He rushed seven times for just 18 yards, while also catching a two-yard pass out of the backfield. Meanwhile, starting running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed for 82 yards and a touchdown. In Week 6, the Commanders face a 49ers defense that has been rather stingy against the run. The Niners are allowing 97.6 rushing yards per clash, which is 10th in the league. In addition, San Fran has surrendered just three rushing scores to date, which is tied for sixth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.8: Rachaad White will serve as the No. 1 running back for the Commanders in Week 8, as starter Jacory Croskey-Merritt was placed on Injured Reserve with a groin injury. White has found the end zone in two of the last three games as a receiver out of the backfield, but is averaging just 4.0 yards per carry as a rusher. Still, the expanded role should give him double-digit touches against a floundering Eagles defense. Philadelphia is allowing 119.3 rushing yards per clash, which is 21st in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Rachaad White has scored in back-to-back games for Washington. White rushed 11 times for 55 yards and a touchdown in the 27-10 win over the Eagles. White has found the end zone in each of the last two contests since taking over the starting running back job for the injured Jacory Croskey-Merritt. Jeremy McNichols also left this game with an injury, leaving Austin Ekeler as the only other healthy option. In Week 9, Washington will face a Rams defense allowing 109.3 yards per tilt on the ground, which is 14th in the NFL. However, the Rams have surrendered just four rushing scores in 2026, which is tied for third in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Rachaad White continues to operate as the top back for the Commanders, though has found little room to roam on the ground. White has failed to rush for more than 55 yards in any game this season. However, he does have at least two receptions in three-straight contests. In Week 10, White will face a Giants defense that has been better against the pass than the run in 2026. New York is allowing just 177.8 passing yards per clash, which is third in the NFL. However, the Giants are surrendering 123.6 rushing yards per tilt, which is 21st in the league.
outlooksByWeek.11: Rachaad White is averaging at least four yards per carry over his last three games with the Commanders. Though White is technically the starting running back, he has only had double-digit carries twice this season. Moreover, Jacory Croskey-Merritt could return soon from Injured Reserve. For now, though, White remains the top dog in the backfield heading into a Week 11 clash with the Bengals. Cincy has been better against the pass than the run in 2026. The Bengals are allowing 123.9 rushing yards per tilt, which is 21st in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: Rachaad White dressed last game for the Commanders, but did not record a carry. Perhaps his heel issue was more concerning than initially thought, as Jacory Croskey-Merritt had 13 carries against the Bengals, while Austin Ekeler registered seven. Croskey-Merritt's return from injury likely relegates White to backup duty in Week 12 versus Arizona anyway, though the matchup is extremely favorable. The Cardinals are allowing 128.8 rushing yards per clash, which is 27th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: White signed with the Commanders after spending his first four seasons with the Buccaneers. The 2022 third-round pick operated as a feature back in 2023 (he finished in the top five among backs in touches, yards and fantasy points), but he played a situational role during his other three seasons. White is fine as a rusher, but he's a standout as a receiver. He's the only back in the NFL with 40-plus catches in each of the past four seasons, and his 89.1% career catch rate is easily best in NFL history among players with 100-plus targets. The 27-year-old is the favorite to lead the Washington backfield, but Jacory Croskey-Merritt and perhaps others will be involved. White will find himself on the weekly flex radar as long as he remains atop the depth chart.

outlooksByWeek.2: Harrison Butker was perfect in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, connecting on all four of his extra points and converting his only field-goal attempt from 28 yards. The offense looked more potent with a healthy Patrick Mahomes under center, Kenneth Walker as the new bell-cow back, and a returning Eric Bieniemy as offensive coordinator, and Butker should see his opportunities rise if that trend holds. He could be busy in Week 2 against a Colts team that just got routed by the Ravens and was tied for 20th in points per game allowed in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Harrison Butker missed a 51-yard field-goal attempt in the second quarter of Week 2, but he made up for it by converting the rest of his opportunities, including a 40-yard FG that gave Kansas City the overtime win over the Colts. The veteran kicker has been busy in the early going with six FG attempts and seven PATs, and a resurgent offense led by a healthy Patrick Mahomes and new bell-cow back Kenneth Walker should continue to supply Butker with volume. He'll face a Dolphins team in Week 3 that's giving up 31.0 points a game in the early going.
outlooksByWeek.4: Harrison Butker missed a field goal for a second straight game in Kansas City's Week 3 win over the Dolphins. A resurgent offense under a healthy Patrick Mahomes has given the veteran kicker a solid floor in terms of PATs, and he's a perfect 10-for-10 to begin the year with at least three in each contest. Butker's two FG misses have also been from 50-plus yards, and he's a perfect 8-for-8 from shorter distances. He may not be able to squander any chances in Week 4 against a Raiders team that's allowed 18.0 points a game, seventh in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Harrison Butker has been more floor than ceiling to begin the season. The Kansas City kicker has kicked at least three extra points in all four games, but he's logged more than one field goal only once, going 7-for-9 over that span with both his misses coming from 50-plus yards. With Patrick Mahomes and Kenneth Walker having the offense operating at a very high level, Butker's mix of opportunities isn't likely to change much. He could be busy in Week 6 against a Chargers team allowing 25.8 points per game, tied for 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Harrison Butker missed two kicks in Kansas City's Week 6 win over the Chargers, but he still came away with one of his more productive games of the season, connecting on three of four field goals and one of two extra points. It was the first time in 2026 that the veteran kicker had failed to convert multiple extra points, but his overall volume has been inconsistent, and through five contests he's gone 10-for-13 on FGs and 14-for-15 on PATs. Butker may not be able to afford to squander any chances in Week 7 against a Seahawks team allowing 20.3 points per game, tied for seventh in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Harrison Butker went just 1-for-3 on field-goal attempts in Kansas City's Week 7 loss to the Seahawks, the first time he's missed multiple attempts in a single game since 2018. The veteran kicker has missed five of 16 FG attempts overall this season, including one from inside 50 yards, and he may need to turn things around quickly to prevent KC from beginning a search for his replacement. Butker will try to bounce back in Week 8 against a Broncos team that's allowing 20.1 points a game, seventh in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Harrison Butker's job security continues to shrink. The veteran kicker missed a 54-yard field goal in the fourth quarter of a Week 8 loss to the Broncos, forcing Kansas City to go for a touchdown on its next possession to try and overcome a four-point deficit, rather than give Butker a chance to play hero. He's missed at least one FG in three straight games, and his 66.7% success rate (12-for-18) through seven games is over 20 points lower than his 2025 performance. Head coach Andy Reid hasn't yet made a move to replace Butker, but the team did sign Justin Tucker to its practice squad last week. If Butker gets a chance to turn things around in Week 9, he'll be facing a Jets team allowing 23.5 points per game, 16th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Harrison Butker missed another field goal in Kansas City's Week 9 win over the Jets, but he converted all five of his extra points. The veteran kicker has an awful 63.2% success rate on field goal attempts through eight games, going just 12-for-19 including a weak 2-for-8 showing from 50-plus yards, but so far Andy Reid has stuck with him. Butker will try to regain some confidence indoors in a Week 10 road trip to Atlanta against a Falcons team that's given up 24.8 points per game this season, tied for 20th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.11: Harrison Butker hasn't converted a field goal attempt in two straight games and hasn't kicked more than one in four straight, going a weak 2-for-6 on attempts during that stretch. The Kansas City offense has been providing him with more PATs, however, and he's gone 13-for-13 on extra points over the last three contests. Butker's struggles have left him with little job security, but for now he still holds the job. He could be busier in Week 11 against a Cardinals team allowing 28.9 points per game, tied for 31st in the league with the Raiders.
outlooksByWeek.12: Harrison Butker appears to be taking the threat to his job security seriously. The veteran kicker has been perfect over the last two weeks, converting both his field goal attempts and all nine of his PATs. He had missed seven FGs in 10 games, although six of those shanks have come from 50-plus yards out. With the Kansas City offense ramping up its efficiency, Butker's volume is likely to skew more toward extra points, giving him a safer floor at the expense of his ceiling. He'll look to stay locked in during a Week 12 clash with a Bills team that ranks ninth in points per game allowed.

outlooksByWeek.2: Carnell Tate tied for the team lead in receiving yards during his NFL debut, but he had just 38 yards on six targets as Titans QB Cam Ward threw for a meager 140 yards. Tennessee's passing game is likely to struggle again in Week 2 against Philadelphia's excellent secondary, led by cornerback Quinyon Mitchell. Tate is likely to maintain a prominent role on the rebuilding Titans after being drafted fourth overall out of Ohio State, but the rookie WR is hard to trust as anything more than a fantasy WR3 or flex play until Tennessee's offense shows some life.
outlooksByWeek.3: Carnell Tate is off to an uninspiring start, with seven catches for 65 yards on 11 targets through two games with the Titans. A Week 3 road game against the injury-riddled Giants presents a nice opportunity for the rookie fourth overall pick out of Ohio State to break out, as the Giants just allowed 195 receiving yards and two TDs to Rams WR Davante Adams. Tate leads his team in targets through two games, but the Titans have struggled to move the ball through the air. Given Tate's draft pedigree and matchup, he's a high-ceiling fantasy WR3 for Week 3, though it's fair for fantasy managers to be hesitant given the highly touted rookie's lackluster production so far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Carnell Tate has 20 targets through three games heading into the Titans' Week 4 road game against the Ravens, turning that decent volume into a pedestrian 13 catches for 123 yards, averaging 41 yards per game.
