Tennessee's entire passing game is tough to trust given the struggles of QB Cam Ward, but Tate has the most upside among the team's pass catchers. A Week 4 breakout is possible against a Ravens defense that has given up the second-most catches to WRs, especially if the Titans fall behind and are forced to air it out, but Tate can't be trusted as anything more than a flex option until Ward shows signs of progress.
outlooksByWeek.5: Carnell Tate broke out in Week 4 against the Ravens, recording 145 receiving yards after totaling just 123 yards over his first three games for the Titans. The rookie fourth-overall pick has been limited by the struggles of second-year QB Cam Ward, who is averaging just 182 passing yards per game. Tate is likely to match up frequently with top Texans CB Derek Stingley in Week 5, but Stingley and company have allowed the second-most catches (60), receiving yards (830), and touchdown receptions (six) to wide receivers. With Tate trending in the right direction, he's a high-upside flex option for Week 5 as the promising rookie continues to search for his first NFL touchdown.
outlooksByWeek.6: Carnell Tate crashed back down to earth in Week 5, producing just one catch for six yards against the Texans while playing through a back injury after breaking out for a career-high 145 receiving yards against the Eagles in Week 4. Tennessee's fourth overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft will likely remain a boom-or-bust fantasy option throughout his rookie campaign while occupying a starting role in what has been the worst offense in the league. A Week 6 road game against the Colts appears more likely to deliver a peak than a valley, assuming Tate is close to full health, as Indianapolis is giving up 160 receiving yards per game and 15 yards per catch to wideouts. Tate is a high-ceiling Week 6 flex option.
outlooksByWeek.7: Carnell Tate had 70 receiving yards and his first NFL touchdown in Tennessee's Week 6 win over the Colts and broke out for 145 receiving yards against the Ravens in Week 4, but he was held to just six yards by the Texans in between. The rookie, fourth overall pick is still searching for consistency in a Titans passing game that ranks among the league's worst, but Tate has shown enough upside to warrant a lineup spot as a flex option in most formats heading into a Week 7 home game against the Browns. Cleveland has been weaker than league average at defending wide receivers, allowing 157 yards per game and seven TDs in six games to the position.
outlooksByWeek.8: Carnell Tate has recorded at least 69 receiving yards in three of his last four games, establishing himself as a reliable fantasy option despite the ongoing struggles of Titans QB Cam Ward. Facing a Bengals defense that just allowed eight catches for 137 yards and a TD to top Ravens WR Zay Flowers, Tate is a high-end flex option for Week 8. The rookie fourth overall pick is averaging more than seven targets per game and could get plenty of opportunities if the 1-6 Titans fall behind as expected on the road against the 4-2 Bengals.
outlooksByWeek.10: Carnell Tate sat out Tennessee's Week 8 loss to the Bengals prior to a Week 9 bye due to a shoulder injury. The rookie, fourth overall pick is expected to return in Week 10 against the Jaguars and will likely reprise his role as the top option in Tennessee's underwhelming passing offense. Tate racked up at least 69 yards in three of his last four appearances, making him a strong flex play in a game that's likely to feature a negative game script for the 1-7 Titans, leading to more passes. The 6-2 Jaguars are allowing 175 yards per game to WRs, though they have limited the position to four TDs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Carnell Tate hasn't played since Week 7 due to a shoulder injury. Prior to his absence, the rookie fourth overall pick had at least 69 receiving yards in three of his last four appearances. If Tate gets the green light to play in Week 11, he would be a high-end flex option against a Dallas defense that's allowing 158 yards and a TD per game through the air to wide receivers. Titans QB Cam Ward is coming off his two best outings of the season in Tate's absence.
outlooksByWeek.12: Carnell Tate got into his first game action since Week 7 and scored a 59-yard touchdown in his return from a shoulder injury in Week 11 against the Cowboys. His other four targets went for a combined minus-1 yard, and Tate finished third on the Titans in both receiving yards and targets, trailing Chimere Dike and Calvin Ridley. Tate continues to have the highest ceiling among Tennessee's pass catchers, and the team's entire offense has been trending up lately, even though that improvement hasn't translated to wins heading into a Week 12 trip to Jacksonville. This will be Tate's first encounter with a Jaguars defense that's allowing 162 yards per game to WRs but has held the position to five TDs, as he missed the Week 10 meeting between these AFC South rivals. The rookie, fourth overall pick is a solid fantasy WR3 or flex option.

player.seasonOutlook: Tate was selected by the Titans with the fourth overall pick of April's draft. He didn't see a ton of volume at Ohio State, but he was efficient, averaging 13.1 yards per target (first in this rookie WR class) and 3.06 yards per route run (third) in 2025. He also paced the class in YPT for his career (11.6) and caught an impressive 75% of his targets during the 39-game span. Tate underwhelmed in the 40-yard dash at the combine (4.53 at 192 pounds), but he measured in with big hands and a large wingspan. Wide receivers selected in the top 10 handle, on average, one-quarter of their team's targets and generally deliver WR2/3 fantasy production. Cam Ward's development will be key here, but Tate's combination of talent and projected target volume is enough to make him an appealing WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jared Goff will look to build off a season-opener win as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. Goff's performance and Detroit's overall in Week 1 weren't pretty, but he got the job done, finishing with 206 passing yards and two touchdowns. The game also showed that the Lions will continue to have a high-volume air attack, as the veteran ended with 39 pass attempts. Goff will now turn his focus to a Bills defense that ceded 274 passing yards and two touchdowns to C.J. Stroud in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jared Goff will look to keep his high production rolling as the Lions take on the Jets in Week 3. Goff benefited from playing from behind in Week 2 at Buffalo, racking up 327 passing yards and four touchdowns on a 68.4 percent completion rate. The veteran quarterback has now totaled 533 passing yards with a 6:0 TD:INT across his first two games, and Detroit's lacking defense has only helped his output so far. Goff will take on a Jets defense that's allowed a top-10 fantasy points per game (14.2) to quarterbacks in the first two games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jared Goff will continue to benefit from a high-powered offense as the Lions travel to Carolina in Week 4. Goff kept it rolling in Week 3, throwing for 269 yards with two touchdowns and zero interceptions. The veteran quarterback has completed 70.6 percent of his passes for 802 yards and eight touchdowns with no interceptions across three games. He'll face a Carolina defense that's allowed the ninth-most fantasy points per game (23.5) to QBs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jared Goff will remain a high-volume option as the Lions travel to Arizona in Week 5. No matter the outcome of each game so far, Goff has delivered consistent output, and Week 4 against the Panthers was no different. The veteran quarterback recorded season-high totals in completions, pass attempts and passing yards, completing 32 of 52 passes for 412 yards and one touchdown in what was an eventual loss. He's now thrown for 250 or more yards in his last three games, and he's yet to commit a turnover this year. Goff will face a Cardinals defense that's ranked 28th against fantasy quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jared Goff will seek to stay hot as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. Goff recorded another monster performance heading into Detroit's bye week, and he's yet to throw an interception this season. The veteran quarterback has now completed 67 percent of passes for 1,485 yards with 12 touchdowns and zero interceptions in five games. He'll face a Green Bay defense that allowed 258 passing yards and a 1:2 TD:INT ratio to Dak Prescott in Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jared Goff will aim to keep it rolling as the Lions play the Vikings in Week 8. Goff's story stayed the same in a Week 7 win over the Packers, completing 22 of 32 passes for 303 yards and two touchdowns. The veteran quarterback has now passed for 300-plus yards in three of six games, and he's also dished out two or more touchdowns in all but one outing. He'll have his biggest test of the season this week, though, as Minnesota has allowed the fewest fantasy points per game to the quarterback position.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jared Goff will aim to return to dominance as the Lions travel to Miami in Week 9. Goff finished Week 8 against a tough Minnesota defense with his worst fantasy performance of the season, completing 18 of 25 passes for 176 yards with a 1:1 TD:INT. The veteran quarterback still has excellent figures this year with 1,964 passing yards 15 touchdowns and one pick across seven games. He'll face a Dolphins defense that's ranked 26th in fantasy points allowed to QBs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jared Goff will look to return to dominance as the Lions play the Patriots in Week 10. Goff was stuffed again in a narrow Week 9 win over the Dolphins, completing 17 of 25 passes for just 170 yards with zero touchdowns and an interception. The veteran quarterback has now thrown for a disappointing 346 yards and a 1:2 TD:INT in the last two weeks. He'll face a New England defense that ceded 372 passing yards and three touchdowns to Jordan Love in Week 9.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jared Goff will aim to take some momentum into Week 11 as the Lions play the Buccaneers. Goff broke a two-game stretch of struggles in a Week 10 win over the Patriots, completing 65 percent of passes for 303 yards with a 3:2 TD:INT. The veteran has now dished out 18 touchdowns with 2,437 passing yards across nine games this campaign. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked top five in fantasy points allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Jared Goff will look to keep Detroit rolling in Week 12 against the Bears. Goff put together another solid performance in a Week 11 win over the Buccaneers, slinging for 278 yards and two touchdowns. The veteran now sports a 20:4 TD:INT and has thrown for 2,716 yards across 10 games. He'll face a Chicago defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack versus fantasy quarterbacks so far this year and allowed 222 passing yards, one touchdown and one interception to Tyler Shough this past Sunday.

player.seasonOutlook: Goff is entering his 10th NFL season, including his sixth with the Lions. The 2016 No. 1 draft pick has been extremely successful through the air over the past three seasons (4,500-plus yards and 30-plus touchdowns in all three), which has helped him to fantasy finishes of seventh, sixth and ninth. Of course, there's some survivorship bias here, as Goff's per-game finishes during the span are 15th, seventh and 12th. The reason for the limited fantasy output is a lack of rushing, as Goff has never cleared 108 rushing yards in a season and was held to 45 yards in 2025. Playing at his absolute ceiling as a passer and still no more than a fringe QB1, the 31-year-old is just a solid backup/occasional streaming option in fantasy.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tre Tucker was fairly quiet in the Raiders' season-opening win over the Dolphins, catching two of four targets for 27 yards. All three of the team's top wideouts, including Jalen Nailor and Jack Bech, produced very similar numbers, with Bech catching the trio's only TD. The group figures to remain secondary pieces in the passing game as RB Ashton Jeanty and TE Brock Bowers, when healthy, project to be the top weapons for Kirk Cousins and, eventually, Fernando Mendoza. Tucker isn't likely to break out in Week 2 against a Chargers' secondary that finished last season tied for eighth in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tre Tucker produced his first ceiling game of 2026 in the Raiders' Week 2 win over the Chargers. churning out a 5-119-1 line on seven targets. The volatile wideout is showing some early chemistry with new quarterback Kirk Cousins, and no one else has yet shown any indication that they'll be able to challenge him for the top spot on the depth chart, even if Tucker's skill set would be better suited for a WR2 or even WR3 role. Tucker will try to build on last week's effort in Week 3 against a Saints secondary that ranks in the middle of the pack in terms of volume allowed to wide receivers so far, but which has given up three TDs to the position in two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tre Tucker remains in the top spot on the Raiders' wide receiver depth chart, but he's a boom-or-bust option. After popping for a big game in Week 2, Tucker fell back to a 4-43-0 line on just four targets in a Week 3 win over the Saints. With Las Vegas off to a 3-0 start, changes in the offensive mix aren't likely, but Tucker simply doesn't have the physical tools to consistently get open and win 1-on-1 matchups in the NFL. Another rare ceiling game is unlikely in Week 4 against a Kansas City secondary that ranks first in the league in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tre Tucker handled a season-high eight targets in the Raiders' Week 4 loss to Kansas City, but he turned them into just four catches for 44 yards. The fourth-year wideout has reached 50 receiving yards only once in four games to begin the season, producing a 15-233-1 line on 23 targets. With a healthy Brock Bowers back as Kirk Cousins' No. 1 option, Tucker's chances of another ceiling game have shrunk. He'll face a Patriots secondary in Week 5 that ranks 21st in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs and could be without top cornerback Christian Gonzalez.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tre Tucker has hauled in at least four passes in four straight games as the Raiders' top wide receiver, although he plays a clear second fiddle to tight end Brock Bowers in the passing game. Tucker has failed to reach 50 receiving yards in three of those games, and his only touchdown came during his Week 2 eruption against the Chargers. The fourth-year wideout will have a ceiling game once in a blue moon, but his weekly floor is low, at least while Kirk Cousins remains under center instead of rookie Fernando Mendoza. Tucker will try to get enough volume to take advantage of a Week 6 matchup against a Bills secondary that ranks last in the league in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tre Tucker continues to build chemistry with Kirk Cousins. The Raiders' No. 1 wide receiver hauled in two touchdowns in the Raiders' Week 6 loss to the Bills, and through six games Tucker has produced a 24-371-3 line on 35 targets, putting him on pace for his first 1,000-yard effort. Tight end Brock Bowers remains the top option in the passing game, and Tucker has yet to record more than eight targets in a game in 2026. The prospect of Fernando Mendoza replacing Cousins under center at some point offers additional uncertainty for Tucker. He'll have a hard time delivering another ceiling game in Week 7 against a Rams secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tre Tucker is on his way to a career-best season with Kirk Cousins under center for the Raiders. The fourth-year wideout has caught 10 of 19 targets for 200 yards and three touchdowns over the last two games, and through seven contests Tucker sports a 29-474-4 line on 47 targets. Brock Bowers is still the team's top downfield threat, but Tucker is establishing himself as a strong No. 2 option, although the eventual switch at QB to rookie Fernando Mendoza could change things. Tucker will look to keep rolling in Week 8 against a Jets secondary that is tied for 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Tre Tucker put his boom-bust tendencies on full display in the Raiders' Week 8 win over the Jets, failing to catch his only look from Kirk Cousins one week after producing a 5-103-1 line on 12 targets against the Rams. Tucker is Las Vegas' top option at wide receiver, but Brock Bowers is the focal point of the passing attack, and Michael Mayer and Ashton Jeanty get their share of the target volume as well. Tucker is still on pace for a career-best campaign with a 29-474-4 line on 48 targets through eight games, but his floor will always be risky. He'll look to bounce back in Week 9 against a 49ers secondary that ranks 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Tre Tucker caught at least four passes for the seventh time in the last eight games during the Raiders' Week 9 loss to the 49ers, hauling in four of eight targets for 55 yards. The fourth-year wide receiver has been a boom-or-bust option throughout his career, and 2026 is no exception. In his three best performances, he's amassed a 15-319-4 line on 26 targets, but he hasn't reached 60 receiving yards or found the end zone in any of his other six contests. Tucker isn't likely to deliver a ceiling game in Week 10 against a Seahawks secondary that ranks first in the league in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Tre Tucker didn't show much chemistry with Fernando Mendoza in the rookie quarterback's first NFL start, catching just one of two targets for nine yards in the Raiders' Week 10 loss to the Seahawks. He remains the team's top wide receiver, and with Brock Bowers now dealing with an ankle injury, there could be less competition for targets in the short term. Tucker produced a 34-538-4 line on 58 targets through the first nine games of the year, mainly with Kirk Cousins under center. He'll try to establish that kind of rapport with Mendoza in Week 11 against a Broncos secondary that ranks sixth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Tre Tucker has yet to get on the same page as new starting quarterback Fernando Mendoza. Tucker recorded 10 targets in the Raiders' Week 11 loss to the Broncos, but he was able to haul in just two for 50 yards. Meanwhile, Jack Bech posted an 8-88-1 line on nine targets, and he may be making a push to replace Tucker as the team's No. 1 wide receiver. Tucker will attempt to prove he deserves to continue seeing high volume from Mendoza in Week 12 against a Browns secondary that ranks 14th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: A team's No. 1 wide receiver is often a household name, but that's certainly not the case for the underrated Tucker, Las Vegas' top wideout for most of the 2025 season. Tucker has finished in the top 10 among wide receivers in both snaps and routes each of the last two seasons and ranked just outside of the top 30 in targets, catches, yards and touchdowns in 2025. Tucker, who also contributes as rusher, has yet to deliver a top-35 fantasy campaign while working in the Raiders' struggling offenses and would need a terrific rookie season from Fernando Mendoza to get there in 2026. That's a long shot for the undersized receiver, so he's only worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ka'imi Fairbairn remains locked in as a starting fantasy kicker in Week 2, when the Texans host a Bengals team that allowed the third-most points in the NFL last season. Fairbairn led the league in both made and attempted field goals last season. He was limited to one field-goal attempt in Week 1 as the Texans scored four TDs, but the standout kicker showed off his mix of power and accuracy by converting a go-ahead 58-yard field goal in the fourth quarter, though that ultimately wasn't enough to beat the Bills.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ka'imi Fairbairn had a rare miss on a difficult 58-yard field-goal attempt in Houston's Week 2 loss, but he remains one of the NFL's best kickers after leading the league in both made and attempted field goals last season. Fairbairn is locked in as a high-end fantasy starter for a Week 3 road game against a Colts team that has been the NFL's worst defensively. Indianapolis is allowing 37.0 points and 514.5 yards per game, both league highs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ka'imi Fairbairn is just 4-for-5 on field-goal attempts through three games for the 0-3 Texans. It's a less-than-ideal start for the standout kicker, but Fairbairn remains a hold for fantasy purposes considering the Texans bounced back from a 0-3 start last season while supplying Fairbairn with enough opportunities to lead the league in both field goals made (44) and field goals attempted (48) during the 2025 regular season. He has a golden opportunity to break out in Week 4, as the Texans shouldn't have as much trouble moving the ball against the Cowboys, who are allowing 387.0 yards and 27.3 points per game, both of which are among the league's 10 most generous totals.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ka'imi Fairbairn connected on all three of his Week 4 field-goal attempts, improving to 7-for-8 this season. Houston's excellent kicker could be busy in Week 5 against the Titans, whose nine made field goals allowed are tied for fifth-most in the NFL. Fairbairn has established himself as one of the busiest and most accurate kickers in the league, which is an excellent combination for fantasy purposes. He remains a set-and-forget fantasy starter.
outlooksByWeek.6: Ka'imi Fairbairn has connected on all seven of his field-goal attempts over Houston's past two games after going just 4-for-5 through Week 3. He's among the most reliable kickers in the league and can be started with confidence in Week 6 despite a tricky matchup against the Jaguars, who have allowed just seven made field goals and 14.0 points per game through five games. Fairbairn is 55-for-60 on field-goal attempts in 20 regular-season appearances since the start of last season, including a perfect 42-for-42 from inside 50 yards.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ka'imi Fairbairn has missed just one kick all season for the Texans and remains a high-end starting fantasy kicker for Week 7 against the Giants, whose defense is trending in the wrong direction. The Giants allowed just 18.3 points per game through Week 3 but have surrendered 28.3 points per game across their last three, including 34 to the Saints in Week 6. Meanwhile, the Texans have won two consecutive games after starting 0-4, and Fairbairn has made all nine of his field-goal attempts over the past three weeks.
outlooksByWeek.9: Ka'imi Fairbairn connected on multiple field goal attempts in four consecutive games prior to Houston's Week 8 bye. The standout kicker should pick up where he left off in Week 9 against the 0-7 Chargers, who have allowed 14 made field goals in seven games while giving up 25 points per game. Fairbairn has missed just one kick all season and remains a set-and-forget starter at the position. It's worth checking whether Fairbairn was dropped in your league during his Week 8 bye.
outlooksByWeek.10: Ka'imi Fairbairn has made multiple field goals in five consecutive games, going 14-for-14 over that productive stretch. Houston's standout kicker remains a set-and-forget fantasy starter for a Week 10 road game against the Browns, who are allowing 21.8 points per game. Cleveland has allowed 19 made field goals in nine games, while Fairbairn has missed just once on 19 attempts through eight games while making all 21 of his PAT tries.
outlooksByWeek.11: Ka'imi Fairbairn is 19-for-20 on field-goal attempts and 24-for-24 on PAT tries for the Texans heading into a Week 11 home game against the Colts. Indianapolis is tied for the second-most made field goals allowed (21) and is surrendering 27.1 points per game overall. Fairbairn is a set-and-forget fantasy starter at the kicker position, as usual, in Week 11 as the 3-6 Texans try to bolster their dwindling playoff hopes.
outlooksByWeek.12: Ka'imi Fairbairn has missed just one of his 48 kicks this season, going 20-for-21 on field-goal attempts and 27-for-27 on PAT tries. Houston's excellent kicker should get plenty of opportunities at home in Week 12 against the Ravens, who are giving up 26.7 points per game overall and 32.4 points per game over their last five, all of which Baltimore lost. Fairbairn is a set-and-forget fantasy starter in this appetizing matchup.

outlooksByWeek.7: Bam Knight got an extended opportunity in the absence of Jeremiyah Love (ankle) in Week 6 against the Rams and made the most of the situation, notching 15 carries for 80 yards and outplaying Tyler Allgeier, who mustered just 38 rushing yards on 18 rushing attempts. It remains to be seen whether Love will be an option in the backfield in Week 7, as much of that will depend on whether Love is cleared to play, but he's a player worth keeping close tabs on in the event Love isn't 100 percent ready. The matchup is favorable on paper, as the Broncos have given up the sixth-most fantasy points per game to opposing tailbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Bam Knight's status for Arizona's Week 9 battle in Seattle is in question due to a concussion he suffered this past Sunday. The head injury happened when Knight took a shoulder from a Dallas defender to his helmet, and he subsequently entered concussion protocol. He'll need to clear the NFL's concussion protocol before being eligible for game action again, but if he is able to play in Week 9, he could see a decent share of action given that No. 1 RB Jeremiyah Love is dealing with an ankle injury. The Arizona run game could struggle against a Seattle defense that is giving up just 3.28 yards per carry to running backs, though Chicago's D'Andre Swift did just burn the Seahawks for three rushing scores on Monday Night Football.
outlooksByWeek.10: Bam Knight will look to clear concussion protocol in time to play in Arizona's Week 10 matchup against the Rams. Knight missed the team's Week 9 loss to Seattle after being concussed Week 8. If he's able to play against Los Angeles, Knight could have a prominent role in the backfield beside Tyler Allgeier, as Jeremiyah Love is on IR due to an ankle injury. However, the Cardinals' backfield as a whole faces a tough test against a Rams defense that is yielding just 3.55 yards per carry to running backs, fourth-best in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Bam Knight appears set to work in a backfield timeshare with Tyler Allgeier for the Cardinals in Week 11 against Kansas City. Knight returned from a one-game absence to face the Rams this past Sunday, and he logged a 56 percent offensive snap share to Allgeier's 44 percent. However, Knight didn't do much with the opportunity, gaining just 19 yards on five carries and going without a catch on two targets. Both running backs could find the sledding tough against a Kansas City defense that ranks seventh in the NFL with 15.2 fantasy points per game allowed to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Bam Knight appears to be working in a RB timeshare for the Cardinals ahead of a Week 12 clash against the Commanders. Knight logged eight touches for 45 yards in this past Sunday's loss to Kansas City, while Tyler Allgeier finished with seven touches for 23 yards. Neither back has forced his way into a workhorse role, and rookie Jeremiyah Love could be on the verge of returning from an ankle injury, so Arizona's backfield is tough to get a read on at the moment. The team's running game also doesn't have the greatest Week 12 matchup, as Washington ranks in the top half of the league with 16.4 fantasy points per game allowed to running backs so far this year.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mack Hollins will look to capitalize on an elevated role in Week 2 when the Patriots face the Steelers. Hollins caught four of his five targets to open the year, finishing with 51 yards, and could slide into A.J. Brown's (ankle) vacated outside role. Hollins and DeMario Douglas have the trust of Drake Maye, something that can't currently be said for Romeo Doubs, suggesting Hollins will play against a secondary that's without top corner Joey Porter Jr. Hollins' size makes him a capable red zone target, which generates upside.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mack Hollins will seek a bounce back performance in Week 3 when the Patriots face the Jaguars. After a solid four catch, 51-yard opener with A.J. Brown leaving early, Hollins notched only two targets in Week 2. New England's passing game is struggling with Drake Maye completing just 14 passes in Week 2. Until he begins to bounce back, trusting any of his pass catchers appears a risky proposition even against a defense that is allowing a generous 10.3 yards per target.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mack Hollins will look to lead the Patriots' receiving corps in Week 4 against the Bills. Hollins gathered a season-high nine targets in Week 3, following just seven total in the team's first two games, as the Patriots continue to search for a top option without A.J. Brown (ankle) available. Drake Maye is struggling to move this offense, but Week 4 offers the potential to match the Bills' high-scoring offense. Buffalo is allowing the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing receivers and an enticing 9.2 yards per target.
outlooksByWeek.5: Mack Hollins' availability for Week 5 against the Raiders is in doubt due to a calf injury. Hollins has been a steady but unspectacular piece for the Patriots' receiving corps, going for 51 or more yards three times despite topping five targets just once with A.J. Brown sidelined by an ankle injury. Las Vegas can be vulnerable to opposing receivers, surrendering 70 or more yards four times. Efton Chism filled in after Hollins' early Week 4 exit and would likely do so again if Hollins does not suit up.
outlooksByWeek.10: Mack Hollins' opportunities for the Patriots in Week 10 against the Lions appear unsettled with A.J. Brown (knee) potentially returning to action. Hollins returned from a four-week absence in Week 9, catching half of his six targets and finding the end zone for the first time all season. While Detroit's secondary has been picked on often and allows 8.0 yards per target, Hollins doesn't have a clear path to heavy volume, leading to big-play or touchdown dependency.
outlooksByWeek.12: Mack Hollins is slated for an uptick in opportunity but with sketchy quarterback play when the Patriots face the Chargers in Week 12. He hauled in five catches for 48 yards in Week 10 despite losing Drake Maye on the opening drive and Tommy DeVito completing just 12 passes for 81 yards in relief. It's unlikely that DeVito airs it out, but with A.J. Brown (hamstring) likely out and the Chargers allowing 13 touchdowns and 9.1 yards per target to opposing wideouts, Hollins could surprise.

player.seasonOutlook: Anthony Campanile's defense was one of the most surprisingly productive of 2025, finishing fifth in fantasy points, and the team was fortunate to get him back for this year. That said, the team had modest sack and fumble recovery numbers, and it did lose LB Devin Lloyd and CB Greg Newsome over the offseason. Fantasy managers can still freely select this defense, knowing it has one of the best opening-week matchups by hosting the Browns, but they'll likely need to swap them out for Weeks 2 through 6 (@DEN, NE, @CIN, PHI, HOU).

outlooksByWeek.2: Samaje Perine and the Bengals travel to face the Texans for a Week 2 tilt. He was highly efficient with his touches in the season-opening win, tallying five carries for 20 yards while catching all three targets for 30 yards. Perine was the only other running back to record a carry, so his status as the No. 2 RB is not in question. Houston's defense is tied for third in fantasy points allowed per game (10.5) to RBs, but it surrendered 409 total yards of offense in their Week 1 loss to the Bills.
outlooksByWeek.3: Samaje Perine and the Bengals travel to take on the division-rival Steelers in Week 3. After dealing with an illness that forced him to miss two days of practice, he was active in Week 2 and recorded two carries for six yards and caught his lone target for 16 yards during Cincinnati's win over the Texans. With backfield mate Chase Brown handling 23 total touches, Perine's limited involvement on offense makes him a solid fantasy insurance policy, but nothing more. Pittsburgh's defense ranks 28th in rushing yards (233) and 29th in receiving yards allowed (97) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Samaje Perine and the Bengals play host to the Jaguars in Week 4. He rushed three times for nine yards and caught one of three targets for five yards during Cincinnati's 30-27 Week 3 loss. Lead back Chase Brown handled 13 carries, so Perine is firmly established as the No. 2 option and primary passing-down option out of the backfield. Jacksonville's defense ranks seventh in fantasy points allowed (17.2) to RBs, and it has surrendered just one rushing TD to the position through three contests.
outlooksByWeek.5: Samaje Perine and the Bengals are on the road to take on the Dolphins in Week 5. He tallied three carries for seven yards and failed to bring in his only target during Cincinnati's Week 4 defeat. Perine's offensive snaps and involvement continue to fluctuate as the clear back behind Chase Brown, even despite his team playing from behind more recently. Miami's defense ranks last in fantasy points (29.7) allowed to RBs, but Perine should remain on fantasy benches.
outlooksByWeek.7: Samaje Perine and the Bengals travel to take on the 4-2 Ravens in Week 7. He rushed 14 times for 68 yards and caught both of his targets for 10 yards and a TD during Cincinnati's Week 5 victory. Perine out-carried starter Chase Brown (13) and was much more efficient, as Brown managed just 39 yards on the ground. If Brown continues to struggle, Perine could have a larger role than initially anticipated at the beginning of the campaign. However, it might be wise to wait until we know more about the backfield hierarchy following the matchup against Baltimore's seventh-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (18.6) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Samaje Perine and the Bengals host the 1-6 Titans in Week 8. He had four carries for 16 yards and a one-yard touchdown but was not targeted during Cincinnati's Week 7 victory. The Bengals' backfield has been tricky with Chase Brown struggling as of late, and it looks like it could be headed toward more of a timeshare than initially thought at the start of the year. Perine will try to continue building momentum against the Titans' 19th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (22.3) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Samaje Perine and the Bengals travel to Spain for a Week 9 clash against the Falcons. He rushed four times for 10 yards and caught his only target for nine yards during Cincinnati's overtime victory in Week 8. Perine played 33% of the offensive snaps but was unable to produce much on a day the Bengals put up a season-high 43 points. He'll aim to get more involved against an Atlanta defense that ranks 30th, giving up 28.1 fantasy points per game to opposing RBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Samaje Perine and the Bengals host the Steelers on Sunday Night Football in Week 10. He rushed 11 times for 43 yards and was not targeted during Cincinnati's 34-17 victory in Week 9. Perine played 42% of the offensive snaps compared to 62% for Chase Brown, although their workloads were much closer, with the latter out-touching the former 12-11. As it stands, with the Bengals lighting up opponents through the air, fantasy managers should find it difficult to trust either running back.
outlooksByWeek.11: Samaje Perine and the Bengals travel to take on the Commanders in Week 11. He rushed six times for 14 yards and a touchdown and caught all four targets for 25 yards during Cincinnati's Week 10 victory. Perine watched as Chase Brown produced 83 yards and two TDs on 18 touches, with both backs helping the Bengals win a fifth straight game. Perine has been valuable to Cincinnati's offense, but his limited role doesn't offer fantasy upside with Brown still atop the depth chart.
outlooksByWeek.12: Samaje Perine and the Bengals return home to host the 3-7 Saints in Week 12. He had six carries for 26 yards and caught all four targets for 71 yards during Cincinnati's Week 11 defeat. Perine finished with one fewer touch than starter Chase Brown, but Perine was much more productive. Perine could be a sneaky fantasy play versus a New Orleans defense allowing 28.5 fantasy points per game (31st) to opposing RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Perine is expected to resume his role as Chase Brown's primary backup in Cincinnati. The veteran back played 31% of the Bengals' snaps last season, totaling 84 carries and 21 targets. He cleared 400 total yards for the fifth consecutive season, though he has yet to reach 200 touches in a single season in his career, nor has he produced a top-30 fantasy campaign. The 30-year-old has reached double-digit fantasy points three times over the last two seasons and would require a Brown injury in order to flirt with flex appeal. He can be left on waivers.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brandon Aubrey was surprisingly quiet in Week 1 for the Cowboys versus the Giants. With New York dominating time of possession, Aubrey did not even attempt a field goal. He also missed one of his extra points when Javonte Williams was assessed a taunting penalty following a touchdown, leading to a 48-yard PAT try. Aubrey has nowhere to go but up in Week 2 versus the Commanders, though. Washington allowed 26.5 points per game just a season ago, which was 27th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brandon Aubrey connected on all three of his field goals last game for Dallas, including a 60-yarder. Aubrey also booted four extra points, shaking off a surprising miss in Week 1 versus the Giants. In Week 3, the Cowboys clash with the Ravens. Baltimore is allowing 23.5 points per tilt, which is in the middle of the pack so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brandon Aubrey connected on three field goals and two extra points last game for Dallas, but his missed three-pointer will likely be the most talked about boot. Aubrey was blocked from 59 yards out, a makeable distance for the strong-legged kicker, and the Cowboys lost to the Ravens by that margin. However, Aubrey has made six field goals in the last two games, and remains a standout option kicking for one of the top offenses in the league. In Week 4, Dallas will face a disappointing Houston squad allowing 25 points per contest, which is 19th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Brandon Aubrey missed two field goals last game for Dallas. Such a sensational headline needs explanation, though, as both of Aubrey's misses came from over 60 yards away. Aubrey had a 62-yarder blocked, and missed a 65-yarder wide left. Otherwise, Aubrey connected on two field goals from 50 yards and in, while also making all four of his extra points. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay squad allowing 24.0 points per clash, which is tied for 19th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Brandon Aubrey did not have much work last game for Dallas. Aubrey connected on one field goal and one extra point in the dismal 24-16 loss to the Bucs. Aubrey has made just nine field goals through five games for Dallas, which is tied for 10th in the league. In Week 6, the Cowboys face the Packers. Green Bay is allowing 22.4 points per tilt, which is tied for 15th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Brandon Aubrey managed one single, solitary extra point last game for Dallas. The Cowboys offense has sputtered of late, scoring a combined 29 points over the last two contests. Aubrey has registered just one field goal and two PATs over that span. In Week 7, Dallas will look to right the ship against another struggling NFC East squad, the Philadelphia Eagles. Philadelphia is allowing 22.8 points per tilt, which is 16th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: Brandon Aubrey connected on three field goals and three extra points for Dallas last game. Unfortunately, Aubrey also missed a kick from 50-plus yards out, and the Cowboys ended up losing to Arizona by three points in overtime. Still, Aubrey has now made three field goals and three extra points in each of the last two games for the Cowboys. A tasty matchup lurks in Week 9 versus the folding Colts. Indy is allowing 27.8 points per clash, which is 30th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Brandon Aubrey missed yet another long field goal last game for Dallas. Aubrey did make two other tries, though pulled a 50-yarder wide left in the 27-23 win over the Colts. Aubrey is now 3-for-8 on attempts from 50-plus yards out this season. In Week 10, the Cowboys will face the 49ers. Points may be hard to come by, as San Fran is allowing just 19.5 points per tilt, which is sixth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.11: Brandon Aubrey connected on two field goals and two extra points for the Cowboys in the 46-40 loss to the 49ers. Aubrey did miss an extra point, his second of the season. However, both of Aubrey's field goals came from 50-plus yards out, giving him five such field goals on the season to date. In Week 11, Dallas will face a bumbling Titans squad. Tennessee is allowing 26.6 points per contest, which is 27th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.12: Brandon Aubrey made one field goal and six extra points last game for the Cowboys. Dallas destroyed Tennessee by a score of 51-30, though all the touchdowns left Aubrey with only a modest kicking performance. In fact, it was the first time in five outings that he failed to kick multiple field goals in a single game. In Week 12, Dallas will face division rival Philadelphia. The Eagles are allowing 23.7 points per tilt, which is 18th in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.2: Matthew Stafford and the Rams will look to bounce back from a rough season-opening loss when they face the Giants in Week 2. Stafford threw for just 155 yards with no TDs and one interception against San Francisco last Thursday. He did still manage to connect with favorite target Puka Nacua five times for 74 yards, but no other Rams pass catcher had more than 26 yards in the defeat. A matchup with the Giants awaits, but New York had good results against Dallas' passing game in Week 1, holding QB Dak Prescott to 175 yards with one interception, albeit with two TDs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Matthew Stafford will look to replicate a huge Week 2 performance when the Rams face Denver in Week 3. On Monday Night Football, Stafford threw for 327 yards and four touchdowns with one interception against the Giants. The reigning NFL MVP didn't have star wideout Puka Nacua (hip) for that contest, so he turned to veteran Davante Adams, who logged eight catches for 195 yards and two of Stafford's TDs. Denver could pose a more potent threat, as the Broncos have a talented secondary and have limited QBs to a 74.5 passer rating, fifth-best in the NFL, through two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Matthew Stafford will look to help guide the Rams to a much-needed win in Week 4 against Philadelphia following a disappointing 1-2 start to the season. Stafford threw for 390 yards and two touchdowns in Week 3 against Denver, but he also tossed two costly interceptions, including a pick-six. The reigning NFL MVP already has four interceptions on his ledger through three contests after logging just eight interceptions across 17 regular-season games last year. The Eagles have yet to pick off a pass this year, and they just got torched by Bears QB Case Keenum for 247 passing yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.5: Matthew Stafford will look to clean things up in the turnover department when the Rams host Buffalo in Week 5. Stafford was picked off twice and didn't throw any touchdowns in Week 4 against Philadelphia, but he also threw for 317 yards and led Los Angeles to a comeback victory. Still, Stafford has recorded a mediocre 6:6 TD:INT through four games, with the pickoff total nearly reaching the eight interceptions he tossed across 17 regular-season contests during his MVP campaign last year. The Bills have given up 10 passing touchdowns and have picked off just two passes this year, so Week 5 may be a good opportunity for Stafford to get back on track.
outlooksByWeek.6: Matthew Stafford will look to help Los Angeles rebound from a crushing loss on Monday Night Football with a Week 6 matchup against Arizona. Stafford threw for 383 yards and three touchdowns in Week 5 against Buffalo, but the team was defeated in overtime. Still, it was an impressive showing for the reigning NFL MVP, as he posted his fourth consecutive effort of 300-plus passing yards. Stafford could be in for another big performance versus a Cardinals defense that has given up the second-highest passer rating (117.2) this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Matthew Stafford enters the Rams' Week 7 matchup against the Raiders having completed 164 of 249 passes for 1,794 yards, 11 touchdowns and six interceptions through six games. The veteran quarterback is averaging 299 passing yards per contest, but his production has been inconsistent, and Los Angeles has stumbled to a 2-4 record. The absence of Davante Adams, who is expected to miss six to 10 weeks with a hamstring injury, creates another obstacle for Stafford. However, Las Vegas has allowed the sixth-most fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season, making Stafford an appealing bounce-back candidate despite the Rams' recent offensive struggles.
outlooksByWeek.8: Matthew Stafford continues to put up prolific numbers for the Rams heading into a Week 8 matchup versus the Chargers. The reigning NFL MVP threw for 195 yards and three touchdowns against Las Vegas in Week 7, though he also tossed his seventh interception. Stafford has now compiled over 300 passing yards and/or multiple passing touchdowns in all but one game so far this season, and he leads the league with 1,989 total passing yards. The Chargers could at least offer some resistance, as they've allowed a modest 18.6 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season, ninth-best in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Matthew Stafford will try to help the Rams move above .500 for the first time this season with a win in Week 9 against Washington. Stafford was pretty quiet against the Chargers this past Sunday, throwing for just 157 yards with one touchdown and one interception, but his performance was good enough to lead his team to a second straight victory. The veteran quarterback continues to rely heavily on star wideout Puka Nacua with Davante Adams (hamstring) expected to remain sidelined for multiple more games. Stafford has a prime matchup against the Commanders, who have given up the third-most fantasy points per game (24.6) to quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Matthew Stafford will have to operate without his favorite target in the Rams' Week 10 tilt against Arizona. Puka Nacua, who Stafford has targeted at least 10 times in five of his past six games, has a knee injury that is expected to require a stint on IR. The Rams are also still without Davante Adams (hamstring - IR), so Stafford will have to look to other wideouts, as well as the tight-end corps, more often moving forward. He'll at least have a promising matchup in Week 10, as the Cardinals have allowed the third-most fantasy points (23.9) to quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Matthew Stafford emerges from the Rams' bye with the prospect of facing Green Bay in Week 12 still without either of his two top wideouts. Davante Adams (hamstring) isn't expected to come off IR this week, and Puka Nacua (knee/toe) is slated to miss the remainder of the campaign. Stafford was able to guide Los Angeles to a win without both stars in Week 10 against Arizona, throwing for 249 yards with three touchdowns and one interception, but he'll likely face a tougher challenge this week. Whereas the Cardinals rank 30th in the NFL in fantasy points per game allowed to quarterbacks, the Packers sit at a very respectable eighth in that category.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning NFL MVP, Stafford returns for his 18th NFL season and his fifth with the Rams. The 38-year-old is fresh off an elite season in which he led the NFL in passing yards and touchdowns, which allowed him nine top-10 fantasy weeks (tied for third most at the position). Stafford's third-place finish in fantasy points per game was his first top-10 finish since 2019, and some regression is likely due to a complete lack of rushing (65 or fewer rushing yards in five straight seasons and one rushing touchdown since 2017). Stafford still has receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams and a strong offensive line at his disposal, so another big passing season is possible. That's just enough to keep him in the fringe QB1 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: Blake Corum was one of few Rams players to have a good game on offense in their season-opening loss, and he'll look for more success in Week 2 against the Giants. Corum led Los Angeles with 54 rushing yards on just 10 carries versus San Francisco last Thursday, averaging 5.4 YPC after putting up an average of 5.1 YPC during the regular season last year. Kyren Williams remains the Rams' lead back, but there's little doubt that Corum has forced his way into a substantial role as well. The Giants held Dallas' No. 1 RB Javonte Williams to 3.4 YPC on 12 totes in Week 1, though Williams did score a rushing TD and put up a 5-31-1 line through the air.
outlooksByWeek.3: Blake Corum should continue to be a big part of the Rams' backfield versus the Broncos in Week 3. Against the Giants on Monday Night Football, Corum racked up 79 yards on 12 carries while adding a 13-yard reception. Through two weeks, Corum has 22 carries to Kyren Williams'  23, so the pair appear to be headed for a pretty even workload in 2026. Denver could be vulnerable to both ball carriers, as the Broncos have given up a whopping 5.40 YPC to RBs this season -- third worst in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Blake Corum will look to bounce back following a quiet Week 3 performance when the Rams visit Philadelphia in Week 4. Corum was held to season-low marks of six carries and 15 yards this past Sunday versus Denver while Kyren Williams put up 158 total yards. Though some expected Corum to challenge Williams for touches even more this season, the latter has emphatically cemented his No. 1 RB role with his strong early-season performance. Both Corum and Williams may need to rely on their work on the ground against the Eagles, who have given up the fewest receiving yards to running backs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Blake Corum will aim to rebound from a pair of quiet games when the Rams host the Bills in Week 5. After after averaging 66.5 rushing yards in Los Angeles' first two games, Corum has totaled just 29 yards on the ground over his past two contests. He's been quite inefficient with his carries, logging just 2.6 yards per carry on his 11 totes while Kyren Williams has dominated backfield touches. Buffalo has given up six TDs to running backs this season, but three have come through the air. That's not Corum's forte -- he has just four catches for 20 yards with no scores as a receiver through four weeks.
outlooksByWeek.6: Blake Corum's role as a ball carrier seems to fading ahead of the Rams' Week 6 game versus Arizona. Corum rushed just five times for 19 yards Monday against Buffalo, marking his third straight contest with six or fewer carries after averaging 11 totes across the first two weeks. However, Corum did score his first TD of 2026 and had easily his best game this season as a receiver against the Bills, catching three passes for 53 yards. Given his recent downturn in carries, Corum may need to get into the end zone to come away with serviceable fantasy production, but the Cardinals have given up only four total TDs to running backs through five weeks this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Blake Corum has developed into a legitimate complementary option in the Rams' backfield to star tailback Kyren Williams, rushing 47 times for 223 yards and a touchdown while adding nine receptions for 91 yards and another score through six games. His 4.7 yards per carry almost equals Williams' 4.9 mark, but the main difference is the touches, as Corum is averaging just 7.8 carries per game compared to Williams' 13.3. Still, Corum faces an encouraging Week 7 matchup against the Raiders, who have surrendered 19.6 fantasy points per game to RBs in 2026, the ninth-worst mark in the NFL.His limited receiving involvement and secondary role make him a touchdown-dependent flex option rather than a dependable weekly starter.
outlooksByWeek.8: Blake Corum is coming off his biggest workload of the campaign with the Rams' Week 8 matchup versus the Chargers on tap. After entering Sunday with fewer than 10 carries in four straight contests, Corum rumbled for 93 yards and a touchdown on a season-high 17 totes against the Raiders. Backfield mate Kyren Williams equaled Corum with 18 touches and figures to continue to lead the team's backfield, but Corum certainly reminded fantasy managers that he's worth consideration even in the No. 2 RB role. Both Corum and Williams could find room to run against a Chargers defense that ranks 21st in the league with 4.19 yards per carry allowed to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Blake Corum should continue to have a big role in the Rams' backfield in Week 9 against the Commanders. Corum logged five fewer carries than backfield make Kyren Williams this past Sunday versus the Chargers, but Corum led the team with 73 rushing yards and also scored a touchdown for the fourth straight contest. After taking fewer than 10 totes four straight weeks, Corum has averaged 14 carries across his past two contests and seems to have regained his role as Los Angeles' 1B option next to Williams' 1A role. Washington has been pretty tough on running backs so far this season, tying for 10th in the league with 15.5 fantasy points allowed per game to the position.
outlooksByWeek.10: Blake Corum continues to get a hefty share of work out of the Rams' backfield heading into a Week 10 visit to Arizona. Corum led Los Angeles with 58 rushing yards and scored a touchdown on 11 carries in a Week 9 win against Washington. Though he remains marginally behind Kyren Williams in the Rams' backfield, Corum has logged double-digit carries in three straight games and has scored in each of those contests. There could be an opportunity for both Corum and Williams to succeed against a Cardinals defense that is giving up 99.6 rushing yards per game to RBs, ranking 19th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.12: Blake Corum will look to build on a season-best performance when the Rams host the Packers in Week 12. Corum rumbled for a season-high 100 rushing yards and a touchdown in Week 10 against Arizona while adding three catches for 19 yards. He should be fresh with Los Angeles having been on bye in Week 12, and Corum could be even more important than usual if backfield mate Kyren Williams' sore toe inhibits him at all. Both ball carriers could be productive against a Green Bay defense that ranks 26th in the NFL with 21.1 fantasy points per game allowed to RBs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Corum has spent his first two NFL seasons as Kyren Williams' backup, and that's expected to be the case again in 2026. The 2024 third-round NFL draft pick played well in the role last season, averaging a healthy 5.1 yards per carry (seventh among RBs) and scoring six touchdowns on 145 carries. However, Corum played only 29% of the Rams' snaps and remained a nonfactor as a receiver (36 yards on 14 targets). The 25-year-old has no standalone fantasy value, but he's an elite insurance stash, as he'd launch into the fringe-RB1 mix in the Rams' high-powered offense should Williams miss time.

outlooksByWeek.2: A.J. Brown won't suit up for at least four weeks for the Patriots, beginning in Week 2 against the Steelers, after landing on injured reserve due to a high-ankle sprain. Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas and Mack Hollins figure to be New England's top three wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.7: A.J. Brown will continue shaking off some rust when the Patriots face the Bears in Week 7. Returning from a four-week absence due to an ankle injury, Brown amassed 10 targets in Week 6 but finished with just three catches for 27 yards while struggling with drops. With New England's passing game operating at a high level, featuring 10 touchdown passes in three weeks, Brown should have ample opportunity for a breakout performance against a Chicago secondary that's allowing 9.8 yards per target to opposing wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.8: A.J. Brown will look to get on track when the Patriots face the Dolphins in Week 8. Brown has caught three passes in each of his three outings for his new squad, failing to score or top 48 receiving yards. While Miami has surrendered 14 touchdown passes overall, only three have gone to wide receivers, resulting in the second-fewest fantasy points allowed despite an appealing 8.8 yards per target. Brown may still be a week away from a breakout in his new uniform.
outlooksByWeek.9: A.J. Brown's availability for the Patriots' Week 9 game against the Packers is uncertain due to lingering knee and ankle injuries. Brown was a late-week addition to the injury report with a knee issue that has seemingly persisted since last season, in addition to an ankle problem that previously cost him four games. When healthy, Brown has been targeted regularly but has struggled with drops, posting a season-high 48 yards in Week 7. Should he play, he'll face a Packers defense that has allowed the sixth-fewest fantasy points to opposing receivers but has been vulnerable to their opposition's top option, allowing 70 or more yards six times.
outlooksByWeek.10: A.J. Brown will look to return from a two-week absence when the Patriots face the Lions in Week 10. Limited to just three games thus far, Brown amassed 16 targets in his last two outings and figures to again draw heavy volume if healthy. In a game where the Patriots could be down their top two running backs, a pass-heavy shootout appears possible, setting Brown up for a big game against a Lions secondary that's allowing 8.0 yards per target to opposing wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.12: A.J. Brown seems unlikely to play in Week 12 when the Patriots face the Chargers due to lingering hamstring issues. Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams could see elevated roles, but with Tommy DeVito under center, all will be volatile options.

player.seasonOutlook: Brown was traded to the Patriots in June. The veteran receiver enters 2026 looking to continue his streak of finishing in the top 15 in fantasy points per game during each of the four seasons he was with the Eagles. That includes an 11th-place finish in 2025 in which Brown reached the 1,000-yard mark for the sixth time in his seven NFL seasons while finding the end zone exactly seven times for the third year in a row. Brown continues to benefit from elite usage (he has finished no lower than seventh among WRs in target share each of the past seven seasons) and elite efficiency (he has finished 80th percentile or better in yards per route run all seven years). He could use more end zone targets in New England (he had a career-low four last season), but Brown, 29, is set to work as Drake Maye's top target in a good Patriots' offense. He is a fringe fantasy WR1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Romeo Doubs will seek a larger role in the Patriots' passing game in Week 2 against the Steelers. Doubs failed to record a catch on three targets in his team debut, playing only 56% of the snaps despite New England losing A.J. Brown to a high-ankle sprain. With Brown set to miss significant time, Doubs should garner more opportunities, but it looks as though he's still developing chemistry with Drake Maye. Questions remain regarding the Steelers' secondary, which is likely to remain without Joey Porter Jr. They weren't tested last week, but counting on a breakthrough from Doubs is risky.
outlooksByWeek.3: Romeo Doubs will look to build on Week 2's uptick in workload in the Patriots offense when they face the Jaguars in Week 3. After not catching a pass in his Week 1 debut, Doubs snagged three of four targets for a team-high 96 yards in Week 2. New England's passing game is sputtering, and despite A.J. Brown missing the last game and a half, Doubs has not logged heavy volume. Jacksonville's secondary was just beaten for 138 yards by Jaylen Waddle, but otherwise, has held up with only one touchdown to opposing wideouts. Until his opportunities increase, Doubs presents a risky profile.
outlooksByWeek.4: Romeo Doubs' workload remains minimal for the Patriots ahead of their Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Despite A.J. Brown's absence (ankle), Doubs has just 11 targets through three weeks. He's averaging a robust 24.2 yards per reception, and the Bills are allowing a big 9.3 yards per target to opposing wideouts. With Drake Maye struggling, gambling on a few Week 4 chunk plays is risky.
outlooksByWeek.5: Romeo Doubs has an ascending role in the Patriots' passing game ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Raiders. He collected a season-high nine targets in Week 4, and while it resulted in just six catches and 58 yards, he found the end zone twice. Las Vegas will rush the passer, which has troubled Drake Maye. The secondary is allowing 8.2 yards per target to wideouts, so Doubs can capitalize on whatever volume he receives.
outlooksByWeek.6: Romeo Doubs' opportunities have been limited through five games, with the Patriots hosting the Jets in Week 6. After recording nine targets in Week 4, Doubs hauled in just one of three looks in Week 5, giving him three or four targets in four of the first five games with his new team. Though the Jets have been statistically stout against the pass, allowing just 195.4 yards per game, they've allowed five opposing wide receivers to post at least 58 yards in as many games. With Drake Maye spreading targets around, Doubs' ceiling is low, making him a fringe flex option.
outlooksByWeek.7: Romeo Doubs was placed on the injured list after injuring his shoulder while making a diving touchdown catch in Week 6. The Patriots expect him to return following their Week 11 bye. While Doubs is out, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism, and Kyle Williams should log more targets.

player.seasonOutlook: Doubs signed with the Patriots during free agency after spending his first four NFL seasons with the Packers. He was a serviceable player during his Green Bay tenure, but he never finished a season in the top 30 among receivers in targets, catches, yards or fantasy points. Consistently mediocre, Doubs has averaged either 10.2 or 10.3 fantasy PPG each of the last three seasons. In New England, Doubs is likely to settle in as Drake Maye's No. 2 target behind A.J. Brown, though his target ceiling figures to be capped with the likes of DeMario Douglas, Mack Hollins and Kyle Williams also in the mix at receiver. Doubs, 26, is a fine addition to your bench, but his upside is limited.

outlooksByWeek.2: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain an important part of the Saints' offense in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Vele saw nine targets in the Week 1 overtime loss, tying his career high and trailing only Chris Olave in the Saints' receiving corps. Vele should continue to benefit from the absence of Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) and is expected to see consistent volume until Tyson returns. It'll be a tough Week 2 matchup for Vele, however, as the Ravens' defense has given up just 4.8 yards per pass attempt this season, which is tied for the second-best mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain the Saints' No. 2 wideout in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders, whose defense has given up just 15 receptions to WRs through two contests. Vele has clearly positioned himself as one of New Orleans' top receiving options early in the season, catching 12 of 16 targets for 133 yards and one touchdown thus far. He's expected to continue benefitting from the Saints' high volume of pass attempts, as Tyler Shough has already thrown the ball 90 times in two games, the second-most in the NFL. Despite this, Vele is in for a difficult Week 3 matchup against a Las Vegas defense that has yet to allow a receiving touchdown this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Devaughn Vele is likely to remain the Saints' second option at wideout in the Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. While Jordan Tyson (hamstring) has been sidelined, Vele has been very fantasy-relevant, catching 15 of 22 targets for 172 yards and a touchdown (12.7 PPR points per game). Vele has almost no competition outside of Chris Olave in the Saints' WR room, which bodes well for his fantasy outlook going forward. Additionally, New Orleans' offense is averaging 44 pass attempts per game, which suggests Vele will continue having scoring opportunities. He's in for a favorable Week 4 matchup, as Atlanta's defense has allowed 604 receiving yards to wideouts this season, the most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain very involved in the Saints' offensive game plan in the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Vele has been targeted 30 times (second-most on the team) through New Orleans' first four contests this season, logging 226 receiving yards and a pair of touchdowns. With Tyler Shough averaging a whopping 45 pass attempts per game this season, Vele will likely remain a solid fantasy option as the year progresses, at least until the return of Jordyn Tyson (hamstring, IR). However, Vele is in for a difficult Week 5 matchup against a Minnesota defense that's allowed just 7.7 yards per target to opposing WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain one of the Saints' top receiving options in the Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Vele was quiet in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings, catching four of six targets for just 26 yards. He still ranks second on the Saints in targets (36) and receiving yards (252) through five contests, which is a positive sign for his outlook moving forward. Vele could thrive in Week 6 against a Giants defense that's already allowed five touchdowns to opposing WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain New Orleans' No. 2 wideout in the Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. Vele has been relatively quiet over the last two weeks, catching seven of 12 targets for 68 yards. Despite this, he's played over 90% of the Saints' offensive snaps in the last two contests, suggesting more fantasy production is coming soon, especially if New Orleans continues throwing the ball at such a high clip (39.2 pass attempts per game -- fourth-most in the NFL). Vele could struggle against a strong Steelers defense in Week 7 though, as they've allowed just 6.1 yards per pass attempt this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain the Saints' No. 2 wideout in the Week 9 matchup against the Browns. Vele has recorded over 50 receiving yards in four of seven appearances this season, ranking second on the team in yards (348), targets (46) and receptions (33). He's expected to continue benefitting from head coach Kellen Moore's high-volume passing attack, as Tyler Shough currently leads the NFL with 39.0 pass attempts per game. Vele could struggle in Week 9, however, as Cleveland's secondary has allowed just 10.1 yards per completion this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain one of New Orleans' top wideouts during the Week 10 matchup against the Panthers. With the debut of 2026 first-round pick Jordyn Tyson in the Week 9 overtime win over the Browns, Vele caught just two of four targets for 17 yards, which are all season-lows in a single game. Even with Tyson on the field, Vele should remain a valuable part of the Saints' offense, but he likely won't be as consistent for fantasy purposes for the remainder of the year. Vele could still be productive in Week 10 against an injury-riddled Carolina secondary that's allowed 7.4 yards per target to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Devaughn Vele is expected to operate as the Saints' No. 3 wideout during the Week 11 matchup against the Bears. Since 2026 first-round pick Jordyn Tyson returned from injury in the Week 9 win over the Browns, Vele has caught just four of six targets for 31 yards. It appears as if his role on New Orleans' offense has diminished, suggesting his fantasy value is limited without scoring a touchdown on a weekly basis. He's set to face a solid Chicago secondary in Week 11 that's given up just eight receiving touchdowns to wideouts through nine games this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain one of the Saints' top wideouts during the Week 12 matchup against the Bengals. Vele delivered a much-needed bounce-back performance during the Week 11 loss to the Bears, catching all seven of his targets for 76 yards. Despite playing behind Chris Olave, Vele appears to be a valuable portion of this New Orleans' offense and will likely compete for the No. 2 WR role with rookie Jordyn Tyson as the season progresses. Vele is still expected to struggle in Week 12 against a tough Bengals secondary that's given up just 10.2 yards per completion through nine games this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Vele is expected to open the season as New Orleans' No. 2 receiver behind Chris Olave until Jordyn Tyson returns from injury near midseason. Vele's first season with the Saints was marred with injuries. The 2024 seventh-round pick, who posted a 41-475-3 receiving line with Denver as a rookie, barely played throughout most of 2025 prior to taking on an every-down role during Weeks 10-15. In those five games (one of which he left hurt), he averaged 5.6 targets per game, but reached 12.0 fantasy points once (an 8-93-1 effort in Week 13 against Miami). The 28-year-old has yet to show he can be relied on for consistent targets and fantasy production, but he'll play an every-down role early on, which makes him a sleeper for flex value in deep leagues. He'll be worth a roster spot until Tyson returns.

outlooksByWeek.2: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers hope to improve to 2-0 when they visit the Patriots in Week 2. He secured all five targets for 46 yards and Aaron Rodgers' lone passing TD, and finished second on the team in receiving yards while tying for first in receptions. Freiermuth led Pittsburgh's TEs in offensive snaps (49), but Darnell Washington was a close second with 43. He and the Steelers will try to scheme up a way to beat a New England defense that is tied for second in receiving yards allowed to the position (13).
outlooksByWeek.3: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers play host to the Bengals for an AFC North clash in Week 3. He paced the team's tight ends in snaps (46), receptions (4), yards (32) and targets (5) during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to the Patriots. Freiermuth appears to have the upper hand over Darnell Washington (1-7-0) in the passing game, but his fantasy floor and ceiling are relatively low in an underwhelming Steelers offense. He'll have the added benefit of facing a Cincinnati defense that allows 18.5 fantasy points per game to TEs (27th) and just got torched for 12 receptions and 140 yards by Dalton Schultz.
outlooksByWeek.4: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 4 AFC North clash against the Browns. He caught two of four targets for 30 yards and rushed once for one yard during Pittsburgh's Week 3 victory. Aaron Rodgers continues to spread the ball around, as six different Steelers receivers registered at least four targets, and four tied for the team lead in receptions with three. Freiermuth could be a sneaky play versus a Cleveland defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points allowed (14.9) to TEs and gave up eight receptions (on 12 targets) for 92 yards to the position in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers welcome the Colts to town for a Week 5 home tilt. He played 75% of snaps on offense and caught three of five targets for 17 yards and his second touchdown of the season. Fellow tight end Darnell Washington (3-27-1) was slightly more productive while playing 70% of the offensive snaps during Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss in Week 4. They're both listed as starting tight ends for the Steelers, and it looks like it'll be a toss-up between the two on any given week as long as they're healthy. Indianapolis allows 13.7 fantasy points per game to TEs, which ranks 17th.
outlooksByWeek.6: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers visit the Buccaneers for an interconference clash in Week 6. He played 38 snaps on offense (70%) and was highly productive, catching five of seven targets for 44 yards and two of Aaron Rodgers' three TD passes during Pittsburgh's Week 5 victory. Freiermuth finished third on the team in receptions and yardage, while his seven looks were the second-most. Fellow starting tight end Darnell Washington was on the field for 34 offensive snaps (63%) and caught two of three targets for 12 yards. Freiermuth recorded a second consecutive outing with a score and now has four TDs on the season, and he'll aim to take advantage of a Tampa Bay defense allowing 15.7 fantasy points per game (22nd) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers travel to Paris to take on the Saints in Week 7. He caught two of three targets for 11 yards during Pittsburgh's 26-19 comeback win in overtime in Week 6. Freiermuth and fellow tight end Darnell Washington each played 71% of snaps on offense, but it was the latter who made the bigger impact in this one, as Washington tallied a 4-25-1 line on six targets. Freiermuth will try to rebound versus a New Orleans defense that just surrendered six receptions for 99 yards and a TD to Isaiah Likely.
outlooksByWeek.8: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers return home to host the Browns for an AFC North showdown in Week 8. He caught two of four targets for 20 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 7 win in Paris. Freiermuth played 34 offensive snaps to fellow TE Darnell Washington's 36, but the two have been essentially neck-and-neck in playing time through seven outings this season. Freiermuth will aim to stand out versus Cleveland's 20th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (13.9) to the position.
outlooksByWeek.10: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers travel to Cincinnati for an AFC North showdown in Week 10. He caught both of his targets for 35 yards and rushed once for a one-yard touchdown during Pittsburgh's Week 8 victory. Freiermuth finished second on the team in yardage and accounted for one of three rushing TDs despite playing only 53% of the offensive snaps. Over his last three contests, he strung together a 6-66-0 receiving line on nine targets to go along with his one-yard TD run, securing two receptions in each outing. Freiermuth could struggle to hit paydirt for the sixth time this season in a matchup versus a Bengals defense that's given up only one score to opposing TEs through eight games.
outlooksByWeek.11: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers visit the Eagles for an in-state showdown in Week 11. He caught two of three targets for 35 yards and one touchdown during Pittsburgh's Week 10 loss, making it two straight outings with a score. Freiermuth fought hard to break the goal line on his 27-yard TD reception, even with his team down big in the fourth quarter. He played 53% of the offensive snaps compared to 50% for Darnell Washington, so snap counts have essentially been a coin flip between the two tight ends. Freiermuth is a tough sell for fantasy managers in a matchup versus Philadelphia's defense, as they're tied for the fourth-fewest points allowed per game (10.5) to opposing TEs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers battle the Broncos at home on Black Friday in Week 12. He caught all five targets for 39 yards and rushed once for one yard during Pittsburgh's Week 11 loss. Freiermuth has recently been more involved on offense than fellow tight end Darnell Washington as Washington finished with a 3-22-0 line on three targets. Freiermuth remains a TD-or-bust fantasy option and he'll face a Denver defense that's allowed the third-most receiving yards (702) and eight TDs (T-27th) to opposing TEs in 2026.

player.seasonOutlook: Freiermuth's career trajectory has been quite the head-scratcher, but the bottom line is he is yet to emerge as a consistent fantasy starter. The 2021 second-round pick flirted with TE1 status in both 2022 (11th in fantasy PPG) and 2024 (14th) but saw a dramatic dip in usage in Pittsburgh's crowded tight end room in 2025. Freiermuth posted a career-low 10% target share and finished outside the top 20 at the position in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards and end zone targets, and 30 tight ends bested his 6.7 fantasy PPG. The 27-year-old figures to play more in 2026 with Jonnu Smith gone and Mike McCarthy running the offense, but Pittsburgh is also better at wide receiver with Michael Pittman Jr. and Germie Bernard in the fold. Freiermuth has some sleeper appeal, but he's best valued as a back-end TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rhamondre Stevenson will look for a heavier workload when the Patriots face the Steelers in Week 2. Stevenson notched 23 touches to open the year, and despite the potential return of TreVeyon Henderson (ankle), Stevenson should handle early-down work at a minimum. He's mainly an accumulator, averaging 4.0 yards per carry or less in two of the previous three seasons and just 2.8 to open 2026. But volume is king, and Stevenson likely has that since he also catches passes out of the backfield. Pittsburgh was vulnerable in Week 1 to receiving backs, plus Stevenson likely handles goal-line work, making him intriguing even in a difficult spot against a defense that allowed 3.8 yards per carry to open the year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rhamondre Stevenson's opportunities are questionable as the Patriots prepare for the Jaguars in Week 3. After a 23-touch season debut, Stevenson lost a fumble early in Week 2, an issue that's plagued him throughout his career, and ended with just seven touches. In a split backfield with Treveyon Henderson, New England will likely ride the Week 3 hot hand. Facing a defense that hasn't allowed an opposing rusher to go over 39 yards, both backs could be running uphill.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rhamondre Stevenson's role in the Patriots offense is declining ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the Bills. The return of TreVeyon Henderson limited Stevenson to 13 rushes in Weeks 2 and 3, and unfavorable game flow and poor quarterback play are limiting his receiving opportunities. Buffalo is allowing the fifth-most fantasy points per game to opposing backs, but more receiving touchdowns (three) than rushing (two). Without certainty for double-digit touches, Stevenson comes with risk against a defense allowing a frugal 3.9 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.5: Rhamondre Stevenson continues to share work in the Patriots backfield ahead of an inviting Week 5 matchup against the Raiders. He amassed 13 carries in Week 4, one fewer than TreVeyon Henderson's 14, but Stevenson found the end zone while catching three passes for the third time in four weeks. Las Vegas is allowing 4.97 yards per carry and was just solved by Kansas City's Kenneth Walker for 177 yards, so while split work will limit Stevenson's ceiling, his continued involvement as a pass-catcher paired with double-digit carries can result in fantasy-worthy production in Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rhamondre Stevenson could garner workhorse carries in the Patriots' Week 6 match against the Jets with TreVeyon Henderson dealing with an ankle issue.
