Stevenson had 13 carries in Week 5 for the second straight week and now has double-digit carries in three of five games while adding at least three catches four times. With double-digit touches seemingly certain, Stevenson can exploit a defense that's allowing 4.3 yards per carry and one where he posted 102 yards and two touchdowns on only 13 touches last season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Rhamondre Stevenson hasn't had much room to run for the Patriots in advance of a Week 7 clash with the Bears. Stevenson has logged double-digit carries in four of his first six games but is averaging a career-low 3.7 yards per carry while sharing time with TreVeyon Henderson, who surprisingly played in Week 6 despite a high-ankle sprain. Chicago has allowed only three rushing scores, and no opposing runner has topped 61 yards since Week 3, so while volume will remain Stevenson's friend, he'll likely need to find the end zone to provide fair returns.
outlooksByWeek.8: Rhamondre Stevenson's role in the Patriots' passing game will keep him active in Week 8 against the Dolphins. While he is coming off his third single-digit carry game of the season, he's caught at least three passes in five games and five in two outings, an area where Miami's defense is particularly vulnerable. The Dolphins allow a moderate 4.3 yards per carry and just three rushing touchdowns to backs, yet have given up 34 catches, including five touchdown receptions, to running backs in six games. Stevenson has multiple paths to meaningful production.
outlooksByWeek.9: Rhamondre Stevenson will look to lead the Patriots backfield again in Week 9 against a stingy Packers defense. Stevenson earned double-digit touches in seven of New England's first eight games and has at least 13 carries in four of his last five contests, despite sharing backfield touches with TreVeyon Henderson and Corey Kiner. Green Bay has allowed 10 rushing touchdowns through eight games, which Stevenson may need for solid Week 9 production, as the Packers are allowing just 3.96 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.10: Rhamondre Stevenson is uncertain to suit up for the Patriots in Week 10 against the Lions due to a knee injury. New England fell into a big hole in Week 9, limiting Stevenson's carries prior to the injury, and he finished with a season-low six for the third time this season. His passing game involvement included a second touchdown reception in three weeks. If he plays, Stevenson figures to again lead the Patriots' backfield since TreVeyon Henderson will also likely be sidelined. Stevenson's rushing yard expectations can be tempered against a defense that's allowing a mere 3.9 yards per carry. Corey Kiner would be in line for lead back duties assuming both Stevenson and Henderson are sidelined.
outlooksByWeek.12: Rhamondre Stevenson could see heavy volume for the Patriots in Week 12 against the Chargers, with Tommy DeVito unlikely to spark the passing game. Emerging from a Week 11 bye, Stevenson can hopefully avoid an injury designation after a knee issue limited him to 36 yards on 12 carries over his last two outings. Facing a stacked front, Stevenson will rely on volume to beat a defense that's allowing 4.1 yards per carry and 10 touchdowns to backs in as many games, landing him in RB2/flex territory.

player.seasonOutlook: Stevenson will battle with second-year back TreVeyon Henderson for touches in the New England backfield. The duo shared the backfield at times last season, but it was the veteran Stevenson who usually operated as the lead back. He earned the role, ranking fifth among backs in forced missed tackle rate, per PFF, second in yards after contact (2.82) and first in yards per target (9.1). Stevenson, who is entering his sixth season, did miss three games (he has missed time three seasons in a row), and his overall volume was limited (9.3 carries and 2.7 targets per game), which led to a 25th-place finish in fantasy points. Now 28 years old and with Henderson still very much in the mix, Stevenson, who has one top-20 fantasy campaign to his name, is a low-upside bench option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ryan Flournoy managed two catches for 22 yards on four targets in the Week 1 loss for Dallas to the Giants. Flournoy finished fourth on the team in targets for the game. The Dallas passing attack struggled as a whole, leaving no receiver with more than 45 yards receiving in the contest. In Week 2, the Cowboys will look to rebound versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ryan Flournoy managed six targets last game for Dallas. Flournoy parlayed those looks into five catches for 23 yards. Flournoy was third in targets behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ryan Flournoy tied for the second on the Cowboys in targets last game. Flournoy saw eight balls thrown his way, though managed just two catches in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens. Flournoy also gained just 22 yards for the game; in fact, he has yet to gain more than 25 yards in any contest in 2026. In Week 4, Dallas faces a Houston defense that has been surprisingly subpar against the pass.  The Texans are allowing 238.7 passing yards per clash, which is 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ryan Flournoy has been targeted at least four times in every game this season for the Cowboys. However, he has yet to cross 40 yards receiving in any contest. Versus the Texans, he had four catches but only for a season-high 37 yards. With a lot of mouths to feed like CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and even tight end Jake Ferguson, Flournoy's output may continue to be depressed. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league. Flournoy is still looking for his first score of the season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Ryan Flournoy set a season high in receiving yardage last game for the Cowboys. Flournoy brought in three passes for 90 yards in the 24-16 loss to the Bucs. CeeDee Lamb was dealing with a quadriceps issue, which also likely contributed to Flournoy's success. However, Lamb's injury does not appear serious, which would knock Flournoy back down the pecking order in Week 6 versus the Packers. Green Bay's defense is also allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered only six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ryan Flournoy found the end zone last game for Dallas. Flournoy reeled in seven passes for 40 yards and the score in the 23-13 loss to the Packers. Flournoy has at least four targets in every game this season, though has gone over 40 yards receiving just once. He remains firmly behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens heading into a Week 7 clash with Philly. The Eagles are allowing 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL. However, Philadelphia has given up just eight passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 14th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Ryan Flournoy was second on the Cowboys in receiving yards last game. Flournoy reeled in four passes for 70 yards in the 38-21 win over the Eagles. Flournoy has at least three catches in four-straight contests. In Week 8, the Cowboys will face an Arizona Cardinals defense that has been prone to surrendering the touchdown pass. In fact, Arizona has given up 17 passing scores, which is dead last in the NFL. The Cardinals are also giving up 228 passing yards per tilt, which is 20th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Ryan Flournoy could not take advantage of the absence of George Pickens last game for Dallas. Despite Pickens being sidelined with a hamstring issue, Flournoy managed his fewest catches since Week 3. He finished with just two grabs for the contest, though did gain 53 yards total on the receptions. While Pickens may be shelved for Week 10 as well, Flournoy will face a difficult task versus the San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 211 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just 11 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for seventh in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Ryan Flournoy has scored in three of the last five contests for the Cowboys. Flournoy has caught at least two passes in every game this season, and has drawn at least four targets in all but one contest. In Week 11, Flournoy has a tasty matchup against the Titans. Tennessee is allowing 266.9 passing yards per tilt, which is dead last in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: Ryan Flournoy was not invited to the party last game for the Cowboys. While CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens each had over 100 yards receiving and a touchdown in the win over the Titans, Flournoy caught just one pass for 11 yards. It was his lowest output of the season. In Week 12, Flournoy will look to get back on track versus a mediocre Eagles pass defense. Philadelphia is allowing 222.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 17th in the NFL. However, the Eagles have only given up 14 passing touchdowns, which is tied for ninth in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Flournoy is an intriguing deep sleeper as the favorite for No. 3 wide receiver duties behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens in Dallas. Flournoy flashed in 2025, putting up 14.2 fantasy PPG during the only five games in which his route participation was at least 60%. Flournoy did disappear quite a bit behind the heavily targeted Lamb and Pickens (three or fewer targets in seven of his final 10 games), so he's a long shot for standalone fantasy value even if he locks down the No. 3 gig. The 26-year-old should be added to rosters only if Lamb or Pickens are sidelined.

The Texans led the league with 13 weeks as a top-10 scoring defense, allowed the fewest yards and second-fewest points and totaled the third-most interceptions and seventh-most sacks, last season. Edge rushers Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter and cornerback Derek Stingley were among five Pro Bowlers from their roster, which largely returns the same personnel for 2026. The Texans make a compelling case to be the first D/ST picked, with one caveat: Their tricky September schedule includes the Bills (Week 1), Bengals (2) and Cowboys (4) and will probably demand fantasy managers seek fill-ins for those matchups.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jakobi Meyers maintains a high floor, though he's a low-ceiling fantasy WR3 or flex play for Jacksonville's Week 2 home game against Denver's elite defense. Meyers has posted at least 39 receiving yards in all 10 of his games with the Jaguars since coming over in a midseason trade last year, including 40 receiving yards and a TD in the Week 1 win over Cleveland. Parker Washington and Brian Thomas have more downfield playmaking capability, but Meyers should see his share of short targets with Trevor Lawrence likely looking to get the ball out quickly to counter a Broncos pass rush that led the league with 68 sacks last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jakobi Meyers has been targeted just three times through Jacksonville's first two games. That lack of volume makes him hard to trust as anything more than a deep-league dart throw in Week 3 against a Patriots defense that held the Seahawks and Steelers to a combined 16 points. Parker Washington (18 targets), Brian Thomas (11 targets), and even TE Brenton Strange (five targets) have all been higher on Trevor Lawrence's priority list than Meyers. To the veteran wide receiver's credit, Meyers's 28-yard effort on one target in the Week 2 loss to Denver marked the first time in 11 games as a member of the Jaguars that he failed to record at least 39 receiving yards. Therefore, he could rebuild a solid fantasy floor if Lawrence starts looking Meyers's way more frequently.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jakobi Meyers led the Jaguars with seven catches for 64 yards and a touchdown on eight targets in Week 3 against the Patriots after catching all three of his targets for 68 yards and a TD across Jacksonville's first two games. The veteran wideout has been playing alongside Parker Washington in two-WR sets and working ahead of Brian Thomas, as Meyers' 79% snap share this season is nearly double Thomas' mark. Washington is the clear No. 1 receiving option for the Jaguars, but Meyers is shaping up as the team's next-most reliable pass catcher, which is enough to be deployed as a WR3 or flex option in Week 4 against the Bengals, who didn't allow a touchdown pass through Week 2 before giving up TDs to three separate Steelers wideouts in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jakobi Meyers has been efficient with his opportunities for the Jaguars, catching 13 of 15 targets for 165 yards and two touchdowns heading into a Week 5 trip to London to face the Eagles. His usage has fluctuated in a Jacksonville passing game with many mouths to feed, but Meyers is a viable flex option for Week 5, especially in deeper leagues. The Eagles are giving up 164 yards and one receiving touchdown per game to WRs, and they could be without top CB Quinyon Mitchell (knee) in Week 5, which would make things easier for some combination of Meyers, Parker Washington, Brian Thomas, and Josh Cameron.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jakobi Meyers is averaging 40 yards per game and has scored twice through five outings heading into Jacksonville's Week 6 matchup with the Texans in London. Houston has struggled to cover wide receivers, having allowed 193 yards per game and six TDs to the position through five games. Meyers is a distant second on the WR depth chart behind Parker Washington, but the plus matchup makes Meyers a viable flex option.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jakobi Meyers has established himself as the No. 2 WR for the Jaguars behind Parker Washington, putting Meyers firmly in the fantasy flex conversation for a Week 8 home game against the Colts. Meyers is averaging 48 receiving yards on 4.7 targets per game, and he set season highs in both of those categories with 83 yards on 10 targets in Jacksonville's Week 6 loss to the Texans prior to a Week 7 bye. The veteran wideout faced the Colts three times last season. Two of those meetings came after Meyers was acquired by the Jaguars in a midseason trade, and he mustered exactly 39 receiving yards in both games while scoring a touchdown in one of those matchups. He has five TDs in 15 regular-season games with Jacksonville.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jakobi Meyers was held to two catches in Week 8 while playing through a hamstring injury. He has had an up-and-down season for the Jaguars while working as the No. 2 WR behind Parker Washington. The Jaguars visit the Ravens on Thursday in Week 9, so Meyers may not have time to regain health on a short week. The injury risk lowers his floor, but he's a passable flex option against a Ravens defense that's giving up 177.6 yards per game to wideouts. Meyers is averaging 3.1 catches for 44.1 yards per game, with two TDs in seven outings.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jakobi Meyers is a strong Week 10 flex play against a Titans defense that has struggled to cover wide receivers. Tennessee is allowing a league-high 15.3 catches for 195 yards per game to the position. Meyers has had an up-and-down season as Jacksonville's No. 2 WR but has trended in the right direction recently, notching two of his three best performances this season for both receiving yards and targets within the last three games. He's more likely to produce a peak than a valley in the first of Jacksonville's two meetings this season against Tennessee's league-worst secondary.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jakobi Meyers ranks second on the Jaguars behind Parker Washington in both receiving yards (408) and targets (43), but the gap between Washington and Meyers is far larger than the gap between Meyers and TE Brenton Strange for the role of Trevor Lawrence's No. 2 target. Meyers has exceeded 65 yards just once all season and hasn't scored since Week 3, so he has been a disappointment more often than not for fantasy managers plugging him into a flex spot. He'll have a decent opportunity to end his six-game touchdown drought in Week 11 against a Giants secondary that has allowed WRs to score 11 times in nine games, though the Giants hold wideouts to just 127 yards per game. As usual, Meyers is a fine deep-league flex but not a player to get particularly excited about.
outlooksByWeek.12: Jakobi Meyers has drawn at least six targets in four of Jacksonville's last five games, reaching 10 targets twice over that span. His decent volume as the Jaguars' No. 2 WR makes Meyers an appealing Week 12 flex option against Tennessee's league-worst secondary, which is allowing an average of 16 catches for 210 yards per game to wide receivers. Meyers turned six targets into just three catches for 34 yards in Week 10 at Tennessee, but he's capable of producing a more impressive stat line in this home rematch as he tries to snap a TD drought that dates back to Week 3.

player.seasonOutlook: One of the league's most underrated players, Meyers is entering his first full season with Jacksonville after being acquired via trade in November. The 2019 UDFA has produced 800-plus receiving yards in five consecutive seasons while operating primarily as a short-to-intermediate target. More of a solid producer than a high-ceiling contributor, Meyers has finished no lower than 32nd in fantasy points over the last five seasons, but has yet to do better than 19th. The 29-year-old isn't much of a touchdown scorer (23 TDs in 78 games since 2021) and has substantial target competition via Parker Washington, Brian Thomas Jr., Brenton Strange and Travis Hunter. Meyers is a good player, but is likely to cap out as a flex option.

outlooksByWeek.2: George Pickens was held to just 28 yards in the season opener for the Cowboys. Pickens did finish second on the team in targets with six, but was rather quiet still by his standards. Despite a porous secondary, the Giants kept the star wideouts for the Cowboys in check, leaving Pickens with an uninspiring output in Week 1. Pickens will look to rebound in Week 2 versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: George Pickens was second on the Cowboys in targets last game.  Pickens managed six catches for just 40 yards, though, as CeeDee Lamb went wild for Dallas. Lamb caught eight passes for 153 yards and two touchdowns in the win over Washington. Pickens has a disappointing nine catches for only 68 yards through two games for Dallas. The task may not get easier in Week 3, as Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: George Pickens is coming off his best game of the season for the Cowboys. Pickens led Dallas in targets with 11 opportunities, parlaying those looks into seven grabs for 82 yards in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens. However, Pickens has yet to find the end zone this season, and his overall numbers remain disappointing following a standout 2025 campaign. In Week 4, the Cowboys will face a Texans defense that has been surprisingly suspect against the pass in 2026.  Houston is allowing 238.7 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the NFL. Moreover, teammate CeeDee Lamb could be guarded by all-pro corner Derek Stingley Jr., which could free up Pickens for more targets.
outlooksByWeek.5: George Pickens has had back-to-back games with at least 75 yards receiving for the Cowboys. On the downside, Pickens was targeted just three times last game as compared to a staggering 21 targets for fellow wideout CeeDee Lamb. The targets are unlikely to be so lopsided in Week 5 versus the Bucs, but Pickens certainly appears to be playing second-fiddle to the aforementioned Lamb in 2026. Tampa Bay's defense has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: George Pickens stepped up last game for the Cowboys. CeeDee Lamb was limited to two catches for just nine yards as he was dealing with a quadriceps issue. As a result, Pickens was the primary target in the passing game and corralled nine of 13 targets for 130 yards and a touchdown.  Lamb is not expected to miss the Week 6 clash versus the Packers, though Pickens would benefit even if Lamb is limited. However, Green Bay's defense is allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered only six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: George Pickens led the Cowboys in receiving last game. With the Cowboys trailing for the entire contest, the passing game took center stage, though admittedly still struggled. Despite 11 looks, Pickens managed just 73 yards on six catches in the 23-13 loss to the Pack. Pickens has an impressive 24 targets over his last two contests alone. He will look to get back over the 100-yard receiving mark in Week 7 versus Philadelphia. The Eagles are allowing 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL. However, Philadelphia has given up just eight passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 14th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: George Pickens found the end zone last game for Dallas. Pickens snagged four passes for 57 yards and the touchdown. It was his second score in three outings. In Week 8, the Cowboys will face an Arizona Cardinals defense that has been prone to surrendering the touchdown pass. In fact, Arizona has given up 17 passing scores, which is dead last in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: George Pickens was held to just 48 yards receiving last game for Dallas. This was his lowest receiving total since the second week of the season. Pickens has just 10 targets combined over the last two games and was seen leaving the field early following the OT loss to Arizona, meaning there could be trouble in paradise. In Week 9, Dallas will face a Colts defense allowing just 211.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 12th in the NFL. However, Indianapolis has given up 14 passing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: George Pickens did not suit up last game for Dallas due to a hamstring ailment. His status for Week 10 versus the 49ers remains up in the air. Even if Pickens is able to play, he will face a difficult task. The Niners are allowing just 211 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just 11 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for seventh in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: George Pickens snagged three touchdowns last game for the Cowboys. Pickens racked up an incredible 18 targets, parlaying those looks into 11 grabs for 145 yards and the three scores. The targets and receptions set career highs, while the yardage total was his best on the season. In Week 11, Pickens has a delectable matchup against the Titans. Tennessee is allowing 266.9 passing yards per tilt, which is dead last in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: George Pickens crossed the 100-yard threshold yet again for the Cowboys last game. Pickens caught seven passes for 102 yards and a touchdown in the 51-30 dismantling of the Titans. Pickens has gone over the 100-yard receiving mark in two-straight contests, having scored a gaudy four touchdowns during that span. In Week 12, the Cowboys will face a mediocre Eagles pass defense. Philadelphia is allowing 222.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 17th in the NFL. However, the Eagles have only given up 14 passing touchdowns, which is tied for ninth in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Pickens drew the franchise tag from Dallas after a career year in which he ranked near the top of the wide receiver position in most categories, including catches, yards, TDs, end zone targets (second with 18) and air yards (fourth with 1,576). Fantasy's No. 5-scoring receiver in 2025 certainly benefited from CeeDee Lamb missing time (24% target share, or 8.8 per game, and 24.2 fantasy PPG in four games Lamb was injured), but his "with Lamb" splits were also strong. Consider: In 12 full games with Lamb, Pickens handled a 23% target share (8.3 per game) and averaged 16.1 fantasy PPG, which would've ranked eighth at the position over the full season. The 25-year-old will play the same role in Dallas' high-scoring offense in 2026 and has the look of a strong fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: D'Andre Swift will aim to replicate a huge game as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Swift was dominant against the Panthers in Week 1, carrying the ball 18 times for 124 yards and three touchdowns. The veteran ball carrier topped any of his games in the 2025 season, showcasing that he should also benefit from a higher-scoring Chicago offense this year. He'll play a Minnesota defense that shelled Green Bay on the ground in their opener, but he has established himself more than the Packers' current RB room.
outlooksByWeek.3: D'Andre Swift will be a top option in Chicago's offense in Week 3 against the Eagles. Swift cooled down in Week 2 after a monster opener, logging 16 rushes for 45 yards on the ground. The veteran RB did see success in the passing game, logging five catches for 54 yards. With Tyson Bagent expected to start at quarterback for the Bears, Swift could be utilized more heavily on the ground. Philadelphia has also allowed 216 rushing yards to running backs this season, a bottom-10 mark in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: D'Andre Swift should remain Chicago's top option in the rushing game against the Jets in Week 4. Swift saw a season-high 20 carries in Week 3 versus Philly , taking them for 84 yards and adding on two catches for four yards. The veteran ball carrier eclipsed 80 rushing yards in two of the first three games of the campaign, but he's seen his only end zone appearances come from Week 1. He'll now turn his attention to a Jets defense that ceded 99 rushing yards and two touchdowns off 20 carries to Jahmyr Gibbs in their most recent outing.
outlooksByWeek.5: D'Andre Swift will seek to get back on track as the Bears travel to Green Bay in Week 5. Swift rushed the ball 15 times for 58 yards and caught two targets for 16 yards against the Jets in Week 4, but he also lost a fumble and was stopped at the goal line twice. The veteran was outplayed by his younger counterpart, Kyle Monangai, who posted a 30-146-2 rushing line. Either way, Swift should still get plenty of usage against a Packers defense that's ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to running backs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.6: D'Andre Swift could be in line for a featured role once again as the Bears play the Falcons in Week 6. Swift should have benefited hugely from Kyle Monangai being out with a toe injury in Week 5, but he rushed nine times for 43 yards and a touchdown and caught four passes for 30 yards in a blowout loss. The status of Monangai remains up in the air ahead of Chicago's away bout, and Swift's value is very much contingent on his position mate's status. Atlanta has ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy RBs so far.
outlooksByWeek.7: D'Andre Swift could see his workload take a hit as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Swift was inefficient on the ground in Week 6 with 16 carries for 44 yards, but he was able to salvage his outing with two rushing touchdowns and four catches for 26 yards. The veteran has benefited from Kyle Monangai being out the last two weeks with turf toe, especially given that three of his six touchdowns this season have come in that stretch. Whether Monangai plays or not, Swift will face a New England front that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy RBs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: D'Andre Swift's role will be up in the air heading into Week 8 as the Bears travel to Seattle. Swift produced once again in Week 7, tallying 22 rushes for 78 yards and a touchdown, along with catching four passes for 12 yards. The veteran has benefited from a workhorse role with Kyle Monangai (toe/thumb) out the last three weeks, finding the end zone four times and averaging over 19 touches per game in that stretch. Monangai could be in line to return this week, but the pair of running backs have proven to both hold value even when both active. Either way, Swift will face a Seahawks defense that's ranked top 10 in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs (15.4).
outlooksByWeek.9: D'Andre Swift will look to build on a high-volume performance as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Swift was, for the most part, stymied by a tough Seattle front in Week 8, averaging just 2.6 yards per carry, but he still put together a monster game with three touchdowns and 69 yards off a season-high 27 rushes. The veteran has directly benefited from the absence of position mate Kyle Monangai in the last four weeks, which can especially be seen through his seven touchdowns in that stretch. With or without Monangai active, Swift should have a tough time, especially if he can't find the end zone, against a Tampa Bay front that's ranked first in fantasy points allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.11: D'Andre Swift will look to bounce back from a tough showing as the Bears play the Saints in Week 11. Swift was shelled by a tough Tampa Bay front before Chicago's Week 10 bye, rushing the ball 12 times for 31 yards. The veteran still racked up seven touchdowns in the preceding four games without Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) out, so there is still hope for him to deliver moving forward. Even if Monangai returns, New Orleans ranking 31st in fantasy points allowed to running backs could allow for an entire backfield to eat.
outlooksByWeek.12: D'Andre Swift will aim to continue to lead Chicago's running game in Week 12 at Detroit. Swift remained the top running back in a Week 11 win over the Saints even with Kyle Monangai back from a turf toe injury. Swift's 15 touches easily outweighed Monangai's eight touches, but it wouldn't be crazy if the Bears ramped up the younger running back in the upcoming away matchup. Swift will look to build on a career-high 11 touchdowns versus a Lions defense that's ranked fifth in fantasy points allowed to running backs.

player.seasonOutlook: Swift is entering his seventh NFL season and third with Chicago. The veteran back was busy as both a rusher and receiver en route to clearing 1,300 scrimmage yards in each of his first two seasons with the Bears. Though he found the end zone 10 times and finished 17th among backs in fantasy points per game last season, Swift deferred substantial work to Kyle Monangai and is likely to be in even more of a timeshare in 2026. Still in his prime at age 27, Swift continues to play at a high level (4.87 yards per carry last season), but his role in the Chicago offense figures to limit him to low-ceiling RB2/flex production.

outlooksByWeek.2: Justin Jefferson will look to keep it rolling in Week 2 as Minnesota takes on the Bears. Jefferson returned to a fantasy level in Week 1 that he didn't see much of in 2025, reeling in eight of nine targets for 92 yards and two touchdowns. The star wideout also had a solid connection with veteran Carson Wentz, who came in for an injured Kyler Murray (concussion). Given that Jefferson still produced with the Vikings' QB2, he could be in line for big games no matter who lines up under center, so long as it isn't J.J. McCarthy. He'll face a Chicago defense that allowed the fourth-most PPR points to Panthers wide receivers (46.3) in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Justin Jefferson will look to rebound from a quieter week as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Jefferson was held to three catches for 55 yards against the Bears in Week 2, but the game was played in bad weather and ended with a 9-3 score. The superstar pass catcher has 11 catches for 147 yards and two touchdowns this season, and he could increase those numbers twofold against a Bucs defense that ceded 95 yards and a touchdown to Cleveland receiver Denzel Boston this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.4: Justin Jefferson will look to return as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. Jefferson exited Week 3 against the Buccaneers with an ankle injury, but there don't appear to be any concerns beyond a sprain at this point. The star wideout has totaled 13 catches for 179 yards and two touchdowns on the season even in just five halves, and he's been a major piece of Minnesota's 3-0 start. If he is healthy, Jefferson will face a Miami defense that's ranked top-five (24.2 fantasy points per game) against wide receivers this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.5: Justin Jefferson will aim to make a return for Minnesota's Week 5 clash at New Orleans. Jefferson sat out of the Vikings' Week 4 win over the Dolphins with an ankle injury, but the hope is that his absences will be limited to that game. The star pass catcher has totaled a quieter 13-179-2 receiving line over his first two-plus games, so he'll look to make a bang if he does return to action. The Saints have ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs so far this season, which could provide everything Jefferson needs to deliver.
outlooksByWeek.7: Justin Jefferson remains Minnesota's top target in Week 7 against the Colts. Jefferson put together a solid performance against the Saints in Week 5 before the Vikings' bye, recording six catches for 79 yards and a touchdown. The star pass catcher looks to have a solid connection with quarterback Kyler Murray, which could be even more solid after a week of rest. Indianapolis ceded a 6-70-1 receiving line to Titans' WR1 Carnell Tate in Week 6, which could bode well for Jefferson.
outlooksByWeek.8: Justin Jefferson will look to get back in the end zone as the Vikings play the Lions in Week 8. Jefferson had a quiet performance out of the bye in Week 7, reeling in four of seven targets for 44 yards, which was his second-lowest yardage total of the year. The star wideout has now pieced together a 23-302-3 receiving line across five games this season. He'll have plenty of chances to carve up a Detroit secondary that's ranked 26th in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Justin Jefferson will aim to ramp up his output as the Vikings play the Bills in Week 9. Jefferson brought in five of nine targets for 33 yards and a touchdown in Week 8 against the Lions, finding the end zone for the fourth time this season. The superstar wide receiver is on pace to finish the season with the fewest catches and yards of his career, and he's yet to record a 100-yard receiving game. Luckily, he'll face a Buffalo defense that's ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to WRs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.10: Justin Jefferson will hope to see better play at the QB position in Week 10 as the Vikings travel to Green Bay. Jefferson reeled in just three of his whopping 11 targets for 58 yards in a Week 9 loss to the Bills. The all-out struggles of Carson Wentz, who filled in for an injured Kyler Murray (hamstring), were fully seen in Jefferson's receiving line, but the trade deadline acquisition of Kirk Cousins re-united him with the QB he's had the most success with. The talented wideout doesn't have any 100-yard games and has posted less than 60 yards in five of seven games. Jefferson will face a Packers defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to the wide receiver position this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Justin Jefferson could be in store for better output again as the Vikings play San Francisco in Week 11. Jefferson benefited from the addition of Kirk Cousins to Minnesota in a Week 10 win over Green Bay, logging season highs in catches (9) and targets (13). The star wideout's 74 yards were also his best total since Week 5, further supporting that he may be in store for a return to dominance. He'll take on a 49ers defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.12: Justin Jefferson will look to get back in the end zone as the Vikings play the Falcons in Week 12. Jefferson has benefited greatly from the reintroduction of Kirk Cousins in the last two weeks, totaling 16 catches for 142 yards in that stretch. The star pass catcher has now put together a 47-553-4 receiving line over nine games, which could be greatly improved in the coming weeks if he keeps a strong connection with Cousins. He'll shift his attention to an Atlanta defense that's ranked 25th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: After finishing in the top 10 among receivers in fantasy PPG during each of his first five seasons, Jefferson plummeted to 30th in 2025. The fall was, of course, unrelated to Jefferson's ability, as the team's quarterback woes limited the star receiver to career-low showings in yardage (1,048), touchdowns (two), catch rate (60%) and yards per target (7.4). Jefferson's fall came despite him seeing a career-high 30.1% target share and ranking in the top six at the position in targets (141) and end zone targets (15). The 27-year-old remains an elite player, but the quarterback concerns aren't fully solved, with dual-threat Kyler Murray (one receiver managed a top-25 fantasy campaign during his time as a starter in Arizona) set to work as the starter. Perhaps Murray can ignite Jefferson similar to how he did DeAndre Hopkins at times, but there's certainly some risk. Jefferson is best considered as a mid-range WR1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Deshaun Watson and the Browns visit the Buccaneers for an interconference clash in Week 2. In his first regular-season game since Oct. 20, 2024, Watson completed 16 of 22 pass attempts for 205 yards with one TD and one INT while rushing six times for 38 yards. Although his debut was uninspiring, head coach Todd Monken said he will stick with the 31-year-old as the starting quarterback after seeing enough positive glimpses on film. Watson will face another difficult matchup against Tampa Bay's 14th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (18.7) to QBs and therefore should remain on waiver wires.
outlooksByWeek.3: Deshaun Watson and the Browns host the Panthers for their home opener in Week 3. He completed 24 of 30 pass attempts for 238 yards with two TDs and no INTs, while rushing seven times for 22 yards during Cleveland's surprising Week 2 win over the Buccaneers. Watson led the comeback victory with scoring strikes of 55 and 17 yards, and chemistry appears to be brewing between him and the Browns' young playmakers. He'll face a Carolina defense that held the Falcons to 129 yards passing and forced three INTs and two fumbles in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Deshaun Watson and the Browns host the division-rival Steelers on Thursday night in Week 4. He completed 16 of 30 pass attempts for 144 yards with two TDs and no INTs while adding 11 rushes for 45 yards during Cleveland's 21-18 victory in Week 3. Watson did a lot of damage with his legs, a growing trend as he's racked up 105 yards on 24 carries across three outings. The Browns' offense continues to surprise, but they'll have their hands full versus a Pittsburgh defense that ranks seventh in fantasy points allowed (16.9) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Deshaun Watson and the Browns take their surprising 3-1 record into a road battle against the Jets in Week 5. In Week 4's 27-24 victory, he threw for 268 yards (24-for-33) with one TD and one INT, while rushing seven times for 22 yards. Watson lost one of his two fumbles, but he was able to do enough to lead his team to a third straight win. He hit seven different receivers en route to his highest passing yardage total since 2023. Watson aims to keep improving in a tough matchup versus the Jets, who have the second-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (16.0) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Deshaun Watson and the Browns host the division-rival Ravens in Week 6. He completed 15 of 33 passes for 155 yards with one TD and no INTs while rushing six times for 40 yards during Cleveland's 17-12 loss in Week 5. Watson was sacked eight times for 53 yards and fumbled three times, although he recovered two of them. After leading the Browns to a three-game win streak behind strong performances, Watson struggled with pressure and the rainy conditions in the Week 5 defeat. He'll aim to bounce back versus Baltimore's 12th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (18.7) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Deshaun Watson and the Browns travel to square off against the Titans in Week 7. He completed 16 of 26 pass attempts for 164 yards and rushed eight times for 29 yards during Cleveland's 13-10 win in Week 6. Watson is not much of a fantasy-friendly quarterback, but he has the Browns at 4-2 and tied for first in the AFC North. Next up is a stingy Tennessee defense that ranks 10th in fantasy points allowed per game (18.6) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Deshaun Watson and the Browns travel to Pittsburgh for a divisional clash in Week 8. He completed 25 of 36 pass attempts for 308 yards with no touchdowns and one interception, while rushing three times for 19 yards and a TD during Cleveland's Week 7 victory. Watson mounted a game-winning drive in the fourth quarter for the fifth time this season, leading the Browns to a 5-2 record and a tie with the Steelers atop the AFC North. He'll face Pittsburgh's fourth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (17.1) to QBs for the second time in 2026. Watson threw for 268 yards with one TD and one INT to go along with 22 rush yards in a Week 4 win over the Steelers.
outlooksByWeek.9: Deshaun Watson and the Browns visit New Orleans for an interconference clash in Week 9. He completed 27 of 39 pass attempts for 324 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions and rushed three times for two yards during Cleveland's 27-6 loss in Week 8. Watson lost a fumble and was sacked eight times in another tough showing for the Browns' offense. He'll try to turn things around against a Saints defense allowing 20.5 fantasy points per game (T-14th) to opposing QBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Deshaun Watson and the Browns welcome his former team to town when they host the Texans in Week 10. He was inactive for Cleveland's 23-22 overtime loss in Week 9 due to a concussion sustained in Week 8's loss. Shedeur Sanders earned his first start of the season, but Watson is healthy and expected to retain his role as the starting QB versus Houston. He'll battle a Texans defense allowing 21.8 fantasy points per game (25th) to the position.
outlooksByWeek.12: Deshaun Watson and the Browns host the Raiders in a Week 12 showdown on Sunday Night Football. During Cleveland's Week 10 victory, he threw for 312 yards (25-of-40) with zero TDs and one INT, and had eight carries for 49 yards and a TD. Watson spread the ball around to nine different receivers to help lead a comeback win, but he's now failed to record a TD pass in four straight outings. That streak could come to an end as Las Vegas allows 23.8 fantasy points per game (29th) to QBs and has given up the second-most passing TDs (23) this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Watson will return to the field this season after a disastrous four years in Cleveland. A top-six fantasy QB (points per game) during each of his first four NFL seasons, Watson has appeared in a total of 19 games since joining the Browns, averaging a poor 13.1 fantasy points during the span. A torn Achilles suffered in Week 7 of 2024 (followed by tearing it again less than three months later) cost Watson all of 2025. Now 30 years old, with a young, unproven supporting cast and having not been a factor since 2020, Watson will open the season as Cleveland's starter, but he's a long shot to return to fantasy relevance. He should be considered only in superflex formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Adonai Mitchell will look to stretch the field for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers. Mitchell hauled in all three of his targets to open the year, finishing with 60 yards. Green Bay allowed a mere 7.7 yards per target in Week 1, but that was largely due to facing Carson Wentz for the bulk of the game. Their secondary remains vulnerable and will likely commit multiple bodies to Garrett Wilson, setting up Mitchell for a few plays downfield in single coverage. Mitchell seems likely to continue his low-volume, high-upside role in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Adonai Mitchell hopes for a continued elevated workload in Week 3 when the Jets face the Lions. After just three targets in a run-heavy Week 1, Mitchell logged an eye-opening 12 targets in Week 2, with the Jets throwing 41 times. Detroit's defense has been a fantasy bonanza for opposing offenses, allowing the sixth-most fantasy points to wideouts. Assuming the Lions score plenty themselves, the Jets should throw heavily, giving Mitchell ample opportunities for a big play or two.
outlooksByWeek.4: Adonai Mitchell is questionable for the Jets in Week 4 against the Bears after missing Week 3 due to a finger injury. Mitchell has been a valuable secondary option opposite Garrett Wilson in his first two games, garnering 15 targets and averaging 13.7 yards per catch. With minimal options behind him and running back Breece Hall (thigh) likely to miss Week 4, Mitchell could have a stable workload against a defense that's allowing 8.5 yards per target to opposing receivers.
outlooksByWeek.5: Adonai Mitchell needs to overcome a finger injury that has cost him the last two weeks if he's to help the Jets against the Browns in Week 5. Prior to injury, Mitchell was giving the Jets a field-stretching option, averaging 13.7 yards per catch on nine grabs. Targets will continue to be heavily funneled toward Garrett Wilson, but Mitchell will be in a favorable spot if cleared to play, as Cleveland has allowed six touchdowns to opposing receivers through four games. Sterling Shepard and Isaiah Williams would continue to register additional snaps should Mitchell miss his third straight game.
outlooksByWeek.6: Adonai Mitchell will need to overcome a finger issue that's cost him the last three weeks if he's to help the Jets against the Patriots in Week 6. He had emerged as a field stretcher for the Jets, but it's an offense that prefers to run and heavily target Garrett Wilson. New England has allowed five touchdown catches by opposing receivers in as many games, and Mitchell would likely require that end-zone success to be considered a starting option. Isaiah Williams and Tim Patrick will continue to get additional snaps if Mitchell remains sidelined.
outlooksByWeek.7: Adonai Mitchell will need to overcome a finger injury that cost him four games if he's to help the Jets against the Dolphins in Week 7. Mitchell looked firm in his role opposite Garrett Wilson prior to injury, but it's fair to question his immediate role should he be active in Week 7. Facing a Dolphins' secondary that's surprisingly allowing the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing wide receivers despite a desirable 8.2 yards per target doesn't profile as a re-emergent spot, especially with Omar Cooper healthy and surging.
outlooksByWeek.8: Adonai Mitchell has a minimal role in the Jets' limited passing attack entering a Week 8 clash with the Raiders. Returning from a four-week absence in Week 7, Mitchell failed to record a catch on his three targets. Omar Cooper's emergence paired with Garrett Wilson's steady presence won't leave a plethora of opportunities for the remaining Jets' receivers in a run-first offense, giving Mitchell too few chances to exploit a defense that's allowing a generous 8.9 yards per target through seven games.
outlooksByWeek.9: Adonai Mitchell faces an uphill battle if he hopes to repeat a career outing when the Jets face the Chiefs in Week 9. After being shut out since Week 2, Mitchell popped for seven catches, 142 yards, and a touchdown in Week 8, shifting the spotlight from surging rookie Omar Cooper. Mitchell has always shown big-play potential but sees inconsistent opportunities. This sets him up as a high-potential, low-ceiling option against a Chiefs secondary that's allowing just 6.9 yards per target and the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.10: Adonai Mitchell's roller coaster season heads into a favorable spot when the Jets face the Bills in Week 10. He failed to record a catch in Week 9 despite seven targets, his second game in three weeks without a reception. Mitchell remains a vertical option, and he's averaged 6.8 targets across five healthy appearances. With the Jets likely throwing from behind as the game progresses, he's a reasonable bet to flourish against a secondary that's allowed 28 receptions of 20-plus yards, the eighth-most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.11: Adonai Mitchell continues to bring inefficiency through steady opportunity with the Jets set to face the Chargers in Week 11. Mitchell has 24 targets over the last three weeks but has converted them into just 10 catches, tallying a solid 201 yards. The Chargers' secondary is allowing the sixth-most fantasy points to wideouts, and Mitchell figures to see consistent volume, particularly with Omar Cooper (ankle) uncertain to play. But Geno Smith's ankle injury also brings ambiguity to this passing game, making Mitchell a high-upside, low-floor option.
outlooksByWeek.12: Adonai Mitchell remains an inconsistent, high-upside option in the Jets' low-volume passing game ahead of a Week 12 matchup with the Dolphins. Mitchell has three or fewer catches in four of five games since returning from a four-game injury absence, and the Jets have now failed to complete 20 passes for three straight games. Miami's secondary is vertically vulnerable, allowing 9.2 yards per target. The Dolphins are vulnerable to the run, and the Jets prefer to grind it out, so Mitchell will be a boom-or-bust option, likely excluding him from fantasy lineups.

player.seasonOutlook: Mitchell is entering his first full campaign with the Jets, having been acquired in the Sauce Gardner trade during the 2025 season. After playing sparingly during his first 25 NFL games (all with the Colts), the 2024 second-round pick handled a hefty 24.4% target share in eight games with New York last season. The usage led to two fantasy outings with 17-plus points, but he was otherwise a nonfactor (4.0 PPG). Efficiency remains an issue, as Mitchell's 44% catch rate ranks last, and his 6.0 yards per target is fourth worst among 77 receivers with 100-plus targets since he entered the league. The vertical threat will compete with rookie Omar Cooper Jr. for No. 2 duties opposite a now-healthy Garrett Wilson in the Jets' Geno Smith-led offense. Mitchell, 23, is not worth much more than late-round consideration.

outlooksByWeek.8: Austin Ekeler managed just three touches for seven yards last game for Washington. Even with starting running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt on Injured Reserve with a groin injury, Ekeler was on the field for just seven of 67 offensive snaps. Rachaad White should get the start in Week 8 versus the Eagles, and Jeremy McNichols may see more work than Ekeler between the tackles. McNichols had five carries for 13 yards in his return from injury. Whomever gets touches does have a favorable matchup, as Philadelphia is giving up 119.3 yards per clash on the ground, which is 21st in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Austin Ekeler rushed eight times for 36 yards last game. Starter Rachaad White  rushed 11 times for 55 yards and a touchdown in the 27-10 win over the Eagles. Jeremy McNichols left this game with an injury, leaving Ekeler as the only other healthy backup option. In Week 9, Washington will face a Rams defense allowing 109.3 yards per tilt on the ground, which is 14th in the NFL. However, the Rams have surrendered just four rushing scores in 2026, which is tied for third in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Austin Ekeler had a season-high 10 touches last game for Washington. Unfortunately, he managed just 34 yards with those opportunities, and the Commanders fell to the Rams by a score of 20-13. Ekeler has 16 carries over the last two contests, though continues to serve as the backup to Rachaad White. In Week 10, Ekeler will face a Giants defense that has been better against the pass than the run in 2026. New York is allowing just 177.8 passing yards per clash, which is third in the NFL. However, the Giants are surrendering 123.6 rushing yards per tilt, which is 21st in the league.
outlooksByWeek.11: Austin Ekeler has received at least eight touches in three-straight games for the Commanders. He rushed nine times for 26 yards in the most recent win over the Giants, while also catching four passes for 26 yards out of the backfield. However, Jacory Croskey-Merritt may return from injury in Week 11 versus the Bengals, which would reduce Ekeler's workload behind Rachaad White.  If Croskey-Merritt cannot suit up, Ekeler would see more opportunities against a Cincy defense surrendering 123.9 rushing yards per clash, which is 21st in the league.
outlooksByWeek.12: Austin Ekeler had seven carries for 41 yards last game for Washington, though ceded the majority of touches out of the backfield to Jacory Croskey-Merritt. Bill rushed 13 times for 54 yards and a touchdown in the surprising 22-20 win over the Bengals, nearly doubling up Ekeler in terms of carries. Rachaad White dressed but did not play, likely due to a heel injury, so his status for Week 12 versus the Cardinals could also affect Ekeler's usage. Arizona is allowing 128.8 rushing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the league, so there should be room to roam if Ekeler gets the opportunity.

outlooksByWeek.2: Breece Hall will look to remain busy when the Jets face the Packers in Week 2. Hall handled 24 total touches to open the year, finishing with 118 total yards and a touchdown-an encouraging start under new OC Frank Reich. The Packers allowed just 3.7 yards per carry last week but did give up two rushing scores. Much of Hall's volume came in a favorable game script, something that may not repeat in Week 2, but with better than a 2:1 touch split with Braelon Allen, Hall will garner ample opportunity.
outlooksByWeek.3: Breece Hall will look to find more running room for the Jets in Week 3 against the Lions. He was limited to 1.8 yards per carry in Week 2, but 16 rushes was encouraging, as were his five catches on five targets. Detroit's defense is leaky, and while their secondary has been the more glaring weakness, they're allowing 5.2 yards per carry. The Jets' offensive limitations will likely temper Week 3 production, but Hall's workload in a plus matchup boosts his outlook.
outlooksByWeek.4: Breece Hall is uncertain to face the Bears in the Jets' Week 4 matchup due to a thigh injury. Hall has struggled over the last two weeks, gaining just 61 yards on 29 carries, but his workload in the passing game has been steady. Should he play, Hall has an inviting matchup against a defense that's allowing 4.9 yards per carry. Braelon Allen would likely lead the backfield in the event of Hall's absence, with Isaiah Davis playing second fiddle.
outlooksByWeek.5: Breece Hall is uncertain to face the Browns in the Jets' Week 5 matchup due to a quad injury. He missed Week 4 with the issue, and when healthy, he was limited to 32 or fewer yards in his last two outings. Should he suit up, it's possible he'd be eased into his return and share snaps with Braelon Allen, but it's a favorable spot if a normal workload can be anticipated. While Cleveland has yet to allow a running back to score, they're allowing 4.8 yards per carry, with the last three lead backs all reaching at least 82 yards.
outlooksByWeek.6: Breece Hall needs to overcome a quad injury to suit up for the first time in three weeks when the Jets face the Patriots in Week 6. Braelon Allen has shouldered the load in Hall's absence, and a split workload can be anticipated once Hall returns. Hall would require an unlikely heavy volume to be a top option facing a New England defense that's allowed just 399 rushing yards through five games.
outlooksByWeek.7: Breece Hall has missed three straight games due to a quad injury as the Jets get set to face the Dolphins in Week 7. Braelon Allen has shined during Hall's absence, and should Hall be deemed healthy, it would appear safe to assume he'd be eased back into action. Miami's defense ranks in the middle of the pack against opposing rushers, allowing 4.0 yards per carry and three rushing scores, but five touchdowns through the air to opposing backs. With questionable volume if he returns to action, it's probably wise to wait one more week before deploying Hall.
outlooksByWeek.8: Breece Hall's role is uncertain if he returns from a quad injury in Week 8 when the Jets face the Raiders. Hall has not played since Week 3 and has topped 32 yards just once, while Braelon Allen has shined during his absence. Being eased back into action appears more likely than immediately commanding the Jets' backfield, but he may not require heavy volume to be an intriguing asset, as the Raiders are allowing the second-most fantasy points per game to opposing running backs and 5.2 yards per carry. Five opposing backs have rushed for 94 yards or more against them.
outlooksByWeek.9: Breece Hall is poised to return from a five-game absence due to a quad injury when the Jets face the Chiefs in Week 9. In Hall's absence, Braelon Allen shined and has likely earned at least a portion of the carries, leaving Hall's role uncertain. Pairing that with a matchup against a Kansas City defense that's allowing just 3.3 yards per carry, Hall doesn't offer a solid floor or much upside in Week 9.
outlooksByWeek.10: Breece Hall's workload should be strong in the Jets' Week 10 matchup against a tough Bills run defense. Returning to action in Week 9 after a five-game absence, Hall collected 18 touches to Braelon Allen's 10, despite Allen's success while Hall was sidelined. Hall has logged at least 13 carries in all four games when healthy, adding 13 receptions. His viability in the passing game should allow him to be a fantasy factor despite facing a defense that's allowing just 3.8 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.11: Breece Hall brings steady volume into a somewhat challenging matchup in Week 11 when the Jets face the Chargers. Hall has amassed at least 11 carries in both games since returning from injury while adding seven receptions, tallying 195 total yards though not reaching the end zone and continuing to share reps with Braelon Allen. The Chargers are allowing the 10th most fantasy points per game to opposing backs, but just 4.0 yards per carry and an even lower 3.9 yards per reception. Hall remains a lineup mainstay and could surge in the receiving game if Cade Klubnik is forced into action over Geno Smith (ankle).
outlooksByWeek.12: Breece Hall is slated for a heavy workload for the Jets' run-first offense entering an inviting matchup against the Dolphins in Week 12. Hall amassed 20 rushes in Week 11, adding three catches, and has now topped 100 total yards in consecutive outings. Miami is allowing a modest 4.3 yards per carry but 11 total touchdowns (six rushing, five receiving) to running backs. Braelon Allen excelled against the Dolphins in Hall's absence earlier in the season, so Hall should produce in Week 12, even if ceding some carries to Allen. Hall remains a must-start.

player.seasonOutlook: Hall received the franchise tag during the offseason and will return for his fifth season with the Jets. Having worked in the Jets' underwhelming offenses the past two years, Hall has struggled to finishes of 17th and 21st in fantasy points per game among RBs, which is a far cry from top-eight finishes during his first two seasons. Hall has remained busy, however, producing 266-plus touches each of the past three seasons. The 2022 second-round pick saw a dip in receiving work in 2025 (career-low 10% target share) but finished fourth in that category in both 2023 and 2024, so a rebound is possible with pocket QB Geno Smith now under center. Though the Jets' offense might continue to limit Hall's upside, the 25-year-old's combination of workload and talent positions him as a solid RB2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Trevor Lawrence threw four touchdown passes in the first 33 minutes of Jacksonville's lopsided Week 1 win over the Browns before the Jaguars took their foot off the gas. He has 22 touchdown passes in his last eight starts, but the surging QB could face a stiffer test in a Week 2 road game against the Broncos. They boasted the NFL's third-stingiest scoring defense last season but just gave up 31 points to the Chiefs in Week 1. Lawrence has been effective enough recently to warrant starting in fantasy despite the daunting matchup, but he's unlikely to give managers a top-five performance in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Trevor Lawrence crashed back down to earth with 189 passing yards and no TDs in the Jaguars' Week 2 loss at Denver after tossing four touchdown passes in the season-opening win over Cleveland. Lawrence and the Jaguars return home for a Week 3 showdown with the Patriots, who have allowed just 16 total points in two games. The daunting matchup drops Lawrence to the QB1/QB2 borderline, so this could be the week to plug in an alternative option if available. Lawrence threw 22 touchdown passes in the eight starts preceding his Week 2 dud, so the 2021 first-overall pick maintains elite upside.
outlooksByWeek.4: Trevor Lawrence has thrown at least three touchdown passes in two of three games this season but is averaging just 205 passing yards per game. He'll maintain an elite ceiling in Jacksonville's Week 4 road game against the Bengals, who have allowed the third-most passing yards. Cincinnati just gave up three passing TDs to Aaron Rodgers in Week 3 but hadn't allowed a touchdown pass prior to that game this season. Lawrence has been a fantasy QB1 more often than not since Parker Washington emerged as his go-to receiver in the second half of last season, and that looks unlikely to change in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.5: Trevor Lawrence is off to an inconsistent start this season, with seven touchdown passes in two home games but just one touchdown pass in two road games. The Jaguars are the nominal home team in Week 5 against the Eagles, but the game will be played in London at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium rather than in Jacksonville. Given Lawrence's struggles away from home coupled with a matchup against an Eagles defense that has allowed just four touchdown passes in as many games, this could be a week to look elsewhere at QB if a viable alternative is available on your bench or waiver wire. Jacksonville's passing game has enough upside for Lawrence to deliver a starter-level performance, but his floor is well below that.
outlooksByWeek.6: Trevor Lawrence threw for a season-high 331 yards against the Eagles as the Jaguars improved to 4-1 with a Week 5 win. He brings a 10:3 TD:INT into a Week 6 matchup against the Texans, which will be the Jaguars' second consecutive game in London. Houston has surprisingly been one of the league's most generous pass defenses, allowing QBs to throw for 256 yards per game, though the Texans have allowed only six TDs through the air. Lawrence produced just 380 passing yards with a 1:2 TD:INT in two meetings with the AFC South rival Texans in 2025, but since Houston's defense has taken a step back this season, Lawrence can continue to be deployed as a starting fantasy QB for Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.8: Trevor Lawrence profiles as a strong Week 8 fantasy starter as the Jaguars return home to host the Colts following their Week 7 bye. In two previous starts at EverBank Stadium this season, Lawrence has thrown seven touchdown passes. He has a 14:4 TD:INT through six outings, the last two of which came in London. Back stateside, Lawrence should keep rolling at home against a Colts secondary that has allowed an 11:2 TD:INT and could remain without top CB Sauce Gardner (calf).
outlooksByWeek.9: Trevor Lawrence has thrown seven touchdown passes across Jacksonville's last two games, so he remains a top-10 fantasy QB option ahead of a Week 9 road game against the Ravens. He has just one touchdown pass across two road games this season, but Jacksonville's offense should get plenty of opportunities with the Ravens unlikely to sustain drives in the expected absence of Baltimore's top two QBs, Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe). Baltimore's defense has allowed an 11:4 TD:INT ratio while ranking in the middle of the pack against the pass. Despite his lackluster road production, Lawrence has thrown touchdown passes on a league-high 8.6% of his passes this season en route to a 17:4 TD:INT overall.
outlooksByWeek.10: Trevor Lawrence has thrown 18 touchdown passes, leading the Jaguars to a 6-2 record heading into a Week 10 trip to Tennessee. However, he has just three touchdown passes in three road games. Jacksonville has won its last two games by a 75-17 margin, so Lawrence has been afforded the luxury of taking his foot off the gas. This has limited his production after back-to-back 300-yard passing performances in a pair of competitive games in London. Another lopsided win is likely to materialize against the 1-7 Titans, but Lawrence is capable of producing elite numbers while the game is still up for grabs. He has top-five fantasy QB upside against a Tennessee secondary that is giving up the second-most passing yards per game, but it wouldn't be surprising if he finished outside the top 15 in Week 10, either.
outlooksByWeek.11: Trevor Lawrence has thrown at least three touchdown passes in three of his last four starts and topped 300 passing yards in three of his last five, firmly placing him in the fantasy QB1 range for a Week 11 road game against the Giants. The 7-2 Jaguars and 5-3-1 Giants both lead their respective divisions, but Jacksonville's plus-125 point differential is far more impressive than the Giants' plus-7 mark. Pass defense has been a strength for the Giants, as they allow the third-fewest yards per game through the air (184). However, Lawrence maintains an elite ceiling regardless of opponent and could actually benefit statistically if this game remains close throughout, forcing the Jaguars to keep their foot on the gas. This season, he has thrown for 1,430 passing yards and 13 touchdowns in first halves, compared to 854 passing yards and eight touchdowns in second halves, with Jacksonville nursing large second-half leads on multiple occasions.
outlooksByWeek.12: Trevor Lawrence was held to a 1:2 TD:INT ratio in Jacksonville's Week 11 road loss to the Giants, but he has been sensational at home, with a 10:1 TD:INT ratio in three games at EverBank Stadium. He's a set-and-forget fantasy starter for Week 12 with No. 1 overall QB upside against Tennessee's generous secondary. The Titans have allowed 12 touchdown passes over their last three games, three of which were thrown by Lawrence in Jacksonville's 40-23 Week 10 win at Tennessee. Lawrence should have little trouble carving up Tennessee's secondary like a Thanksgiving turkey as long as the game stays competitive; however, Jacksonville's high-powered offense could throttle down late if the heavily favored Jaguars build a comfortable lead.

player.seasonOutlook: Lawrence is entering his sixth NFL season after a breakout 2025 in which he ranked no lower than seventh among quarterbacks in pass attempts, completions, yards and touchdowns, as well as top 10 in carries, yards and TDs. He reeled off seven consecutive top-10 fantasy outings to finish the season. Lawrence's efficiency has been fine, at best, but he continues to generate big volume, having finished in the top 10 among QBs in pass and rush attempts in each of his four full seasons. With a strong, deep group of pass catchers and Liam Coen back as playcaller, the 26-year-old is well positioned for mid-to-back-end QB1 production.

outlooksByWeek.2: Patrick Mahomes proved he was fully recovered from last year's ACL injury in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, scoring a 15-yard rushing TD in addition to completing 15 of 27 passes for 184 yards and two touchdowns with one interception. The offense flowed through new lead back Kenneth Walker and benefited from some short fields, but Mahomes still took advantage of his opportunities. The star QB could be headed for better individual numbers in Week 2 against a Colts defense that looked awful in its opener and which ranked 31st in passing yards allowed in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Patrick Mahomes has Kansas City's offense humming, and through two games, he's produced 566 passing yards and a 5:1 TD:INT while adding a touchdown on the ground. The superstar QB has spread the ball around effectively, as five different targets have been on the end of those TDs, and a revitalized running game with Kenneth Walker has prevented defenses from laying back and clogging the passing lanes. Mahomes could be headed for big numbers in Week 3 against a Dolphins defense that has yet to record a sack in 2026 and which sits 32nd in completion rate against at a stunning 78.8%.
outlooksByWeek.4: Patrick Mahomes continued his strong start to the season in Kansas City's Week 3 win over the Dolphins, producing multiple touchdowns for a third straight game. The two-time MVP has a 7:2 TD-to-INT ratio in those three contests while adding another score on the ground, and his 8.3 yards per attempt would be his highest mark since 2019. He's done it without the benefit of a single dominant receiver, as Travis Kelce, Kenneth Walker, Rashee Rice, and Xavier Worthy have all logged between 15 and 18 targets. Mahomes will look to keep rolling in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Patrick Mahomes comes out of Kansas City's bye with a strong 9:2 TD:INT and 8.1 yards per attempt through four games. The presence of Kenneth Walker in the backfield has opened things up for the team's passing game, but Mahomes did lose Week 4 breakout Tyquan Thornton to a dislocated ankle that could potentially sideline the speedy wideout for the rest of the season. Rashee Rice also picked up a minor hamstring strain prior to the bye, which could leave Mahomes working with a very inexperienced group of WRs, although he still has Travis Kelce to fall back on. Mahomes will be facing a Chargers defense in Week 6 that is tied for 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Patrick Mahomes didn't have much to do in Kansas City's Week 6 easy win over the Chargers. With Kenneth Walker and the defense doing most of the work in a 22-6 victory, Mahomes failed to throw a touchdown pass for the first time this season, although he did rack up 272 passing yards and 9.1 yards per attempt. His 8.3 mark on the year is his best since 2019, and through five games he's produced 10 TDs-nine passing and one rushing-against three turnovers. Mahomes faces a much tougher test in Week 7 against a Seahawks defense that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Patrick Mahomes is coming off one of the worst performances of his career in Kansas City's Week 7 loss to the Seahawks. The two-time MVP threw for a season-low 165 yards with zero touchdowns and failed to get his team into the red zone for the first time in 153 career starts, including regular season and playoffs. With his wide receiver room thinned by injuries, Mahomes is again having a tough time stretching the field or taking advantage of a defense's focus on Kenneth Walker. He'll try to bounce back in Week 8 against a Broncos defense playing below expectations, which sits tied for 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Patrick Mahomes bounced back from a two-game touchdown drought to throw three TDs in Week 8, but it wasn't enough as Kansas City lost to the Broncos and ceded first place in the AFC West. Despite a lack of consistent help at wide receiver, something that could be addressed at the trade deadline, Mahomes is on pace for his best passing yards total since 2021. With a 12:4 TD:INT ratio through seven games, he could produce 30-plus touchdowns for the first time since 2022. He'll look to keep rolling in Week 9 against a Jets defense that ranks 16th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Patrick Mahomes put together another strong performance in Kansas City's Week 9 win over the Jets, completing 74.2% of his 31 pass attempts with two touchdowns and zero interceptions, but he suffered an elbow injury during the contest. He finished the game, but the team is awaiting the results of testing to determine the severity. For now, Mahomes has been deemed day-to-day. If he's cleared to play in Week 10, he'll be facing a Falcons defense that ranks 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs but just traded starting safety Jessie Bates. If Mahomes is held out, Justin Fields would get his first start of the season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Patrick Mahomes is coming off a huge performance in a Week 10 win over the Falcons, as he threw five touchdown passes for the first time since Week 1 of the 2022 season. The trade-deadline addition of Josh Downs revitalized the passing game, as four different Kansas City players had receptions of 30-plus yards. Mahomes has a 10:0 TD:INT ratio over the last three games with two 300-yard performances, giving him significant momentum heading into a Week 11 clash with a Cardinals defense that ranks 29th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Patrick Mahomes continues to roll, tossing multiple touchdowns for a fourth straight game and topping 300 passing yards for the third time during that stretch in Kansas City's Week 11 win over the Cardinals. The two-time MVP finally seems to be back in top form after last season's knee injury, and the trade deadline addition of Josh Downs has given him another downfield option. Mahomes will need to stay hot in Week 12 in a marquee AFC clash against the Bills, who rank 10th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Mahomes is a bit of a wild card as he embarks on his 10th season. The two-time NFL MVP followed up a pair of disappointing fantasy seasons (2023-24) with an elite start to 2025 (24.5 points per game during Weeks 1-8) and a disappointing finish that included 15.0 points per game during his final six games and a torn ACL in Week 15. Mahomes' efficiency has dipped the past three seasons, and while he made up ground as a rusher in 2025 (fifth among QBs in rushing yards and TDs despite three missed games), he might not be able to run as often this season as he recovers fully from the knee injury. Mahomes will be ready to play in Week 1, but he hasn't been a consistent fantasy QB1 since 2022. He's a risky mid-round flier in drafts.

outlooksByWeek.2: Derrick Henry and the Ravens play host to the Saints for their 2026 home opener in Week 2. Henry rambled for 144 yards and three TDs on 24 carries and caught his only target for 19 yards in Baltimore's 41-23 victory. Next up is a Saints defense that surrendered 165 yards and two TDs on the ground to Jahmyr Gibbs and the Lions. Henry has tallied 16 rushing TDs in consecutive years, and he's nearly a quarter of the way there already after just one game.
outlooksByWeek.3: Derrick Henry and the Ravens travel to Texas to battle the Cowboys in Week 3. In Baltimore's Week 2 loss, Henry rushed 16 times for 68 yards and one score, and he caught all three targets for another 19 yards. He accounted for 16 of 18 carries out of the backfield, and he'll continue earning a massive workload on the ground in order to take pressure off Lamar Jackson. Henry faces a Dallas defense that ranks 25th in fantasy points per game (25.9) and 27th in rushing yards allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Derrick Henry and the Ravens return from Brazil to host the winless Titans in Week 4. He tallied 26 carries for 89 yards and two TDs and caught his only target for no gain during Baltimore's 34-31 last-second victory in Week 3 over Dallas. Tennessee's defense ranks 17th in fantasy points allowed (20.7) to RBs after giving up 138 rushing yards to the Giants. Henry will handle his usual workhorse role and could benefit from a positive game script versus a Titans team that ranks third in fewest points allowed per contest, at 12.3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Derrick Henry and the Ravens are on the road for a Week 5 clash against the Falcons. He tallied 23 carries for 73 yards and one touchdown while catching both of his targets for six yards during Baltimore's Week 4 victory. Henry notched his seventh rushing TD of the season and now has at least one score in all four outings. With Lamar Jackson's (ankle) status up in the air, Henry should continue to be the focal point of the Ravens' offense versus Atlanta's ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (17.9) per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Derrick Henry and the Ravens travel to Cleveland for a divisional clash in Week 6. He rushed 24 times for 102 yards and caught one of two targets for an 18-yard touchdown during Baltimore's 30-23 overtime win in Week 5. The game marked Henry's first scoreless outing on the ground in 2026, and he draws a difficult Week 6 matchup against a Browns' defense that has surrendered just one combined TD to the position. Cleveland ranks seventh by allowing 17.6 fantasy points per game to RBs, but the Jets' Braelon Allen racked up 116 rushing yards and one score on 24 attempts in Week 5. The Browns could again be without two starters on the defensive line, and with Lamar Jackson's (ankle) status in question, Henry has another opportunity to be the primary engine of the offense.
outlooksByWeek.7: Derrick Henry and the Ravens welcome the Bengals to town for a divisional clash in Week 7. He rushed 17 times for 58 yards and caught his lone target for two yards during Baltimore's 13-10 loss in Week 6, also losing a costly fumble in the fourth quarter. The outing marked Henry's first this season without a touchdown, and his 60 scrimmage yards were his lowest output through six games. He will aim to bounce back at home in Week 7 versus a Cincinnati defense that allows 19.0 fantasy points per game to RBs, which is tied for ninth.
outlooksByWeek.8: Derrick Henry and the Ravens aim to snap a two-game losing streak when they visit Buffalo in Week 8. He rushed 17 times for 45 yards and caught one of two targets for four yards during Baltimore's 35-13 loss in Week 7. Henry has averaged fewer than 3.5 yards per carry (YPC) in two straight outings, rushing 34 times for 103 yards (3.0 YPC) during that stretch. He'll look to turn things around versus a Bills defense allowing 28.0 fantasy points per game to RBs, which ranks 29th.
outlooksByWeek.9: Derrick Henry and the Ravens hope to snap a three-game losing streak when they host the Jaguars in Week 9. He had 11 carries for 53 yards and Baltimore's lone TD while catching both of his targets for seven yards during Week 8's 36-10 loss. Henry has failed to top 60 rushing yards since Week 5, and things likely won't be any easier for him moving forward with Lamar Jackson (thumb) possibly done for the season. Henry will face a Jaguars defense that ranks second-best in the league at defending opposing RBs, allowing 17.3 fantasy points per game.
outlooksByWeek.10: Derrick Henry and the Ravens welcome the Chargers to town for a Week 10 clash on Monday Night Football. He rushed 17 times for 57 yards and did not record a target during Baltimore's Week 9 loss.
