Henry has struggled mightily over his last four outings, gaining 213 yards on 62 carries (3.4 yards per carry) with just one touchdown. Jacoby Brissett, who's expected to start under center in Week 10, should provide some relief for the passing game, so the hope is that this will begin to have a positive effect on Henry.
outlooksByWeek.11: Derrick Henry and the Ravens take to the road in Week 11 to battle the 4-5 Panthers. In Baltimore's Week 10 loss, he rushed 10 times for 10 yards and two touchdowns and caught all five of his targets for 10 yards. Henry was able to salvage an otherwise miserable outing with two scores, the 32-year-old's ninth and tenth rushing TDs on the season. The Ravens attempted 49 passes with Jacoby Brissett making his team debut under center. The hope is that Brissett will allow Henry more breathing room between the tackles versus Carolina's 29th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (27.3) to opposing RBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: In Week 12, Derrick Henry and the Ravens travel to Houston for an AFC showdown between playoff hopefuls. He rushed 13 times for 94 yards and a TD and caught four of five targets for 17 yards during Baltimore's Week 11 loss. Henry also lost a fumble, his second of the season, and was evaluated and cleared for a concussion in the fourth quarter. All signs point to him being good to go for the road tilt versus the Texans, who rank 14th in fantasy points allowed per game (21.4) to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Henry continues to defy the odds, playing at a high level despite now entering his age-32 season. In 2025, he finished exactly second in the NFL in rushing yards for the fourth season in a row, and his 24 carries inside the 5-yard line were easily the most in the league. Henry leads the NFL in carries inside the 5-yard line (42) and is second in touchdowns (34) since joining Baltimore prior to the 2024 season, and he hasn't finished lower than eighth among RBs in touchdowns since 2017. Henry continues to run at a high level (his 5.20 yards per carry last season ranked fifth among qualified backs), but he's still a nonfactor as a receiver (outside the top 45 backs in targets, catches and yards last season). He remains a featured rusher in a terrific offense and is well positioned for his fifth consecutive top-eight fantasy campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: Amon-Ra St. Brown will aim to keep it rolling as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. St. Brown kicked off the season with a bang against the Saints, catching 10 of 14 targets for 67 yards and two touchdowns. The star wide receiver continues to hold the monopoly in Detroit's passing game, and his production doesn't look to be taking a dip any time soon. He'll take on a Bills defense that ceded a seventh-most PPR points to Houston wide receivers (40.0) in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Amon-Ra St. Brown will aim to stay hot as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3. St. Brown finished with a monster performance in Week 2, bringing in nine of 13 targets for 142 yards and two touchdowns. Not only has the star pass catcher recorded back-to-back two-TD performances, but he's also now amassed 19 catches for 209 yards in that stretch. He should continue to benefit from Detroit's shaky defense, even against a New York defense that's allowed 27.2 PPR points per game to its first two opponents, a top-10 mark.
outlooksByWeek.4: Amon-Ra St. Brown will look to bounce back from a quieter game as the Lions travel to Carolina in Week 4. St. Brown finished Week 3 against the Jets with a touchdown, but other than that, he has just four catches for 19 yards. The eight targets he finished with did still tie  Jahmyr Gibbs for a team lead, so the volume remains for the pair of stars to both produce highly. St. Brown will face a Panthers defense that's allowed a top-five 23.2 fantasy points per game to wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Amon-Ra St. Brown will look to find the end zone again as the Lions travel to Arizona in Week 5. St. Brown returned to a solid eight catches for 75 yards against the Panthers in Week 4, but he also broke his three-game touchdown streak. The star pass catcher has now totaled 31 receptions for 303 yards and five touchdowns this season. He'll take on a Cardinals defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Amon-Ra St. Brown will seek to find the end zone again as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. St. Brown has remained hot as of late with 14 catches for 144 yards in his last two outings, but he's been unable to find the end zone since Week 3. The star wide receiver will take a 37-372-5 receiving line into a big matchup versus a Green Bay secondary that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs this year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Amon-Ra St. Brown will look to heal from an ankle injury in time for Detroit's Week 8 matchup versus Minnesota. St. Brown played a full game in Week 7 against the Packers, finishing with nine catches for a season-high 153 yards. The star pass catcher also tweaked his ankle in the game, and while he's not expected to miss any time, his situation is worth monitoring. St. Brown will aim to expand on a 46-525-5 receiving line opposite to a Vikings defense that's ranked fourth in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.9: Amon-Ra St. Brown will look to make a return to the end zone as the Lions play the Dolphins in Week 9. St. Brown logged seven receptions for 46 yards and recorded one rush for 10 yards in a Week 8 win over Minnesota. The featured pass catcher has remained a dominant option week in and out, but he hasn't posted a touchdown since Week 3. He'll face a Miami defense that's ranked third in fantasy points allowed to WRs this season but 18th in the last three weeks.
outlooksByWeek.10: Amon-Ra St. Brown will seek to get back in the end zone as the Lions play the Patriots in Week 10. St. Brown led Detroit in all receiving categories against the Dolphins in Week 9, bringing in eight of 10 targets for 86 yards. The star wide receiver is on track for another dominant year, but he hasn't logged a touchdown since Week 3. He enters a favorable matchup versus a New England defense that's ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Amon-Ra St. Brown will seek to stay hot as the Lions play the Buccaneers in Week 11. St. Brown finally broke his touchdown drought in a Week 10 blowout win over New England, catching four of five targets for 98 yards and two scores. The star pass catcher has now posted a 65-755-7 receiving line on 91 targets across nine contests. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked 11th in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Amon-Ra St. Brown will look to keep his touchdown streak alive as the Lions play the Bears in Week 12. St. Brown punched in another score in a Week 11 win over the Buccaneers, which made up for his otherwise mediocre five catches for 37 yards. He's now brought in 70 of 97 targets for 792 yards and eight touchdowns this campaign. Chicago has ranked a tough 10th in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.

player.seasonOutlook: The only player in NFL history with 90-plus catches in each of his first five NFL seasons, St. Brown continues to assert himself as one of the league's best players. The 2021 fourth-round pick has finished exactly third among receivers in fantasy points three seasons in a row, ranking no lower than fourth in catches, yards and touchdowns each year. St. Brown actually enjoyed a career-high target share in 2025 (31.6%), which helped him to 13 top-20 fantasy outings. The 26-year-old has no added target competition and remains Jared Goff's clear No. 1 target. He should be off the board in the first round of your draft.

outlooksByWeek.2: George Kittle had a quiet season opener but will look to increase his production when San Francisco faces the Dolphins in Week 2. Kittle tallied a modest two catches (on five targets) for 12 yards in last Thursday's win over the Rams. That was his first game back after tearing his Achilles in January, which may have been a factor in his receiving line following below his usual standards. Miami allowed Raiders tight end Michael Mayer to record six catches in Week 1, suggesting that Kittle could find room to operate against the Dolphins defense.
outlooksByWeek.3: George Kittle will look to build upon Sunday's strong performance when San Francisco hosts the Cardinals in Week 3. In just his second regular-season game since tearing his Achilles in January, Kittle led the 49ers with 80 receiving yards on four catches with one touchdown Sunday in a win over Miami. The veteran tight end remains a key target for QB Brock Purdy, and Kittle's importance in the passing game could be even more elevated with WRs Demarcus Robinson (ankle) and Mike Evans (hip) both managing injuries. Through two weeks, Arizona has allowed tight ends to catch all 10 of their targets for 105 yards.
outlooksByWeek.4: George Kittle enters San Francisco's Week 4 game against Denver as one of the hottest tight ends in the league. Following a quiet season opener in Australia, Kittle has put up 10 catches for 162 yards and three touchdowns over the subsequent two weeks. He's caught all but one of his 11 targets during that span, as he has been clicking very well with QB Brock Purdy. Kittle could continue rolling against a Broncos defense that has given up the eighth-most receiving yards (199) to tight ends so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: George Kittle could again be a key component of San Francisco's offense in Week 5 against Seattle. Kittle has scored a touchdown in three straight games, and he got into the end zone on a game-sealing 56-yard reception in Week 4 versus the Broncos. The veteran tight end enters the clash against Seattle with 244 receiving yards on the season, third-most among NFL tight ends. With that said, the Seahawks' defense has given up the fourth-fewest receiving yards to tight ends, so Kittle has his work cut out for him in Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.6: George Kittle should be past an illness by the time the 49ers face Washington on Monday Night Football in Week 6. Kittle suited up this past Sunday against Seattle despite falling under the weather near game day. He ended up with a modest five catches on six targets for 24 yards but logged his usual big workload with a season-high 93 percent offensive snap share. Kittle could be primed for a big game against the Commanders, who have surrendered 15.8 fantasy points per game -- second-most in the league -- to tight ends.
outlooksByWeek.7: George Kittle and the 49ers are in Atlanta as they look to stay undefeated in Week 7. He caught five of eight targets for 69 yards and a touchdown during San Francisco's 23-17 win in Week 6. Kittle finished second on the team in receptions, yardage and targets on a night where Brock Purdy attempted just 29 passes. The talented tight end boasts a 26-337-5 line on 36 targets through six outings, and he'll aim to keep rolling versus a Falcons defense tied for 23rd in fantasy points allowed per game (16.0) to the position.
outlooksByWeek.9: George Kittle enters San Francisco's Week 9 matchup versus the Raiders well-rested following his team's Week 8 bye. Kittle had his snaps managed each of the first two weeks following his January surgery to repair a torn Achilles tendon, but amid multiple injuries to the 49ers' WR corps, the star tight end logged at least an 85% offensive snap share (and at least six targets) in each of his past five games. San Francisco could get multiple of the injured wideouts back for Week 9, but Kittle should still be a big part of the passing game, as he ranks fifth among NFL tight ends with a 22.4% target share this season. He'll face a Las Vegas defense that has given up eight touchdowns to tight ends, tied for second-most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: George Kittle's health and productivity have been huge this season for the 49ers heading into a Week 10 tilt against Dallas. After undergoing surgery in January to repair a torn Achilles, Kittle has played in every one of San Francisco's games this season and leads the club with 38 receptions, 483 receiving yards and five receiving touchdowns. His role in the passing game has been especially important of late, as Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) have been sidelined due to injuries, and the addition of veteran possession receiver Keenan Allen at the trade deadline isn't likely to impact Kittle's routes down the seams. Kittle will look to find success against a Dallas defense that has been middle-of-the-pack against tight ends, yielding 7.7 fantasy points per game to the position (tied for 12th in the league).
outlooksByWeek.11: George Kittle continues to be one of the NFL's most consistent tight ends ahead of the 49ers' Week 11 clash with Minnesota. Kittle tallied six catches for 74 yards this past Sunday in a win over Dallas, marking his eighth straight contest with at least four receptions. He's also registered at least 58 yards seven times during that span, giving him a very reliable weekly floor. Kittle could find the sledding tough against Minnesota, though, as the Vikings have given up the fewest fantasy points per game (5.1) to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: George Kittle enters San Francisco's Week 12 clash against Seattle fresh off a two-touchdown performance in Mexico City. While Kittle caught just three passes (on three targets) this past Sunday versus the Vikings, two of those receptions resulted in touchdowns. Kittle is up to seven scores on the season, tied for the most among NFL tight ends. With that said, Seattle has allowed just two TDs to tight ends this season and is giving up the third-fewest fantasy points per game (5.5) to the position, so Kittle faces a stiff task in replicating his Week 11 performance.

player.seasonOutlook: Kittle is undoubtedly among the best tight ends in the NFL and fantasy, but he simply can't dodge the injury bug. The 2017 fifth-round pick has played one full season (2018) and tore an Achilles in the team's wild-card victory after missing six regular-season games last season. Kittle may be ready for Week 1 and isn't expected to miss more than a game or two, though he's now 32 years old and might not be his usual, dominant self even when he returns. Kittle has finished sixth or better in fantasy PPG in each of the past eight seasons (including first in 2024), so his upside makes him worth a late-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 2 matchup against the Patriots. He rushed eight times for 15 yards and caught two of five targets for another six yards during Pittsburgh's Week 1 20-13 win over Atlanta. Dowdle's backfield partner, Jaylen Warren, was much more efficient with his 15 touches, which he turned into 73 scrimmage yards. It will be difficult to trust Dowdle in a tilt versus New England's 14th-ranked defense, which has allowed 84 rushing yards to the position.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers host the Bengals and their 14th-ranked run defense in Week 3. He finished Pittsburgh's loss last week with seven carries for 22 yards and caught both targets for 22 yards. Dowdle left the game in the second quarter with a toe injury, was cleared and returned to play in the second half but then left for good after appearing to re-injure the same toe. Keep an eye on his status in practice this week, as there's a good chance he'll be limited, thus leaving his status for Sunday's contest against the Bengals in question.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers visit the division-rival Browns for a Week 4 road tilt. He sat out Pittsburgh's Week 3 victory with a toe injury he sustained in Week 2, and it looks like he's in real jeopardy of missing a second consecutive contest. Dowdle didn't practice at all last week and was not present at Monday's walkthrough session, which isn't a great sign for his availability on a short week. He'll have to practice in some capacity if he hopes to face Cleveland's sixth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (17.1) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers host the Colts in a battle between 2-2 teams in Week 5. He missed his second consecutive game with a toe injury sustained in Week 2. Jaylen Warren accounted for 20 of 22 touches by running backs during Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss, a pattern that would surely continue if Dowdle remains sidelined against Indianapolis. Monitor his practice participation leading up to a favorable matchup versus the Colts' 23rd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (24.2) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers travel to face off with the Buccaneers in Week 6. After sitting out the last three games with a toe injury, it appears Dowdle is ready to make his return against the 1-4 Bucs. He was brought to Pittsburgh to form a dynamic one-two punch alongside Jaylen Warren, but the incumbent starter has excelled as the featured player out of the backfield, particularly over the last three weeks. Assuming Dowdle takes the field in Week 6, he's likely to work as the clear backup to Warren, so it's best he remains on fantasy benches versus Tampa Bay's sixth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (17.4) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers travel to Paris for a Week 7 meeting with the Saints. He returned from a three-game absence due to a toe injury and registered seven carries for 40 yards and three catches on four targets for nine yards during Pittsburgh's overtime win in Week 6. Dowdle played just 28% of snaps on offense as he works his way back into game shape, and he was pretty effective in limited action, so his workload should rise steadily in Week 7. Jaylen Warren started and earned 16 touches to Dowdle's 10, and there's a good chance they'll both be heavily involved versus a New Orleans defense that ranks dead-last in fantasy points allowed per game (30.7) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers look to even the season series against the Browns in Week 8. He rushed nine times for 41 yards and caught all six of his targets for 45 yards in Week 7 during Pittsburgh's 16-10 victory in Paris. Dowdle finished first in receptions and second in yardage despite being out-touched by starter Jaylen Warren, who turned his 21 touches into 137 scrimmage yards. Dowdle was inactive for the Week 4 loss against Cleveland, so he'll look to make an impact with first place in the AFC North at stake.
outlooksByWeek.10: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers travel to take on the Bengals for a Week 10 AFC North showdown. He had his best showing of the season during Week 8's victory, rushing 15 times for 56 yards and his first touchdown with Pittsburgh. Dowdle battled a toe injury in the early portion of the season, but he's starting to come along, tallying 15 touches in each of his previous two outings. He will look to keep improving versus Cincinnati's 15th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (20.9) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.11: In Week 11, Rico Dowdle and the Steelers visit the Eagles for an interconference tilt. He rushed five times for 26 yards and caught both targets for eight yards during Pittsburgh's 38-18 loss in Week 10. Dowdle and Jaylen Warren (7 carries, 15 yards) both struggled to make much of an impact, as the Steelers managed just 247 total yards of offense on the night. Dowdle could be more involved against an Eagles squad that has lost seven in a row, but Philadelphia's defense is allowing the seventh-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing RBs (19.7) in the league.
outlooksByWeek.12: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers welcome the Broncos to town for a Week 12 meeting on Black Friday. He rushed five times for 15 yards and hauled in four of five targets for 19 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 11 loss. Dowdle again trailed Jaylen Warren in backfield touches, as the former earned nine to the latter's 11. Dowdle will look to make the most of his opportunities against Denver's 25th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (24.9) to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Dowdle signed with the Steelers after nearly identical campaigns with the Cowboys in 2024 (1,328 yards and five TDs on 274 touches) and Panthers in 2025 (1,373 yards and seven TDs on 275 touches). He was effective as a rusher (4.57 yards per carry) and fairly busy as a receiver (50 targets both years) en route to finishing just inside the top 25 in fantasy points per game both seasons. Now in Pittsburgh, the 28-year-old is expected to share work with Jaylen Warren. Earning lead-rusher duties could get Dowdle into the weekly flex discussion, but the ceiling will be low and he'll likely need an injury in order to find his way to consistent fantasy output. Consider him for your bench.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dalton Schultz was second on the Texans in targets behind Nico Collins during the season opener, which matched Schultz's usage last season. After being thrown to eight times in Week 1 against a Bills defense that allowed the fewest yards in the NFL to TEs last season, Schultz is poised for a hefty Week 2 workload against a Bengals defense that surrendered the most yards to his position in 2025. Schultz's role and matchup make him a top-10 fantasy TE for Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dalton Schultz paced the Texans with 12 catches for 140 yards on 14 targets in the Week 2 loss to Cincinnati, working as C.J. Stroud's top target in the absence of WR Nico Collins (hamstring). The veteran TE is the favorite to lead the team in targets if Collins sits in Week 3 against a Colts defense that has allowed the most yards and TDs in the NFL this season. Indianapolis just allowed nine catches for 101 yards and a TD to Chiefs TE Travis Kelce in Week 2. Schultz is locked in as a fantasy TE1 for Week 3 if Collins sits and has a strong argument to stay in that range even if Collins suits up.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dalton Schultz is coming off a disappointing 30-yard outing in Week 3 against the Colts, but he'll remain a fantasy TE1 in Week 4 against the Cowboys if Texans WR Nico Collins (hamstring) misses a third consecutive game. Schultz had 12 catches for 140 yards in Week 2 and is averaging 85 receiving yards per game since Collins got hurt. The Cowboys have struggled to defend TEs, allowing three TDs while forcing only two incompletions on 19 passes to the position. If Collins returns, Schultz will maintain fantasy starter-level upside but with a lower floor due to dropping a spot in the pass-catching hierarchy.
outlooksByWeek.5: Dalton Schultz has recorded just 39 yards in two games since his 140-yard outburst for the Texans in Week 2. He's back to working as a supporting piece in Houston's passing game now that Nico Collins has recovered from a hamstring injury. The 30-year-old TE's inconsistent workloads keep him from being a reliable fantasy starter, and Schultz will be tough to trust in Week 5 against a Titans defense that's holding his position to 27 receiving yards per game, fourth-fewest in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Dalton Schultz leads the Texans with 24 catches heading into a Week 6 matchup with the Jaguars in London, though half of those receptions came in Week 2 against the Bengals. Jacksonville has been among the five stingiest defenses against TEs, limiting the position to 3.6 catches for 34 yards per game. The Jaguars have allowed two TDs to the position, but Schultz has scored only five times in 39 regular-season games since the start of the 2024 season and is still searching for his first TD of the season. Despite Schultz's respectable target volume, he's best left on the bench in single-TE formats in Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.7: Dalton Schultz has exceeded 35 receiving yards just once through Houston's first six games of the season and has yet to score a TD heading into a Week 7 home game against the Giants. He's a secondary option in a Houston passing game that has gotten more production out of its WRs in recent weeks, and Schultz's lack of red-zone involvement compared to other middling TE options makes him an unappealing fantasy play. The Giants have limited TEs to two TDs this season, so Schultz is best left on the bench or waivers since his TD drought is unlikely to end in Week 7.
outlooksByWeek.9: Dalton Schultz isn't a recommended Week 9 fantasy option in most formats for Houston's road game against the Chargers. The veteran TE has 33 catches for 322 yards through Houston's first seven games of the season, but Schultz has yet to score this season, and the Chargers have allowed just one TD to a TE. Frustratingly for Schultz's fantasy managers, backup TE Foster Moreau has scored three TDs on 11 catches this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Dalton Schultz is a borderline fantasy starter at TE for Week 10 against the Browns. He ranks ninth among TEs with 46 receiving yards per game but has yet to score this season and has a meager five TDs in 42 regular-season appearances since the start of the 2024 season. Cleveland has allowed five TDs to the position in nine games, as well as 58 yards per game.
outlooksByWeek.11: Dalton Schultz is coming off a bittersweet Week 10 performance against the Browns. He scored his first touchdown of the season on his only catch but was held to a single reception for the first time all season. The reliable TE is a borderline fantasy starter for Week 11 against the Colts; however, there are certainly higher-upside options to be found at the position. Schultz hasn't topped 45 yards since his 140-yard Week 2 outburst, which occurred while the Texans were without top WR Nico Collins, who has since recovered from a hamstring injury. The Colts have allowed seven TDs in 10 games to TEs, which is tied for fifth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: Dalton Schultz has been held to one catch for 11 yards in each of Houston's last two games, though one of those receptions was his first touchdown of the season. He has been utilized primarily as a blocker in Houston's recent games, so Schultz hasn't benefited much from the strong play of QB C.J. Stroud. In Week 12, Schultz will face a Ravens defense that has struggled to defend TEs, allowing 54 yards per game and seven TDs in 11 games to the position. He's a viable low-end starter at a position that lacks depth, but nobody's getting excited about starting Schultz these days.

player.seasonOutlook: Schultz has been one of the league's most consistent tight ends over the past six years, but with the exception of one season, he hasn't been overly useful in fantasy. Schultz was fantasy's No. 3 tight end in scoring while he was in Dallas in 2021, but he has finished 10th or worse in his other eight campaigns (that includes exactly 10th in three of the past four seasons). In 2025, Schultz ranked sixth or better at the position in targets, catches and yards, but he found the end zone only three times and has now cleared five touchdowns once in his career (eight in 2021). Schultz is a reliable target for QB C.J. Stroud, but with Houston's depth at wide receiver, he simply doesn't offer much upside. Consider him a low-ceiling TE2.

The defending Super Bowl champions, who benefited greatly from what was the league's top-scoring fantasy defense, draw one of the toughest overall schedules as a ?reward.? Only the Cardinals (Weeks 2 and 9), Raiders (Week 10) and Giants (Week 14) appear to be clear plus matchups, and the team must also deal with the offseason losses of S Coby Bryant, edge rusher Boye Mafe and CB Riq Woolen. Mike Macdonald might extract maximum effort from his defenses, but some regression should be expected with this unit.

outlooksByWeek.2: Keenan Allen can still get open on short passes, but the 34-year-old WR's lack of big-play potential limits his fantasy relevance to deeper formats heading into the Colts' Week 2 road game against the Chiefs. Allen caught all six of his targets in his Colts debut, leading the team in receptions, but he totaled just 32 receiving yards. Expect him to post plenty of similar stat lines this season after averaging a career-low 9.6 yards per catch with the Chargers last year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Keenan Allen should get plenty of playing time in Week 3 against the Texans with the Colts' banged-up WR room, but the 34-year-old wideout may not have enough gas in the tank to make much of the opportunity. Allen has exceeded 44 yards just once and failed to score a TD in his last 12 games. Despite that lack of recent production, he's a viable deep-league dart throw, as Indianapolis will be without Alec Pierce (heel) and possibly Ashton Dulin (ankle), leaving Allen as the top option for snaps at WR alongside Josh Downs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Keenan Allen turned back the clock in the Colts' Week 3 win over the Texans, catching six of nine targets for 63 yards and his first TD since Week 7 of the previous season. The 34-year-old WR is poised to maintain an expanded role in Week 4 against Washington's weak secondary as the Colts continue to play without starting WR Alec Pierce (heel), who is on IR. A repeat effort may be too much to ask from Allen, who averaged just 32 yards per game during his 12-game touchdown drought, but he's a viable flex option considering the Commanders have allowed league-high totals in catches and touchdowns to WRs, with 46 and six, respectively.
outlooksByWeek.5: Keenan Allen missed the Colts' Week 4 win over the Commanders due to a groin injury. If the 34-year-old WR is cleared to return in Week 5, he could play a prominent role opposite Josh Downs in a Colts WR room that remains without Alec Pierce (heel), who is on IR. Concerns about Allen's injury and performance limit his viability to deeper formats, even against a Steelers secondary that's giving up 149 receiving yards per game to wide receivers. Allen snapped a 12-game touchdown drought in the Colts' Week 3 win over Houston.
outlooksByWeek.6: Keenan Allen has caught 11 of 18 targets for 108 yards and a TD in his last two outings for the Colts, sandwiched around a Week 4 absence due to a groin injury. The 34-year-old wideout has stepped up in the absence of WR Alec Pierce (heel), who remains on injured reserve ahead of a Week 6 home game against the Titans. Allen lacks Pierce's ability to stretch the field, but a steady diet of short targets should put Allen back into the flex mix in Week 6 against a Titans defense that ranks among the 10 most generous units in terms of catches and yards allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Keenan Allen has turned back the clock over his past three appearances for the Colts, securing 19 of 29 targets for 190 yards and a TD over that span while drawing at least nine targets in every game. The 34-year-old wideout should continue to fill a high-volume role in a Colts WR room that lacks appealing alternatives in the continued absence of Alec Pierce (heel). Allen is a high-floor fantasy WR3 in Week 7 against the Vikings, who are allowing 10 catches for 133 yards per game to WRs. Minnesota's aggressive blitz packages will likely force the Colts into plenty of the quick and short throws on which Allen thrives.
outlooksByWeek.8: Keenan Allen is averaging over seven targets per game and has operated as the Colts' co-No. 1 WR alongside Josh Downs since Alec Pierce went down with a heel injury. Pierce remains on injured reserve ahead of a Week 8 trip to Jacksonville. Allen will be a high-floor flex candidate against a Jaguars defense that's giving up a league-high 210 yards per game to wide receivers. He's averaging 55 receiving yards per game over the past four and has scored one TD this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Keenan Allen has recorded at least six receptions in four of seven appearances for the Colts this season and is likely to maintain a prominent role in Week 9 against a Dallas defense that's giving up 11.9 catches, as well as 164.1 receiving yards and 1.0 TD per game to WRs. Allen leads the Colts with 34 catches despite missing a game, and his 325 receiving yards are just five shy of Josh Downs' team-leading total. However, the 34-year-old Allen has scored just one TD in his last 17 regular-season games, dating back to last season with the Chargers. He remains a rock-solid, high-floor flex play for Week 9.
outlooksByWeek.10: Keenan Allen led the Colts with 40 catches on 58 targets, and his 351 receiving yards were just three shy of Josh Downs' team-leading total, with Allen having played one fewer game. Both players were shipped out of Indianapolis at the trade deadline however, with Allen landing with a San Francisco team in dire need of wide receiver depth. If the veteran gets up to speed on Kyle Shanahan's playbook quickly, he could find himself as Brock Purdy's No. 1 WR in Week 10 against a Cowboys secondary that is tied for 25th in fantasy points were game allowed to wideouts, although Allen could also be as low as No. 3 on the chart chart if Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel are both able to return from their respective injuries.
outlooksByWeek.11: Keenan Allen is coming off an impactful 49ers debut heading into a Week 11 matchup versus Minnesota. After being acquired by San Francisco at the trade deadline, Allen caught five of seven targets for 61 yards this past Sunday in a win over Dallas. Despite having a relatively short amount of time to learn his new team's offense, Allen looked to have good chemistry with QB Brock Purdy, which is an encouraging sign for his production moving forward. His work as a possession receiver could be especially useful against the Vikings, who own the highest blitz rate in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: Keenan Allen has served as a steadying presence in the 49ers' wideout corps ahead of a key NFC West clash against Seattle in Week 12. In his two games since joining San Francisco, Allen has caught eight passes for 99 yards on 11 targets, with seven of those catches resulting in a first down. The veteran wideout is one of many pass-catching mouths for QB Brock Purdy to feed, along with fellow vets Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and George Kittle. The team's WR corps will have to battle a tested Seahawks defense that has given up the second-fewest receptions per game (9.0) to wideouts this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Malik Washington hopes for more efficiency when the Dolphins face the 49ers in Week 2. Washington recorded a healthy eight targets in the team's opener, and while 17.7 yards per catch is encouraging, he caught only three balls. Washington has value as a returner in some leagues, and passing volume will likely remain high with Miami forced to throw from behind in the second half. Even so, Week 2's matchup against a defense that held more talented receivers to just 6.4 yards per target in their opener is a risky endeavor.
outlooksByWeek.3: Malik Washington brings steady volume ahead of the Dolphins' Week 3 matchup with the Chiefs. With Malik Willis under center, Miami has completed just 29 passes through two games, but seven have gone to Washington, who's averaging 6.5 targets. Kansas City's rebuilt secondary has been terrific through two games, allowing just 204 yards to opposing wideouts. Washington seems unlikely to produce any massive numbers, but he also appears to be a steady cog in this limited offense, keeping him on WR3/Flex radars.
outlooksByWeek.4: Malik Washington remains heavily involved in the Dolphins' low-profile passing game heading into Week 4 against the Vikings. Washington is coming off of a season-high 10 targets in Week 3, and has collected three rushing attempts over the last two weeks while also being involved in kickoff returns, but he's yet to top 61 rushing/receiving yards per game or score. Washington's workload creates a viable floor, and Minnesota is allowing a healthy 8.2 yards per target to opposing receivers.
outlooksByWeek.5: Malik Washington's volume continues to be steady for the Dolphins as they enter a Week 5 matchup with the Bengals. He hauled in five of QB Malik WIllis' nine completions in Week 4, his fourth-straight week with at least five targets while increasing his yardage in each of the last three outings. Cincinnati's secondary hasn't allowed an opposing receiver to top 63 yards, and while Washington's workload shouldn't be questioned, his potential remains capped by Miami's low-scoring offense.
outlooksByWeek.7: Malik Washington brings a steady workload but limited yardage potential into the Dolphins' Week 7 matchup with the Jets. Washington has commanded at least five targets in all five games, three times reaching eight or more, but has topped out at 67 yards, operating mainly on short, slot routes while Miami struggles to find a vertical passing game. The Jets are allowing just 7.3 yards per target; Washington too is averaging 7.3 yards per target, setting him up for a rather predictable Week 7 outing where he'll need a heavy target share to offer anything more than bye-week replacement scoring.
outlooksByWeek.8: Malik Washington will hope for additional volume in Week 8 when the Dolphins host the Patriots. He collected a season-low three targets in Week 7, and volume has been the key to his fantasy relevance, having topped 56 yards once all season. It's a low-volume passing game that may be pressed into higher throw rates if Miami falls behind early, but Washington's role underneath doesn't create much upside despite facing a secondary that's surrendering a generous 8.8 yards per target.
outlooksByWeek.9: Malik Washington's usage is on a slight decline as the Dolphins prepare to face the Lions in Week 9. Washington has just nine targets over the last two games, and while he scored his first touchdown of the year in Week 8, he's averaged under 10 yards per reception in three straight games. Detroit is allowing the ninth-most fantasy points to opposing receivers, but they have been far more vulnerable to tight ends. Washington will require higher volume if he's to return meaningful fantasy production.
outlooksByWeek.10: Malik Washington's workload appears to be drying up ahead of the Dolphins' Week 10 matchup with the Colts. Washington averaged 7.2 targets in five games prior to Miami's Week 6 bye but has just 12 looks over the three games since, reaching 28 yards just once. Indianapolis is allowing a generous 8.8 yards per target to opposing wideouts, but with Miami's passing game struggling and Caleb Douglas emerging, Washington's decreasing role will make for a risky play with minimal upside.
outlooksByWeek.11: Malik Washington's opportunities continue to decline as the Dolphins get set to face the Bills in Week 11. Washington recorded three targets in Week 10, the third time in four weeks since Miami's Week 6 bye that he's failed to garner more looks. While Miami figures to throw from behind against Buffalo, Kyle McCord spread his 32 pass attempts in Week 10 across 11 different options, all while rookie Chris Bell was sidelined. With just one touchdown catch all season, Washington doesn't seem likely to pop against a defense that's allowed 11 touchdown catches to wide receivers, the fourth-highest total in the league.
outlooksByWeek.12: Malik Washington brings steady but middling production for the Dolphins into a Week 12 matchup with the Jets. For the fourth time in five games since Miami's Week 6 bye, Washington caught three passes in Week 11, finishing with just 30 yards. With Caleb Douglas emerging as Miami's top option, their low-success passing game hasn't proven capable of sustaining multiple receivers. The Jets are allowing 7.6 yard per target, ranking towards the bottom portion of the middle-tier, not suggesting Washington can break out on limited opportunities.

player.seasonOutlook: Washington was a sixth-round flier back in 2024, but that didn't stop him from working his way into a substantial offensive role last season. Washington finished third on the Dolphins in targets, trailing only Jaylen Waddle and De'Von Achane. Of course, Miami's shaky group of offensive personnel was an obvious factor and Washington's efficiency wasn't very good (5.0 yards per target, 7.0 yards per reception, 0.9 yards per route run). The 25-year-old is fine as a short-range target and occasional rusher, but that's likely his ceiling with newcomers Jalen Tolbert, Chris Bell, Caleb Douglas and Kevin Coleman Jr. expected to factor in at wide receiver.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bhayshul Tuten is likely to get the majority of touches in Jacksonville's backfield in Week 2 against the Broncos, just as he did in the season-opening win over the Browns. Tuten turned 16 touches into 88 yards in Week 1, while Chris Rodriguez and Ameer Abdullah combined for 55 yards on 11 touches, though Rodriguez siphoned some valuable goal-line work. Denver's defense gave up the second-fewest rushing yards in the NFL last season but just allowed Chiefs RBs Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson to combine for 259 scrimmage yards and two TDs in a Week 1 loss. Tuten has RB2 upside given his prominent role in a high-powered Jaguars offense, but he's more of a flex/RB3 for Week 2 against a talented Broncos defense searching for a rebound in their home opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bhayshul Tuten emerged as the clear No. 1 option in Jacksonville's backfield heading into a Week 3 home game against the Patriots, ahead of Chris Rodriguez and pass-catching specialists LeQuint Allen and Ameer Abdullah. Through the first two games of his sophomore season, Tuten turned 28 carries and three targets into 150 scrimmage yards and one TD. The speedster is a viable RB3/flex for Week 3, though expectations should be tempered against a New England defense that's off to an elite start, having allowed just 16 points through two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bhayshul Tuten is averaging 80 scrimmage yards and takes a two-game touchdown streak into Jacksonville's Week 4 road game against the Bengals. Tuten is locked in atop the running back depth chart in one of the league's best offenses, which makes him a reliable fantasy RB2, even with Chris Rodriguez, LeQuint Allen, and Ameer Abdullah siphoning touches here and there. Cincinnati has been better than average against the run, but the Bengals have allowed a league-high 141 receiving yards to RBs, so Tuten is likely to make some plays as a pass-catcher even if running room is hard to come by.
outlooksByWeek.5: Bhayshul Tuten has recorded at least 88 scrimmage yards in three of the first four games of his second season with the Jaguars. The 2025 fourth-round pick has thrived in the lead role, establishing himself as an every-week fantasy RB2. He'll face an Eagles defense in Week 5 that's allowing 106 rushing yards per game to RBs and just surrendered a pair of late rushing scores to the Rams' Kyren Williams in a Week 4 loss. Tuten and the Jaguars will have a 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff Sunday in Week 5 when they face the Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
outlooksByWeek.6: Bhayshul Tuten remains Jacksonville's starting RB heading into a Week 6 matchup with the Texans. He has recorded at least 88 scrimmage yards in four of five games while occupying that role and has two rushing TDs this season. Houston has been among the league's stingiest defenses against RBs, limiting the position to 89 scrimmage yards per game and allowing only three TDs on 103 carries. Tuten's prominent role in an above-average offense keeps him in the fantasy RB2 range despite the tricky Week 6 matchup.
outlooksByWeek.8: Bhayshul Tuten scored two receiving TDs against the Texans in Jacksonville's last action prior to a Week 7 bye. The well-rested lead back is a high-end fantasy RB2 for his return to action in Week 8 against the Colts, who are allowing 134 scrimmage yards per game to RBs. Tuten is averaging 86 scrimmage yards on 18 touches per game and has scored four total TDs through six outings. His well-rounded skill set gives him a high touch floor regardless of how the game unfolds.
outlooksByWeek.10: Bhayshul Tuten played through foot and ankle injuries in Jacksonville's Week 9 win over the Ravens. He scored his fifth touchdown in the past three games but was held to a season-low 29 scrimmage yards, less than half of his previous low of 62 yards from Week 2. Tuten has had a few extra days to recover since last Thursday's win and should be ready to assume his usual role as Jacksonville's top RB for a juicy Week 10 road matchup against the Titans, who are allowing 135 scrimmage yards per game to RBs. He profiles as a low-end RB1 or high-end RB2 in fantasy for Week 10, especially if his practice participation levels indicate that Tuten's injury scare is behind him.
outlooksByWeek.11: Bhayshul Tuten has scored six times during his current four-game TD streak, and he has mustered at least 87 scrimmage yards in seven of Jacksonville's nine games this season. The second-year stud has crept into fantasy RB1 territory ahead of Jacksonville's Week 11 road game against the Giants, who have allowed just four rushing TDs to RBs but also three receiving TDs to the position through nine games. Tuten has five rushing TDs and three receiving scores this season while notching at least 12 carries in every game and two-plus receptions in all but two outings. His well-rounded skill set allows Jacksonville's lead back to maintain a prominent role regardless of the score.
outlooksByWeek.12: Bhayshul Tuten aggravated an ankle injury in Jacksonville's previous game. However, he reportedly avoided a serious injury and could still suit up in Week 12 against the Titans. The 2025 fourth-round pick hasn't missed a game during his second NFL year, though Tuten had a season-low 29 yards in Week 9 while playing through this ankle injury and just posted his second-lowest total of the season with 53 scrimmage yards in Week 11. If Tuten gets the green light, he can be plugged in as a fantasy RB2 against a Titans defense that's allowing 133 scrimmage yards per game to RBs, despite his injury concerns. Should Tuten sit, Chris Rodriguez would be in line to lead Jacksonville's ground game, while LeQuint Allen and Ameer Abdullah offer receiving upside out of the backfield.

player.seasonOutlook: Tuten is positioned to take over lead-back duties in Jacksonville following the offseason departure of Travis Etienne Jr. Tuten played sparingly as a rookie, totaling 83 carries and 14 targets in 15 games. He cleared 10 touches in only one game (a 15-touch, 74-yard effort in Week 11), but he did find the end zone in all four games in which he had at least eight touches. The 2025 fourth-round pick will see some scoring regression (seven TDs on 93 touches), but he flashed in limited work, can contribute as a rusher and receiver, is working in a good offense and has only journeyman Chris Rodriguez Jr. and passing-down specialist LeQuint Allen Jr. as his competition. Tuten is still unproven, but the 23-year-old has a path to a breakout season.

outlooksByWeek.2: KC Concepcion and the Browns are on the road in Week 2 to face the Buccaneers and their eighth-ranked defense in receiving yards allowed to WRs (101). The rookie looked hungry and fought for more on every play, catching four of five targets for 43 yards and rushing three times for 15 yards while losing a fumble. Concepcion's blunder came on a play from behind as he tried to gain extra yardage, but it was still a promising debut for the 24th overall pick in the 2026 draft, as he led the team in receptions and targets. Still, it's difficult to trust anyone on the Browns' offense, especially against a Tampa Bay defense that held Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins to 71 combined yards.
outlooksByWeek.3: KC Concepcion and the Browns return home in Week 3 to host the Panthers and their 18th-ranked passing defense. He finished Cleveland's upset win over the Buccaneers in Week 2 with six catches on six targets for 28 yards and had one rush for minus-6 yards. Concepcion led the team in receptions but was last in average yards per touch at just 4.7. His general involvement on offense is a great sign, but it appears fellow rookie Denzel Boston is the Browns receiver to roster thanks to his big-play ability.
outlooksByWeek.4: KC Concepcion and the Browns welcome Pittsburgh to town for an AFC North clash in Week 4. He caught just two of nine targets for nine yards during Cleveland's upset victory in Week 3. Concepcion wasn't able to contribute much despite tying for the team lead in targets with Harold Fannin Jr., but it's still a positive sign that the Browns are looking to get the ball in his hands. He'll get his first chance to face the division-rival Steelers and their 14th-ranked defense in receiving yards allowed (403) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: KC Concepcion and the Browns visit the Jets for a Week 5 showdown. The rookie receiver finished second on the team in receptions (5) and yardage (64), while his eight targets led the way in Cleveland's Week 4 victory. Concepcion also returned two punts for 10 yards, as it remains clear the Browns want the ball in his hands in a variety of ways for him to shine as a playmaker. However, he'll face a talented Jets secondary that allows 28.5 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks ninth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: KC Concepcion and the Browns welcome the division-rival Ravens to town in Week 6. He caught his lone target for five yards before leaving Cleveland's 17-12 loss in Week 5 with a head injury after a hard hit. Concepcion has entered the league's five-step concussion protocol and will have to be cleared by an independent neurologist before returning to the field. The promising rookie's status should be monitored leading up to a Week 6 showdown against Baltimore's 23rd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per contest (36.2) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: KC Concepcion and the Browns visit the Titans in Week 7. He hauled in four of six targets for 37 yards and rushed twice for two yards during Cleveland's 13-10 comeback win in Week 6. The rookie first-round pick led the team in targets, tied for first in receptions, and was second in yardage behind veteran Jerry Jeudy (69). Concepcion will look to deliver more, along with the entire Browns' offense, versus Tennessee's 24th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (35.9) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: KC Concepcion and the Browns travel to Pittsburgh for a Week 8 divisional clash. He caught eight of 10 targets for 129 yards and had three carries for another 23 yards during Cleveland's comeback victory in Week 7. The rookie broke out with season highs in receptions, yardage and targets while leading the Browns in every category. Concepcion will aim to score his first touchdown of his career versus the Steelers 14th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (30.5) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.10: In Week 10, KC Concepcion and the Browns are home for the first time since Week 6 to host the Texans. He grabbed four of six targets for 85 yards, including a 64-yard touchdown, during Cleveland's 23-22 overtime loss in Week 9. The score was the rookie wideout's first of his young career, and he now sports a 37-437-1 receiving line on 55 targets to go along with 10 carries for 37 yards through nine games. Concepcion will aim to take advantage of a Houston defense allowing the third-most fantasy points per game (38.5) to opposing WRs.
outlooksByWeek.12: KC Concepcion and the Browns are home for a Week 12 clash against Las Vegas on Sunday Night Football. He corralled three of eight targets for 21 yards and rushed once for a six-yard TD during Cleveland's Week 10 victory. Concepcion finished second on the team in targets but was sixth in yardage, although he salvaged the outing with his first career rushing score. He draws a winnable matchup versus a Raiders defense allowing 33.5 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Concepcion was selected by the Browns in the first round of April's draft. He is a quick and explosive short-to-intermediate receiver whose career 27.2% target share topped this entire rookie class. Primarily a slot receiver during his first two seasons at NC State, Concepcion played more on the outside in 2025 at Texas A&M, but he figures to primarily work inside in the pros (career 72% slot rate), while also helping as a rusher and returner. Concepcion will need to fend off the likes of Jerry Jeudy, Harold Fannin Jr. and fellow rookie Denzel Boston for targets in an offense with quarterback issues, so while he has upside, he's best valued as a flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Bass continues to be busy for the high-scoring Bills' offense as they enter a Week 2 matchup with the Lions. In Week 1, Bass made three extra points and three field goals, though none were 50-plus yards. Detroit's defense, particularly the secondary, was suspect a week ago, and the Bills should score plenty, making Bass appealing.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Bass will attempt to bounce back from his first miss of the season when the Bills host the Chargers in Week 3. Bass wasn't afforded a field goal try in Week 2, with Buffalo's offense finding the end zone with ease, but still provided a reasonable floor, hitting five of six extra points. The Bills' offensive efficiency could cap Bass' scoring potential, but historically, the highest-scoring kickers come from the highest-scoring teams.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Bass' opportunities have been limited ahead of a Week 4 matchup between the Bills and Patriots. Through three weeks, Bass has attempted only four field goals, though Buffalo's high-powered offense has generated 12 extra points. New England's defense remains stingy, allowing just 15 total points to opposing kickers, likely keeping Bass out of Week 4 consideration.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Bass remains a stable floor, low ceiling kicking option for the Bills as they enter a Week 5 matchup with the Rams. Bass has collected 14 extra points through four weeks as Buffalo routinely converts drives into touchdowns, but only six field goal attempts, where he's perfect, keeping his scoring capacity limited. The Rams' defense has been stingy to opposing kickers, so don't expect Week 5 to be Bass' breakout party.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Bass is trending up as the Bills get set to face the Raiders in Week 6. Extra points will remain consistent in Buffalo's efficient offense, as Bass has at least three attempts in four of five games, but his field goals increased each of the last three weeks. Las Vegas, however, has been stingy to opposing kicker scoring, surrendering 16 PATs but just six field-goal tries as teams routinely convert drives into touchdowns. Bass' floor Sunday looks stable, but the ceiling may be low.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tyler Bass has increased his workload over the last three weeks as Buffalo gets set to face Baltimore in Week 8. Always a steady source for PATs in Buffalo's high-scoring offense (Bass has made at least two in every game), he went from four field goals across his first three games to nine over his last three. None have come from 50-plus yards, potentially keeping bonus scoring off the table. Baltimore is a mid-tier defense for points allowed to kickers, but they've allowed as many field goal attempts as extra points through seven games, setting Bass up for a strong Week 8.
outlooksByWeek.9: Tyler Bass has been busy for the Bills ahead of a difficult Week 9 matchup with the Vikings. He has multiple field goals in four straight weeks, 12 in total. Bass has added upside to his stable floor in Buffalo's high-scoring offense, which has yielded 21 extra points in seven games. Minnesota has allowed only six field goals and 11 made PATs all season, putting Bass' hot streak in jeopardy.
outlooksByWeek.10: Tyler Bass continues to see heavy volume in the Bills' prolific offense ahead of a Week 10 matchup with the Jets. Seemingly always assured of a handful of PATs, making at least two in every game, Bass has at least three field goals in four straight games, creating double-digit scoring upside with consistency. The Jets are allowing the ninth-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing kickers however, largely due to opponents converting drives into touchdowns, surrendering just 13 field goal attempts in nine games, which should test Bass' current form.
outlooksByWeek.11: Tyler Bass faces unsettled scoring chances when the Bills host the Dolphins in Week 11. After attempting multiple field goals in five straight games, Bass tried just one in Week 10 with Buffalo coasting to a win and converting drives into touchdowns. That script seems likely to manifest again in Week 11 against an overmatched Miami defense, so while Bass will have a multi-PAT floor, his ceiling could be capped.
outlooksByWeek.12: Tyler Bass continues to thrive in the Bills' potent offense ahead of a Week 12 matchup with the Chiefs. He converted four of five field goal attempts and two extra points in Week 11, his fifth game in his last six with at least three field goals. While the Chiefs have allowed only 12 PATs in 10 games, they've surrendered 22 field goals, and with Buffalo likely to test that defense more than other opponents, Bass should again earn enough scoring chances to merit heavy fantasy consideration.

outlooksByWeek.2: Isaac TeSlaa remains a touchdown-dependent option as the Lions take on the Bills in Week 2. TeSlaa was unable to convert on his one target in Week 1 against the Saints, which only made season hopes lower for him after a subpar training camp. He also remains the fifth option in the Detroit passing game behind Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Jahmyr Gibbs and Sam LaPorta. Luckily, Buffalo gave up a whopping 40.0 PPR points to Houston wide receivers in Week 1, so this upcoming week could be TeSlaa's chance to return to relevance.
outlooksByWeek.3: Isaac TeSlaa will seek to stay involved as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3. TeSlaa recorded his first catches of the season against the Bills in Week 2, reeling in two of five targets for 26 yards. While his final stat line was still modest, the second-year receiver's five targets are promising. With that being said, he still hasn't done enough to be considered more than a depth option, especially against a New York defense that's been tougher on wide receivers so far this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: Isaac TeSlaa will look to replicate a solid performance as the Lions travel to Carolina in Week 4. TeSlaa started the season quietly with just two catches for 26 yards across the first two games, but he reeled in all three targets for 66 yards against the Jets in Week 3. While this output isn't enough to warrant a start and is more translatable to a stash move, TeSlaa could be in store for more looks. The Panthers have also allowed a second-least 23.2 fantasy points per game to wide receivers on the year.
outlooksByWeek.5: Isaac TeSlaa could continue to have a big role as the Lions play the Cardinals in Week 5. TeSlaa finished Week 4 against the Panthers with season-high targets, catches and yards, reeling in four of eight looks for four catches and 95 yards. After a slow start to the season, the second-year pass catcher has now posted a 7-161-0 receiving line in the last two games. He'll face an Arizona defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to the wide receiver position.
outlooksByWeek.7: Isaac TeSlaa will aim to bounce back as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. After it appeared the second-year pass catcher was starting to carve out a role for himself again, TeSlaa recorded zero catches against the Cardinals before Detroit's bye. Hopefully the second game this year with zero catches was another anomaly, as there is plenty of love to spread with the Lions' high-volume offense. Green Bay has ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.8: Isaac TeSlaa will seek to stay involved as the Lions play the Vikings in Week 8. After a promising stretch from Weeks 2-5, TeSlaa has now recorded just one catch for 10 yards off four targets in his last two games. The young pass catcher will aim to get back to relevance against a Minnesota defense that's ranked fourth in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.10: Isaac TeSlaa will be a secondary option in Detroit's passing offense again in Week 10 against the Patriots. TeSlaa was quiet again in a gritty Week 9 win over Miami, reeling in one of two targets for just nine yards. After a solid stretch from Weeks 2 to 4, the second-year pass catcher has now recorded just two catches for 19 yards in his last four showings. Luckily, he'll face a New England defense that's ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Isaac TeSlaa remains a touchdown-dependent option heading into Week 11 as the Lions play the Buccaneers. TeSlaa found his first score of the season in a Week 10 win over the Patriots, but he was quiet otherwise. The second-year pass catcher has now recorded 13 catches for 225 yards and a touchdown across nine showings this season. He'll be hard to trust against a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked 11th in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.12: Isaac TeSlaa will look to take better advantage of his targets as the Lions play the Bears in Week 12. TeSlaa was unable to record a catch in Week 11 against the Buccaneers, even off three targets. The second-year pass catcher has had a volatile season after finding the end zone six times in his rookie campaign. He'll face a Chicago defense that's ranked a tough 10th in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.

player.seasonOutlook: TeSlaa is a candidate for a Year 2 leap as the favorite for No. 3 WR duties in Detroit behind Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams. TeSlaa barely played as a rookie (27 total targets), but he had a very specific role and, believe it or not, tied for 11th in the entire NFL with 11 end zone targets. That helped lead to six touchdowns, four of which came when his snaps increased during Detroit's final six games. The 2025 third-round pick has a big size edge on both St. Brown and Williams, so while consistent targets are a long shot, he's still likely to remain busy near the goal line. TeSlaa won't be more than a boom/bust situational target most weeks, but if one of the starters misses time, he'll be on the flex radar. Consider him with a late pick.

The first team to make it through a season without recording an interception since the category began being tracked in 1933, the Jets finished last in defensive fantasy scoring last season. Hey, they can only go up from here, right? Perhaps, but offseason additions of LB Demario Davis, S Minkah Fitzpatrick and LB David Bailey (the No. 2 overall pick in the draft) hardly vault this unit into the position's upper echelon. They do get a great matchup against the Titans in Week 1, though, so there's that?

outlooksByWeek.2: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to operate as Carolina's top pass catcher in the Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. McMillan caught just five passes for 75 yards and lost a fumble in last week's loss, despite the game ending with the most points ever scored in a Week 1 contest. He was out-shined by third-year wideout Jalen Coker, who paced Carolina's receiving corps in targets (nine), receptions (eight), yards (138) and touchdowns (two). McMillan will look to return to form in Week 2, but he's in for a tough matchup against a Falcons defense that gave up just 22.4 PPR fantasy points to wideouts in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain one of the Panthers' top targets in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. McMillan bounced back in Week 2 after a lackluster Week 1 performance, catching five of 10 targets for 101 yards while leading the team in receiving. The 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year is tied with Jalen Coker for the most targets on Carolina (18) entering Week 3, which is a positive sign for both players' outlooks going forward. With the Panthers' offensive success through two games, McMillan should be in for a great Week 3 matchup, especially while facing a Browns defense that's given up four receiving touchdowns to WRs through two contests.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tetairoa McMillan will look to bounce back from an underwhelming performance in the Panthers' Week 4 matchup against the Lions. The 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year was held to just two catches for 17 yards in the Week 3 loss to the Browns, the second-fewest yards he's ever recorded in an NFL game. Despite this, McMillan has an extremely positive outlook going forward, as both Jalen Coker (quadriceps) and Xavier Legette (knee) are dealing with injuries, making him the clear number one target. Additionally, McMillan is in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a Lions defense that's allowed 39.0 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain the Panthers' top receiving option in the Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. McMillan is coming off the best performance of his young career in the Week 4 win over the Lions, recording career highs in targets (16), receptions (14) and yards (192) while scoring two touchdowns. He ranks ninth in the NFL in receiving yards per game (96.3) through four appearances this season, leading Carolina in yards, targets and receptions. Expect McMillan to remain productive in Week 6 against an Eagles secondary that's allowed 38.6 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain one of Carolina's top wideouts in the Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers. McMillan has been one of the league's most productive wideouts this season, catching 32 of 48 targets for 471 yards and two touchdowns in just five contests. He's averaged 94.2 receiving yards per game, the seventh-best mark in the NFL, and is expected to continue benefitting from the Panthers' aggressive style of offense (40.2 pass attempts per game). Additionally, McMillan is in for a favorable Week 7 matchup against a Buccaneers secondary that's allowed 32.2 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain the Panthers' top wideout in the Week 8 matchup against the Packers. Despite Carolina's offensive struggles in the Week 7 loss to the Buccaneers, McMillan was relatively productive, catching four of six targets for 40 yards. On the season, the second-year pro has nabbed 36 of 54 targets for 511 yards (11th-most in the NFL) and two touchdowns in just six contests. He could find success in Week 8 against a Packers secondary that's given up six receiving touchdowns to opposing WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain the Panthers' top wideout in the Week 9 matchup against the Broncos. Following his huge performance against the Lions in Week 4 (14-192-2), McMillan has cooled off, catching just 16 of 26 targets for 184 yards and no scores over Carolina's last three games. Despite this, McMillan ranks 11th in the NFL in receiving yards per game (81.1) 12th in targets per game (9.3), which suggests more production is coming in the near future. However, he's in for a tough Week 9 matchup against a Denver secondary that's allowed just 27.5 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain the Panthers' top wideout during the Week 10 matchup against the Saints. McMillan salvaged his fantasy day with a late score in the Week 9 loss to the Broncos, catching four of six targets for 56 yards. The Arizona product has cooled down since his monstrous performance in Week 4 (14-192-2), averaging 5.0 receptions and 60.0 receiving yards per game over his last four contests. Despite this, McMillan could find success against a Saints secondary that's allowed 31.7 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain Carolina's top wideout during the Week 11 matchup against the Ravens. McMillan was limited to just three catches on seven targets during the Week 10 win over the Saints, his fewest reception total since the Week 3 loss to the Browns. However, he ranked first on the team in targets while the rest of Carolina's receiver room combined for five targets, which is positive sign for McMillan's fantasy outlook going forward. McMillan could thrive against the Ravens in Week 11, as they have given up 34.3 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts through nine games this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain the Panthers' top wideout during the Week 12 matchup against the Buccaneers. McMillan had a nice bounce-back performance in the Week 11 win over the Ravens, catching six of nine targets for 71 yards and a score. The second-year pro is averaging team-highs in targets (8.7), receptions (5.5) and receiving yards per game (73.1), which bodes well for his fantasy outlook going forward. McMillan is in for a tough Week 12 matchup, however, as the Buccaneers' defense has allowed just 30.4 fantasy points per game to opposing wide-receiver rooms this year.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year, McMillan is a candidate to make the leap into the "elite" conversation at wide receiver this season. The 2025 eighth overall pick was very busy as a rookie (top 15 among WRs in snaps, routes, target share, targets, yards, end zone targets and touchdowns) and, while he finished 16th among receivers in fantasy points (22nd PPG), he lacked upside, producing only one top-10 outing (Week 9). Improving on a 56% catch rate will be key in Year 2, though that would require improvement from Bryce Young. McMillan, 23, remains positioned as Carolina's clear top target and, though Young's limitations may cap his ceiling a bit, McMillan's talent/usage combo supplies him with top-10 upside. He's safest as a midrange fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: TreVeyon Henderson could make his season debut in Week 2 when the Patriots host the Steelers. Henderson missed last week due to an ankle injury but has returned to practice ahead of the matchup. Pass-blocking concerns were rumored to be an issue during the preseason, and facing a Steelers defense that rushes the passer well may keep Henderson on the sideline more than managers would like, in addition to a potentially limited role in his first game back. Pittsburgh allowed a mere 3.8 yards per carry in Week 1 but did allow 90 receiving yards to running backs, albeit that was Bijan Robinson. Split touches in a likely low-scoring game would require Henderson's patented big-play ability for him to be fantasy relevant.
outlooksByWeek.3: TreVeyon Henderson will look to build on an impressive debut when New England faces Jacksonville in Week 3. After missing Week 1 due to an ankle injury, Henderson shouldered 16 carries in Week 2, putting up 76 yards and a touchdown. While he wasn't targeted in the passing game, Henderson showed his elite big-play ability. Rhamondre Stevenson was an afterthought after losing an early fumble, but with New England struggling to pass the ball effectively, this has the look of a run-first, split backfield. Jacksonville is allowing just 3.2 yards per carry and 110 total rushing yards through two weeks, which will keep Henderson's Week 3 expectations in check.
outlooksByWeek.4: TreVeyon Henderson remains mired in a split backfield for the Patriots ahead of their Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Henderson's snap share dropped from 60% to 35% in Week 3 as the Patriots played from behind, forcing Rhamondre Stevenson into a pass-blocking role. With only one catch through two games, Henderson isn't getting many opportunities to create his signature big play. Facing a defense that's allowing just 3.9 yards per carry while being more vulnerable to receiving backs, Henderson figures to be a boom-or-bust option.
outlooksByWeek.5: TreVeyon Henderson will seek chunk plays in the Patriots' Week 5 matchup against a vulnerable Raiders run defense. Henderson had one more rush than Rhamondre Stevenson in this shared backfield in Week 4 but converted his 14 carries into only 42 yards. Henderson has not been a factor in the passing game, catching just one ball on the season. Las Vegas is allowing 4.97 yards per carry and has been picked apart by Kenneth Walker and Omarion Hampton, so Henderson appears set up for an ideal opportunity at a few long runs even if the volume won't be high.
outlooksByWeek.6: TreVeyon Henderson is uncertain for Week 6 when the Patriots face the Jets due to an ankle injury. When healthy, he hasn't logged more than a 37% snap share in any of the last three games and has only two catches on the season. The Jets have not faced a prolific rushing offense through five games but have allowed two opposing backs to gain at least 99 yards. If active, a split role with Rhamondre Stevenson caps Henderson's appeal against a defense allowing a stingy 4.3 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.7: TreVeyon Henderson figures to handle a modest workload in the Patriots' Week 7 matchup against the Bears. Making a surprise appearance in Week 6 after suffering a high-ankle sprain, Henderson recorded seven carries for 31 yards while also catching his third pass of the season. Rhamondre Stevenson continues to garner a bigger workload but has plodded to a career-low 3.7 yards per carry. Until New England trusts Henderson in pass protection and ball security, however, a change in roles appears unlikely. Facing a Chicago defense on a short turnaround with Week 7's Thursday night kickoff, Henderson will need to solve a run defense that's allowed just three touchdowns to date.
outlooksByWeek.8: TreVeyon Henderson's declining role in the Patriots' rushing approach leads to low expectations in a Week 8 matchup against the Dolphins. He has logged single-digit carries in three straight games and sits with a 3.9 yards per carry average after a 5.1 mark as a rookie. He's also only caught four passes, an area where Miami has been particularly vulnerable against running backs. With New England seemingly happy to distribute the workload across multiple players, an uptick in usage for Henderson appears unlikely.
outlooksByWeek.9: TreVeyon Henderson will look to return from an illness that cost him Week 8 when the Patriots face the Packers in Week 9. Henderson has just 14 carries over his last three healthy games and has added only five catches all season. Always a big-play threat, Henderson doesn't appear to be in a spot to pop a long run against a Packers defense that's allowed only four runs of 20 or more yards through eight games.
outlooksByWeek.10: TreVeyon Henderson is uncertain to face the Lions in Week 10 due to an ongoing illness when the Patriots travel to Munich. Henderson has not played since Week 7, and New England has a bye week following their travels, which will allow Henderson additional time to recover. With Rhamondre Stevenson dealing with a knee injury, Corey Kiner could lead this backfield against a defense that is allowing the third-fewest fantasy points to opposing rushers.

player.seasonOutlook: Henderson enters Year 2 after a roller-coaster rookie campaign in which he delivered three huge fantasy performances (28-plus points in all three) but otherwise played second fiddle to Rhamondre Stevenson (8.3 points per game in his other 14 games). Though his role was limited, Henderson was effective, averaging 5.1 yards per carry (eighth best) and catching 83% of his targets while scoring 10 touchdowns. The 2025 second-round pick is a candidate for a similar role in 2026, but it's unlikely that Stevenson will completely disappear after he also had a strong 2025. Henderson is safest as a bench option, but there's upside for a lot more if the 23-year-old is promoted to a lead role.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bijan Robinson will continue to lead Atlanta's offense in a Week 2 divisional matchup against the Panthers. Robinson received a whopping 29 touches in Week 1, tying Ashton Jeanty for the second-most in the NFL. The Texas product looked explosive despite the Falcons' offensive struggles, which is a good sign for his outlook going forward. Robinson is in for a great matchup as well, with the Panthers defense allowing 291 rushing yards and six rushing touchdowns in a Week 1 loss to the Bears.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bijan Robinson is expected to lead the Falcons' offense in the Week 3 matchup against the Packers, whose defense has given up 22.9 PPR fantasy points per game to running backs this season. Despite Atlanta's offensive struggles through two weeks, Robinson has continued to produce, having recorded 254 total yards and a touchdown on 48 touches. With Michael Penix back at the helm for the Week 3 contest, Robinson should be in for even more production. Additionally, he's in for a favorable matchup, as Green Bay's defense has allowed three rushing touchdowns in its first two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bijan Robinson is expected to continue being the main playmaker on the Falcons' offense in the Week 4 matchup against the Saints. Robinson has been stellar despite Atlanta's offensive struggles three weeks into the season, accounting for 467 total yards and three touchdowns. He's already recorded 79 touches (26.3 per game) this year, suggesting this massive fantasy output will continue as the season progresses. Additionally, Robinson is in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a Saints defense that's allowed 27.9 PPR fantasy points per game to the RB position.
outlooksByWeek.5: Bijan Robinson is expected to continue leading Atlanta's offense during the Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. Robinson has excelled through the Falcons' first four games, averaging 153.5 total yards per game and scoring five touchdowns on 99 touches. He ranks second in the NFL in total yards and will likely remain the focal point of a Falcons offense that's averaged 40 points per game over their last two contests. Despite this, Robinson is in for a difficult Wek 5 matchup against a Ravens defense that's allowed just 19.1 fantasy points per game to RBs this year.
outlooksByWeek.6: Bijan Robinson will lead Atlanta's offensive attack in the Week 6 matchup against the Bears. Robinson remained one of fantasy's top running backs in Week 5 despite the overtime loss, totaling 128 yards on 21 touches. He ranks as the No. 3 RB in all of fantasy through five contests, averaging a whopping 26.3 points per game. He could be in for a tough Week 6 matchup, however, as Chicago's defense has given up just 18.8 fantasy points per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Bijan Robinson is expected to remain the focal point of the Falcons' offense in the Week 7 matchup against the 49ers. Robinson logged a season-low nine carries in the Week 6 loss to the Bears, as Atlanta was trailing by 24 points in the second half. Despite this, he remained productive when given the opportunities, averaging 6.8 yards per carry. Expect Robinson to bounce back and remain one of fantasy's top running backs in Week 7, as San Francisco's defense has allowed 24.5 fantasy points per game to opposing RBs through five contests.
outlooksByWeek.8: Bijan Robinson is expected to remain the focal point of Atlanta's offense during the Week 8 matchup against the Buccaneers. Robinson has underwhelmed relative to his usual standards over the last two weeks, accounting for 175 total yards and no touchdowns on 36 touches. Despite the lack of scoring, Robinson has still managed to accumulate 4.3 yards per carry during that span. It will likely be tough for Robinson to have a bounce-back performance in Week 8 as well, with Tampa Bay's defense allowing just 18.2 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Bijan Robinson is expected to remain the focal point of Atlanta's offense in the Week 9 matchup against the Bengals.
