Bijan struggled along with the rest of the Falcons' offense in a Week 8 loss to the Buccaneers, rushing 19 times for 76 yards while failing to haul in his lone target. Despite this poor performance, Robinson ranks third in the NFL in touches per game (21.9) and fifth in total yards per game (122.9), so the production will likely follow. He's could thrive against a Bengals defense that just allowed Tony Pollard to account for 137 yards and two touchdowns in a Week 8 win over the Titans.
outlooksByWeek.10: Bijan Robinson is expected to remain the focal point of the Falcons' offense in the Week 10 matchup against the Chiefs. Robinson was one of Atlanta's few bright spots during the Week 9 loss to the Bengals, accumulating 147 yards and a touchdown on 25 touches. The Texas product is currently averaging the third-most touches per game (22.2) in the NFL, suggesting he'll remain one of fantasy's top running backs despite a tough matchup. Kansas City's defense has given up just 20.1 fantasy points per game to opposing RBs through eight games this year.
outlooksByWeek.12: Bijan Robinson is expected to remain the focal point of Atlanta's offense during the Week 12 matchup against the Vikings. Robinson has been one of fantasy's most productive running backs this season, ranking fourth in the NFL in scrimmage yards (120.7) and touches (22.0) per game. Despite the Falcons' recent offensive struggles, Robinson has continued to be impactful for fantasy purposes, averaging 17.3 points per game over the team's last three games. However, he could struggle against a strong Vikings defense that's allowed just 18.7 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Robinson enters his fourth season having finished in the top five among running backs in carries, rushing yards, touches, yards and fantasy points in each of the past two seasons. Also a big factor as a receiver, he has ranked no lower than fifth at the position in routes, targets, receptions and receiving yards in his three pro seasons. In 2025, PFF tracked him with 86 forced missed tackles, which was easily the most among backs. The 24-year-old is in his prime and, though he has a new coach in Kevin Stefanski, his path to a massive offensive role remains clear. He's on the short list of players who should be considered with the first pick of your fantasy draft.

outlooksByWeek.2: Puka Nacua managed to put up decent numbers despite the Rams' dismal offensive performance in their season opener, and he'll look to ramp up his production further in Week 2 against the Giants. Nacua recorded 74 of Matthew Stafford's 155 passing yards in Week 1 versus San Francisco, though he caught just five of nine targets. No other Rams pass catcher had more than three catches or 26 yards, so there's little doubt that Nacua unsurprisingly remains Stafford's favorite target. The Giants' defense looked good in a win over Dallas in Week 1, with top wideout CeeDee Lamb posting a modest 5-44-1 receiving line.
outlooksByWeek.3: Puka Nacua (hip) is uncertain to play in the Rams' Week 3 clash against Denver. Nacua missed Monday's Week 2 game versus the Giants, though he wasn't ruled out until game day. That lends some hope that Nacua could return soon, though his availability for practice during the week should provide more insight about his potential to return versus the Broncos. Should Nacua suit up, he'll draw a tough Denver secondary that have given up just 203 receiving yards to wideouts so far, tied for third-fewest in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Puka Nacua (hip) could return to action when the Rams face Philadelphia in Week 4. Nacua has missed Los Angeles' past two games due to a hip injury, but there is some hope that he can return against the Eagles. While Nacua has been out, Davante Adams has thrived statistically as the Rams' top wideout. The team's receiving corps as a whole could find success against an Eagles squad that ranks 24th in the NFL through three weeks by giving up an average of 24.0 fantasy points per game to wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.5: Puka Nacua appears to be past his early-season injury woes as the Rams prepare to host Buffalo in Week 5. The star wideout missed Weeks 2 and 3 due to a hip/groin issue, but he returned this past Sunday against the Eagles and put up a 9-125-0 receiving line on 12 targets while adding a two-yard rushing touchdown. Nacua logged a 90% percent offensive snap share in the contest, so it doesn't appear that he is going to be inhibited by the injury, at least in terms of playing time, moving forward. The Bills present a good matchup on paper, as they've given up the fourth-most fantasy points (27.8) to wideouts so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Puka Nacua is coming off a massive performance on Monday Night Football with the Rams' Week 6 clash against the Cardinals on tap. Nacua recorded career-best marks with 17 catches and 24 targets in Week 5 against Buffalo, turning that enormous volume into 138 yards and a touchdown while adding nine yards on two carries. The TD was Nacua's first over three games this season, but he's otherwise been massively productive in averaging 10.3 receptions and 112.3 receiving yards per game. The Cardinals don't figure to offer much resistance, as they've yielded the second-most fantasy points per game (28.0) to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Puka Nacua should handle an even bigger role on offense following the news that Davante Adams will miss between six and 10 weeks due to a hamstring injury, so fantasy managers who have rostered Nacua could expect a sizable uptick in both volume and production. Nacua has already compiled 37 receptions for 417 yards and a touchdown through four appearances in 2026, and he's had over 75 receiving yards in every game, so the floor is clearly there. The Week 7 matchup against the Raiders looks like an ideal opportunity to deliver one of his best performances of the season, as Las Vegas has allowed the 10th-most fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.8: Puka Nacua will look to move further beyond a calf injury when the Rams face the Chargers in Week 8. Nacua played through the issue Sunday against Las Vegas and tallied eight catches on 10 targets for 68 yards and a touchdown while adding 10 yards on two carries. He logged an 85 percent offensive snap share, so he didn't seem to be inhibited by the calf injury. With Davante Adams (hamstring) expected to be sidelined several more games, Nacua should continue to see a lot of balls thrown his way against the Chargers, who have yielded a 68.9% catch rate to wideouts, third-worst in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Puka Nacua continues to take on a monumental target share for the Rams heading into a Week 9 matchup versus the Commanders. With Davante Adams (hamstring) sidelined the past two weeks, Nacua has racked up 19 receptions for 148 yards and two touchdowns on 22 targets. Quarterback Matthew Stafford targeted other wideouts just seven times this past Sunday in a win over the Chargers, so Nacua is likely to continue to draw a lot of attention in the passing game, though that should be the case even after Adams returns. The Commanders present a great opportunity for Nacua's continued success, as they rank 20th in the NFL with 21.0 fantasy points per game allowed to wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.10: Puka Nacua is expected to miss the Rams' Week 10 clash against the Cardinals and several weeks beyond that. Nacua suffered a knee injury in this past Sunday's win over Washington and is likely to be placed on IR. Davante Adams (hamstring) remains on IR, so the Rams' WR corps will be led by the likes of Tutu Atwell, Konata Mumpfield and Jordan Whittington.

player.seasonOutlook: Nacua has defied the odds, emerging from fifth-round flier in 2023 to one of the most relied upon and productive offensive players in the league. Nacua has finished each of his three pro seasons sixth or better among receivers in fantasy PPG and peaked with a first-place finish last season. Matthew Stafford's top target led the league with 129 receptions and finished no lower than third among receivers in targets, yardage and touchdowns, while also adding 105 yards and one score as a rusher. More goal-line work would be nice (he has 11 end zone targets over the past two seasons), but Nacua's heavy usage in an elite offense locks in the 25-year-old as arguably the top receiver in fantasy.

outlooksByWeek.2: Josh Allen appears to have the Bills' offense humming as they get set to host the Lions in Week 2. Facing a stout Texans defense last week, Allen accounted for 357 total yards and four touchdowns, against a unit he had previously struggled. No such fears should exist Thursday night, as the Lions' depleted secondary is coming off a game where they allowed 410 yards and three touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Allen has the Bills offense firing on all cylinders heading into a Week 3 matchup with a slumping Chargers squad. Allen has thrown for five touchdowns and run in four in a dominating start to his 2026 season. The Chargers are a desperate team, but they'll also be traveling across the country and have been victimized by far less capable quarterbacks in Jacoby Brissett (277 yards, one TD) and Kirk Cousins (253/3), suggesting the elements are there for Allen to continue his elite production.
outlooksByWeek.4: Josh Allen will look for a bounce-back performance when the Bills face the Patriots in Week 4. Allen failed to throw a touchdown pass in Week 3 for the first time this season, while also tossing his first two interceptions. He rushed for two scores for the third straight week and has at least six carries in three straight games, but he's completed 20 passes or fewer in every outing. He'll oppose a familiar opponent in a Patriots defense that is allowing the third-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks despite yielding three touchdown passes by Trevor Lawrence in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Josh Allen brings a multi-touchdown streak into the Bills' Week 5 matchup at the Rams. Allen has provided multiple scores in each of Buffalo's first four games, throwing six scores while rushing for seven, though his yardage has topped 253 just once. The Rams, however, have allowed only one rushing touchdown and a mere 4.84 yards per pass attempt in what looks to be a battle of elite versus elite.
outlooksByWeek.6: Josh Allen looks to continue to provide elite returns when the Bills face the Raiders in Week 6. Allen is coming off his best rushing effort of the year in Week 5, finishing with 121 yards while scoring on the ground for the eighth time in five games, adding further upside to his reliable passing efforts. Facing a Raiders defense in Week 6 that's allowing the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks likely won't hinder Allen's appeal, as he's set for top-tier dual-threat production Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.8: Josh Allen hopes to have his full complement of receivers when the Bills come out of their bye to host the Ravens in Week 8. He failed to record a rushing score in Week 6 for the first time all season, but threw multiple touchdowns for the first time since Week 2, maintaining his elite fantasy scoring. This game could bring shootout potential if Baltimore gets Lamar Jackson back under center. Baltimore's defense has been solid against opposing passers, allowing just five touchdown passes in six games before being solved by Joe Burrow for four in Week 7. They've also allowed just one rushing touchdown to the position, but Allen is matchup-proof.
outlooksByWeek.9: Josh Allen has his work cut out for him when the Bills face the Vikings in Week 9. He ran for his ninth touchdown in seven games during Week 8 and tossed two touchdown passes for the fourth time this season. He's matchup-proof, but Allen will face constant pressure from Minnesota's heavy blitzing scheme that's allowed only four touchdown passes and 81 rushing yards to opposing quarterbacks through seven games.
outlooksByWeek.10: Josh Allen will seek a bounce-back performance when the Bills face the Jets in Week 10. In Week 9 at Minnesota, Allen, in the face of constant pressure, had his first game of the year with just one touchdown while being held under 250 yards for the fourth time. The Jets have allowed a 16:1 TD:INT ratio through nine games, but Allen threw for only 148 yards and no scores against them in his lone 2025 matchup, suggesting a lower-than-usual ceiling for arguably the league's best quarterback.
outlooksByWeek.11: Josh Allen faces potential workload limitations in the Bills' Week 11 game against the Dolphins. Allen completed only 11 of 21 passes against the Jets in Week 10, his second-lowest volume of the season, as Buffalo was able to get out to a comfortable lead and not challenge the Jets through the air. Another potentially uncompetitive game seems to be looming, and while Allen has 11 rushing touchdowns to go with his 13 passing scores, Miami has allowed quarterbacks to run for just two touchdowns all season. Allen routinely gets his fantasy points, but Week 11 expectations can be tempered slightly.
outlooksByWeek.12: Josh Allen will look to steal the spotlight in a marquee Week 12 Thursday matchup when the Bills face the Chiefs. Allen is coming off a curious outing in Week 11 against the Dolphins, throwing a season-high 45 times while not attempting a rush and tossing a season-high two interceptions. Kansas City has allowed the third-fewest fantasy points per game to quarterbacks, with just eight touchdown passes and no rushing scores through 10 games. Allen is a touch more vulnerable than his typical elite status.

player.seasonOutlook: Allen enters his age-30 campaign having finished each of the past six seasons no worse than second among quarterbacks in fantasy points. Despite seeing less passing volume the past two seasons (14th or lower in pass attempts both years), the 2024 NFL MVP has finished in the top 10 in passing TDs six seasons in a row and remains a major threat with his legs (top five in carries and rushing TDs among quarterbacks all eight seasons of his career). Allen's 21.4 fantasy points per game in 2025 was actually his lowest since 2019, but it was still enough to lead the position. With Joe Brady returning as playcaller and the Bills adding a No. 1 receiver in DJ Moore, Allen remains an elite fantasy quarterback.

outlooksByWeek.2: RJ Harvey's workload was limited in the Broncos' season-opening loss to Kansas City. He gained 18 rushing yards on three carries and caught all four of his targets for 23 yards. That volume was comparable to J.K. Dobbins, who got eight touches-all carries-to Harvey's seven. Turnovers and game flow played a part in limiting their opportunities. Harvey's role as the primary pass-catching back still bodes well for his production in his second NFL season after posting a 47-356-5 line on 58 targets over 17 regular-season games in 2025. He'll get a potentially tough matchup in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that ranked third in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: RJ Harvey wasn't able to suit up in Week 2's win over the Jaguars due to a hamstring strain, putting his availability for a Week 3 matchup against the Rams in question. The second-year back was expected to be the pass-catching complement to J.K. Dobbins for the Broncos, but rookie Jonah Coleman handled that role and didn't look out of place. If Harvey misses too much time, Coleman could take his job, but Dobbins' own checkered injury history could leave Denver patching together a backfield from whoever is healthy.
outlooksByWeek.4: RJ Harvey returned from a one-game absence due to a hamstring strain in Week 2 to contribute to the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams, gaining just six rushing yards on two carries but producing a 6-41-0 line on seven targets. The second-year back is secure in his role as Denver's top pass-catcher out of the backfield while J.K. Dobbins is the main option on early downs. Rookie Jonah Coleman could challenge both once he's back from IR. Harvey will look to make a bigger impact in Week 4 against a 49ers defense that's already given up 17 catches to RBs this season, 28th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: RJ Harvey is coming off the best performance of his career as a pass catcher, posting a 10-68-0 line on 10 targets while adding 25 rushing yards on seven carries in the Broncos' Week 4 loss to the 49ers. Denver trailed most of the game, which helped boost the second-year back's usage, but J.K. Dobbins' struggles in the early-down role are also opening the door for Harvey to log more touches in general, as his seven carries were also a season high. The eventual return of rookie Jonah Coleman from a high-ankle sprain could shake up the backfield further, but until then Harvey's arrow appears to be pointed up. He'll look to build on last week's effort in Week 5 against a Chargers defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs..
outlooksByWeek.6: RJ Harvey all but vanished from the Broncos' game plan in Week 5, gaining seven yards on three carries and failing to catch his only target as Sean Payton returned to play-calling duties. His usage as a pass-catcher was especially disappointing after the second-year back was fed 17 targets over the prior two weeks, turning that volume into a 16-109-0 line. J.K. Dobbins is the preferred early-down option in the backfield, and Harvey's value could become very dependent on game flow as a result. He might see more work in Week 6 if Denver falls behind early against a Seattle team that's in the bottom seven in the league in receptions per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: RJ Harvey found the end zone for the first time in 2026 during the Broncos' overtime win over the Seahawks in Week 6. The second-year running back managed just 56 scrimmage yards on nine touches as he continues to work behind J.K. Dobbins in the backfield. Harvey's target volume has declined since Sean Payton took back play-calling duties, notching only five targets the last two weeks while producing a 3-31-0 line through the air. Harvey will try to reclaim a more consistent role in Week 7 against a Cardinals defense that ranks 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: RJ Harvey logged just five touches in the Broncos' Week 7 win over the Cardinals, but he turned one of them into a 52-yard TD reception in the third quarter to salvage his day. The second-year back finished third in the backfield in workload behind rookie Jonah Coleman (11 touches) and veteran J.K. Dobbins (six touches), but Harvey seems to have a steady role as a passing-down option for Bo Nix. Even if Sean Payton continues to roll with a committee approach to his ground game, Harvey's floor should be relatively secure, even if his ceiling is limited to occasional big plays. He's unlikely to make a splash in Week 8 against a Kansas City defense that ranks seventh in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Harvey will go into his sophomore campaign looking to overtake J.K. Dobbins as Denver's lead back. In the 10 games in which both backs were active last season, Harvey handled 50 carries (20% team share) and 29 targets (9%), compared to Dobbins' 153 carries (60%) and 15 targets (4%). With Dobbins sidelined for the team's remaining nine games (including the playoff run), Harvey handled 115 carries (55%) and 41 targets (13%). He averaged 10.0 fantasy points with Dobbins and 14.2 without, though his 3.3 yards per carry during the final nine games was very poor. The entire Denver backfield is set to return in 2026, so similar deployment (which would include receiving specialist Tyler Badie) could be in the cards, though fourth-round rookie Jonah Coleman could factor in eventually as well. Harvey, 25, has a slight bit of breakout potential, but the committee setup suggests he's safest viewed as no more than a flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Trey McBride marches into a Week 2 matchup versus Seattle fresh off a strong season-opening performance in Arizona's victory against the Chargers. McBride led Cardinals pass catchers across the board with nine catches, 13 targets and 95 yards in that win, and he scored the team's lone passing touchdown. The All-Pro is essentially matchup-proof as possibly the league's premier tight end, though he'll draw a tough Seahawks defense in Week 2. However, it's worth noting that Seattle gave up the sixth-most receiving yards to tight ends during the regular season last year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Trey McBride remains one of the most matchup-proof pass catchers in the league heading into the Cardinals' Week 3 tilt versus San Francisco. Though QB Jacoby Brissett threw for just 95 yards in a loss to Seattle on Sunday, McBride accounted for 41 of those yards and got into the end zone. Through two weeks, McBride leads NFL tight ends with 17 receptions and ranks fourth with 136 receiving yards. The 49ers have been tough on the position so far, though, giving up just seven catches for 52 yards.
outlooksByWeek.4: Trey McBride will look to continue a strong start to the campaign when the Cardinals face the Giants in Week 4. McBride posted a 9-75-0 receiving line in a Week 3 loss to San Francisco, though he didn't get into the end zone for the first time this season. The All-Pro has now logged at least eight catches and at least 10 targets in every contest so far in 2026, giving him the highest floor of any TE in the NFL. The Giants rank in the bottom 10 leaguewide in catch rate and receiving yards allowed to tight ends, so they don't figure to be a threat to McBride's run of success.
outlooksByWeek.5: Trey McBride enters Arizona's Week 5 matchup against Detroit coming off his quietest performance of the season. While the star tight end logged a healthy 12 targets and seven catches against the Giants in Week 4, he finished with just 31 receiving yards. It's a testament to McBride's excellence that such a stat line represents a downturn by his standards, and he'll have a good chance of bouncing back against the Lions. Detroit has allowed a whopping 19.2 fantasy points per game to tight ends so far this season, by far the most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Trey McBride will look to remain productive for Arizona's offense in Week 6 against the Rams. McBride put up another big line against Detroit this past Sunday, catching nine of 10 targets for 66 yards and a touchdown. The star tight end leads all NFL players with 42 receptions this season, and only Amon-Ra St. Brown (57) has more targets than McBride's 56. That should mean McBride gets plenty of opportunities against the Rams, but to find success he'll have to overcome a defense that is giving up the fewest fantasy points per game (3.2) to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Trey McBride remains Arizona's most dependable receiving weapon, compiling 49 receptions for 361 yards and three touchdowns through six games. His 49 catches lead the Cardinals by a wide margin, and his consistent involvement provides a strong PPR foundation despite the team's struggles to generate explosive plays, as he has had at least seven catches in each of his six appearances to date. McBride also led Arizona's passing attack during its Week 6 victory over the Rams, reinforcing his importance to Jacoby Brissett. He faces a relatively neutral matchup against Denver in Week 7, with the Broncos allowing 8.2 fantasy points per game to opposing TEs in 2026, the 15th-best mark in the league. Given his involvement on offense, however, McBride should remain a reliable TE1 regardless of the opponent.
outlooksByWeek.8: Trey McBride has established himself as one of the NFL's top pass catchers ahead of Arizona's Week 8 matchup in Dallas. The star tight end posted season-best marks with 10 catches and 111 yards while scoring his fourth touchdown in Week 7 against Denver. McBride leads the NFL with 59 catches on the campaign, and he's tied for second with 78 targets. The Cowboys rank middle-of-the-pack against tight ends this season, but McBride is as matchup-proof as any player at his position in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Trey McBride doesn't seem likely to slow down despite a quarterback change in Arizona with a Week 9 tilt in Seattle on tap. McBride logged seven receptions for 72 yards and a touchdown on eight targets in an overtime win over Dallas in Week 8, extending his streak of games with seven-plus catches to eight to begin the season. Five of his receptions (including his TD catch) and 52 of his yards came after Gardner Minshew took over at quarterback in the third quarter, so the Cardinals' switch to Minshew as the starter in Week 9 doesn't figure to slow down McBride's production. However, the Seahawks present a tough challenge, as they've given up the fourth-fewest fantasy points per game (5.4) to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Trey McBride could be extremely busy for the Cardinals in Week 10 against the Rams. McBride has already been drawing constant attention in the Arizona passing game, recording at least seven catches and eight targets in all nine of the team's games this year. Now that top wideouts Michael Wilson (neck) and Kendrick Bourne (tibia) are likely done for the season, McBride may be even more heavily targeted. However, he'll be working with rookie QB Carson Beck for the first time due to Gardner Minshew's potentially season-ending elbow injury. McBride will also be going up against a Rams defense that is tied for second in the league in fewest fantasy points per game allowed to tight ends, though he notched a fine 7-53-0 line against them in Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.11: Trey McBride is set to work with rookie quarterback Carson Beck for the second time when the Cardinals travel to Kansas City for a Week 11 clash. McBride had his season-opening streak of logging at least seven receptions snapped this past Sunday in a loss to the Rams, when he managed a quiet 5-37-0 receiving line on five targets. Nonetheless, every part of his line (catches, receiving yardage and targets) led the Cardinals in a game during which Beck struggled mightily to move the ball. There could be an opportunity for McBride to post better numbers against Kansas City, who have given up the fifth-most fantasy points per game (9.8) to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Trey McBride stands as perhaps the Cardinals' last healthy reliable producer ahead of a battle against the Commanders in Week 12. With WR Michael Wilson (neck) done for the season and RB Jeremiyah Love (ankle) still on IR, McBride has been counted on to carry the offense. The star tight end has mostly held up, including in a loss to Kansas City this past Sunday when he posted a 9-54-0 line on a team-high 14 targets. It remains to be seen if McBride will be catching passes from rookie Carson Beck (back) or veteran journeyman Josh Johnson this weekend, but either way he'll likely be the team's offensive focus in a matchup versus a Washington defense that has allowed the second-most fantasy points per game (13.5) to tight ends this season.

player.seasonOutlook: McBride has emerged as one of the league's top pass catchers -- not just tight ends -- as he trails only Ja'Marr Chase in targets (317) and receptions (252) over the past two seasons and is sixth in receiving yards (2,385). McBride led the tight end position in every fantasy-relevant counting stat in 2025, and his league-high 15 top-12 fantasy weeks were six more than any other player at the position. He finished third in the NFL with 17 end zone targets. McBride really thrived when Jacoby Brissett (21.1 PPG) replaced Kyler Murray (12.5) under center, which only adds to his 2026 appeal. The 26-year-old should be on your radar at the first-/second-round turn.

outlooksByWeek.2: James Cook will seek higher volume when the Bills face the Lions in Week 2. Cook logged just 13 carries in a surprisingly high-scoring opener in Houston, going for 57 yards while adding three catches on four targets but failing to reach the end zone after scoring 32 times over the last two seasons. Detroit's defense allowed a fair 4.0 yards per carry last week but is far more vulnerable through the air. Cook's bulk role is unquestioned, keeping his floor stable while a potential shootout creates more chances for him to reach pay dirt.
outlooksByWeek.3: James Cook faces a challenge for fantasy managers in the Bills' Week 3 matchup with the Chargers. Cook and Buffalo's offense motored through Detroit last week, their lead back finishing with 139 total yards and a touchdown. The Chargers have been stingy against the run, allowing a mere 2.98 yards per carry to the likes of Ashton Jeanty and Jeremiah Love. Teams beat them through the air with far greater ease. Cook's role in this potent offense is unquestioned, but tempered expectations in Week 3 appear prudent.
outlooksByWeek.4: James Cook figures to see a heavy workload in Week 4 when the Bills face the Patriots. Cook has consecutive games with at least 21 carries, topping 134 yards in each while scoring twice. He's not heavily involved in the passing game, with just four catches after at least 32 grabs the last two years, and the return of Ty Johnson doesn't inspire confidence. New England just allowed a season-high 73 yards to Jacksonville's lead back Bhayshul Tuten, but they held Cook to 156 yards in two meetings last year. There's little doubt Cook will be heavily featured, but he may need to reach the end zone for a massive Week 4 contribution.
outlooksByWeek.5: James Cook will likely require volume to exploit a Rams defense when the Bills face them in their Week 5 Monday night affair. Cook has now scored in three straight games, but his workload was minimal in Week 4 against New England, rushing a season-low 12 times. The Rams have been stout against the run, not allowing a running back to score through four games and allowing just 3.9 yards per carry, and Cook's lack of involvement in the passing game further dampens the outlook. So long as Buffalo doesn't fall behind early and is forced to throw often, Cook remains stable, but Week 5 profiles as a night to temper lofty expectations.
outlooksByWeek.6: James Cook will seek the end zone for the fifth straight week when the Bills face the Raiders in Week 6. While Cook hasn't been heavily targeted in the passing game, he's posted 100-plus yard rushing efforts in three of his last four outings, garnering at least 21 carries at the same rate. Buffalo is a run-first offense, and the Week 6 matchup is very appealing; Las Vegas allows 5.2 yards per carry, again setting up Cook to be a top-tier option.
outlooksByWeek.8: James Cook needs heavy volume in Week 8 to bolster Buffalo's offense against the Ravens. That hasn't been a problem, as he's amassed 20-plus touches in four of the Bills' first six outings, and he's continued scoring, finding the end zone in each of his last five games. Prior to a Week 7 bye, Cook had his best game as a receiver, possibly elevating his floor even higher. Baltimore is a stout defense against the run, allowing just 3.8 yards per carry, the eighth-lowest total in the league, but they have surrendered 86 yards or more to an opposing back three times. Barring an unexpected change in usage, Cook should be able to flirt with those numbers in Week 8.
outlooksByWeek.9: James Cook brings a six-game scoring streak into the Bills' Week 9 matchup against a stingy Vikings defense. He topped 20 carries in three straight contests and five of seven overall. Cook added five catches for 79 yards in his last two games after just 31 yards in his first five. Minnesota has allowed only four rushing scores through seven games, but a healthy 4.6 yards per carry in a blitz-heavy scheme. With Cook assured of heavy usage, he appears poised for solid production.
outlooksByWeek.10: James Cook's high volume creates a high floor and ceiling heading into the Bills' Week 10 matchup with the Jets. Cook amassed a season-high 31 carries in Week 9, his sixth game in eight outings with 20-plus touches, and has topped 100 total yards at the same ratio while scoring in seven straight games. While the Bills have a short week coming off a Monday night game, nothing has been shown to suggest Cook's role will be reduced. This suggests he'll run wild on a Jets defense that's allowing the eighth-most fantasy points to opposing running backs and one he posted 132 yards and two touchdowns against in one healthy outing in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.11: James Cook brings an eight-game scoring streak into the Bills' Week 11 matchup with the Dolphins. He has at least 18 carries in five straight games and has topped 100 rushing yards in five of nine outings overall. Cook hasn't caught a pass in two weeks, an area where Miami has been vulnerable, allowing five touchdown receptions to running backs, the same number of rushing touchdowns they've surrendered. A quick turnaround to a Week 12 Thursday night game is the only concern for Cook's workload and high-end production.
outlooksByWeek.12: James Cook brings his usual heavy workload and a nine-game scoring streak into the Bills' challenging Week 12 matchup with the Chiefs. Cook collected 22 carries (on only 40 snaps) in Week 11 and is averaging 20.9 carries through 10 games. Despite a short turnaround to Thursday in Week 12, Cook's bell-cow role is secure, and he'll need that volume against a Kansas City front that's allowing just 3.5 yards per carry and six touchdowns.

player.seasonOutlook: Cook signed a contract extension last offseason and was immediately vaulted into the biggest role of his career. The 2022 second-round NFL draft pick finished in the top five among backs in carries, rushing yards (league-high 1,621), touchdowns and yards per carry (5.25). The one limiting factor in Cook's fantasy output was a minimal receiving role (his 40 targets ranked 26th among RBs), but he still came through with a sixth-place finish in fantasy points. The 26-year-old is set to play the same role in Joe Brady's scheme and will be a candidate for his third straight double-digit touchdown campaign as long as Josh Allen is under center. Consider Cook a midrange RB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mike Evans had a strong 49ers debut last Thursday versus the Rams and will next face Miami in Week 2. Evans caught six passes for 49 yards and a touchdown in the season opener, with his score coming on a two-yard connection with quarterback Brock Purdy. The veteran wideout tied with Deebo Samuel for the most targets among SF wideouts, so he looks to have already established a good rapport with Purdy. Evans could be in for another strong performance Sunday against a Titans defense that allowed three passing touchdowns in a Week 1 loss to Las Vegas.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mike Evans picked up a hip injury in San Francisco's win over Miami on Sunday, but early indications suggest he'll be fine for a Week 3 matchup versus the Cardinals. Evans has established a nice rapport with QB Brock Purdy so far this season, as the veteran wideout has caught nine of 10 targets for 103 yards and a touchdown. San Francisco's WR corps has been thinned by the season-ending injury to rookie De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) and Demarcus Robinson's more recent ankle injury, which will likely sideline him for Week 3, so Evans' availability as a reliable target for Purdy has taken on increased importance. Arizona was crushed by star wideout Jaxon Smith-Njigba (9-155-3 receiving line) in Week 2 and has given up four total receiving TDs to wideouts through two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mike Evans' status for San Francisco's Week 4 game against Denver is cloudy due to injuries to his ribs and oblique. Evans was injured in the second quarter of Sunday's win over Arizona and wasn't able to return to the contest. He had gotten off to a strong start prior to the injury, catching three passes for 34 yards and a touchdown. If he's able to suit up against Denver, he'll face a tough challenge against star cornerback Patrick Surtain and a defense that has allowed the NFL's second-lowest catch rate (50.9%) to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Mike Evans seems likely to continue playing through an injury to his ribs for San Francisco's Week 5 matchup against the Seahawks. The veteran wideout toughed out the injury in Week 4 and posted a 5-76-0 receiving line against a tough Broncos secondary. That receiving yardage was a season-high mark for Evans, as were his eight targets. Seattle could pose a significant challenge to the 49ers' receiving corps, however, as the Seahawks have yielded just 12.8 fantasy points per game to wideouts this season -- third-fewest in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Mike Evans is coming off his best game as a member of the 49ers heading into a Week 6 tilt against Washington. Evans posted a 7-113-1 receiving line and added a two-point conversion in a tight win over the division-rival Seahawks this past Sunday. Fellow wideout Deebo Samuel injured his hamstring in the victory, and if he's unable to return for Week 6, Evans' importance in the passing game could be elevated even higher. The Commanders may be ripe for the picking, as they've given up the seventh-most fantasy points per game (25.0) to wideouts on the campaign.
outlooksByWeek.7: Mike Evans and the 49ers are in Atlanta for a Week 7 road tilt. Unfortunately for him, he'll likely be spending it, and possibly more, on the sidelines after aggravating his Achilles injury in San Francisco's Week 6 win. Evans is expected to sit out the contest against the Falcons with a Week 8 bye on the horizon, giving him extra time and recovery for a chance to suit up in Week 9.
outlooksByWeek.9: Mike Evans is expected to return from a one-game absence for the 49ers' Week 9 matchup against Las Vegas. Evans was held out of the Week 7 loss to Atlanta due to a lingering Achilles issue, but San Francisco's Week 8 bye enabled him to get some much-needed rest. It still bears monitoring the veteran wideout's practice participation throughout the week, though, as Achilles injuries can be tricky. Should Evans indeed suit up, he'll face a struggling Raiders defense that has given up the sixth-most fantasy points per game (23.9) to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Mike Evans continues to tend to an Achilles injury and is iffy to suit up for San Francisco in Week 10 against Dallas. The injury has prevented Evans from playing in each of the 49ers' past two games despite the team's bye being sandwiched between those contests. Fellow starting wideout Deebo Samuel (hamstring) has also been out, but the 49ers did add depth at the trade deadline by bringing in Keenan Allen. If Evans can return in Week 10, he'll square off against a Cowboys defense that ranks a poor 25th in the league with 23.4 fantasy points per game allowed to wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.11: Mike Evans reportedly has a chance to return from an Achilles injury for San Francisco's Week 11 tilt against the Vikings. Evans has missed the 49ers' past three games while dealing with right Achilles tendinitis. San Francisco recently acquired veteran Keenan Allen to bolster the wideout corps, and Deebo Samuel returned in Week 10 from a multi-game absence caused by a hamstring injury, but Evans' ability to get back on the field would still be a big boost given his chemistry with QB Brock Purdy this season. The 49ers can use all the help they can get on Sunday Night Football, as Minnesota has been tough on opposing passing games this season and has allowed just 16.2 fantasy points per game to wideouts -- fourth-best in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: Mike Evans will look to move further past his Achilles injury when the 49ers host Seattle in Week 12. Evans returned from a three-game absence this past Sunday against Minnesota and posted a 6-109-1 receiving line on seven targets. The veteran wideout did log just a 42% offensive snap share, so San Francisco may have been easing him back in workload-wise despite his big stat line. Evans could find the sledding tougher against the Seahawks, who have allowed the fewest fantasy points per game (12.8) to wideouts this season, though Evans burned Seattle for a 7-113-1 receiving line in their first meeting this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Evans signed with the 49ers after spending his first 12 NFL seasons with the Buccaneers. The future Hall of Famer famously opened his career with 11 consecutive 1,000-yard seasons, but that streak ended when he missed nine games due to injury last season. Even when active, Evans wasn't his usual, productive self, delivering only one weekly fantasy finish better than 23rd and none better than 11th. Now 33 years old, Evans is past his prime, but he's in line for a decent chunk of the targets, especially near the goal line, in Kyle Shanahan's high-scoring offense. Evans is best valued as a touchdown-dependent WR3/flex with more value in non-PPR formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Parker Washington can safely be started as a fantasy WR2 in Week 2, even with the Jaguars facing a stout Broncos secondary. Washington paced Jacksonville's pass catchers with five catches for 83 yards and a TD on six targets in the season opener. In his last five games, including the playoffs, Washington has racked up 31 catches, 537 yards, and four TDs. Fellow Jaguars WR Brian Thomas (shoulder) tends to draw significant defensive attention, which should keep top Broncos CB Patrick Surtain from shadowing Washington as long as Thomas suits up.
outlooksByWeek.3: Parker Washington has established himself as the No. 1 WR for the Jaguars and is headed toward weekly fantasy WR1 territory ahead of a Week 3 home game against the Patriots. New England has one of the league's best secondaries, led by CB Christian Gonzalez, but Washington appears largely matchup-proof considering the 24-year-old WR just accounted for 98 of Trevor Lawrence's 189 passing yards in a Week 2 loss to Denver that could wind up being Lawrence's worst performance of the season. Washington has at least five catches and 83 receiving yards in each of his last five games, as well as three touchdown catches over that span, so the breakout star can be started with confidence regardless of the opponent.
outlooksByWeek.4: Parker Washington has entered set-and-forget fantasy WR1 territory. Jacksonville's top wideout is likely to thrive in Week 4 against a suspect Bengals secondary that just allowed touchdowns to Steelers WRs Roman Wilson, DK Metcalf, and Ben Skowronek. Despite facing the strong Cleveland, Denver, and New England secondaries, Washington is averaging 74 yards per game with two TDs through three weeks to start 2026 after averaging 116 receiving yards and scoring twice in the final three games of the 2025 regular season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Parker Washington has recorded just 47 receiving yards on eight targets over Jacksonville's last two games after turning 18 targets into 181 yards over the preceding two games. Washington could have an easier time getting back on track in Week 5 if the Eagles are without top cornerback Quinyon Mitchell (knee). Philadelphia's secondary still has plenty of talent but hasn't been nearly as effective this year, allowing four touchdown catches to WRs after holding the position to six TDs in the entire 2025 regular season. Washington leads the Jaguars in all receiving categories and remains a fantasy WR2 at worst despite the recent hiccup.
outlooksByWeek.6: Parker Washington bounced back from a seven-yard Week 4 dud with his best game of the season in Week 5, racking up 124 yards and two TDs against the Eagles. Jacksonville's No. 1 receiver is averaging 70 yards per game and has four TDs through five outings while leading the Jaguars in every receiving category. Washington can be penciled in as a fantasy WR1 for Week 6 against a Texans pass defense that has been surprisingly weak, allowing 193 receiving yards per game to wideouts and six TDs in five games to the position, making it one of the five most generous defenses against wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.8: Parker Washington leads the Jaguars with a 26-416-4 receiving line on 46 targets through the Week 7 bye, and he has a nice opportunity to add to his team-best receiving totals in Week 8 against a Colts defense that may remain without top CB Sauce Gardner (calf) for a second consecutive game. Indianapolis ranks in the middle of the pack against WRs, allowing 142 yards per game to the position, though the Colts give up 25.7 points per game overall, ranking among the league's 10 most generous scoring defenses. Washington is on the fantasy WR1/WR2 borderline for this Week 8 home game.
outlooksByWeek.9: Parker Washington has been held to a single catch twice in Jacksonville's last four games but is averaging a team-high 61.7 receiving yards per game and has four TDs through seven games. His occasional down games keep Washington out of the set-and-forget WR1 range, but he's a high-end fantasy WR2 for a Week 9 road game against the Ravens, who are allowing 177.6 yards per game to WRs. Baltimore has given up plenty of yards to the position but has held wideouts to just five TDs. There are numerous mouths to feed in Jacksonville's high-octane passing game, but Washington continues to have the most upside among the team's pass catchers.
outlooksByWeek.10: Parker Washington has had some quiet second halves with the Jaguars building big leads lately, and a similar scenario could be on the table in Week 10 against the 1-8 Titans. Washington remains a fantasy WR2 with WR1 upside for this matchup, as Trevor Lawrence's top target should feast as long as this game is competitive against a Titans secondary that has surrendered some big individual performances to WRs, allowing at least 117 yards to six different players this season, including a combined 296 yards and three TDs to Cincinnati's WR duo of Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase in Tennessee's most recent game. Washington has failed to exceed two catches in three of his last five games but easily leads the Jaguars with 493 receiving yards and five touchdown catches.
outlooksByWeek.11: Parker Washington capitalized on a favorable Week 10 matchup against the Titans, dissecting Tennessee's league-worst secondary for seven catches, a season-high 152 receiving yards, and a touchdown. Heading into a Week 11 road game against the Giants, Washington leads the Jaguars in all major receiving categories with a 36-645-6 line on 64 targets. He has had some down games with Trevor Lawrence spreading the ball around, as Washington has finished with a single catch on two occasions this season. That lower floor, compared to some of the elite wideouts around the NFL, makes Washington more of a fantasy WR2, but he offers weekly WR1 upside. The Giants are holding wideouts to 127 yards per game but have allowed 11 touchdown catches to the position in nine games.
outlooksByWeek.12: Parker Washington had a career-high 152 receiving yards and a touchdown on seven receptions against the Titans in Week 10, and he'll face the AFC South's cellar-dwellers again in Week 12, this time in Jacksonville. Another fantasy WR1 performance is on the table for Washington against Tennessee's reeling secondary, which has allowed the most catches and receiving yards to wideouts this season. The Titans are giving up 16 catches for 210 yards and 1.1 TDs per game to WRs, while Washington leads the Jaguars with a 44-748-6 receiving line through 10 games, with two of his three 100-yard receiving performances this season coming in the last two weeks.

player.seasonOutlook: A strong finish to the 2025 season has made Washington one of the fascinating breakout candidates of 2026. Though he's primarily worked as a situational/depth player since being drafted in the sixth round in 2023, Washington has flashed when asked to play a bigger role. In 21 games since the start of 2024 in which he had a route participation above 50%, Washington handled a 20% target share and averaged 12.2 fantasy PPG. He surprisingly emerged as Jacksonville's top target late last season, which included a stretch of four straight games with at least nine targets and 19 fantasy points to end the season. The 24-year-old appears to have cemented a big role in Jacksonville, though Jakobi Meyers, Brian Thomas Jr. and perhaps Travis Hunter will battle him for snaps and targets. Washington should be targeted for your flex spot.

The No. 1 D/ST selected on average last season, the Steelers finished a disappointing 14th in fantasy points and scored fewer than five points in 8-of-17 games. They've since overhauled their coaching staff, with Mike McCarthy replacing Mike Tomlin, and Patrick Graham as defensive coordinator, the same role he held with the Raiders from 2022-25. The offseason additions of S Jaquan Brisker and CB Jamel Dean should bolster this unit, and it benefits greatly from one of the softest September and October schedules in the league. Get this D/ST early, but be prepared to seek a replacement after that point.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jason Sanders hopes to maintain his job when the Jets host the Packers in Week 2. Sanders secured the team's opportunities in Week 1 over Blake Grupe, finishing with eight points, more where distance matters as he made two field goals from beyond 50 yards. Assuming he's again active, a higher-scoring game could be on tap against a defense that allowed 39 points in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jason Sanders appears on track to serve as the Jets' kicker again in Week 3 at Detroit. Despite Blake Grupe being on the roster, Sanders has been the active option through two games, hitting four extra points and four of five field goals. Volume is questionable as the Jets' offense isn't highly efficient, and Detroit's defense has allowed just two field goal attempts while surrendering nine touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jason Sanders appears in line to handle kicking duties for the Jets again in Week 4 against the Bears. Sanders has routinely been activated from the practice squad in advance of game day and has made all five of his PATs and 5-of-6 field goals. Chicago has allowed just 17 points to opposing kickers through three weeks, and with the Jets not offering a high-powered offense, Sanders seems unlikely to provide a top-end fantasy return.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jason Sanders hasn't notched many scoring chances in the Jets' limited offense entering Week 5 against the Browns. Through four games, Sanders has eight field goal attempts and only five PATs, keeping his floor and ceiling low. Cleveland has allowed the second-most field goal attempts (12) through four games, so perhaps there's a chance at a productive Week 5 if the Jets continue to be held out of the end zone, but Sanders' overall body of work doesn't suggest fantasy relevance.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jason Sanders hasn't collected ample attempts to create a floor or ceiling ahead of the Jets' Week 6 matchup with the Patriots. Sanders has just seven PATs through five games, while only attempting multiple field goals in two of five outings. New England is the fourth-stingiest team to opposing kickers, allowing just six made field goals, likely again keeping Sanders out of the Week 6 fantasy mix.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jason Sanders could offer bye-week replacement production for the Jets in a Week 7 meeting with the Dolphins. Sanders drilled a season-high four field goals in Week 6, his third game in six appearances with multiple 3-point connections, and he's added multiple PATs at the same 50% clip. Miami's defense has allowed plenty of points to opposing kickers, surrendering three extra point attempts and two field goals per game, setting Sanders up for a potentially busy, high-scoring Week 7.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jason Sanders hasn't been a high-scoring option in the Jets' limited offense ahead of a Week 8 matchup with the Raiders. Through seven games, Sanders has only 10 PATs while making one or two field goals in five of those outings. The Raiders are allowing the 10th-fewest fantasy points to kickers, as opponents routinely convert drives into touchdowns (24 PATs, just 10 field goal attempts). There are likely safer kickers available for Week 8 fantasy production.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jason Sanders' opportunities have been uneven for the Jets ahead of a Week 9 game against the Chiefs. For the second time in three weeks and third time overall in Week 8, Sanders attempted four field goals. Unfortunately, he has four games with just one made 3-pointer, while three times collecting one or zero PATs. Kansas City has allowed 15 field goals through seven games but only 10 PATs, so while suggesting the Jets will have stalled drives is fair, field goals likely won't keep them competitive, making Sanders a risky Week 9 option.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jason Sanders brings a high ceiling into the Jets' Week 10 game against the Bills. He has attempted at least four field goals in consecutive games and three of his last four, with the Jets' offense failing to convert drives into touchdowns, evident by just six PATs over this four-game stretch. Buffalo is allowing the eighth-fewest fantasy points to opposing kickers, and field goals aren't likely to help the Jets in Week 10, but Sanders' recent run of scoring puts him in the streaming mix.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jason Sanders surged into fantasy relevance for an inefficient Jets offense ahead of a Week 11 matchup with the Chargers. The Jets have been kept out of the end zone in consecutive games, forcing Sanders to kick four field goals in each outing, something he's now done in four of their last five games. Sanders has double-digit scoring potential against a defense that's allowing the fourth-most fantasy points per game to opposing kickers.
outlooksByWeek.12: JJason Sanders continues to get multiple scoring opportunities for the Jets ahead of a Week 12 matchup with the Dolphins. For the fourth consecutive week and fifth time in six games, Sanders made at least two field goals, giving him 19 in that stretch to go with nine extra points. The outlier was a Week 7 matchup with Miami, as the Jets played from behind and chose not to kick. With Kyle McCord under center for Miami in Week 12, that's not a likely script, suggesting Sanders can again be busy against a defense allowing the fifth-most fantasy points per game to kickers.

player.seasonOutlook: This already highly regarded defense only got stronger in June with the acquisition of two-time Defensive Player of the Year (2023, 2025) Myles Garrett. He wasn't their only addition, as CBs Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson were brought in from the Chiefs. Expect another productive season from this unit, though it does face one of the tougher early-season schedules, with the 49ers (Week 1), Broncos (3), Eagles (4) and Bills (5) among their first five opponents. The Rams' second-half schedule is one of the easiest, meaning they might be a better in-season trade target than a draft-day pickup.

Raheem Morris comes aboard as the 49ers' defensive coordinator this season, and between questions about his scheme's fit to the team's personnel and the injuries that have struck this roster in recent years, it's tough to get fully behind a rebound from this D/ST. An opening-week road matchup with the Rams should make this a no-go draft day pick, but the 49ers could have their matchup moments later in the year.

outlooksByWeek.2: Davante Adams will look to get going when the Rams face the Giants in Week 2. Adams was held to a 3-26-0 receiving line versus San Francisco in Week 1, though the Rams' offense as a whole was held in check. Adams did draw the second-most targets (six) among Los Angeles pass catchers, as he continued to draw QB Matthew Stafford's attention more than any other player besides star Puka Nacua (nine targets). The Giants largely held Dallas' passing game in check during a Week 1 win, with no Cowboys pass catcher logging more than five receptions or 44 yards.
outlooksByWeek.3: Davante Adams is coming off an explosive Monday Night Football performance heading into the Rams' Week 3 matchup versus Denver. With Puka Nacua sidelined by a hip injury, Adams starred Monday against the Giants, posting a massive 10-195-2 line. Nacua's status for Week 3 is up in the air, and Adams would logically stand to be Matthew Stafford's top target again if Nacua can't suit up. However, Denver is a tough matchup, as the Broncos have yielded just 6.55 yards per target to wideouts this season (fifth-best in the NFL).
outlooksByWeek.4: Davante Adams has looked resurgent of late ahead of the Rams' Week 4 tilt against the Eagles. With Puka Nacua (hip) sidelined the past two weeks, Adams has gone off for 15 catches, 332 yards and two touchdowns. However, Nacua has a chance to return to action against Philadelphia, which would potentially result in Adams seeing less attention from QB Matthew Stafford. With that said, both wideouts could feast against an Eagles defense that ranks in the bottom half of the league by giving up an average of 157.7 receiving yards per game to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Davante Adams is coming off a quiet performance as the Rams prepare to host the Bills in Week 5. Against Philadelphia in Week 4, Adams was held to four catches for 32 yards. That was a substantial downturn after Adams averaged 7.5 catches and 166 yards over the previous two contests, though he still got a healthy nine targets against the Eagles. It has to be mentioned that star wideout Puka Nacua returned to action in Week 4 and posted a 9-125-0 line, while Adams' big performances the previous two weeks took place in games Nacua missed due to injury. Both WRs could find success against the Bills, who have allowed the fourth-most receiving yards to wideouts this year.
outlooksByWeek.6: Davante Adams is coming off his second two-TD game of the campaign heading into the Rams' Week 6 battle versus Arizona. Against Buffalo on Monday Night Football in Week 5, Adams recorded a 5-51-2 line on seven targets. While he lagged far behind Puka Nacua's 24 targets and massive 17-138-1 line, Adams continued to work as a top option for QB Matthew Stafford in the red zone. That could come in handy again versus the Cardinals, who have surrendered a league-high 10 receiving touchdowns to wide receivers so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Davante Adams was placed on Injured Reserve due to a ruptured left hamstring in the Week 6 loss to the Cardinals and is expected to be sidelined until after the Rams' Week 11 bye in a best-case scenario. With Adams out, names such as Jordan Whittington, Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell should be in line for more targets, while established threats in the passing game like Puka Nacua, Tyler Higbee and Kyren Williams will also be in line for an uptick in numbers. Adams has 30 catches for 480 yards and four touchdonwns this season, and he will be sidelined for the time being, so he'll miss out on the chance of being productive in a favorable Week 7 matchup against a below-average Raiders defense.
outlooksByWeek.12: Davante Adams (hamstring) is expected to remain sidelined for the Rams' Week 12 clash against Green Bay. That may be due in part to the game taking part on Wednesday, but even with an extended break afterward, the star wideout is currently thought to have just an "outside chance" to suit up in Week 13 against Kansas City. Los Angeles will turn to a hodgepodge of wideouts, including Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels, Tutu Atwell and Xavier Smith, for wideout production in the absence of Adams and Puka Nacua (knee/toe).

player.seasonOutlook: Adams' first season in Los Angeles was a success, as the veteran led the wide receiver position in touchdowns for the third time in the past six seasons. His 27 end zone targets were nine more than any other player and he now sits second in that category (148) and in TDs from scrimmage (117) since entering the league in 2014. Adams' ninth-place finish in fantasy PPG marked his ninth top-10 in his past 10 seasons. Now 33 years old, he isn't targeted as much as in years past (24% target share in 2025 was his lowest since 2016), but he's the clear No. 2 behind Puka Nacua in the Rams' elite, Matthew Stafford-led offense. Adams' heavy usage near the goal line helps cement him as a fine fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyle Pitts will look to rebound for a disappointing Week 1 performance in the Falcons' Week 2 matchup against the Panthers. Pitts failed to haul in his lone target during last week's loss, with Bijan Robinson and Drake London combining for a 73.6% of Cooper Rush's targets. Despite this, Pitts could very well rebound against a Panthers defense that just allowed a whopping 59 points in Week 1, as they also gave up 11.5 PPR fantasy points to tight ends. His rebound could depend on Atlanta's quarterback situation, with both Michael Penix (knee) and Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) looking to return from injury in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyle Pitts will look to bounce back from a slow start in the Falcons' Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Pitts has really struggled along with the majority of Atlanta's offense throughout the first two weeks, catching just one of four targets for 15 yards. However, he could really benefit from the return of Michael Penix as the team's starting quarterback heading into Week 3. While Penix was healthy during the 2025 season, Pitts averaged 4.2 receptions and 41.7 yards per game -- a vast difference from his 2026 production thus far. He's also in for a favorable matchup, as the Packers' defense has allowed 12.0 PPR fantasy points per game to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kyle Pitts will look to bounce back from a disappointing start in the Falcons' Week 4 matchup against the Saints. Despite Michael Penix returning to the field in the Week 3 win over the Packers, Pitts' role remained limited, catching just one of two targets for five yards. He was overshadowed by Drake London (9-194-0) and appears to be operating as the Falcons' No. 3 pass catcher, also behind Bijan Robinson (16 targets to Pitts' six). However, Pitts could rebound in Week 4, as the Saints' defense has allowed 20.7 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kyle Pitts is expected to remain one of the Falcons' top pass catchers in the Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. Pitts had his most productive game of the season in the Week 4 win over the Saints, catching all three of his targets for 47 yards. Despite this, he played just 50% of Atlanta's offensive snaps and has now logged an average of 2.3 targets per game, suggesting he may not be as involved in the team's offensive game plan as he has been in past years. Additionally, Pitts in in for a difficult Week 5 matchup against a Ravens defense that's allowed just 10.4 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kyle Pitts will look to stay hot in the Falcons' Week 6 matchup against the Bears. Pitts had his best game of the 2026 season during the Week 5 overtime loss to the Ravens, catching five of six targets for 42 yards and a touchdown. Since the return of quarterback Michael Penix (ribs) in Week 3, Pitts has caught nine of 11 targets for 94 yards and a touchdown. Pitts could struggle in Week 6, however, as he's set to face a Chicago defense that's allowed just 7.7 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kyle Pitts is expected to remain one of the Falcons' top offensive weapons in the Week 7 matchup against the 49ers. Pitts is coming off his best performance of the season in a Week 6 loss to the Bears, catching five of seven targets for 60 yards and two scores. It appears as if he's been more involved in Atlanta's offensive game plan over the last two weeks, catching 10 of 13 targets for 102 yards and three touchdowns after receiving just nine targets in his first four contests. However, Pitts could struggle against a solid 49ers defense that's given up just 8.4 fantasy points per game to opposing TEs through five games this year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Kyle Pitts will look to stay hot in the Falcons' Week 8 matchup against the Buccaneers. Pitts has really found a rhythm over the last three weeks after a slow start to the season, catching 15 of 18 targets for 124 yards and four touchdowns over that span. Despite ranking fourth on the team in yards, Pitts has tallied the third-most targets (27) and the most touchdowns (four) on the Falcons through seven weeks. He's in for a favorable matchup as well, with the Buccaneers' defense giving up 16.2 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Kyle Pitts is expected to remain one of the Falcons' top pass catchers in the Week 9 matchup against the Bengals. Despite catching just two of five targets for six yards in the Week 8 loss to the Buccaneers, Pitts finished tied for the most receptions in the game. Prior to last week's loss, Pitts appeared to be finding his groove, averaging 5.0 receptions, 41.3 yards and 1.3 touchdowns per game from Weeks 5 through 7. He's expected to bounce back against a Bengals defense that's given up 15.9 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this year.
outlooksByWeek.10: Kyle Pitts will look to rebound from a poor performance in Atlanta's Week 10 matchup against the Chiefs. After catching 15 of 18 targets for 122 yards and four touchdowns from Weeks 5 through 7, Pitts has really struggled. In his last two games, the Florida product has hauled in just five of 10 targets for 29 yards and no scores, making him too inconsistent to be a week-in and week-out starter going forward. However, he's in for a favorable Week 10 matchup against a Kansas City defense that's allowed 17.0 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Kyle Pitts is expected to remain one of Atlanta's top pass catchers during the Week 12 matchup against the Vikings. Pitts has been relatively inconsistent this year, catching 29 of 42 targets for 270 yards and four touchdowns. He's tallied fewer than 10 fantasy points in seven of 10 games this season, making him hard to trust as a weekly fantasy starter. This is especially true due to a difficult matchup in Week 12, as Minnesota's defense has allowed just 9.9 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season, the best mark in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Right when it seemed like Pitts might never live up to the hype, the 2021 No. 4 pick put together the best season of his career. Pitts finished second among tight ends in routes, targets, catches, yards and fantasy points, setting career highs in all but the yardage category. He scored five touchdowns and has increased his total in that category (by exactly one) each season in the league. Pitts did a big chunk of his damage with Kirk Cousins under center (some with WR Drake London sidelined), which is notable as Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr. are set to battle for the Atlanta QB job. There's some obvious risk here considering Pitts finished 17th or lower in PPG three straight seasons before 2025, but he nonetheless enters his age-25 season as a priority target in the Atlanta offense. Consider him a midrange TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: T.J. Hockenson will look to build off a solid Week 1 performance as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Hockenson was second in targets against the Packers behind Justin Jefferson, reeling in four of five targets for 36 yards and a touchdown. The veteran tight end was a go-to outlet for veteran Carson Wentz, and he could continue to be one no matter who lines up under center moving forward. He'll take on a Bears defense that allowed a middle-of-the-pack 11.5 PPR points to Carolina tight ends in a high-scoring season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: T.J. Hockenson will look to stay involved as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Hockenson saw his volume go down a bit in Week 2 against the Bears, reeling in just three catches for 29 yards. The starting tight end looks like he'll be a touchdown-dependent fantasy option. With that being said, Kyler Murray is slated to start Sunday, and he's been known to rely on his tight ends in the past. The Bucs have allowed 22.1 PPR points per game to TEs so far this season, 31st in the lerague.
outlooksByWeek.4: T.J. Hockenson remains a secondary option in Minnesota's passing game heading into Week 4 against the Dolphins. Other than a 4-36-1 receiving line in Week 1, Hockenson has looked otherwise like a disappointment this season. The veteran tight end has stayed consistent with four targets in back-to-back games, but he's converted them into a combined five catches for 40 yards in the stretch. Miami has allowed the fourth-most fantasy points per game to tight ends (16), but even then, Hock will likely need to find the end zone to have relevance beyond a depth option.
outlooksByWeek.5: T.J. Hockenson will look to build on a huge performance as the Vikings play New Orleans in Week 5. Hockenson finished Week 4 with a bang after starting the season quietly, catching all 13 of his targets for a whopping 119 yards. The veteran tight end could continue to be an outlet for quarterback Kyler Murray, especially with some struggles from the quarterback so far. The Saints have ranked bottom five against fantasy TEs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: T.J. Hockenson holds a questionable tag heading into Minnesota's Week 7 matchup against the Colts. Hockenson sustained a concussion in the Vikings' Week 5 win over the Saints heading into the bye, so his status is up in the air just two weeks later. The veteran tight end will need to clear protocol if he hopes to get back on the field, and that'll be evident through his practice availability. Indianapolis has ranked in the middle against fantasy TEs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.8: T.J. Hockenson remains a top option in Minnesota's passing game heading into Week 8 against the Lions. Hockenson found the end zone for the second time of the season in a Week 7 win over the Colts, and he complemented his score with four catches for 35 yards. The veteran tight end has now brought in 27 catches for 237 yards and two touchdowns this season. He enters a favorable matchup versus a Detroit defense that's ranked 32nd in fantasy points allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.9: T.J. Hockenson will look to keep his touchdown streak alive as the Vikings play the Bills in Week 9. Hockenson was a key piece in Minnesota's passing game once again in a Week 8 loss to Detroit, reeling in four of five targets for 58 yards and a touchdown. The veteran has now registered five targets in back-to-back games, and he's found the end zone in each as well. He'll face a Buffalo defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy TEs this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: T.J. Hockenson should remain a top option in Minnesota's passing game versus the Packers in Week 10. Hockenson led the Vikings in catches in a Week 9 loss to the Bills, which was a quiet four grabs for 33 yards. The veteran tight end has now reeled in four receptions in each of the last three weeks. The addition of Kirk Cousins at the trade deadline to be the new starting QB may not be good news for Hockenson, however, as he's more likely to targets wideouts Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison than Kyler Murray or Carson Wentz did. Hockenson will face a Green Bay defense that he posted a 4-36-1 receiving line against in Week 1, and which ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.11: T.J. Hockenson will aim to make a return as the Vikings play the 49ers in Week 11. Hockenson missed his first game of the year in Week 10 against the Packers due to a wrist and chest injury. The veteran was unable to participate in practice prior to the matchup, so he'll likely need to get out there if he hopes to play in Mexico City. San Francisco has ranked middle-of-the-pack in fantasy points allowed to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: T.J. Hockenson figures to be a top option in Minnesota's passing offense against the Falcons in Week 12. Hockenson was busy again in his return to the field against the 49ers in Week 11, catching six of seven targets for 55 yards. The veteran has now brought in four of more catches in each of his last four games. Atlanta has ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy TEs so far this season.

player.seasonOutlook: It's been a rough go for Hockenson since he peaked with a 95-960-5 receiving line in 2023. He tore an ACL in Week 16 that season and was limited to a 41-455-0 receiving line upon his return in 10 games in 2024. A bounce-back was expected in 2025, but Hockenson handled a weak 16% target share (his lowest since he was a rookie in 2019) and couldn't overcome the team's QB woes en route to a 51-438-3 showing. Hockenson has now followed four straight top-seven fantasy PPG seasons with finishes of 17th and 26th. The 29-year-old could very well get back on track in 2026, but he'll need solid play from Kyler Murray. Hockenson is a fringe TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaxon Smith-Njigba will likely have Drew Lock throwing balls to him when Seattle faces Arizona in Week 2. Lock took over for an injured Sam Darnold (glute) in the Seahawks' season-opening win, and Darnold is expected to miss Week 2. However, the QB change didn't impact Smith-Njigba's stat line in Week 1, as he finished with eight catches for 122 yards and a touchdown. He's as matchup-proof a WR as there is in the NFL, and he's set to take on a Cardinals defense that allowed Ladd McConkey (ribs) to put up a 5-82-1 line in less than a full game during a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaxon Smith-Njigba enters Seattle's Week 3 matchup versus Washington riding the wave of a three-touchdown performance. That effort came Sunday versus Arizona, when the star wideout also caught nine passes for 155 yards. Smith-Njigba worked with backup QB Drew Lock in that victory due to Sam Darnold being sidelined with a glute injury, and it seems that the reigning AP NFL Offensive Player of the Year is more than capable up dominating regardless of who is throwing him the ball. Smith-Njigba could be in for another huge effort against a Commanders defense that has surrendered the 10th-most receiving yards (337) to wideouts through two contests.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is coming off another huge game as Seattle prepares to host the Chargers in Week 4. Versus Washington in Week 3, Smith-Njigba recorded 10 catches on 14 targets for 128 yards and two touchdowns. The star receiver has logged at least eight catches, 120 yards and one score in each of his first three games this season, making him among fantasy's most valuable assets once again. The Chargers don't figure to be able to contain Smith-Njigba given that they're allowing 9.76 yards per target to wideouts, fifth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jaxon Smith-Njigba should once again be the centerpiece of Seattle's passing game in a big Week 5 clash against the 49ers. The star wideout posted a fine 5-76-0 receiving line against the Chargers this past Sunday, though he didn't get into the end zone for the first time this season. It's telling that despite his final stats being quite adequate, Smith-Njigba's targets, catches and yards were each a season-low mark in what has been a standout campaign thus far. San Francisco is allowing just 6.96 yards per target to wideouts though four weeks (fifth-best in the league), though Smith-Njigba has proven to be essentially matchup-proof since the beginning of last season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is arguably the most matchup-proof wideout in the NFL, but he could be challenged in Seattle's Week 6 matchup in Denver. Smith-Njigba caught five of eight targets for 102 yards and a touchdown against San Francisco in a loss this past Sunday. He's now recorded at least 100 receiving yards and one touchdown in four of his five games this season, and Smith-Njigba leads the league with 583 receiving yards. He'll be matched up Week 6 against a Broncos defense that has allowed the third-lowest catch rate (54.5%) to wideouts, but Smith-Njigba figures to get a big boost by not having to face star cornerback Patrick Surtain, who is expected to miss the contest due to an ankle injury.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jaxon Smith-Njigba and the Seahawks return home for a Week 7 interconference clash against the Chiefs on Sunday Night Football. He corralled 12 of 16 targets for 134 yards during Seattle's overtime loss in Week 6, setting season highs in receptions and targets. Smith-Njigba paced his team in all receiving categories despite a quiet first half, and he now owns a 49-717-7 line on 65 targets through six outings. Kansas City's top-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (21.2) to WRs will try to make it tough on the 2025 Offensive Player of the Year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jaxon Smith-Njigba continues to look like an unstoppable force for Seattle with a Week 8 matchup against the Bears on tap. Smith-Njigba caught nine of 12 targets for 150 yards and a touchdown against Kansas City this past Sunday, marking his sixth performance of 100-plus receiving yards through seven weeks. The budding superstar leads the NFL with 867 receiving yards and eight receiving touchdowns through seven weeks. He'll next face a Chicago defense that ranks 30th in the NFL with 9.51 yards per target yielded to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is on a record-setting pace heading into Seattle's Week 9 game against the Cardinals. Though the Seahawks were crushed by Chicago in Week 8, Smith-Njigba put up another big game with six catches for 118 yards and a touchdown on 11 targets. The star wideout is up to a league-leading 985 receiving yards through eight weeks, putting him on pace to break the NFL's all-time record for receiving yards in a season. He'll have a prime opportunity to add onto his impressive stat line in Week 9, as the Cardinals are tied for 25th in the league with 23.7 fantasy points per game allowed to wideouts on the campaign.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is coming off a rare quiet game with Seattle's Week 10 matchup in Las Vegas on tap. The All-Pro wideout logged a season-low 51 yards on seven catches this past Sunday against Arizona, though he still drew a healthy 10 targets. Drew Lock (oblique) started at quarterback for the Seahawks in that contest and is expected to do so again in Week 10, as Sam Darnold (quadriceps/rib) is likely to remain sidelined. Regardless, Smith-Njigba could feast against a Raiders defense that ranks 26th in the league with 23.6 fantasy points per game allowed to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.12: Jaxon Smith-Njigba will look to continue his dominant campaign in Seattle's Week 12 matchup versus San Francisco. Prior to the Seahawks' Week 11 bye, Smith-Njigba had one of his biggest games of the season, posting an 8-171-1 receiving line against the Raiders. The talented wideout has worked with QB Drew Lock over Seattle's past two games, but Sam Darnold (quad/ribs) is expected to be back for this Sunday's NFC West clash. Smith-Njigba recorded 102 receiving yards and a touchdown when Seattle and San Francisco battled in Week 5, and the 49ers have given up 11 receiving TDs to wideouts this season, tied for eighth-most in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning NFL Offensive Player of the Year, Smith-Njigba is fresh off a breakout season in which he paced all receivers in target share (36%), receiving yards (1,793), air yards (1,858) and yards per route run (3.8), while finishing no lower than fourth in targets, catches, touchdowns and fantasy points. JSN delivered top-10 fantasy weeks 10 times throughout 2025 and scored at least 13 points in 16 of 17 games.
