The 24-year-old is just now entering his prime and remains well positioned to handle one-third of the targets in Seattle's Sam Darnold-led offense. Smith-Njigba is an elite fantasy option who should be off the board in the early-to-middle part of Round 1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jordan Mason will be out for Week 2 as the Vikings take on the Bears. Mason hurt his thumb after week one against the Packers, and he's now been placed on IR for the injury. The fifth-year running back (30 of 65 offensive snaps) and Aaron Jones (29 snaps) had a near-even split of the backfield reps against the Packers, with Mason leading the ground attack with 59 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries. Unfortunately, Mason will now be out for at least the next four weeks, priming Jones for a bigger role moving forward.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jordan Mason will be out for Week 3 as the Vikings take on the Bears. Mason hurt his thumb after week one against the Packers, and he's been placed on IR for the injury. Mason will remain sidelined for at least the next three weeks, priming veteran Aaron Jones for a continued big role moving forward.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jordan Mason will remain out for Week 4 as the Vikings take on the Dolphins. Mason hurt his thumb in Week 1 against the Packers, and he's been on IR since. The fifth-year running back will remain sidelined for at least the next two weeks, priming veteran Aaron Jones for a continued big role.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jordan Mason will remain out for Week 5 as the Vikings travel to New Orleans. Mason hurt his thumb in Week 1 against the Packers, and he's been on IR since. The fifth-year running back will remain sidelined for at least the next week, priming veteran Aaron Jones for a continued big role.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jordan Mason could be set to return as the Vikings play the Colts in Week 7. Mason has been sidelined since Week 1 with a thumb injury that landed him on IR, but he's set to return to practice this week. The fifth-year running back's return should put him at least in a complementary role with veteran Aaron Jones. Indianapolis' defense has ranked 23rd in fantasy points allowed to RBs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jordan Mason could be in line for a workhorse role as the Vikings travel to Detroit in Week 8. Mason made his return from IR in Week 7 against the Colts and logged 15 carries for 68 yards, leading the ground game with Aaron Jones hurting his knee in the matchup. Jones' status is up in the air moving forward, so Mason's role could be even bigger if he has full command of the backfield. The Lions have ranked 11th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jordan Mason should remain a part of a two-punch backfield in Week 9 as the Vikings play the Bills. Mason led Minnesota's backfield with eight carries in a Week 8 loss to the Lions, but he finished with just 20 yards compared to Aaron Jones' five carries for 22 yards. The current timeshare between the two could continue to keep both in check, but Buffalo ranking 29th in fantasy points allowed to RBs is favorable.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jordan Mason will look to see a more favorable game script in Week 10 as the Vikings travel to Green Bay. Mason rushed just six times for 35 yards and reeled in two of three targets for seven yards in a Week 9 loss to the Bills. As expected, the fifth-year ball carrier has been a part of a two-pronged backfield approach next to Aaron Jones this season, but it appears Mason might be the more efficient of the pair. The Packers have ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jordan Mason will aim to make the most of his situation as the Vikings play the 49ers in Week 11. Mason led Minnesota's backfield with 16 carries for 59 yards in a Week 10 win over the Packers, but teammate Aaron Jones punched in the only touchdown from the pair. Mason has yet to record a score in four outings since returning from a thumb injury, but he's put together 182 rushing yards on 4.0 yards per carry. He'll face a San Francisco defense that's ranked 11th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Jordan Mason will aim to make the most of his usage as the Vikings play the Falcons in Week 12. Mason rushed the ball 11 times for 38 yards and logged one catch for minus-1 yard in a Week 11 loss to the 49ers. He's now been unable to find the end zone since returning from injury in Week 7, and his receiving work has yet to make up for otherwise subpar rushing totals. Luckily, Atlanta has ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Mason is back for his second season in Minnesota and will battle 31-year-old Aaron Jones Sr. for backfield opportunities. Mason's role was almost exactly as expected last season, as he was utilized often as a rusher (9.9 carries per game), but a nonfactor as a receiver (1.0 targets per game). Mason reached 13 fantasy points just once in his 16 games and it was a 23.6-point effort in Week 3, one of five games Jones missed. Mason, 27, is an effective rusher -- his 5.10 YPC ranks third and his 2.42 YAC second among 54 RBs with 350-plus carries since he entered the league -- but adding so little as a receiver (34 career targets) severely limits his fantasy output. Even if Jones were to miss time, Mason would max out as a flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Malik Nabers looked spry in his first game of the season for the Giants, a Week 1 victory over the Cowboys. Nabers led the G-Men in targets with nine, en route to six catches for 69 yards in the 28-20 triumph. Nabers showed no ill effects from his torn ACL and meniscus suffered in Week 4 last season, only needing to get tackled by his new head coach John Harbaugh to prove he could take a hit before suiting up. In Week 2, Nabers will face a Rams defense that struggled against the pass in Week 1, allowing 205 passing yards and three passing scores in its season opener. Nabers will likely be covered by all-pro cornerback Trent McDuffie, though.
outlooksByWeek.3: Malik Nabers injured his shoulder last game for the Giants. He was able to return, but still may undergo additional testing this week. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, Nabers will likely see his stock take a hit. However, if Nabers can suit up in Week 3, the Giants will face a lackluster Titans defense allowing 233.5 passing yards per clash, which is 20th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Malik Nabers shook off a shoulder injury to suit up last game for the Giants. He responded with five catches on six targets, though racked up a mere 26 yards in the 12-7 win over the Titans. Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which limits the upside for Nabers. However, Winston should remain under center in Week 4 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Malik Nabers exploded last game for 112 yards and a touchdown to help the Giants to victory. Nabers snagged six passes on seven targets for a season-high in terms of receiving yardage. He and quarterback Jameis Winston finally appeared to be on the same page. In Week 5, Nabers and company will face a Commanders defense that has struggled to defend the pass.  Washington has allowed 11 passing scores, which is tied for last in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders are yielding 242.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Malik Nabers saw a staggering 20 targets last game for the Giants. Nabers parlayed those ample opportunities into 11 grabs for 121 yards and a touchdown. It was the second-straight 100-yard outing for Nabers, who also scored for the second-consecutive contest. His newfound connection with starting quarterback Jameis Winston has been evident. In Week 6, the G-Men face a New Orleans defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026. The Saints are allowing just 212.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the league. However, New Orleans has also given up eight passing scores already, which is tied for 20th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Malik Nabers continues his torrid stretch for the Giants. Nabers snagged 12 passes for 165 yards in the 34-27 loss to the Saints. Regardless of who has lined up under center for the Giants, Nabers has crossed the 100-yard receiving mark in three-straight contests. He has racked up a staggering 35 targets in his last two outings alone. In Week 7, Nabers has another favorable matchup against a leaky Texans secondary. Houston is allowing 246 passing yards per contest, which is 27th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Malik Nabers has crossed the 100-yard receiving mark in four-straight contests for the Giants. Nabers has racked up a staggering 36 catches for 509 yards and two touchdowns over that span. He has drawn an insane 51 targets during that time period, an average of nearly 13 opportunities per clash. In Week 9, the G-Men will face a scuffling Eagles squad. Philadelphia's defense is allowing 235.4 passing yards per tilt, which is 24th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Malik Nabers had a four-game 100-yard receiving streak snapped last game for the Giants. Nabers had five catches for 43 yards in the 19-11 win over the Eagles. He was targeted eight times. He will look to rebound in Week 10 against a porous Washington secondary. The Commanders are allowing 240 passing yards per clash, which is 30th in the league. In addition, Washington has surrendered 16 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.11: Malik Nabers had a costly fumble last game for the Giants. Nabers had the ball punched out of his hands in scoring territory versus the Commanders, who ultimately defeated the G-Men by a score of 24-21. Nabers has now been held under 50 yards receiving in each of the last two outings following a dazzling four-game stretch of 100-yard outbursts. In Week 11, he will look to rebound against a Jacksonville defense that has been mediocre against the pass in 2026. The Jags are allowing 228.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 19th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: Malik Nabers snagged a touchdown pass for the Giants last game. Nabers finished the win over the Jags with seven catches for 55 yards and his third score of the season. Nabers was targeted 12 times, the third time in 2026 he received double-digit targets. In Week 12, the Giants will face a Colts defense allowing 220.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 14th in the NFL. However, Indy has also surrendered 20 throwing scores, which is 28th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Nabers is on the comeback trail after a torn ACL limited him to only four appearances last season. In 18 full games in his career, Nabers has a massive 35% target share (11.3 per game) and he's averaging 18.2 fantasy PPG. As a rookie, the 2024 sixth overall pick finished seventh or better among receivers in targets, receptions, yards and fantasy points despite missing two games and dealing with New York's offensive struggles. Nabers' massive target share allowed him a high floor, as he was a top-30 fantasy scorer in 13 of 15 games, including 10 straight to end the 2024 season. He essentially has a new quarterback (Jaxson Dart threw only three passes his way last season), a new coach (John Harbaugh), a new offensive playcaller (Matt Nagy) and is recovering from the knee, so there are a lot of variables here, but the 23-year-old still holds elite upside. A healthy Nabers should be valued as a mid-to-back-end WR1, but the potential for a slow start needs to be considered on draft day.

outlooksByWeek.2: Aaron Jones is primed to lead Minnesota's backfield in Week 2 at Chicago. Jones (29 of 65 offensive snaps) and Jordan Mason (30 snaps) had a near-even split of the backfield reps in Week 1, but Mason led the ground attack with 59 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries. Jones still remained heavily involved, as he logged 12 rushes for 40 yards and one touchdown. This week and beyond, Jones will be set to lead the backfield with Mason on IR for a thumb injury. Jones will look to make the most of his likely increased opportunities against a Bears defense that allowed 33.7 PPR points to Panthers running backs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Aaron Jones should continue to have a high-usage role as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Jones saw a big workload in Week 2 with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, rushing the ball 23 times for 105 yards. The veteran running back should continue to have a huge role in the coming weeks, while questions remain with the passing game under returning quarterback Kyler Murray. Jones will face a Buccaneers defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 19.5 PPR points per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Aaron Jones should remain a high-volume option as the Vikings play Miami in Week 3. Jones saw a big workload in Week 3 once again with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, rushing the ball 17 times for 58 yards and recording five catches for 34 yards. The veteran running back's high share in the backfield doesn't look to be changing with Mason out another week, even with DeeJay Dallas and Demond Claiborne fighting for touches. Jones will face a Miami defense that's allowed the most fantasy points per game (32.9) to running backs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Aaron Jones will remain a high-usage option as the Vikings travel to New Orleans in Week 5. Jones saw a big workload in Week 4 once again with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, rushing the ball 20 times for 94 yards and recording four catches for 34 yards. The veteran running back's high share in the backfield shouldn't change with Mason out another week, even with DeeJay Dallas and Demond Claiborne fighting for touches. Jones will face a Saints defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack versus fantasy RBs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.7: Aaron Jones could be set to share the backfield in Week 7 as the Vikings play the Colts. Jones logged his best game of the season in Week 5 against the Saints before Minnesota's bye, rushing the ball 25 times for 113 yards and a touchdown. The veteran could unfortunately now be in store for a shared role again, as position mate Jordan Mason is primed to return from IR, but the two have proven to be productive together in the past. Indy's defense has ranked 23rd in fantasy points allowed to RBs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.8: Aaron Jones could be at risk of missing Week 8 as the Vikings travel to Detroit. Jones suffered a knee injury in Minnesota's Week 7 win over the Colts, and he's currently day-to-day. What this means for his status moving forward is unknown until practices start up this week, but it is promising that he avoided a significant injury. The veteran running back logged eight carries for 26 yards before his departure, and it appeared he was still holding a prominent role even with Jordan Mason back on the field. If Jones can get healthy, he'll face a Lions defense that's ranked 11th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Aaron Jones will aim to make the most of his opportunities as the Vikings play the Bills in Week 9. Jones shook off a knee injury and ended up playing in Week 8 against the Lions, but he logged a season-low five carries and 22 rushing yards, with two catches for 18 yards as well. The veteran's output moving forward is likely to remain capped with Jordan Mason sharing the backfield, but the pair could carve out some success versus a Buffalo defense that's ranked 29th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Aaron Jones will look to make the most of his opportunities as the Vikings play the Packers in Week 10. Jones saw just five carries and one target in a Week 9 loss to the Bills, and he took them for 16 yards and five yards, respectively. The veteran running back has now seen his rushing yardage totals drop in three straight games, logging 18 carries in total during that stretch. He's not likely to see crazy value with Jordan Mason active, but a Green Bay defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to RBs is favorable.
outlooksByWeek.11: Aaron Jones will look to build off a solid showing as the Vikings travel to San Francisco in Week 11. Jones did well against his former squad in Week 10, logging 47 rushing yards and a touchdown on 11 carries, along with catching one pass for eight yards. The veteran remains in a timeshare with Jordan Mason, but he still holds some value moving forward. The 49ers have ranked 11th in fantasy points allowed to RBs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.12: Aaron Jones will look to keep his touchdown streak alive as the Vikings play the Falcons in Week 12. Jones rushed the ball eight times for 30 yards and a touchdown, and he caught one pass for 13 yards in a Week 11 loss to the 49ers. While the committee approach of Minnesota's backfield hasn't allowed for dominance for him or Jordan Mason, Jones has been the one to find the end zone more often. Atlanta has ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to running backs this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Jones is back for a third season in Minnesota after an injury-plagued 2025 campaign limited him to 747 yards (his fewest since his rookie season in 2017) and three touchdowns in 12 games. Jones remained fairly busy (11.0 carries and 3.4 targets per game) but didn't perform well, ranking dead last among 65 backs with 50-plus carries in forced missed tackle rate and elusive rating, per PFF. Jones failed to record a single top-10 fantasy outing. Now 31 years old, Jones remains a starter and will get some run, but he's well past his prime and unlikely to return to consistent fantasy output. Jones is best valued as a bench player with occasional flex appeal.

outlooksByWeek.2: Omarion Hampton looked like the clear lead back for the Chargers in their season-opening loss to the Cardinals, taking 12 carries for 43 yards and a touchdown, while backup Keaton Mitchell saw only four carries. Neither RB caught a pass as Justin Herbert had a very narrow target tree under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, connecting with just five different receivers. Hampton had been headed for a big rookie campaign before getting injured, so staying healthy will be the biggest factor in any potential 2026 breakout. He could post better numbers in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that ranked 21st last season in points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Omarion Hampton has been one of the few Chargers who seems to be benefiting from new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. The second-year back racked up 115 scrimmage yards and a touchdown in Week 2's loss to the Raiders, and he's been the clear top option in the backfield, getting 37 touches through two weeks compared to Keaton Mitchell's 10 and Kimani Vidal's zero. Hampton lost a fumble in each game, and that split could begin to shift Mitchell's way if ball security is deemed an issue for the 2025 first-round pick. Hampton could cash in on his bell-cow role in Week 3 against a Bills defense that's allowed four touchdowns to RBs so far, two on the ground and two through the air.
outlooksByWeek.4: Omarion Hampton's workload took a step backward in a Week 3 loss to the Bills, as the Chargers' backfield teeters toward a committee. The second-year back hasn't been awful, producing 214 scrimmage yards and two rushing touchdowns in three games while averaging 3.9 yards per carry, but Keaton Mitchell is averaging 5.0 yards per carry on limited usage and may be a better fit for offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. Kimani Vidal also had his first touches of the season in Buffalo. Hampton is the most talented player of the three on paper, but with the 0-3 Chargers struggling to generate offense, every possible solution will be on the table. He isn't likely to start turning things around in Week 4 against a Seahawks defense that ranks fifth in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Omarion Hampton scored a touchdown for the third time in four games during the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, but his role in the backfield continues to slip. The second-year back's nine carries and 11 touches were season lows for a spark for his unit. Hampton has still been the most productive of the trio this season with 267 scrimmage yards and three rushing TDs, but his 4.0 yards per carry trails Mitchell's, while Keaton Mitchell handled 15 touches and Kimani Vidal got seven, indicating that offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is moving toward a full-blown committee as he searches 4.6 mark. Hampton will try to re-establish himself as the clear No. 1 on the depth chart in Week 5 against a Broncos defense that ranks 26th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Omarion Hampton continues to struggle in offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme while working behind a patchwork Chargers offensive line. Hampton does have three rushing touchdowns in five games, but his 3.7 yards per carry is a significant downturn from his 4.4 mark as a rookie, and he's averaging just 61.2 scrimmage yards per contest. He's also lost snaps and touches to Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal as the backfield devolves into a committee. Hampton will try to find a spark in Week 6 against a Kansas City defense that is tied for 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Omarion Hampton will look to turn his season around coming out of the Chargers' Week 7 bye. He failed to reach 50 scrimmage yards or get into the end zone in his last two games before the break, as Mike McDaniel turned his backfield into a committee. Hampton is the most talented back on the roster, but as long as Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal are garnering significant shares of the workload, all of them will have limited ceilings. Hampton will try to reassert himself as the No. 1 option in Week 8 against a Rams defense that's tied for 14th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Omarion Hampton remains stuck in a backfield committee for the Chargers while running behind an injury-weakened offensive line. Hampton led the team's RBs with 11 touches in a Week 8 loss to the Rams, while Keaton Mitchell got seven touches and Kimani Vidal handled 10, and none of the three managed more than 30 scrimmage yards. Hampton hasn't found the end zone since Week 4, and while he's nominally at the top of the depth chart, his current usage holds little appeal. He's unlikely to break out without significantly more volume in Week 9 against an underperforming Texans defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Omarion Hampton turned 13 carries into a team-high 60 rushing yards in the Chargers' Week 9 loss to the Texans, his second-highest total of the season. Keaton Mitchell handled 10 touches, and Kimani Vidal got eight, as offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel continues to deploy a backfield committee that limits the ceiling of all three players. Hampton appears to be first among equals for now, but the struggles of the entire offense present an extra obstacle for him to overcome. He'll try to build on last week's modest numbers in Week 10 against a Ravens defense that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Omarion Hampton is coming off his best performance of the season in the Chargers' Week 10 win over the Ravens, topping 100 rushing yards for the first time and scoring his first touchdown since Week 4. It was a big step toward Hampton regaining the clear No. 1 job in the backfield, as Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal combined for just seven touches and 18 scrimmage yards. Hampton will look to keep rolling in Week 11 against a Jets defense that's tied for 23rd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Omarion Hampton has re-established himself as the clear No. 1 option in the Chargers' backfield. Over the last three games, the second-year running back has turned 49 carries into 254 rushing yards and a touchdown, averaging a robust 5.2 yards per carry. Keaton Mitchell picked up a knee injury in a Week 11 loss to the Jets, which could leave Kimani Vidal as the primary backup. Hampton will look to keep surging in Week 12 against a Patriots defense that's tied for 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Hampton is primed for a breakout second season following an impressive but injury-shortened rookie campaign. The first-round pick was busy during nine appearances, averaging 13.8 carries and 3.9 targets. He scored five touchdowns, averaged 15.1 fantasy points per game (13th best) and ranked third among backs in forced missed tackle rate, per PFF. With Kimani Vidal and Keaton Mitchell as his primary competition, Hampton has a clear path to lead rusher duties in 2026, and his targets only figure to increase with Greg Roman out and Mike McDaniel in as the team's playcaller. Add in a much-improved offensive line with star tackles Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater back healthy, and Hampton has nothing short of elite upside. Value him as a fringe RB1 with room for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brock Purdy and the 49ers head into a Week 2 tilt against Miami fresh off a big season-opening win over the Rams. Purdy threw for 205 yards and three touchdowns in that contest, connecting with wideouts Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and Demarcus Robinson for the three scores while adding 29 yards on five rushes. It was a big victory against a vaunted NFC West rival that many have pegged as Super Bowl favorites, so San Francisco will look to avoid a letdown in Week 2 against a much less revered Dolphins team. Miami was beaten soundly by the Raiders in Week 1 while allowing QB Kirk Cousins to toss three touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brock Purdy will look to build upon a historic performance when San Francisco faces Arizona in Week 3. Purdy completed 20 of 22 passes for 287 yards and two touchdowns with no turnovers against Miami on Sunday, adding 30 yards and a touchdown on the ground. That stat line made Purdy the second passer in NFL history with 250 passing yards on a 90 performance completion rate in multiple games. The fifth-year signal caller may be without some of his weapons in Week 3 if Mike Evans (hip) and Demarcus Robinson (ankle) need to sit out, though early reports suggest Evans isn't dealing with a serious injury. The Cardinals could have a hard time containing Purdy after giving up 235 passing yards and three TDs to Seattle QB Drew Lock in a Week 2 loss.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brock Purdy will lead the 3-0 49ers in a Week 4 matchup against the Broncos. Purdy threw for 297 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions in a Week 3 win against Arizona, and he currently holds the highest passer rating (133.1) in the NFL. Purdy is also tied for the league lead with nine TD passes, three of which have gone to star tight end George Kittle. However, Denver figures to pose a tough challenge, as the Broncos' defense -- led in the secondary by star cornerback Patrick Surtain -- has limited opponents to a 74.5 passer rating, fifth-best in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Brock Purdy will look to help keep San Francisco's perfect record alive with a win over Seattle in Week 5. Purdy has been outstanding to the begin the campaign, completing 70% of his passes and recording an 11:1 TD:INT. He's also getting great protection from the offensive line, as he's yet to take a sack this season. The Seahawks could pose a stiff challenge, however, as they've collected seven sacks through five games and have allowed the fifth-lowest passer rating (76.2) in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Brock Purdy and the 49ers will look to remain perfect with a Week 6 win over Washington. Purdy was sacked for the first time this season and threw his first pickoff since Week 1 this past Sunday against Seattle, but he also threw two touchdowns to help guide San Francisco to victory. He was especially synched up with veteran wideout Mike Evans, with whom he connected seven times for 113 yards and a score. Purdy could feast on a Commanders defense that has given up 14 passing touchdowns (tied for most in the NFL) and 27.9 fantasy points per game (second-most in the league) to quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Brock Purdy and the 49ers travel to take on the Falcons in Week 7. He completed 21 of 29 pass attempts for 264 yards with one TD and no INTs while rushing five times for 28 yards during San Francisco's 23-17 victory in Week 6. Purdy found seven different receivers as the 49ers improved to 6-0 on the season, but it sounds like they could be without Mike Evans (Achilles) for an extended period of time. Purdy will take aim at Atlanta's 20th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (21.6) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Brock Purdy should be well-rested off the 49ers' bye week for a Week 9 clash against Las Vegas. Purdy will be looking to bounce back from his first multi-turnover game of the campaign, as he threw two interceptions in a Week 7 loss to the Falcons. Despite that performance, Purdy still ranks in the top five leaguewide with a 110.1 QB rating in 2026. He could also be getting a big boost Week 9, as injured wideouts Mike Evans (Achilles), Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and Demarcus Robinson (ankle) all have a chance to return from absences. Purdy should be able to find success against the Raiders, who have allowed a 103.2 QB rating this season, third-worst in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Brock Purdy will continue to push toward MVP consideration when the 49ers face Dallas in Week 10. Purdy helped San Francisco improve to 7-1 this past Sunday with a win over the Raiders during which he threw for 232 yards with two touchdowns and one interception despite working without the team's top two wideouts, Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring). Purdy also ran for 40 yards and a score in the victory, and he currently ranks sixth among NFL quarterbacks with 201 rushing yards on the campaign. Even if Evans and/or Samuel remain out for Week 10, the addition of Keenan Allen at the trade deadline should provide him with a reliable fallback option. Purdy is primed for a big day against a Cowboys defense that ranks 25th in the league by allowing a 99.1 quarterback rating this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Brock Purdy is coming off one of the best performances of his career as the 49ers prepare to host Minnesota in Week 11. Purdy threw for a career-best 389 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions this past Sunday in a win over Dallas. The star quarterback now ranks second among QBs with at least 100 pass attempts in QB rating (115.2) and has posted an impressive 20:5 TD:INT. However, Purdy faces a tough test in the Vikings, who lead the NFL with 37 sacks and have allowed only six passing touchdowns while recording 10 interceptions.
outlooksByWeek.12: Brock Purdy will face another tough defense when the 49ers host Seattle in Week 12. The star quarterback solved Minnesota's previously stingy defense this past Sunday in a 35-10 victory in Mexico City, throwing for 255 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions. Purdy and San Francisco's offense seems to be firing on all cylinders right now, especially after the return of All-Pro wideout Mike Evans. Still, the Seahawks could present a stiffer test than most, as they have yielded the fewest fantasy points per game (14.1) to quarterbacks and held Purdy to a season-low 189 passing yards in their first meeting Week 5.

player.seasonOutlook: Purdy enters his fifth NFL season looking to rebound after injuries caused him to appear in only nine games in 2025. The good news is Purdy played well, scoring 17-plus fantasy points in seven of the nine games, including 26-plus points in three straight games during Weeks 15-17. A highly effective passer and solid contributor as a rusher, Purdy has quietly finished in the top 10 in fantasy points per game in each of the past three seasons. With a good supporting cast led by Christian McCaffrey, George Kittle and free agent additions Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel, Purdy is an underrated mid-to-back-end QB1 in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Luther Burden will look to stay highly involved as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. While Week 1 was the highest-scoring game in NFL history, Burden and Chicago's pass-catching corps were overshadowed by a dominant ground game. The second-year wideout's five catches for 63 yards wasn't bad, but he definitely has potential to be more dominant moving forward. He'll take on a Minnesota defense that gave up a 6-147-2 receiving line to Christian Watson and 6-95-0 to Matthew Golden in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Luther Burden will aim to get things going as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Burden has had a slow start to his sophomore campaign, with just eight catches on 12 targets for 95 yards across two games. He could also be in for even worse output, given the unknowns that come with Tyson Bagent starting under center in place of Caleb Williams (hamstring). Burden will take on a Philadelphia defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 29.4 PPR points per game to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Luther Burden will aim to build on an impressive performance as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Burden had his first big time of the season against the Eagles in Week 3, turning 11 targets into seven catches for 61 yards and a touchdown. The second-year wideout had a solid connection with veteran Case Keenum, who is likely to fill in under center for at least one more week, if not more. This bodes well for the future of Burden, but he will have to face a New York defense that's allowed the eleventh-least fantasy points per game (28.2) and fourth-least receiving yards (337) to wide receivers across three outings.
outlooksByWeek.5: Luther Burden will aim to stay involved as the Bears travel to Green Bay in Week 5. Burden tied his season high of 63 receiving yards in Week 4 against the Jets, and he's now recorded 60 or more yards in all but one game this season. The second-year wide receiver appears to be a pivotal part of Chicago's offense, and he could be a key piece towards a win in Tundratown. He'll face a Packers defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.6: Luther Burden will continue to be a top option in Chicago's passing game in Week 6 at Atlanta. Burden brought in four of six targets for a team-high 47 receiving yards and rushed the ball four times for two yards in a Week 5 blowout loss to the Packers. The second-year pass catcher has been unable to get things going in multiple games this season, but this can be attributed to the struggles at the quarterback position. No matter who is throwing him the ball, the Falcons ranking 27th in fantasy point allowed to wide receivers this campaign could be favorable for Burden.
outlooksByWeek.7: Luther Burden will seek to stay busy as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Burden secured all eight of his targets for 95 yards in a Week 6 win over the Falcons, leading Chicago in receptions, receiving yards and targets. The second-year wideout has a 31-361-1 line on 43 targets across six games this season, and a dominant connection looks to be growing with quarterback Caleb Williams. Burden will now turn his sights to a New England defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.8: Luther Burden will look to build off a season-best performance as the Bears play the Seahawks in Week 8. Burden was on fire in Week 7 against the Patriots, turning four catches into 130 yards and a touchdown and taking his one carry for seven yards. The second-year pass catcher has now totaled 35 receptions for 491 yards and two touchdowns this season, and he's becoming Caleb Williams' favorite option in the passing game. Burden will now shift focus to a tough Seattle defense that's ranked first in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.9: Luther Burden will look to stay busy as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Burden stayed hot in a Week 8 MNF win over the Seahawks, bringing in seven of nine targets for 56 yards and a touchdown. The second-year wide receiver now has a 19-281-2 line on 21 targets across the last three games, and he's surpassed 50 receiving yards in all but two games this season. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Luther Burden will aim to recover from a concussion ahead of Chicago's Week 11 game against the Saints. Burden got concussed in the fourth quarter of a Week 9 win over the Buccaneers before the Bears' bye week, so hopefully he's had enough time to heal. The second-year star has now posted a 49-644-4 receiving line across nine games with career highs in catches and touchdowns, with one more game likely to get him over the hump in yards as well. If he's active, Burden will face a New Orleans defense that's ranked a tough eighth in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Luther Burden will look to bounce back as the Bears play the Lions in Week 12. Burden posted a season-worst performance in Week 11 against the Saints, hauling in two of three targets for just 10 yards. Either way, he's posted a career-best 51-654-4 receiving line across just 10 games this season. He'll face a Detroit defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack versus fantasy WRs this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Burden enters his second NFL season as one of the most popular breakout candidates in fantasy. The 2025 second-round pick played sparingly during most of his rookie season, but flashed elite efficiency when called upon, ranking in the top five among wide receivers in catch rate (77%), yards per target (10.8), RAC (7.3) and YPRR (2.9). Burden is obviously an unproven commodity (he has two career top-20 fantasy outings, after all), but with DJ Moore no longer on the roster, he's a lock for a larger role and very well could lead Chicago in targets. He could cost a pretty penny on draft day, but Burden, 22, is a fine WR3 target with upside for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chuba Hubbard is expected to continue leading the Panthers' backfield in the Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. Hubbard out-touched Jonathon Brooks 13 to five in the Week 1 loss, which is a good sign for his fantasy outlook going forward. Hubbard also found the end zone twice and looked very efficient, averaging 6.7 yards per touch. He's in for a tougher Week 2 matchup, however, as Atlanta allowed just 16.4 PPR fantasy points to the running back position last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the Panthers' top running back in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Hubbard appears to have returned to his 2024 form over Carolina's first two games this season, rushing for 102 yards (4.6 yards per carry) and a touchdown while catching all five of his targets for 49 yards and a score. Additionally, with Jonathon Brooks (groin) exiting the Week 2 win in the fourth quarter, Hubbard's role could continue growing. He faces a difficult matchup, however, as the Browns' defense has given up just 16.9 PPR fantasy points per game through two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the Panthers' lead back in the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Without Jonathon Brooks (groin) in the Week 3 loss, Hubbard accounted for 82.1 percent of the Panthers' running back touches (23 to AJ Dillon's five). Despite Carolina throwing the ball over 40 times per game this season, Hubbard has remained one of fantasy's most productive backs, averaging 16.7 opportunities and 17.7 PPR points per game. He's likely to remain the bell-cow in Carolina's Week 4 matchup against a Lions defense that's allowed 19.7 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain productive in the Panthers' Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. Hubbard is coming off one of the best games of his career in the Week 4 win over the Lions, totaling 129 yards and two touchdowns on 21 touches. He's been a true work-horse running back for the Panthers since Jonathon Brooks' (groin) injury, playing 84% of Carolina's snaps in Weeks 3 and 4. Expect Hubbard to continue producing in the Week 6 matchup against an Eagles defense that's given up 20.8 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the Panthers' lead back in the Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers. Hubbard has been extremely productive for Carolina over its last three games, averaging 120 yards and a touchdown per game on 73 total touches. While Jonathon Brooks (groin) remains on the injured reserve list, Hubbard is expected to continue taking the vast majority of work in the Panthers' backfield. Despite this, he's in for a tough Week 7 matchup against a Buccaneers defense that's allowed just 17.4 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the Panthers' lead back in the Week 8 matchup against the Packers. Hubbard had his worst performance of the season in the Week 7 loss to the Buccaneers, accumulating just 60 yards on 11 touches. Across six contests this season, Hubbard has amassed 459 rushing yards, 112 receiving yards and six total touchdown, the 19th-most total yards in the NFL. He'll have a good opportunity to rebound in Week 8 against a Packers defense that's allowed 25.8 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain a vital piece of the Panthers' offense in the Week 9 matchup against the Broncos. Hubbard was one of the few bright spots in Carolina's Week 8 loss to the Packers, totaling 119 yards and a touchdown on 29 touches. He ranks 10th in the NFL in touches per game (20.0) and 11th in total yards per game (98.6), which bodes well for his outlook going forward. Hubbard could thrive against a Broncos defense that's allowed 25.3 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain Carolina's bell-cow back during the Week 10 matchup against the Saints. Hubbard has now logged 20-plus touches in five of the Panthers' last six games, averaging the eighth-most touches per game (20.0) in the NFL this year. His receiving volume has jumped over the last three weeks as well, catching 15 of 18 targets for 82 yards during that span. Hubbard figures to have a huge game in Week 10 against a New Orleans defense that has allowed the most fantasy points per game to opposing running backs (28.6) this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Chubba Hubbard will continue operating as the Panthers' bell-cow back in the Week 11 matchup against the Ravens. Hubbard put Carolina on his back during the Week 10 win over the Saints, accumulating 172 yards and two touchdowns on 32 touches. On the season, Hubbard ranks fifth in the NFL in touches per game (21.3) eighth in scrimmage yards per game (106.4), suggesting he'll remain one of fantasy's top running backs as the year progresses. Despite this, he could struggle against a good Ravens defense that's allowed just 19.9 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs through nine games this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the focal point of the Panthers' offense in the Week 12 matchup against the Buccaneers. Hubbard has now received 59 touches over his last two games, accounting for 292 total yards (212 rushing and 80 receiving) and four touchdowns. He ranks fifth in the NFL in touches per game (21.9) and seventh in scrimmage yards per game (107.8), likely remaining one of fantasy's top running backs for the remainder of the season. Hubbard is in for a very difficult Week 12 matchup, however, as Tampa Bay's defense has allowed the fewest fantasy points per game to opposing running backs (17.2) in the league this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Hubbard is coming off a disappointing 2025 campaign in which he battled injury and lost lead-back duties to Rico Dowdle. The veteran was limited to 734 yards on 164 touches (he cleared 275 touches and 1,100 yards in 2023 and 2024), and he ranked 64th among 65 qualified backs in forced missed tackle rate and elusive rating, per PFF. Still in his prime at age 27, a bounce-back season is possible, especially with Dowdle gone and unproven Jonathon Brooks as his competition for touches. Hubbard should be considered a flex/bench option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Allgeier heads into a Week 2 clash against Seattle with a big role in Arizona's backfield. Allgeier logged 17 carries for 61 yards in a season-opening win against the Chargers, getting more totes and producing more yards than rookie Jeremiyah Love. It remains to be seen if that will hold true throughout the campaign, but for the time being Allgeier seems set to be heavily involved in the Cardinals' ground game. With that said, both Allgeier and Love could find the sledding tough in Week 2 versus a Seahawks defense that yielded the third-fewest rushing yards per game during the regular season last year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Allgeier will seek to improve his efficiency on the ground during Arizona's Week 3 visit to San Francisco. Allgeier gained just 10 yards on five carries Sunday in a loss against Seattle, and he's averaging a meager 3.2 YPC through two contests. He paced the Cardinals with 17 carries in the team's season opener, but  Jeremiyah Love jumped ahead with him with nine carries Week 2 and could continue to settle in as the club's clear No. 1 RB moving forward. The 49ers have yielded 4.04 YPC to running backs so far, but that's led to just one rushing TD.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Allgeier seems to have fallen well behind Jeremiyah Love for ball-carrying opportunities heading into Arizona's Week 4 matchup with the Giants. Love carried the ball 21 times against San Francisco this past Sunday, while Allgeier handled a season-low two totes. The latter did reel in a season-best four catches, but they amounted to just 10 receiving yards. Though the Giants are struggling against the run, ranking in the bottom half of the league in allowing 18.5 fantasy points per game to RBs, Allgeier will likely need to see more opportunities in order to make an impact.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Allgeier may be lined up for a big role for Arizona in Week 5 against the Lions. Rookie Jeremiyah Love is dealing with an ankle injury, and if he can't suit up Sunday, Allgeier will likely lead the team's backfield. Even with Love healthy for nearly the entire game in Week 4, Allgeier posted good production, recording an 8-42-1 rushing line and two catches for seven yards. The Cardinals' RB group could find success against a Lions defense that is giving up 4.64 yards per carry to running backs, eighth-worst in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Allgeier's role in Arizona's backfield seems to be fading ahead of a Week 6 matchup against the Rams. Allgeier logged just three carries for seven yards this past Sunday against Detroit while adding nine yards on two catches. The veteran running back has logged three or fewer totes two of the past three weeks and seems to be far behind rookie Jeremiyah Love, who got 12 carries versus the Lions, in the pecking order. With that said, he could get some opportunities as a pass catcher against the Rams, who have given up the fourth-most receiving yards per game (42.6) to running backs through five weeks.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyler Allgeier could continue handling a significant share of Arizona's backfield workload in Week 7 against Denver, regardless of whether Jeremiyah Love remains sidelined with an ankle injury or returns after a one-game absence. Allgeier has rushed 53 times for 157 yards and a touchdown through six games, but he's averaging just 3.0 yards per carry, so he needs to be more efficient when he gets the ball. Bam Knight's emergence adds another obstacle to consistent fantasy production. However, Denver has allowed the sixth-most fantasy points per game to opposing RBs in 2026, so Allgeier should have flex appeal if he has an expanded role for a second consecutive week.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tyler Allgeier's role in Arizona's background is looking shaky ahead of a Week 8 battle in Dallas. Rookie Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is expected to practice this week and could return from a two-game absence, which would likely push Allgeier down in the pecking order. Even if Love doesn't return, Bam Knight has outperformed Allgeier during Love's absence and could take over the lead-back role. Still, Allgeier at least has a good matchup, as the Cowboys rank 25th in the league in giving up 4.36 yards per carry to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Tyler Allgeier may be asked to log a heavy workload for the Cardinals in Week 9 against Seattle. Fellow RBs Jeremiyah Love (ankle) and Bam Knight (concussion) are both dealing with injuries, leaving Allgeier to potentially carry the run game on his shoulders versus the Seahawks. Allgeier thrived with that responsibility this past Sunday in an overtime win over Dallas, logging 147 yards and a touchdown on 11 carries along with 44 yards and another score on five catches. However, he could find the sledding tougher against a Seattle defense that is allowing just 3.28 yards per carry to running backs, the second-best mark in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Tyler Allgeier should remain Arizona's lead RB against the Rams in Week 10. Allgeier took on that role this past Sunday in a loss to Arizona and finished with 46 yards on 17 carries along with zero yards on two catches while drawing three targets. It was a quiet performance against a premier defense, but Allgeier seems likely to continue to lead the Cardinals' backfield while Jeremiyah Love (ankle) remains sidelined. Allgeier faces another tough draw in Week 10, as the Rams have yielded the fourth-fewest fantasy points per game (14.2) to running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Tyler Allgeier and the Cardinals will face a tough Kansas City defense in Week 11. Allgeier struggled in this past Sunday's loss to the Rams, gaining only 14 yards on five carries and failing to catch his only target. What's more, he logged just a 44 percent offensive snap share despite the absence of Jeremiyah Love (ankle), who's slated to miss several more weeks. Allgeier may be splitting backfield work with Bam Knight against a sturdy KC run defense that is yielding the second-fewest yards per carry (3.46) to running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Tyler Allgeier may be losing his grasp on the Cardinals' starting RB role ahead of a Week 12 matchup versus the Commanders. Allgeier couldn't get much going this past Sunday in a loss to Kansas City, managing just 23 yards on seven carries. Meanwhile, Bam Knight gained 45 yards on eight touches, and it's possible that Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will return to action soon. Washington has been pretty solid against the run this season, yielding just 3.67 yards per carry to running backs, the eighth-best mark in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Allgeier signed with the Cardinals during free agency. The 2022 fifth-round NFL draft pick impressed as a rookie in Atlanta, totaling 1,174 yards on 226 touches, but he hasn't come close to those marks while playing second fiddle to Bijan Robinson over the past three seasons, and he has yet to produce a top-25 fantasy campaign. Allgeier did score eight touchdowns last season, but he remains a nonfactor as a receiver, never clearing 18 catches in a season. The 26-year-old will step into a similar role in Arizona, as the primary backup and change-of-pace option behind No. 3 overall pick Jeremiyah Love. Same as in Atlanta, Allgeier has no standalone value, but he's a very good insurance stash.

outlooksByWeek.2: Alec Pierce led the Colts with 61 receiving yards in the season opener despite battling a heel injury heading into the game. In addition, he left during the first half to get X-rays on his hand and wrist after hitting a defender's helmet. His practice participation is likely to be affected by those injuries, but Pierce is seemingly on track to suit up in Week 2 against the Chiefs and can be viewed as a solid WR3 or flex option. He brings big-play ability to an otherwise underwhelming Colts passing game, averaging at least 21.3 yards per catch in each of the past two seasons and leading the team with 1,003 receiving yards in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Alec Pierce aggravated a left heel injury in Week 2, stemming from his offseason left ankle surgery. The Colts' leading receiver from last season probably faces a multi-week absence and won't play against the Texans in Week 3. Josh Downs and Keenan Allen are set to lead Indianapolis' underwhelming WR room versus Houston.

player.seasonOutlook: Pierce has spent the majority of his first four NFL seasons as a situational deep threat, but that didn't stop him from becoming one of the league's highest-paid wide receivers during the offseason. The 2022 second-round pick is fresh off a career year and he's now paced all receivers in YPR, YPT and aDOT each of the last two seasons. However, he's yet to finish a season better than 48th at WR in target share (18%), 42nd in targets (84), 45th in catches (47), 18th in yards (1,003), 18th in TDs (seven) or 25th in fantasy PPG. Of course, with Michael Pittman Jr. no longer in the mix, Pierce is a good bet for a more well-rounded role as Daniel Jones' top target. There's some risk here, but the 26-year-old's hefty contract suggests we should take him seriously as a fantasy WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Khalil Shakir will look to remain Josh Allen's security blanket in Week 2 when the Bills host the Lions. Shakir managed four grabs on six targets to open the season, finishing with 50 yards. He operated underneath while newly acquired DJ Moore stretched the field. The Lions' vulnerable secondary gave up 410 yards passing in Week 1, but Shakir will likely be limited by shorter routes, creating a safe but uninspiring fantasy option.
outlooksByWeek.3: Khalil Shakir remains a steady, stable cog in Buffalo's passing game entering a Week 3 matchup with the Chargers. Shakir logged six targets in each of the Bills' first two games but hasn't topped 50 yards or scored. Shakir didn't take on an elevated role in Week 2 following DJ Moore's (shoulder) early exit, but he faces a secondary that allowed 75 yards to Kendrick Bourne and 119 yards to Tre Tucker, and both operate in a similar slot role to Shakir.
outlooksByWeek.4: Khalil Shakir seeks more opportunities in Week 4 when the Bills face the Patriots. Despite a season-high 71% snap share in Week 3, Shakir had his lowest output of 2026, catching just a six-yard pass on three targets in a game where Josh Allen struggled. Shakir could benefit from additional looks in Week 4 if DJ Moore is matched up consistently with CB Christian Gonzalez. Operating primarily out of the slot tempers high yardage totals.
outlooksByWeek.5: Khalil Shakir maintains a steady role out of the slot for Buffalo as they prepare to face the Rams in Week 5. Shakir is coming off a season-high 82 yards in Week 4, his third game with at least six targets. His workload is independent of DJ Moore's shoulder status. Shakir will either garner more targets if Moore is out, or benefit from the attention Moore usually draws. However, the Rams defense hasn't allowed an opposing receiver to top 50 yards, suggesting Shakir is a risky floor and limited ceiling option.
outlooksByWeek.6: Khalil Shakir continues to play a minimal role in the Bills' passing game as they enter a Week 6 matchup with the Raiders. Shakir had just three targets in Week 5, the second time he's experienced that limited volume in three weeks despite the continued absence of DJ Moore (shoulder). Shakir is averaging a career-best 14.2 yards per catch and with Las Vegas proving vulnerable over the middle (nine catches, 122 yards, two touchdowns last week to DeMario Douglas and Efton Chism), Shakir could exploit a favorable matchup despite a lack of heavy volume.
outlooksByWeek.8: Khalil Shakir will reprise his slot role in Week 8 when the Bills host the Ravens. Shakir hasn't directly benefited from DJ Moore's (shoulder) absence, with a largely unchanged role prior to Buffalo's Week 7 bye, logging six or more targets in four of six contests. While he's topped four catches just once, he's averaging 13.2 yards per catch, his highest mark since 2023. Baltimore's secondary has been more vulnerable to larger, outside X receivers, with Drake London, Tee Higgins, and Carnell Tate all topping 100 yards against them. Shakir will need to continue to take advantage of his opportunities to be a viable fantasy option.
outlooksByWeek.9: Khalil Shakir continues to provide stability in Buffalo's passing game ahead of a Week 9 matchup with the Vikings. Shakir has recorded at least six targets in five of seven outings, going for 50 or more yards four times. It's a modest floor with only one touchdown catch, and it's even lower facing a Minnesota defense that's allowing the third-fewest fantasy points to opposing receivers, including just four touchdowns in seven games.
outlooksByWeek.10: Khalil Shakir remains an efficient secondary option in the Bills' passing game ahead of a Week 10 matchup with the Jets. He caught four passes in Week 9, the fifth time in eight outings he's done so, resulting in 50 or more yards at the same rate. Shakir has only one touchdown, and the Jets' secondary has allowed just nine touchdown catches by receivers, likely limiting Shakir's potential in Week 10, but his role and usage are clear and steady, setting him up for stability as a potential streamer.
outlooksByWeek.11: Khalil Shakir is in search of a bounce-back outing in Week 11 when the Bills face the Dolphins. He logged only three targets in Week 10, the second time this season he's had such low volume, and now has four games with 38 yards or fewer in nine outings. Buffalo threw only 21 times against the Jets, and if they jump to a big lead again against Miami, a similar game flow could emerge, potentially giving Shakir too few opportunities to better a secondary that's allowing 9.3 yards per target.
outlooksByWeek.12: Khalil Shakir will be challenged to match Week 11's season-best outing when the Bills face the Chiefs in Week 12. With Dalton Kincaid sidelined in Week 11, Shakir turned nine targets into 101 yards, both season highs. With a quick turnaround to Week 12's Thursday affair hurting Kincaid's availability, Shakir could again see added looks, though against a much tougher secondary that's allowing the second-fewest fantasy points per game to wideouts.

player.seasonOutlook: Shakir has settled in as a reliable, short-range target for Josh Allen, though the role hasn't led to much fantasy success. The 2022 fifth-round pick has cleared a 20% target share and 70 catches in consecutive seasons, ranking top five among receivers in catch rate and RAC both years. A nonfactor near the goal line, however, Shakir totaled eight TDs and five end zone targets during the span. Shakir finished the two seasons just outside of the top 35 fantasy receivers and will now have to compete with DJ Moore for the team lead in targets. Shakir was already barely worth flex consideration, so the potential for a slight decrease in target volume suggests the 26-year-old is no more than a low-ceiling bench option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Hunter Henry will look for more opportunities in Week 2 when New England hosts Pittsburgh. Henry caught all three of his targets to open 2026, and with the Patriots losing A.J. Brown (ankle) for the foreseeable future, additional targets could come Henry's way. Pittsburgh didn't allow a catch to tight ends last week, but that was a product of poor opponent quarterback play. Henry can be considered a back-end option at the position with the potential for far more against a defense he posted two touchdowns and 90 yards against a season ago.
outlooksByWeek.3: Hunter Henry will look to keep expanding his role for the Patriots in Week 3 against the Jaguars. In their first full game without A.J. Brown in Week 2, Henry logged a 92% snap share but drew only five targets, turning them into three catches for 40 yards. Drake Maye has struggled to open the season, posting a 1:4 TD:INT ratio, and while someone has to catch the limited passes, Henry faces a challenging matchup against a defense that hasn't allowed an opposing tight end to top 32 yards against them so far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Hunter Henry is laboring for opportunity in a sputtering Patriots passing offense ahead of a Week 4 game against the Bills. Henry caught just one of two targets in Week 3, finishing with five yards, and has yet to score or top 40 yards. There are likely better Week 4 options with Henry facing a defense that's allowed one opposing tight end to top 35 yards.
outlooksByWeek.5: Hunter Henry could have an expanded role in Week 5 when the Patriots face the Raiders with Eli Raridon (ankle) uncertain. Henry was already playing at least 70% of the snaps, and he posted a season-high five catches for 62 yards in Week 4, collecting five targets for the second time this season. Las Vegas has allowed five touchdown catches to opposing tight ends, but also just 6.1 yards per target through four games, suggesting Henry may need to find the end zone for the first time in 2026 to be a fantasy asset.
outlooksByWeek.6: Hunter Henry has been steady in the Patriots passing game ahead of a potentially difficult Week 6 matchup with the Jets. He has three catches in four of the Patriots' first five games, three times recording at least 40 yards, and he posted 45 and 49 yards in two matchups last season against this divisional opponent. However, the Jets have been stingy against tight ends, allowing just 191 yards (6.0 yards per target) and zero touchdowns through five games.
outlooksByWeek.7: Hunter Henry brings a two-game scoring streak into the Patriots' Week 7 matchup with the Bears. With Drake Maye clicking on all cylinders over the last three weeks (10 touchdown passes), Henry has posted at least three catches and 44 yards during that stretch. Chicago has defended tight ends well for most of the season, but over the last two weeks, an opposing tight end has gone for 60 or more yards, and they've surrendered their first two touchdowns of the year to the position. Henry's volume is steady, giving him a bit more of a reliable floor than high potential.
outlooksByWeek.8: Hunter Henry is poised to build on a season-high performance in Week 7 when the Patriots face the Dolphins in Week 8. While he failed to reach the end zone for the first time in three games, Henry hauled in all seven of his targets for 71 yards, all season bests. Miami has been exploited by opposing tight ends with six touchdown receptions in six games and 9.3 yards per target, the second highest mark in the league. New England continues to spread targets around, but it seems wise to scheme into this vulnerability, making Henry a preferred Week 8 option.
outlooksByWeek.9: Hunter Henry will need to overcome a foot injury if he's to help the Patriots loosen up a stingy Packers defense in Week 9. Henry hauled in all three of his first-half targets in Week 8 before exiting. Should he play, the challenge becomes finding holes against a Green Bay defense that's allowing just 5.8 yards per target and the second-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends. Eli Raridon has shown promise and would benefit from a potential Henry absence, but the matchup concerns remain.
outlooksByWeek.10: Hunter Henry figures to be a popular option for the Patriots in Week 10 against a Lions defense that struggles against opposing tight ends. Henry has just three targets in each of his last two games and has topped 48 yards just twice all season, but Week 10 presents an inviting opportunity. Detroit has allowed 11 touchdown receptions to tight ends and 8.2 yards per target, the highest numbers across the league. With New England potentially missing its top two running backs, a pass-heavy script would set Henry up for top-end production.
outlooksByWeek.12: Hunter Henry is saddled with an unfavorable Week 12 matchup when the Patriots take on the Chargers. He has just three targets in each of New England's last three games. Tommy DeVito playing quarterback could lead to additional check-downs, but that wasn't the case in Week 10 against Detroit. The Chargers have allowed one touchdown to a tight end, though a league-high 9.4 yards per target. Still, Henry isn't set up for a productive effort.

player.seasonOutlook: Henry has settled in as one of Drake Maye's top targets, having reached 85 targets, 60 catches and 650 yards each of the past two seasons (each ranked in the top 10 among tight ends). A threat downfield and near the goal line, Henry has finished in the top 15 in aDOT each of the past seven seasons and 12th or better in end zone targets in seven of his nine campaigns. Despite the solid usage, Henry hasn't sported much fantasy upside, as he has failed to finish in the top 12 in fantasy PPG since 2020 (he has never finished better than eighth). The 31-year-old has added target competition this season (Romeo Doubs and A.J. Brown), so he's no more than a fringe TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Spencer Shrader made a 58-yard field goal but also missed an extra point in a confounding performance during the Colts' season-opening loss. The big-legged kicker may not get many opportunities in Week 2 against the Chiefs, especially since the Colts are one of the league's most efficient red-zone teams thanks to the presence of star RB Jonathan Taylor. Shrader is a middling fantasy option, and you can likely find a kicker in a more appealing situation on your league's waiver wire.
outlooksByWeek.3: Spencer Shrader has made all four of his field-goal attempts and five of six extra point tries through two games this season. The Colts are averaging a robust 26.5 points per game, but their success on offense has been overshadowed by a league-worst defensive performance en route to a 0-2 start. Shrader is gaining some streaming appeal heading into a Week 3 home game against the Texans, who are allowing 28.0 points per game in the early going after giving up just 17.4 points per game last season. He's a borderline fantasy starter at this point.
outlooksByWeek.4: Spencer Shrader is coming off a heroic performance in the Colts' 19-17 Week 3 win over the Texans, as the kicker overcame an early groin injury to make all four of his field-goal attempts, including a go-ahead 53-yarder with 16 seconds left in the fourth quarter. He's off to an 8-for-8 start this season and has made kicks from as deep as 58 yards. Shrader is making a case for a starting fantasy kicker role, and he'll have a chance to showcase his skills on the international stage in Week 4, when the Colts face the Commanders at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London. Scoring opportunities are likely to be plentiful for Shrader since Washington is giving up 30.7 points per game.
outlooksByWeek.5: Spencer Shrader has made all seven of his field-goal attempts over the Colts' last two games and all 11 attempts this season. He has been one of the hottest waiver-wire options at kicker over the past couple of weeks and could be worth picking up if he's still available ahead of a Week 5 trip to Pittsburgh. The Steelers have allowed eight made field goals in four games and 21.8 points per game. Those who streamed Shrader against Washington in Week 4 may as well keep rolling with him in Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.6: Spencer Shrader has emerged as an elite fantasy kicker through five weeks, converting all 12 of his field-goal attempts over the Colts' last three games. He's 16-for-16 overall this season, including a perfect 6-for-6 from 50-plus yards. Indianapolis' offense generated plenty of field-goal opportunities in the first half of last season before falling off a cliff in the second half, so the risk of regression is substantial. However, Shrader has an excellent opportunity to keep rolling in Week 6 against the winless Titans, who have allowed 13 field goals through five games, tied with Pittsburgh for the most in the NFL. Keep starting Shrader if you have him.
outlooksByWeek.7: Spencer Shrader has been one of the few bright spots for the 2-4 Colts, converting all of his league-high 18 field-goal attempts through six weeks, including six from beyond 50 yards. His lone blemish on the season is a missed extra point. Indianapolis could struggle to consistently reach scoring range in Week 7 against the Vikings, who are allowing a league-low 12.8 points per game, but Shrader has been too good recently to bench, and the Colts could find themselves kicking more field goals than PATs once again in this difficult matchup.
outlooksByWeek.8: Spencer Shrader leads the league in field goals made (19) and attempted (21), but he was just 1-for-3 in the Week 7 loss to Minnesota after starting 18-for-18 through six games. The Colts' kicker will attempt to bounce back in Week 8 against the Jaguars, who boast the league's third-stingiest scoring defense, allowing just 17.3 points per game. Shrader has earned some goodwill from fantasy managers with his hot start, but he could find himself back on the waiver wire before long if the misses start to pile up.
outlooksByWeek.9: Spencer Shrader is quickly losing his luster as the reeling Colts continue to struggle on offense. He still leads the league with 19 made field goals, but Shrader has slowed down significantly after an 18-for-18 start through Week 6. Shrader has gone just 1-for-3 on field goal attempts over the past two games while the Colts have been outscored 58-17 in that span. It's tempting to cut bait given his recent downturn, but fantasy managers should give Shrader one more chance to get back on track in Week 9 against the Cowboys, who are giving up 26.6 points per game, which is the sixth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Spencer Shrader leads the league in field goals made and attempted, even with his volume and effectiveness dropping off in recent weeks as the 2-7 Colts continue to struggle as a team. He's 22-for-24 this season but just 4-for-6 over the past three games. Indianapolis faces a Dolphins defense in Week 10 that has allowed 15 made field goals in eight games and 25.0 points per game. If you have Shrader on your roster, you may as well keep starting him.
outlooksByWeek.11: Spencer Shrader has made no more than one field goal in three of the last four games. His recent downturn has knocked Shrader out of first place in field goals made and attempted, though he's still top-three in both categories thanks to a torrid start that has the Colts' kicker at 23-for-25 through 10 games. That strong start included a 4-for-4 Week 3 performance against the Texans, whom Shrader will face again in Week 11. The Colts' offense has been depleted by a few trades and will likely struggle to generate consistent kicking opportunities moving forward, but Shrader is viable in Week 11 since Houston ranks in the middle of the pack with 24.3 points allowed per game and 18 made field goals against. If you see an enticing alternative on your league's waiver wire, it may be time to move on from Shrader.
outlooksByWeek.12: Spencer Shrader's stellar start is a distant memory. The struggling kicker has gone just 6-for-10 on field-goal attempts over the past five games after making all 18 of his attempts through Week 6. Indianapolis has switched QBs from Daniel Jones to Anthony Richardson after dropping six of its last seven games, but moving the ball will likely remain difficult for the Colts' underwhelming offense in Week 12 against the Giants, who allow the seventh-fewest scrimmage yards (310.5) and 12th-fewest points (21.4) per game. Shrader is a risky Week 12 fantasy option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Pat Bryant was the Broncos' surprise target leader in their season-opening loss to Kansas City, catching four of six targets for 42 yards. Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton were both taken out of the equation by the Chiefs secondary, forcing Bo Nix to look underneath for options like Bryant and tight end Evan Engram. Bryant had a solid finish to his rookie season in 2025, posting a 26-332-1 line on 39 targets over his final eight regular-season games, and his snap count and production suggest he's moved past Marvin Mims and Troy Franklin to take over the No. 3 wideout role for Denver. Bryant will look to stay involved in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that was tied for 17th last season in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Pat Bryant fell back to earth after a promising season opener, failing to catch his only target in the Broncos' Week 2 win over the Jaguars. Quarterback Bo Nix made it a priority to get Jaylen Waddle going, and there wasn't much volume available for anyone else. Bryant gained 16 rushing yards on his only carry, but the No. 3 role in the Denver passing game doesn't figure to offer consistent production, and Bryant could face a challenge for the job once Marvin Mims overcomes a foot injury. Bryant will face a Rams secondary in Week 3 that's allowed just 19 receptions to WRs through two weeks, tied for seventh in the NFL, but three of them have gone for touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.4: Pat Bryant scored his first touchdown of the season in the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams, connecting with Bo Nix for a five-yard strike in the third quarter. It was one of just two catches on the night for the second-year wide receiver. Through three games, he's produced a 6-86-1 line on nine targets while adding a 16-yard gain on one carry. Bryant is well behind Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton in the pecking order, but he seems to have secured the No. 3 role ahead of Troy Franklin. Bryant will look to build some momentum in Week 4 against a 49ers secondary that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Pat Bryant caught all three of his targets for 47 yards in the Broncos' Week 4 loss to the 49ers, but an ankle sprain knocked him out of the contest early. The second-year wide receiver is expected to miss multiple weeks, but Denver hasn't placed him on IR yet. In Bryant's absence, Marvin Mims and Troy Franklin will get more work behind Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton, beginning with a Week 5 matchup against a Chargers secondary that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Pat Bryant has missed the last four games for the Broncos due to an ankle injury, but his time on IR could be coming to an end. Prior to the injury, the second-year wideout had put together a 9-133-1 line on 12 targets over his first four contests of the season, serving as a reliable possession receiver for Bo Nix. If Bryant is cleared to suit up in Week 9, he'll be facing a Panthers team that just fired its defensive coordinator and is tied for 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Pat Bryant returned from a four-game absence due to an ankle injury in the Broncos' final game before their Week 10 bye, catching four of five targets for 56 yards and a touchdown. It was his most productive outing of the season, but it also came as Jaylen Waddle left the contest early with a concussion. Bryant has shown some chemistry with Bo Nix, but assuming Waddle doesn't miss additional time, his target volume figures to remain limited. Bryant will try to return to the end zone in Week 11 against a Raiders secondary that ranks 24th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Pat Bryant posted modest numbers over two games since returning from an ankle injury, catching seven of nine targets for 88 yards and a touchdown. The Broncos' passing game has been sluggish all year, and with the offense leaning more heavily on rookie running back Jonah Coleman, Bo Nix hasn't been required to do too much through the air. Bryant seems to have good chemistry with the quarterback, giving him a stable floor even if his ceiling is TD-dependent. Bryant will try to stay busy in Week 12 against a Steelers secondary that ranks 12th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: A 2025 third-round pick, Bryant played a situational role throughout his rookie season and is likely to do the same in 2026 after Denver added Jaylen Waddle as a running mate for Courtland Sutton. Bryant will battle the likes of Troy Franklin, Marvin Mims Jr. and Lil'Jordan Humphrey for No. 3 duties. During his rookie campaign, Bryant barely saw the field early on, but eventually passed Franklin on the depth chart and earned more work down the stretch. That led to more snaps but not much fantasy production, as he failed to clear 13.2 fantasy points in a single game and found the end zone once. The 23-year-old isn't on the fantasy radar right now, but he makes for a fine dynasty stash.

outlooksByWeek.2: David Montgomery scored three total TDs in his Texans debut in Week 1 and profiles as a borderline fantasy RB1 for a Week 2 home game against a Bengals defense that gave up 93 scrimmage yards and a score to Tampa Bay's Bucky Irving. Montgomery had 23 touches to Woody Marks' 10 in Week 1 against the Bills, so the former Lions RB is operating as the clear lead back for his new team. Montgomery's 23 Week 1 touches were more than he had in any game last season with Detroit. Cincinnati beefed up its defensive front in the offseason after allowing the most rushing yards in the NFL last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: David Montgomery produced just 24 scrimmage yards in Houston's Week 2 loss to the Bengals after scoring three TDs in his Texans debut. The veteran RB will cede some backfield work to Woody Marks, particularly if the Texans are forced to play catch-up, but Montgomery is the team's preferred option in valuable red-zone and short-yardage situations. Montgomery is poised for a bounce-back effort in Week 3 and can be trusted as a fantasy RB2 against a Colts defense that's allowing 177 yards per game on the ground.
outlooksByWeek.4: David Montgomery is averaging a paltry 2.8 yards per carry, and Houston's offensive line has struggled to open up holes heading into a Week 4 home game against the Cowboys. The offseason trade acquisition scored three TDs in his Texans' debut but hasn't found the end zone since. Through three games, Montgomery has out-touched Woody Marks 44-29, but Marks scored a one-yard touchdown in the Week 3 loss to the Colts, so Montgomery doesn't have a monopoly on short-yardage opportunities. The Cowboys are allowing 27.3 points per game and have surrendered four total TDs to RBs, so Montgomery is a fantasy RB2 for Week 4, albeit a touchdown-dependent one.
outlooksByWeek.5: David Montgomery has plodded to 2.7 yards per carry and has failed to find the end zone since scoring three TDs in Week 1, his Texans debut. Fellow Houston RB Woody Marks has scored twice during Montgomery's three-game touchdown drought. Montgomery and Marks will likely split carries again in Week 5 against the Titans, who are allowing 100 rushing yards per game to RBs, though Tennessee is giving up only 3.6 yards per carry. If Houston's defense can recapture last season's elite form and stifle the underwhelming Titans offense, Montgomery could get enough volume to wear down Tennessee's defense and make up for a lack of quality with quantity. With Houston's running game stuck in first gear, Montgomery is an unexciting flex candidate for Week 5.
