outlooksByWeek.6: David Montgomery is considered week-to-week after departing Houston's Week 5 win over the Titans due to a groin injury. He's likely to sit out in Week 6 against the Jaguars, leaving Woody Marks to lead Houston's backfield against Jacksonville's league-best run defense in London. Montgomery is averaging just 2.7 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.7: David Montgomery (groin) sat out Houston's Week 6 win over the Jaguars and is considered week-to-week. If he returns for Week 7 against the Giants, Montgomery would likely split carries with Woody Marks and possibly Jawhar Jordan. Montgomery is averaging just 2.7 yards per carry. The Giants have struggled to defend RBs, allowing 108 rushing yards and one total TD per game to the position.
outlooksByWeek.9: David Montgomery (groin) sat out Houston's last two games prior to the Week 8 bye, and it sounds like he may not be ready to suit up in Week 9 against the Chargers. Even if Montgomery is cleared to return, he'll be a risky flex option, as he was averaging a meager 2.7 yards per carry prior to getting injured while splitting carries with Woody Marks. The Chargers rank among the league's 10 most generous run defenses, allowing 124.6 yards per game on the ground. Running backs have scored nine total touchdowns in seven games against the Chargers, with eight of those TDs coming on the ground.
outlooksByWeek.10: David Montgomery (groin) is apparently nearing a return to practice, but he still looks likely to remain sidelined in Week 10 against the Browns. He hasn't suited up since exiting in Week 5, with Woody Marks leading Houston's backfield in the interim. Even if Montgomery gains clearance to play in Week 10, he'll be a risky flex option considering he was averaging just 2.7 yards per carry prior to getting injured while working in a timeshare with Marks.
outlooksByWeek.11: David Montgomery (groin) remained sidelined for Houston's Week 10 loss against the Browns despite practicing without limitations the Friday preceding the game. He hasn't played since Week 5, but Montgomery has the green light to suit up against the Colts in Week 11 and is in line for a prominent role, as Woody Marks (concussion) will miss Thursday's game on a short week after getting hurt in Week 10. No other RB besides Montgomery or Marks has more than 13 carries for the Texans this season. Despite averaging just 2.7 yards per carry prior to his injury, Montgomery has RB2 upside given the lack of competition for backfield opportunities against a Colts defense that's allowing 151 scrimmage yards and a touchdown per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: David Montgomery rushed for a season-high 107 yards in Week 11 against the Colts, successfully returning to action from a groin injury that had sidelined him since Week 5. Montgomery handled 29 touches in a workhorse role due to the absence of Woody Marks (concussion), who has a chance to return in Week 12 against the Ravens. If Marks plays, both Houston RBs would be solid flex plays, likely working in a timeshare. Should Marks sit again, Montgomery would be a high-end RB2 with another heavy workload anticipated against a Ravens run defense that allowed Omarion Hampton and Chuba Hubbard to rush for a combined 225 yards and three TDs over the past two games. Montgomery is averaging a meager 3.1 yards per carry, so he relies on volume and scoring opportunities to counteract his poor efficiency.

player.seasonOutlook: Montgomery was traded to Houston after spending his first seven NFL seasons with Chicago and Detroit. The veteran back is coming off a down year in 2025, when he posted career lows in touches (182), yardage (908, his first season under 1,000) and fantasy points per game (9.8). Montgomery was still effective as a rusher (4.53 yards per carry, 2.28 yards after contact) but lost work to Jahmyr Gibbs and wasn't involved much as receiver. The latter doesn't figure to change much in Houston, and while Montgomery is a decent bet to pace the team in carries, second-year back Woody Marks figures to sustain a substantial offensive role. Montgomery enters his age-29 season as a touchdown-dependent flex with limited upside.

After a miserable 2025 that saw them surrender the most yards while scoring the third-fewest fantasy points, the Commanders brought in a slew of offseason reinforcements, though it was more of a quantitative than qualitative process. There's no reason to trust this D/ST in Weeks 1 and 2, which are road matchups with the Eagles and Cowboys, but if the Commanders show midseason promise, bear in mind its most favorable matchups come during the season's second half.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cam Skattebo showed no ill effects from last season's injury in Week 1 for the New York Giants. Skattebo rushed 18 times for 81 yards and a touchdown in he stunning 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys. With the Giants poised to possess the ball and feed the running game under new coach John Harbaugh, Skattebo should continue to be in line for a heavy workload. In Week 2, the Giants will face a Rams defense that was surprisingly suspect against the run in their first game of the season.  The Rams allowed 174 yards on the ground, which currently ranks them 30th in the league. However, Aaron Donald will return to the fold out of retirement versus the G-Men.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cam Skattebo managed just 55 yards from scrimmage last game for the Giants. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, teams will likely gameplan to stop the run, which starts with Skattebo. That could mean tough sledding for the running game for the G-Men overall. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a mediocre Titans run defense that has given up 120.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is 21st in the NFL. In addition, the Titans have already surrendered three rushing scores in the first two games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cam Skattebo racked up 100 yards from scrimmage in the 12-7 win for the Giants over the Titans. Skattebo took 20 carries for 60 yards while also catching three passes for 40 yards out of the backfield. With Jameis Winston under center, the Giants should continue to rely on the running game led by Skattebo in Week 4 versus Arizona. The Cardinals have been suspect against the run in 2026, allowing 127.7 yards per clash on the ground, which is 26th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cam Skattebo has struggled to find room to roam for the Giants thus far this season. Skattebo rushed 18 times for 58 yards in the 36-24 win over the Cardinals last game. He is averaging just 3.5 yards per carry as teams dare the Giants to throw with backup quarterback Jameis Winston. In Week 5, Skattebo will face a rather stingy Washington run defense as well. The Commanders are allowing just 93.5 yards per tilt on the ground, which is sixth in the league. However, Washington did allow three rushing touchdowns last game versus the Colts.
outlooksByWeek.6: Cam Skattebo was mostly a non-factor last game against the Commanders, at least until the end of a wild contest which resulted in a tie. Skattebo managed 40 of his 71 scrimmage yards in overtime, though coughed up the ball as the Giants were in field goal range to potentially win the game. Skattebo would have truly been the goat for this contest had Washington not botched the final seconds of overtime. Skattebo has had 60 rushing yards or less in four-straight games, and has failed to score since the opener. However, in Week 6, the Giants will face a Saints defense that has been gutted on the ground thus far in 2026. New Orleans is allowing148.8 rushing yards per clash, which is 30th in the league. In addition, New Orleans has allowed the most rushing touchdowns in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Cam Skattebo had zero touches last game for the Giants. One week after losing a key fumble, Skattebo was removed from his starting job as the Giants backfield devolved into a four-man committee. Tyrone Tracy was the team's most productive back, scoring one rushing and one receiving touchdown, but managed just 45 scrimmage yards on eight touches. Devin Singletary had 33 yards on five touches and Najee Harris eked out just two rushing yards on four carries. Skattebo could return to a more significant role in Week 7 against the Texans, but it will be hard to trust any New York running back until one emerges from the pack. Houston is also allowing just 83 rushing yards per contest, which is third in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: Cam Skattebo retained his starring role for the Giants last game, gaining 121 scrimmage yards and scoring a touchdown in the thrilling 27-21 OT win over the Texans. Tyrone Tracy went on Injured Reserve following the victory, leaving Devin Singletary as the only other legitimate option at running back behind Skattebo. Though talks of a trade for Jonathan Taylor have intensified, nothing appears imminent heading into a tasty Week 9 clash with Philadelphia. The Eagles have been torched on the ground in 2026, allowing 131.9 rushing yards per tilt, which is 28th in the league. Likewise, the Eagles have given up 10 rushing scores, which is tied for 24th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Cam Skattebo did not suit up in New York's last game due to a hamstring issue. However, Skattebo pushed to play in the contest, and as a result looks primed to return to the starting lineup in Week 10 versus the Commanders. Washington has been fairly stingy against the run in 2026, though, allowing just 102.3 rushing yards per tilt, which is 12th in the league. In addition, the Commanders have yielded just seven rushing touchdowns, which is tied for 11th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Cam Skattebo scored twice last game for the Giants. He also gained over 120 scrimmage yards for the second-straight contest. Following being benched versus the Saints, Skattebo has responded with 39 touches in the subsequent two tilts, though he did miss the win over Philadelphia due to a hamstring ailment. He will have his work cut out for him in Week 11 versus the Jags. Jacksonville is allowing just 91 rushing yards per clash, which is sixth in the NFL. In addition, the Jags have surrendered only five rushing touchdowns this season, which is tied for fourth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.12: Cam Skattebo fumbled yet again for the Giants last game. The turnover ultimately did not cost his team the win this time, though Skattebo managed just 34 yards on 14 carries overall versus a stout Jacksonville run defense. If Skattebo can hold onto the ball, he should have better luck against the Colts in Week 12. Indianapolis is allowing 134.4 rushing yards per tilt, which is 29th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Skattebo is a Year 2 breakout candidate following an impressive but injury-shortened rookie season. The fourth-round pick first played a significant offensive role in Week 2 and went on to average 16.0 carries, 4.7 targets and 96.3 yards while scoring six TDs during his six full games. His 19.1 fantasy points per game during the span would've ranked sixth over the full season. The 24-year-old enters 2026 with a new coach (John Harbaugh) and playcaller (Matt Nagy), but his competition for touches are Najee Harris and the same guys he beat out for work in 2025 (Tyrone Tracy Jr., Devin Singletary). Assuming his ankle heals up as expected, Skattebo will be on the RB2 radar with upside for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to keep it rolling in Detroit's Week 2 matchup at Buffalo. Gibbs was the bell cow managers hoped for in Week 1 against the Saints, logging 29 rushes for 156 yards, two touchdowns and catching all five of his targets for 30 yards. He'll also face a Bills defense that fared badly against the ground game in their season opener, allowing Gibbs' former teammate David Montgomery to total 79 yards and three touchdowns off 23 touches.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jahmyr Gibbs will aim to keep things rolling as the Lions take on the Jets in Week 3. Gibbs finished with huge numbers once again in Week 2, but most of his output came from six catches for 61 yards and a touchdown. The superstar running back has seen high volume so far, with 56 touches for 299 scrimmage yards and three touchdowns to his name this season. He'll face a Jets defense that's been tough against the run in its first two games, but New York hasn't faced anyone of Gibbs' caliber.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to keep his touchdown tear alive as the Lions travel to Carolina in Week 4. Gibbs was a beast once again in Week 3 against the Jets, turning 20 carries into 99 yards and two touchdowns, as well as catching the ball six times for 65 yards and another touchdown. The fourth-year star has now found the end zone six times across three games, and he's totaled 463 yards from scrimmage. He'll face a Panthers defense that's allowed the third-most fantasy points per game (30.5) to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jahmyr Gibbs will aim to return to dominance as the Lions play the Cardinals in Week 5. Gibbs produced for fantasy managers in Week 4, but he still rushed 15 times for a season-low 46 yards with a touchdown, tacking on four catches for 31 yards. Either way, the superstar running back has found the end zone in every game this season, and he's surpassed 100 total yards in three of four games. He'll face an Arizona defense that's ranked top five against fantasy RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to come out of the bye week with a bang as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. Gibbs was a monster in Week 5 against the Cardinals, rushing 25 times for 151 yards and two touchdowns, with five catches for 56 yards as well. The premier running back has now surpassed 100 scrimmage yards in all but one game this season, and he's found the end zone nine times across five games. He'll face a Green Bay front that's ranked 29th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to get back in the end zone as the Lions play the Vikings in Week 8. Gibbs hit the century mark on the ground for the third time this season in Week 7 versus Green Bay, rushing the ball 29 times for 116 yards and adding five catches for 27 yards. The superstar unfortunately was held to zero touchdowns for the first time this season, with nine to his name across the first five games. He'll change focus now to a Minnesota defense that's ranked third in fantasy points allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jahmyr Gibbs will aim to stay hot as the Lions travel to Miami in Week 9. Gibbs recorded another monster performance on the ground in a Week 8 win over Minnesota, rushing the ball 23 times for 153 yards and a touchdown, with two catches for 15 yards as well. The superstar has now surpassed 100 rushing yards in three straight games, and he's found the end zone in all but one outing this season. He'll take on a Dolphins defense that's ranked a favorable 27th in fantasy points allowed to running backs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jahmyr Gibbs will seek to return to dominance as the Lions play the Patriots in Week 10. Gibbs punched in another rushing score alongside 74 yards on the ground in Week 9 against the Dolphins, but he was unable to record a catch for the first time this season. The star ball carrier has now recorded 20 or more carries in each of his last four outings, but he's seen his receiving work decline each week in that stretch. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked a tough fifth in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to keep up his dominance as the Lions play the Buccaneers in Week 11. Gibbs had another monster performance in a Week 10 win over the Patriots, totaling 252 yards off 29 touches and tacking on two rushing touchdowns. The superstar has now amassed 1,384 scrimmage yards and 13 total touchdowns through nine showings. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's allowed the fewest fantasy points per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to keep his tear going in Week 12 as Detroit faces Chicago on Thanksgiving. Gibbs eventually broke down an otherwise stingy Tampa Bay run defense in Week 11, rushing 23 times for 98 yards and two touchdowns and catching four passes for 20 yards. The superstar has now surpassed 95 rushing yards in seven of 10 games this season, and he's totaled 13 scores on the ground. He'll face a Bears defense that's ranked relatively middle-of-the-pack versus fantasy RBs this season, and that Travis Etienne averaged 5.42 yards per carry against this past Sunday.

player.seasonOutlook: Gibbs has finished in the top 10 among running backs in yards per carry, routes, targets, receptions, touchdowns and fantasy points in each of his first three campaigns. In fact, his 38 touchdowns over the past two seasons are four more than any other player. Though Gibbs has finished as a top-three fantasy back in each of the past two years, he has yet to finish a season higher than seventh in touches. That very well could change this season with David Montgomery no longer in the mix. The 24-year-old Gibbs is one of the NFL's top playmakers in one of its best offenses. He's a strong option with the first pick of fantasy drafts.

outlooksByWeek.2: Emeka Egbuka is expected to operate as Tampa Bay's top receiver in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns, whose defense struggled against wideouts in Week 1. Despite logging just six targets last week, Egbuka led the Buccaneers in receiving yards, solidifying himself as the team's top WR. Additionally, Egbuka had been nursing a toe injury leading up to the Week 1 loss, so he should only become more explosive as the season progresses. He's in for an incredible Week 2 matchup, as Cleveland's secondary allowed 50.6 PPR fantasy points to wideouts last week, the third-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Emeka Egbuka is expected to remain the Buccaneers' top receiving option in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings, whose defense has given up 38.9 PPR fantasy points to WRs this season. Egbuka had a rough Week 2 outing, finishing third on Tampa Bay in receptions (three) and targets (five) while slotting in at fifth in yards (16). However, he did score a touchdown and was on the field for 85 percent of the Buccaneers' offensive snaps, suggesting he'll remain the team's WR1. He's set for a tough Week 3 matchup against a Minnesota defense that gave up just three points and 163 passing yards to the Bears in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Emeka Egbuka will remain the Buccaneers' top wideout in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Despite another relatively underwhelming Week 3 performance (5-62-0), Egbuka clearly remains atop Tampa Bay's receiving corps, leading the team in targets, receptions, and receiving yards. Baker Mayfield (thumb) will be sidelined in Week 4, which suggests Egbuka will likely see less opportunities. Regardless of who starts at quarterback, Egbuka is in for a favorable matchup against a Green Bay defense that's allowed 34.7 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Emeka Egbuka will look to bounce back from a poor performance in the Buccaneers' Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Egbuka was targeted just four times during the Week 4 loss to the Packers, his lowest mark of the season. While Baker Mayfield (thumb) remains sidelined and Jalon Daniels acts as the Buccaneers' signal caller, Egbuka may continue receiving less opportunities. However, he's in for a great Week 5 matchup against a Dallas defense that's given up 36.9 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Emeka Egbuka is expected to remain the Buccaneers' top wideout in the Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. Egbuka had a good bounce-back performance in the Week 5 win over the Cowboys, catching six of nine targets for 38 yards while adding 14 yards and a touchdown on the ground. Despite a relatively underwhelming start to the season, Egbuka still leads Tampa Bay in yards (192), targets (33) and receptions (21) through five games. He could struggle in Week 6 against a Pittsburgh secondary that's allowed just 27.7 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Emeka Egbuka is expected to remain the Buccaneers' top wideout in the Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. Egbuka had his most promising game of the 2026 season in the overtime loss to the Steelers, turning a whopping 16 targets into seven receptions for 48 yards and a score. Tampa Bay's offense has struggled without Baker Mayfield (thumb), averaging just 167 passing yards per game since his injury. Despite this, Egbuka has remained productive and could benefit from the potential return of Mayfield in Week 7. Regardless of who starts at quarterback, Egbuka could struggle against a Panthers defense that's allowed just 29.6 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) is expected to operate as the Buccaneers' top wideout if active for the Week 8 matchup against the Falcons. Egbuka was sidelined for the Week 7 win over the Panthers but still leads Tampa Bay in targets (49), receptions (28) and receiving touchdowns (two) this season. With Baker Mayfield at quarterback this year, Egbuka has averaged 4.3 receptions, 47 yards and 0.3 touchdowns per game. He could find success against a Falcons defense that's given up 34.4 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Emeka Egbuka (foot) is expected to operate as the Buccaneers' top wideout if active for the Week 9 matchup against the Bears. He has been sidelined for two consecutive games due to a concussion and a foot injury. During that span, the Buccaneers completed just seven of 14 pass attempts for 64 yards and one touchdown, proving Egbuka's importance to the passing game. He's expected to lead the team's WR room against a tough Bears secondary that's allowed just 29.5 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts through seven games this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Emeka Egbuka is expected to lead the Buccaneers' receiving corps during the Week 11 matchup against the Lions. Egbuka has had an underwhelming start to his 2026 season, catching 31 of 54 targets for 278 yards and two touchdowns in seven games. Despite this poor start, he ranks first on the Buccaneers in receiving yards, receptions, targets and touchdowns this year, suggesting more fantasy production is imminent. Egbuka could thrive against the Lions' secondary in Week 11, as they have allowed 32.6 fantasy points per game to opposing wide receiver groups this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Emeka Egbuka is expected to remain the Buccaneers' top wideout during the Week 12 matchup against the Panthers, Egbuka was relatively quiet during the Week 11 loss to the Lions, catching two of five targets for 18 yards. The second-year wideout has struggled to find his footing since returning from injury in the Week 9 loss to the Bears, catching just five of 10 targets for 56 yards in two contests. Despite this, he's expected to remain the team's top receiving option against a Carolina defense that's allowed 31.9 fantasy points per game to opposing WR groups this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Egbuka is a fascinating evaluation following a rookie season that couldn't have started much better (five TDs and 20.5 fantasy PPG during his first five games), but that fell apart from there (one TD and 7.8 PPG during his final 12 games). By season's end, Egbuka sat in the top 10 in targets and air yards, but a horrific 49% catch rate led to a 34th-place finish in fantasy PPG. The good news is that, with Mike Evans out of the picture and Chris Godwin now 30 years old, Egbuka has a shot to emerge as Baker Mayfield's No. 1 target. The 2025 first-round pick is a strong bet for a leap forward and should be viewed as a WR2 with the potential for a full-on breakout.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Olave is expected to remain the Saints' top wideout in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Olave definitely benefitted from Tyler Shough's 56 pass attempts during the Week 1 overtime loss. However, New Orleans averaged 34.8 pass attempts per game in 2025, so Olave will likely continue to see loads of volume. Additionally, he saw a 25 percent target share, which should remain steady until Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) returns later this season. Olave is in for a tough matchup this week, however, with Baltimore's defense allowing just 25.0 PPR fantasy points to WRs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Olave is expected to remain one of fantasy's top receivers in the Saints' Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Olave ranks second in the NFL in both receptions (18) and receiving yards (268) through the first two weeks, cementing himself as New Orleans' top wideout. Currently, he's received a 25.6 percent target share, which should continue proving valuable with the Saints high-volume of pass attempts (90 through two weeks, second-most in the NFL). Olave could struggle against the Raiders, however, whose defense has allowed just 21.9 PPR fantasy points to wideouts per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chris Olave is expected to remain one of fantasy's most productive wideouts in the Saints' Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. Olave has surpasses 100 receiving yards in two of three games this season, catching 27 of 36 targets for 373 yards and a touchdown. He's expected to continue benefitting from New Orleans' pass-happy offense that has averaged 44 pass attempts per game through three weeks. Additionally, Olave is in for a very favorable Week 4 matchup against a struggling Falcons secondary that's allowed 38.5 PPR fantasy points per game to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chris Olave is expected to lead New Orleans' receiving corps again in the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Olave has been spectacular through the Saints' first four games this season, catching 35 of 48 targets for 491 yards (second in the NFL) and a touchdown. He's expected to continue benefitting from head coach Kellen Moore's pass-heavy offense, which has led to ample opportunities for Olave this season. Despite this, Olave could struggle in Week 5 against a tough Vikings secondary that's given up just 30.1 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chris Olave will look to return to form in the Saints' Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Olave struggled along with the rest of New Orleans' offense in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings, catching four of six targets for 46 yards. On the season, Olave ranks second in the NFL with 537 receiving yards and will likely continue benefitting from head coach Kellen Moore's aggressive style of offense (averaging 41 pass attempts per game). Expect Olave to bounce back against a solid Giants defense that's allowed 30.9 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chris Olave is expected to remain one of fantasy's top wideouts in the Saints' Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. Olave didn't receive his usual volume in Week 6 but remained productive, catching four of seven targets for 43 yards and a score. He's expected to continue benefitting from Kellen Moore's aggressive offense that's averaged 39.2 pass attempts per game through six weeks. However, Olave is in for a difficult Week 7 matchup, as Pittsburgh's defense has given up just 29.0 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Chris Olave is expected to remain one of fantasy's most productive wideouts in the Saints' Week 9 matchup against the Browns. Olave ranks fifth in the NFL in receiving yards per game (90.9) and sixth in receptions per game (7.0) through seven contests. Additionally, quarterback Tyler Shough is averaging a league-high 39.0 pass attempts per game, which suggests Olave will continue to produce at a high level going forward. He's in for a tough Week 9 matchup against a Browns defense that's given up just 29.8 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Chris Olave is expected to remain the Saints' top pass catcher in the Week 10 matchup against the Panthers. Olave added another productive outing to his impressive 2026 campaign during the Week 9 overtime win against the Browns, catching seven of 12 targets for 98 yards. On the season, Olave ranks sixth in the NFL in targets per game (10.4) and seventh in receiving yards per game (91.8). Olave's high volume will likely continue as well, with Tyler Shough tied for the most pass attempts per game (38.5) in the league through eight games. Expect Olave to succeed against a depleted Panthers secondary that's allowed 31.9 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Chris Olave is expected to bounce back from an underwhelming performance in the Saints' Week 11 matchup against the Bears. Olave was overshadowed by 2026 first-round pick Jordyn Tyson in the Week 10 loss to the Panthers, as he logged season-lows in targets, receptions and yards. Despite this poor showing, Olave remains eighth in the NFL in receiving yards per game (84.9) and 10th in targets per game (9.7), so his fantasy outlook remains very positive going forward. However, he's set to face a tough Bears defense that's allowed just 29.4 fantasy points per game to opposing wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Chris Olave is expected to remain the Saints' top wideout during the Week 12 matchup against the Bengals. Olave bounced back from a poor Week 10 performance in last week's loss to the Bears, catching nine of 15 targets to 102 yards. He remains one of seven NFL players to average 10-or-more targets per game (10.2) while ranking seventh in the league in receiving yards per game (86.6). Despite his impressive season, Olave could struggle in Week 12 against a solid Bengals secondary that's given up just 29.7 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts through nine games this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Olave is fresh off a career year in which he reached new highs in targets (156), receptions (100), yardage (1,163) and touchdowns (nine). He finished eighth among receivers in fantasy PPG, which beat out his previous career best of 19th in 2023. Olave finished no lower than seventh among receivers in nearly every counting stat, including end zone targets (12) and air yards (1,816). The big season was a sigh of relief after a 2024 campaign riddled with concussions, and it positions the 26-year-old right back in the fringe-WR1 discussion. Especially with No. 8 overall pick Jordyn Tyson expected to miss a month or two with a hamstring injury, Olave will remain Tyler Shough's top target, and that sets him up for another highly productive campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jonathon Brooks is expected to operate as Carolina's No. 2 running back in the Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. Brooks received just four carries in the Week 1 loss, which is fewer than Chuba Hubbard (10) and AJ Dillon (five). However, all of Dillon's work came when the Panthers were down substantially in the fourth quarter. Brooks showed flashes of brilliance when on the field, most notably on a 48-yard catch and run. He could continue to take work from Hubbard as the season continues. However, he's in for a tough Week 2 matchup, with Atlanta allowing just 2.8 yards per rush attempt in Week 1, the best mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jonathon Brooks (groin) is expected to operate as the Panthers' No. 2 running back if active for the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Brooks is considered week-to-week after tweaking the same groin he first injured during training camp in the Week 2 win over the Falcons. Prior to his injury, the Texas product was clearly operating as Carolina's second RB, tallying just nine carries for 30 yards and two catches for 43 yards over the team's first two contests. Brooks will likely to find fantasy relevance if active in Week 3, with Cleveland's defense allowing just 16.9 PPR fantasy points per game to the position thus far.

player.seasonOutlook: Brooks is hoping to get his career on track in 2026 after appearing in only one game since being drafted in the second round of the 2024 draft. Brooks spent most of his rookie season recovering from a torn ACL suffered while at the University of Texas. He returned in Week 12 and handled 12 touches in three games prior to retearing the same ACL and missing the entire 2025 season. Only 23 years old and skilled as a rusher and receiver, Brooks figures to eventually get his shot at a lead-back role in the pros. He's expected to battle for touches with Chuba Hubbard this season, so it's possible he quickly earns his way into a fantasy-relevant role. Consider him in the middle rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Denzel Boston and the Browns travel to battle the Buccaneers in Week 2. The rookie pass-catcher corralled two of four targets for 59 yards and a TD during Cleveland's 34-10 season-opening loss. Boston's touchdown was a 46-yard dime from Deshaun Watson, and he finished as the team leader in receiving yards. He draws a tough matchup against Tampa Bay, which ranked fourth in receptions allowed to WRs (8).
outlooksByWeek.3: Denzel Boston and the Browns host the Panthers in a Week 3 clash between 1-1 teams. The rookie followed up his 2-59-1 receiving line in the opener with an even better outing against the Buccaneers, tallying five catches on seven targets for 95 yards and another TD. Boston led the team in yardage and targets, as he's quickly becoming Deshaun Watson's preferred target, particularly downfield. He faces a vulnerable Carolina defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points allowed (30.3) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Denzel Boston and the Browns host the Steelers and their eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (28.0) to WRs in Week 4. The rookie wideout caught two of four targets for 41 yards and scored on a two-point conversion during Cleveland's 21-18 victory in Week 3. Boston finished second on the team in yardage behind Harold Fannin Jr. (51) as he continues to develop chemistry with QB Deshaun Watson. He's shaping up to be a boom-or-bust fantasy option but offers plenty of upside as the Browns' deep option for an improving offense.
outlooksByWeek.5: Denzel Boston and the Browns are on the road to take on the Jets in Week 5. He caught four of seven targets for a team-high 89 yards during Cleveland's 27-24 win in Week 4. Boston tied for third in targets and continued to prove himself as a big-play option, generating 60 yards on one reception that helped set up a Browns' touchdown run. He'll face a strong Jets secondary that allows 28.5 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks ninth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Denzel Boston and the Browns host the division-rival Ravens for an AFC North clash in Week 6. He caught three of seven targets for 46 yards, including a 29-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter, during Cleveland's 17-12 Week 5 loss. The rookie wideout continues to shine for the Browns, as he now has a 16-330-3 line on 29 targets through five games to begin his career. With KC Concepcion (concussion) questionable for Week 6, Boston should remain Deshaun Watson's top target versus Baltimore's 23rd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per contest (36.2) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Denzel Boston and the Browns are on the road for an interconference clash against the Titans in Week 7. He caught just one of five targets for 15 yards during Cleveland's comeback victory in Week 6. Boston tied for last in receptions but finished second in targets, as Deshaun Watson completed only 16 of his 26 pass attempts. It's still a positive sign that the Browns want to get the ball in the rookie's hands despite the meager offensive output. Boston will aim to bounce back versus Tennessee's 24th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (35.9) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Denzel Boston and the Browns head to Pittsburgh for an AFC North clash in Week 8. He hauled in three of eight targets for 27 yards in Cleveland's 27-24 victory in Week 7. Boston finished third on the team in targets but was a distant fourth in yardage behind fellow rookie KC Concepcion (129), Harold Fannin Jr. (91) and Dylan Sampson (32). Boston will look to rebound against a Steelers defense he posted a 4-89-0 receiving line on seven targets back in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.10: Denzel Boston and the Browns welcome the 3-5 Texans to town in Week 10. He corralled six of seven targets for 98 yards during Cleveland's 23-22 overtime loss in Week 9. Boston just missed the 100-yard mark but established a new career high in receiving yards, pacing his team in receptions, yardage, and targets. He showed great rapport with Shedeur Sanders, who earned his first start of the season, but Deshaun Watson (concussion) is likely to return from a one-game absence to face his former team. Boston will look to build upon this effort against a Houston defense allowing the third-most fantasy points per game (38.5) to opposing WRs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Denzel Boston and the Browns host the 4-7 Raiders on Sunday Night Football in Week 12. He brought in one of two targets for 16 yards during Cleveland's 27-24 win in Week 10. Boston struggled while appearing to aggravate a toe injury in the victory, but hopefully, the rookie has had enough time to get close to 100% following the team's bye. Boston will aim to find the end zone for the first time since Week 5 against a Las Vegas defense that's given up 13 TDs to the position, tied for fourth most in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Boston was selected by the Browns in the second round of April's draft. He is a big receiver with terrific ball skills and touchdown-scoring upside. He's not the fastest, but that didn't stop him from producing 62-plus receptions, 830-plus yards and nine-plus TDs during both of his seasons as a starter at Washington. He handled 45% of his team's air yards in 2025 (highest in this rookie class). Boston dropped only four of 209 career targets (1.9% drop rate is fourth best in this WR class) and has the look of a reliable possession receiver. He'll begin his career battling Jerry Jeudy, Harold Fannin Jr. and fellow rookie KC Concepcion for targets in a Cleveland offense yet to sort out its quarterback situation. Boston is a fine late-round-upside flier.

Brian Flores' blitz-happy defense has managed exactly 49 sacks, fourth-most in the league, in each of the past two seasons, playing a big part in the team finishing among the position's top seven in fantasy scoring in each of those years. Though Jonathan Allen and Jonathan Greenard are no longer with the team, the Vikings' draft selections of DTs Caleb Banks and Domonique Orange should at least keep them competitive up front. That said, the Vikings face a brutal opening schedule (GB, Week 1; @CHI, Week 2) and have one of the toughest second-half schedules in the league. Be prepared to pivot if this D/ST starts slowly.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jordan Love should continue to lead a high-volume passing attack as the Packers take on the Jets in Week 2. Love finished Week 1 with the second-highest passing yard total of his career (387), completing 21 of 42 passes with two touchdowns and one interception. Most of his success came in the first half, with then two turnovers and virtually no offensive prowess in the fourth quarter. With that being said, Green Bay should continue to rely on the passing offense, especially given that there's no return timeline for RB1 Josh Jacobs (personal). Given that Love was able to find success against one of the best defenses in the game, he should have no problem piecing up a New York unit that allowed the seventh-most fantasy points per game (22.1) to QBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jordan Love will look to make a statement as the Packers take on the Falcons in Week 3. Love snuck out a win for Green Bay in Week 2, but a 55.2 percent completion rate for 145 yards, even with a 2:0 TD:INT, was uninspiring against the Jets. The sixth-year gunslinger luckily still sits at 532 passing yards on the year with four touchdowns and one interception, and his high volume only looks to continue with Josh Jacobs' return date uncertain. He'll face an Atlanta defense that gave up 287 passing yards and three touchdowns to Bryce Young this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jordan Love will look to get the Packers back in the win column against Tampa Bay in Week 4. Love posted friendly fantasy numbers in Week 3 even amidst a disappointing loss, completing 52.8 percent of passes for 312 yards, two touchdowns and one interception. The sixth-year quarterback has now thrown two touchdowns in every game so far this season, and he's eclipsed 300 passing yards twice. Love remains a solid, high-volume option moving forward, especially given the struggles of Green Bay's run game. He'll face a Bucs defense that's allowed a top-10 18.3 fantasy points per game to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jordan Love will look to deliver a big win for the Packers in Week 5 against the Bears. Love completed 22 of 30 passes for 197 yards with a 2:1 TD:INT in a close win over Tampa Bay in Week 4. The veteran quarterback has now completed a career-low 56 percent of passes for 1,041 yards with eight touchdowns and three interceptions this season, with 300 or more passing yards in two of four outings. Love will take on a Chicago defense that's ranked 12th in fantasy points allowed to quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jordan Love will look to keep it rolling as the Packers play the Cowboys in Week 6. Love was on fire in a blowout win over the Bears in Week 5, completing 25 of 31 passes for 367 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions. After a shaky but still touchdown-heavy start to the season, he's now completed 73 percent or more of his passes in back-to-back weeks and totaled 564 passing yards with a 4:1 TD:INT ratio in that stretch. Love will have the perfect opportunity to replicate his greatness again, as Dallas has ranked 25th in fantasy points allowed to quarterbacks (23.8) so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jordan Love will look to keep an electric stretch going as the Packers travel to Detroit in Week 7. Love was solid in another Packers win in Week 6, completing 23 of 41 passes for 276 yards with a 1:1 TD:INT ratio, and he also made some noise on the ground with two rushes for 14 yards and a touchdown. The fourth-year starter has now thrown for more than 275 yards in four of six games this season, and he's thrown two touchdowns in all but one outing. He'll enter another favorable matchup as the Lions have allowed the most fantasy points per game to quarterbacks on the year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jordan Love will aim to get the Packers back in the win column in Week 8 versus the Panthers. Even with Josh Jacobs back on the field at Detroit in Week 7, Green Bay still leaned on the passing game, with Love completing 27 of 45 passes for 274 yards with a 2:1 TD:INT ratio. He's now thrown for two touchdowns in all but one game this season, but he's still totaled two in every outing. Love should have no problem continuing his success against a Carolina defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy quarterbacks.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jordan Love will aim to keep it rolling as the Packers play the Patriots in Week 9. Love stayed hot in a Week 8 win over the Panthers, completing 30 of 41 passes for 288 yards with a 3:1 TD:INT ratio. He's now thrown for 250-plus yards in six of eight games and recorded two or more touchdowns in every outing of the season. Love will face a New England defense that ceded 211 passing yards, two touchdowns and one interception to his former backup, Malik Willis, this past weekend.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jordan Love will look to keep his MVP campaign rolling as the Packers play the Vikings in Week 10. Love was on fire again in a Week 9 win over the Patriots, completing 23 of 29 passes for 372 yards with three passing touchdowns and a 13-yard rushing score. Green Bay's signal caller has now dished out two or more touchdowns and passed for 270 or more yards in each of his last three outings. He'll rematch a Vikings defense that he threw for 387 yards, two touchdowns and one interception against in a Week 1 loss.
outlooksByWeek.12: Jordan Love will travel to take on the Rams in a Week 12 matchup for Green Bay out of the bye. Love and the Packers went into their off week with many questions, with the starting quarterback throwing for 220 yards and a 1:1 TD:INT versus Minnesota in Week 10. Love has still put together an impressive first half of the season, with multiple touchdowns in all but one game and 2,838 passing yards across 10 weeks. Los Angeles has ranked a tough fourth in fantasy points allowed to QBs this campaign, so Love might have his work cut out for him to return to dominance.

player.seasonOutlook: Love is back for his fourth season as the Packers' starting quarterback. The 2020 first-round pick has emerged as one of the league's best passers (he has finished ninth, fifth and third in QBR during his three seasons as a starter), but that hasn't converted to much fantasy production as of late. After finishing sixth in fantasy points per game in 2023, Love has finished 17th and 21st the past two seasons. A dramatic dip in both passing (19th in pass attempts both years) and rushing (282 yards and one TD total during the two seasons) has been the culprit. Love, who produced just five weekly finishes better than 16th last season, has a limited ceiling in Matt LaFleur's scheme. He's best valued as a back-end QB2.

outlooksByWeek.2: DeMario Douglas will seek more production in Week 2 when the Patriots face the Steelers. He logged a reasonable seven targets to open the season but turned that into just 20 yards on five grabs. Douglas has a rapport with QB Drake Maye as a safety valve, and while snaps seem safe with A.J. Brown (ankle) sidelined for the foreseeable future, Douglas topped 40 yards just four times last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: DeMario Douglas' role in New England's struggling passing offense is questionable ahead of a Week 3 game at Jacksonville. In Week 2, Douglas logged just two targets in his first full game without A.J. Brown after a seven-target opener, and he's averaging just 4.8 yards per reception to start the season. Jacksonville is allowing a hefty 10.3 yards per target to opposing wideouts, but Douglas' inability to stretch the field would require uncharacteristic heavy volume to provide a modest fantasy return.
outlooksByWeek.4: DeMario Douglas hasn't been consistently targeted in the Patriots struggling passing attack ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Douglas has just one catch in each of his last two games, and while last week's popped for 38 yards, he's averaging just 9.4 yards on his seven snags to date. Buffalo's defense has been friendly to opposing wideouts, allowing 9.3 ypt with six receivers going for 40+ yards, but with limited volume, Douglas doesn't seem destined to exploit that.
outlooksByWeek.5: DeMario Douglas hasn't emerged in the Patriots' receiving corps ahead of a Week 5 matchup against the Raiders. Despite A.J. Brown's continued absence, Douglas has just four total catches over the last three weeks, tallying 62 yards. An uptick in volume appears unlikely against an exploitable secondary that allows 8.2 yards per target, leaving Douglas as a dart throw as opposed to a reliable lineup option.
outlooksByWeek.6: DeMario Douglas faces an uphill battle to match Week 5's success when the Patriots face the Jets in Week 6. Douglas shined with two touchdowns and a season-high 65 yards against the Raiders, but he's still hauled in no more than two balls in three of five outings while being held to 38 yards or fewer in his first four games. New England is spreading the ball around in its surging passing attack, so Douglas seems unlikely to retain heavy volume. The Jets have allowed four opposing receivers to register 63 yards or more in the last two weeks, giving Douglas a shot at some upside.
outlooksByWeek.7: DeMario Douglas is emerging as a viable option for the Patriots ahead of a Week 7 matchup with the Bears. Over the past two weeks, Douglas has garnered 13 targets, turning them into 11 catches and three touchdowns. Though A.J. Brown is back from an ankle injury, New England could be without Romeo Doubs due to a shoulder ailment, suggesting Douglas' place in the receiving pecking order may be unchanged, giving him a chance to post solid numbers against a secondary that's allowed nine opposing receivers to gain at least 55 yards.
outlooksByWeek.8: DeMario Douglas will seek a rebound in Week 8 when New England travels to Miami. He was on a two-game heater entering Week 7, but finished with just three catches for 23 yards and has been held to 38 yards or fewer in five of seven outings. Miami is allowing an attractive 8.8 yards per target, the eighth-highest total league-wide, but because of vulnerabilities to tight ends and running backs in the passing game, opposing wideouts have the second-fewest yards, suggesting it may be better to look elsewhere for meaningful production.
outlooksByWeek.9: DeMario Douglas' volume has been sporadic despite the Patriots' receiving corps rarely being at full strength entering a Week 9 matchup with the Packers. Douglas has four touchdowns over his last four games, but he has four or fewer targets in half of New England's eight games, failing to top 23 yards at the same rate. Green Bay is allowing just 7.0 yards per target to wideouts, suggesting Douglas would need to maintain his scoring prowess to be a viable Week 9 option.
outlooksByWeek.10: DeMario Douglas will look to continue his recent surge when the Patriots face the Lions in Week 10. Douglas had a season-high 102 yards on nine targets in Week 9, a game that developed into a pass-heavy shootout. A similar game script could be on tap against a Detroit defense that has allowed the fourth-most passing yards. A potential return for A.J. Brown may reduce Douglas' targets, but with the expectation the Patriots will throw often, he can post 65 yards or better for the sixth time in seven weeks.
outlooksByWeek.12: DeMario Douglas has an uncertain role ahead of the Patriots' Week 12 matchup against the Chargers. Douglas was held to a season-low three-yard catch in Week 10 with Drake Maye injured on the opening drive. The Week 11 bye is likely not sufficient for Douglas and new QB Tommy DeVito to develop a rapport. The Chargers offer an exploitable matchup, allowing 9.1 yards per target, but Douglas' volume will be in question, suggesting a wait-and-see approach is prudent.

outlooksByWeek.2: Caleb Douglas will look to build on his Week 1 emergence when the Dolphins face the 49ers in Week 2. Douglas logged an impressive five catches for 94 yards in his NFL debut, garnering seven targets. Miami will likely continue to pass while playing from behind on a weekly basis, and it appears Douglas and QB Malik Willis have a solid connection. San Francisco's defense was stingy against the pass to open the year, allowing just 6.4 yards per target, but volume can reign supreme and Douglas appears to have that potential, making him an intriguing Week 2 option.
outlooksByWeek.3: Caleb Douglas' status for the Dolphins' Week 3 matchup with the Chiefs is uncertain due to an ankle injury. Douglas played a hefty 85% of the team's offensive snaps before suffering the injury late in Week 2 but recorded just 19 yards after a 94-yard career debut. Should he play, Douglas is a speculative upside play for fantasy teams in need of Week 3 help.
outlooksByWeek.4: Caleb Douglas will need to overcome an ankle injury keeping him out of Week 3 to help the Dolphins in Week 4 against the Vikings. After an impressive Week 1, Douglas recorded only three targets in Week 2 despite an 86% snap share. Malik Willis' play under center remains shaky, leading to inconsistency among Miami's receivers. Willis will be scrambling facing a blitz-heavy Vikings defense, but they are allowing generous 8.2 yards per target to opposing wideouts if Douglas is able to push downfield.
outlooksByWeek.5: Caleb Douglas will need to overcome an ankle injury to help the Dolphins against the Bengals in Week 5. He missed the last two weeks, and his role in this low-volume passing offense is questionable; he drew seven targets in Week 1 and only three in Week 2. The Bengals defense is much improved and ranks 14th in points allowed to opposing wideouts, with no receiver topping 63 yards against them. While Douglas can stretch the field, availability and usage remain question marks.
outlooksByWeek.7: Caleb Douglas hopes to emerge from the Dolphins' bye week healthy and help their struggling passing game in Week 7 against the Jets. Douglas hasn't played since Week 2 due to an ankle injury and was used at varying rates when healthy: seven targets in his debut followed by just three the following week. While his 94 yards in Week 1 show potential, uncertain availability and opportunity likely keep him off the radar for lineup consideration against a slightly above-average Jets' secondary that's surrendering 7.3 yards per target.
outlooksByWeek.8: Caleb Douglas appears to be emerging as a big-play option in the Dolphins' low-volume passing game ahead of a Week 8 matchup with the Patriots. Returning from a three-game absence in Week 7, Douglas brought in two of three targets for 70 yards and two touchdowns. He's only caught two balls in two of his three healthy appearances, but is averaging 20.3 yards per catch, and his large frame makes him a potential red zone candidate. If New England jumps out to an early lead, it could help Douglas' snap share, setting him up as a low-floor, high-ceiling option against a defense allowing a generous 8.8 yards per target.
outlooksByWeek.10: Caleb Douglas appears to be the best option among Dolphins receivers entering a Week 10 matchup with the Colts. He has 14 targets over the last two weeks as Malik Washington's role shrinks, and Douglas has 70 receiving yards in two of his last three outings despite Malik Willis' struggles. Indianapolis is more vulnerable against the run, which figures to be Miami's plan offensively, especially with Kyle McCord replacing the injured Willis, but Douglas has proven he can take advantage of whatever opportunities come his way, setting him up for a deep league play against a defense that's allowing 8.8 yards per target to opposing wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.11: Caleb Douglas continues to make big plays on increased chances ahead of the the Dolphins' Week 11 game against the Bills. Douglas notched eight targets for the second-straight game in Week 10, reaching 70 yards for the third time in four outings. While new quarterback Kyle McCord threw 32 passes to 11 different teammates in his debut, Douglas remained the steady top option. Buffalo allows just 7.3 yards per target, the eighth-lowest in the league, but with Miami likely to be throwing from behind often, Douglas can be a preferred option.
outlooksByWeek.12: Caleb Douglas is emerging as the top option in Miami's limited passing game ahead of a Week 12 matchup with the Jets. He amassed a career-high 10 targets in Week 11 but brought in only two of them, finishing with 30 yards. The Dolphins have failed to reach the end zone through the air in two games with Kyle McCord at the helm, but Douglas brings volume into Week 12. He solved the Jets with two touchdowns and 70 yards on just two receptions in Week 7, but given McCord's volatility, lowering Douglas on your wide receiver depth chart is prudent in Week 12. Douglas is a high-upside WR/flex.

player.seasonOutlook: Douglas was selected by the Dolphins in the third round of April's draft. Douglas is a tall, perimeter receiver with big hands and long arms who, after not seeing much work during two seasons at Florida, exploded for 60-877-6 and 54-846-7 receiving lines at Texas Tech over the last two seasons. His overall efficiency was underwhelming, including six drops and a shaky 1.81 YPRR in 2025. He impressed with a 4.39 40-yard dash at 206 pounds (111 speed score) at the combine. Douglas has a path to a large offensive role as a rookie (Malik Washington, Jalen Tolbert and fellow rookie Chris Bell are his primary competition), but life may be tough in a rebuilding Miami offense led by unproven Malik Willis. He's only worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Isaiah Likely scored twice in his debut for the Giants in Week 1, leading a stunning victory over the Cowboys. Likely caught all eight of his targets for 78 yards and the two scores to lead the Giants in receiving. Especially in the red zone and on third down, quarterback Jaxson Dart leaned heavily on his new tight end, something that should continue in Week 2 versus the Rams. Los Angeles allowed 205 passing yards and three touchdowns in its dismal season-opening loss to the 49ers, while also losing star acquisition Myles Garrett to a knee injury. Aaron Donald will make his return from retirement to help out the defensive line, though.
outlooksByWeek.3: Isaiah Likely led the Giants in both receptions and targets last game. Despite seeing 10 opportunities, though, Likely caught five passes for just 33 yards in the dismal loss to the Rams. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, Likely will likely see his stock take a hit. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a lackluster Titans defense allowing 233.5 passing yards per clash, which is 20th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Isaiah Likely's breakout season likely came to a crashing halt with the injury to Jaxson Dart. Likely managed just two catches for 13 yards in the win over the Titans last game. Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which has limited the opportunities for Likely.  Winston should remain under center in Week 4 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Isaiah Likely led the Giants in targets last game. Likely saw a staggering 12 balls thrown his way en route to seven catches for 66 yards in the win over Arizona. However, fellow tight end Theo Johnson stole a touchdown from him. Still, Likely's renewed usage with quarterback Jameis Winston under center was a pleasant surprise, as Likely only had five targets in the prior game versus Tennessee. A tasty matchup lurks in Week 5 versus Washington. The Commanders defense has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. Washington has allowed 11 passing scores, which is tied for last in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders are yielding 242.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Isaiah Likely exploded for 11 receptions and two touchdowns last game for the Giants. The 11 receptions set a career high, and Likely scored twice for the second time in five contests. Likely has a staggering 25 targets over the last two outings alone. In Week 6, the Giants host the Saints. New Orleans has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, allowing just 212.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the league. However, New Orleans has also given up eight passing scores already, which is tied for 20th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Isaiah Likely has remained extremely busy for the Giants, regardless of who lines up at quarterback. Likely has received double-digit targets in four of the last five games for the G-Men. Likely has scored three times in the last two contests, and five times on the season overall. Likely leads all NFL tight ends in receiving yards and touchdowns, and is second in receptions to Trey McBride. Likely should be primed for another big outing in Week 7 versus the Texans. Houston is allowing 246 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: Isaiah Likely had a surprisingly poor game for the Giants his last time on the field. Likely managed just two catches for 12 yards in the thrilling 27-21 OT win over the Texans. Likely had managed double-digit targets in each of the previous three games for the G-Men, so the lack of looks was eye-opening. Still, new quarterback J.J. McCarthy was working under center and targeted star wideout Malik Nabers with reckless abandon. Likely should see more work in Week 9 versus the Eagles. Philadelphia is allowing 235.4 passing yards per contest, which is 24th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Isaiah Likely found the end zone again for the Giants last game. Likely snagged five passes for 53 yards and a touchdown in the 19-11 win over Philadelphia. Likely now has scored four touchdowns in his last four contests. He is a great bet to find the end zone again versus a suspect Washington pass defense. Washington has surrendered 16 passing touchdowns this season, which is tied for 25th in the league.  In addition, the Commanders are allowing 240 passing yards per clash, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.11: Isaiah Likely notched a career-high 127 yards receiving last game for the Giants. Likely reeled in nine passes, one of which went for a 66-yard touchdown, though the G-Men fell to Washington by a score of 24-21. Still, Likely has scored in back-to-back contests, and has five scores in his last five outings.  In Week 11, the Giants will face a Jacksonville defense that has been mediocre against the pass in 2026. The Jags are allowing 228.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 19th in the NFL. However, Jacksonville has surrendered just 10 passing scores this season, which is fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: Isaiah Likely had an unexpectedly quiet game for the Giants last week.  Despite the win, Likely managed just one grab for 35 yards. he had a season-low three targets for the contest.  Likely is having a breakout campaign for the G-Men overall, though, so expect a return to normalcy in Week 12 versus the Colts. Indy is allowing 220.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 14th in the NFL. However, the Colts have also surrendered 20 throwing scores, which is 28th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Likely signed with the Giants after four years of backing up Mark Andrews in Baltimore. Likely is reuniting with coach John Harbaugh and is finally expected to play a consistent offensive role. During his time in Baltimore, Likely was limited to 50% of the team's offensive snaps and never finished a season better than 20th among tight ends in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards or fantasy PPG. His only extensive stretch with Andrews sidelined came back in 2023. During the seven-game span, Likely posted a 23-356-6 receiving line on a 16% target share and averaged a solid 13.5 fantasy PPG. The 26-year-old is obviously unproven, but his receiving skills in New York's ascending offense are enough to put him on the TE2 radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: Emmett Johnson contributed in his NFL debut, gaining 24 yards on eight carries and catching both his targets for 44 yards in a season-opening win over the Broncos. Kansas City leaned heavily on its ground game, with Kenneth Walker having a career-best day on 26 touches. Johnson's volume may be repeatable if this proves to be the team's offensive formula in 2026 and they continue building big second-half leads. Johnson will look to take advantage of his opportunities in Week 2 against a Colts defense that was just steamrolled by Derrick Henry but ranked 11th in points per game allowed to RBs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Emmett Johnson logged only four touches as Kenneth Walker's primary backup in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, as the fifth-round rookie continues to get his feet wet in the NFL. Johnson also saw a little work as a kickoff returner as the team looks to find ways to get the ball in his hands. As long as Walker is healthy, Johnson's workload will remain limited, but he's flashed some big-play potential in the early going with 64 receiving yards on just four catches. He'll face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's been more vulnerable through the air than on the ground so far in 2026, allowing 3.5 yards per carry, which ranks sixth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Emmett Johnson remains in a limited role behind Kenneth Walker in the Kansas City backfield. Through three games, the fifth-round rookie has only 20 touches-16 carries and four receptions-but has managed to turn that into 120 scrimmage yards. Coach Andy Reid has hinted that Johnson's workload will increase as the season wears on, but as yet there's been no actual sign of that happening. Johnson will be a dart throw, albeit one with big-play upside, in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that is tied for 10th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs and has given up just one touchdown to the position so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.6: Emmett Johnson has seen little work to begin his career as the No. 2 running back for Kansas City behind bell cow Kenneth Walker. Johnson is averaging just 3.5 yards per carry, but the fifth-round rookie has teased his big-play potential as a pass catcher, catching all five of his targets for 74 yards. As long as Walker remains healthy, Johnson will remain little more than an upside bench stash. He could get some garbage-time touches in Week 6 against a Chargers defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Emmett Johnson remains stuck in a low-volume role behind Kenneth Walker in the Kansas City backfield. Johnson hasn't logged double-digit touches since Week 1, and his three targets in a Week 6 win over the Chargers were a season-high. The rookie running back will likely need an injury to Walker to contribute. Johnson will look for his first NFL touchdown in Week 7 against a Seahawks defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Emmett Johnson continues to work his way into the Kansas City game plan as a pass-catcher. Over the last two games, the rookie has corralled four of six targets for 35 yards while the team deals with injuries to its wide receiver corps. Johnson will not challenge a healthy Kenneth Walker as the lead back, but Andy Reid is trying to find ways to get Johnson the ball in space. The result has been a 9-109-0 line on 11 targets through his first six NFL games. Johnson will look to score his first career touchdown in Week 8 against a Broncos defense that ranks 23rd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Emmett Johnson took advantage of his opportunities again in Kansas City's Week 9 win over the Jets, scoring his first career rushing touchdown while gaining 34 yards on six carries. Kenneth Walker, who found the end zone three times in the victory, remains firmly on top of the depth chart, but Johnson is beginning to earn a steady workload as the No. 2 option in the backfield. The rookie is averaging a tidy 4.3 yards per carry on the ground, while adding a 14-237-1 line on 16 targets over eight games. Johnson could make an impact on limited touches again in Week 10 against a Falcons defense that's tied for 29th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Emmett Johnson was incredible in his first career NFL start in Week 10 against the Falcons, leading Kansas City to a big win with 171 scrimmage yards and two receiving touchdowns. The opportunity came with Kenneth Walker sidelined by a groin injury, but the issue isn't expected to keep the former Seahawk sidelined for long. Johnson's performance does make a case for him to take on a bigger workload as the No. 2 option in the backfield once Walker is back. Johnson will look to exploit what volume he gets in Week 11 against a Cardinals defense that's tied for 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Emmett Johnson has taken full advantage of Kenneth Walker's absence from the Kansas City backfield due to a groin strain. Over two games with Walker on the sideline, Johnson has erupted for 206 rushing yards and a touchdown while adding a 10-108-2 line on 11 targets. While the rookie running back will return to the No. 2 role once Walker is cleared to return, Johnson's performance could encourage Andy Reid to use more of a timeshare between them in order to keep both fresh ahead of the playoffs. Walker is expected to return in Week 12 against the Bills, but Johnson might be able to make a difference on limited touches against a defense that ranks 21st in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Johnson was selected by the Chiefs in the fifth round of April's draft. His career 3.4 forced missed tackle rate is fourth best in this RB rookie class and his elusiveness helped him to 1,451 rushing yards (fourth in the nation and first in this class) last season. His lack of speed -- last among 10 RBs who ran the 40-yard dash (4.56) and speed score (93) at the combine -- and size limits him after initial contact (career 2.86 YAC), but he can help out in the passing game (92 collegiate receptions). Johnson and Brashard Smith are set to handle No. 2/3 duties behind Kenneth Walker III. Smith will be worth rostering only if Walker misses action.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Boswell and the Steelers are on the road to face the Patriots in Week 2. He finished Pittsburgh's 20-13 Week 1 win versus the Falcons 2-for-3 on field-goal attempts and 2-for-2 on PATs. Boswell's first miss of the season was from 56 yards out, but he was able to connect from 43 and 28 yards. The Steelers have several talented players on offense, but until they prove they can consistently put up 24-28 points a week, Boswell may not generate enough scoring opportunities to warrant a roster spot.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Boswell and the Steelers host the Bengals in Week 3. The 12th-year kicker went 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to New England. Both of Boswell's attempts came from 50-plus yards out, and he's now 1-for-3 from that distance and 3-for-5 overall through two outings in 2026. He'll look to get back on track this Sunday versus a Cincinnati defense allowing 16.5 points per game, tied for eighth.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chris Boswell and the Steelers visit the division-rival Browns in Week 4. He made all three of his field-goal attempts and went 3-for-3 on PATs during Pittsburgh's 30-27 win in Week 3. It was Boswell's first perfect outing through three games, and his 33-yard kick just before the two-minute warning gave the Steelers the lead for good. He'll look to stay hot against Cleveland's 18th-ranked scoring defense, which is allowing 23.7 points per game thus far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chris Boswell and the Steelers return home to take on the Colts in Week 5. He finished Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss in Week 4 converting one of two field-goal attempts while connecting on his lone extra-point try. Boswell's miss came from 48 yards out, and he's now 1-for-4 on kicks equal to or longer than that across four games in 2026. He'll aim to bounce back versus an Indianapolis defense giving up 26.0 points per contest, which ranks 21st in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chris Boswell and the Steelers are on the road to battle the Buccaneers in Week 6. He connected on both of his field-goal attempts and went 4-for-4 on extra-point tries during Pittsburgh's 34-22 victory in Week 5. Over his last three outings, Boswell is 6-for-7 on field goals while making all eight of his PATs. He's on the fantasy radar with the recent strong performances by the Steelers offense, as they've averaged 29.3 points during this three-game stretch. Boswell will try to make an impact against a Tampa Bay defense allowing 22.4 points per game in 2026, but just 15.0 PPG over their previous two.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chris Boswell and the Steelers are in Paris for a Week 7 clash against the Saints. He converted four of five field-goal attempts, including a season-long 58-yarder, and both of his PATs during Pittsburgh's 26-19 overtime win in Week 6. Boswell missed his first kick from 48 yards out, but he made up for it by making four in a row, with three of those makes coming in the fourth quarter to help send the game to OT. He'll get another chance to make an impact versus a New Orleans defense that allows 29.7 points per game, which is tied for the most in the NFL in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.8: Chris Boswell and the Steelers play host to the division rival Browns in Week 8. He went 3-for-3 on field goals and converted his lone PAT during Pittsburgh's 16-10 victory over the Saints in Paris. Boswell is looking to avenge his underwhelming performance against Cleveland in Week 4, as the 35-year-old missed one of two FGAs in the 27-24 defeat. Since then, Boswell is 9-for-10 on FGs and 7-for-7 on extra points. He'll try to keep rolling versus a Browns defense allowing 20.9 points per game, the 12th-fewest in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Chris Boswell and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 10 AFC North showdown against the Bengals. In Week 8, he went 2-for-3 on field goal attempts and connected on all three of his PATs to help Pittsburgh win its fourth straight game. Boswell misfired on a 57-yarder to end their first offensive possession, as the 35-year-old is now 4-for-7 on kicks from 50-plus yards out in 2026. However, he's had three or more FGAs in three consecutive outings, a trend that is likely to continue versus a Cincinnati team scoring the second-most points per game (30.0).
outlooksByWeek.11: In Week 11, Chris Boswell and the Steelers are back on the road to face the 2-7 Eagles. He connected on his only field goal attempt and lone PAT during Pittsburgh's 38-18 loss in Week 10. The Steelers offense struggled mightily to gain any traction until the game was well out of reach, leaving Boswell on the sidelines while his team opted to go for two on their final touchdown. He'll look to get more involved against a Philadelphia defense giving up 24.6 points per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Chris Boswell and the Steelers aim to improve to 5-0 at home when they host the Broncos in Week 12 on Black Friday. He went 3-for-3 on field goal attempts and drilled his lone PAT during Pittsburgh's 19-16 loss in Week 11. Boswell has now converted all of his field goals in consecutive games for the first time all season. The veteran kicker will try to stay perfect versus a Denver defense allowing 21.0 points per game through 10 outings.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bo Nix was held in check by the Kansas City defense in the Broncos' season opener, completing 17 of 28 passes for just 131 yards and a touchdown. He also threw an interception and committed three fumbles, losing one of them, while getting sacked four times. Nix also wasn't able to take advantage of his newest asset, as Jaylen Waddle logged only three targets and caught one of them for two yards. It was a hugely disappointing effort from Nix and the reigning AFC West champions, but they'll look to bounce back in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that ranked 18th last season in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bo Nix rebounded from a sluggish opener to lead the Broncos to a comeback win over the Jaguars in Week 2. The third-year QB has a meager 2:2 TD:INT through two games and has yet to add any production on the ground, but his 288 passing yards In Week 2 were more than double the Week 1 total, and his completion rate jumped from 60.7% to 71.0%. Nix also began establishing some chemistry with new top wideout Jaylen Waddle, who erupted for an 8-138-0 line on 10 targets. Nix will face a Rams defense in Week 3 that has held opposition QBs under a 60% completion rate to begin the season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bo Nix engineered an impressive second-half comeback in the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams, producing two passing TDs and one rushing score despite completing just 50.0% of his passes. The third-year quarterback hasn't had a statistically impressive start to the season, posting a 4:3 TD:INT ratio and passing for barely over 200 yards a game, but Nix has led his team to a 2-1 record. He'll take on a 49ers defense in Week 4 that's been stingy to begin the year, ranking eighth in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Bo Nix wasn't able to pull off another comeback win for the Broncos in a Week 4 loss to the 49ers. The third-year QB failed to complete 60% of his passes for a second straight game, and through four weeks, he's produced just six touchdowns (five passing, one rushing) while committing four turnovers. Denver's lack of a consistent running game isn't helping the offense find a rhythm, but Nix shoulders plenty of responsibility for the team's 2-2 start to the season. He'll try to bounce back in a Week 5 road game against a Chargers defense that's tied for 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to quarterbacks.
outlooksByWeek.6: Bo Nix didn't show any improvement in Week 5 as the Broncos switched back to Sean Payton as their play-caller, throwing for a season-low 123 yards and producing just one touchdown in a win over the Chargers. The third-year QB has a meager 6:3 TD:INT through five games and is completing fewer than 60.0% of his passes, averaging fewer than 200 passing yards per game. There's still reason to believe Nix's numbers will improve once Payton gets back in a rhythm, but the Denver offense's ceiling seems limited even if it's operating at peak efficiency. Nix isn't likely to break out in Week 6 against a Seahawks defense that ranks sixth this season in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Bo Nix continues to struggle, failing to throw a touchdown in Week 6 for the first time this season while compiling a season-low 107 passing yards. The third-year quarterback has produced fewer than 6.0 yards per attempt in four straight games, and the Broncos' switch back to Sean Payton as the play-caller hasn't yet sparked the offense. Nix has just seven total touchdowns (six passing and one rushing) against five turnovers through seven games, but he'll get a chance to build some momentum in Week 7 against a Cardinals defense that's tied for 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Bo Nix contributed most with his legs in the Broncos' Week 7 win over the Cardinals, throwing one TD and running for another. The second score came in the second quarter on a 62-yard scamper, the longest rushing touchdown by a QB in an NFL regular-season game since 2022. Nix's 73 rushing yards on the day nearly doubled his total from the first six weeks combined. Despite that performance, Nix is still on pace for a career-worst campaign, and things won't get easier for him in Week 8 against a Kansas City defense that ranks third in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Bo Nix put together another fourth-quarter comeback in the Broncos' Week 8 win over Kansas City. While the third-year QB's own numbers are nothing special this season, he's led his team to a 6-2 record and first place in the AFC West. Week 8 was only the second time in eight games he's thrown for multiple touchdowns, and his 59.6% completion rate and 6.0 yards per attempt are both career lows. Nix could be poised for his best game of the season in Week 9 against a Panthers defense that just fired its defensive coordinator and is tied for 14th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Bo Nix comes out of the Broncos' bye having built up a bit of momentum, producing multiple touchdowns in three straight games prior to the break while turning the ball over only once during that stretch.
