The third-year quarterback didn't get any reinforcements at the trade deadline, but the emergence of rookie Jonah Coleman in the backfield gives Denver a legitimate running option to help balance the offense, and second-year wideout Pat Bryant returned from IR right before the bye. In Week 11, Nix will take aim at a Raiders defense that ranks 31st in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Bo Nix didn't need to do much in the Broncos' Week 11 win over the Raiders, as rookie running back Jonah Coleman carried the offense. Nix has thrown for 240-plus yards just once all season, and he's produced more than two TDs only once, as the Denver offense has mostly been stuck in neutral. Coleman's emergence could provide Nix with the security he needs to try to throw downfield more often. The third-year quarterback will take on a Steelers defense in Week 12 that ranks fifth in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Nix enters his third NFL season after finishing exactly seventh among quarterbacks in fantasy points during each of his first two campaigns. Nix's passing efficiency has a ways to go (career 6.5 yards per attempt), but his dual-threat ability has kept him in the weekly QB1 mix. Nix has finished both seasons no lower than 11th in pass attempts, completions, passing TDs, carries, rushing yards and rushing TDs. Last season, he provided a solid floor (11 games with 15-plus fantasy points), but his ceiling was low (four top-10 weeks). In 2026, he'll have a new playcaller in Davis Webb and an upgraded group of pass catchers with Jaylen Waddle added to the mix. The 26-year-old is a fringe QB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Courtland Sutton was held in check along with the rest of the Broncos' offense in their season-opening loss to Kansas City, catching two of five targets for just 11 yards. Quarterback Bo Nix couldn't connect with either of his top two wideouts, as Jaylen Waddle also had a poor showing in his Denver debut, and new offensive coordinator Davis Webb may need to go back to the drawing board quickly to get his passing game going. Sutton should face a softer matchup in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that was tied for 17th last season in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Courtland Sutton has had a slow start to the season as the focus of the Broncos' passing game has shifted to Jaylen Waddle. Through two games, Sutton has posted only nine targets, catching five for a meager 36 yards. He still has plenty of existing chemistry with quarterback Bo Nix, and the duo could rekindle it once defenses begin shifting more attention to Waddle, but Sutton figures to be hard-pressed to reach 1,000 receiving yards in 2026 for a third straight season. He'll take on a Rams secondary in Week 3 that's allowed just 19 receptions to WRs through two weeks, tied for seventh in the NFL, though three of them have gone for touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.4: Courtland Sutton continues to fade into a support role in the Broncos' passing game following the acquisition of Jaylen Waddle. His seven targets in a Week 3 win over the Rams were a season-high, and through three games, he's managed just an 8-82-0 line on 16 total looks from Bo Nix. Sutton should see more volume once new play-caller Davis Webb settles in, but he'll have an uphill battle to produce his fourth career 1,000-yard season. He'll face a 49ers secondary in Week 4 that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Courtland Sutton was nearly invisible in the Broncos' Week 4 loss to the 49ers, catching only one of six targets for a measly four yards. The veteran wideout remains firmly behind Jaylen Waddle on the depth chart, but the entire Denver offense is struggling under first-time play caller Davis Webb, and Sutton has produced a weak 9-86-0 line on 22 targets through four games. How long Sean Payton lets that situation last before reclaiming play-calling duties is an open question. Sutton will try to get going in Week 5 against a Chargers secondary that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Courtland Sutton ended his touchdown drought in the Broncos' Week 5 win over the Chargers, catching two of three targets for 18 yards and his first score of the season. The team's entire offense has been sluggish to begin the year, and having Sean Payton take over play-calling duties didn't pay immediate dividends, but it should bode well for Sutton in the long run. He'll face another tough challenge in Week 6 against a Seahawks secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Courtland Sutton's struggles continued in the Broncos' overtime win over the Seahawks in Week 6. The veteran wideout has yet to catch more than three passes in a game this season or reach 50 receiving yards, leaving him with a paltry 13-123-1 line on 28 targets through six games. With quarterback Bo Nix unable to build any momentum, Sutton and the entire passing game offer little upside. He could at least get into the end zone again in Week 7 against a Cardinals secondary that's given up 10 touchdowns to WRs this season, 31st in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Courtland Sutton had another quiet day in the Broncos' Week 7 win over the Cardinals, managing to catch three of five targets for 45 yards. The veteran wideout has been held under 50 receiving yards and three catches or fewer in all seven games so far this season, and he's scored just one TD after hauling in 25 over the prior three years. Sutton isn't likely to break out in Week 8 against a Kansas City secondary that ranks third in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Courtland Sutton set new season highs in catches and receiving yards during the Broncos' Week 8 win over Kansas City, but he still came away with just a 4-53-0 line on four targets. The struggles of quarterback Bo Nix, as well as the offseason addition of Jaylen Waddle, have reduced Sutton's target volume considerably from 2025, and he's on pace for only 79 targets this season after topping 120 in each of the prior two years. He'll try to make do with new role in Week 9 against a Panthers team that just fired its defensive coordinator, and which is tied for 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Courtland Sutton caught a season-high five passes in the Broncos' last game before their Week 10 bye, turning one of the receptions into his second touchdown of the season. The veteran wide receiver's target volume increased after Jaylen Waddle left the contest early due to a concussion. He has yet to reach 50 receiving yards or see double-digit targets in any game this year as the No. 2 option in a sluggish passing game. Sutton will attempt to contribute in Week 11 against a Raiders secondary that ranks 24th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Courtland Sutton disappeared from the game plan in the Broncos' Week 11 win over the Raiders, failing to catch either of his two targets. It's the first time since Week 7 of the 2024 season he hasn't caught a pass, but with the offense leaning more heavily on rookie running back Jonah Coleman, there hasn't been much need for Bo Nix to air it out. Sutton is on pace to fall short of 500 receiving yards over a full season for the first time in his career, and fail to reach 50 catches for the first time since he was a rookie in 2018. He'll be a risky play in Week 12 against a Steelers secondary that ranks 12th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: After producing one season with 1,000 yards and a top-20 fantasy finish during his first six NFL campaigns, Sutton has achieved both in each of the past two years. The 2018 second-round pick's target share actually dipped from 24% in 2024 to 21% in 2025, but he remained heavily involved near the goal line and has now ranked in the top 12 among receivers in TDs each of the last three seasons. In fact, Sutton has now finished in the top 10 at the position in end zone targets four years in a row, tying for third with 56 during the span. Sutton will remain one of Bo Nix's go-to targets, but now 30 years old and with added target competition in Jaylen Waddle, he's best valued as a fantasy WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: De'Von Achane should again be featured for the Dolphins against the 49ers in Week 2. Achane recorded only 11 carries to open the year, with Miami falling behind early-something that is likely to be a weekly occurrence-but he logged five targets. In Week 1, San Francisco allowed 114 rushing yards and a touchdown plus four receptions to backs, and with Achane rarely leaving the field (88% snap share), the makings are there for a safe outing with scoring upside.
outlooksByWeek.3: De'Von Achane's volume remains elite as the Dolphins get set to host the Chiefs in Week 3. Achane has amassed 31 carries and 11 targets through two weeks, and while his 3.5 yards per carry is modest, there aren't many other options with such a safe workload. Kansas City is allowing 4.0 yards per carry, and they'll surely stack the box against Achane, as everyone else is doing. However, the Chiefs have allowed four catches to an opposing back in consecutive weeks. Achane's volume generates a floor, with scoring providing upside.
outlooksByWeek.4: De'Von Achane will miss the remainder of the season after tearing his ACL. Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright will handle the bulk of the Dolphins' carries.

player.seasonOutlook: Achane has quickly staked his claim as one of the best running backs in the league. The 2023 third-round pick has scored either 11 or 12 touchdowns in each of his three seasons and put up a career-high 1,838 scrimmage yards in 2025. Achane's elite receiving production is nothing new (he has finished in the top five among backs in targets and receiving yards in each of the past two years), but he made another leap forward as a rusher last season, finishing fifth at the position in rushing yards. His 5.62 yards per carry is best among qualified backs since he entered the league. The 24-year-old is eyeing his third straight top-five fantasy campaign, and while that might be tricky in an overhauled Miami offense led by quarterback Malik Willis, Achane has minimal competition for touches and should easily be the offensive centerpiece. He's a solid RB1 option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brock Bowers sat out the Raiders' season-opening win over the Dolphins after undergoing minor knee surgery just before the start of the campaign. The star tight end isn't expected to be out for long, and in his absence Michael Mayer will top the team's depth chart at the position, although running back Ashton Jeanty may have been the biggest beneficiary in terms of production against Miami. If Bowers is cleared to return in Week 2, he'll be facing a Chargers defense that finished fifth in PPR points allowed to TEs in 2025, although it couldn't contain Trey McBride to begin the current campaign.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brock Bowers is on track to make his season debut in Week 3 against the Saints after missing the Raiders' first two games due to minor knee surgery at the end of training camp. Knee trouble in 2025 prevented Bowers from repeating his dynamic rookie campaign, but if he's able to get fully healthy again, the star tight end should quickly emerge as the team's top option in the passing game, with little competition from a wide receiver room led by Tre Tucker. Bowers will initially be catching passes from Kirk Cousins, but at some point this season Las Vegas will transition to Fernando Mendoza under center, providing one more wrinkle for the offense. If he gets cleared this week as expected. Bowers will be facing a New Orleans defense that has yet to allow a touchdown to a TE in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brock Bowers made up for lost time after missing the Raiders' first two games while recovering from minor knee surgery. In his Week 3 season debut against the Saints, the star tight end turned 13 targets into a 10-116-1 receiving line. Bowers is the clear No. 1 downfield option for Kirk Cousins, especially considering the lack of talent in the wide receiver room, and as long as he can stay healthy, he should continue to see big volume. He's in a good position to put up big numbers again in Week 4 against a Kansas City defense that's been the stingiest in the league against WRs but ranks just 19th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Brock Bowers shook off an illness to once again be the Raiders' top receiving option in a Week 4 loss to Kansas City. He caught six of 11 targets for 86 yards and a touchdown, finding the end zone for a second straight game after missing the first two weeks of the year while completing his recovery from knee surgery. The star tight end is the most dangerous weapon in Kirk Cousins' arsenal, and he's likely to continue getting double-digit targets on a weekly basis while posting elite numbers. Bowers faces his toughest test of the season so far in Week 5 against a Patriots defense that has allowed the fewest fantasy points per game to TEs in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.6: Brock Bowers continues to make up for lost time, producing an 8-110-1 line on 10 targets in the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots. After missing the first two games of the season while completing his recovery from knee surgery, the superstar tight end has gotten into the end zone in three straight weeks, amassing 24 catches for 312 yards and three scores on 35 targets. Bowers is the clear top option for Kirk Cousins in the passing game, and that isn't likely to change even if Las Vegas eventually switches to rookie Fernando Mendoza under center. Bowers will face a Bills defense in Week 6 that ranks 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Brock Bowers was held somewhat in check by the Bills in Week 6, failing to get double-digit targets for the first time in 2026 and managing a 4-70-0 line on nine looks from Kirk Cousins. Fellow TE Michael Mayer popped for a big game, but Bowers probably won't stay contained for long. Over his four appearances this season, Bowers has a 28-382-3 line on 44 targets as the clear top option in the Raiders' passing game. He'll face a tough test in Week 7 against a Rams defense that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Brock Bowers has been held slightly in check the last two weeks, failing to see double-digit targets in either contest and managing a 10-143-0 line on 17 targets. Those are still strong numbers for a tight end, but a mild disappointment for an elite talent like Bowers. He remains the top option in the Raiders' passing game, even as No. 2 TE Michael Mayer continues to get more work than expected. Bowers will face a tough test in Week 8 against a Jets defense that ranks sixth in fantasy points per game allowed to tight ends, and which has given up just one TD to the position through seven games.
outlooksByWeek.9: Brock Bowers produced his first multi-TD game of the season in the Raiders' Week 8 win over the Jets, turning 10 targets into seven catches for 92 yards and two scores. The star tight end remains the top downfield option for Kirk Cousins, and over six games since making his belated 2026 debut, Bowers has amassed a 41-547-5 line on 62 targets. He could be poised to make another big impact in Week 9 against a 49ers defense that's tied for 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Brock Bowers was nearly the only Raider to find any success in a Week 9 loss to the 49ers, turning eight targets into seven catches for 111 yards and a touchdown. The star tight end has scored six times in seven games since making a belated season debut, and Bowers delivered a 48-658-6 line on 70 targets as Kirk Cousins' clear No. 1 downfield option. He's now likely Francisco Mendoza's top option and will look to keep rolling in Week 10 against a Seahawks defense that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Brock Bowers played just 11 offensive snaps in the Raiders' Week 10 loss to the Seahawks due to an ankle injury, catching both his targets for 18 yards. The star tight end's injury isn't thought to be too serious, but he could miss at least a game or two, potentially opening the door for Michael Mayer to have a bigger role. If Bowers is able to suit up in Week 11 and continue building chemistry with rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza, he'll be taking on a Broncos defense that ranks 30th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Brock Bowers sat out the Raiders' Week 11 loss to the Broncos while dealing with quadriceps and ankle injuries. In his place, Michael Mayer caught just one of four targets, while Ian Thomas secured a one-yard touchdown from Fernando Mendoza. Bowers' absence prevented him from building more chemistry with the rookie quarterback, but the team is optimistic he'll be able to return in Week 12 and resume his spot as the clear No. 1 downfield option in the passing game. If Bowers does get cleared to return, he'll be facing a Browns defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: Bowers entered 2025 with high expectations and appeared well on his way to another productive season with 103 yards in Week 1, but a late-game injury limited him for three weeks and led to five full missed games. Bowers remained productive when healthy, finishing second among tight ends in fantasy PPG. Incredibly, he tied for fifth in the NFL with 13 end zone targets despite all the missed action. Bowers, who posted a 112-1,194-5 receiving line as a rookie in 2024, will be the top target for No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza. The 23-year-old is well positioned for a highly productive season and should be on your radar in the second or third round.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jonathan Taylor carried the Colts' offense with 121 scrimmage yards and two TDs on 22 touches in the season opener. His heavy Week 1 workload was encouraging considering the Colts trailed by 18 points at halftime and lost by that same margin to the Ravens. Indianapolis could face another negative game script in Week 2 at Kansas City, but Taylor remains locked in as a fantasy RB1, even with the team around him looking shaky. Taylor led the NFL with 323 carries and 18 rushing TDs last season while compiling 1,963 scrimmage yards.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jonathan Taylor has scored multiple rushing TDs in both of the Colts' games heading into a Week 3 home tilt against the Texans. The star RB led the NFL with 20 scrimmage TDs last season and looks poised to finish near the top of the leaderboard again this season. Taylor is a set-and-forget fantasy RB1, even against a stout Texans front seven that allowed the fourth-fewest rushing yards to RBs last season and has yet to allow a TD to the position.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jonathan Taylor has four rushing TDs through three games and is averaging 25 touches per game heading into the Colts' Week 4 game against the Commanders in London. Washington has allowed the third-fewest rushing yards in the NFL while struggling to defend the pass, but the Colts have proven they intend to feed their star RB a steady diet of carries regardless of opponent. A positive game script is certainly possible against a Commanders team that's starting backup QB Marcus Mariota, so Taylor has a clear path to another heavy workload and remains a must-start fantasy option.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jonathan Taylor has three multi-TD performances through four games and is averaging 88 rushing yards per game heading into the Colts' Week 5 trip to Pittsburgh. The Steelers rank among the 10 most generous defenses against RBs, allowing 138 scrimmage yards and one TD per game to the position. Taylor remains locked in as a fantasy RB1 while working as the focal point of the Colts' offense, which lacked talent at wide receiver even before injuries further depleted that position. His 26 scrimmage touchdowns since the start of last season are the most in the NFL over that span.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jonathan Taylor has three multi-TD outings on the ground through five games, and he's likely to be the focal point of the Colts' offense in Week 6 against the winless Titans, who are surrendering 120 scrimmage yards per game to RBs. Taylor averages 23 touches per game and should handle a heavy workload, with the Colts expected to play from ahead at home. Start the star RB, who is averaging 101 scrimmage yards per game, with confidence in this clash between AFC South rivals.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jonathan Taylor has topped 90 rushing yards four times this season and has seven TDs, while the rest of the Colts' offense has scored six touchdowns combined. The star RB remains a set-and-forget fantasy RB1 for Week 7, even in a difficult matchup with a stout Vikings defense that's allowing 86.6 rushing yards per game (fifth-fewest) and a league-low 12.8 points per game. Opponents have been stacking the box against Taylor with Daniel Jones struggling to make defenses pay through the air, but Taylor has overcome those difficult situations to rank among the league's most productive players at his position as usual, despite the lack of help from his teammates.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jonathan Taylor has at least 92 rushing yards and a TD in five of the Colts' seven games, keeping him firmly in set-and-forget fantasy RB1 territory for Week 8 despite a difficult matchup against Jacksonville's elite front. The Jaguars are allowing a league-low 72 rushing yards per game and boast the league's third-best scoring defense at 17.3 points per game. Taylor has handled 20-plus touches in all but one game this season and should remain busy in Week 8, as long as the 2-5 Colts stay within striking distance of the 4-2 Jaguars.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jonathan Taylor set season lows with 12 touches for 47 yards in the Colts' 42-7 Week 8 loss to the Jaguars. Indianapolis got down big early and had to abandon the run. The Cowboys have enough talent on offense to repeat the scenario, but it's more likely that the Colts keep things close enough for Taylor to capitalize on facing a Dallas defense that has been among the most generous in the league to RBs, allowing 11 total TDs to the position through eight games. Taylor has eight rushing TDs in eight games, accounting for more than half of the Colts' offensive touchdowns this season. He'll be a fantasy RB1 if he's in his usual role, though it's possible Indianapolis limits Taylor's usage as trade rumors swirl around the star RB.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jonathan Taylor was not traded prior to Tuesday's deadline. He has rushed for 656 yards and eight TDs through nine games with the Colts, putting the star RB on pace for a fifth campaign with at least 1,169 rushing yards and 11 TDs. Taylor has a juicy Week 10 matchup against the 1-7 Dolphins. Despite staying with the Colts, he remains a set-and-forget fantasy RB1.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jonathan Taylor exceeded 100 scrimmage yards for the fifth time in 10 tries during the Colts' Week 10 win over the Dolphins, but he was held without a touchdown for a third consecutive game. Seth McGowan has two rushing TDs during Taylor's three-game drought, both of which came from inside the 5-yard line. The rookie seventh-round pick could remain a thorn in Taylor's side if the Colts continue to give McGowan goal-line opportunities. McGowan's emergence, coupled with the Colts' offensive struggles as a team, knocks Taylor down to the fantasy RB1/RB2 borderline moving forward, and expectations should be tempered in Week 11 against a stout Texans front that limited Taylor to just 72 yards on 25 touches for a season-low 2.9 yards per touch in their first meeting this season. You're still starting Taylor if you have him in virtually every fantasy format, but he's likely to perform closer to his floor than his superstar ceiling in Week 11.
outlooksByWeek.12: Jonathan Taylor has averaged just 16.3 touches over the Colts' last four games after averaging 22.4 touches in the first seven. Part of that decline has to do with the 3-8 Colts failing to remain competitive. Taylor has also started to cede a larger portion of rushing opportunities, including goal-line carries, to Seth McGowan, who won't suit up in Week 12 against the Giants due to a hamstring injury. Taylor remains too good to bench in most leagues, and perhaps Indianapolis' entire ground game will pick up the pace now that mobile, big-armed QB Anthony Richardson is running the show rather than Daniel Jones, but Taylor's nowhere near the top-five fantasy RB conversation at the moment. Treat the star RB as a fantasy RB2 for Week 12 against the Giants, who have been elite at defending the pass but rank in the middle of the pack against the run.

player.seasonOutlook: Taylor enters the 2026 season having improved in fantasy points per game in each of the past three years. Last season, he delivered his best production since his huge 2021 campaign, as he paced the NFL in carries and TDs while finishing second in carries inside the 5-yard line (19) and fourth in fantasy points. A piece of the step forward was increased usage in the passing game, as he ranked in the top 10 among backs in routes, targets, catches and receiving yards, setting career highs in each. Taylor's season likely would've been even better had QB Daniel Jones not been injured, as the running back averaged 24.8 points with Jones but 12.9 without him. Jones is expected to be ready to play in Week 1, so the 27-year-old Taylor is safe to value as a mid- to high-end RB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: DJ Moore will look to build on an impressive debut when the Bills host the Lions in Week 2. Despite new quarterback Josh Allen continuing to spread the ball around, Moore popped with a 100-yard outing on eight targets. The Lions gave up 410 passing yards to open the year, but just 7.3 yards per attempt as New Orleans was forced to throw from behind. That may not be the case Thursday, and Moore is unlikely to garner high volume. Even so, facing a secondary void of high-end talent, Moore can get deep and provide big yardage without a lot of opportunity.
outlooksByWeek.3: DJ Moore will need to overcome a shoulder injury if he is to help the Bills in Week 3 against the Chargers. After showing sound chemistry with Josh Allen in his first action for Buffalo, Moore failed to haul in a touchdown late in the second quarter in Week 2, suffering the injury that forced him to miss the second half. The Chargers have allowed three touchdowns to opposing receivers through two weeks and two 75-plus yardage performances, which should thrust Moore back into fantasy relevance if he's able to reprise his No. 1 WR role.
outlooksByWeek.4: DJ Moore aims to remain heavily involved in the Bills' Week 4 game against the Patriots. In two healthy games, Moore has 18 targets as Josh Allen's top option, creating a stable floor. New England's secondary is middling, allowing the 18th-most fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts, but outside of Jaxon Smith-Njigba, no one has topped 64 yards against them. Moore's potential could be further capped if he draws shadow coverage from Christian Gonzalez.
outlooksByWeek.5: DJ Moore continues to battle a shoulder issue as the Bills get set to travel in Week 5 to face the Rams. Moore exited Week 4's game against New England after aggravating the injury, his second early departure in four games. When playing an entire four quarters, Moore has dominated targets from Josh Allen, averaging nine looks. However, pairing injury concerns with the Rams' secondary not allowing an opposing receiver to top 50 yards, Moore could struggle in Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.6: DJ Moore continues to battle through a shoulder issue that's cost him the better part of three games as the Bills head towards a Week 6 matchup with the Raiders. Moore has drawn 18 targets in his two healthy games, making his shoulder the only factor to worry about when considering him in lineups. The Raiders have allowed at least 91 yards to an opposing wideout in three straight weeks, adding confidence to Moore's viability if he proves healthy.
outlooksByWeek.8: DJ Moore hopes to be fully healthy following Buffalo's bye week in advance of their Week 8 matchup with the Ravens. Moore hasn't played since a brief appearance in Week 4 due to a shoulder injury that has lingered since Week 2. When on the field, he has been Josh Allen's favorite target, collecting 18 looks in two games. Baltimore has allowed four 100-yard receivers and an attractive 9.3 yards per target, the fifth-highest in the league, making Moore an attractive option if he suits up.
outlooksByWeek.9: DJ Moore will look to overcome a knee injury and help the Bills in Week 9 against the Vikings. It's been simple: when Moore plays, he's heavily involved, amassing 25 targets in three games. Minnesota is allowing the third-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts, surrendering just four touchdown catches and 7.4 yards per target, but if he's on the field, Moore will have the volume necessary to be a viable lineup consideration.
outlooksByWeek.10: DJ Moore will look for increased volume when the Bills face the Jets in Week 10. Moore collected only five targets in Week 9, his lowest total in any healthy outing of 2026, in a game where Josh Allen had minimal time to throw. While he'll likely have more time Sunday and Moore has remained the preferred option on drop-backs, the Jets have allowed only nine touchdown receptions to wideouts, seemingly capping Moore's potential.
outlooksByWeek.11: DJ Moore will seek more big plays in Week 11 when the Bills face the Dolphins. Moore is averaging 16.3 yards per catch, the second-highest mark of his nine-year career, and gets an inviting matchup with a secondary that's allowing 9.3 yards per target to wideouts, the sixth-highest mark league-wide. Moore will need those big yardage chances as Buffalo threw only 21 times in Week 10 while blowing out the Jets, and a similar game script is likely against Miami.
outlooksByWeek.12: DJ Moore will try to maintain his recent scoring spree when the Bills face a strong Chiefs secondary in Week 12. Moore tied a season-high with 10 targets in Week 11, recording at least 82 yards receiving and scoring for the second time in as many games and third in four outings. Kansas City counters with only three touchdowns allowed to receivers in 10 contests, and a mere 6.6 yards per target. Moore will need steady volume to finish in the upper tier of receivers.

player.seasonOutlook: Moore was traded to Buffalo after spending his first eight NFL seasons with Carolina and Chicago. A featured target throughout most of his career, Moore was reduced to a 16% target share in 2025 -- his lowest since his rookie year in 2018. The result was a 35th-place finish in fantasy points, which ended a streak of six consecutive top 25s. Moore now heads to Buffalo with Khalil Shakir as his only roadblock to emerging as Josh Allen's No. 1 target in Buffalo's high-scoring offense. Still in his prime at age 29, Moore has the look of a fantasy WR3 with upside for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Josh Downs is hard to trust as anything more than a deep-league flex for the Colts' Week 2 trip to Kansas City. His four targets in the Week 1 loss to Baltimore tied for fourth on the team with Jonathan Taylor, as Daniel Jones threw more frequently to Alec Pierce, Keenan Allen and Tyler Warren. In 17 appearances since the start of last season, Downs is averaging a pedestrian 35.5 receiving yards per game in the Colts' run-heavy offense.
outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Downs is poised to work as the Colts' top wide receiver in Week 3 against the Texans, making him a solid WR3 or flex option in fantasy. Alec Pierce (heel) is expected to sit out, and the Colts lack viable alternatives, with over-the-hill veteran Keenan Allen and recent signing Darius Slayton representing the top options behind Downs in the wide receiver room. Downs caught seven of nine targets for 72 yards to lead the Colts in all three categories during the Week 2 loss to the Chiefs, which Pierce exited in the first half. Downs figures to see plenty of star Texans CB Derek Stingley, but the 25-year-old WR should get plenty of targets from Daniel Jones despite the tricky matchup.
outlooksByWeek.4: Josh Downs has exceeded 70 receiving yards in each of the Colts' last two games while racking up 20 targets over that span. With fellow Colts WR Alec Pierce (heel) on IR, Downs is a recommended Week 4 starting option since he is poised to see plenty of targets from Daniel Jones against a weak Washington secondary that has allowed the most catches (46) and touchdown receptions (six) to WRs, as well as the third-most receiving yards (573) to the position. Downs, TE Tyler Warren, and WR Keenan Allen accounted for 20 of Jones' 24 completed passes in Pierce's absence against the Texans in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Josh Downs disappointed with 16 receiving yards against Washington's vulnerable secondary in Week 4 after notching at least 72 yards in each of the Colts' previous two games. Downs remains the de facto No. 1 WR for the Colts, as Alec Pierce (knee) is still on IR heading into a Week 5 road game at Pittsburgh. The Steelers are allowing 149 receiving yards per game to wideouts and traded starting CB Joey Porter to Dallas prior to Week 4. Downs is well-positioned to shake off his Week 4 dud and deliver as a solid Week 5 flex play.
outlooksByWeek.6: Josh Downs is averaging 50 receiving yards per game and has exceeded 70 twice through five games. However, the 25-year-old wideout has yet to score in his fourth NFL season after compiling 11 TDs across his first three years. He's the de facto No. 1 WR for the Colts in the continued absence of Alec Pierce (heel) heading into a Week 6 home game against the Titans. Tennessee has allowed a couple of big individual performances to wideouts, surrendering at least 117 yards and a TD to both Zay Flowers and DeVonta Smith. However, those are established No. 1 wideouts, putting them a cut above Downs, whose career average is just 46 yards per game. With the Colts likely to rely primarily on their ground game in Week 6, Downs is a decent flex play but far from an elite fantasy option.
outlooksByWeek.7: Josh Downs has been outplayed by Keenan Allen since the Colts lost Alec Pierce to a heel injury. After exceeding 70 receiving yards twice through Week 3, Downs has compiled a meager 103 receiving yards over the the past three games combined, topping out at 47 yards in a game over that span. His role as a locked-in starter at WR for the Colts makes Downs a viable Week 7 flex play against the Vikings, though he has now gone nine consecutive games without a TD dating back to last season. Minnesota is allowing 133 yards per game to WRs but has limited the position to three TDs in five games, so Downs looks unlikely to end his scoring drought.
outlooksByWeek.8: Josh Downs has opened his fourth season in Indianapolis on a seven-game touchdown drought, and he has reached the 50-yard threshold just twice this season, with the last such performance coming in Week 3. It has been Keenan Allen rather than Downs stepping up during the continued absence of Alec Pierce (heel), who remains on injured reserve. Despite his disappointing production so far, Downs leads the Colts with 46 targets and is a decent flex option for Week 8 against a Jaguars defense that's allowing a league-high 210 receiving yards per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Josh Downs scored his first TD of the season, accounting for the Colts' lone score in their 42-7 Week 8 loss to Jacksonville, but he fell short of 50 receiving yards for the fifth consecutive game. Downs continues to start in Indianapolis' low-octane passing game and has drawn at least four targets in every game. Ahead of a Week 9 home game against a Cowboys defense that's giving up 164.1 receiving yards and one TD per game to wide receivers, Downs' consistent involvement, coupled with Dallas' defensive struggles, makes him a viable fantasy WR3 or flex option for Week 9.
outlooksByWeek.10: Josh Downs was traded to the Chiefs where he'll be catching passes from Patrick Mahomes, assuming the QB is healthy after hurting his elbow in Week 9. Downs will enjoy a QB upgrade, but he'll face more competition for targets from Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy and Travis Kelce. With Worthy also nursing an injury, Downs could log a big workload in Week 10 against a Falcons secondary that just traded away safety Jessie Bates and ranks 19th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Josh Downs made an immediate difference in his Kansas City debut, catching four of five targets for 53 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's win over the Falcons despite running just eight routes and playing only 10 snaps. Picked up from the Colts at the trade deadline, Downs' efficiency on a limited workload bodes well, but he'll still be the No. 2 wide receiver behind Rashee Rice, with Travis Kelce and the team's running backs also factoring significantly into the passing game. Downs will try to build on this performance in Week 11 against a Cardinals secondary that ranks 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Josh Downs has seen very consistent usage in his two games with Kansas City, catching four passes on five targets in each with yardage in the 50s. The main difference was a touchdown in Week 10, something he wasn't able to repeat in a Week 11 win over the Cardinals. Downs is adapting quickly to his new offense, but Patrick Mahomes has plenty of other options in Rashee Rice, Travis Kelce, Xavier Worthy, and running backs Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson. Downs will look to continue building chemistry with Mahomes in Week 12 against a Bills secondary that's tied for 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Downs has settled in as a serviceable slot receiver, which has helped him to finish in the 35-to-45 range among WRs in total fantasy points in each of his three NFL seasons. Downs peaked with a 72-803-5 receiving line in 2024, but took a step back in a crowded offense last season, and failed to deliver a single fantasy week better than 15th at the position. The undersized Downs isn't an option near the goal line, as he hasn't cleared five touchdowns or three end zone targets in a single season. The 25-year-old has a path to a slightly larger role in 2026 with Michael Pittman Jr. gone, leaving Alec Pierce, Tyler Warren and Keenan Allen as his primary target competition. Downs is a sleeper for flex production in PPR formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bucky Irving is expected to operate as the Buccaneers' lead back in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns. Irving out-touched Kenneth Gainwell 15 to six in the Week 1 loss, which is a very promising sign for his outlook moving forward. The most impressive part about Irving's Week 1 performance was receiving, where he caught all seven of his targets for 48 yards. He could be in for another big week against a Browns defense that allowed 34 points in Week 1. However, Cleveland did give up just 3.9 yards per carry, so Irving may need to continue his success as a receiver for fantasy production.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bucky Irving is expected to remain Tampa Bay's lead back in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Irving remained efficient despite the Buccaneers' offensive struggles in Week 2, accounting for 90 total yards on 21 touches. Additionally, he's operated as the clear No. 1 running back, out-touching Kenneth Gainwell 36 to 11 in two contests. Irving will likely struggle in Week 3, however, as he'll be facing a Vikings defense that's allowed just 14.7 PPR fantasy points to RBs this season, the fourth-best mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bucky Irving is expected to continue leading the Buccaneers' backfield in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Irving was held in check by a strong Vikings defense in Week 3, totaling 58 yards on 17 touches. Despite this inefficient effort, Irving remained the Buccaneers' bell-cow back, as Kenneth Gainwell received just five touches (10 total yards). With Baker Mayfield (thumb) dealing with injury following the Week 3 loss, Irving could see less opportunities through the air. Regardless, Irving's strong workload should bode well for the Week 4 matchup, as Green Bay's defense has allowed the second-most PPR fantasy points per game to the RB position (30.7) this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Bucky Irving is expected to remain the Buccaneers' main offensive weapon in the Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Irving was largely ineffective against the Packers in a Week 4 loss, rushing for 61 yards on 16 carries. Additionally, the Oregon product was held without a target after accumulating 15 in Tampa Bay's first three games, suggesting Irving is likely in for less pass-catching opportunities while Jalon Daniels remains the starting quarterback. Irving could still thrive in Week 5 against a Cowboys defense that's given up 22.4 fantasy points per game to opposing RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Bucky Irving is expected to remain the focal point of Tampa Bay's offense in the Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. Irving was phenomenal in the Week 5 upset win over the Cowboys, totaling 175 yards and two touchdowns on 23 touches. Despite this, Irving is seeing less receiving work since Jalon Daniels took over for the injured Baker Mayfield (thumb) at quarterback, getting just three targets over his last two games. Even so, Irving should remain productive in Week 6 against a Steelers defense that's allowed 22.9 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this year.
outlooksByWeek.7: Bucky Irving is expected to remain the focal point of the Buccaneers' offense in the Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. Irving was relatively quiet in the Week 6 overtime loss to the Steelers, totaling 49 yards on 22 touches. Despite this, he remains firmly ahead of Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker in Tampa Bay's backfield and could thrive in Week 7, as Carolina's defense has allowed 25.7 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season. Additionally, Irving could benefit from the possible return of quarterback Baker Mayfield (thumb), as Irving averaged 5.0 targets per game while Mayfield was healthy (just 2.0 since Mayfield's injury).
outlooksByWeek.8: Bucky Irving will look to stay hot in the Buccaneers' Week 8 matchup against the Falcons. Irving carried the load for Tampa Bay's offense in the Week 7 win over the Panthers, rushing for 106 and two touchdowns while catching one of two targets for four yards. Irving has been the focal point of the Buccaneers' offense over the last three weeks, averaging 111.3 total yards and 1.3 touchdowns per game during that span. He's in for a very favorable Week 8 matchup as well, with Atlanta's defense allowing 26.8 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Bucky Irving is expected to remain the focal point of the Buccaneers' offense in the Week 9 matchup against the Bears. He has rushed for over 100 yards in three of his last four games, averaging a whopping 121.8 rushing yards per game during that span. He now ranks fifth in the NFL in rushing yards per game (91.0) while scoring six total touchdowns in eight appearances this season. Offensive coordinator Zac Robinson is expected to continue leaning on the run game, which has led the Buccaneers to a 3-1 record over the last four weeks-a positive sign for Irving's outlook. However, he is in for a tough Week 9 matchup against a Chicago defense that has given up just 18.9 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs through seven contests this year
outlooksByWeek.11: Bucky Irving will likely remain the focal points of the Buccaneers' offense during the Week 11 matchup against the Lions. Irving has carried Tampa Bay's offense throughout the season, ranking sixth in the NFL in touches per game (21.0) and 10th in total yards per game (103.4). However, head coach Todd Bowles said that the Buccaneers "will try and lessen the load" on Irving following the team's Week 10 bye, suggesting he could see less work going forward. Additionally, Irving may struggle in Week 11 against a Lions defense that's held opposing running backs in check this season, allowing just 17.5 fantasy points per game.
outlooksByWeek.12: Bucky Irving is expected to remain one of fantasy's top running backs during the Buccaneers' Week 12 matchup against the Panthers. Irving was one of Tampa Bay's few bright spots during the Week 11 loss to the Lions, accounting for 100 scrimmage yards and one touchdown on 21 touches. He ranks sixth in the NFL in touches (21.0) and ninth in scrimmage yards (103.1) per game, which bodes well for his fantasy look going forward. Additionally, he's in for a very favorable Week 12 matchup against a Carolina defense that's allowed 28.6 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season, the most in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Irving enters his third season coming off a disappointing 2025 campaign in which he missed seven games and struggled with efficiency. After averaging 5.42 yards per carry and producing 1,514 yards and eight touchdowns as a rookie, Irving fell to 3.40 YPC (fourth worst among qualified RBs), 865 yards and four touchdowns in 2025. He failed to clear 4.2 YPC in any of his 10 outings and had zero carries inside the opponent's 5 yard line. The 24-year-old remains positioned as the lead back in Tampa Bay, but the combination of his small frame (5-foot-9, 192 pounds) and the arrival of Kenneth Gainwell (not to mention Sean Tucker at the goal line) suggest he might play a lesser role moving forward. Irving should be valued as a back-end RB2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers travel in Week 2 to face the Patriots, who have the ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (15.0) to RBs. He rushed 10 times for 46 yards and caught five of six targets for 27 yards in Pittsburgh's 20-13 win against Atlanta. Warren lost a fumble, but he still out-touched fellow RB Rico Dowdle 15-10 and had much better results from those opportunities. If the Steelers continue to favor the passing game against New England, or if they're forced into it via game flow, Warren would carry a bit more value in what looks to be a true timeshare.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers welcome the Bengals to town for a Week 3 AFC North matchup. He rushed 11 times for 43 yards and brought in two of four targets for 34 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to New England. Warren handled 11 of 20 carries from backs in this one, but the Steelers weren't able to get much going on offense. It looks like he's the 1A out of the backfield, and although it's not by a substantial amount, Rico Dowdle is considered questionable to suit up on Sunday with a toe injury. Warren faces a 14th-ranked Cincinnati defense in fantasy points allowed (19.0) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers travel to take on the Browns for an AFC North clash in Week 4. He rushed 17 times for 127 yards and caught three of four targets for 49 yards during Pittsburgh's thrilling 30-27 victory in Week 3. Warren handled a workhorse role with Rico Dowdle (toe) out, and it looks like that could again be the case with a short turnaround for Week 4's Thursday Night Football showcase in Cleveland. He'll face a tough matchup as the Browns rank sixth in fantasy points allowed (17.1) to RBs and are one of seven teams yet to surrender a TD to the position.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers welcome the Colts to town in Week 5. He tallied 17 carries for 93 yards while catching three of six targets for 33 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss. Warren handled a massive workload for the second straight week with Rico Dowdle (toe) on the sidelines. There's a chance Dowdle remains out against Indianapolis, leaving Warren as the unquestioned lead back versus the Colts' 23rd-ranked defense, which has allowed 24.2 fantasy points per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers travel to face the Buccaneers in Week 6. He rushed 15 times for 101 yards and a touchdown and caught all six of his targets for 87 yards, including an 80-yard TD reception, during Pittsburgh's Week 5 win. Warren continued to handle a workhorse role with Rico Dowdle (toe) out for the third straight contest. He compiled 490 scrimmage yards and two TDs on 61 touches over that stretch, and head coach Mike McCarthy stated Monday that Warren is viewed as "our featured player right now." Even if Dowdle can suit up versus Tampa Bay's sixth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (17.4) in Week 6, Warren is likely to keep working as the lead back for a Steelers offense averaging 29.3 points through their last three outings.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers face off against the Saints in Paris in Week 7. He had 14 carries for 50 yards and caught two of four targets for 28 yards during Pittsburgh's overtime victory in Week 6. With Rico Dowdle (toe) back on the field, Warren's opportunities dipped noticeably despite out-touching Dowdle 16-10. He should still handle a larger volume than Dowdle going forward, but managers should certainly temper expectations as long as both backs are healthy. Warren draws a very favorable matchup against a New Orleans defense that ranks dead last in fantasy points allowed per game (30.7) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers host the Browns for a Week 8 divisional clash. He had 18 carries for 101 yards and corralled three of four targets for 36 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 7 victory in Paris. Fellow running back Rico Dowdle amassed 86 scrimmage yards on 15 touches, and it appears he's rounding into form after missing nearly a month with a toe injury. Warren remains atop the backfield hierarchy, but he'll face a tough test against Cleveland's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (19.7) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: In Week 10, Jaylen Warren and the Steelers visit their divisional-rival Bengals on Sunday Night Football. He rushed 17 times for 143 yards and a touchdown while catching one of two targets for no gain during Pittsburgh's 27-6 victory in Week 9. Warren matched his career high for rushing yards and produced his third 100-plus-yard effort in his last four games. In Week 3, he generated 176 scrimmage yards on 20 touches in his first matchup against Cincinnati, so he'll be hungry to put up similar numbers on the road.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers travel to take on the Eagles in Week 11. He had seven carries for 15 yards and caught five of six targets for 26 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 10 loss. Warren and the entire Steelers offense found little success until the game was already out of reach, as several backups took the field in the fourth quarter. Warren will look to shake off the tough outing, but he'll have to do so against Philadelphia's seventh-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (19.7) to opposing RBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: In Week 12, Jaylen Warren and the Steelers aim to snap a two-game losing streak when they host the Broncos on Black Friday. He had nine carries for 28 yards and caught two of three targets for one yard during Pittsburgh's Week 11 loss. Warren got 11 touches compared to nine for backfield mate Rico Dowdle, but it was an overall quiet outing for both. The Steelers have shifted to more of a timeshare with Dowdle now fully healthy, leaving Warren as a TD-or-bust option versus Denver's 25th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (24.9) to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Warren reached career-high marks in touches (251), yardage (1,291) and touchdowns (eight) last season, his fourth in the league. The former undrafted free agent put up 13.6 fantasy points per game (19th among backs) and PFF tracked him with 56 forced missed tackles (seventh). Pittsburgh swapped out Kenneth Gainwell for Rico Dowdle as Warren's running mate, and the two are expected to split work in a Mike McCarthy offense that rarely deploys its backs in the passing game. Warren is capable and effective as a rusher and receiver, but his ceiling figures to be limited in this committee. He's likely to cap out as a flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Sam LaPorta should remain a big part of Detroit's offense in Week 2 at Buffalo. In Week 1 against the Saints, LaPorta's 5-48-0 receiving line put him second to Amon-Ra St. Brown in receiving yards while tying Jahmyr Gibbs for second in catches. The fourth-year tight end will face a Bills defense that allowed 14.4 PPR points to Texans tight ends this past Sunday, so he'll have plenty of opportunities to build on his season-opening performance.
outlooksByWeek.3: Sam LaPorta will look to remain a top target as the Lions take on the Jets in Week 3. LaPorta recorded six catches for 52 yards and his first touchdown of the season against the Bills in Week 2. The starting tight end has now been targeted 15 times across two games, and he's converted these into 11 grabs for 100 yards and a touchdown. He'll face a New York defense that held Green Bay's Tucker Kraft to just two catches for 15 yards this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.4: Sam LaPorta should remain a complementary option as the Lions play the Panthers in Week 4. LaPorta caught three of four targets for 44 yards against the Jets in Week 3, which was his quietest game of the year. Detroit's ability to score and defensive problems keep the passing game alive even when running back Jahmyr Gibbs is tearing it up on the ground, so there don't look to be any issues with LaPorta's usage moving forward. He'll face a Carolina defense that ceded a 7-51-2 stat line to Harold Fannin in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Sam LaPorta will look to build on a season-best showing as the Lions travel to Arizona in Week 5. LaPorta impressed even in a Week 4 loss to Carolina, reeling in eight of 13 targets for 84 yards and a touchdown. The fourth-year tight end has now registered a 22-228-2  receiving line this season, and he remains a consistent option for Jared Goff, especially in important situations. LaPorta will face a Cardinals defense that's ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Sam LaPorta will aim to stay hot as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. LaPorta recorded another statement performance in Week 5 over the Cardinals heading into Detroit's bye, bringing in all five of his targets for 88 yards and a touchdown. The featured tight end has now surpassed 50 yards in three of his last four games, and he's found the end zone in each of those outings as well. He'll face a Green Bay defense that's ranked fifth in fantasy points allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Sam LaPorta will aim to bounce back as the Lions play the Vikings in Week 8. LaPorta was silenced in a Week 7 win over the Packers, catching one of two targets for 18 yards. The starting tight end's performance will hopefully be an anomaly, and he still has a 28-334-3 receiving line through six outings this season. He'll face a Minnesota defense that's ranked a tough first in fantasy points allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Sam LaPorta will look to get back on track as the Lions travel to Miami in Week 9. LaPorta had another quiet performance in Detroit's Week 8 win over the Vikings, bringing in three of five targets for 33 yards and logging one rush for two yards. After an impressive stretch heading into a Week 6 bye, the starting tight end has now logged just four catches for 51 yards in the last two weeks. LaPorta will face a Miami defense that's ranked a favorable 30th in fantasy points allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Sam LaPorta will look to get back on track as the Lions play the Patriots in Week 10. LaPorta was quiet again in Week 9 versus the Dolphins, amid a struggling Detroit passing offense, recording four catches for 32 yards. The starting tight end has totaled just 83 receiving yards in his last three games after going back-to-back weeks with 80-plus receiving yards and a touchdown heading into the Lions' bye. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Sam LaPorta will aim to get back on track as the Lions return home against the Patriots in Week 11. LaPorta has had an extremely dry stretch ever since Detroit's bye week, failing to reach 40 yards in four straight games. The starting tight end has now recorded 36 receptions for 415 yards and three touchdowns, with most of his volume coming from the first five outings of the season. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked 23rd in fantasy points allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Sam LaPorta will look to build off a bounce-back showing as the Lions play the Bears in Week 12. LaPorta hauled in three of six targets for 62 yards in a Week 11 win over Tampa Bay, with most of his output coming from a 47-yard catch early in the game. Still, this receiving line included his best yardage total since before Detroit's bye in Week 5, so he'll hopefully be able to build on it in the weeks to come. He'll face a Chicago defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy tight ends in the last four weeks.

player.seasonOutlook: LaPorta has settled in as one of the league's top tight ends, but the 2023 second-round pick simply hasn't been able to match the fantasy success he enjoyed as a rookie. Since posting an 86-889-10 receiving line in 17 games that first season, LaPorta has totaled a 100-1,215-10 line in 25 games over the past two seasons. LaPorta's 2025 campaign was cut short by a back injury, otherwise he was well on his way to his third straight top-10 fantasy campaign (he finished seventh in PPG). The 25-year-old joins Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams and Jahmyr Gibbs as the clear "Core Four" targets in a good, pass-friendly Detroit offense, and is thus a solid fantasy TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Christian McCaffrey heads into a Week 2 matchup against Miami with perhaps a bit less pressure to carry the 49ers' offense. Whereas McCaffrey led the NFL with 413 touches last season, he logged a modest 15 in last Thursday's Week 1 win over the Rams. Rookie Kaelon Black actually got more carries (14) than McCaffrey (10), though McCaffrey was still productive with 68 rushing yards along with 20 receiving yards on five catches. McCaffrey could feast upon a Dolphins defense that allowed Ashton Jeanty to accumulate 147 total yards and two touchdowns in a season-opening loss to Las Vegas.
outlooksByWeek.3: Christian McCaffrey will look to once again show off his dual-threat skill set when the 49ers host the Cardinals in Week 3. McCaffrey is coming off a productive game against the Dolphins,  totaling 66 yards (23 rushing, 43 receiving) and getting into the end zone twice. The veteran RB has been ceding a fair amount of carries to rookie No. 2 RB Kaelon Black so far this season, but McCaffrey's work as a receiver (nine catches for 63 yards through two contests) has remained a key part of his game. Arizona has been middle-of-the-pack against running backs so far, yielding an average of 14.0 fantasy points per game to the position.
outlooksByWeek.4: Christian McCaffrey is coming off his best game of the campaign heading into San Francisco's Week 4 tilt versus the Broncos. McCaffrey compiled season-high marks with 75 rushing yards and 116 total yards in Sunday's win against Arizona while scoring his third TD of 2026. His 15 carries were also his most so far this season, as the 49ers appear to be pulling back on his workload a bit after he led the NFL with 413 touches last year. McCaffrey could find room to run on Denver, as the Broncos have so far given up the second-most rushing yards to RBs (129.7 per game) this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Christian McCaffrey will look to reach the end zone again for San Francisco in a Week 5 NFC West clash against the Seahawks. McCaffrey has scored at least one touchdown in three straight games and has four rushing TDs on the season. The scoring has helped keep his fantasy value high despite the fact that he's averaging a modest 16.5 touches per game so far after leading the NFL with 24.3 touches per game last season. Seattle has yielded just 3.35 yards per carry and one total rushing touchdown to running backs this season, but they've been more vulnerable through the air, allowing two receiving scores and an 88.5% catch rate to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Christian McCaffrey has had a nose for the end zone this season and will look to score again when the 49ers face the Commanders in Week 6. McCaffrey produced 83 total yards and a TD this past Sunday in a big win over Seattle, giving him at least one score four straight weeks. While his 16.0 touches per game this year are considerably lower than his 24.3 last season, he's been more efficient on the ground with 4.7 yards per carry (he averaged just 3.9 YPC during the regular season in 2025). With that said, Washington has been stingy against RBs through five weeks, yielding just 3.76 YPC and only two total touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.7: Christian McCaffrey and the 49ers are on the road for a meeting against the Falcons in Week 7. He rushed 16 times for 64 yards and two TDs while losing a fumble, adding nine catches on 10 targets for 53 yards during San Francisco's Week 6 victory. McCaffrey set season highs in carries, receptions, receiving yards and targets while notching his seventh rushing TD in six games. He'll once again lead the 49ers backfield for their matchup against an Atlanta defense allowing 23.3 fantasy points per game (21st) to RBs and just surrendered three rushing TDs to the Bears.
outlooksByWeek.9: Christian McCaffrey's hamstring issue will be worth keeping an eye on ahead of San Francisco's Week 9 matchup against the Raiders. McCaffrey suffered a mild hamstring strain Week 7 against Atlanta, but a well-timed Week 8 bye provided an opportunity for him to get abundant rest. Should McCaffrey be unable to suit up in Week 9, however, rookie Kealon Black is likely to take on lead RB duties for the 49ers. Whichever player leads the team's backfield has a juicy matchup against a Las Vegas defense that has yielded a league-worst 5.31 yards per carry to running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Christian McCaffrey will seek to add to his seven-game scoring streak when San Francisco faces Dallas in Week 10. With two touchdowns (one rushing, one receiving) this past Sunday against Las Vegas, McCaffrey has gotten into the end zone at least once in each of his past seven games. While he has been logging fewer touches per game this season, McCaffrey continues to be a workhorse for the 49ers and has averaged 4.5 yards per rush, his highest mark since 2023. He could be in for a big game against the Cowboys, who are giving up 22.0 fantasy points per game to running backs, fourth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Christian McCaffrey enters San Francisco's Week 11 matchup against Minnesota on the heels of one of the biggest performances of his career. In this past Sunday's win over Dallas, McCaffrey recorded a career-best 161 receiving yards en route to 223 total yards and three touchdowns. The star RB has logged at least one TD in each of his past eight games and has multiple scores in three of his past four contests, making him an elite week-to-week fantasy asset. With that said, McCaffrey is slated for a tough matchup against the Vikings, who rank eighth in the NFL by allowing 15.3 fantasy points per game to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Christian McCaffrey will look to extend his touchdown streak to 10 games when San Francisco faces Seattle in Week 12. Though McCaffrey finished with a modest 62 total yards in this past Sunday's win over Minnesota, he got into the end zone for the ninth straight game with a six-yard touchdown run. McCaffrey is tied for second in the NFL with 11 rushing TDs this season, and he's added three scores as a receiver. He figures to be challenged by a Seahawks defense that leads the NFL with just 3.16 yards per carry allowed to wideouts on the season.

player.seasonOutlook: McCaffrey is back for his fifth season with the 49ers after a bounce-back 2025 campaign in which he led all running backs in snaps, routes, touches, targets, receptions, receiving yards, receiving touchdowns and fantasy points. McCaffrey's rushing efficiency wasn't great (3.86 yards per carry), and he's entering his age-30 season after handling 450 touches (including the playoffs) in 2025. The history of overworked backs suggests we should expect a step back in 2026, but CMC is a unicorn, and the combination of his skill set and hefty usage in Kyle Shanahan's offense suggests he can overcome history. There's obvious risk here, but McCaffrey will be an elite option whenever he's on the field.

outlooksByWeek.2: Joe Burrow and the Bengals travel to take on the Texans in Week 2. Burrow completed 25 of 35 passes for 254 yards with one TD and one INT, and he rushed five times for 20 yards in their season-opening win. Houston ranks 28th in fantasy points allowed per game (39.0) to QBs after Josh Allen torched them for 357 scrimmage yards and four TDs. Burrow will look to get Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins more involved after the receivers combined for 71 yards on just five catches.
outlooksByWeek.3: Joe Burrow and the Bengals are on the road to face the Steelers in Week 3. After dealing with back spasms in practice, Burrow was a full go in Week 2, throwing for 207 yards (20-for-31) with two TDs and no INTs in the 20-6 victory. He faces a stout Pittsburgh defense that ranks first in fantasy points allowed (11.6) to QBs and seventh in passing yards allowed. Burrow is one of the best at his position, but fantasy managers should approach this matchup with caution after the Steelers held Drake Maye to 208 passing yards (14-for-22) with one pick while sacking him three times in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Joe Burrow and the Bengals host the Jaguars for a battle between 2-1 teams in Week 4. He threw for 282 yards (28-for-37) with three TDs and no INTs and added 13 yards on two carries during Cincinnati's 30-27 loss in Week 3. Burrow also lost a fumble in the final minute of the contest, but he had a strong outing overall against a tough defense. Up next is another difficult task, as Jacksonville's defense is tied for fifth, allowing 16.8 fantasy points per game to opposing QBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Joe Burrow and the Bengals travel to take on the 0-4 Dolphins in Week 5. He completed 39 of 54 pass attempts for 428 yards with one TD and two INTs while rushing three times for six yards and another score during Cincinnati's 22-17 loss in Week 4. The Bengals leaned on Burrow while playing from behind most of the game, but with Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) both questionable to suit up against Miami, they're hoping a better start will allow them to rely on the ground game a bit more. The Dolphins' defense is certainly beatable, allowing 21.2 fantasy points to QBs (T-18th) and 29.7 to RBs, which ranks dead last.
outlooksByWeek.7: Joe Burrow and the Bengals are in Baltimore for an AFC North clash in Week 7. During Cincinnati's Week 5 win over Miami, he threw for 190 yards (23-for-32) with four TDs and no INTs while rushing four times for 10 yards. Now coming off their bye week, Burrow will look to find holes in a tough Ravens defense that allows 17.5 fantasy points per game to QBs, which ranks seventh. The good news is that he'll have his vast array of complementary skill players available following a week of rest, headlined by Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.
outlooksByWeek.8: Joe Burrow and the Bengals return home to host the 1-6 Titans in Week 8. He completed 22 of 30 pass attempts for 292 yards with four touchdowns and zero interceptions and rushed twice for 12 yards during Cincinnati's 35-13 victory in Week 7. It was Burrow's second straight outing with four TDs and no INTs, as he threw all of his scores in the second half. Up next is a Tennessee defense allowing 19.2 fantasy points per game to QBs, which ranks 12th.
outlooksByWeek.9: Joe Burrow and the Bengals are in Spain for a Week 9 overseas tilt against the Falcons. In Week 8, he completed 38 of 48 pass attempts for 462 yards with five TDs and three INTs, and he had three carries for 10 yards and another score during Cincinnati's 43-36 overtime win. Burrow recorded season highs in passing yards, completion percentage, TDs, and INTs, and he has posted a 13:3 TD:INT ratio over his last three outings. Burrow faces a Falcons defense allowing 18.7 fantasy points per game (10th) to opposing QBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Joe Burrow and the Bengals welcome the divisional-rival Steelers to town for a Week 10 meeting on Sunday Night Football. He stayed red-hot in Week 9, completing 24 of 29 pass attempts for 271 yards and three TDs with no INTs, while rushing three times for seven yards and another score. Burrow owns a 16:3 TD:INT ratio and has two rushing TDs over his last four outings, and he continues to lead the NFL with 23 passing TDs through eight games. He'll look to avenge a Week 3 loss to Pittsburgh, when he went 28-for-37 for 282 yards and three scores but lost a fumble with 53 seconds remaining and Cincinnati down by three.
outlooksByWeek.11: Joe Burrow and the Bengals visit the Commanders on Monday Night Football in Week 11. His hot streak continued during Cincinnati's Week 10 victory, as he threw for 409 yards with four TDs and no INTs while rushing once for eight yards. Over his last five outings, all Bengals wins, Burrow has compiled 1,624 passing yards with a 20:3 TD:INT ratio, while adding 47 rushing yards and another two scores. The NFL's leading passer in terms of TDs (27) will aim to keep rolling versus the Commanders' 27th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (23.3) to opposing QBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: In Week 12, Joe Burrow and the Bengals host the Saints in an interconference clash. He completed 28 of 40 pass attempts for 300 yards with two TDs and zero INTs while rushing twice for minus-one yard during Cincinnati's Week 11 loss. Burrow delivered his fourth 300-yard outing of the season while extending his streak of games without an interception to three. He'll look to get his team back in the win column versus a New Orleans defense allowing 19.8 fantasy points per game (T-11th) to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Burrow will attempt to bounce back after injuries limited him to eight games in 2025. The 29-year-old has now missed at least six games in three of his six pro seasons, including two of his past three. Burrow was still a starting-caliber fantasy quarterback when active last season (top-12 scorer in five of his final six games), but his ceiling was limited by a near complete lack of rushing (41 yards on 14 carries). Burrow was a top-five scoring quarterback in each of his past two full seasons, and coach Zac Taylor cut back a bit on his extreme pass-heavy playcalling last season, so Burrow is best valued as more of a midrange QB1 than an elite option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Marvin Harrison will look to get going in Arizona's Week 2 tilt against Seattle. Harrison notched just one catch on three targets in a season-opening win over the Chargers, though that reception did go for a robust 33 yards. With that said, the fact that he drew such a small amount of QB Jacoby Brissett's 37 targets provides some cause for concern, especially with newcomer Kendrick Bourne getting a healthy eight targets and No. 2 wideout Michael Wilson drawing seven. The Cardinals' wideout corps as a whole faces a tough challenge in the Seahawks, who didn't allow any Patriots pass catcher to exceed 51 yards in a Week 1 victory.
outlooksByWeek.3: Marvin Harrison will look to bounce back from his Week 2 goose egg when the Cardinals face San Francisco in Week 3. Harrison was targeted by QB Jacoby Brissett just once Sunday in a loss to the Seahawks and finished without a catch. The third-year receiver concerningly has just one catch for 33 yards through two weeks, and perhaps even more distressingly for his fantasy managers, he's drawn only four targets to Michael Wilson's 14 so far. The 49ers rank in the top 10 through two weeks by giving up only 247 receiving yards to wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.4: Marvin Harrison heads into the Cardinals' Week 4 matchup against the Giants having yet to get going this season. Harrison did record a campaign-best three catches and 40 yards this past Sunday in a loss to San Francisco, but he was far outshined by fellow wideout Michael Wilson, who posted an 11-89-1 line on a massive 17 targets. Star tight end Trey McBride also continued to shine with a 9-75-0 receiving line, so Harrison appears to be QB Jacoby Brissett's third option in the passing game at the moment. The Giants could present an opportunity for Harrison to get into the end zone, as they've given up four receiving TDs to wideouts so far this year, tied for fifth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Marvin Harrison heads into Arizona's Week 5 matchup against Detroit struggling to build chemistry with QB Jacoby Brissett. Though Harrison recorded a 12-yard touchdown reception in Week 4 against the Giants, that was his only catch on four targets. The third-year wideout has exceeded one reception just once through four games this season and has totaled only 12 targets, remarkably far behind the 44 targets fellow wideout Michael Wilson has logged. With that said, the Lions could provide a prime opportunity for Harrison to get back on track, as Detroit has surrendered 207.3 receiving yards per game to wideouts, third-worst in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Marvin Harrison could make his Texans debut in Week 6 against the Jaguars. Harrison will likely be brought along slowly after being acquired in a trade from Arizona, so expectations should be tempered for Week 6, though the 2024 fourth overall pick is at least worth a flier in deeper leagues against a Jacksonville secondary that has allowed the most yards in the NFL to wide receivers. Harrison had just 85 receiving yards in four games for the Cardinals this season, but a reunion with former Ohio State QB C.J. Stroud could be what Harrison needs to get his career back on track. While catching passes from Stroud in 2022, Harrison posted his best college season, with 77 catches for 1,263 yards and 14 touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.7: Marvin Harrison was on the field for only 12 snaps in his Texans debut against the Jaguars in Week 6 but came away with three catches for 34 yards from former college teammate C.J. Stroud. Harrison's role figures to grow as he gets acclimated to his new surroundings and learns the playbook. The trade acquisition from Arizona had only 85 receiving yards through four games with the Cardinals this season, but Harrison was considered an elite wide receiver prospect when he was drafted fourth overall in 2024. He's certainly worth a speculative add if available, but Harrison will remain a risky flex option in Week 7 against the Giants since his usage is likely to be limited again.
outlooksByWeek.9: Marvin Harrison has drawn four targets in each of his first two games with the Texans. The 2024 fourth overall pick of the Cardinals could start to earn a larger role with his new team, especially after having a chance to further familiarize himself with the playbook during Houston's Week 8 bye. Harrison won't be a recommended fantasy option until he earns a larger role, as he played just 19% of offensive snaps in his Texans debut and 21% in his second game with the team. He'll be a risky Week 9 option against the Chargers' mediocre secondary, but Harrison's future looks brighter in Houston than it did in Arizona.
outlooksByWeek.10: Marvin Harrison accounted for just 20 of C.J. Stroud's 384 passing yards and none of Stroud's five touchdown passes in Houston's Week 9 win over the Chargers. The trade acquisition from Arizona has just six catches for 60 yards and one TD in three appearances for Houston heading into a Week 10 trip to Cleveland. With Nico Collins, Tank Dell, Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte also vying for targets in Houston's deep WR room, Harrison isn't a trustworthy Week 10 fantasy option. The 2024 fourth overall pick is droppable in most redraft formats, as the change of scenery hasn't improved Harrison's short-term fantasy outlook.
outlooksByWeek.11: Marvin Harrison sat out Houston's Week 10 loss to the Browns due to a hamstring injury and is out again for Week 11 against the Colts. He won't be a trustworthy fantasy option for the foreseeable future while battling for targets in a deep Texans WR room that also includes Nico Collins, Tank Dell, Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte. Harrison has 11 catches for 145 yards and two touchdowns in seven games split between the Cardinals and Texans this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Marvin Harrison hasn't suited up since Week 9 due to a hamstring injury. Even if he returns in Week 12 against the Ravens, Harrison will be tough to trust considering he has just six catches for 60 yards and one touchdown in three appearances for Houston. Fellow Houston wideouts Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson, Tank Dell and Kayshon Boutte (hip) are all more likely to capitalize on facing the reeling Ravens defense, which has allowed at least 33 points in four of the last five games.

player.seasonOutlook: Harrison's pro career is off to a slow start after he was selected with the No. 4 overall pick back in 2024. The Ohio State product was serviceable as a rookie (885 yards and eight TDs), but he missed five full games and was limited in others en route to a 41-608-4 receiving line in 2025. Harrison has finished 41st and 39th, respectively, in fantasy PPG despite a massive role near the goal line (he's third in the NFL in end zone targets since he was drafted and finished both seasons in the top five). Harrison is only entering his prime at age 24 and perhaps he'll make a Year 3 leap with new coach Mike LaFleur calling the plays and with Kyler Murray no longer under center. Harrison performed better with Jacoby Brissett under center last season and has the raw talent to make him well worth post-hype consideration in the middle rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylen Waddle did not contribute much in his Broncos' debut, catching just one of three targets for a meager two yards in the Week 1 loss to Kansas City. Steve Spagnuolo's rebuilt secondary prioritized taking Waddle out of the picture, and the former Dolphin wideout hasn't yet established enough chemistry with QB Bo Nix to overcome consistent double teams. Waddle will look to bounce back in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that was tied for 17th last season in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaylen Waddle broke out in the Broncos' Week 2 win over the Jaguars, erupting for an 8-138-0 line on 10 targets as he began to get on the same page as quarterback Bo Nix. Waddle logged plenty of downfield targets but also had a red zone look, usage that promises plenty more big performances. The former Dolphin hasn't had a 1,000-yard season since 2023, but the early returns in Denver suggest he'll have little trouble returning to that level in 2026. He'll face a Rams secondary in Week 3 that's allowed just 19 receptions to WRs through two weeks, tied for seventh in the NFL, but three of those have gone for touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylen Waddle is struggling to adjust to his new offense with the Broncos. The former Dolphins wide receiver caught only two of his seven targets in a Week 3 win over the Rams for 10 yards, while adding a 14-yard run.
