Waddle leads Denver with 20 targets through three games, but he's turned them into just 11 catches for 150 yards, and he's still looking for his first TD of the season. He'll face a 49ers secondary in Week 4 that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jaylen Waddle scored his first touchdown with the Broncos in a Week 4 loss to the 49ers, but it was overall another disappointing performance from the former Dolphin. Waddle has recorded double-digit targets only once in four games to begin the season, leading to a modest 16-185-1 line on 26 looks from Bo Nix. That's still better numbers than Courtland Sutton, and the issue seems to be the overall struggles of the offense under first-time play caller Davis Webb. How long Sean Payton lets that situation last before reclaiming those duties is an open question for Denver. Waddle will try to hit paydirt again in Week 5 against a Chargers secondary that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jaylen Waddle continues to struggle in his first season with the Broncos. He's been held to 35 receiving yards or fewer in four of five games, including a 2-19-0 line on five targets in a Week 5 win over the Chargers. Having Sean Payton reclaim play-calling duties should help the offense in the long run, but Waddle will be tough to trust until he begins to display consistent chemistry with Bo Nix. Waddle will face a Seahawks secondary in Week 6 that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jaylen Waddle remains stuck in neutral as part of a sluggish Broncos passing game. The former Dolphin has gone four straight games without reaching 40 receiving yards, managing just a 13-88-1 line on 25 targets over that stretch while quarterback Bo Nix tries to find a rhythm. Waddle showed his upside back in Week 2 with an 8-138-0 line, but until the Denver offense begins clicking, his production will remain erratic. He could break out in Week 7 against a Cardinals secondary that's given up 10 touchdowns to wide receivers this season, 31st in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jaylen Waddle left the Broncos' Week 7 win over the Cardinals in the fourth quarter with a chest injury after producing a modest 4-48-0 line on seven targets. The former Miami wideout hasn't been able to get comfortable in his new environment; he has been held under 50 receiving yards in six of his first seven games for Denver. The severity of Waddle's injury isn't clear, but the team had little incentive to get him back on the field with a big lead. Assuming he is cleared to play in Week 8, he'll have a tough time producing a ceiling game against a Kansas City secondary that ranks third in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jaylen Waddle caught his second touchdown of the season in the Broncos' Week 8 win over Kansas City, but his overall numbers remain disappointing, The former Dolphin has just a 29-315-2 line on 51 targets through eight games, and the struggles of quarterback Bo Nix have prevented Waddle from finding a rhythm in his new offense. Waddle has been targeted 10 or more times only once in those eight games, while last season's No. 1 wide receiver for Denver, Courtland Sutton, handled double-digit targets six times in 2025. Waddle will look for more volume in Week 9 against a Panthers team that just fired its defensive coordinator, and which is tied for 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jaylen Waddle sustained a concussion in the Broncos' final game before their bye, winding up with just a 22-yard reception on his only target. The former Dolphin has struggled to adjust to his new offense, and through nine games this season he's produced a 30-337-2 line on 52 targets, putting him on pace for a career low in receiving yards. Assuming he clears the concussion protocol in time to suit up in Week 11, he'll be facing a Raiders secondary that ranks 24th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Jaylen Waddle continues to struggle to make a big difference in the Broncos' passing game. In a Week 11 win over the Raiders, the former Dolphin caught three of six targets for 61 yards, his highest yardage total since Week 2. Waddle is on pace to record fewer than 700 receiving yards in a season for the first time, and with the Denver offense leaning more heavily on rookie running back Jonah Coleman, Bo Nix hasn't had to air it out much. Waddle seems unlikely to break out in Week 12 against a Steelers secondary that ranks 12th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Waddle was traded to Denver after spending his first five seasons in Miami. The 2021 first-round pick was solid during his Dolphins tenure, finishing in the top 30 among receivers in fantasy PPG four times, though never reaching the top 10 while often playing second fiddle to Tyreek Hill. Although he has been a reliable target and has missed only seven games in five years, Waddle hasn't finished a season higher than 20th in targets or catches since 2021. In Denver, the 27-year-old Waddle will compete with Courtland Sutton for the team lead in targets in a scheme that likes to spread the ball around. Not utilized near the goal line much at 5-foot-10 and 180 pounds (he's yet to clear seven end zone targets in a season), Waddle is likely to max out as a back-end WR2 in Denver.

outlooksByWeek.5: Tank Dell (knee) is expected to have his practice window opened ahead of the Texans' Week 5 road game against the Titans. The 2023 third-round pick hasn't played since sustaining a significant knee injury in Week 16 of the 2024 season. Dell is currently on injured reserve and will likely take some time to ramp up. He's unlikely to return in Week 5 against Tennessee, but forward-looking fantasy managers should take notice of Dell's impending return, as he averaged 55 receiving yards and scored 10 TDs in 25 games prior to his injury.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tank Dell (knee) had his 21-day return window opened ahead of Houston's Week 5 win over the Titans and has rejoined his teammates at practice but remains on injured reserve ahead of the team's Week 6 trip to London to face the Jaguars. Considering the Texans just traded for WR Marvin Harrison, Dell seems unlikely to be a major contributor in Week 6, even if he is activated from IR. Dell isn't viable in Week 6 but could be worth stashing if you have an open bench or IR slot, as Houston's 2023 third-round pick averaged 55 receiving yards and scored 10 TDs in 25 games prior to sustaining a major knee injury late in the 2024 season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tank Dell (knee) had his 21-day window to return from IR opened ahead of Houston's Week 5 win over the Titans, and he has a realistic chance of being activated ahead of the Week 7 home game against the Giants after sitting out against the Titans in Week 5 and the Jaguars in Week 6. Even if Dell suits up in Week 7, he's likely to be brought along slowly in a Texans WR room that also has Nico Collins, Marvin Harrison, Jaylin Noel, Xavier Hutchinson, and Kayshon Boutte vying for playing time. Dell is a viable bench stash, but he isn't a recommended starting option against the Giants.
outlooksByWeek.9: Tank Dell made his season debut in Week 7, ahead of Houston's Week 8 bye. The 2023 third-round pick showcased his trademark big-play ability with a 43-yard catch on his only target. This was Dell's first game action since Week 16 of the 2024 campaign due to a knee injury. The Texans also have Nico Collins, Marvin Harrison, Xavier Hutchinson, and Kayshon Boutte vying for snaps at wide receiver, which makes Dell a risky Week 9 fantasy option against the Chargers. The Chargers rank in the middle of the pack at defending WRs. Dell is worth stashing on the bench, as he delivered starter-level fantasy production prior to his extended absence, but he'll need to increase his involvement to regain fantasy relevance.
outlooksByWeek.10: Tank Dell looked like his old self in his second game back from a nearly two-year absence due to a knee injury. He caught four of nine targets for 105 yards and a TD in Houston's Week 9 win over the Chargers after securing a 43-yard catch against the Giants in Dell's Week 8 return to action. If Dell is still floating around on waivers in your league, he's worth adding in most formats, as he was a viable fantasy WR2 prior to his injury and just turned 27 years old. Dell is a viable option in Week 10 against Cleveland's decent secondary, but he should at least be rostered even if you have safer flex options for Week 10.
outlooksByWeek.11: Tank Dell had just 21 yards on four targets in the Week 10 loss to Cleveland after turning nine targets into 105 yards and a TD in Houston's Week 9 win over the Chargers. The speedy wideout continues to offer big-play potential in Week 11 against the Colts, who give up 15.4 yards per catch to wide receivers. Dell's floor is low in Houston's deep WR room, but his ceiling is certainly high enough to warrant flex consideration, especially with surging QB C.J. Stroud having thrown 13 touchdown passes in the Texans' last four games.
outlooksByWeek.12: Tank Dell has just six catches for 48 yards in two games since his 105-yard outburst in Week 9, which included a 63-yard touchdown catch. A Week 12 home game against the Ravens offers Dell a chance to showcase his ability to generate big plays, as Baltimore's struggling defense has allowed at least 33 points to four of its last five opponents. Dell has a high enough ceiling to warrant flex consideration in most formats, though his floor remains shaky as he competes for targets in a deep Texans WR room that also includes Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte (hip), and Marvin Harrison (hamstring).

player.seasonOutlook: Dell is on the comeback trail after suffering a devastating knee injury late in 2024 that cost him the entire 2025 season. It was a tough break for the 2023 third-round pick, who finished 18th among receivers in fantasy PPG as a rookie. While he wasn't quite as productive the next season, he was on pace for career highs in catches and yardage. The undersized Dell is certainly a question mark off the major injury, but, with Jayden Higgins out for the 2026 season, he has a path back to a role behind Nico Collins at some point this year. The 26-year-old will begin on injured reserve, but he'll be a fine end-of-bench stash once activated.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dak Prescott was held to just 175 passing yards in the season opener for the Cowboys.  Dak did toss two touchdowns, but he also threw a costly interception before the end of the first half, which led to a Giants touchdown. Despite a porous secondary, the Giants kept the star wideouts for the Cowboys in check, leaving Dak with an uninspiring output. Prescott will look to rebound in Week 2 versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dak Prescott tossed four touchdowns last game in a virtuoso performance for the Cowboys. Prescott completed 26-of-31 throws for 279 yards and the four scores in the dominant 37-20 win over the Commanders. Prescott has six touchdowns and just one pick through the first two games of the young season. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dak Prescott threw for 276 yards and a touchdown in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens last game. Dak has passed for at least 275 yards through the air in each of the last two contests for the Cowboys, while also failing to toss a single interception over that span. In Week 4, the Cowboys will face a Texans defense that has been surprisingly suspect against the pass in 2026.  Houston is allowing 238.7 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Dak Prescott crossed the 300-yard passing mark last game for the Cowboys for the first time in 2026. Prescott actually threw for 335 yards in the thrilling comeback win over the Texans. More than half of the yards came via CeeDee Lamb, as the duo combined for a staggering 17 of Dak's 32 completions. Dak has eight passing scores and just one interception through four games. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Dak Prescott went over the 300-yard passing mark for the second-straight game for Dallas. Unfortunately, Dak threw just one touchdown pass for the second-consecutive contest, while also tossing two picks in the dismal 24-16 loss to the Bucs. Nevertheless, Dak is currently fourth in the NFL in passing yards, and tied for eighth in the league in passing touchdowns. However, in Week 6, Dallas will face a Green Bay defense allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered just six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Dak Prescott has thrown four interceptions in his last two games for the Cowboys. While Dak has also thrown for over 250 yards in five-straight outings, he has passed for one touchdown apiece in four consecutive contests. Dallas has lost three of those four games. He will look to right the ship in Week 7 versus division foe Philadelphia. The Eagles are allowing 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL. However, Philadelphia has given up just eight passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 14th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Dak Prescott tossed multiple touchdowns last game for Dallas for the first time since the middle of September. Prescott threw for 212 yards and three touchdowns in the 38-21 win over the Eagles. Prescott now has 13 touchdowns in seven starts in 2026. In Week 8, the Cowboys will face an Arizona Cardinals defense that has been prone to surrendering the touchdown pass. In fact, Arizona has given up 17 passing scores, which is dead last in the NFL. The Cardinals have also given up the most points per game in the NFL overall to date.
outlooksByWeek.9: Dak Prescott scored two total touchdowns last game for Dallas. However, Prescott passed for one touchdown or fewer for the fifth time in six contests. Dak was also held under 200 yards passing for just the second time in 2026. In Week 9, Dallas will face a Colts defense allowing just 211.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 12th in the NFL. However, Indianapolis has given up 14 passing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Dak Prescott posted his third 300-yard passing outing of the season for Dallas in Week 9, throwing for 335 yards and two touchdowns in a win over the Colts. He's thrown for multiple touchdowns in two of the last three contests. However, in Week 10, Prescott will face a difficult task versus the San Francisco 49ers. The 49ers are allowing just 211 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Francisco has given up just 11 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for seventh in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Dak Prescott tied a career high with five touchdown passes last game for Dallas. Unfortunately, the Cowboys defense could not stop a nosebleed, as they fell by a staggering score of 46-40 to the 49ers. Dak also threw for a season-high 343 yards, notching his second-straight 300-yard output overall. Dak has tossed multiple touchdowns in three of the last four contests. In Week 11, Dak will look to keep rolling against a suspect Tennessee pass defense. The Titans are allowing 266.9 passing yards per tilt, which is dead last in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: Dak Prescott scored five touchdowns for the second-straight game for the Cowboys. Prescott threw for 325 yards and four touchdowns, while rushing for another score in the 51-30 thrashing of the Titans. Prescott has thrown for over 300 yards in three-straight contests, and now has 25 passing touchdowns on the season. That places him second in the NFL behind Joe Burrow. In Week 12, the Cowboys will face a mediocre Eagles pass defense. Philadelphia is allowing 222.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 17th in the NFL. However, the Eagles have only given up 14 passing touchdowns, which is tied for ninth in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Prescott is entering his 11th NFL season following a successful 2025 campaign in which he led the NFL in completions and ranked no lower than fourth in dropbacks, pass attempts, passing yards and passing TDs. Prescott appeared in all 17 games and has now finished no worse than 11th in fantasy points during all seven seasons in which he has played at least 16 games. Last season, his nine top-10 fantasy weeks were tied for third most at the position. Prescott is no longer much of a threat with his legs, but he should continue to put up big passing numbers with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens at his disposal. The 33-year-old is a fringe QB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Loop and the Ravens look to keep rolling at home versus the Saints in Week 2. Baltimore put up 41 points in their Week 1 victory, and Loop was a perfect 7-for-7 on his attempts. He made all five PATs and drilled both field-goal attempts-one from 57 yards out and one from 45. As long as he's the starting kicker, Loop should see plenty of scoring chances in this high-scoring Ravens offense. He'll try to stay perfect against a New Orleans defense that gave up 31 points to the Lions in the season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Loop and the Ravens visit the Cowboys for a Week 3 showdown. He finished 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts and connected on both PATs during Baltimore's 24-17 loss in Week 2. Loop's first attempt from 49 yards was blocked, but he followed up by making his second attempt from the same distance. He should have plenty of opportunities to score in what's expected to be a high-scoring contest versus Dallas inside the AT&T Stadium dome in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Loop and the Ravens return home to square off against the 0-3 Titans in Week 4. He was perfect again in Baltimore's dramatic 34-31 victory in Brazil in Week 3, making both of his field-goal attempts, including a 56-yard game-winning kick as time expired, and all four of his extra points. Loop is now 5-for-6 on field-goal attempts and 11-for-11 on extra-point tries in 2026. The Ravens are fifth in scoring at 30.7 points per game, so he should continue earning plenty of opportunities for one of the best offenses in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Loop and the Ravens pay a visit to the surging Falcons for a Week 5 interconference clash on Sunday Night Football. The second-year kicker went 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts and connected on all three PATs during Baltimore's 24-18 win in Week 4. Loop missed his second field goal of the season but set a new career high with his make from 64 yards out, and he's now 6-for-8 on field goals and a perfect 14-for-14 on extra points. Atlanta has scored the most points in the league over its last two games (80), meaning Loop and the Ravens will have to keep up in a potential high-scoring game.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Loop and the Ravens travel to square off against the division-rival Browns in Week 6. He made all three of his field-goal attempts and his lone PAT during Baltimore's 30-23 overtime victory in Week 5. Two of Loop's makes came from 50-plus yards, and he's now 5-for-5 on kicks from that distance this season and 9-for-11 on field goals overall. He's turning into a very reliable fantasy asset for a Ravens team that scores 29.2 points per game, making him a strong play against Cleveland.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyler Loop and the Ravens host the division-rival Bengals for a Week 7 showdown. He finished 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts and converted his lone PAT during Baltimore's 13-10 loss in Week 6. Through six contests this season, Loop is 10-for-13 (76.9%) on field goals and a perfect 16-for-16 on extra-point tries. He has three outings with 100% accuracy and three with 50% accuracy, making him an inconsistent fantasy option despite kicking for a Ravens offense that scores 26.0 points per game, which ranks seventh so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tyler Loop and the Ravens visit the 5-1 Bills in Week 8. He connected on both of his field-goal attempts and his lone PAT during Baltimore's 35-13 loss in Week 7. Following a 30-point outing in an overtime victory in Week 5, the Ravens' offense has struggled mightily over the last two games, combining for just 23 points over that stretch. However, with Lamar Jackson (ankle) progressing toward a return from a three-game absence, Loop could have more opportunities to score versus a Bills defense allowing 28.5 points per contest, the third-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: Tyler Loop and the Ravens are back home for a Week 9 clash against the 5-2 Jaguars. He went 1-for-2 on field goal attempts and converted his lone PAT during Baltimore's 36-10 loss in Week 8. Loop has attempted more than two FGs just once this season, and there's a good chance his limited involvement will continue with Lamar Jackson (thumb/IR) probably done for the year. The Ravens have scored a combined 33 points over their last three outings, and their struggles are likely to persist versus a Jacksonville defense allowing just 15.9 points per game, the second-best mark in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mason Taylor will push for more involvement when the Jets host the Packers in Week 2. Taylor logged a decent 68% snap share to open the year despite Kenyon Sadiq being available but turned three targets into two catches for minus-two yards. Week 2 figures to be a more pass-heavy game script, and the Packers allowed six catches and a touchdown to the position in Week 1, but Taylor likely needs to prove he's part of the game plan before managers take notice and consider him a viable option.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mason Taylor's availability for the Jets' Week 3 matchup with the Lions is uncertain due to a thumb injury that forced him to exit Week 2 early. Taylor didn't record a catch prior to exiting and has only three targets on the season, leaving him with a very questionable role. The matchup could make him a sneaky option if desperate, as Detroit has allowed two touchdown catches to the position in each of their first two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mason Taylor will need to overcome a thumb injury if he's to help the Jets in Week 4 against the Bears. In Taylor's absence, Kenyon Sadiq had a breakout performance in Week 3, snagging seven passes for 105 yards and a touchdown. It seems likely he'll at least share snaps if Taylor is deemed healthy for Sunday. Chicago hasn't allowed 30 yards to an opposing tight end, and when splitting the workload, Taylor doesn't profile favorably.
outlooksByWeek.6: Mason Taylor could serve as the Jets top tight end in Week 6 against the Patriots with Kenyon Sadiq dealing with a concussion. Returning from a two-week absence, Taylor caught all three of his targets in Week 5, finishing with 24 yards. New England had not allowed a tight end to top 32 yards or score against them prior to Week 5 when they faced Brock Bowers, so even if Taylor assumes the top spot on the depth chart, he seems unlikely to garner enough volume to be a viable option.
outlooksByWeek.7: Mason Taylor brings low volume into an inviting Week 7 matchup as the Jets face the Dolphins. Taylor is coming off a season-high six targets in Week 6, but had previously been limited to three or fewer looks, and hasn't topped 33 yards or scored all season. Miami is allowing the fourth-most fantasy points to opposing tight ends, including a whopping 9.3 yards per target, the second-highest mark across the league. Taylor seems unlikely to provide a useful week with Kenyon Sadiq siphoning a portion of the tight end workload.
outlooksByWeek.8: Mason Taylor has an increasing role in the Jets' passing attack ahead of an inviting Week 8 matchup with the Raiders. Despite the presence of Kenyon Sadiq, Taylor's catch totals have increased in each of the last three games, spiking with a season-high five catches, 62 yards, and two touchdowns in Week 7. Las Vegas has been vulnerable to tight ends, allowing eight touchdowns in seven games; however, no one has topped 58 yards, setting Taylor up to be a bit touchdown-dependent.
outlooksByWeek.9: Mason Taylor brings potential in a favorable matchup for the Jets against the Chiefs in Week 9. Taylor earned five targets in Week 8, his third straight game with at least that many looks, but he converted them into just 19 yards on three catches. That matchup came against the Raiders, who allow the fourth-most fantasy points to tight ends. The Chiefs allow the fifth most, with five of the seven touchdown receptions they've surrendered coming from the position. Though Taylor failed to capitalize in a plus spot, the opportunity is there again.
outlooksByWeek.10: Mason Taylor is trending in the wrong direction ahead of the Jets' Week 10 matchup with the Bills. After a Week 7 flash, scoring twice on five receptions, Taylor has only four catches and 30 yards over the subsequent two weeks. While the Jets will likely throw at least 30 times in Week 10 for the sixth straight game, Buffalo has allowed only one tight end to score, which could limit Taylor's ceiling.
outlooksByWeek.11: Mason Taylor brings low volume in an otherwise promising matchup in Week 11 when the Jets face the Chargers. Taylor hasn't collected more than six targets all season while topping 33 yards just once, but with Omar Cooper (ankle) potentially sidelined, more targets could be available in Week 11. The Chargers have allowed only one touchdown to tight ends but have surrendered over 100 yards to the position twice in the last four weeks, giving Mason potential for a yardage uptick.
outlooksByWeek.12: Mason Taylor's involvement in the Jets' low-volume passing game remains limited ahead of a Week 12 clash with the Dolphins. He has been held to 25 yards or fewer in seven of nine games this season, drawing just 31 targets on the year. He provided a spike week of five catches, 62 yards, and two touchdowns against Miami in Week 7, but his usage and form don't portend a repeat against a defense that's allowing 8.0 yards per target to tight ends but only four additional touchdowns outside of Taylor's prior effort.

player.seasonOutlook: Taylor was a busy man during his rookie season, playing 81% of the Jets' offensive snaps and handling a healthy 19% of the targets in 13 games. The 2025 second-round pick struggled badly with efficiency while dealing with the team's quarterback woes, ranking near the basement in catch rate (65%) and yards per target (5.4). Taylor also dropped five passes (fourth most), scored only one touchdown and finished 30th in fantasy PPG. Taylor would've been a potential 2026 breakout candidate, but that was quickly derailed when the Jets selected Kenyon Sadiq in the first round of April's draft. Taylor will play a role in the New York offense, but he won't see nearly enough targets to allow any sort of fantasy relevance.

outlooksByWeek.5: Tez Johnson is expected to remain a depth piece in Tampa Bay's wide-receiver room in the Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Johnson has had an underwhelming start to his 2026 campaign, catching four of nine targets for 74 yards through four games. Additionally, the Buccaneers will likely continue relying on the running game more, as it favors rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels while Baker Mayfield (thumb) remains out. Despite this, Johnson should be in for a favorable matchup against a Cowboys defense that's allowed 8.3 yards per pass attempt this year.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tez Johnson is expected to play a depth role in the Buccaneers' receiving corps in the Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. Although Johnson was targeted just once in the Week 5 win over the Cowboys, he made the most of his opportunity, totaling 64 receiving yards. He's appears firmly behind Emeka Egbuka, Chris Godwin and Cade Otton in Tampa Bay's passing attack, and likely won't be fantasy relevant without a touchdown going forward. Johnson is in for a tougher Week 6 matchup against a Pittsburgh secondary that's allowed 7.9 yards per target to opposing WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tez Johnson is expected to remain a depth option in the Buccaneers' receiving corps in the Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. Johnson played just 34% of Tampa Bay's offensive snaps in the Week 6 overtime loss to the Steelers, catching two of three targets for seven yards. He could find more fantasy value if Baker Mayfield (thumb) were to return for the Week 7 contest, but Johnson will likely remain irrelevant for fantasy purposes without scoring a touchdown. Additionally, Johnson is in for a difficult matchup against a Panthers defense that's given up just two touchdowns to wideouts all season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tez Johnson is expected to play a depth role in the Buccaneers' receiving corps in the Week 8 matchup against the Falcons. Johnson has operated as Tampa Bay's top deep threat over the last three weeks, catching five of six targets for 104 yards and a touchdown. Due to his lack of opportunities, he's unlikely to be fantasy relevant without scoring a touchdown. However, he could find the end zone against a Falcons defense that's allowed four receiving touchdowns to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Tez Johnson is expected to remain one of Tampa Bay's top pass-catchers in the Week 9 matchup against the Bears. His offensive role expanded with Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) sidelined over the last two weeks. However, Johnson has logged just two receptions for 33 yards and a touchdown during that span, largely because Tampa Bay attempted just 14 total passes. While the Buccaneers' offense remains extremely run-heavy, Johnson will likely be irrelevant for fantasy purposes without finding the end zone. He could struggle against a Bears secondary that's allowed just seven total touchdowns to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Tez Johnson is expected to play as Tampa Bay's No. 3 wideout during the Week 11 matchup against the Lions. Johnson led the Buccaneers' in receiving yards (76) during the Week 9 loss to the Bears, though he had two costly drops as well. Over Tampa Bay's last four games, Johnson has emerged as the team's third option at wide receiver, catching six of 10 targets for 116 yards and a touchdown. He could be successful in Week 11 against a Lions secondary that's allowed 6.4 yards per pass attempt this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Tez Johnson is expected to play a depth role in the Buccaneers' receiving corps during the Week 12 matchup against the Panthers. After leading the team in receiving yards during the Week 9 loss to the Bears, Johnson played just 19 offensive snaps in Week 11. He appears to be losing playing time to rookie Ted Hurst, who caught five of seven targets for 56 yards and two touchdowns during last week's loss. Thus, Johnson will likely remain in a reserve role in Week 12 against a Panthers defense that's given up just 7.6 yards per target to opposing wideouts this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Evan McPherson will look to stay perfect when the Bengals visit the Texans in Week 2. He nailed all four of his field-goal attempts, including kicks of 55 and 58 yards, and made all three PATs during Cincinnati's 33-27 win in the season opener. McPherson should remain a top fantasy kicker as a member of one of the NFL's elite offenses. Houston gave up 36 points and 409 total yards in their Week 1 loss to the Bills.
outlooksByWeek.3: Evan McPherson and the Bengals visit the Steelers for an AFC North divisional matchup in Week 3. He remained perfect on the season after connecting on both of his field-goal attempts and both PATs during Cincinnati's Week 2 win over Houston. McPherson drilled both of his field goals from 50-plus yards out, and he's now 6-for-6 on the season, with four of his makes coming beyond 50 yards. He'll continue to earn plenty of scoring opportunities on an elite offense, even despite Pittsburgh's strong defense.
outlooksByWeek.4: Evan McPherson and the Bengals host the 2-1 Jaguars in Week 4. He stayed perfect on the year after drilling both field-goal attempts and all three PATs during Cincinnati's 30-27 loss in Week 3. McPherson is now 8-for-8 on FGAs and extra-point tries, including five kicks from at least 50 yards out. He'll aim to stay hot against one of the league's best defenses, as Jacksonville allows just 12.0 points per game, which ranks first. Still, McPherson should continue seeing plenty of scoring opportunities for a Bengals squad averaging 26.7 PPG (12th).
outlooksByWeek.5: Evan McPherson and the Bengals visit the Dolphins for a Week 5 road tilt. He made his only field-goal attempt from 29 yards out and connected on both of his PATs during Cincinnati's 22-17 loss in Week 4. McPherson remained perfect on his kicks through four outings, but he'll hope to get more involved against a Miami defense that ranks 21st in the league, allowing 25.3 points per game.
outlooksByWeek.7: Evan McPherson and the Bengals travel to face the Ravens for an AFC North clash in Week 7. He made his lone field-goal attempt and all four of his PATs during Cincinnati's 31-24 win in Week 5. McPherson was forced to do his damage with extra points, as the victory marked his second straight outing with only one FGA. He'll look to make more of an impact against a Baltimore defense allowing 22.0 points per game, which ranks 15th.
outlooksByWeek.8: Evan McPherson and the Bengals return home for a Week 8 showdown against the 1-6 Titans. He did not attempt a field goal but converted all five of his extra-point tries during Cincinnati's 35-13 win in Week 7. McPherson is perfect through six contests this season, going 10-for-10 on FGs and 19-for-19 on PATs. However, with the Bengals offense routinely finding the endzone, his opportunities to make a big fantasy difference have suffered.
outlooksByWeek.9: Evan McPherson and the Bengals travel to take on the Falcons for a Week 9 interconference tilt in Spain. He made all five of his PATs for the second consecutive game during Cincinnati's 43-36 overtime victory in Week 8. It was also the second time in as many weeks that McPherson did not attempt a field goal, as Joe Burrow and the Bengals offense racked up six total TDs in the win. McPherson has yet to miss a single kick in 2026, going 10-for-10 on FGs and 24-for-24 on PATs, but his fantasy ceiling is seemingly capped with Cincinnati frequently finding the endzone.
outlooksByWeek.10: Evan McPherson and the Bengals battle the Steelers for an AFC North showdown in Week 10. He went 2-for-2 on field goals and made all four of his PATs during Cincinnati's 34-17 victory in Week 9. McPherson is one of two kickers who are still perfect at this point in the season, and he'll look to keep that going versus a Pittsburgh defense allowing just 18.0 points per game, tied for the fourth fewest.
outlooksByWeek.11: In Week 11, Evan McPherson and the high-flying Bengals offense will travel to Washington for an interconference showdown. He went 1-for-2 on field goals while connecting on all five PATs during Cincinnati's 38-18 win in Week 10. McPherson's miss was his first of the season, so he'll be looking to get back on track versus a Commanders team allowing 24.8 points per game.
outlooksByWeek.12: In Week 12, Evan McPherson and the Bengals will attempt to extend a three-game home win streak when the Saints come to town. He went 2-for-2 on both field goal and extra point attempts during Cincinnati's Week 11 loss. McPherson's 56-yard field goal with less than a minute remaining gave the Bengals the lead, but only for the time being, as their five-game win streak was snapped in the end. He bounced back nicely after missing his first kick of the season in Week 10, and McPherson will continue earning plenty of scoring opportunities in Cincinnati's high-powered offense.

player.seasonOutlook: No team has as soft a schedule on the defensive side of things than do the Ravens; only the Cowboys (Week 3), Bengals (7 and 17) and Bills (8) stand out as particularly challenging matchups. That's a good thing, considering this unit finished a disappointing 21st in scoring last season. The Ravens still have stars on the defensive side, and the change in head coach to Jesse Minter and defensive coordinator to Anthony Weaver should fuel a rebound to some degree.

outlooksByWeek.2: Travis Etienne is expected to remain New Orleans' top running back in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Despite Alvin Kamara (knee) being sidelined for the Week 1 overtime loss, Etienne only received nine carries, tying Kendre Miller for the most on the team. However, Etienne was busy as a receiver, catching seven of nine targets for 46 yards, which is a positive sign for his fantasy outlook going forward. He could be in for another productive week, as Baltimore's defense allowed 28.1 PPR fantasy points to running backs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Travis Etienne is expected operate as New Orleans' top running back in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Despite signing a big contract with the Saints this past offseason, Etienne saw just 10 opportunities in the Week 2 win over the Ravens. He still leads the team in carries (17) but saw less work through the air, with Alvin Kamara (five catches on six targets) returning to the lineup. With Kamara back, Etienne may struggle to be fantasy relevant without finding the end zone against a Raiders defense that's allowed just 17.5 PPR fantasy points per game to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Travis Etienne (hamstring) will likely operate as New Orleans' top running back if active for the Week 10 matchup against the Panthers. Etienne has been sidelined for the Saints' last five games due to a hamstring issue, but his 21-day practice window is expected to be opened soon. If active for the Week 10 divisional matchup, Etienne is expected to thrive against a Panthers defense that's already allowed 12 touchdowns to opposing running backs in just eight games this year.
outlooksByWeek.11: Travis Etienne will look to make a larger impact as the Saints' take on the Bears in Week 11. Etienne was relatively ineffective in his return from injury during the Week 10 loss to the Panthers, logging 11 touches for 34 yards. Despite Etienne serving as New Orleans' top running back, Audric Estime took most of the short-yardage work, and Alvin Kamara operated as the team's top red-zone back, scoring two touchdowns. Thus, Etienne's fantasy upside may be capped if his red-zone touches don't increase in the near future. He's set to face a solid Bears defense in Week 11 that's allowed just 20.4 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Travis Etienne is expected to remain the Saints' top rusher during the Week 12 matchup against the Bengals. In his two games since returning from a hamstring injury, Etienne has accumulated 90 rushing yards (4.1 yards per carry) and 20 receiving yards without finding the end zone. Despite his lack of production, Etienne was received 14 of the Saints' 16 running back carries during the Week 11 loss to the Bears, suggesting he's got a firm hold on the No. 1 role. Etienne is also in for an unfavorable matchup, as Cincinnati has allowed just 20.8 points per game to opposing running backs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Etienne signed with the Saints after spending the first five seasons of his pro career with the Jaguars. The 2021 first-round pick has produced at least 1,399 scrimmage yards in three of the past four seasons and scored a career-high 13 touchdowns in 2025. A capable rusher and receiver, Etienne has already reached 1,000-plus rushing yards three times and has 35-plus catches in each of the past four seasons. Even if the Saints retain Alvin Kamara as a situational player, Etienne will have a clear path to feature-back duties in an ascending offense led by second-year QB Tyler Shough. That will be enough to position the 27-year-old for his third top-15 fantasy campaign in four years. Consider Etienne a solid RB2 target with backend RB1 upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ladd McConkey seemed headed for a big performance in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals, catching five of seven targets for 81 yards and a touchdown. However, he was knocked out of the game in the third quarter after a big hit left him with a rib injury. McConkey still led the team in receiving yards and was on the receiving end of Justin Herbert's only TD pass, and the club doesn't seem to believe the injury is serious. His status for Week 2 will remain up in the air until later in the week, if not right up to kickoff. If he is able to suit up, McConkey will be facing a Raiders secondary that was tied for 21st in points per game allowed to WRs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ladd McConkey was clearly limited by a rib injury in the Chargers' Week 2 loss to the Raiders, catching all three of his targets for 35 yards. That was still good enough to tie for the team lead in receptions, however, as Justin Herbert and the entire offense continue to adjust to the new scheme instituted by OC Mike McDaniel. McConkey is Herbert's clear top downfield option, and as he gets healthier, his production should begin to look more like the 5-82-1 line he delivered in the season opener before getting hurt in the third quarter. McConkey will get a favorable matchup in Week 3 against a Bills secondary that's given up the fourth-most receiving yards to WRs so far this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ladd McConkey seemed hampered by his rib injury in the Chargers' Week 3 loss to the Bills, but he still managed to turn five targets into four catches for 66 yards. The clear top option for Justin Herbert, McConkey has 15 targets through three games despite missing most of the second half in Week 2 after getting hurt, turning that volume into a 12-183-1 line. That's the only touchdown Herbert has thrown to a wide receiver so far in 2026. McConkey should be a little healthier in Week 4, but he'll be facing a Seahawks secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ladd McConkey failed to catch either of his targets in the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, leaving the game early after aggravating a foot injury he picked up in practice during the week. The third-year wideout was already playing through a rib issue, and an absence of one or more games seems almost assured. The Chargers' passing game has struggled with or without him on the field, but if McConkey does miss time, Quentin Johnston and Tre' Harris would become Justin Herbert's top downfield options in Week 5 against a Broncos secondary that ranks eighth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs but which could be missing its top two cornerbacks, including Patrick Surtain.
outlooksByWeek.6: Ladd McConkey continues to deal with injuries, sitting out the Chargers' Week 5 loss to the Broncos with a foot issue after dealing with a rib injury earlier in the season. He hasn't caught a pass since Week 3, but in those first three games, McConkey managed a 12-183-1 line on 15 targets as Justin Herbert's clear No. 1 option. The rest of the team's wide receiver room is also banged up, which could give the team extra incentive to get McConkey back in the lineup as quickly as possible. Even if he suits up in Week 6, he'll struggle to contribute against a Kansas City secondary that ranks first in the NFL in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Ladd McConkey has only missed one game so far in 2026, but injuries have marred the season for the Chargers' top wide receiver, and he comes out of the team's bye still in the league's concussion protocol. The offense as a whole has struggled, but McConkey's been productive when reasonably healthy, posting a 12-182-1 line on 15 targets over the first three weeks. If he's cleared to return in Week 8, he'll take on a stingy Rams secondary that ranks fifth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Ladd McConkey came out of the Chargers' bye looking healthy, and he was one of the few bright spots on offense for the team in a Week 8 loss to the Rams. The third-year wideout caught four of six targets for 86 yards, and over six games this season -- only two of which he saw a full snap share in -- he's produced a 17-286-1 line on 24 targets. If McConkey can stay on the field, he figures to continue being Justin Herbert's top downfield option, on a winless team that's been trailing early and often in 2026. McConkey will face an underperforming Texans secondary in Week 9 that ranks a stunning 30th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Ladd McConkey didn't log any snaps in the Chargers' Week 9 loss to the Texans, as back spasms during pregame workouts kept him on the sideline. The third-year wide receiver has seen a full workload in just two of the seven games he's been active for, and with the team winless on the season, there's little incentive for the Chargers to take any risks with his health. McConkey has been productive when he's been in the lineup, but it's becoming harder to predict when that will be. If he manages to play in Week 10, he'll be facing a Ravens secondary that's tied for 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Ladd McConkey missed his third game of the season in Week 10, this time due to back trouble, as the Chargers' beat the Ravens for their first win of the season. McConkey's been fully healthy for only two games so far in 2026, posting an 8-152-0 line on 11 targets in those contests, and his only touchdown of the year came back in the first half of Week 1 before he suffered his initial rib injury, which was followed by a foot injury and a concussion. If McConkey is cleared to return in Week 11, he'll face a Jets secondary that ranks seventh in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Ladd McConkey made his mark in the red zone during the Chargers' Week 11 loss to the Jets, catching five of eight targets for 37 yards and two touchdowns. The third-year wide receiver hadn't found the end zone since Week 1 as he endures an injury-plagued season, but when he's been in the lineup, he's been Justin Herbert's clear top option. Unfortunately, it could be Herbert's turn on the sideline, as the quarterback was diagnosed with a concussion after the loss to the Jets. McConkey's outlook would get a big downgrade if DJ Uiagalelei is under center for his first career NFL start, but regardless of who is throwing him the ball, he'll be facing a Patriots secondary that ranks an enticing 31st in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: McConkey is looking to rebound after falling short of high expectations in 2025. The 2024 second-round pick was terrific as a rookie (82-1,155-7 receiving line and a 12th-place finish among WRs in fantasy points), but dipped to 66-789-6 line and a 30th-place finish last season. Though he ran considerably more routes, saw similar target numbers and was used a lot more near the goal line (seventh among WRs with 12 end zone targets), McConkey's efficiency plummeted, with his catch rate dipping from 74% to 62% and his yards per target from 10.4 to 7.4. The good news is that there's reason for optimism that he'll bounce back, as he has a new playcaller in Mike McDaniel, the Chargers' offense figures to improve with a much healthier line, and Keenan Allen is out of the picture. McConkey, 24, makes for a fine fantasy WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Zay Flowers and the Ravens welcome the Saints to town for a Week 2 matchup. Flowers left Baltimore's 41-23 Week 1 win in the second quarter and did not return. He is considered day-to-day with a hamstring injury, per head coach Jesse Minter. Soft tissue injuries can be tricky, especially for someone as shifty as Flowers, but it sounds like the issue is not considered serious. He's fresh off posting a career-high 150 receiving yards on five catches (six targets) and a TD, so if the speedster is active against New Orleans, he should see plenty of looks from Lamar Jackson.
outlooksByWeek.3: Zay Flowers and the Ravens are in Dallas for a Week 3 matchup between 1-1 teams. He was ruled out of Baltimore's Week 2 loss with a hamstring injury he suffered in the season opener, so his status in practice this week will be something to monitor. If he's able to suit up in Week 3, Flowers will face a Cowboys defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game (31.2) and 13th in receiving yards allowed to WRs. In his absence, Rashod Bateman put up a 7-88-1 receiving line on nine targets as Lamar Jackson's No. 1 receiver.
outlooksByWeek.4: Zay Flowers and the Ravens welcome the Titans to town in Week 4. He returned from a one-game absence in Week 2 due to a hamstring injury and handled a full workload, catching five of six targets for 84 yards while taking his lone carry for 20 yards during Baltimore's Week 3 victory. Flowers led the team in receptions, targets, and yardage, and that should remain the same against Tennessee, which has the 18th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (32.9) to WRs. The hamstring issue appears to be behind him for now, but managers will want to keep an eye on his practice reps leading up to Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.5: Zay Flowers looks to continue his hot start in 2026 when the Ravens visit the Falcons in Week 5. He grabbed eight of 10 targets for 118 yards and a touchdown during Baltimore's 24-18 win in Week 4. The fourth-year wideout owns an 18-352-2 receiving line on 22 targets across three contests. However, if Lamar Jackson (ankle) is unable to suit up, Flowers will be catching passes from Tyler Huntley, who completed eight of nine passes for 63 yards in relief of Jackson. He'll have the added benefit of facing an Atlanta defense that allows 38.4 fantasy points per game (T-27th) to WRs and gave up eight receptions for 116 yards to Chris Olave.
outlooksByWeek.6: Zay Flowers and the Ravens travel to take on the division-rival Browns in Week 6. He hauled in eight of nine targets for 53 yards during Baltimore's overtime victory in Week 5. Flowers paced the team in receptions and targets and was second in yardage, showing a strong rapport with Tyler Huntley, who started in place of the injured Lamar Jackson (ankle). No matter who's under center, Flowers remains the top receiving threat against Cleveland's 24th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (36.4) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Zay Flowers and the Ravens return home for a divisional showdown against the Bengals in Week 7. He caught six of 11 targets for 66 yards and had one carry for one yard during Baltimore's Week 6 loss. Flowers led Baltimore in receptions, yardage, and targets, with no other player earning more than five looks from Tyler Huntley. With Lamar Jackson's (ankle) status in question for a third consecutive week, Huntley is in line for his second start under center. Regardless of who is at QB, Flowers will continue operating as the clear-cut No. 1 option in the passing game versus Cincinnati's ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (29.3) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Zay Flowers and the Ravens look to halt a two-game losing skid when they visit the Bills in Week 8. He caught eight of 11 targets for 137 yards and a touchdown in Baltimore's 35-13 Week 7 defeat. Flowers led the team in receptions, yardage, and targets by a wide margin, recording the Ravens' only touchdown in the loss. There's a good chance Lamar Jackson (ankle) will return from a three-game absence in Week 8, but Flowers has proven to be a fantasy stud this season no matter who's under center. He'll face a Buffalo defense that surrenders 42.3 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs, the most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Zay Flowers and the Ravens host the Jaguars on Thursday Night Football in Week 9. He was held without a catch on five targets during Baltimore's 36-10 Week 8 loss. With Lamar Jackson (thumb/IR) and Tyler Huntley (toe) both leaving the game with injuries, Flowers struggled mightily to get anything going. The Ravens could be forced to start Joe Fagnano (knee) against the Jaguars' 29th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (37.2) to WRs, but the uncertainty at the QB position greatly lowers Flowers' fantasy appeal.
outlooksByWeek.10: Zay Flowers and the Ravens are at home to take on the Chargers in Week 10. He brought in three of six targets for six yards and rushed three times for another 17 yards during Baltimore's defeat in Week 9. Flowers and his fantasy managers are hoping the acquisition of Jacoby Brissett will provide a boost for the Ravens' passing game, as the former Cardinal will get his first Ravens start on Monday Night Football. Flowers does have a favorable matchup against a Chargers defense allowing 36.9 fantasy points per game (27th) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Zay Flowers and the Ravens look to snap a five-game losing streak when they visit the Panthers in Week 11. He corralled six of seven targets for 74 yards but lost a key fumble during Baltimore's Week 10 loss. Flowers turned it over with 2:11 remaining, ultimately ending his team's chance to tie or take the lead. On a brighter note, Jacoby Brissett attempted 49 passes and threw for 340 yards, meaning Flowers should have no shortage of opportunities to make up for the costly mistake versus Carolina's 14th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (31.5) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Zay Flowers and Baltimore travel to square off against the Texans in Week 12. He caught eight of 11 targets for 97 yards and rushed once for minus-13 yards during Baltimore's Week 11 loss. Flowers led his team in receptions, yardage and targets, but it was Rashod Bateman who was on the receiving end of Jacoby Brissett's 52-yard TD pass. Flowers' fantasy stock is on the rise with Brissett under center, and they'll face a favorable matchup against Houston's 27th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (35.7) to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Flowers' emergence into a star continued in 2025, as the 2023 first-round pick posted career-best marks in target share (29%), targets (118), catches (86) and yardage (1,211). Despite still lacking a role near the goal line (he has never cleared seven end zone targets or six touchdowns in a single season), Flowers finished seventh among receivers in fantasy points (13th PPG), which marks his first finish better than 25th (31st PPG). A highly targeted, short-range RAC specialist, Flowers' ceiling is lower than other top receivers, but the 25-year-old remains positioned as Lamar Jackson's top target in Baltimore's new-look offense. Flowers makes for a solid fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaxson Dart was electric in Week 1 for the New York Giants. Dart threw for 230 yards and three touchdowns, while also rushing for an additional 54 yards in the stunning 28-20 win over the Cowboys. Dart threw just five incompletions and showed excellent rapport with new tight end Isaiah Likely. Dart was accurate, decisive and poised in what amounted to an extremely promising start to the season for the G-Men. In Week 2, the Giants will face a Los Angeles Rams defense that was surprisingly poor in their opener, allowing 379 scrimmage yards, which ranks them in the bottom third of the NFL. The Rams were torched on the ground in particular to the tune of 174 yards. While Myles Garrett will be sidelined due to a knee injury, the Rams will get Aaron Donald back from retirement when they host the Giants on Monday Night Football.

player.seasonOutlook: Dart is a strong 2026 breakout candidate following an impressive rookie campaign in which he delivered eight top-10 fantasy weeks (tied for fifth most) despite playing the bulk of the snaps in only 12 games. Dart was solid as a passer but elite as a rusher, finishing in the top five at the position in rushing attempts, yards, TDs and carries inside the 5-yard line. Dart's aggressive playing style raises concerns about his durability, but it also provides the 23-year-old with elite fantasy upside. With a new coaching staff led by John Harbaugh and a new playcaller in Matt Nagy, as well as an improved supporting cast that includes a healthy Malik Nabers and newcomers Isaiah Likely and Darnell Mooney, Dart is best valued as a midrange QB1 with a high ceiling.

outlooksByWeek.2: Javonte Williams scored twice in the season opener for Dallas. Williams rushed for 41 yards and a touchdown, while catching five passes for 31 yards and a second score, though the Cowboys fell to the Giants by a score of 28-20. Nevertheless, Williams appears to have picked up right where he left off in 2025 during his career year. In Week 2, Williams will face a Washington defense that was gutted on the ground in its season opener. The Commanders yielded 136 yards on the ground, which places them 26th in the NFL in that category currently.
outlooksByWeek.3: Javonte Williams was rather quiet last game for Dallas. Williams managed just 50 yards from scrimmage and did not find the end zone versus Washington, as the passing game took the spotlight in the 37-20 win. Williams may also have a difficult time finding room in Week 3 versus Baltimore. The Ravens are allowing just 83.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is sixth in the NFL. However, Baltimore has allowed three rushing touchdowns already, which is tied for 23rd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Javonte Williams rushed for a season-high 98 yards last game for the Cowboys. Williams also found the end zone for the third time this year. He has received at least 15 touches in every game this season. In Week 4, WIlliams should continue to remain heavily involved against the Houston Texans. The Texans have been extremely stingy against the run, though. Houston is surrendering just 86.7 rushing yards per clash, which is fifth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Javonte Williams scored three times in the second half of the last game for the Cowboys, leading a thrilling comeback victory over the Texans. Williams is averaging just 3.7 yards per tote this season, but has six combined touchdowns through four outings. He has also made his presence felt in the passing game with 15 receptions over that span. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been stellar against the run in 2026. The Bucs are allowing just 78.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is third in the NFL. In addition, Tampa Bay has yielded just one rushing touchdown through four games.
outlooksByWeek.6: Javonte Williams found the end zone yet again last game for Dallas. Williams rushed 12 times for 45 yards and the score, notching his sixth rushing touchdown of the young season. Williams is averaging just 3.7 yards per tote, but has received double-digit carries in every contest in 2026. In Week 6, Williams looks primed for another jaunt to the end zone versus the Packers. Green Bay has given up eight rushing touchdowns already this season, which is 31st in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Javonte Williams found the end zone yet again for Dallas last game. Williams rushed 11 times for 41 yards in the 23-13 loss to the Packers. Williams has scored in four-straight games for the Cowboys, though is averaging just 3.7 yards per tote overall. In fact, he has failed to cross the 50-yard rushing mark in two-straight games. In Week 7, Williams will face a sliding Eagles defense. Philadelphia is allowing 119.3 rushing yards per contest, which is 19th in the league. The Eagles have also yielded eight rushing touchdowns, which is tied for 28th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: Javonte Williams was largely held in check last game for Dallas. Williams managed just 56 yards rushing on 24 carries. He was also held out of the end zone for just the second time all season. The workload remains stellar, though, as Williams now has a staggering 49 carries in the last two contests alone. In Week 9, Dallas will face a Colts defense that has been subpar against the run. Indy is allowing 131.8 rushing yards per tote, which is 27th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Javonte Williams got back into the end zone last game for Dallas. Williams scored his ninth rushing touchdown of the season in the 27-23 win over the Colts. Williams also crossed the 100-yard rushing plateau for the second time in 2026. Williams has at least 20 carries in each of the last three outings. However, in Week 10, he will face a difficult task versus the San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 80.9 rushing yards per game, which is second in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just four rushing scores in 2026, which is tied for second in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Javonte Williams was held out of the end zone for the second time in three games for the Cowboys. Williams rushed 16 times for 63 yards in the 46-40 loss to the 49ers. Williams was also held under 65 yards rushing for the second time in three contests. However, his usage remains high, as he has received double-digit carries in every game in 2026. In Week 11, Williams will face a Titans squad that has been lackluster against the run. Tennessee is allowing 124 rushing yards per tilt, which is tied for 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.12: Javonte Williams scored twice last game for the Cowboys.  Williams rushed 18 times for 67 yards and one touchdown on the ground, while also catching three passes for 24 yards and a second score during the 51-30 blowout of the Titans. Williams has 12 combined touchdowns through 11 contests for Dallas. In Week 12, he will face an Eagles defense allowing 120.8 rushing yards per tilt, which is 21st in the NFL.  Likewise, Philadelphia has surrendered 10 rushing scores this season, which is tied for 18th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams re-signed with the Cowboys following a successful first year with the team. After failing to produce a top-25 fantasy campaign during his final three seasons in Denver, Williams finished 12th in 2025, setting career-best marks in carries, rushing yards, touches (287), scrimmage yards (1,338) and yards per carry (4.77). He also scored a career-high 13 touchdowns after totaling 16 during his first four campaigns, and his 16 carries inside the 5-yard line were fifth most among backs. That helped offset his receiving struggles, as his 2.7 yards per target was last among qualified RBs. With minimal competition for touches in a high-scoring Dallas offense, the 26-year-old is a solid RB2 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens host the Saints for an interconference showdown in Week 2. Jackson was stellar in the opener despite losing a fumble, throwing for 324 yards (17-for-25) with one TD and no picks while rushing seven times for another 40 yards and a TD. Although he still offers elite upside at the QB position, it's important to note that his favorite receiver, Zay Flowers, is dealing with a hamstring injury that coach Jesse Minter considers "day-to-day." The two connected on five of six targets for 150 yards and a score in the victory. The New Orleans defense ranks 12th in fantasy points allowed per game (18.5) to QBs after Jared Goff's 206 yards and two TDs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens look to bounce back after a tough loss when they visit the Cowboys in Week 3. Jackson threw for 235 yards (21-for-31) with one TD and one INT while rushing four times for 34 yards in Week 2's 24-17 loss. Baltimore draws a favorable matchup against a Dallas defense that ranks 27th in fantasy points allowed (27.2) and 31st in rushing yards allowed to QBs. Zay Flowers (hamstring) missed Week 2's contest, but the hope is that Jackson's speedy receiver makes it back on the field in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens host the 0-3 Titans for a Week 4 showdown. In Baltimore's thrilling 34-31 win over Dallas in Week 3, he connected on 15 of 20 throws for 186 yards with two TDs and no INTs while rushing six times for 50 yards, including a 27-yard strike to Zay Flowers that helped set up the game-winning field goal as time expired. Tennessee's defense has been stingy, allowing just 13.9 fantasy points per game to QBs through three games, which ranks first. Jackson should have his full complement of receivers available as the Ravens aim to improve to 3-1 on the season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens travel to face the Falcons on Sunday Night Football in Week 5. Prior to missing the entire second half of Baltimore's 24-18 win in Week 4, the two-time MVP threw for 222 yards (15-for-20) with two TDs and no INTs while rushing twice for 20 yards. Jackson was well on his way to a stellar outing with his team up 24-7 at halftime, but an ankle injury forced him out early and has him in jeopardy of missing the upcoming road tilt in Atlanta. Head coach Jesse Minter said Monday that the Ravens are uncertain of Jackson's status for Week 5, and if he's unable to suit up, Tyler Huntley will get the nod at quarterback.
outlooksByWeek.6: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens visit the division-rival Browns in Week 6. The two-time league MVP sat out Baltimore's 30-23 overtime win in Week 5 with a sprained left ankle. Head coach Jesse Minter relayed Monday that Jackson is "definitely doing better" in his recovery, but there's still no guarantee that he'll be ready for the trip to Cleveland. Tyler Huntley filled in admirably as the starting QB, throwing for 201 yards with two TDs and no INTs while rushing six times for 20 yards and another score in the OT victory. Jackson will need to practice in some form before the Ravens can determine his status against the Browns' 18th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (20.7) to the position.
outlooksByWeek.7: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens host the Bengals for an AFC North showdown in Week 7. He missed a second consecutive game in Week 6, a 13-10 loss to Cleveland, due to an ankle injury sustained in Week 4. Head coach Jesse Minter said Monday that Jackson could potentially get back on the practice field during Week 7 prep, but Baltimore is still considering their star quarterback day-to-day. If he's unable to suit up for the third straight contest, Tyler Huntley will continue to start under center versus Cincinnati's 19th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (21.5) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens visit the Bills in Week 8. After missing the last three contests with an ankle injury, he appears to be headed in the right direction, as head coach Jesse Minter stated Jackson is "in a decent spot" to return to action against Buffalo. His practice participation bears monitoring following his limited activity prior to Baltimore's Week 7 loss. If active, Jackson will aim to snap a two-game losing streak versus a Bills defense allowing 26.5 fantasy points per game (30th) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Lamar Jackson is heading to the IR after taking just one snap for the Ravens in Week 9. He missed the prior three contests with a high-ankle injury, and now thumb surgery could end his season. Tyler Huntley took over, but he had to exit with a toe injury, forcing emergency third-string QB Joe Fagnano into action. More will be known about Jackson's status after he goes under a very small knife.

player.seasonOutlook: Jackson, 29, is eyeing a rebound after a disappointing, injury-plagued 2025. Jackson started the season strong (26-plus fantasy points in each of his first three games) but left Week 4 because of an injury and wasn't the same once he returned in Week 9 (13.5 fantasy points per game in his final nine outings). Jackson's overall rushing was down, but that was likely a product of him not being fully healthy, especially considering his scramble rate (8.4%) remained high. Jackson has a new coach (Jesse Minter) and playcaller (Declan Doyle), but his supporting cast is otherwise similar to a 2024 campaign in which he paced all quarterbacks in fantasy points. Assuming he's back to full health, Jackson is a strong bet for a rebound and should be valued as a high-end QB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Christian Watson will seek to build off a monster outing as the Packers travel to take on the Jets in Week 2. Watson ended a Week 1 loss to the Vikings with a dominant stat line, catching six of his eight targets for 147 yards and two touchdowns. The fifth-year wideout could be a breakout star this season, especially if Green Bay continues to deploy a pass-heavy offense. The Jets secondary, who gave up a middle-of-the-pack 26.4 PPR points to wide receivers in Week 1, looks weaker than Minnesota's as well.
outlooksByWeek.3: Christian Watson remains the top option in Green Bay's offense as they take on the Falcons in Week 3. Watson finished with a quieter four catches for 41 yards and a touchdown against the Jets in Week 2, but he did garner an impressive 11 targets. The fifth-year wideout has now scored three touchdowns on a team-high 19 targets across two games. He'll take on an Atlanta defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 30.3 PPR points per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Christian Watson will look to keep his touchdown streak rolling as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 4. Watson finished Week 3 against the Falcons with seven catches for 96 yards and a touchdown, putting him at a 17-284-4 receiving line on the year. The fifth-year wideout remains quarterback Jordan Love's top option at this point in the year, with him and Matthew Golden making for a dangerous duo so far. Watson will face a Tampa Bay defense that's allowed a top-ten 25.4 fantasy points per game to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.5: Christian Watson will remain a top option in Green Bay's passing game against the Bears in Week 5. Watson finished Week 4 at Tampa Bay with a quiet three catches for 47 yards, but Jordan Love threw for just 197 yards. The go-to wideout has now posted a 20-331-4 receiving line on 32 targets so far this campaign, and he's on pace for his first 1,000-yard season if he can stay healthy. Watson could have a tough task versus a Chicago defense that's ranked top five in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Christian Watson will look to continue his dominance as the Packers take on the Cowboys in Week 6. Watson recorded a stellar performance in Week 5 against the Bears, bringing in six of eight targets for 143 yards and two touchdowns. The fifth-year wideout has cemented himself as Jordan Love's top option in the passing game, with a 26-474-6 receiving line through five games. Watson will face a Dallas defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.7: Christian Watson will look to get back in the end zone as the Packers play the Lions in Week 7. Watson finished Week 6 against the Cowboys tying a season-low of three catches, but he was still able to convert them into 64 yards. The fifth-year wideout has now amassed 29 catches for 538 yards and six touchdowns this season. He'll face a Detroit defense that's ranked 30th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Christian Watson will aim to return to dominance as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Watson brought in five of eight targets for a team-leading 57 yards in a Week 7 loss to the Lions, which was his lowest yardage total since Week 4. The wideout still has a 34-595-6 receiving line through the first seven games of the season, and he's not far off from outpacing his stat totals from the 2024 and 2025 season. Carolina has ranked a stern fifth in fantasy points allowed to WRs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.9: Christian Watson will look to heal from a broken rib ahead of Green Bay's Week 9 matchup at New England. Watson injured himself in the second quarter of Week 8 against the Panthers, but he returned to the game in the third quarter after a brief trip to the hospital. Even with these setbacks, the starting wideout finished the game with an impressive stat line, hauling in eight of 10 targets for 113 yards. He's now sitting at a receiving line of 42-708-6, which is career-high in both receptions and yards. He'll face a Patriots defense that's ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to WRs in the last three weeks.
outlooksByWeek.10: Christian Watson will look to build off a career day as the Packers play the Vikings in Week 10. Watson put together a prolific performance in a Week 9 win over the Patriots, bringing in seven of eight targets for 171 yards and a touchdown. The wideout now holds a career-high receiving line of 49-879-7 on 74 targets. He'll face a Minnesota secondary that he tore up with 6 catches for 147 yards and two touchdowns against in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.12: Christian Watson will look to make a bang out of the bye week as the Packers play the Rams in Week 12. Watson struggled against a tough Minnesota defense in Week 10, catching three of five targets for a season-low 37 yards. The premier wideout has still impressed across the first 10 games of his fifth campaign, posting a 52-916-7 receiving line on 79 targets. His next challenge will be a Los Angeles defense that's ranked third in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.

player.seasonOutlook: Watson has had quite the boom/bust NFL career and that was on full display in 2025. After missing the first seven games due to injury, Watson returned and scored 18-plus fantasy points four times, but averaged 7.7 in his other six outings. The oft-injured 2022 second-round pick has still yet to play a full regular season, but has weirdly finished with between 611 and 620 receiving yards in three of his four campaigns. Though Watson has yet to deliver a top-40 fantasy season, he's been extremely efficient in his vertical role, ranking exactly second in average depth of target, YPR and YPT each of the last two seasons. Durability is an obvious concern, but the 27-year-old could very well lead Green Bay in targets following Romeo Doubs' departure. Watson should be valued as a volatile flex option with added value in non-PPR leagues.

outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Jacobs is unlikely to play in the Packers' Week 3 matchup against the Falcons. Jacobs remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List at this point in the season, with no current indications of when he'll be back in action. A committee of MarShawn Lloyd, Chris Brooks and Kaleb Johnson will continue to provide Green Bay's rushing attack while the veteran is absent.
outlooksByWeek.8: Josh Jacobs will look to ramp it up even more as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Jacobs carved out a solid performance in his return to the field against the Lions in Week 7, rushing the ball for 36 yards off 11 carries but catching five passes for 55 yards and a touchdown. While the rushing efficiency wasn't there, the usage definitely was, which bodes well for the veteran ball carrier. He could also be in store for a better outing on the ground, as Carolina has ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to RBs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.9: Josh Jacobs will again have an asterisk next to his name as the Packers face the Patriots in Week 9. Jacobs has been active the last two weeks, and while he's averaged an inefficient 2.3 yards per carry on 32 attempts, he's salvaged his performances with three total touchdowns in this stretch. The veteran ball carrier also could be at risk of not playing in the near future, as the NFL continues to investigate his alleged physical incidents. This makes him an uncertain play, especially against a New England defense that's ranked sixth in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Josh Jacobs is unlikely to play in Week 10 as the Packers take on the Vikings. Jacobs hurt his finger in a Week 9 win over the Patriots, and he's now set to undergo surgery, which will keep him out for a maximum of three weeks. The veteran ball carrier has now recorded 36 rushes for 80 yards and a touchdown, with 11 catches for 68 yards and two touchdowns as well. Kaleb Johnson, Pierre Strong, and banged-up Chris Brooks and MarShawn Lloyd will be Green Bay's available running backs against a tough Minnesota defense.
outlooksByWeek.12: Josh Jacobs will look to make a return as the Packers play the Rams in Week 12. Jacobs missed Week 10 against Minnesota with a finger injury, and while he's had a week off to get back to full health, he was unable to practice fully on Monday. If the veteran ball carrier is good to go, he'll look to come out on top of a crowded backfield against a Los Angeles defense that's ranked third in fantasy points allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Jacobs' 2025 season can be split in two parts: pre-injury and post-injury. While healthy during his first nine games, Jacobs picked up where he left off from a terrific 2024 debut season with Green Bay, averaging 21.1 touches and 19.6 fantasy points while scoring 11 TDs. After missing all but 11 snaps during Weeks 11 and 12, Jacobs returned and wasn't quite the same, averaging 14.6 touches and 11.3 points while totaling three touchdowns in his final five games. But Jacobs, 28, was still effective overall (PFF's fourth-highest-graded back) and has a clear grasp on lead-back duties in a good Green Bay offense that has afforded him 30 touchdowns (fifth most in the NFL) in 32 games. He's a fine back-end RB1 when active, but a likely suspension makes him less valuable on draft day.He's worth a mid-round flier until the dust settles.

outlooksByWeek.2: CeeDee Lamb found the end zone for the Cowboys while leading the squad in receiving in Week 1. However, Lamb finished with five catches for just 44 yards in the dismal 28-20 loss to the Giants. Still, Lamb led the team in targets, and the touchdown salvaged his day from a fantasy perspective. In Week 2, the Cowboys will look to rebound versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: CeeDee Lamb went wild last game for the Cowboys. Lamb caught eight passes for 153 yards and two touchdowns in the win over Washington. Lamb had nine targets for the game. He has scored three touchdowns in his first two contests of the 2026 campaign. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: CeeDee Lamb crossed the 100-yard mark for the second-straight week for the Cowboys. Lamb snagged seven balls for 112 yards in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens. Unfortunately, Lamb was held out of the end zone for the first time all season. However, Lamb has at least eight targets in each of the first three games for Dallas, and should stay in busy in Week 4 versus the Texans, even if he is guarded by all-pro cornerback Derek Stingley Jr. The Cowboys will face a Texans defense that has been surprisingly suspect against the pass in 2026.  Houston is allowing 238.7 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: CeeDee Lamb is coming off a game for the ages. Lamb was targeted a staggering 21 times en route to an absurd 17 catches for 189 yards and a touchdown in the comeback win over the Texans. It was the third-straight 100-yard outing of the season for Lamb, and he scored for the fourth time in four contests. Following this outing, Lamb leads the NFL in receiving yards and receptions, and is tied for third in the NFL with four receiving scores.
