In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: CeeDee Lamb is said to be dealing with a bruise of his quadriceps, but he is not expected to miss any time for the Cowboys. Lamb was limited to two catches for just nine yards last game as he was dealing with the issue. That snapped a three-game streak for Lamb of at least 112 yards receiving. He will look to get back on track in Week 6 versus the Packers. However, Green Bay's defense is allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered only six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: CeeDee Lamb was targeted a staggering 18 times last game for Dallas. With the Cowboys trailing for the entire contest, the passing game took center stage, though admittedly had a difficult time. Despite the bevy of looks, Lamb managed just 70 yards on nine catches in the 23-13 loss. Lamb has an absurd 44 targets over his last three contests. He will look to get back over the 100-yard receiving mark in Week 7 versus Philadelphia. The Eagles are allowing 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL. However, Philadelphia has given up just eight passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 14th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: CeeDee Lamb scored twice last game for the Cowboys.  Lamb led the Cowboys receivers in all categories, snagging five passes for 74 yards and the two touchdowns. He has found the end zone six times in seven contests. In Week 8, the Cowboys will face an Arizona Cardinals defense that has been prone to surrendering the touchdown pass. In fact, Arizona has given up 17 passing scores, which is dead last in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: CeeDee Lamb led the Cowboys in receiving last game. Unfortunately, he managed just 58 yards and failed to find the end zone in the 33-30 OT loss to Arizona. Lamb has accumulated a staggering 41 targets over the last three contest, though has failed to cross 75 yards receiving in any of those contests. In Week 9, Dallas will face a Colts defense allowing just 211.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 12th in the NFL. However, Indianapolis has given up 14 passing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: CeeDee Lamb took advantage of the absence of George Pickens last game for Dallas. While Lamb is always the top target in the offense, with Pickens out of the lineup Lamb was targeted even more frequently than usual, a total of 16 times against the Colts. Lamb responded with 10 catches for a staggering 195 yards and a touchdown. Lamb has double-digit targets in four-straight games, and Pickens remains questionable for the Week 10 clash with the 49ers. However, the Niners are allowing just 211 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just 11 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for seventh in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: CeeDee Lamb continues to pile up statistics for the Dallas Cowboys. Lamb found the end zone for the second-straight game and eighth time overall in 2026 in the 46-40 loss to the 49ers. Lamb finished with seven catches for 72 yards and the score. Lamb has drawn double-digit targets in five-straight contests, a trend that should continue in Week 11 versus the Titans. Tennessee is allowing 266.9 passing yards per tilt, which is dead last in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: CeeDee Lamb crossed the 100-yard threshold yet again for the Cowboys last game. Lamb caught 11 passes for 132 yards and a touchdown in the 51-30 dismantling of the Titans. Lamb has scored in three-straight contests, and has gone over the 100-yard receiving mark in two of those outings. He is second in the NFL in receiving yardage overall, and first in receptions. In Week 12, the Cowboys will face a mediocre Eagles pass defense. Philadelphia is allowing 222.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 17th in the NFL. However, the Eagles have only given up 14 passing touchdowns, which is tied for ninth in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Lamb is eyeing a bounceback season following a 2025 campaign in which he finished 12th among receivers in fantasy PPG � his worst finish since 2021. Lamb did go over 1,000 yards for the fifth season in a row, but he missed three games, led all receivers with eight drops and was unlucky in the TD department, having scored three touchdowns (6.6 expected) despite seeing 11 end zone targets. Lamb, 27, remains in his prime and he was fantasy's top-scoring receiver the last time he played a full season (2023). As long Dak Prescott is on the field with him, Lamb will be a solid fantasy WR1 with elite upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dalton Kincaid will look to match a career outing when the Bills face the Lions in Week 2. Kincaid had a personal-best 130 yards in his season debut but, more importantly, played 77% of the team's snaps after topping 50% just three times last year. If Kincaid remains on the field at this rate, he's likely to soar past his previous season's output. He'll face a defense on Thursday night that allowed 87 yards and two touchdowns to tight ends in Week 1, suggesting his statistical surge can continue.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dalton Kincaid brings momentum into the Bills' Week 3 matchup with the Chargers. After a 130-yard opener, Kincaid posted seven catches for 95 yards and a touchdown in Week 2 against Detroit, playing on 66% of the offensive snaps. Opportunity, not talent, has been an issue as he hasn't played over a 50% snap share since Week 5 in 2025. The Chargers were dominated by Tre McBride in Week 1 but rebounded against the Brock Bowers-less Raiders tight end room last week. Kincaid's big numbers are poised to continue in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dalton Kincaid will seek to rebuild momentum when the Bills face the Patriots in Week 4. After gaining 225 yards in Weeks 1 and 2, Kincaid had just two catches for 38 yards in Week 3. Part of the decrease in volume could be DJ Moore's return to health, but Buffalo remains run-heavy, limiting Kincaid's looks. He recorded a 67% snap share, more than usual, so opportunity remains. Facing a Patriots defense that has defended the tight end position well dampens hope, having allowed only 84 total yards to the position.
outlooksByWeek.5: Dalton Kincaid faces an uphill battle for a bounce-back performance when the Bills face the Rams in Week 5. He is coming off a season-low seven yards on two targets (one catch), and after a productive two-game start, has only five targets in Weeks 3 and 4. The Rams have defended tight ends at an elite level, allowing a mere 2.9 yards per target and only 85 total yards through four games.
outlooksByWeek.6: Dalton Kincaid's role in the Bills' passing game is shrinking ahead of a Week 6 matchup with the Raiders. After snagging 12 of 14 targets in his first two games, Kincaid has been limited to four catches on seven targets over the last three weeks, amassing just 52 yards. His snap share remains strong and elevated from 2025; Buffalo just seems more inclined to be a run-first offense. Las Vegas has allowed six touchdowns to opposing tight ends, resulting in the fifth-most fantasy points allowed to the position. Kincaid can be a viable starting option in a favorable bounce-back matchup.
outlooksByWeek.8: Dalton Kincaid hopes to rediscover some early season success with the Bills coming out of a bye week to host the Ravens in Week 8. After snagging 12 of 14 targets for 225 yards in his first two games, Kincaid has not topped 38 yards or scored in his subsequent four outings, despite maintaining a higher snap share than last season. Baltimore is allowing only 39.0 yards per game to opposing tight ends, setting up Kincaid for another quiet week, but the Ravens allowed two touchdowns to the position last week and five overall, potentially helping Kincaid break his scoring drought.
outlooksByWeek.9: Dalton Kincaid faces a challenging matchup in Week 9 when the Bills face the Vikings. He has 11 catches over the last two weeks, scoring in Week 8 for the first time since Week 2, and finished with 86 yards after hauling in just 90 total yards in his previous four games. Minnesota has allowed the fewest points per game to opposing tight ends, surrendering only 6.2 yards per target and no touchdowns through seven games. Kincaid needs volume to be productive in the Week 9 Monday night affair, and that's not a sure thing.
outlooksByWeek.10: Dalton Kincaid's role in the Bills offense may be sliding as they enter a Week 10 matchup against the Jets. In Buffalo's first six games, Kincaid garnered less than a 66% snap share just once, but since the team's Week 7 bye, he's been under 60% in two outings, resulting in just nine targets. The Jets have been vulnerable against tight ends, allowing at least 72 yards in three straight weeks, but Kincaid's recent workload is a concern.
outlooksByWeek.11: A lack of opportunities could keep the Bills' Dalton Kincaid from exploiting the Dolphins' defense in Week 11. He had just three targets for the second straight game in Week 10, and his snap share has declined in each of the last three games since Buffalo's Week 7 bye, reaching a season-low 46% in Week 10. Buffalo has been a run-heavy offense, often leaving Kincaid off the field in favor of more traditional blocking tight ends. With declining snaps, he will be left with too few chances to beat a defense that's allowing the seventh-most fantasy points per game to the position.
outlooksByWeek.12: Dalton Kincaid will need to overcome thumb and ankle injuries if he's to help the Bills in a promising Week 12 matchup with the Chiefs. His playing time and production have slid over the last three weeks coming out of Buffalo's Week 7 bye. Kincaid's snap share has dropped to around 50%, ceding his slot role to Dawson Knox, who is serving as an additional blocker on the line. If Kincaid plays, opportunities await, with Kansas City allowing tight ends to catch at least four passes in three straight games and five overall touchdowns. They have also yielded the seventh-most fantasy points per game to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Kincaid is perhaps fantasy's biggest wild card among tight ends. The 2023 first-round pick has occasionally flashed a high ceiling (he actually led qualified tight ends in YPT and YPRR last season), but he also has missed substantial action (nine games the past two years) and has disappeared way too often (he failed to clear 13.1 fantasy points in any game in 2024, and never cleared six targets in a game in 2025). Kincaid was limited to a 37% snap share when active last season, and he has yet to finish a season better than 14th in fantasy PPG. The 26-year-old has TE1 upside, but he's tough to trust and has added target competition (WR DJ Moore) in 2026. Consider Kincaid only in the mid-to-late rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jadarian Price is set for his second NFL start when Seattle travels to Arizona in Week 2. Price was efficient in his professional debut last Wednesday versus New England, rushing 10 times for 52 yards while catching both of his targets for six yards. George Holani was given eight carries in the win, which helped limit Price's workload. The split between the two going forward remains to be seen, but there's certainly a chance that Price's touches will increase as the season progresses. The Cardinals' run defense looked good against the Chargers in Week 1, holding Omarion Hampton to 43 yards on 12 carries.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jadarian Price injured his shoulder in the Seahawks' Week 2 win over Arizona, and it's unclear if he'll be able to play in Week 3 against Washington. The rookie RB was injured in the fourth quarter versus the Cardinals and finished the game with 13 carries for 52 yards and one catch for eight yards. Should Price not be able to play in Week 3, Emanuel Wilson would be he lead candidate to take over as the Seahawks starting RB. The Commanders have been awful against the pass but decent against the run this season and are yielding just 3.79 YPC against running backs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jadarian Price heads into Seattle's Week 4 matchup against the Chargers with potentially a lot on the line. After fumbling early in Sunday's Week 3 win over the Commanders, the rookie ended up logging just five totes for 15 yards while adding one catch for seven yards. Meanwhile, Emanuel Wilson (nine carries) and George Holani (three carries and five catches) each out-touched Price, casting uncertainty about the Seahawks' backfield plans moving forward. Price would benefit from a productive (and fumble-free) performance against the Chargers, who rank 19th in the league in giving up 17.2 fantasy points per game through three weeks.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jadarian Price (chest) is eligible to return from IR for Seattle's Week 8 matchup against Chicago. Price hasn't played since Week 3, but he's expected to be designated to return this week. It remains to be seen if the rookie will be able to suit up against the Bears, and even if he does play, he may be part of a backfield committee that also includes Emanuel Wilson and the potentially returning Zach Charbonnet (knee). With that said, Seattle's backfield could find success against a Chicago defense that has given up 4.33 yards per carry to running backs, 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jadarian Price is coming off an inefficient return from IR heading into Seattle's Week 9 clash against the Cardinals. Price moved past a chest injury to lead Seattle's backfield in carries against Chicago on Monday Night Football, but he garnered just 29 yards on 10 totes and eight yards on two catches. He shared RB snaps fairly equally with Zach Charbonnet, and if the duo continues in a timeshare, both players may have a limited week-to-week fantasy ceiling. The Cardinals do present a relatively favorable matchup, as they're middling or worse in most statistical categories versus running backs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jadarian Price looks to be settling in as Seattle's No. 2 RB ahead of a Week 10 clash against Las Vegas. The rookie running back handled 13 touches this past Sunday in a win over Arizona while Zach Charbonnet logged 17 touches. However, Charbonnet had 16 carries to Prize's nine, suggesting that the former may be leaning more toward a change-of-pace role. Both Charbonnet and Price could be utilized heavily against the Raiders, who have given up the second-most fantasy points per game (23.1) to running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Jadarian Price's role at running back for Seattle could gain further clarity in Week 12 against San Francisco. Though he scored his first career touchdown in Week 10 against Las Vegas, Price's 10 touches lagged well behind those of Zach Charbonnet, who rushed 20 times for 94 yards. Seattle was on bye Week 11, so if Charbonnet again gets the lion's share of work this weekend, it could be an indication that Price is locked into the team's No. 2 RB role. Both he and Charbonnet could face tough sledding against a 49ers defense that has given up the fourth-fewest yards per carry (3.55) to running backs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Price was selected by the Seahawks with the No. 32 overall pick of April's draft. Price managed only 280 career carries while stuck behind Jeremiyah Love at Notre Dame, but he showed well, posting a 4.13 YAC (second best in this rookie class) and 3.6 forced missed tackle rate (third best). He wasn't a factor as a receiver, however, totaling 15 receptions in 41 games. Price has a path to an immediate feature role in Seattle's run-first offense, though he may eventually defer substantial work to Zach Charbonnet (ACL recovery). Value Price as a flex, though he should land on the weekly RB2 radar while Charbonnet is sidelined.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kirk Cousins had a bumpy Raiders debut in a season-opening win over the Dolphins, completing 21 of 30 passes for 160 yards and three touchdowns with two interceptions. The veteran quarterback is just keeping the starting job warm for 2026 first overall pick Fernando Mendoza, but the team is in no hurry to get the rookie in the lineup before he's ready, and wins will only give Cousins more job security. His passing numbers could improve once star tight end Brock Bowers is cleared to play, as his most productive connection was running back Ashton Jeanty, who was on the other end of two of Cousins' TD passes. Cousins will face a Chargers defense in Week 2 that had trouble slowing down Jacoby Brissett in its opener but finished fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kirk Cousins has had an impressive start to the season, throwing three touchdowns in back-to-back games for a Raiders team that's a surprising 2-0. The veteran quarterback hasn't played completely mistake-free football under Klint Kubiak, throwing three interceptions, but he's only been sacked twice and has completed 67.8 percent of his passes. As long as Cousins remains productive and the team is winning, there will be little incentive for Las Vegas to hand the reins to rookie Fernando Mendoza, but that switch still figures to be coming at some point in 2026. Cousins will face a Saints defense in Week 3 that has done a good job holding Jared Goff and Lamar Jackson in check through its first two contests.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kirk Cousins is having a late-season renaissance with the Raiders. The 38-year-old quarterback has thrown exactly three touchdown passes in each of the first three games of the season, leading his new team to a 3-0 record and keeping first overall pick Fernando Mendoza firmly on the bench. Cousins has also thrown three INTs, and those mistakes could catch up against tougher competition, as two of those victories have come against the NFL's five remaining winless squads. On the other hand, that production came despite Brock Bowers missing the first two weeks, and the star tight end erupted for a 10-116-1 line in his Week 3 debut. Cousins will get his first real test of the year in Week 4 against a Kansas City defense that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kirk Cousins went down swinging in the Raiders' Week 4 loss to Kansas City, setting season highs with 52 pass attempts and 365 yards while throwing multiple TDs for a fourth straight game to begin the season. While rookie first-overall pick Fernando Mendoza waits in the wings, Cousins' 11 touchdowns are tied for the league lead, and he sits just outside the top 10 in passing yards and completion rate, which should give him plenty of job security. The veteran quarterback will try to keep rolling in Week 5 against a Patriots defense that is tied for ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kirk Cousins' production is declining, potentially reducing his time as the Raiders' starting quarterback. After throwing for nine touchdowns during the team's 3-0 start to the season, the veteran has a 3:1 TD:INT over the last two contests, both losses. During a lopsided Week 5 loss to the Patriots, Cousins ceded the final drive to prized rookie Fernando Mendoza, which could be the first step toward Mendoza taking the reins. Cousins' job doesn't seem to be in immediate peril, and he could bounce back in a big way in Week 6 against a Bills defense that ranks 29th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kirk Cousins is coming off a productive effort in the Raiders' near-upset of the Bills in Week 6, throwing for over 300 yards for the second time in six games and tossing multiple TDs for the fifth time. The veteran quarterback is on pace for his first 4,000-yard, 30-TD campaign since 2021 with the Vikings, but to reach those numbers he would need to keep first overall pick Fernando Mendoza on the bench, which looks increasingly unlikely after three straight losses for Las Vegas. Cousins will remain under center for now, but he faces another tough test in Week 7 against a Rams defense that is second in the league in passing yards per game allowed.
outlooksByWeek.8: Kirk Cousins lost a fourth straight start in Week 7, but for now he'll remain the Raiders' starting quarterback ahead of rookie Fernando Mendoza. Cousins has cooled off against tougher competition, but he's still playing well and has a 7:2 TD:INT during the losing streak while averaging 304 passing yards a game. Brock Bowers and Tre Tucker remain his only reliable targets however, and Ashton Jeanty hasn't been able to force defenses to pay more attention to the team's ground game. Cousins may not need to air it out as much in Week 8 against a Jets defense that ranks 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Kirk Cousins is coming off arguably his best performance of 2026, completing a season-high 73.1% of his passes and tossing three touchdowns in a Week 8 win over the Jets. He also ran for his first score of the year. Cousins' 19 TD passes through eight games puts him second in the NFL behind Joe Burrow's 20, and his 2,124 passing yards puts him third behind Matthew Stafford (2,146) and Jordan Love (2,246). As long as Cousins keeps producing at a high level and the Raiders are in the playoff picture, rookie Fernando Mendoza should remain on the bench. Cousins faces a tougher test in Week 9 against a 49ers defense that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Kirk Cousins is coming off his worst performance of the season, getting picked off three times while throwing just one touchdown in the Raiders' Week 9 loss to the 49ers. With Las Vegas now 4-5, the team elected to hand the reins of the offense to rookie Fernando Mendoza by trading Cousins back to the franchise he had the most success with, the Vikings. Cousins' 20 TD passes through nine games is second in the NFL behind Joe Burrow's 23, and he's fifth in passing yards. Given his familiarity with Kevin O'Connell's offense, he should immediately step in as the starter for Minnesota in Week 10 against a Packers defense that ranks eighth in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Kirk Cousins will take the reins again as the Vikings take on the 49ers in Week 11. Cousins shone in his Week 10 return to Minnesota, completing 68 percent of passes for 207 yards with a 2:1 TD:INT. The veteran will look to regain his form even more with his old squad this week ahead of what could be a tough matchup in Mexico City. The 49ers have ranked 14th in fantasy points allowed to QBs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Kirk Cousins will look to bounce back in Week 12 as the Vikings play the Falcons. Cousins struggled against the 49ers for the second time this season, throwing for 235 yards with zero touchdowns and one interception in a Week 11 loss. With that being said, the veteran has played just two games with Minnesota this season, so he's still getting situated in his reunion. He'll face an Atlanta defense that's ranked 26th in fantasy points allowed to QBs this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Cousins signed with the Raiders and will work as the team's starter to open the 2026 season ahead of No. 1 overall draft selection Fernando Mendoza. Cousins made eight starts for Atlanta last season and was not much of a fantasy option, averaging 12.5 fantasy points per game while reaching 18 points only once. The 38-year-old will be a bridge starter at best until Mendoza is ready and is no longer a threat with his legs (7 yards on 14 carries last season). He won't be a fantasy option, even when on the field. He should only be drafted late in superflex leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chase McLaughlin will look to remain perfect in the Buccaneers' Week 2 matchup against the Browns. McLaughlin made all five of his kicks during last week's loss, including a 51-yard field goal. With the Browns defense allowing 34 total points and 10 kicking points in a Week 1 loss, McLaughlin is likely in for lots more scoring opportunities in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chase McLaughlin could remain one of the top kickers in fantasy despite the Buccaneers' tough Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. McLaughlin remained perfect in the Week 2 loss to the Browns, as he's now converted on all six field-goal tries this season, including two from 50-plus yards. Despite McLaughlin being tied for the league-lead in field-goals made this season, he could struggle against a Minnesota defense that's allowed just 6.5 kicking points per game thus far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chase McLaughlin is expected to remain one of fantasy's top kickers in the Buccaneers' Week 4 matchup against the Packers. McLaughlin remained perfect in the Week 3 loss to the Vikings, converting on all four of his kicks, including a 54-yard field goal. He's now made all nine of his field-goal tries and all five point-after attempts through three weeks. If Baker Mayfield (thumb) were to miss the Week 4 contest, McLaughlin may have fewer scoring opportunities. However, he's still in for a relatively favorable matchup with the Packers allowing 7.0 kicking points per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chase McLaughlin is expected to have plenty of scoring opportunities in the Buccaneers' Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. McLaughlin didn't attempt a field goal in the Week 4 loss to the Packers but made both of his point-after attempts. On the season, he's converted on all nine of his field-goal tries, including three from beyond 50 yards. McLaughlin could get fewer kicking chances with Jalon Daniels starting at quarterback for the injured Baker Mayfield (thumb), but the Cowboys remain a favorable matchup, allowing 8.5 kicking points per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chase McLaughlin will look to stay hot in the Buccaneers' Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. McLaughlin impressed during the Week 5 win over the Cowboys, converting on his lone field-goal try and all three point-after attempts. He remains perfect on the season, making all 20 of his kicks this season (10 field goals and 10 extra points). He could have plenty of scoring chances against a Steelers defense that's given up 9.8 kicking points per game this season, tied for the most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chase McLaughlin is expected to remain one of fantasy's top kickers in the Buccaneers' Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. McLaughlin had an impressive showing in the Week 6 overtime loss to the Buccaneers, converting on all four of his field-goal tries, including three from 40-plus yards. The veteran kicker is perfect on the season, making 14 field goals and 11 extra points. He'll likely have multiple scoring opportunities in Week 7, as the Panthers defense has allowed 7.4 kicking points per game this year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Chase McLaughlin could have few scoring opportunities in the Buccaneers' Week 8 matchup against the Falcons. McLaughlin converted on all seven of his kicks in the Week 7 win over the Panthers, making two field goals and five extra points. On the season, McLaughlin has been perfect, making all 16 of his field-goal tries and all 16 of his point-after attempts. Despite this, McLaughlin could struggle against a solid Falcons defense that's allowed just 6.4 kicking points per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Chase McLaughlin is expected to remain one of fantasy's top kickers in the Buccaneers' Week 9 matchup against the Bears. He made all three of his field goal attempts despite the heavy rain in the Week 8 win over the Falcons. On the season, he's converted all 19 of his field goal tries and all 17 of his point-after attempts. Despite his incredible season, McLaughlin is in for a tough Week 9 matchup against a Bears defense that's allowed just 5.0 kicking points per game through seven weeks this year.
outlooksByWeek.11: Chase McLaughlin could have limited scoring opportunities in the Buccaneers' Week 11 matchup against the Lions. McLaughlin has been one of fantasy's top kickers through nine games this season, converting on all 22 of his field-goal tries and all 18 of his point-after attempts. Despite this, he could have few scoring chances in Week 11 against a Detroit defense that's given up just 5.3 kicking points per game on the season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Chase McLaughlin could receive few scoring chances during Tampa Bay's Week 12 matchup against the Panthers. McLaughlin didn't attempt a field goal during the Week 11 loss to the Lions but converted on all three of his extra points. On the season, the veteran has been perfect, making all 22 of his field-goal tries and all 21 of his point-after attempts. Despite his impressive season, Carolina has held opponents to just 7.1 kicking points per game, making this an unfavorable matchup for McLaughlin.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Higbee remains in a crowded Rams tight-end corps heading into a Week 2 matchup versus the Giants. Though Higbee led Los Angeles TEs with two catches in a Week 1 loss to San Francisco, he logged only 12 offensive snaps -- fourth-most among the group. The Rams frequently use three-TE sets, so Higbee figures to be involved in some capacity each week, but he could have a hard time carving out consistent production if he remains at the bottom of the pecking order in terms of playing time. The Giants held a trio of Cowboys tight ends to five catches for 32 yards in a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Higbee may be in line for an upgraded role for the Rams in Week 4 versus Philadelphia. After falling below a 30% offensive snap share each of the first two weeks and producing just two catches for 12 yards, Higbee exploded for an 8-62-1 receiving line on 11 targets and a 71% percent offensive snap share in Week 3 against Denver. That was partly due to fellow tight ends Terrance Ferguson (ankle) and Colby Parkinson (shoulder) getting hurt, and at least Ferguson (and possibly Parkinson) is expected to be sidelined for Week 4. However, the Eagles have been stingy versus tight ends so far, yielding only 89 receiving yards and no touchdowns to the position through three weeks.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Higbee may have worked his way back up to the Rams' No. 1 tight-end role with a Week 5 matchup against Buffalo on tap. After logging just two catches over the first two weeks of the season, Higbee has tallied a 13-129-1 line over the past two weeks. He's led Los Angeles tight ends in offensive snaps in each of those contests, with injuries to Colby Parkinson (shoulder) and Terrance Ferguson (ankle - IR) contributing to the uptick in playing time. Buffalo has given up just one touchdown to tight ends so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Higbee has become a key target for Rams QB Matthew Stafford ahead of a Week 6 battle against Arizona. Higbee recorded a season-high 83 receiving yards on five catches while drawing six targets Monday versus Buffalo. After beginning the campaign with just two catches for 12 yards over his first two contests, Higbee has posted no less than five receptions and 62 yards each of the past three weeks. He could find more success against the Cardinals, who have surrendered a league-worst 9.81 yards per target to tight ends on the season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyler Higbee has emerged as the Rams' most productive receiving tight end, catching 24 passes for 246 yards and a touchdown through six games. Even though he delivered a subpar showing in Week 6 against the Cardinals, finishing with four catches for 22 yards, he's clearly ahead of Colby Parkinson in the pecking order in the passing game. With Davante Adams (hamstring) sidelined for the time being, Higbee should be one of the players in line for an uptick in targets and touches. The Week 7 matchup against the Raiders is favorable on paper, as Las Vegas has allowed the sixth-most fantasy points per game to TEs in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tyler Higbee continues to work in an unpredictable Rams tight-end timeshare ahead of a Week 8 matchup against the Chargers. While Matthew Stafford targeted tight ends 14 times in Sunday's win over Las Vegas, Higbee got just three of those looks and put up a meager 2-14-0 line. Meanwhile, fellow TEs Colby Parkinson (5-48-0) and Davis Allen (4-20-2) had bigger performances. Wideout Davante Adams (hamstring) is expected to miss several weeks, so Stafford will likely continue to look to his tight ends often, but it's anyone's guess which of the trio will be the top performer on a week-to-week basis. The Chargers have been relatively stingy against tight ends, giving up 6.8 fantasy points per game, tied for 10th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Tyler Higbee will look to snap a recent downturn in production when the Rams take on the Commanders in Week 9. After logging at least five catches and at least 62 yards in three straight games Weeks 3-5, Higbee has topped out at four receptions and 22 yards over his past three contests. The problem hasn't been opportunity -- in fact, Higbee's offensive snap share has actually increased during the more recent three-game span. He could rediscover success against a Washington defense that has given up the second-most fantasy points per game (14.4) to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Tyler Higbee may need to ramp up his production for the Rams' passing game to be successful, beginning with a Week 10 matchup in Arizona. Higbee continued his recent trend of limited production this past Sunday against Washington, logging just one catch for 13 yards on five targets. He's recorded two or fewer receptions in three straight games, but Los Angeles may need Higbee to be more impactful after losing star WR Puka Nacua for what is likely to be multiple weeks due to a knee injury. The Cardinals rank 27th in the NFL with 10.4 fantasy points per game allowed to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Tyler Higbee could be an important part of the Rams' passing game against the Packers in Week 12. Higbee hasn't exceeded 17 receiving yards in his past four games, but he did catch a touchdown in his most recent appearance, Week 10 against Arizona. The Rams continue to be without star wideouts Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring), so it's been all-hands-on-deck for the team's pass catchers. However, Green Bay has been tough on tight ends this season, giving up just 5.9 fantasy points per game -- fifth-best in the league -- to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Higbee re-signed with the Rams and will battle for work with the likes of Colby Parkinson, Davis Allen, Terrance Ferguson and rookie Max Klare. The 2016 fourth-round pick has a pair of top-10 fantasy campaigns in his career, but the last one came in 2022 and he's finished 24th or worse in three consecutive seasons. Injuries have been part of the issue (21 missed games over the last two seasons), but so has a lesser role and minimal goal-line work (seven touchdowns and four end zone targets over the last three years). Now 33 years old, Higbee is likely third in line for targets at his position on his own team and, thus, nowhere close to fantasy relevance.

outlooksByWeek.2: Makai Lemon was listed as the No. 3 wideout for the Eagles heading into their Week 1 clash with Washington. Unfortunately, Lemon lost five yards on three catches in his NFL debut.  On the bright side, he was targeted four times and was one of only three Eagles receivers to record a catch. Better outputs lie ahead, perhaps as early as Week 2 versus Tennessee.  The Titans surrendered 215 yards passing to Geno Smith of the Jets in their opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Makai Lemon had just one catch in Philadelphia's win over Tennessee. Lemon is battling with Darius Cooper for the No. 3 wideout spot, as Dontayvion Wicks has all but claimed No. 2 for his own. Lemon had just one target last game, while Cooper had three and Wicks managed six. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Makai Lemon is coming off his best game as a member of the Eagles.  Unfortunately, the output was rather pedestrian, as Lemon managed three catches and 29 yards on four targets in the ugly 27-7 loss to the Bears. Lemon has yet to find the end zone as a rookie. In Week 4, he will face a rather stingy Rams pass defense allowing just 171.3 yards per game through the air, which is fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Makai Lemon saw a career-high six targets last game for the Eagles. With DeVonta Smith shelved due to a hamstring ailment, Lemon finished with the second-most targets on the team behind Darius Cooper.  However, the Philadelphia passing game struggled mightily overall, with no wideout gaining more than 33 yards through the air. While Smith should remain sidelined for Week 5, it remains to be seen how the targets will be divided between Lemon, Cooper and Dontayvion Wicks. Nevertheless, an intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 against the Jags. Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Makai Lemon set career highs across the board last game for the Eagles. Lemon was targeted seven times en route to five catches for 43 yards in the 19-17 loss to the Jags. Lemon has 13 targets in his last two outings. The continued absence of DeVonta Smith with a hamstring injury has boosted the opportunities for Lemon, a trend that could continue in Week 6 versus Carolina. In addition, the Panthers are allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Makai Lemon caught three passes for 19 yards last game for the Eagles. Lemon was third on the team in targets with six, though the return of DeVonta Smith to the lineup may have limited his production overall. Tanner McKee should start at quarterback for the foreseeable future, which could cap Lemon's upside as well.  In Week 7, the Eagles will face a Dallas defense that has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. The Cowboys are allowing 232.7 passing yards per game, which is 23rd in the NFL. In addition, Dallas has surrendered 11 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 24th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Makai Lemon set career highs across the board last game for the Eagles. With both DeVonta Smith as well as Dontayvion Wicks sidelined due to injury, Lemon snagged seven passes for 67 yards and his first NFL touchdown. He was targeted eight times in the contest. If Smith and/or Wicks are unable to suit up in Week 8 versus the Commanders, Lemon could have a delicious matchup, even with backup quarterback Tanner McKee under center. Washington is allowing 254 passing yards per game, which is 28th in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders have surrendered 15 passing scores, which is tied for 28th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.11: Makai Lemon has been the top target for the Eagles of late due to several injuries, though that could change following the bye. Lemon has at least eight targets in three-straight contests, but DeVonta Smith and/or Dontayvion Wicks could return from the shelf in Week 11 versus the Steelers. While Lemon should still remain involved, his opportunities could decrease despite the favorable matchup with the Steelers. Pittsburgh is allowing 242.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 30th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: Makai Lemon had a quiet output for the Eagles with the return of DeVonta Smith. While Smith managed a healthy 12 targets in the 19-16 win over the Steelers, Lemon had just three looks for the game. Lemon finished with just one reception for three yards.  Brighter days could be ahead for Lemon, though, as the Eagles face a porous Dallas Cowboys defense in Week 12. Dallas is allowing 237.9 passing yards per tilt, which is 28th in the league. "America's Team" has also given up 21 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 29th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Lemon was selected by the Eagles with the 20th overall pick of April's draft. Lemon is on the small side (5-foot-11, 192 pounds), but he posted a 3.04 YPRR (best in this rookie class) during his collegiate career, dropping only three of 190 career targets (his 1.6% drop rate also paced this class). Lemon, who aligned in the slot on 74% of his collegiate routes, posted a dominant 79-1,156-11 receiving line in 2025, while also contributing as a rusher (two TDs) and returner. With A.J. Brown now in New England, Lemon will battle Dontayvion Wicks for No. 2 work opposite DeVonta Smith. Lemon's skill set provides him with upside, but with plenty of mouths to feed in Philly's low-volume pass offense, he's best valued as a flex option in 2026.

A middling, matchups-driven D/ST last season, the Buccaneers saw much change among their linebacker corps during the offseason. Lavonte David retired, and the team drafted Rueben Bain Jr. 15th overall and signed Alex Anzalone and Christian Rozeboom. Take a wait-and-see approach to how the new personnel jells, especially since the Buccaneers get a tough opening matchup in a road game against the Bengals.

outlooksByWeek.6: Zach Charbonnet continues to rehab from a torn ACL and isn't expected to play in Seattle's Week 6 matchup in Denver. Charbonnet did have his 21-day practice window opened last week, and he got in a couple limited practice sessions, but the fact that the Seahawks are playing on Thursday night this week complicates his outlook for a return to action. As such, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani are slated to lead Seattle's RB corps again. Charbonnet does have a chance to make his 2026 debut in Week 7 against Kansas City.
outlooksByWeek.7: Zach Charbonnet (knee) and the Seahawks welcome the Chiefs to town for Sunday Night Football in Week 7. He's been on the physically unable to perform (PUP)/reserve list to begin 2026, but Seattle opened his three-week practice window back on Oct. 1. With that being said, Charbonnet will need to be activated by Thursday in order to avoid him being out for the rest of the season. He's expected to join the official roster after practicing in a limited fashion the last couple weeks. However, Charbonnet will likely be eased into the backfield rotation if he is indeed able to make his debut, so it would be wise to wait until after the meeting with Kansas City's defense that's tied for ninth in fantasy points allowed per game (19.0) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Zach Charbonnet (knee) has a chance to return to Seattle's backfield in Week 8 against Chicago. Charbonnet has yet to play since tearing his ACL in January, but he was activated off the reserve/PUP list last week and logged a trio of full practices. Though he ultimately didn't play Sunday against Kansas City, another week of practice could be enough for Charbonnet to make his return Monday against the Bears. Should that happen, he'll face a Chicago defense that has given up five total touchdowns (three rushing, two receiving) to running backs through seven games.
outlooksByWeek.9: Zach Charbonnet will look to build upon an uneventful season debut when the Seahawks host the Cardinals in Week 9. Charbonnet logged his first game action since January this past Monday against Chicago and finished with 23 yards on six carries along with six yards on three catches. He shared the backfield primarily with Jadarian Price (12 touches), and that arrangement may cap both players' weekly production moving forward. Arizona does present a decent matchup, as the Cardinals are tied for 20th in the NFL with 18.2 fantasy points per game allowed to running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Zach Charbonnet seems to be emerging as Seattle's No. 1 running back heading into a Week 10 tilt against the Raiders. In his second game back from ACL surgery, Charbonnet led the Seahawks with 16 carries and 77 receiving yards against Arizona this past Sunday while adding one catch for nine yards. Rookie Jadarian Price still managed 13 touches, so Charbonnet doesn't seem likely to have the backfield all to himself. Both tailbacks could thrive against a Las Vegas defense that has allowed a league-worst 5.21 yards per carry to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Zach Charbonnet appears to have seized the lead-RB role for Seattle heading into a Week 12 matchup against the 49ers. Charbonnet didn't debut until Week 8 against Chicago and had just nine touches in that game, but in his most recent appearance -- Week 10 versus Las Vegas -- he carried 20 times for 94 yards while logging a season-high 72% offensive snap share. Jadarian Price should continue to factor into the backfield mix as well, but there's a good chance that Charbonnet will be the leader of the team's backfield moving forward. He'll face a tough test against the 49ers, who have given up the fourth-fewest fantasy points per game (14.0) to running backs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Charbonnet would've been entering his fourth NFL season as the clear lead back in Seattle, but a torn ACL during the team's playoff game against the 49ers has put his 2026 campaign in jeopardy. It's a tough break for the 2020 second-round NFL draft pick, who set career-high marks in touches (204) while ranking fifth among backs in rushing touchdowns (12) and carries inside the 5-yard line (16) last season. Charbonnet's minimal receiving role (career-low 24 targets) limited him to 11.3 fantasy points per game, however, and he has yet to deliver a top-20 fantasy campaign. Kenneth Walker III is gone, but first-round rookie Jadarian Price could very well cement himself a big offensive role by the time Charbonnet is healthy. The 25-year-old is worth only a late-round lottery ticket.

outlooksByWeek.2: Drake London looks poised to bounce back from a tough Week 1 in the Falcons' Week 2 matchup against the Panthers. Carolina's defense just allowed a whopping 59 points to the Bears in Week 1, giving up 42.2 PPR fantasy points to wide receivers. London's rebound could depend on the quarterback play, as Michael Penix (knee) and Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) are both questionable for Sunday's contest. However, with Carolina's defensive struggles during Week 1, London should be in for a fantastic matchup.
outlooksByWeek.3: Drake London will look to bounce back from a slow start in the Falcons' Week 3 matchup against the Packers. London has caught just six of nine targets for 80 yards in Atlanta's first two games, as Cooper Rush and Jack Strand struggled to get the offense going. However, Michael Penix is set to return as the Falcons' QB1 during the Week 3 contest, giving London a far more optimistic projection. He's in for a favorable matchup as well, with Green Bay's defense allowing three receiving touchdowns and 34.5 PPR fantasy points per game to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Drake London will look to stay hot in the Falcons' Week 4 matchup against the Saints. With Michael Penix returning from injury in the Week 3 win over the Packers, London had one of the best performances of his career, catching nine of 10 targets for 194 yards. With Penix on the field, London has averaged 6.7 receptions, 98.7 receiving yards and 0.6 touchdowns per game, suggesting he'll remain one of fantasy's top wideouts as long as Penix remains healthy. Despite this, London is in for a tough Week 4 matchup against a Saints secondary that's given up 29.0 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Drake London is expected to remain the Falcons' top wideout in the Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. London has excelled since the return of Michael Penix in Week 3, catching 14 of 16 targets for 290 yards across his last two contests. With Penix at the helm, London has averaged a whopping 6.6 receptions and 98.5 yards per game, suggesting that he'll remain one of fantasy's top wideouts as the season progresses. Additionally, London is in for a terrific matchup against a Ravens secondary that's allowed 37.9 fantasy points per game to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Drake London will likely remain the Falcons' top pass catcher in the Week 6 matchup against the Bears. London impressed in the Week 5 loss despite not finding the end zone, totaling 118 yards on seven receptions. He's been one of fantasy's top wideouts since Michael Penix (ribs) returned in Week 3, averaging seven receptions and 136 yards per game across three contests. As long as Penix is healthy for the Week 6 contest, London should have another fantastic opportunity to put up big numbers against a Bears defense that's given up 32.0 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.7: Drake London is expected to remain the Falcons' top wideout in the Week 7 matchup against the 49ers. Despite logging double-digit targets for the third time in his last four games, London recorded just four receptions and 62 yards in the Week 6 loss to the Bears. Since Michael Penix returned from injury in the Week 3 win over the Packers, London has averaged 9.3 targets, 6.3 receptions and 117.5 yards per game, making him one of fantasy's most productive receivers. Even so, London could struggle against a tough 49ers defense in Week 7 that's given up just 28.1 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts through five games this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Drake London is expected to remain one of fantasy's top wideouts in the Falcons' Week 8 matchup against the Buccaneers. London paced Atlanta's pass catchers in the Week 7 win over the 49ers, catching seven of nine targets for 66 yards and a score. Since quarterback Michael Penix returned from injury in the Week 3 win over the Packers, London has averaged a whopping 6.4 receptions and 107.2 yards per game, making him one of the league's most productive WRs. He's in for a tough matchup in Week 8, however, as Tampa Bay's secondary has allowed just 29.6 fantasy points per game to the position this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Drake London will look to bounce back from a tough Week 8 performance when the Falcons plays the Bengals in Week 9. London struggled along with the rest of Atlanta's offense in a rainy loss to the Buccaneers, catching just one of six targets for eight yards. However, he's still been one of the NFL's most productive receivers with Michael Penix at quarterback this year, averaging 5.5 receptions and 90.7 receiving yards per game. London will have a good opportunity to rebound against a Cincinnati secondary that's allowed 33.1 fantasy points per game to opposing wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Drake London is expected to remain the Falcons' top pass catcher during the Week 10 matchup against the Chiefs. London has cooled down after a terrific stretch of games from Weeks 3 through 5, averaging just 4.3 receptions and 52.8 receiving yards per game over Atlanta's last four contests. He's also averaging just 7.6 targets per game this season, his lowest mark since 2023, so it appears the Falcons are struggling to get him involved. Additionally, London is in for a difficult Week 10 matchup against a Chiefs secondary that's allowed just 23.5 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this year.
outlooksByWeek.12: Drake London is expected to remain the Falcons' top wideout during the Week 12 matchup against the Vikings. Prior to Atlanta's Week 11 bye, London had one of his best performances of the 2026 season, catching six of 12 targets for 109 yards. With Michael Penix at quarterback this year, London has averaged 5.5 receptions and 90.1 receiving yards per game, making him one of the league's most productive receivers. Despite this, London could definitely struggle against the Vikings in Week 12, as they have allowed just 27.8 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this year.

player.seasonOutlook: London enters his fifth NFL season with eyes on finishing in the top 15 in fantasy points per game for the third season in a row. The 2022 first-round pick broke out with a 100-1,271-9 receiving line and a fifth-place finish in fantasy points (14th PPG) in 2024. Last season, he missed five games and fell to 19th in fantasy points, but he was actually better on a per-game basis (seventh) and was the top scorer among receivers three times between Weeks 6 and 10. London remains heavily targeted (career 28% share) and sees plenty of work near the goal line (25 end zone targets over the past two seasons). As long as one of Tua Tagovailoa or Michael Penix Jr. can play somewhat competent ball, the 25-year-old London shouldn't have trouble providing fringe-WR1 fantasy production.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ashton Jeanty looked like a franchise back in the Raiders' season-opening win over the Dolphins, turning 29 touches into 147 scrimmage yards and two receiving touchdowns. The ankle injury that limited him in training camp and the preseason was no longer an issue, and the second-year RB dominated the workload, as rookie backup Mike Washington notched only seven carries. Jeanty's pass-catching role could be cut back once star tight end Brock Bowers is cleared to return, but he will remain a focal point of the offense heading into a Week 2 clash with a Chargers defense that ranked second in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ashton Jeanty has looked the part of a bell-cow running back to begin his second NFL season, amassing 54 touches through two games and turning them into 210 scrimmage yards and two receiving touchdowns. The 2025 first-round pick is still only averaging 3.4 yards per carry however, and the Raiders' offseason upgrades to the offensive line haven't yet led to better efficiency on the ground for Jeanty. He'll try to take advantage of a Week 3 clash with a Saints defense that ranks in the bottom four in rushing yards and rushing TDs allowed to RBs so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ashton Jeanty continues to garner a big workload for the Raiders, but he isn't yet consistently producing big numbers. Through three games, the second-year back is tied for third in the NFL in touches with 76, behind only Jahmyr Gibbs and Bijan Robinson, but Jeanty's averaging just 3.3 yards per carry and his 303 scrimmage yards are only 14th in the league. He also has yet to score a rushing touchdown in 2026, although he did haul in two TD catches in Week 1. Jeanty will try to improve his efficiency in Week 4 against a Kansas City defense that ranks 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ashton Jeanty continues to bolster his lackluster rushing numbers with big production through the air. In the Raiders' Week 4 loss to Kansas City, the second-year RB managed just 58 rushing yards on 15 carries, but he added six catches for 68 yards on a season-high eight targets. Jeanty's 3.4 yards per carry and zero TDs on the ground through four weeks are a concern, but his 19-165-2 line on 24 targets softens the blow. He'll take on a Patriots defense in Week 5 that ranks 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Ashton Jeanty continues to keep his production afloat via his skills as a pass-catcher. The second-year running back is averaging just 3.3 yards per carry after another poor showing on the ground in the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots, but he's supplied a 22-215-2 line on 30 targets through five games. The 30 targets are third in the league among RBs, behind the Lions' Jahmyr Gibbs and the Rams' Kyren Williams, while Jeanty's receiving yards are third behind Gibbs and the Steelers' Jaylen Warren. Jeanty will try to deliver a more well-rounded line in Week 6 against a Bills defense that ranks 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs and 31st in receiving TDs allowed to the position.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ashton Jeanty scored his first rushing touchdown of the season in the Raiders' Week 6 loss to the Bills, but it was otherwise another lackluster performance for the second-year running back. Jeanty is averaging just 3.2 yards per carry, and the inefficiency is costing him volume, as he hasn't handled 20-plus touches in a game since Week 4. He remains involved as a pass catcher, however, hauling in at least three passes in every game this year while compiling a 26-251-2 line on 36 targets through six contests. Jeanty could contribute through the air in Week 7 against a Rams defense that ranks 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs, but 29th in receiving yards per game allowed to the position.
outlooksByWeek.8: Ashton Jeanty continues to struggle on the ground while making an impact as a pass catcher. In the Raiders' Week 7 loss to the Rams, the second-year player gained a season-low 15 rushing yards on eight carries, but caught all eight of his targets for 61 yards and a touchdown. Jeanty has gotten at least six targets in six of seven games so far in 2026, turning that volume into a 34-312-3 line on 44 looks. but his 3.1 yards per carry suggests he simply isn't cut out to be a No. 1 back. He'll try to bring some balance to his stat line in Week 8 against a Jets defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Ashton Jeanty is coming off another poor effort, managing just 20 scrimmage yards on 11 touches in the Raiders' Week 9 loss to the 49ers. This time, he wasn't overshadowed by rookie Mike Washington, who lost a total of three yards on his six carries. Jeanty maintains a shaky hold on the top spot in the backfield, but he hasn't reached 30 rushing yards in a game since Week 4, and his contributions of late have been limited to his usage as a pass-catcher. Jeanty isn't likely to turn things around in Week 10 against a Seahawks defense that ranks 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Ashton Jeanty failed to generate much production in the Raiders' Week 10 loss to the Seahawks, gaining 18 rushing yards on nine carries and catching all four of his targets for 46 yards. It's the sixth time in the last seven games he's generated more yards through the air than on the ground, but his hold on the No. 1 job in the backfield may have tightened a bit with Mike Washington struggling over the last two weeks as well. Jeanty's outlook as a pass-catcher could improve if Brock Bowers misses time due to an ankle injury. During the two games the star tight end sat out at the beginning of the season, Jeanty caught 10 of 13 targets for 60 yards and two touchdowns. He'll try to break out in Week 11 against a Broncos defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Ashton Jeanty finally had a breakout performance in the Raiders' Week 11 loss to the Broncos. The second-year running back gained 79 yards on the ground on just 11 carries, while adding a 5-90-1 line on eight targets. With the Las Vegas offense looking like it will stay effective with rookie Fernando Mendoza at quarterback, Jeanty should get more opportunities to establish himself as a three-down threat, but his primary strength still appears to be as a pass catcher, and he leads all RBs this season in targets, catches and receiving yards. In Week 12, Jeanty will take aim at a Browns defense that has been among the stingiest in the NFL in receiving production allowed to backs, but which ranks 12th in fantasy points per game allowed to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Jeanty is eyeing a leap forward in his second NFL season after an uneven rookie campaign in which the first-round pick enjoyed a ton of volume (seventh among backs in carries, targets and receptions) and played fairly well (eighth among RBs in forced missed tackle rate, per PFF) but struggled to overcome the shaky Las Vegas offense. The good news is that the Raiders' offense should improve in 2026 with a better/healthier offensive line, a new coach in Super Bowl champion Klint Kubiak and a new quarterback in projected No. 1 NFL draft pick Fernando Mendoza. Jeanty has a clean path to a massive offensive role and is a strong bet for a leap forward. The 22-year-old is a midrange RB1 with elite upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rashee Rice took advantage of his limited volume in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, catching both his targets for 19 yards and a touchdown. Patrick Mahomes didn't have to throw much, as Kenneth Walker had a career-best day on the ground and the team had a comfortable lead in the second half. Better performances should be ahead for Rice in more favorable game scripts, but returning offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy could also be planning to lean on his running game more heavily than in years past. Rice will look to follow in Zay Flowers' footsteps in Week 2 against a Colts secondary that ranked 30th in points per game allowed to WRs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rashee Rice's volume ticked up in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, posting a 4-83-0 line on six targets. Xavier Worthy has been getting more looks from Patrick Mahomes, and Rice's targets have mainly come very close to the line of scrimmage. He's got the run-after-catch ability to turn those short receptions into big gains, but he may not be a high-volume option in an offense that has prioritized Kenneth Walker and the running game. Rice will face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's given up five passing TDs through two games, but only one to a wide receiver.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rashee Rice hasn't yet put together a breakout game for Kansas City in 2026. The fourth-year wide receiver has a solid 13-190-1 line on 17 targets through three weeks, but Patrick Mahomes hasn't focused on any one pass catcher and has been spreading the ball around effectively. Rice, Travis Kelce, Xavier Worthy, and Kenneth Walker all have between 15 and 18 targets. Rice could have a hard time improving on his numbers in Week 4 against a Raiders secondary that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs and has yet to allow a TD to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rashee Rice picked up a minor hamstring strain and was limited to just six snaps in Kansas City's Week 4 win over the Raiders, but coming out of a Week 5 bye, the issue may not cost him any further time. In his first three games of the season, Rice produced a 13-190-1 line on 15 targets, and his volume could increase with speedster Tyquan Thornton out due to an ankle injury that could sideline him for the remainder of the year. Rice could pop for big numbers in Week 6 against a Chargers secondary that ranks 16th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Rashee Rice wasn't able to get healthy over Kansas City's Week 5 bye, and the wide receiver sat out a Week 6 win over the Chargers due to knee and hamstring issues. His absence didn't significantly affect the offense as Kenneth Walker dominated against the Chargers. In his three full games this season, Rice has produced a 13-190-1 line on 17 targets. If he's able to return in Week 7, he'll have a tough matchup against a Seahawks secondary that ranks third in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Rashee Rice continues to work his way back from a hamstring strain, missing his second straight game in Kansas City's Week 7 loss to the Seahawks. Before getting injured in Week 4, Rice had produced an 11-171-0 line on 15 targets over the prior two games. Once he's cleared to return, he should immediately be Patrick Mahomes' top option in the passing game. If Rice does get back in the lineup in Week 8, he'll be facing a Broncos secondary that could once again be without Pat Surtain but still ranks sixth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Rashee Rice returned in Week 8 from a two-game absence due to a hamstring issue and caught his second touchdown of the season in Kansas City's loss to the Broncos. In four full games this season, Rice has managed a 20-243-2 line on 25 targets as Patrick Mahomes' top downfield option, but he has yet to receive double-digit targets in any game. That's a volume he reached four times in eight contests in 2025. Rice will look to put the injury further behind him in Week 9 against a Jets secondary that ranks 10th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Rashee Rice put together another quiet performance in Kansas City's Week 9 win over the Jets, catching five of seven passes for 49 yards. The fourth-year wide receiver has a 12-102-1 line on 15 targets over the last two weeks since returning from a two-game absence due to lower-body injuries, and his breakout potential could be limited even further if Patrick Mahomes misses any time after picking up an elbow injury against the Jets. Rice will try to make a bigger contribution in Week 10 against a Falcons secondary that just traded away safety Jessie Bates and ranks 19th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Rashee Rice's role and volume did not change much in Week 10 against the Falcons, even with trade deadline acquisition Josh Downs in the lineup for Kansas City. Rice caught five of six targets for 82 yards, the third time in seven games he's recorded at least 80 receiving yards. The fourth-year wide receiver is the top downfield option for Patrick Mahomes, but his 30-374-2 line on 38 targets is far from elite production. Rice will look to take a step forward in Week 11 against a Cardinals secondary that ranks 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Rashee Rice continues to handle a steady role in the Kansas City passing attack. Over four games since returning from a hamstring injury, the fourth-year wide receiver has caught at least five passes each time out, producing a 23-237-1 line on 27 targets. Patrick Mahomes appears to be back in peak form, but that hasn't yet translated into a ceiling game for Rice, who has yet to haul in more than 88 yards in any game this year and has only two touchdowns in eight appearances. Rice will look to break out in Week 12 against a Bills secondary that's tied for 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Rice enters Year 4 of his career still seeking his first full season as a starter. The 2023 second-round pick was sidelined for most of 2024 due to injury and missed nine games last season due to suspension (Weeks 1-6) and injury (Weeks 16-18). The good news is that Rice remained highly productive when active. He handled 9.8 targets per game and was a top-12 fantasy receiver in five of his eight outings in 2025. Rice is Patrick Mahomes' top target, and his 8.0 RAC is tops among qualified receivers over the past three seasons. With Mahomes (ACL recovery) ready to go in Week 1 as expected, Rice finds himself in the WR1 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Warren salvaged his fantasy day in the Colts' season-opening loss with a nine-yard touchdown catch in the fourth quarter, but he had only four receiving yards across the rest of the game. The 2025 first-round pick has just 213 receiving yards in his last eight games after recording 617 yards in his first 10 outings. Warren did enough in Week 1 to warrant another fantasy start in most formats for a Week 2 road game against the Chiefs, but his lack of yards since the halfway point of his rookie season is becoming a worrying trend.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Warren has started his second NFL season on a two-game TD streak but has a meager 34 receiving yards on 12 targets. The Colts' 2025 first-round pick is poised to keep logging plenty of targets in Week 3 against the Texans, as Indianapolis is running out of NFL-caliber pass catchers in the absence of Alec Pierce (heel). Warren had six catches in the Week 2 loss to Kansas City, a game Pierce exited early. Given Warren's mix of talent and usage, he remains a top-10 fantasy TE in Week 3 against Houston's talented defense.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Warren has increased his catch total by three with each subsequent game this season, and he has scored in two of the Colts' three games heading into a Week 4 international game against the Commanders in London. Coming off a nine-catch game, Warren is a set-and-forget starting fantasy TE against a Washington defense that has allowed five TDs to the position through three games. The 2025 first-round pick is a key part of a Colts passing game that's missing top WR Alec Pierce (heel), who is on injured reserve.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Warren has emerged with a consistent role as a short outlet for Colts QB Daniel Jones. Warren has caught 23 of 27 targets for 130 yards and two TDs, averaging almost six catches per game but just 5.7 yards per catch. His floor is high enough to be trusted as a weekly fantasy starter at TE, as Warren leads the Colts in catches and is one target shy of Josh Downs' team-leading total. Week 5 at Pittsburgh is no exception, even though the Steelers are tied for the fourth-fewest catches allowed to TEs with 13. Two of those 13 receptions have resulted in touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Warren had a season-high 83 receiving yards and a short rushing TD in the Colts' Week 5 loss to Pittsburgh. The versatile TE has been the team's second-best offensive player behind star RB Jonathan Taylor. Warren has accounted for three of the team's five non-Taylor touchdowns and leads the Colts with 30 catches through five games. Warren remains a set-and-forget fantasy starter in Week 6 due to his prominent involvement in the game plan every week, even against a Titans defense that has allowed the third-fewest receiving yards to TEs at 29 per game.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyler Warren sat out the Colts' Week 6 loss to the Titans after being a late addition to the injury report due to a groin injury. If the 2025 first-round pick is cleared to return in Week 7 against the Vikings, he would reclaim his role as a key cog on offense for the Colts and a borderline top-five fantasy TE. Jonathan Taylor has seven of the Colts' 13 offensive TDs this season, and Warren has scored three of the other six while averaging six receptions per game. Minnesota hasn't allowed a TE to score this season while giving up 44 receiving yards per game to the position.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tyler Warren hasn't suited up since Week 5 due to a groin injury. He leads the Colts with 30 catches despite missing the past two games, so Warren would immediately return to the fantasy starting range if he gains clearance to return in Week 8 against a Jaguars defense that has been much more vulnerable through the air than on the ground. Jacksonville is holding TEs to 35 yards per game but has allowed the position to score four times in six outings, and Warren has accounted for three of the six TDs scored by Colts other than Jonathan Taylor.
outlooksByWeek.9: Tyler Warren turned 10 targets into just 18 yards in his return from a two-game absence due to a groin injury in the Colts' 42-7 Week 8 loss to the Jaguars. That performance sums up the sorry state of Indianapolis' passing game, but Warren's volume remains elite for a TE. He's back to being a set-and-forget starting option at the position now that he's healthy, especially with a favorable Week 9 home matchup on tap against the Cowboys. Dallas' defense is allowing 51 yards per game to TEs and has given up four TDs to the position, surrendering 26.6 points per game overall.
outlooksByWeek.10: Tyler Warren has drawn at least seven targets in five of his last six appearances. The 2025 first-round pick remains a weekly fantasy starter at TE thanks to his hefty volume, even though he's averaging just 5.2 yards per target in the Colts' low-octane passing offense. Warren and the Colts will face a Dolphins defense in Week 10 that has allowed six receiving TDs in eight games to TEs. In addition to two touchdown catches, Warren has one rushing score this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Tyler Warren had a season-low three targets in a head-scratching Week 10 performance against the Dolphins after the Colts traded away starting WRs Josh Downs and Keenan Allen. Even after that dud, Warren is still averaging a healthy seven targets per game, and his 276 receiving yards and two receiving TDs lead all players still rostered by the Colts. Warren had a season-high nine catches when the Colts faced the Texans in Week 3 and should be similarly busy in the Week 11 rematch against a Houston defense that ranks among the league's 10 most generous units through the air. Don't let Warren's down game in Week 10 dissuade you from continuing to deploy him as a high-floor fantasy starter at TE.
outlooksByWeek.12: Tyler Warren has been held to just three catches in two games since the Colts traded starting WRs Josh Downs and Keenan Allen. Rather than collecting even more targets as the team's top remaining pass catcher, Warren has struggled to create separation as defenses have focused on stopping him. Warren can't sink much lower following the Colts' QB change from Daniel Jones to Anthony Richardson, even though Richardson's 15-game sample as an NFL starter suggests he's more likely to air it out deep to wide receivers or take off running than find his TE on a short or intermediate route. Week 12 against the Giants will mark the first time that Warren, a 2025 first-round pick, and Richardson, a 2023 first-round pick, start in the same game. Benching Warren is justifiable if you have a solid alternative, but leaving him in and hoping for a spark with Richardson is defensible.

player.seasonOutlook: Warren put together a solid rookie season, but it could've been even better. In 12 games with a healthy Daniel Jones, Warren scored five touchdowns and averaged 13.1 fantasy PPG. In five games without Jones, Warren fell to 6.3 PPG and failed to find the end zone. In fact, the 2025 first-round pick was unlucky in the scoring department, ranking fifth among tight ends in end zone targets (seven) and expected TDs (7.5). Warren finished the season third among tight ends in targets and also had three goal-line carries. The 24-year-old was already a featured target and might see even more work with Michael Pittman Jr. shipped to Pittsburgh. Warren is a quality TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tee Higgins and the Bengals visit the Texans for a Week 2 battle between two playoff hopefuls. He caught three of six targets for 59 yards during Cincinnati's season-opening victory. Higgins tied for second on the team in receptions and targets while finishing behind Mike Gesicki for the lead in receiving yards. He draws a favorable matchup against Houston's 26th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (41.5) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tee Higgins and the Bengals are in Pittsburgh to take on their division rivals in Week 3. He finished Week 2's win over Houston with five catches on 10 targets for 95 yards, pacing Cincinnati in yardage and targets. Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase accounted for 19 of Joe Burrow's 31 pass attempts, and that's likely to remain the case despite an unfavorable Week 3 matchup. The Steelers' defense ranks second in fantasy points allowed per game (15.5) and has yet to surrender a TD to WRs in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tee Higgins and the Bengals return home to host the 2-1 Jaguars in Week 4. He tallied six catches for 90 yards and one TD on seven targets during Cincinnati's tough 30-27 loss in Week 3. Higgins was second on the team in receptions, yardage, and targets behind Ja'Marr Chase, but he led the way with 15.0 yards per catch. He'll aim to keep rolling against a Jacksonville defense that ranks 17th in fantasy points allowed (31.5) and 27th in yards per target to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tee Higgins and the Bengals are on the road to take on Miami's third-ranked defense against wide receivers in Week 5. He erupted for 11 catches and 157 yards on 16 targets during Cincinnati's Week 4 loss. With Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) exiting in the second quarter, Joe Burrow relied heavily on Higgins, as he paced the team in yardage and targets while tying for the lead in receptions. Unfortunately for the Bengals, Higgins sustained an adductor injury in the final minutes of the game, leaving his status questionable for Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tee Higgins and the Bengals travel to Baltimore for a divisional clash in Week 7. He caught two of four targets for 22 yards during Cincinnati's 31-24 victory in Week 5. Higgins was able to battle through an adductor injury that kept him limited in practices leading up to the contest, and he has now had a bye week for some added rest. He draws a favorable matchup against a Baltimore defense allowing 34.1 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks 22nd.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tee Higgins and the Bengals return home for an AFC showdown against the Titans in Week 8. He caught six of seven targets for 148 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's 35-13 win in Week 7. Higgins tied with Ja'Marr Chase (5-62-1) in targets but paced the Bengals in receptions and yardage for the second time in three contests. Higgins will aim to keep rolling against a Titans defense allowing 35.8 fantasy points per game to WRs, which is tied for 24th.
outlooksByWeek.9: Tee Higgins and the Bengals battle the Falcons in a Week 9 interconference clash in Spain. He caught 10 of 11 targets for 155 yards and two touchdowns during Cincinnati's 43-36 overtime victory in Week 8. Higgins led the team in yardage and TDs while finishing second in both receptions and targets behind Ja'Marr Chase (11-141-1). Higgins has tallied at least 148 receiving yards in three of his last four outings, and he'll aim to stay hot against an Atlanta defense that ranks 14th in fantasy points allowed per game (30.1) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Tee Higgins and the Bengals welcome the Steelers to town for a Week 10 divisional clash. He caught five of six targets for 32 yards and two touchdowns during Cincinnati's Week 9 victory. Higgins recorded two TDs for the second consecutive game, and he now has five receiving scores over his last three outings. He'll look to keep up the pace versus a Pittsburgh defense he cooked for a 6-90-1 line on seven targets in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.11: Tee Higgins and the Bengals visit Washington on Monday Night Football in Week 11. He brought in five of six targets for 66 yards during Cincinnati's Week 10 victory, extending the team's win streak to five games. Higgins' consecutive outings with a TD snapped, however, as he failed to find the end zone for the first time since Week 5. Head coach Zac Taylor relayed Higgins' workload was being managed toward the end of the win over Pittsburgh, so keep an eye on his status in practice during Week 11 prep.
outlooksByWeek.12: Tee Higgins and the Bengals return home for an interconference clash against the Saints in Week 12. He brought in two of three targets for 43 yards, including a beautiful over-the-shoulder 31-yard touchdown, during Cincinnati's Week 11 defeat. Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase (5-31-0) were both held in check, but Higgins was able to reach the end zone for the sixth time in his last five games. He will aim to tally his first 100-yard outing since Week 8 against a New Orleans defense giving up 28.6 fantasy points per game (eighth) to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Higgins may be overshadowed by teammate Ja'Marr Chase, but that hasn't stopped the veteran receiver from playing a key role near the goal line in the Bengals' pass-friendly offense. Despite missing seven games over the past two seasons, Higgins sits eighth among receivers in end zone targets (24) and fourth in touchdowns (21) during the span. The 2020 second-round pick finished both seasons in the top 20 in fantasy points (overall and per game). Durability (he hasn't played a full season since 2020) and a limited target share are concerns here, but Higgins' combination of talent and role in a Joe Burrow-led offense are enough to allow fringe-WR2 production.
