outlooksByWeek.2: Kyle Monangai will look to be a big contributor once again for the Bears in Week 2 against the Vikings. While Monangai still took a back-seat role to D'Andre Swift in Week 1 against the Panthers, he still finished the game with 10 carries for 100 yards and a touchdown, along with 24 yards off two catches. The second-year ball carrier should still have plenty of a share in Chicago's rushing game to be fantasy relevant, especially given how much potential their offense showed for the season. Monangai will face a Minnesota defense that shelled Green Bay on the ground in their opener, but the Bears have a much superior RB room as of now.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyle Monangai should remain a high-volume RB2 as the Bears take on the Eagles in Week 3. Monangai saw double-digit carries once again in Week 2, but he totaled just 47 yards on the ground and tacked on 11 yards off two catches. The second-year running back has now seen 12 touches in each of Chicago's two outings this year, and he could see even more with Tyson Bagent slated to start under center. Philly has also ceded 216 rushing yards to RBs this season, a bottom-10 mark in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kyle Monangai should remain the complementary option in Chicago's backfield in Week 4 against the Jets. Monangai logged his third straight showing with 10 carries in Week 3 versus the Eagles, but he converted them for a season-low 31 rushing yards. The second-year running back also garnered no targets in the passing game, which came as a letdown after he posted a 4-35-0 receiving line leading up to the Monday Night win. He'll look to improve on his consistent volume against a New York defense that's allowed an eighth-most 24.1 fantasy points per game to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kyle Monangai will look to shed a questionable tag after a huge performance as the Bears play the Packers in Week 5. Monangai dominated the Jets on the ground in Week 4 with 30 rushes for 146 yards and two touchdowns, but he also injured his thumb and is currently day-to-day. The second-year ball carrier's practice availability should dictate whether he's able to play in Chicago's rivalry debut of the 2026 season. If he's active, he'll face a Green Bay defense that's ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to running backs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kyle Monangai will aim to return to the field as the Bears play the Falcons in Week 6. Monangai sat out in Week 5 with a toe injury, but he's week-to-week and not a candidate for IR. The second-year ball carrier put together a career-best 30 rushes for 146 yards and two touchdowns against the Jets in Week 4, so he could be inching towards a featured role if he can get back to the field. If he plays, Monangai will face an Atlanta defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy RBs so far.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kyle Monangai will look to make a return as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Monangai has missed back-to-back games with turf toe, and he'll need to get back to practice if he hopes to see the field in a TNF matchup. If he is active, he'll return to a favorable backfield role versus a Falcons defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy RBs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Kyle Monangai will aim to make a return as the Bears travel to Seattle in Week 8. Monangai has missed the last three games with a turf toe injury, but Chicago is not planning to place him on IR. This makes it likely the second-year running back at least has a chance to return in the upcoming away tilt. With two 100-yard rushing games and three touchdowns across the first four games of the season, Monangai is an intriguing option if he returns, even against a Seahawks defense that's ranked top 10 in fantasy points allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Kyle Monangai will look to make a return as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Monangai has sat out the last four weeks with thumb and toe issues. The second-year ball carrier recording a 30-146-2 rushing line before his inactive streak makes it even more frustrating, so he'll hopefully get back to practice sooner rather than later. If he is healthy against Tampa Bay, he'll face a defense that's ranked first in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Kyle Monangai will look to make a return as the Bears play the Saints in Week 11. Monangai has sat out five straight games as he works back from a turf-toe injury. The second-year ball carrier's status is very likely correlated with his ability to practice, so this week should reveal his expected return timeline. He accrued 324 rushing yards and three touchdowns off 60 carries in the first four games of the season. If he returns, Monangai will face a New Orleans defense that's ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Kyle Monangai will look to get more opportunities as the Bears play the Lions in Week 12. Monangai was quiet in his return from a five-game absence due to turf toe, carrying the ball eight times for just 18 yards. The second-year ball carrier could be in line for a ramped up role in the upcoming away matchup, but D'Andre Swift currently looks to have the RB1 role in his grasp. Detroit's defense has ranked fifth in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Monangai heads into his second NFL season following an impressive rookie campaign in which he quickly forced his way into a committee with D'Andre Swift. The 2025 seventh-round flier played 41% of Chicago's offensive snaps and averaged a healthy 4.6 yards per carry on 169 attempts. Monangai was limited to 7.7 fantasy PPG during the 16 weeks Swift also played, but he showed his insurance value with a 29-touch, 198-yard effort in the one game Swift was sidelined (Week 9). The 24-year-old could see a slight boost in usage this season, but that usage and production will be limited as long as Swift is also healthy.

outlooksByWeek.10: Jordyn Tyson's role in the Saints' offense is expected to continue growing during the Week 10 matchup against the Panthers. Tyson was sidelined for New Orleans' first seven games this season due to a hamstring. He was relatively underwhelming in his NFL debut, catching four of five targets for 30 yards while also losing a fumble in the Week 9 overtime win over the Browns. Despite this, Tyler Shough is tied for the league-lead in pass attempts per game (38.5) and Tyson is expected to get more involved in the Saints' offense as the season continues, so his fantasy outlook remains positive. He could find success against a depleted Carolina secondary that's given up 145.6 receiving yards per game to opposing WRs this year.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jordyn Tyson will look to build on his breakout performance in the Saints' Week 11 matchup against the Bears. Tyson was one of New Orleans' few bright spots in the Week 11 loss to the Panthers, catching 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards in his second NFL game. He's clearly established himself as one of the Saints' top two receiving options but could struggle if Chris Olave is more involved in Week 11. Tyson could thrive against a solid Bears secondary, however, as they have allowed 9.2 yards per target to opposing WRs this year.
outlooksByWeek.12: Jordyn Tyson will look to bounce back from a rough performance during the Saints' Week 12 matchup against the Bengals. After catching 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards during the Week 10 loss to the Panthers, Tyson was a non-factor in Week 11, logging one reception for six yards. He remains firmly behind Chris Olave in the team's WR corps but could still be valuable for fantasy purposes, with quarterback Tyler Shough averaging the second-most pass attempts per game (38.5) in the NFL. Tyson could struggle in Week 12, however, with Cincinnati's secondary allowing just 7.5 yards per target to opposing wideouts this year.

player.seasonOutlook: Tyson was selected by the Saints with the No. 8 overall pick of April's draft. He is a versatile receiver with decent size who led this rookie class with a 35% target share during the nine weeks he was active in 2025. Injuries cost him time during all four collegiate seasons, but he still managed a 158-2,282-22 receiving line in 33 games, posting a strong 2.73 YPRR along the way (third best in this class). Tyson suffered a hamstring injury in August and will miss a month or two of the regular season prior to taking over as the Saints' No. 2 receiver behind Chris Olave. Once healthy, Tyson has a path to a substantial role in an ascending offense led by second-year QB Tyler Shough and could find himself on the WR3 radar. Of course, with the injury, he's only worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cam Little got off to an accurate start by converting both of his field-goal attempts and all four extra points in Jacksonville's Week 1 win. He made an NFL-record 68-yard field goal last season, so there are no concerns about his leg strength. Getting into scoring range will be tougher than usual for the Jaguars in Week 2 against a Broncos defense that allowed the third-fewest points in the league last season, though 70 yards could be within Little's realistic range in the thin Denver air. Little's upside is high enough to maintain fantasy starter status, even given the tricky Week 2 matchup for Jacksonville's offense.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cam Little had a rare miss in Week 2 but has been one of the NFL's best kickers since entering the league in 2024. Through 36 games with the Jaguars, he has converted 61 of 68 field-goal attempts, including an NFL-record 68-yard field goal. He's a little riskier than usual in Week 3 against a Patriots defense that's allowing just 8.0 points per game, but Little is probably too good to bench regardless of the opponent.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cam Little narrowly missed setting an NFL record in Jacksonville's Week 3 win over the Patriots, as his 70-yard field-goal attempt squeaked just wide right. Little already holds the record for the longest made field goal in a regular-season game with a 68-yarder last season, but the powerful kicker has converted just 4-of-6 field-goal attempts in 2026 while having hit all 10 of his PAT tries. Despite Little's pedestrian start, his impressive range coupled with Jacksonville's ability to move the ball effectively give Little starter-level upside each game, and a Week 4 road matchup against a Bengals team that's allowing 21.0 points per game is no exception.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cam Little made all three of his field-goal attempts in Jacksonville's Week 4 win over the Bengals. The big-legged kicker has yet to miss from inside 50 yards and has tremendous range, as Little made an NFL-record 68-yard field goal last season and narrowly missed a 70-yard attempt this season. Little remains a viable fantasy starter as usual in Week 5 against an Eagles team that's allowing 23.3 points per game but has given up only six successful field goals through four games. This game will be played at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London, where Spencer Shrader and Drew Stevens combined to make all five of their field-goal attempts in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.6: Cam Little made both of his field-goal attempts in Jacksonville's 19-17 Week 5 win over the Eagles in London, including the game-winning 57-yarder on the game's final play. He also missed a PAT, with a bad snap contributing after the Jaguars lost long snapper Ross Matiscik to a shoulder injury in the first quarter. Snaps could again be an issue on Jacksonville's kicking attempts in Week 6, but the big-legged Little has too much upside to bench as the Jaguars play their second consecutive game in London, this time taking on a Texans team that has allowed 12 made field goals (tied for third-most in the league), and 22.0 points per game.
outlooksByWeek.8: Cam Little has started 10-for-12 on field-goal attempts with a long of 60 across Jacksonville's first six games. The big-legged kicker could be in for a busy afternoon in Week 8 at home against the Colts, who are giving up 25.7 points per game and have allowed a league-high 21 field-goal attempts, 18 of which have been successful. Little is worth snagging off waivers if he was dropped during Jacksonville's Week 7 bye, as he profiles as a top-10 kicker for Week 8 and beyond.
outlooksByWeek.9: Cam Little has attempted 23 PATs compared to just 12 field goals this season, a testament to Jacksonville's high-octane offense. His ceiling remains immense given the frequent scoring opportunities and Little's elite range, making him a viable fantasy starter for Week 9. Little will face a reeling Ravens team in Week 9 that has dropped three consecutive games while allowing at least 35 points in each of the last two. Overall, Baltimore has given up 16 made field goals in eight games while allowing 25.4 points per game.
outlooksByWeek.10: Cam Little connected on a season-high four field goals in Jacksonville's Week 9 win over the Ravens, bringing him up to 14-for-16 through eight games this season. He has attempted 10 more PATs than FGs behind Jacksonville's efficient offense, but Little should enjoy plenty of kicking opportunities in Week 10, as the Titans are surrendering 24.9 points per game while the Jaguars are scoring 28.6 points per game. Tennessee has allowed 17 successful field goals, which is tied for 10th most in the NFL, so Little is a set-and-forget fantasy starter for Week 10.
outlooksByWeek.11: Cam Little has gone 4-for-4 on field-goal attempts in each of Jacksonville's last two games, with that two-game stretch accounting for nearly half of his 18 made field goals this season. The Jaguars are consistently moving the ball into scoring range, and while they have been adept at scoring TDs rather than settling for FGs, the team's offensive prowess coupled with Little's big leg keeps Jacksonville's kicker safely in the set-and-forget starter range. In Week 11, Little will face the Giants on the road. MetLife Stadium is one of the tougher kicking environments in the NFL, and the Giants' opponents have made just nine field goals in nine games, but the surging Little has the potential to make fantasy managers who over-index on the matchup look silly given his high ceiling.
outlooksByWeek.12: Cam Little has come up big for fantasy managers recently with three consecutive 4-for-4 performances on field-goal attempts. He's in great position to keep rolling in a Week 12 home game against the Titans, who have surrendered a whopping 44.7 points per game in their last three. That woeful stretch from Tennessee's defense includes Jacksonville's 40-23 win in Week 10, during which Little converted all four of his PAT tries to go with four field goals. Little's a set-and-forget Week 12 fantasy starter.

outlooksByWeek.2: Woody Marks is set to occupy a change-of-pace role behind David Montgomery in Week 2, when the Texans host the Bengals. Marks turned 11 touches into 40 scrimmage yards in Week 1 against the Bills, while Montgomery had 79 yards and three TDs on 23 touches. Cincinnati had the worst run defense in the league last season, but Marks' modest usage makes him no better than a deep-league flex play as long as Montgomery is healthy.
outlooksByWeek.3: Woody Marks capitalized on a negative game flow in Week 2, out-touching David Montgomery 13-8. The 0-2 Texans will face a Colts team that's also 0-2 in Week 3, and Montgomery is likely to reclaim the lead role unless Houston falls into a multi-score hole again. Marks is averaging just 2.9 yards per carry and 4.2 yards per catch in 2026 after averaging a modest 3.6 yards per carry during his 2025 rookie season. He has RB3/flex upside in Week 3 against a Colts defense that's giving up 177 rushing yards per game, but Marks' uncertain role and poor efficiency this season cap his value despite the intriguing matchup.
outlooksByWeek.4: Woody Marks is the 1B option in Houston's backfield, which is enough to earn flex consideration in deeper formats for Week 4 against the Cowboys. The Cowboys are giving up 114 rushing yards per game to RBs and have surrendered four TDs to the position. Marks has 29 touches this season to David Montgomery's 44. Neither RB has found much running room behind Houston's weak offensive line, as Marks is averaging 3.0 yards per carry, while Montgomery is at 2.8 yards per carry. Marks scored his first touchdown of the season in the Week 3 loss to the Colts, while Montgomery has three TDs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Woody Marks takes a two-game touchdown streak into the Texans' Week 5 trip to Tennessee, though he has been out-touched 54-35 by David Montgomery in Houston's backfield. Marks has pulled within one touchdown of Montgomery this season, and neither running back has been efficient behind Houston's struggling offensive line, as Marks is averaging 3.1 yards per carry to Montgomery's 2.7. The Titans are giving up 100 yards per game on the ground to RBs, but Marks' position on the short end of a backfield platoon makes him a deep-league flex candidate at best for Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.6: Woody Marks is set to lead Houston's backfield in Week 6 against the Jaguars, as fellow Texans RB David Montgomery (groin) is considered week-to-week. Marks racked up 85 scrimmage yards on 19 touches in the Week 5 win over Tennessee, a game Montgomery exited in the first half. Jacksonville is allowing a league-low 63.8 rushing yards per game, but RBs are averaging 40 receiving yards per game against the Jaguars. Expectations should be tempered due to the difficult matchup, but Marks is projected to get plenty of touches, making him a high-end Week 6 flex option.
outlooksByWeek.7: Woody Marks has averaged 18 touches and 83 scrimmage yards over Houston's last two games, leading the team's backfield since David Montgomery sustained a groin injury early in Week 5. Prior to that point, Marks averaged nine touches for 30 yards per game. If Montgomery is unable to play in Week 7, Marks would be a fantasy RB2 in the lead role against a Giants defense that has allowed three rushing scores and three receiving TDs to RBs through six games this season. Jawhar Jordan, who had six carries for 43 yards and a TD in the Week 6 win over Jacksonville, would likely work in a change-of-pace role again. If Montgomery returns, Marks would still be a viable flex option, albeit with a far lower floor.
outlooksByWeek.9: Woody Marks looks set to retain the lead role in Houston's backfield for a juicy Week 9 matchup with the Chargers, leaving him firmly in the fantasy RB2 range. David Montgomery hasn't played since getting banged up early in Week 5 against the Titans, and he may not be ready to return after Houston's Week 8 bye. Marks has averaged 18.7 touches over the past three games while recording at least 81 scrimmage yards in each of those three games. He should continue to pile up yardage against a Chargers defense that is allowing 124.6 rushing yards per game, and Marks has a nice opportunity to find the end zone for the first time since Week 4, as RBs have produced nine TDs in seven games against the Chargers.
outlooksByWeek.10: Woody Marks has recorded between 17 and 20 touches for 74-85 yards in each of Houston's last four games, working in a bell-cow role in the absence of David Montgomery (groin). Montgomery looks likely to remain sidelined in Week 10 at Cleveland, which should keep Marks in the fantasy RB2 range thanks to his high touch floor against a Browns defense that's allowing 115 rushing yards per game to running backs. Marks hasn't scored since Week 4, while Cleveland has given up seven TDs to RBs in nine games.
outlooksByWeek.11: Woody Marks entered concussion protocol during Houston's Week 10 loss to the the Browns. He isn't expected to be cleared in time to face the Colts on Thursday Night Football in Week 11. David Montgomery (groin) would likely assume the lead role in Houston's backfield if he gains clearance for his first action since Week 5. Emari Demercado and Dare Ogunbowale are Houston's other options at RB.
outlooksByWeek.12: Woody Marks missed Houston's Week 11 win over the Colts due to a concussion. If he clears protocol in time to face the Ravens in Week 12, Marks would be a decent flex option while splitting carries with David Montgomery, who returned from a groin injury in Week 11. Marks has exceeded 40 scrimmage yards only once in five games alongside Montgomery, and that was a game in which Montgomery exited early due to an injury, but Houston's entire RB room should benefit from facing a reeling Ravens defense that has allowed multiple rushing touchdowns in four consecutive games. Baltimore is giving up 29.2 points per game during its current six-game losing streak.

player.seasonOutlook: Marks, a fourth-round NFL draft pick in 2025, played a substantial role as a rookie, soaking up 220 touches (22nd among RBs), but he struggled with efficiency (his 3.59 yards per carry and 1.61 yards after contact both ranked near the basement) and found the end zone only five times. The result was 9.4 fantasy points per game and one top-10 fantasy outing. Marks appears ticketed for a lesser role in 2026 now that David Montgomery was brought in to serve as the likely leader of a backfield committee. Especially in an offense that doesn't use backs in the passing game very much, Marks is no more than a bench/insurance stash.

outlooksByWeek.2: De'Zhaun Stribling isn't likely to play in San Francisco's Week 2 matchup versus Miami. Stribling suffered an ankle injury during his NFL debut last Thursday against the Rams and is expected to miss at least a month of action. While he's out, Demarcus Robinson is slated to take on the 49ers' No. 3 wideout role.

player.seasonOutlook: Stribling was selected by the 49ers with the 33rd overall pick in April's draft. Stribling had a productive collegiate run, catching 44-plus passes in four of his five seasons, three of which came with different schools. That production included 52-882-6 and 55-811-6 receiving lines at Oklahoma State and Ole Miss over the past two seasons. Stribling primarily worked as a perimeter receiver and peaked with a 22% target share with OSU in 2024. His overall efficiency is pedestrian, but he has good size and speed (4.36 40-yard dash at the combine) and is a plus blocker. Stribling has plenty competition for Year 1 targets (Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, George Kittle, Christian McCaffrey), so a slow start is possible, but it's likely he'll eventually find his way to a bigger role and fantasy relevance. He's a fine mid-round upside pick.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mike Washington's volume was limited in his NFL debut, but he was productive, gaining 41 rushing yards on seven carries in the Raiders' season-opening win over the Dolphins. The quality of his opposition needs to be taken into account, but it was still a strong showing from the 2026 fourth-round pick. Lead back Ashton Jeanty had a huge game, proving he was fully recovered from a preseason ankle injury, but if he has trouble staying on the field, Washington appears very capable of stepping into a larger role. He'll face a tough matchup in Week 2 against a Chargers defense that ranked second in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mike Washington hasn't seen much action to begin his NFL career, getting 10 carries through the Raiders' first two games and turning them into 48 yards. He also failed to bring in his only target. Ashton Jeanty is locked into the top spot in the backfield and has 54 touches, third in the league behind only Jahmyr Gibbs and Kenneth Walker, and unless he gets hurt, Washington's workload figures to be limited. The rookie will look to take advantage of the chances he does get in Week 3 against a Saints defense that ranks in the bottom four in rushing yards and rushing TDs allowed to RBs so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mike Washington showed off his big-play potential in the Raiders' Week 3 win over the Saints, turning one of his five carries into a 36-yard touchdown. The rookie fourth-round pick hasn't logged big volume behind Ashton Jeanty, but that could begin to change if the starting RB continues to average just 3.3 yards per carry, compared to Washington's 6.8 mark. Until his workload ticks up, Washington will be little more than a dart throw or bench stash for fantasy rosters. He'll face a Kansas City defense in Week 4 that ranks 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Mike Washington failed to produce another big play in the Raiders' Week 4 loss to Kansas City, managing only 18 rushing yards on nine carries while catching one of two targets for minus-1 yard. Ashton Jeanty continues to struggle on the ground, but Washington hasn't yet shown enough consistency to be any kind of threat to his workload on early downs. The rookie is averaging 5.0 yards on his first 24 NFL carries, though, well clear of Jeanty's 3.4 mark, so volume could begin to tilt his way a little more if that trend continues. Washington will try to break free in Week 5 against a Patriots defense that ranked 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Mike Washington logged a season-low two touches in the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots, turning one carry and one reception into just 10 scrimmage yards. Ashton Jeanty continues to get a bell-cow workload despite his struggles on the ground, and Washington's 5.0 yards per carry on the season might encourage coach Klint Kubiak to give him more work on early downs. The rookie has flashed his big-play potential, but until he gets more consistent volume, his main value will be as injury insurance behind Jeanty. Washington may not need many touches to contribute in Week 6 against a Bills defense that ranks 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Mike Washington is coming off an intriguing showing in the Raiders' Week 6 loss to the Bills, as he turned nine carries into a team-high 43 yards. The rookie remains behind Ashton Jeanty on the running back depth chart, but Washington has been the more effective option on the ground, averaging 4.9 yards per carry on his limited volume while Jeanty has struggled to a 3.2 mark. Washington has posted double-digit touches in two of the last three games as his usage creeps up, but he's unlikely to make a splash in Week 7 against a Rams defense that ranks 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Mike Washington remains stuck as the backup to Ashton Jeanty in the Raiders' backfield, despite being more effective on the ground. Through seven games, Jeanty has a woeful 3.1 yards per carry on 106 totes, while Washington has produced 4.9 yards per carry on 40 rushes. Jeanty is the superior pass catcher, however, and coach Klint Kubiak has shown no signs of shifting the two closer to a timeshare. Washington will try to capitalize on his opportunities in Week 8 against a Jets defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Mike Washington may be in the process of taking over the early-down role in the Raiders' backfield. The rookie saw a career-high 25 carries in a Week 8 win over the Jets, turning them into 83 yards, while Ashton Jeanty mainly saw usage as a pass catcher and got only two carries. Washington's been far more effective on the ground, averaging 4.3 yards per carry to Jeanty's 3.1 mark, so the move from coach Klint Kubiak seems long overdue. The workload split could tip back toward Jeanty depending on the matchup, and a Week 9 tilt against the 49ers likely favors him over Washington. San Francisco's defense ranks 21st in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs, but 32nd in the league in receptions allowed to the position.
outlooksByWeek.10: Mike Washington crashed back to earth in the Raiders' Week 9 loss to the 49ers, losing a total of three yards on six carries. Ashton Jeanty had little luck either, scratching out 20 scrimmage yards on 11 touches. Washington remains in the No. 2 spot on the depth chart, and his 3.9 yards per carry on the season is only marginally better than Jeanty's 3.2 mark. Washington is making a case for more work on early downs and at the goal line, and coach Klint Kubiak showed a willingness to deploy a backfield timeshare during his Super Bowl-winning stint with Seattle last season. The rookie back will try to get back on track in Week 10 against a Seahawks defense that ranks 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Mike Washington may be letting an opportunity to claim the early-down role in the Raiders' backfield slip through his fingers. Over the last two games, including a Week 10 loss to the Seahawks, the rookie running back has gained just 20 rushing yards on 14 carries. Ashton Jeanty hasn't been any better, but his receiving skills will keep him atop the depth chart for now. Washington will try to get rolling again in Week 11 against a Broncos defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Mike Washington has faded into a depth role in the Raiders' backfield. With Ashton Jeanty looking more effective on the ground, Washington has handled single-digit carries in three straight games, managing 62 rushing yards on 23 total totes. The rookie running back would likely need a Jeanty injury to get another shot at the top spot on early downs. Washington will face a Browns defense in Week 12 that ranks 12th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Washington was selected by the Raiders in the fourth round of April's draft. He's a big back with terrific speed who lit up the combine with a 4.33 40-yard dash at 6-foot-1, 223 pounds (127 speed score), while also checking in with the longest arms in this rookie RB class. His collegiate efficiency wasn't very good during stops in Buffalo and New Mexico State, but it was better in 2025 -- his lone season at Arkansas -- as he averaged 6.41 yards per carry and 3.62 yards after contact, both of which rank seventh or better in this RB class. He might not be much of an option in the passing game, as his career 4.2 yards per target is the worst in this RB class, but his traits make him an intriguing prospect. Washington will open his career as a clear No. 2 option behind Ashton Jeanty, which makes him an intriguing end-of-bench insurance stash.

The Chiefs have fielded a middling fantasy D/ST the past two seasons, scoring in double-digits only seven times  but finishing with zero or negative fantasy points only five times . Top draftee Mansoor Delane replaces CB Trent McDuffie, who was traded to the Rams, but the team otherwise returns largely the same starting lineup. An opening-week matchup against the Broncos should be avoided, but there are pockets of the schedule where the Chiefs would be great for streaming: Weeks 3-4 (@MIA, @LV) and Weeks 9-11 (NYJ, @ATL, ARI) especially.

outlooksByWeek.2: Justice Hill and the Ravens are at home to battle the Saints in Week 2. Hill rushed six times for 18 yards and had one catch for 10 yards in Baltimore's 41-23 win. He's established himself as the clear No. 2 RB, as his 31 offensive snaps trailed slightly behind Derrick Henry's 37. Hill should continue to see opportunities as a change-of-pace back against a New Orleans defense that ranks 28th in fantasy points allowed per game (38.4) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Justice Hill and the Ravens travel to face a Cowboys defense in Week 3 that ranks 25th in fantasy points per game (25.9) allowed to running backs. He tallied two carries for six yards and caught both of his targets for eight yards during Baltimore's 24-17 Week 2 loss to the Saints. As long as Derrick Henry, who accounted for 16 of 18 carries out of the backfield, is healthy, Hill's action will be limited as the No. 2 RB. However, in a contest that is expected to be high-scoring, Hill could contribute as a receiver, but he's still a risky fantasy play outside of deeper leagues.
outlooksByWeek.4: Justice Hill and the Ravens are back home to host the 0-3 Titans in Week 4. He was explosive with his five carries during Baltimore's thrilling Week 3 victory, racking up 33 yards and a 6.6 average. However, Derrick Henry handled 26 of the 31 total carries for running backs, and he remains in firm control of the Ravens' backfield. Tennessee's defense ranks 17th in fantasy points allowed (20.7) to RBs, and despite the possibility of Baltimore playing from ahead, Hill's involvement will continue to be limited.
outlooksByWeek.5: Justice Hill and the Ravens visit the Falcons for a Week 5 showdown. He rushed once for three yards and caught two of three targets for 22 yards during Baltimore's 24-18 victory in Week 4. Derrick Henry out-carried Hill 23-1, even with Lamar Jackson missing the entire second half with an ankle injury. It appears that regardless of who's under center, the Ravens' backfield belongs to Henry. Hill should remain on fantasy benches against an Atlanta defense allowing just 17.9 points per game to RBs, which ranks ninth.
outlooksByWeek.6: Justice Hill and the Ravens visit the division-rival Browns in Week 6. He rushed four times for 73 yards and caught two of four targets for five yards during Baltimore's Week 5 overtime win. Derrick Henry out-carried him 24-4, although Hill led the way with a game-long 47-yard run. However, as long as Henry is the lead back and the Ravens don't fall into a massive deficit, Hill's involvement in the offense will remain limited.
outlooksByWeek.7: Justice Hill and the Ravens host the Bengals for an AFC North clash in Week 7. He did not record a carry but brought in all three of his targets for nine yards during Baltimore's 13-10 loss in Week 6. Derrick Henry accounted for 17 of the 18 rushing attempts out of the Ravens' backfield, a trend that should continue as long as he remains healthy. Hill should remain on fantasy benches against a Cincinnati defense that is tied for ninth in fantasy points allowed per game (19.0) to RBs
outlooksByWeek.8: Justice Hill and the Ravens are on the road for a Week 8 meeting with the Bills. He had three carries for seven yards and caught three of four targets for 26 yards during Baltimore's 35-13 loss in Week 7. Rasheen Ali registered 19 yards on four carries, but that can likely be attributed to the Ravens giving up all 35 points in the second half. Regardless, as long as Derrick Henry is healthy, Hill's involvement on offense will continue to be limited.
outlooksByWeek.9: Justice Hill and the Ravens return home for a meeting with the Jaguars on Thursday Night Football in Week 9. He rushed three times for 15 yards and caught four of eight targets for 20 yards during Baltimore's Week 8 loss. Hill led the team in receptions and targets while finishing second in yardage in a game where the Ravens managed just 167 total yards of offense. He could earn similar opportunities with Lamar Jackson (thumb) on IR and Joe Fagnano (knee) likely to start, but it's going to be difficult to trust any Baltimore player in fantasy going forward.
outlooksByWeek.10: Justice Hill and the Ravens host the winless Chargers on Monday Night Football in Week 10. He erupted for 85 yards on nine carries, including a 65-yard TD run, and caught all three of his targets for seven yards during Baltimore's Week 9 loss. With Jacoby Brissett expected to start under center, Hill and the Ravens' offense could start to become a bit more pass-friendly, but that's certainly no guarantee. He'll look to keep contributing against the Chargers' 21st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (22.8) to opposing RBs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Justice Hill and the Ravens are back on the road for an interconference clash against the Panthers in Week 11. He had three carries for four yards and caught five of seven targets for 34 yards during Baltimore's Week 10 defeat. Hill set new season highs in receptions and yardage with Jacoby Brissett making his team debut, a trend that could continue. Hill will try to exploit a Carolina defense allowing 27.3 fantasy points per game (29th) to opposing RBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Justice Hill and the Ravens are on the road for a Week 12 meeting with the Texans. He had six carries for 69 yards and a touchdown and caught four of five targets for 27 yards during Baltimore's Week 11 loss. Hill lost a fumble but was otherwise very productive with his 10 total touches, as he's now recorded two TDs in his last three games. He'll aim to keep contributing against a Houston defense allowing 21.4 fantasy points per game (14th) to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Hill heads into his seventh NFL season positioned for a larger role following the offseason departure of Keaton Mitchell. Derrick Henry remains the team's lead rusher, but he plays only about half of the snaps, leaving plenty of opportunity for Hill, particularly in passing situations. We've seen Hill in that role recently, including a 2024 campaign in which he posted a 42-383-3 receiving line on 55 targets (11th most among backs). Of course, Hill isn't trusted with much rushing work (his career high in carries is 84), which is why he has never had a top-35 fantasy campaign in his career. The 28-year-old has a limited ceiling and would be on the flex radar in PPR formats only if Henry were to miss time.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cam Ward threw for just 140 yards in Tennessee's 23-10 Week 1 loss to the Jets, bringing the 2025 first-overall pick's career average down to 184 passing yards per game. He's best avoided for fantasy purposes, even in multi-QB formats, for the Titans' Week 2 home game against the Eagles. Philadelphia's stingy pass defense limited Jayden Daniels to 164 passing yards and 4.8 yards per pass attempt in the Eagles' season-opening win over Washington.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cam Ward will be tough to trust outside of deeper multi-QB formats in Week 3, when the Titans face the Giants on the road. The 2025 first overall pick scored two short rushing TDs in Tennessee's surprisingly competitive Week 2 loss to the Eagles, matching his career total in that category heading into that game. Ward has just one touchdown pass this season and 16 touchdown passes through 19 NFL starts, of which he has won three. The Giants allowed two touchdown passes to Dak Prescott and four to reigning MVP Matthew Stafford, but those two veteran QBs are far more effective passers than Ward at this stage in their respective careers.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cam Ward has been arguably the worst starting QB in the NFL since entering the league as the Titans' first overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft. In the first three games of his sophomore season, Ward hasn't thrown for more than 183 yards or recorded multiple touchdown passes in a game. Dynasty managers can continue to stash him on the bench for the Titans' Week 4 trip to Baltimore in hopes of future improvements, but Ward's fantasy value in the present is negligible. The Ravens rank in the middle of the pack against the pass.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cam Ward hasn't thrown multiple touchdown passes in a game during the Titans' 0-4 start, and he's just 3-18 as a starter with 18 touchdown passes in 21 games. The 2025 first overall pick isn't an advisable fantasy option in Week 5 against the Texans, who have surprisingly surrendered the third-most passing yards in the league this season but still boast plenty of talent on defense and allowed the sixth-fewest passing yards in 2025. Dynasty managers looking for a silver lining with Ward can point to his season-high 222 passing yards in the Week 4 loss to Baltimore, 145 of which went to rookie fourth overall pick Carnell Tate.
outlooksByWeek.6: Cam Ward dropped to 3-19 as a starter for the Titans with a 26-3 loss to the Texans in Week 5, throwing an interception that dropped his season TD:INT to 3:3. He has declined in his second season after posting a 15:7 TD:INT as a rookie, while his passing yards per game have dropped from 186 in 2025 to 179 this year. Even against a Colts defense that's giving up the fifth-most passing yards per game, Ward can't be trusted in Week 6 fantasy lineups outside of deep superflex or multi-QB formats.
outlooksByWeek.7: Cam Ward and the Titans finally earned their first win of the season in Week 6 against the Colts, though the second-year QB certainly wasn't the primary driving force in the victory, as he threw for just 102 yards with a 1:1 TD:INT. Ward has mustered just four touchdown passes through six starts in his sophomore season while averaging 166 passing yards per game. He'll face a franchise that's all too familiar with subpar QB play in Week 7, taking on a Browns team that's off to a surprisingly strong 4-2 start this season while boasting one of the league's 10 stingiest defenses in terms of both passing yards and points allowed per game. Between Ward's own shortcomings and the tricky matchup, it's best to avoid him in fantasy for Week 7.
outlooksByWeek.8: Cam Ward has yet to throw multiple touchdown passes in a game heading into the Titans' Week 8 trip to Cincinnati. The second-year QB has an ugly 4:5 TD:INT while throwing for just 168 yards per game. Cincinnati's defense has limited QBs to a 6:4 TD:INT, but the Bengals allowed Baltimore's Tyler Huntley to throw for a career-high 298 yards in a Week 7 game that the Bengals won by 22 points. Until Ward shows signs of progress as a passer, he'll remain a fantasy non-factor, even in superflex formats.
outlooksByWeek.10: Cam Ward had his best game of the season in Tennessee's 43-36 Week 8 loss to the Bengals, prior to a Week 9 bye. He threw for 300 yards for the first time in his career and delivered a pair of touchdown passes for his first multi-TD performance through the air all season. Ward has a chance to build on that effort in Week 10 against a Jaguars defense that has been more vulnerable through the air than on the ground. The far larger sample of subpar football from the 2025 first overall pick prior to his strong outing last game suggests Ward remains tough to trust for now, even in superflex formats. The Jaguars are giving up the 11th-most passing yards per game, though they have more interceptions (11) than touchdown passes allowed (eight).
outlooksByWeek.11: Cam Ward has taken a noticeable step forward in Tennessee's last two games, even though the Titans lost both to drop to 1-8. After throwing for a career-high 304 yards and tossing multiple touchdown passes for the first time this season against the Bengals, Ward threw for 231 yards and two TDs in the Week 10 loss to Jacksonville, his second-highest passing yards total of the campaign. His four touchdown passes in that two-game stretch match Ward's total from his first seven starts of the season. The improving 2025 first overall pick has a nice opportunity to keep building momentum in Week 11 against a dreadful Dallas defense that has surrendered a 19:4 TD:INT ratio en route to allowing 28.2 points per game. Ward's underwhelming larger body of work leaves him out of the starting mix in most single-QB formats, but he's a sneaky-good Week 11 superflex option.
outlooksByWeek.12: Cam Ward has thrown for at least 231 yards and two TDs in three consecutive games after failing to hit either of those passing benchmarks in any of his first seven starts this season. The 2025 first overall pick is growing in confidence, and he's also being forced to air it out as the 1-9 Titans consistently play catch-up. That's unlikely to change in Week 12, when the Titans face a Jaguars team that can put up points in bunches and is better at stopping the run than the pass. Ward's recent uptick in production has him in the conversation as a starter in superflex leagues, but there remain plenty of more reliable options in single-QB formats.

player.seasonOutlook: Ward is eyeing a Year 2 leap following an underwhelming rookie campaign, albeit under tough circumstances. The 2025 No. 1 draft pick was plenty busy as a rookie (eighth in the league in dropbacks and pass attempts), but he struggled to 5.9 yards per attempt and took a league-high 55 sacks. Ward was rarely a factor with his legs (more than 12 yards three times) and produced one weekly fantasy finish better than 12th. The good news is that a tough rookie year isn't overly damning for a quarterback's career trajectory, and he'll be in a better spot in 2026 with new playcaller Brian Daboll and an improved supporting cast (Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson join a now-healthy Calvin Ridley). Ward will need to run more to become an elite fantasy option, but Year 2 is the breakout season for many quarterbacks, so he's well worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kaelon Black is coming off an impressive NFL debut as San Francisco heads into a Week 2 matchup versus the Dolphins. Black surprisingly got more carries than Christian McCaffrey in a season-opening win over the Rams, logging 14 carries for 65 yards to McCaffrey's 10 carries for 68 yards. While there's no chance of Black usurping a healthy McCaffrey in the pecking order anytime soon, the Week 1 usage suggests Black could take on a significant role in San Francisco's offense if the team looks to lighten McCaffrey's workload. Both backs could be in for a good day against Miami, who allowed Las Vegas running backs Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington to combine for 143 rushing yards, 45 receiving yards and two touchdowns in a Week 1 loss to Las Vegas.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kaelon Black enters a Week 3 tilt against Arizona having established himself as San Francisco's clear No. 2 back. While Black has caught only one pass (on one target) through two contests, he's carried the ball 21 times -- one more than starter Christian McCaffrey (20 carries) and well ahead of No. 3 RB Jordan James (four totes). Of course, McCaffrey is the unquestioned leader of the 49ers' backfield, but Black has at least carved out a significant role and put himself on the fantasy radar in his first NFL campaign. The Cardinals just gave up 144 total rushing yards to Seattle's Jadarian Price and Emanuel Wilson in a loss Sunday, so they could be vulnerable against San Francisco's ground game.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kaelon Black has seen his involvement on offense dwindle in recent games as the 49ers prepare to face the Broncos in Week 4. After the rookie garnered a hefty 14 carries in Week 1, he's logged just 11 totes over the subsequent two weeks, including just four this past Sunday in a win over Arizona. Black was at least fairly efficient by gaining 17 yards on those carries, but with only one reception to date this season, he's not getting enough touches to make an impact in fantasy. Perhaps that will change against the Broncos, who are giving up 5.26 yards per carry to running backs, the second-worst mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kaelon Black should continue to back up 49ers star RB Christian McCaffrey in Week 5 against Seattle. Black surprisingly logged 14 carries in Week 1 against the Rams, but since then he's topped out at seven totes as McCaffrey has dominated touches out of the backfield. Black also has just one catch this season, so he hasn't been able to establish much fantasy value except as an insurance policy in case of a McCaffrey injury. It may be hard for Black to find success on what will likely be limited opportunities against Seattle, as the Seahawks are allowing a paltry 3.35 yards per carry to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kaelon Black will likely again get a handful of carries again for the 49ers in Week 6 against Washington. Black has logged between four and seven carries each of his past four games after getting 14 totes in Week 1 against the Rams. The rookie hasn't been particularly efficient with his opportunities, managing just 2.4 yards per carry over the past two weeks and 3.7 overall this season. Things may not get easier against the Commanders, who have yielded the sixth-fewest rushing yards per game to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kaelon Black and the 49ers visit the Falcons for a Week 7 showdown. He had eight carries for 34 yards and caught his lone target for three yards in San Francisco's 23-17 victory in Week 6. Christian McCaffrey tallied 25 touches to the rookie's nine, leaving no doubt about who the leader is in the 49ers' backfield. Black will look to make more of an impact with his limited touches versus Atlanta's 21st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (23.3) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Kaelon Black may have an opportunity for more work in Week 9 versus the Raiders with San Francisco's top RB, Christian McCaffrey, managing a hamstring strain. McCaffrey picked up the injury in Week 7 against Atlanta, and Black ended up logging a healthy 12 carries, which he turned into 63 yards and a touchdown. McCaffrey was able to finish out that game, and the team's Week 8 bye along with optimism that the strain is mild gives him a good chance of suiting up this Sunday, but Black could be productive even if McCaffrey plays. Las Vegas has posted some of the worst numbers in the NFL against running backs, giving up 22.3 fantasy points per game to the position, fifth-most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Kaelon Black has been running well for the 49ers of late and will look to continue to do so Week 10 versus the Cowboys. Black has rushed for at least 63 yards in each of his past two games and is averaging a hearty 5.8 yards per carry during that span. He's still not factoring into the passing game and continues to work considerably behind top RB Christian McCaffrey, but Black is proving himself to be a capable NFL back during his rookie campaign. With enough opportunities, Black could find success against a Dallas defense that has yielded 4.77 yards per carry to running backs, fourth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Kaelon Black could be a key factor for San Francisco in Week 11 versus a tough Minnesota defense. The rookie running back has shown plenty of promise, and he's coming off a performance against the Cowboys during which he accounted for 66 total yards and a touchdown. Despite continuing to work behind superstar Christian McCaffrey, Black has recorded double-digit carries and at least 53 rushing yards in each of his past three games and has scored two touchdowns during that span. He's averaging a healthy 4.5 yards per carry on the season, which could give him plenty of importance against a Minnesota defense that is yielding an NFL-best 14.0 points per game but that ranks in the bottom half of the league with 4.26 yards per carry allowed to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Kaelon Black will face another tough run defense when the 49ers host the Seahawks in Week 12. Black couldn't do much against the Vikings' vaunted defense this past Sunday, gaining just eight yards on six carries while adding seven yards on his lone reception. He also saw a three-game streak of double-digit touches snapped, but the rookie maintained a steady 30% offensive snap share. Black and the 49ers' running game as a whole should be challenged by a Seahawks defense that ranks seventh in the NFL with 15.1 fantasy points per game allowed to running backs.

player.seasonOutlook: Black was selected by the 49ers in the third round of April's draft. It was a bit of a surprise selection after Black failed to clear 190 touches in four collegiate seasons prior to not landing an invite to the scouting combine. He did clear 1,000 rushing yards at Indiana in 2025, but remained a nonfactor as a receiver, totaling exactly four receptions in each of his two seasons with the Hoosiers. Black will open his career handling No. 2 duties behind Christian McCaffrey. He'll be worth an add if the 30-year-old McCaffrey misses time, but a lack of third-down ability may severely limit his fantasy output. Stash Black in dynasty formats.

outlooksByWeek.3: Ollie Gordon's workload could increase if Jaylen Wright misses the Dolphins' Week 3 game against the Chiefs. Despite being No. 3 on the depth chart, Gordon has outsnapped Wright behind Miami's workhorse, De'Von Achane. Kansas City allowed stud Jonathan Taylor to rush for two scores in Week 2 but kept Denver's backs under control in Week 1. Barring an injury to Achane, it's difficult to envision a path to meaningful production for Gordon.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylen Wright will have an elevated role for the Dolphins in Week 4 against the Vikings if he's able to overcome a foot issue that kept him out in Week 3. Miami lost De'Von Achane for the season due to a knee injury, leaving just Wright and Ollie Gordon to handle carries. With the Dolphins often falling behind in most matchups, Wright has the chance to be the preferred pass-catching option. Confidence isn't inspired facing a Vikings defense that's allowing just 3.1 yards per carry and 11 catches to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ollie Gordon could be emerging in the Dolphins' backfield heading into a Week 5 matchup with the Bengals. With De'Von Achane (knee) out, Gordon ran for 100 yards on just nine carries in Week 4, vastly outperforming Jaylen Wright, while also scoring a touchdown for the second straight week. Touches figure to remain low if the Dolphins are forced to play from behind early, but facing a defense that's allowing 4.5 yards per carry could lead to steady yardage without high volume, and Gordon will remain an option near the goal line.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ollie Gordon will likely continue to serve as the lead back for the Dolphins in Week 7 against the Jets. Prior to Miami's Week 6 bye, Gordon had 17 or 18 carries in two of three games. The lone outing with a decrease in carries was also his only 100-yard game, and he scored in each contest. Though he hasn't factored into the passing game, volume remains king for running backs, and Gordon appears to have that in a matchup against a defense that's allowing 4.2 yards per carry, resulting in the 11th-most fantasy points allowed.
outlooksByWeek.8: Ollie Gordon may be hindered by an unfavorable game flow in Week 8 when the Dolphins host the Patriots. He has scored in four straight games, topping 100 yards twice while amassing at least 17 carries three times. Jaylen Wright is uncertain to play in Week 8, which could result in 20-plus carries for Miami's only option in the backfield if they remain competitive and aren't forced to throw the entire second half. New England brings a mid-tier run defense into Week 8, allowing 4.1 yards per carry but just five rushing scores in seven games.
outlooksByWeek.9: Ollie Gordon will bring consistent volume into the Dolphins' Week 9 matchup with the Lions. Since taking over as the team's lead back, Gordon has at least 17 carries in four of his last five games, though he's seen a minimal amount of work in the passing game, snagging just six passes. Detroit has allowed the third-fewest fantasy points to opposing running backs, mainly due to opponents passing on them at will, which Miami isn't equipped to do. With volume paramount for the position, Gordon is a safe bet to pile up carries, creating a nice floor that can be elevated if he finds the end zone.
outlooksByWeek.10: Ollie Gordon should log heavy volume again in an inviting Week 10 matchup when the Dolphins face the Colts. Gordon has 16 or more carries in three straight games and five of his last six, scoring four times and topping 100 yards twice. He has no major competition for carries with Jaylen Wright injured and sparingly used even when healthy. Indianapolis is allowing 4.8 yards per carry, the third-highest mark in the league, setting Gordon up to take advantage of a big workload.
outlooksByWeek.11: Ollie Gordon will have a heavy workload for as long as the Dolphins remain competitive in Week 11 against the Bills. Gordon has at least 16 carries in five straight games and caught a season-high four passes in Week 10, though Miami was in a four-quarter game against the Colts. Buffalo figures to be a far more difficult opponent, which could force a heavier pass-game script. With Buffalo allowing just 3.8 yards per carry, Gordon could be touchdown-dependent for top-end fantasy scoring.
outlooksByWeek.12: Ollie Gordon will look to repeat prior success when the Dolphins face the Jets for the second time this year in Week 12. He drew only 11 carries in Week 11, his lowest total since Week 4, but burst through for 6.3 yards per carry, also his best mark since Week 4. Gordon rushed for 103 yards on 25 carries against the Jets in Week 7. Their defense has allowed 4.6 yards per carry and eight rushing scores through 11 games, surrendering an additional four touchdown receptions, and Gordon is more involved in the passing game with McCord under center.

player.seasonOutlook: Gordon is battling Jaylen Wright for backup work behind lead back De'Von Achane in Miami. Gordon was used sparingly as a rookie and didn't exactly move the needle. The 2025 sixth-round pick averaged an ugly 2.84 yards per carry on 70 attempts and 3.6 yards per target on the nine balls thrown his way. Gordon is still very young (22 years old), and his size (6-foot-1, 226 pounds) adds to his long-term intrigue. He'll have some insurance appeal if he beats out Wright for primary backup duties.

outlooksByWeek.2: Caleb Williams will look to build off a monster performance as the Bears take on the Vikings at home in Week 2. Williams delivered for Chicago in the highest-scoring Week 1 game in NFL history. The third-year quarterback completed 21 of 29 passes for 269 yards and two touchdowns while carrying the ball 10 times for 65 yards and two more TDs. Williams will have more of a challenge this upcoming Sunday, given that the Vikings allowed the fewest fantasy points per game (14.3) to quarterbacks in the 2025 season. Still, Minnesota's secondary is susceptible, as they ceded 387 passing yards, two touchdowns and one interception to Jordan Love this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Caleb Williams is not expected to play in Week 3 as the Bears take on the Eagles. Williams went down with what looked like a freak injury against the Vikings in Week 2, but he now sits week-to-week with a hamstring ailment. Tyson Bagent is slated to get the start versus an Eagles defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 20.6 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks across two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Caleb Williams is unlikely to play in Week 4 as the Bears take on the Jets. Williams went down with what looked like a freak injury against the Vikings in Week 2, but he now sits week-to-week with a hamstring ailment. Case Keenum is slated to get the start again versus a Jets defense that gave up 269 passing yards and two touchdowns to Jared Goff in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Caleb Williams is set to miss another game as the Bears travel to Green Bay in Week 5. Williams went down with what looked like a freak injury against the Vikings in Week 2, but he now sits week-to-week with a hamstring ailment. Tyson Bagent is set to get the start again versus a Packers defense that gave up 148 passing yards, one touchdown and two interceptions to Buccaneers rookie Jalon Daniels in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.6: Caleb Williams' status is up in the air ahead of Chicago's Week 6 matchup at Atlanta. Williams has been sidelined since he injured his hamstring against Minnesota in Week 2, but he could be ready to return if he has a favorable practice week. If he plays, the starting quarterback will face a Falcons defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Caleb Williams will aim to build on a stellar return as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Williams had no struggles in Week 6 against the Falcons in his first game since Week 2, completing 83 percent of passes for 305 yards and one touchdown. The third-year quarterback has now surpassed 250 passing yards in both games that he's played through this season, and the sky's the limit now. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Caleb Williams will aim to stay hot as the Bears play the Seahawks in Week 8. Williams impressed in his second game back from a hamstring injury in Week 7, completing 67 percent of passes for 308 yards and two touchdowns over the Patriots. The third-year quarterback has now passed for 300-plus yards in back-to-back weeks, and he hasn't committed a turnover in that stretch. He'll take on a Seattle defense that's been tougher on QBs, ranking second in fantasy points allowed to the position.
outlooksByWeek.9: Caleb Williams will look to stay solid as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Williams pieced together another solid outing in Chicago's Week 8 MNF win over the Seahawks, completing 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards and one touchdown. The starting quarterback has now thrown for 860 yards and four touchdowns in his last three games, and he's passed for 240 or more yards in all but one outing this season. He'll shift focus to a Tampa Bay squad that's ranked a tough fourth in fantasy points allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Caleb Williams will look to lead a more efficient Chicago offense in Week 12 at Detroit. Williams put together a passable stat line in a Week 11 win over the Saints, but the Bears offense looked sluggish in the matchup. The third-year quarterback has dished out two touchdowns in three of his last four games and thrown for 240 or more yards in all but one of his last five. He'll face a Lions defense that's ranked a favorable 31st in fantasy points allowed to quarterbacks this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams enters his third NFL season after a solid rookie campaign in 2024 followed by a big leap forward in 2025. Williams finished last season no lower than 11th among QBs in pass attempts, completions, pass yards, passing TDs, carries, rush yards, rush TDs and fantasy points per game. While Williams' completion percentage was one of the worst in the league (58%), his dual-threat ability and turnover avoidance (seven INTs both seasons) has led to solid fantasy output. The 2024 No. 1 draft pick has a good supporting cast in playcaller Ben Johnson and a trio of young pass catchers in Rome Odunze, Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland. Williams is a fringe QB1 with upside for another leap.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jalen Hurts tossed three touchdowns in Week 1 for the Eagles. Hurts was not terribly efficient, though did hit on several big plays en route to the 24-22 win. Hurts also rushed for 46 yards in a brand new offense under the direction of offensive coordinator Sean Mannion. In Week 2, Philadelphia will face a dismal Titans squad that allowed 367 yards from scrimmage to the Jets in their season opener. Tennessee was torched on the ground in particular, allowing 152 rushing yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jalen Hurts tossed two touchdowns and two interceptions in a last-second win over Tennessee last game. Hurts threw for 264 yards in the rollercoaster battle and was able to overcome the two picks to find Darius Cooper for the winning score. Hurts has five touchdowns in two games for the Eagles. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jalen Hurts had a performance to forget last game for the Eagles. Hurts threw for just 153 yards and an interception in a dismal loss to the Bears in Week 3. Hurts did score once on the ground, though gained just 25 yards as a rusher. Hurts will look to get back on track in Week 4 versus a Rams defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026. The Rams are allowing just 171.3 passing yards per tilt, which is fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jalen Hurts tossed two touchdowns last game for the Eagles. Unfortunately, he threw for just 93 yards in the 24-20 loss to the Rams. Hurts was missing DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert in the passing game, while Saquon Barkley left early due to an injury of his own, so Hurts cannot shoulder all the blame for this meager performance. Still, he has thrown for less than 250 yards combined in the last two contests. An intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 versus the Jags, though. Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jalen Hurts struggled again last game for the Eagles. Hurts completed just 21-of-40 passes for 220 yards and a touchdown in the ugly 19-17 loss to the Jaguars. Hurts has yet to throw for 300 yards in a game this season. He also had by far his worst rushing output of the 2026 campaign with only two yards on the ground, perhaps due to a nagging calf issue. In Week 6, Philadelphia will face a curious Carolina Panthers pass defense. Carolina is allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the NFL. However, the Panthers have yielded just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Hurts enters his seventh NFL season and sixth as the starter in Philadelphia. The 28-year-old tossed a career-high 25 touchdowns last season, but his rushing production was way down (105-421-8 after delivering at least 139 carries, 605 yards and 10 TDs in each of the prior four seasons). Hurts' fantasy production dipped, as his 18.7 points per game was his lowest as a starter and ranked eighth at the position after three straight top-five campaigns. Hurts' supporting cast remains strong (even without A.J. Brown), and new playcaller Sean Mannion very well could add some juice back to the offense. Hurts' fantasy stock is down a bit from years past, but his dual-threat ability locks him in as a midrange QB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyren Williams may again be part of a pretty evenly split backfield when the Rams face the Giants in Week 2. Though Williams scored Los Angeles' only touchdown in a season-opening loss to the 49ers, he had 13 fewer rushing yards on one more carry than backfield mate Blake Corum. Williams did produce more total yards thanks to logging 24 receiving yards on three catches, but Corum seems to have forced his way into a substantial backfield role after averaging over five yards per carry last year. Both backs will look to break through a Giants defense that gave up just 69 yards and 3.8 YPC against Dallas in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyren Williams will look to get into the end zone for the Rams again in Week 3 versus Denver. Williams posted a 12-85-0 rushing line against the Giants on Monday Night Football and added a 2-12-1 line through the air. The veteran running back has scored each of the first two weeks of the campaign after racking up double-digit scores each of the past three seasons. The Broncos have struggled against the run so far in 2026, allowing the third-most rushing yards (286) to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kyren Williams is fresh off his most productive performance of the campaign heading into the Rams' Week 4 clash against Philadelphia. Williams posted season-best tallies with 15 carries for 88 yards in Week 3 against Denver, and he complemented his output on the ground with a season-high six catches for 70 yards through the air. Whereas fellow running back Blake Corum has frequently eaten into Williams' volume since last season, Corum recorded just six totes and 15 total yards against the Broncos. Corum isn't likely to exit the picture anytime soon, but Williams remains a consistent week-to-week producer. However, he could have his work cut out for him in Week 4 versus an Eagles defense that ranks 12th in the league in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kyren Williams enters the Rams' Week 5 matchup against the Bills with plenty of momentum. Williams totaled 147 yards and two touchdowns in a comeback win over Philadelphia in Week 4, pushing him up to four total TDs on the season. The star running back has logged at least 80 rushing yards in three straight games, and he's averaged 68.5 receiving yards across his past two contests. Buffalo has yielded 22.2 fantasy points per game to running backs so far, sixth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kyren Williams will take aim at the end zone again in the Rams' Week 6 matchup versus the Cardinals. Though Williams was held to 49 yards on 16 carries against Buffalo in Week 6, he added 27 yards as a receiver and scored his fifth touchdown of the season. He also continued to put plenty of space between him and No. 2 RB Blake Corum, logging 11 more totes than his backup. Williams could find ample running room against an Arizona defense that ranks 19th in the league by allowing 4.17 yards per carry to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kyren Williams remains the Rams' leading running back entering Week 7 against the Raiders, having rushed 80 times for 393 yards and four touchdowns while adding 30 receptions for 217 yards and another score. He's averaging an efficient 4.9 yards per carry, and his Week 6 showing against the Cardinals was right in line with that, as he notched 50 rushing yards in just 10 carries. Williams' receiving involvement provides a dependable fantasy foundation, particularly with Davante Adams sidelined for an extended period, and this looks like a favorable matchup on paper for the star tailback since Las Vegas has allowed the ninth-most fantasy points per game to opposing running backs in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.8: Kyren Williams will look to continue his consistent campaign when the Rams face the Chargers in Week 8. Williams posted 121 total yards Sunday against Las Vegas, marking the third time this season's he's logged over 100 total yards in a game. While his backfield mate Blake Corum has at times impacted Williams' workload, the latter has made the most of his carries, averaging a career-best 5.1 yards per rush, and he's also having his best season as a pass catcher. Williams could feast on a Chargers defense that's giving up 20.1 fantasy points per game to running backs to rank 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Kyren Williams will likely continue to share the Rams' backfield in Week 9 against Washington. Williams tallied a modest 56 yards on 16 carries against the Chargers in a win this past Sunday, but he managed to get into the end zone for the fifth time over his past five games. He's faced competition for carries of late from Blake Corum, who has tallied 28 totes for 166 yards and two TDs over the past two weeks. Both Williams and Corum could battle for running room against the Commanders, who are yielding just 3.63 yards per carry to running backs, which ranks seventh-best in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Kyren Williams may be asked to log a heftier workload than usual for the Rams in Week 10 against the Cardinals. Williams rushed for just 45 yards -- his second-lowest mark of the season -- on 15 carries against Washington in Week 9, adding 16 yards on three catches. However, Los Angeles is going to be without wideout Puka Nacua (knee) for multiple weeks, and with Davante Adams (hamstring) still on IR, the team may turn more to its ground game  -- led by Williams and Blake Corum -- to carry the load. Arizona's defense has been middling against the run this season, allowing 18.0 fantasy points per game to RBs, tied for 18th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: Kyren Williams has been dealing with a sore toe but is expected to play in the Rams' Week 12 matchup versus Green Bay. Williams logged a season-low 32 total yards (23 rushing, nine receiving) versus Arizona his last time out, so he'll be looking for a big bounce-back performance against the Packers. With that said, Blake Corum -- who went off for a season-best 119 yards and scored a touchdown in that game against the Cardinals -- continues to get double-digit touches every week, denting Williams' ceiling to an extent. Both backs could find success against a Green Bay defense that has given up 12 rushing TDs to running backs, tied for fourth-most in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams continues to produce at a high level as the Rams' lead back. The 2022 fifth-round pick has produced 1,350-plus scrimmage yards in three straight seasons (including a career-high 1,533 in 2025), and he's one of 11 backs in NFL history who have scored 13-plus touchdowns in three of his first four seasons. Williams' carry share actually dropped quite a bit last season, but it was mostly offset by a boost in both rushing and receiving efficiency, and he still averaged a healthy 15.5 fantasy points. Williams doesn't do much as a receiver (he has never cleared 36 catches in a season), but his overall usage and scoring potential in the Rams' elite offense is enough to make the 26-year-old a solid RB2 option.

outlooksByWeek.2: DK Metcalf and the Steelers are in New England to face the Patriots in Week 2. The veteran wideout corralled four of 10 targets for 40 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-13 Week 1 win against the Falcons. He led the team in targets by four but finished third in receiving yards. Metcalf has a hypothetical advantage over Michael Pittman after playing last year with Aaron Rodgers, and there's a good chance he'll be his favorite target against New England's 21st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (33.1) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: DK Metcalf and the Steelers host the Bengals for a Week 3 divisional clash. He caught four of a team-high nine targets for just 27 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to the Patriots. Metcalf finished fifth in yardage despite tying Germie Bernard and Pat Freiermuth for second in receptions, and he now has an 8-67-0 receiving line on 19 targets through two outings. Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers offense have been underwhelming to begin the season, and they'll face a Cincinnati defense allowing 25.0 fantasy points per game (9th) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: DK Metcalf and the Steelers visit the Browns for an AFC North clash between 2-1 teams in Week 4. He caught three of five targets for 31 yards and his first TD of the season during Pittsburgh's 30-27 victory in Week 3. Metcalf has an 11-98-1 receiving line on 24 targets through three contests, as he and Aaron Rodgers have had a hard time connecting in their second season together. With that being said, it'll be difficult to trust Metcalf until the duo is on the same page, even against a beatable Cleveland secondary allowing 36.7 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks 26th.
outlooksByWeek.5: DK Metcalf and the Steelers host the Colts in a Week 5 clash between 2-2 teams. He caught five of nine targets for 115 yards during Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss in Week 4. Metcalf turned in his best performance of the season by far while leading his team in receptions, yardage, and targets. He'll look to stay hot against a beatable Indianapolis secondary that allows 35.0 fantasy points per game (20th) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.6: DK Metcalf and the Steelers are on the road to take on the Buccaneers in Week 6. He caught three of four targets for 12 yards and rushed once for 11 yards during Pittsburgh's 34-22 victory in Week 5. Metcalf and Darnell Washington tied for the fewest receiving yards on the team, while the veteran wideout finished fourth in targets. He'll try to rebound against a Tampa Bay defense that allows 29.5 fantasy points per game (12th) to WRs and just gave up nine receptions for 130 yards and a TD to George Pickens.
outlooksByWeek.7: DK Metcalf and the Steelers are in Paris for a Week 7 showdown against the Saints. He caught 11 of 15 targets for 93 yards in Pittsburgh's gritty comeback victory in Week 6. Metcalf led the team in yardage and targets while tying with rookie Germie Bernard (11-87-1) for first in receptions. The 11 catches were a product of game flow with the Steelers playing from behind most of the game, and they were Metcalf's most on the season by far, as he had the same number of receptions over his previous three games combined. He'll look to take advantage of a New Orleans defense that just allowed Malik Nabers to record a 12-165-0 line on 15 targets.
outlooksByWeek.8: DK Metcalf and the Steelers host the Browns for a Week 8 showdown with first place in the AFC North on the line. He brought in two of six targets for 56 yards in Week 7 during Pittsburgh's 16-10 win in Paris. Metcalf tied for the lead in targets while pacing the team in yardage despite his low reception count. He'll be ready to face a Cleveland defense he cooked for a season-high 115 yards on five catches in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.10: DK Metcalf and the Steelers travel to Cincinnati for a divisional clash in Week 10. He caught just one of six targets for four yards during Pittsburgh's 27-6 victory in Week 8, giving the 28-year-old a 3-60-0 receiving line on 12 targets over his last two contests. Metcalf and the Steelers didn't have to throw much while playing most of Week 8 with a double-digit advantage, but that could change in Week 10 versus a high-powered Bengals offense on Sunday Night Football. In his first matchup against Cincinnati, Metcalf corralled three of five targets for 31 yards and his only TD of the season.
outlooksByWeek.11: In Week 11, DK Metcalf and the Steelers visit an Eagles defense allowing 37.9 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs. In Week 10, he hauled in two of six targets for 54 yards, including a 32-yard touchdown, during Pittsburgh's 38-18 loss. Metcalf found the end zone for just the second time all season and the first time since Week 3. Despite the favorable matchup, Metcalf remains an inconsistent fantasy option for a team that prefers to run the ball.
outlooksByWeek.12: In Week 12, DK Metcalf and the Steelers look to stay undefeated at home when they battle the Broncos on Black Friday. He caught one of four targets for two yards before being ejected in the third quarter of Pittsburgh's Week 11 loss. Metcalf's season continues to spiral out of control, and luckily for him, the veteran receiver will not face a suspension from the league following the scuffle. Metcalf will be on the field versus Denver, but he should remain on fantasy benches.

player.seasonOutlook: Metcalf returns for Year 2 in Pittsburgh after a solid but unspectacular debut season. The ex-Seahawk missed two games and finished outside the top 20 receivers in targets, catches and yardage (career-low 850), but still did just enough to produce a 21st-place finish in fantasy PPG (his fifth top-25 in his last six seasons). Metcalf soaked up 11 end zone targets and is up to 107 for his career, which leads the NFL since his debut in 2019. The 28-year-old has added target competition this season in the form of Michael Pittman Jr. and rookie Germie Bernard, so while he'll certainly remain busy, a slight dip in usage is probable. Metcalf should be valued as a back-end WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chase Brown and the Bengals are in Houston for a Week 2 showdown versus the Texans. He rushed 16 times for 56 yards and a TD and brought in five of six targets for another 22 yards during Cincinnati's Week 1 victory over Tampa Bay. Brown is the clear-cut lead back on a high-powered offense, and he should continue to see a hefty workload on the ground and in the passing game. However, Houston's defense is tied for third in fantasy points allowed per game (10.5) to RBs, so consider this a less-than-favorable matchup.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chase Brown and the Bengals are in Pittsburgh to battle their division rivals in Week 3. He tallied 20 carries for 80 yards and corralled three of five targets for two yards during Cincinnati's Week 2 win. Brown handled 23 of 26 touches out of the backfield, and he should continue to dominate those looks again in Week 3. The Steelers' defense ranks 26th in fantasy points allowed (27.5) to RBs after giving up 136 rushing yards and 4.9 yards per carry to the Patriots in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chase Brown and the Bengals welcome the 2-1 Jaguars to town for an AFC clash in Week 4.
