He rushed 13 times for 61 yards and caught both his targets for eight yards during Cincinnati's 30-27 loss in Week 3. It was a quiet afternoon for Brown, with his 15 total touches well below his average of 22 accrued over his first two outings. He'll face another stout defensive unit, as Jacksonville ranks seventh in fantasy points (17.2) and fourth in rushing yards allowed (57.7) per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chase Brown and the Bengals visit the 0-4 Dolphins for a Week 5 showdown. He had nine carries for 10 yards but caught all 11 of his targets for 71 yards during Cincinnati's 22-17 loss in Week 4. Brown set a career high in receptions with Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) leaving in the first half, and with Tee Higgins (adductor) picking up a questionable tag, the running back could again get high volume through the air while still handling the bulk of carries. Miami's defense ranks last in fantasy points (29.7) and receiving TDs (4) allowed to the position, giving Brown a very favorable matchup.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chase Brown and the Bengals are on the road for a divisional clash against the Ravens in Week 7. He registered 13 carries for 39 yards and caught three of four targets for 21 yards during Cincinnati's 31-24 victory in Week 5. Brown took a backseat to Samaje Perine, who had 14 carries for 68 yards and caught both of his targets for 10 yards and a touchdown. Over his last two outings, he's rushed 22 times for 49 yards, a miserable 2.2 yards per carry. Next up is another difficult matchup against a Baltimore defense allowing 18.6 fantasy points per game (7th) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Chase Brown and the Bengals welcome the Titans to town for a Week 8 showdown. He rushed 11 times for 39 yards and caught four of five targets for 19 yards during Cincinnati's 35-13 victory in Week 7. Over his last three outings, Brown has 33 carries for 88 yards (2.7 yards per carry). He'll look to bounce back against a Tennessee defense that gave up 183 rushing yards and three total TDs to the Browns in Week 7.
outlooksByWeek.9: Chase Brown and the Bengals take on the Falcons for a Week 9 showdown in Spain. He rushed 12 times for 55 yards and caught eight of nine targets for 46 yards during Cincinnati's 43-36 overtime win in Week 8. Brown lost a fumble but managed to out-touch Samaje Perine 20-5, a good sign for Brown's fantasy outlook. Next up is a Falcons defense allowing 28.1 fantasy points per game (30th) to opposing RBs after giving up 324 rushing yards in their last outing.
outlooksByWeek.10: Chase Brown and the Bengals host the division-rival Steelers for an AFC North clash in Week 10. In Week 9, he had nine carries for 57 yards and caught all three of his targets for another 18 yards to help Cincinnati win a fourth straight game. Brown's production has been somewhat underwhelming from a fantasy perspective, as he's registered just one touchdown across eight outings in 2026. He'll look to find the end zone against a Pittsburgh defense that's allowed just four TDs to the position and is coming off a bye.
outlooksByWeek.11: In Week 11, Chase Brown and the Bengals travel to face the Commanders on Monday Night Football. In Week 10, during Cincinnati's victory, he rushed 10 times for 44 yards and caught eight of nine targets for 39 yards and two TDs. Brown finally found paydirt, doing so for the first time since Week 1, while recording his first two receiving scores of the season. He'll look to exploit a Commanders defense that gave up 78 yards and two TDs to Cam Skattebo in their previous outing.
outlooksByWeek.12: Chase Brown and the Bengals welcome the Saints to town for an interconference showdown in Week 12. He had six carries for six yards and caught five of eight targets for 30 yards during Cincinnati's Week 11 defeat. Brown watched as Samaje Perine erupted for 97 scrimmage yards on 10 touches, as Brown was unable to build upon his two-TD performance from the previous outing. Next up is a juicy matchup against New Orleans' 31st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (28.5) to opposing RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Brown is entering his fourth NFL season and third as Cincinnati's lead back. His 2025 season got off to a rocky start (10.1 fantasy points per game and one touchdown during his first seven games), but it turned around drastically down the stretch (21.2 points per game and 10 TDs during his final 10 games). The improvement coincided with Cincinnati's improved QB play, which should continue into 2026 with a healthy Joe Burrow. Brown has yet to finish a season higher than 16th in carries or rushing yards, but he has scored exactly 11 TDs and has finished fifth in receptions in each of the past two years, both of which have resulted in top-10 fantasy campaigns. The 26-year-old once again has minimal competition for touches in a very good Bengals offense. He's best valued as a fringe RB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Terry McLaurin had a rough Week 1 for the Commanders. On only four targets, McLaurin caught a mere two passes for 14 yards in the 24-22 loss to the Eagles. Meanwhile, both Stefon Diggs and rookie Antonio Williams found the end zone in their respective debuts for Washington. It will be interesting to see if the presence of Diggs in particular impacts McLaurin, as Diggs more than doubled McLaurin in targets with nine. Both wideouts should see plenty of action in Week 2 versus a poor Cowboys defense, though. Dallas allowed 229 passing yards and three touchdowns through the air to Jaxson Dart in their season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Terry McLaurin led the Commanders in targets last game with nine opportunities. Unfortunately, Scary Terry could only cash in two of those chances for 50 yards in a loss to the Cowboys. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, and veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for McLaurin and the rest of the Washington offense.
outlooksByWeek.4: Terry McLaurin is coming off his best game of the season for the Commanders. Scary Terry had six catches for 77 yards and a touchdown in the shocking 33-31 victory over the Seattle Seahawks. McLaurin has posted nine targets in back-to-back contests.  McLaurin caught all of his passes from backup Marcus Mariota, who will likely also line up under center in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been rather poor against the pass in 2026, allowing 276 yards per tilt through the air, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Terry McLaurin missed last game for the Commanders due to a hamstring injury. McLaurin allegedly pushed hard to play, though, meaning he could very well return to the field in Week 5 versus the Giants. He also could have his starting quarterback Jayden Daniels back under center. New York has been stingy against the pass in 2026 thus far, allowing just 205.3 passing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL. Likewise, the G-Men are tied for the league-lead with six picks.
outlooksByWeek.6: Terry McLaurin returned to the lineup for Washington following a one-game absence due to a hamstring issue. McLaurin led the squad in receiving with 62 yards on four catches in the 27-27 tie with the Giants. Fellow wideout Stefon Diggs was inactive with a hamstring ailment of his own, and if Diggs misses more time, McLaurin would certainly benefit in terms of additional looks. In Week 6, the Commanders face the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 199.6 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: McLaurin is eyeing a bounce-back campaign following a lost 2025 season in which both he (seven missed games) and quarterback Jayden Daniels (10 missed games) were sidelined for extended periods. The dud season came after Daniels helped McLaurin to a career year in 2024, which included 13 touchdowns (second most among WRs) and a seventh-place finish in fantasy points. McLaurin's target ceiling remains a concern (he's been in the 21-25% target share range each of his seven seasons), but with his quarterback healthy and his role as a vertical threat in new playcaller David Blough's offense, McLaurin is certainly poised for a rebound. The 30-year-old is best valued as a mid-to-back-end WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jordan Addison will look to record his first reception of the year as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Addison ran the second-most routes for Minnesota in Week 1 against the Packers, but he was unable to convert on either of his two targets. Veteran quarterback Carson Wentz, who filled in for an injured Kyler Murray (concussion), relied more on tight ends T.J. Hockenson and Josh Oliver behind Justin Jefferson. This could make Addison's role remains small as long as Wentz remains under center. With that being said, the Bears' defense did allow the fourth-most PPR points to wide receivers (46.3) in Week 1, which could open up Minnesota's passing game.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jordan Addison will seek to ramp things up as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Addison bounced back from a zero-catch performance in Week 1 this past Sunday, logging two catches for 21 yards against the Bears. Still, his output is nowhere near sufficient for fantasy owners, especially since he's put up WR2 numbers many times throughout the last three seasons. He'll face a Bucs defense that's allowed 24.9 PPR points per game against wide receivers this season, a top-10 mark.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jordan Addison will look to build off a big game as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. Addison saw an uptick in looks after the departure of Justin Jefferson (ankle) in Week 3, finishing the win with five catches for 90 yards and a touchdown on nine targets. While Jefferson very well could return to the field in the coming week, Addison did prove to be a solid option for Kyler Murray. Addison has proven to be an asset for Minnesota alongside Jefferson when being thrown to by a competent quarterback, which could be showcased even against a Miami defense that's ranked top-five (24.2 fantasy points per game) against WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jordan Addison will aim to do more as the Vikings travel to New Orleans in Week 5. Addison logged just four catches for 52 yards in Week 4 against the Dolphins, which was a bit of a disappointment given that Justin Jefferson (ankle) was inactive. Quarterback Kyler Murray also seemed to have built a connection with T.J. Hockenson against Miami, making it less likely that Addison will produce when Jefferson inevitably returns. The Saints have ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jordan Addison will aim to make a return as the Vikings play the Colts in Week 7. Addison missed Week 5 against the Saints with a hamstring injury, but he luckily had a bye week of rest. The fourth-year wideout will now need to return to practice if he hopes to suit up in Minnesota's upcoming home game. He'll face an Indianapolis defense that's ranked in the middle against fantasy WRs this year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jordan Addison will aim to do more with his targets as the Vikings play the Lions in Week 8. Addison didn't do much again in Week 7 against the Colts, reeling in two of his three targets for 30 yards. The speedy pass catcher has put together an underwhelming start to the 2026 season, totaling just 13 catches for 183 yards and one touchdown across five games. He'll look to capitalize on a faulty Detroit defense that's ranked 26th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jordan Addison will seek to build off a team-leading performance as the Vikings play the Bills in Week 9. Addison led Minnesota with 66 receiving yards on three catches in a Week 8 loss to the Lions. The speedy pass catcher has posted a modest 16-249-1 receiving line across six games this season. He'll face a Buffalo defense that's ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to RBs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jordan Addison will look to get more volume in Week 10 as the Vikings play the Packers. Addison finished a Week 9 loss with two catches for 28 yards off three targets, but struggles from the QB room didn't leave much room for any pass catchers to succeed. The trade deadline acquisition of Kirk Cousins to be Minnesota's new starting quarterback could be just the spark Addison needs, as he's recorded less than 30 yards in two of his last three games. Green Bay has ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to WRs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jordan Addison is set to remain out as the Vikings play the 49ers in Week 11. Addison missed a Week 10 win over Green Bay with a thumb injury, and he's likely to require a possible IR-designating surgery. Jauan Jennings (calf), Myles Price and Tai Felton could all see an uptick in usage with Addison inactive.
outlooksByWeek.12: Jordan Addison is unlikely to play in Week 12 as the Vikings take on Atlanta. Addison is set to sit out another week after undergoing thumb surgery, so he'll aim to get back to full health for Week 13 against Carolina. He's sported a quiet 18-277-1 receiving line over seven games this campaign. Addison's absence should continue to boost Jauan Jennings and Tai Felton's playing time.

player.seasonOutlook: After impressing with a 70-911-10 receiving line on 108 targets as a rookie in 2023, Addison has seen his target, reception, yardage and touchdown totals decrease each of the last two seasons. A few missed games were partially to blame for the dips, but Minnesota's quarterback woes were the main culprit in 2025, as Addison went from 10 TDs and a 65% catch rate in both 2023 and 2024 to three TDs and a 53% catch rate last season. Addison already has a pair of top-25 fantasy campaigns to his name, but it may be a stretch for him to get there in 2026 with Kyler Murray leading the Minnesota offense, not to mention Jauan Jennings' addition to the lineup. The 24-year-old is best valued as WR4/flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Xavier Worthy captured three of his six Week 1 targets for only 18 yards. The workload was low, but Kansas City QB Patrick Mahomes completed only five passes to wideouts in the Monday night opener. The third-year pro has the speed to stretch the field, but he's generally used more underneath, along with occasionally carrying the ball. Worthy is a Week 2 flex option when the Chiefs host the Colts. Indianapolis was one of five defenses to allow over 300 yards passing in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Xavier Worthy scored his first touchdown of the season in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, snagging a one-yard toss from Patrick Mahomes in the second quarter. Worthy has notched steady target volume early in the season, with 13 total looks, but that has resulted in just an 8-43-1 line, and he has yet to get a carry. With Mahomes spreading the ball around and the offense prioritizing Kenneth Walker and the run game, Worthy will need some big plays to make a real fantasy contribution. The third-year speedster will face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's given up five passing TDs through two games, but only one to a wide receiver.
outlooksByWeek.4: Xavier Worthy has struggled to break free for a big gain for Kansas City this season. The third-year speedster has managed just a 10-63-1 line on 15 targets, and surprisingly, he has yet to get a carry, perhaps to keep him healthy. Patrick Mahomes has also spread the ball around effectively, as Worthy, Travis Kelce, Rashee Rice, and Kenneth Walker all have between 15 and 18 targets, so a big volume increase isn't likely. Worthy faces a tough matchup in Week 4 against a Raiders secondary that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs and has yet to allow a TD to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Xavier Worthy comes out of Kansas City's Week 5 bye still looking to establish himself as a consistent part of the passing attack. With both Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton getting hurt during a Week 4 win over the Raiders, Worthy caught four of seven targets for a season-high 70 yards. Rice appears to be on track to return quickly, but Thornton is likely to miss the rest of the year, which could open up some downfield routes for Worthy. The third-year speedster will face a Chargers secondary in Week 6 that ranks 16th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Xavier Worthy is coming off his most productive game of the season, catching all seven of his targets for 73 yards in Kansas City's Week 6 win over the Chargers. With Rashee Rice sidelined, Worthy's volume has ticked up, but he hasn't been targeted more than seven times in a game this season. The third-year speedster also hasn't been able to break many big gains, with only one of his 21 catches going for 20-plus yards after nine of his 42 receptions in 2025 went for 20-plus. Worthy isn't likely to produce a ceiling game in Week 7 against a Seahawks secondary that ranks third in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Xavier Worthy struggled in Week 7 while filling in as Kansas City's No. 1 wide receiver, catching just three of six targets for 11 yards in a loss to the Seahawks. The third-year speedster has yet to reach 80 receiving yards this season, and it's looking increasingly like he won't live up to the billing of being the 28th overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft. Once Rashee Rice is cleared to return from a hamstring strain, Worthy might benefit from returning to a more comfortable supporting role. He'll try to bounce back in Week 8 against a Broncos secondary that could again be without Pat Surtain, but still ranks sixth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Xavier Worthy continues to struggle in his third NFL season. The Kansas City wideout has handled at least six targets in four straight games and six of seven in 2026, but that steady volume has resulted in just a 27-230-1 line on 41 total targets. Worthy is being used on downfield routes less often this year, with his 8.8 aDOT being a career low, but Andy Reid hasn't been able to consistently scheme him into open space where he can use his elite speed. If the front office adds reinforcements at wide receiver by the trade deadline, Worthy's role could be squeezed further. He'll try to put together a breakout performance in Week 9 against a Jets secondary that ranks 10th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Xavier Worthy was one of several Kansas City players to emerge from a Week 9 win over the Jets with an injury. The speedy wideout grabbed at his hamstring late in the victory after catching all six of his targets for 48 yards. Patrick Mahomes also suffered an injury to his throwing elbow, so even if Worthy doesn't end up missing time, his fantasy outlook could be affected by having Justin Fields under center instead. Worthy has struggled this season even when healthy, managing just a 33-278-1 line on 47 targets over eight games. If he's in the lineup in Week 10, he'll face a Falcons secondary that just traded away safety Jessie Bates and ranks 19th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Xavier Worthy could be in danger of vanishing from the Kansas City game plan. In a Week 10 win over the Falcons that marked the debut of trade-deadline acquisition Josh Downs, Worthy registered only three targets and failed to catch any. Downs, meanwhile, caught four of five targets and got into the end zone despite playing just 10 snaps. As the former Colt's role increases, Worthy could be squeezed further for looks from Patrick Mahomes, with Rashee Rice, Travis Kelce, and the team's running backs also seemingly ahead of him in the pecking order. Worthy will try to bounce back in Week 11 against a Cardinals secondary that ranks 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Xavier Worthy was finally able to make a splash in Kansas City's Week 11 win over the Cardinals, scoring his first touchdown since Week 2 on an 18-yard connection with Patrick Mahomes. Worthy caught just two of four targets for 38 total yards, and he's gone five straight games without reaching 50 receiving yards. The third-year speedster still has big-play upside, but he appears to be lost in the shuffle while Rashee Rice, Travis Kelce, running backs Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson, and newcomer Josh Downs all get prioritized ahead of him. Worthy will try to build on last week's effort in Week 12 against a Bills secondary that's tied for 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: After impressing as a rookie with 101 touches and 12 touchdowns in 20 games (including the playoffs), Worthy had the look of an emerging star. Things didn't go as planned in Year 2, though, as the 2024 first-round pick was injured on his third snap of the season and wasn't productive or utilized as much as expected upon his return. Worthy was limited to one touchdown (Week 6) and reached 12 fantasy points once in 14 games (Week 4). The speedy Worthy is still only 23 years old, so a Year 3 breakout is certainly possible, especially with Rashee Rice and 36-year-old Travis Kelce as his only legit target competition. He's worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Harold Fannin and the Browns visit the Buccaneers in Week 2, facing the 30th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (25.1) to TEs. The second-year pro managed two catches on three targets for 21 yards during Cleveland's 34-10 loss in the season opener. Fannin has the perfect chance at a rebound performance against Tampa Bay, as Cincinnati's Mike Gesicki cooked their defense with five receptions for 78 yards and a TD in Week 1. Even with poor quarterback play, Fannin has the talent and opportunity as the focal point of an offense that might not be good but will be forced to throw the ball plenty while playing from behind.
outlooksByWeek.3: Harold Fannin and the Browns host the Panthers in Week 3 for their 2026 home opener. He finished Cleveland's 23-19 win over the Buccaneers in Week 2 with five catches on six targets for 54 yards. Fannin is still searching for his first TD of the season after collecting six as a rookie, as fellow tight end Blake Whiteheart was on the receiving end of a 17-yard score from Deshaun Watson. Fannin looks to find the end zone against Carolina's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (9.0) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns host their division rival Steelers in Week 4 for an AFC North clash between two 2-1 teams. He caught seven of nine targets for 51 yards and two TDs during Cleveland's 21-18 victory in Week 3, including the game-winning score. Fannin led the team in receptions and yardage while tying KC Concepcion for first in targets. He now has a 12-126-2 line on 18 targets across three contests as one of Deshaun Watson's favorite receivers. Fannin will have a tough matchup against Pittsburgh's seventh-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (9.3) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns look to stay hot and earn a fourth consecutive victory against the Jets in a Week 5 road clash. He caught three of five targets for 27 yards and a touchdown during Cleveland's 27-24 win in Week 4. The second-year tight end now has three combined TDs over his last two outings. Fannin should once again be a featured target for Deshaun Watson versus the Jets' ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (10.2) to TEs. They have yet to surrender a TD to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns are back home to host the Ravens for an AFC North divisional tilt in Week 6. It was a quiet day for the sophomore tight end, as he caught just one of four targets for four yards during Cleveland's 17-12 defeat in Week 5. Fannin notched at least 50 receiving yards or caught a touchdown in three straight outings prior to this dud, so fantasy managers can blame the poor showing on weather. He'll look to get back into the end zone versus a Baltimore defense that surrendered five receptions for 42 yards and a TD to Kyle Pitts Sr. in their last outing.
outlooksByWeek.7: Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns are in Tennessee for an interconference clash in Week 7. He caught one of three targets for nine yards during Cleveland's 13-10 Week 6 win. Following a three-game stretch in which he recorded a 15-132-3 receiving line on 20 targets, Fannin has now gone two straight outings with one reception and fewer than 10 yards. The second-year TE will try to bounce back versus a Titans defense allowing 10.5 fantasy points per game (T-7th) to the position.
outlooksByWeek.8: Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns visit the Steelers for an AFC North battle in Week 8. He brought in six of nine targets for 91 yards and also lost a fumble during Cleveland's 27-24 Week 7 win. Fannin finished second behind KC Concepcion (8-129-0 on 10 targets) in receptions, yardage, and targets while setting a new season high in receiving yards. Fannin will look to exploit the Pittsburgh defense again after he recorded a 3-27-1 line against them in a Week 4 victory.
outlooksByWeek.10: Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns welcome the Texans to town for a Week 10 AFC clash. He caught both of his targets for 42 yards, including an impressive 39-yard touchdown in overtime, during Cleveland's 23-22 OT loss in Week 9. Fannin was quiet until the extra frame, a disappointing development after he erupted for a 10-154-0 line on 12 targets in his previous outing. He'll look to stay hot despite a difficult matchup versus Houston's fourth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (10.1) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.12: In Week 12, Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns look to go 5-0 at home when the Raiders visit on Sunday Night Football. He caught seven of nine targets for 91 yards during Cleveland's Week 10 victory. Fannin paced his team in every receiving category, finishing as the leader in yardage for the second time in three games. Over his last four outings, he's registered a 25-378-1 line on 32 targets. Fannin will look to stay hot against a Las Vegas defense allowing 16.7 fantasy points per game (28th) to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: Fannin is a rising star at the tight end position after overcoming the presence of David Njoku and a quarterback merry-go-round to produce a 72-731-6 receiving line (plus 7-13-1 rushing) as a 21-year-old rookie last season. The third-round pick's 108 targets rank eighth all time by a rookie tight end, and he finished no lower than eighth at the position in catches, yards, touchdowns and fantasy points last season. Fannin figures to see some touchdown regression (seven TDs, 3.8 expected, three end zone targets) and Cleveland still has quarterback question marks, but with Njoku gone, Fannin has a path to improve a bit on what was already a healthy 22% target share. He's a solid TE1 target.

outlooksByWeek.3: Jonah Coleman didn't see the ball in his NFL debut during the Broncos' opener, but his role increased in Week 2's win over the Jaguars due to RJ Harvey's hamstring strain. Coleman ended up getting more touches than J.K. Dobbins, with the 2026 fourth-round pick turning 10 carries into 39 yards and his first career touchdown while also catching all three of his targets for 19 yards. It's not clear how much time Harvey might miss, but Coleman's solid showing in his first opportunity could begin the process of turning the backfield into a three-man committee, with the workload dependent on whoever happens to be healthy. Coleman could be a risky play in Week 3 against a Rams defense that just saw the return of Aaron Donald in Week 2 and has yet to allow a rushing TD this year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jonah Coleman had the biggest share of the backfield workload in the Broncos' Week 7 win over the Cardinals, handling 11 touches to J.K. Dobbins' six and RJ Harvey's five. Coleman's 69 scrimmage yards led the trio, but the other two each made trips to the end zone while the rookie RB was held out. It was still an impressive effort in his return from an IR stint due to an ankle injury, and Coleman might be the most likely player from the group to emerge as the lead back. A messy committee is the more probable arrangement, however, heading into a Week 8 clash with a Kansas City defense that ranks seventh in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jonah Coleman may be emerging as the Broncos' lead running back. The 2026 fourth-round pick topped 100 scrimmage yards for the first time in a comeback win over Kansas City in Week 8, and he scored the winning touchdown on a five-yard run after getting Denver into the red zone with a 51-yard catch-and-run. J.K. Dobbins logged seven carries, compared to Coleman's 15 total touches, and with RJ Harvey on injured reserve, the path is clear for the rookie to handle a significant workload. Coleman could be headed for a true breakout performance in Week 9 against a Panthers defense that just fired its defensive coordinator and ranks 31st in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jonah Coleman captured the No. 1 job in the Broncos' backfield prior to the team's bye. Over the team's last two games, the rookie running back amassed 192 scrimmage yards and two rushing TDs, with his yardage split almost equally between the ground and the air. Coleman's usage as a pass catcher could decline once RJ Harvey gets healthy in a couple of weeks, but he's clearly surpassed J.K. Dobbins as the preferred ball carrier in all situations, including at the goal line. Coleman will take on a Raiders defense in Week 11 that ranks 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Jonah Coleman cemented himself as the Broncos' No. 1 running back with a stunning performance in a Week 11 win over the Raiders. The fourth-round rookie romped for 129 scrimmage yards on 28 touches while scoring three rushing touchdowns, extending his streak of games with at least one score to three. Coleman appears capable of handling a bell-cow workload and a three-down role, but he could face competition for passing-down snaps once RJ Harvey is cleared to return from a knee injury. Coleman will face a Steelers defense in Week 12 that's tied for 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Coleman was selected by the Broncos in the fourth round of April's draft. He is a 220-pound back who was highly efficient during four collegiate seasons at Arizona and Washington. Coleman didn't get much pre-contact help (1.80 YBC), but he made up for it after contact (3.73 YAC ranks second in this rookie RB class) and his career 3.4 forced missed tackle rate is best in this class. Also solid as a receiver and blocker, Coleman has three-down ability, but may not get that opportunity until 2027. The rookie will begin his career behind J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey. Coleman should be added only if Dobbins or Harvey goes down with an injury.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dylan Sampson and the Browns are in Tampa Bay to face the Buccaneers in Week 2. Unfortunately for the second-year pro, he's expected to miss "significant time" with a left knee injury sustained in Cleveland's 34-10 season-opening loss, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler. The severity of his injury is still being evaluated, but there's a high chance of him being placed on IR once more information comes out.
outlooksByWeek.6: Dylan Sampson and the Browns host the division-rival Ravens in Week 6. The second-year running back, who has been on injured reserve with a knee injury since September 15, could potentially return to practice ahead of their matchup with Baltimore. Head coach Todd Monken said Monday that there's a "possibility" Cleveland opens the 21-day practice window for Sampson this week. If he's able to get back on the field, it couldn't come at a better time for the Browns, as they're currently dealing with injuries to Quinshon Judkins (ankle) and Raheim Sanders (hip) sustained in Week 5's loss. It would be wise to monitor the practice reps for the entire backfield as they prepare for Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.8: Dylan Sampson and the Browns travel to face the division-rival Steelers in Week 8. He rushed six times for 45 yards and caught all three targets for another 32 yards during Cleveland's Week 7 win. Sampson made his first appearance since Week 1 due to a knee injury that forced him to be placed on IR. Quinshon Judkins (ankle) also returned from a one-game absence and out-touched Sampson 18-9, but it was still encouraging for Sampson to take advantage of his opportunities. He'll look to build upon this showing versus a Steelers defense allowing 20.5 fantasy points per game (T-11th) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Dylan Sampson and the Browns return home to face off against Houston in Week 10. He had eight carries for 21 yards and caught three of six targets for 27 yards during Cleveland's Week 9 overtime loss. Sampson finished tied for second on the team in targets, and with the Browns' offense likely to play from behind most weeks, he could provide a boost as the preferred back on passing downs. Sampson will aim to contribute more facing a Houston defense allowing 22.4 fantasy points per game (20th) to opposing RBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Dylan Sampson and the Browns host the Raiders on Sunday Night Football in Week 12. He rushed four times for six yards and caught four of six targets for 31 yards during Cleveland's Week 10 victory. Sampson was out-touched 13-8 by starter Quinshon Judkins, but Sampson continues to push closer to an even timeshare. Sampson will look to contribute more versus a Las Vegas defense allowing 26.9 fantasy points per game to RBs, the fifth most in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Sampson is back for Year 2 in Cleveland after an underwhelming rookie campaign in which he struggled on a small sample of work as a rusher (his 2.69 yards per carry was dead last among 65 qualified backs), but was a contributor in the passing game (23rd among RBs with 33 receptions). Sampson was a young rookie (he doesn't turn 22 until September), so there's still some room for growth, and he's positioned for a larger role behind Quinshon Judkins with Jerome Ford no longer on the roster. Expect Sampson to see some change-of-pace carries and a moderate pass-catching role in 2026. He'll land on the flex radar only if Judkins misses time.

outlooksByWeek.2: Michael Wilson will look to break through against a tough Seattle secondary for Arizona in Week 2. Wilson performed well in a season-opening win over the Chargers, catching five of seven targets for 56 yards. He outproduced presumed No. 1 wideout Marvin Harrison, though newcomer Kendrick Bourne led the WR corps with an 8-75-0 line. All three figure to be challenged by a Seahawks defense that ranked 10th in passing yards allowed last year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Michael Wilson faces a tough challenge in Arizona's Week 3 matchup in San Francisco. Wilson was quiet against Seattle this past Sunday, catching just two of seven targets for 18 yards. However, he was still the Cardinals' second-leading receiver in a game during which QB Jacoby Brissett threw for just 95 yards. The 49ers have surrendered only 15.6 fantasy points per game to wideouts, the ninth-best mark in the league threw two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Michael Wilson appears to be Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett's favorite wideout target heading into a Week 4 matchup against the Giants. Wilson got a whopping 17 targets this past Sunday in a loss to San Francisco, recording 11 catches for 89 yards and a touchdown. Meanwhile, Marvin Harrison posted a quiet 3-40-0 line on five targets. Of course, star TE Trey McBride will consistently draw plenty of Brissett's attention, but it looks like Wilson is in line for lots of looks in the team's offense. He could thrive against a Giants defense that is giving up 23.6 fantasy points per game to WRs, ninth-most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Michael Wilson has settled in atop Arizona's WR depth chart heading into a Week 5 tilt against the Lions. Wilson caught seven passes on 13 targets for 95 yards against the Giants in Week 4, leading or co-leading the Cardinals in all three categories. He's drawn a whopping 30 targets over his past two contests, making it clear that QB Jacoby Brissett sees him as the top option among the team's wideouts. Wilson could be in store for a big game against a Detroit defense that has yielded 28.3 fantasy points per game to wide receivers, third-most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Michael Wilson is set to lead Arizona's wideout corps versus the Rams in Week 6. After Marvin Harrison was made inactive this past Sunday due to a pending trade, Wilson functioned as the no-doubt No. 1 WR for the Cardinals but managed just four catches for 30 yards against Detroit. He was outproduced by fellow wideout Kendrick Bourne, who posted a 5-70-0 line, but Wilson should have plenty of chances to thrive with Harrison officially off to Houston. The Rams have given up the fewest receiving yards per game to wideouts this season, but they've also surrendered seven receiving TDs to the position, tied for third-most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Michael Wilson has emerged as Arizona's leading wide receiver following Marvin Harrison Jr.'s departure, recording 33 receptions for 320 yards and a touchdown through six games. Wilson has averaged 9.7 yards per reception, and his established role as the team's new WR1 should keep him among Jacoby Brissett's preferred targets alongside star tight end Trey McBride. However, the Cardinals' passing attack has struggled to generate explosive plays, limiting Wilson's weekly ceiling. To make things even more complicated, the Week 7 matchup against the Broncos is far from easy, as Denver has allowed the seventh-fewest fantasy points per game to wideouts in 2026. That, coupled with Brissett's inconsistent play under center, limits Wilson's fantasy appeal considerably in most formats.
outlooksByWeek.8: Michael Wilson will look to get back his early-season mojo with a juicy matchup when Arizona faces the Cowboys in Week 8. After hauling in 18 passes on 30 targets for 184  yards across Weeks 3 and 4, Wilson has compiled just 12 receptions on 22 targets for 117 yards over his past three games. The downturn has some in spite of the Cardinals trading away Marvin Harrison to make Wilson the team's clear-cut No. 1 wide receiver, though tight end Trey McBride has continued to feature as QB Jacoby Brissett's top target. Harrison will have a chance to put up big numbers versus a Dallas defense that ranks 27th in the NFL with 23.9 fantasy points per game allowed to wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.9: Michael Wilson could play in Arizona's Week 9 matchup against Seattle despite dealing with two broken ribs. The wideout suffered the injury this past Sunday in a win over Dallas, but he returned to the game after getting hurt and finished with eight catches for 111 yards and one touchdown on 15 targets. Wilson thrived with both Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew under center, so the switch to Minshew as the Cardinals' starting QB shouldn't impact Wilson's production if he's able to suit up in Week 9. However, the ribs issue plus a stout Seattle pass defense that has given up the fewest fantasy points per game this season (14.3) to wideouts could hurt Wilson's production.

player.seasonOutlook: After averaging 4.3 targets and 7.6 fantasy points per game during his first 38 NFL games, Wilson broke out with Jacoby Brissett under center during the final eight games of 2025, averaging 11.0 targets and 21.2 fantasy PPG. The stretch also coincided with Marvin Harrison Jr. dealing with health issues, and it's worth noting that Wilson's receiving lines in the four games Harrison was active weren't quite as good (3-40-0, 3-61-0, 4-34-0, 3-36-0). A healthy Harrison (along with TE Trey McBride) figures to lead to a return to earth for Wilson, but the 26-year-old did enough late last season to warrant WR4/flex consideration in drafts.

outlooksByWeek.2: Matt Gay was perfect in his Raiders debut, converting field goals from 30 and 47 yards and all three extra points in a season-opening win over the Dolphins. A rebuilding opponent certainly provided Gay with extra opportunities, but the Las Vegas offense could also be better than expected. New head coach Klint Kubiak and an improved quarterback situation, with Kirk Cousins steadying the ship until rookie Fernando Mendoza is ready, should help. The pending return of Brock Bowers will also help generate more scoring drives. Gay may not be able to squander any chances in Week 2 against a Chargers team that ranked ninth in points per game allowed in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Matt Gay has been busy to begin his Raiders' career, converting all three of his field-goal attempts and all six of his extra points through the first two games of the season. The outlook for the offense should improve once Brock Bowers is cleared for his 2026 debut, and while there's additional uncertainly on the horizon once first overall pick Fernando Mendoza is deemed ready to replace Kirk Cousins under center, Gay could actually benefit if the young QB struggles to get the ball into the end zone while he figures out NFL defenses. Gay will face a Saints team in Week 3 that's allowed an exact mirror to his production so far, with opposition kickers getting three FGs and six PATs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Matt Gay has been both busy and perfect for the surprising 3-0 Raiders, connecting on all six of his field goal attempts and all eight of his PATs. The veteran kicker was also successful on his only attempt from 50-plus yards, as he looks to boot at least three long-range FGs for a sixth straight season. Gay has also benefited from a favorable early schedule, as all three of Las Vegas' games so far have been played indoors. The team will get a fourth straight game under a roof in a Week 4 home tilt against Kansas City, but Gay likely won't be able to afford to squander any opportunities versus an opponent that has given up just 16.7 points per game, tied for third in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Matt Gay continues to benefit from the Raiders' surprisingly strong start to the season on offense with Kirk Cousins under center. In a Week 4 loss to Kansas City, Gay was a perfect 4-for-4 on FG tries while also converting his only PAT. The veteran has yet to miss an attempt in 2026, going 10-for-10 on FGs and 9-for-9 on extra points, putting him third in the NFL in kicker scoring behind the Vikings' Will Reichard and the Colts' Spencer Shrader. Gay likely won't be able to afford to start squandering opportunities in Week 5 against a Patriots team that's allowed 19.3 points per game so far, tied for sixth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Matt Gay missed his first kick of the season in the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots, pinging the upright on a field goal attempt from 48 yards out. He's still having a strong season, converting all 11 of his PATs and going 11-for-12 on FG attempts, including his only attempt from 50-plus yards. Gay has benefited from a surprisingly potent offense under Kirk Cousins, but the veteran QB may be reverting to his usual level, perhaps opening the door for first overall pick Fernando Mendoza to take the reins, so it's not necessarily bad news for Gay's long-term outlook. Gay will take on a Bills team in Week 6 that's allowing 28.2 points per game, 28th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Matt Gay stayed busy in the Raiders' Week 6 loss to the Bills, going a perfect 3-for-3 on both field goal attempts and extra points. The veteran kicker has benefited from the team's offensive resurgence under new head coach Klint Kubiak, and Gay sits third in scoring in the NFL behind the Colts' Spencer Shrader and the Bills' Tyler Bass. Gay will face a Rams team in Week 7 that's allowed 23.0 points per game, tied for 17th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Matt Gay was perfect in the Raiders' Week 8 win over the Jets, converting all five of his PATs and his only field goal attempt. The veteran kicker has missed just two FGs through eight games this season, going 18-for-20 (90.0%), and he's drilled all 19 of his extra points. Playing his home games indoors appears to suit Gay, after he connected on just 13 of 19 field goals during his 10-game stint with the Commanders in 2025. Gay likely can't afford to squander any opportunities in Week 9 against a 49ers team allowing just 19.9 points per game, tied for sixth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Matt Gay was afforded few opportunities in the Raiders' Week 9 loss to the 49ers, connecting on a 50-yard attempt for his only field goal and converting both his PATs. The veteran kicker has a 90.5% FG success rate on the season, going 19-for-21, and he has yet to miss an extra point in 2026, but his erratic weekly volume limits his fantasy utility. Gay isn't likely to see much volume in Week 10 against a Seahawks team allowing 18.0 points per game, tied for fourth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.11: Matt Gay didn't get much volume in the Raiders' Week 10 loss to the Seahawks, as he converted both his field goal attempts and his only PAT. The veteran kicker has handled two or fewer FG attempts in four of the last six games, but with rookie Fernando Mendoza replacing Kirk Cousins under center, the offense's efficiency could take a step backward and give Gay more field goal chances. He may not be much busier in Week 11 against a Broncos team allowing 20.7 points per game, ninth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.12: Matt Gay has been perfect over the last four weeks, going 5-for-5 on field goal attempts and 11-for-11 on PATs. The veteran kicker's volume hasn't been significantly affected by the switch at quarterback from Kirk Cousins to Fernando Mendoza, and the Raiders' offense might actually take a step forward once Brock Bowers gets healthy, with young skill players Ashton Jeanty and Jack Bech showing signs of breaking out. Gay will look to stay locked in during Week 12's clash with a Browns team that's allowing 22.0 points per game, tied for 14th in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Braelon Allen will look to build on a solid opener when the Jets face the Packers in Week 2. Allen had 10 carries in Week 1 under new OC Frank Reich, after totaling 18 carries in four games before injury in 2025. The volume resulted from the Jets playing with a lead, a game script that's unlikely to repeat in Week 2. Allen remains a secondary option to Breece Hall, so patience is warranted, particularly against a defense that allowed only 3.7 yards per carry in Week 1 and is more vulnerable through the air.
outlooksByWeek.3: Braelon Allen's usage remains questionable as the Jets prepare to face the Lions in Week 3. After a run-heavy Week 1 where Allen had 10 attempts, that number was cut in half in Week 2. He has also only seen two targets through two games. Breece Hall remains the workhorse, and the Lions' vulnerability to chunk plays in the passing game could further phase Allen out of meaningful touches, despite Detroit allowing 5.2 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.4: Braelon Allen is poised for an expanded role in Week 4 when the Jets face the Bears due to Breece Hall's thigh injury. The rushing game has struggled over the last two weeks, averaging a mere 2.7 yards per carry, but the Jets have remained committed to running while also involving their backs in the passing game. With volume seemingly secure, Allen could shine against a defense that's allowing 4.9 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.5: Braelon Allen could be slated for bulk carries in Week 5 when the Jets face the Browns with Breece Hall's (quad) uncertain availability. Filling in for Hall in Week 4, Allen was the only Jet to receive a carry, putting him in line to potentially exploit a Cleveland defense that's allowed at least 82 yards to opposing lead backs in three straight weeks and an appealing 4.8 yards per carry. If Hall returns, he can't be guaranteed a full workload, lending flex appeal to Allen.
outlooksByWeek.6: Braelon Allen's role for the Jets in Week 6 against the Patriots is in flux due to uncertainty surrounding Breece Hall (quad). Allen has dominated carries in two games with Hall out, breaking out in Week 5 with a 24-carry, 116-yard performance. New England hasn't allowed an opposing back to gain over 75 yards, and Allen hasn't been a factor in the Jets' passing game. If Hall does not return, volume will be Allen's best asset.
outlooksByWeek.7: Braelon Allen will hope to again receive the bulk of the opportunities out of the Jets' backfield in Week 7 against the Dolphins. Allen has been a workhorse over the last three weeks with Breece Hall (quad) sidelined, averaging 18.3 carries. Allen's lack of involvement in the passing game could cap his upside against a defense that's allowed five touchdown receptions to opposing running backs but only three rushing scores. Volume remains paramount to a running back's success, and Allen should have that even if Hall is back, as a full workload after three weeks wouldn't seem likely.
outlooksByWeek.8: Braelon Allen's workload is unclear heading into the Jets' Week 8 matchup with the Raiders. He has shined over the last four games with Breece Hall (quad) sidelined, topping 100 total yards three times, but would likely be in a timeshare if Hall can return in Week 8. Both backs can still offer sound production as the matchup is one of the most favorable available. Las Vegas is surrendering 5.2 yards per carry and the second-most fantasy points per game, last week allowing two 90-plus yard rushers to the Rams.
outlooksByWeek.9: Braelon Allen's successful five-week run as the Jets' lead back appears set to end in Week 9 against the Chiefs with the pending return of Breece Hall (quad). Allen had at least 16 touches in every outing with Hall sidelined, capping it off with a career-high 147 yards in Week 8. While he's earned a role in the team's backfield, his workload share is unclear. Facing a defense that's allowing just 3.3 yards per carry further limits Allen's potential production.
outlooksByWeek.10: Braelon Allen has reverted to a secondary option for the Jets with Breece Hall healthy ahead of a Week 10 matchup with the Bills. Allen recorded just 10 touches in Hall's return in Week 9 after 19 or more opportunities over the last five weeks. With Hall a preferred option in the passing game and facing a defense that allows just 3.8 yards per carry, Allen is unlikely to collect enough usage to be in the Week 10 fantasy mix.
outlooksByWeek.11: Braelon Allen remains second fiddle to Breece Hall ahead of the Jets' Week 11 matchup with the Chargers. In two games since Hall's return, Allen has 16 carries compared to Hall's 26. Hall has also caught seven passes to Allen's three. Despite being more efficient than Hall, Allen's role appears clear in a matchup against a defense that's allowing a modest 4.0 yards per carry, likely rendering Allen to flex territory.
outlooksByWeek.12: Braelon Allen may garner enough work in the Jets' Week 12 matchup with the Dolphins to be viable. Despite Breece Hall's return to health, Allen has at least eight carries in three straight games, with the Jets being run-centric. He found ample holes in the Dolphins' front as a lead back in Week 7 and can repeat that per-touch success, worthy of flex consideration.

player.seasonOutlook: Hopes were high for Allen entering 2025, but a slow start was followed by a season-ending knee injury in Week 4. During Weeks 1-3, Allen played 28% of the Jets' snaps and totaled 67 yards and one touchdown on 16 touches. The 2024 fourth-round pick has shown he can contribute as both a rusher (110 career carries) and receiver (32 targets), but he's simply not going to see the field much as long as feature back Breece Hall is healthy. Allen, 22, has some late-round insurance stash appeal, as he'd likely start over Isaiah Davis in the event of a Hall injury and would thus find himself on the flex radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Shough will lead the Saints' offense into a tough Week 2 matchup against the Ravens, whose defense gave up just 12.7 fantasy points to quarterbacks in Week 1. Despite a poor first half, Shough threw for 410 yards and three touchdowns in last week's overtime loss, making him the league's leading passer. However, Shough was prone to turnovers, throwing two interceptions and losing a fumble, which is something Baltimore could capitalize on. It'll be a tough Week 2 matchup, as the Ravens allowed just 166 passing yards in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Shough will lead the Saints' offense into a Week 3 matchup against the Raiders, whose defense has allowed just 17.4 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season. Shough has been one of the NFL's most productive QBs through two weeks, leading the league in passing yards (662) while producing five total touchdowns. Despite throwing the ball 90 times in his first two contests, Shough remains one of the league leaders in completion percentage (68.9 percent). He's in for a difficult Week 3 matchup, however, with the Raiders' allowing just one passing touchdowns this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Shough is expected lead the Saints' offense into a Week 4 matchup against the Falcons, whose defense allowed just 14 points to the Packers in Week 3. Shough continued his stretch of impressive play in the Week 3 loss to the Raiders, throwing for 255 yards, four touchdowns and an interception. Head coach Kellen Moore continues to put his faith in Shough, as the Saints' are throwing the ball 44 times per game through three weeks. Expect Shough to remain one of fantasy's best quarterbacks in Week 4 against a Falcons defense that's given up 21.6 fantasy points per game to the position this year.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Shough is expected to lead the Saints' offense into the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Despite a loss in Week 4, Shough remained productive, throwing for 286 yards and a touchdown with no turnovers. The second-year pro is now averaging a whopping 45 pass attempts per game, suggesting he'll remain productive for fantasy purposes as the season progresses. Despite this, he's in for a very tough Week 5 matchup against a Vikings defense that's allowed just 15.7 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season, the best mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Shough is expected to remain productive in the Saints' Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Shough had his worst performance of the season in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings, completing just 16 of 25 pass attempts for 96 yards and two interceptions. Despite this, he currently ranks sixth in the NFL in passing yards (1,299) through five games, attempting a league-leading 205 pass attempts. He could definitely bounce back in Week 6 against a Giants defense that's given up 22.8 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyler Shough will look to stay hot in the Saints' Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. Shough was very productive in the Week 6 win over the Giants, accounting for just 176 total yards but scoring four touchdowns (three passing, one rushing). Despite attempting just 30 passes in last week's win, Shough is still averaging the third-most pass attempts per game in the NFL (39.2) through six weeks. Shough could struggle against a tough Steelers defense in Week 7, as they have allowed just 16.8 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this year.
outlooksByWeek.9: Tyler Shough is expected to leads the Saints' offense into the Week 9 matchup against the Browns. Through seven contests this season, Shough has thrown for 1,721 yards, 13 touchdowns and six interceptions while averaging the most pass attempts per game (39.0) in the NFL. With this high passing volume, Shough should continue to find fantasy success going forward. However, he could really struggle against a tough Browns defense in Week 9 that's given up just 17.1 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Tyler Shough is expected to continue leading the Saints' offense during the Week 10 matchup against the Panthers. Shough played turnover-free football in the Week 9 overtime win over the Browns, completing 21 of 35 passes for 265 yards and a touchdown. He remains tied for the league-lead in passing attempts per game (38.5). Additionally, 2026 first-round pick Jordyn Tyson made his season debut in Week 9, suggesting Shough's fantasy outlook is very positive going forward. Shough could continue to thrive in Week 10 against a Carolina defense that's allowed 20.4 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Tyler Shough is set to lead the Saints' offense into the Week 11 matchup against the Bears. Shough had an underwhelming outing in the Week 10 loss to the Panthers, completing 25 of 35 pass attempts for 187 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Despite this, he remains tied for the second-most pass attempts per game (38.1) in the NFL this season, suggesting he'll have loads of opportunities for points as the year progresses. Shough is set to face a Bears defense that's given up just 20.8 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Tyler Shough is expected to continue leading the Saints' offense into the Week 12 matchup against the Bengals. Shough has been held in check over the last two weeks, averaging 204.5 passing yards, one touchdown and one interception per game during that stretch. Despite this, Shough ranks second in the NFL in pass attempts per game (38.5), suggesting more fantasy value is imminent as the season progresses. Additionally, he's in for a favorable Week 12 matchup against a Bengals defense that's allowed 20.9 fantasy points per game through nine contests this season.

player.seasonOutlook: One of the surprise second-half breakout players of 2025, Shough scored 17-plus fantasy points in seven of his nine full games, including six straight to end the season. The 2025 second-round pick was a solid producer with his arm (250.1 passing yards per game) and his legs (19.3 rushing yards per game and three TDs). Shough didn't show a high ceiling (he never reached 22 fantasy points in a game), though that can be traced to a shaky supporting cast. That's an area that should be better in 2026 with Travis Etienne Jr. and No. 8 overall pick Jordyn Tyson (once healthy) joining the team. He's still unproven, but Shough enters Year 2 (same as coach Kellen Moore) as an intriguing fantasy breakout candidate. He's worth a look in the later rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chig Okonkwo had a rough debut Week 1 for the Commanders. On only three targets, the former Titan caught a mere two passes for 16 yards in the 24-22 loss to the Eagles. He subsequently injured his hamstring and did not return. Meanwhile, both Stefon Diggs and rookie Antonio Williams found the end zone in their respective debuts for Washington. John Bates and Ben Sinnott would step in at tight end if Chig misses Week 2 versus Dallas. If he suits up, Okonkwo would have a favorable matchup against a Cowboys defense that allowed two touchdowns to Giants tight end Isaiah Likely in the season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chig Okonkwo did not play in Week 2 for the Commanders. Washington's active tight ends did not fare well, catching a combined two passes for 20 yards in the 37-20 loss to Dallas. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, and veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for Okonkwo, even if he is able to suit up.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chig Okonkwo is set to practice with the Commanders as the squad heads to London for Week 4. John Bates has handled the tight end slot amid limited fanfare without Okonkwo, as Bates caught a nine-yard pass last game in Okonkwo's absence. If Okonkwo can suit up in Week 4, he may have an intriguing matchup versus the Colts, even with backup quarterback Marcus Mariota under center. Indianapolis is allowing 276 passing yards per tilt, which is 30th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chig Okonkwo returned to the lineup for the Commanders following a two-game absence due to a hamstring ailment. Okonkwo was targeted four times, but managed two catches for a mere five yards in the dismal 30-13 loss to the Colts. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels could return to the fold in Week 5 versus the Giants, though, which would certainly be a boost for the passing game. However, New York has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, allowing just 205.3 passing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chig Okonkwo made his presence felt for Washington in his return to the lineup. Following a two-game absence due to a hamstring ailment, Okonkwo led the team with six targets en route to four catches for 60 yards in the 27-27 tie with the Giants. In Week 6, the Commanders face the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 199.6 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.8: Chig Okonkwo has posted back-to-back 60-plus yard outings for Washington, and could see an uptick in targets for the remainder of the season.  No. 1 wideout Terry McLaurin will miss the rest of the 2026 campaign for the Commanders due to a knee injury. Okonkwo has amassed 13 targets in the last two games alone. In Week 8, Washington will face division rival Philadelphia. The reeling Eagles have been suspect in defending the pass this season. Philadelphia is giving up 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Chig Okonkwo made a dazzling one-handed catch last game for Washington. The highlight-reel grab is a candidate for one of the top receptions of the NFL season to date. Okonkwo finished with two catches for 32 yards in the 27-10 win over the Eagles. He was targeted four times. In Week 9, Okonkwo will face a stellar Rams pass defense. Los Angeles is allowing just 191.9 passing yards per game, which is fourth in the NFL. In addition, the Rams have yielded just 10 passing scores this season, which is tied for eighth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Chig Okonkwo has been targeted at least six times in three of the last four contests for the Commanders. Okonkwo caught six passes for 57 yards in the 20-13 loss to the Rams last game. Okonkwo has at least 55 receiving yards in three of the last four games for Washington. However, he will face a difficult test in the form of the New York Giants in Week 10. New York is allowing just 177.8 passing yards per tilt, which is third in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Chig Okonkwo has been a frequent target of quarterback Jayden Daniels since returning from injury for the Commanders. Okonkwo has at least six targets in four of the last five contests for Washington.  In fact, Okonkwo has been targeted 15 times over the last two games alone. Okonkwo is still looking for his first touchdown of the season, though. In Week 11, he will face a fairly stingy Cincinnati pass defense. The Bengals are allowing only 216.2 passing yards per clash, which is 11th in the league. Likewise, Cincy has given up just 11 throwing scores, which is tied for fifth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: Chig Okonkwo continues to serve as an excellent safety valve for the Commanders. Okonkwo reeled in four passes for 66 yards in the stunning 22-20 win over the Bengals. Okonkwo has at least four catches in five of his last six games played, though he is still looking for his first touchdown of the season. In Week 12, Chig will face a lackluster Arizona pass defense. The Cardinals are allowing 226.4 passing yards per tilt, which is 20th in the NFL. In addition, the Cardinals have surrendered the most passing touchdowns in the league to date.

player.seasonOutlook: Okonkwo signed with the Commanders after spending his first four seasons in Tennessee. The 2022 fourth-round pick is one of only four tight ends who have appeared in all 68 games since he entered the league, and he's also one of only six tight ends who have registered 50-plus receptions each of the past three seasons. On the other hand, Okonkwo has yet to clear a 16% target share in a single season, and he has been a nonfactor near the goal line (eight TDs and 11 end zone targets in his career). As a result, he has finished exactly 21st in fantasy points each of the past three seasons. Perhaps he'll make a leap as one of Jayden Daniels' top targets, but the 27-year-old is no more than a back-end TE2 lottery ticket.

The Cowboys underwent a major roster overhaul and finished on a massive cold spell defensively late last season, making it difficult to get behind them as a fantasy option at the onset of 2026. Only the Jets scored fewer fantasy points for the year. The Cowboys did restock their roster during the offseason, adding Caleb Downs, Jalen Thompson and Rashan Gary (among others), and they do have a Giants matchup to open their schedule. It's still better to wait and see how this unit jells before diving in, however, even from a streaming standpoint.

outlooksByWeek.2: Xavier Hutchinson remains off the fantasy radar in most formats heading into Houston's Week 2 home game against the Bengals. He was third on the Texans with six targets in the season opener but finished with just three catches for 32 receiving yards. Hutchinson has topped 42 yards just twice through 50 career regular-season appearances.
outlooksByWeek.3: Xavier Hutchinson drew nine targets in Nico Collins' (hamstring) absence in Week 2 but turned that into just three catches for 37 yards. Hutchinson figures to maintain a prominent role in Houston's passing game against the league-worst Colts defense in Week 3, especially if Collins remains sidelined. Whether Hutchinson can turn that significant usage into production is another matter, as he has usually failed to capitalize on such opportunities in the past, with only two career regular-season games of 42 or more receiving yards. Hutchinson is in the Week 3 deep-league flex conversation, but his lack of prior production is concerning.
outlooksByWeek.4: Xavier Hutchinson continues to do little with substantial volume, and that seems unlikely to change in Week 4, even with Houston hosting a weak Cowboys defense surrendering 27.3 points per game. Hutchinson has caught just nine of 21 targets this season and is averaging 40 receiving yards per game. Houston's lack of capable alternatives at WR figures to keep Hutchinson involved enough in Week 4 to earn deep-league flex consideration, especially if top wideout Nico Collins (hamstring) misses a third consecutive game.
outlooksByWeek.5: Xavier Hutchinson has exactly three catches in every game this season for the Texans and is averaging 42 receiving yards per game heading into a Week 5 road game against the Titans. He has drawn 11 targets in two games playing alongside Nico Collins and 15 targets during the two games Collins missed due to a hamstring injury. Collins should continue to work as C.J. Stroud's No. 1 option against Tennessee's beatable secondary, while the remainder of Houston's receiving corps is best left on the bench or waiver wire, Hutchinson included.
outlooksByWeek.6: Xavier Hutchinson set season highs with four catches and 65 yards in Houston's Week 5 win over the Titans, but he has yet to score this season and has just three touchdowns in 54 career regular-season games. He's likely to slide down a spot on the WR depth chart once trade acquisition Marvin Harrison is up to speed, but that may not happen in Week 6 against the Jaguars. Hutchinson should get enough opportunities against a Jaguars defense that has allowed the most yards in the NFL to wide receivers to warrant Week 6 flex consideration in deeper formats.
outlooksByWeek.7: Xavier Hutchinson had season-low totals across the board with two catches for 10 yards on three targets in Houston's Week 6 win over the Jaguars, and he won't be a recommended Week 7 fantasy play against the Giants, even in deeper formats. He was earning decent volume while Houston's WR room was banged up, but the return of Nico Collins from a hamstring injury, coupled with the trade for Marvin Harrison and emergence of Jaylin Noel, have relegated Hutchinson to a depth role. Hutchinson doesn't have the talent to find consistent success with limited usage, as he has just three TDs in 55 career regular-season games.
outlooksByWeek.9: Xavier Hutchinson is likely to continue sliding down the depth chart at wide receiver as Marvin Harrison and Tank Dell get acclimated in Houston. The Texans traded for Harrison prior to Week 6 and activated Dell from injured reserve prior to Week 7. Hutchinson has just 27 receiving yards in two games since Harrison's arrival, though Hutchinson scored his first TD of the season in Week 7 against the Giants, marking just his fourth TD in 56 regular-season appearances for the Texans. Following a Week 8 bye, the Texans take on the winless Chargers in Week 9. Hutchinson isn't a recommended fantasy option against a Chargers defense that has been more stout against the pass than the run.
outlooksByWeek.10: Xavier Hutchinson takes a two-game touchdown streak into Houston's Week 10 road game against the Browns, but he has just 46 receiving yards over that span and is averaging a meager 36 receiving yards per game this season. He has maintained a prominent role in a high-ceiling Houston passing offense, drawing at least five targets in all but one game, but Hutchinson hasn't done much with those opportunities and had just three career TDs in 3.5 seasons prior to his current two-game scoring streak. Nico Collins, Tank Dell, Marvin Harrison, and Kayshon Boutte all have higher upside among Houston's WRs for Week 10 and beyond.
outlooksByWeek.11: Xavier Hutchinson has scored in three consecutive games heading into Houston's Week 11 home game against the Colts. He's averaging six targets per game, and while his paltry average of 6.4 yards per target suggests C.J. Stroud would be better off distributing those looks elsewhere, Hutchinson's volume has propelled the 26-year-old wideout into the weekly flex conversation. Perhaps Hutchinson is just a late bloomer who is finding his groove, but it's fair to remain skeptical considering his three TDs in the last three games match his total of three TDs from 55 regular-season appearances before this streak. The Colts have limited WRs to eight TDs in 10 games, though Indianapolis is allowing 149 yards per game to the position.
outlooksByWeek.12: Xavier Hutchinson has topped 30 yards just once in Houston's last five games. He had a three-game touchdown streak to buoy his stat line during that stretch, but the scoring binge was likely fool's gold for a fourth-year player who had just three career TDs prior to that streak, which was snapped in the Week 11 win over Indianapolis. Starting a new scoring streak won't be easy in Week 12 against a Ravens defense that has held WRs to just seven touchdowns. While the Ravens are giving up 162 yards per game to the position, Hutchinson is competing for targets with Nico Collins and Tank Dell, as well as possibly Kayshon Boutte (hip) and Marvin Harrison (hamstring). Considering that Hutchinson's 6.3 yards per target are second-fewest among that group, ahead of only Harrison, it's tough to trust Hutchinson as anything more than a deep-league flex-spot flier.
